column10: I bought this item because the Arrowhead Mills Puffed Millet was unavailable. At first I didn't think Nature's Path tasted as good as Arrowhead and I figured that was owing to the very different composition of the bags the two companies use. But it's more likely I just got an older box.At this point, I've developed a preference for Nature's Path millet. They do a much better job of filtering out the seed hulls than Arrowhead. The hulls are pesky little buggers that get caught between your teeth and such. They are virtually absent from Nature's Path. Arrowhead on the other hand always gives you a heaping helping of them.I do miss the Arrowhead bags though. They are perfect for bagging up the cat's litter clumps.
If my smoothie or cereal is too thin or sweet, then I add this puffed millet; or eat it with sweet granola bars.  It's also one of the very few grains that is alkaline.

I really love puffed millet and the price here was better than at the local store. However, every time I have ordered it I have received a shipment that is not very fresh and why should I buy a product and then have to place it in the oven in order to make it less stale tasting? When I buy it from the store at least it is crisp and enjoyable to eat which is the way millet should be. I have purchased this product three times but will not again-- yes, I have finally learned my lesson. IMO, cereal should not be limp until you place it in milk or other beverage.
I ordered these with the NP rice puffs and I mixed them together. They're really tasty and are even better with fruit or Splenda.

Nature's Path Organic Millet Puffs Cereal is - together with Kamut from the same brand - a staple in my diet. Particularly good with a tablespoon of La Tourangelles hazelnut oil on 1 oz of millet. The crunchy natural sweet nutty taste is something I don't want to miss in the morning. It starts my day together with yogurt and fresh fruit in a healthy way without giving me a sugar high or weighing me down. And that is why I have subscribed to getting it delivered on a regular basis.

This is a good product and were it certified gluten free, I'd have given it 5 stars. My kids like it, even the older ones. It's plain, naturally, but that's the idea. While it hasn't caused any serious reactions, we're not seriously allergic to gluten, just intolerant.For those who are dairy free, we've served it with rice milk, (we tend to avoid soy milk as too much if it isn't good for kids due to the hormonal influence), hot cocoa (dairy free; this makes it into a hot cereal that can be more fun than simply cooking hulled millet.)We buy it by the case on subscription to save money as it's difficult to find any plain millet where we live.

Some students of nutrition believe that it is good to balance your intake of nutrients in terms of the effect the food will have on your body's pH balance.  Some foods are thought to be more acidic, and others more alkaline.  I like oatmeal, and I feel that it is a very healthy food to eat for breakfast, but it seems that it may be somewhat acidic, from what I can gather.  According to one source of information about the role of foods on one's pH balance, millet is one of the few grains that is more alkaline.  So in the interest of seeking a better pH balance, I ordered Nature's Path Organic Millet Puffs Cereal, and I was not disappointed.  I mix these millet puffs with some oatmeal, a little spelt, some wheat germ, a dusting of cinnamon, and organic nonfat milk.  These millet puffs are tasty, and easy to chew, not to mention that they are very reasonably priced.  I am pleased to include them as part of my breakfast, and I recommend that you try them.
Product very good tasty and fresh was happy experiences and enjoyable . Price better than at health food store . Will buy more

I discovered this cereal while trying to find "gluten-free" and therefore safe foods to consume.  Yes, I have celiac disease, which was ignored years ago by many and I have had to find the foods I could tolerate by trial and error.  Nature's Path Organic Millet Puffs have been a delightful discovery.  Not only are they Gluten-Free and Organic, but the quality remains consistent and they are DELICIOUS.  Excellent as a snack food too!!  Give them a try!!

column4: Dawnielass "exercise addict, book nerd and mom"
column10: I really like cereal, have for years.  I was probably eating too much pumpkin flax and other granolas from nature's path and some local granola from Kingston, WA, Mirracole Morsels.  More expensive the latter and more energy dense.  I haven't ever had a weight problem, but it is easy to get too much of a good thing with the granolas, and I got out of my comfort zone, as in, if I keep eating this am I going to go past my usual set point.  So, I decided I'd wean myself off to something else gluten free and less energy dense.  The 12 packs of puffed millet are a good deal and are much less energy dense.  I like to mix a bowl with a little Himalayan pink salt, stevia, cinnamon and crushed walnuts, 1/2 to 1 walnut per bowl.  The walnuts probably help with the glycemic load.  I'd like to see Amazon carry amaranth puffs, or puffed quinoa.  Puffed quinoa would be ideal.  I'd stock up on it if the price beat what is out there, namely Azure Standard mail/web order truck delivery.
These are a great gluten-free alternative to other cereals. To make them extra tasty, I eat them with some stevia and almond milk to remind me of my corn pops days.

I agree with the other reviewer. The tea was hearty, but there was hardly a trace of vanilla flavor. column9: Reishi Green Tea.... overpriced, but good.
column10: I refuse to refer to the mushroom in this tea as "Ganoderma".  It's Reishi.  It's been Reishi for thousands and thousands of years.  I don't know why the Organo company tried to get all fancy and used a lesser common name for the medicinal mushroom.With that said, onto my review... I like the tea.  I notice beneficial effects of drinking it.  Infused with the Reishi, it seems to sustain the energy you get from the caffeine, rather than a crash and burn I get from other green teas.  I feel the beneficial effects of this tea over a period of sometimes, 3, 4, 5 hours.  It's balanced, easy going energy, and I feel like I do get a slight bit of oxygenation in my body as well.  I can even drink this tea right before bed, and I'll sleep like a baby.The taste... not great.  It does taste like Green Tea, but it tastes like you diluted a normal cup of green tea with 8 oz of water.  It brews very weak.  The color is just an ever so slight tint of green.  It doesn't seem like much even comes out of the bag, and it tastes like it.  I'm assuming since there's the Reishi in there, that's why.  The Reishi actually brews clear, so it would make sense that the tea is a lesser color.All in all, do I think this stuff is worth almost 90 cents per cup?  No.  Certainly not.  I buy bulk organic japanese green tea for literally, 10 cents per tea bag.  So paying 9x that for tea isn't really too appealing.  I'm a big Green Tea drinker.  I usually drink 3 cups a day.  That would be almost $3 per day for this tea.  What I do, to save costs, is buy Reishi tea, and dump that into a cup of green tea for the ultimate cup of tea.Amazon offers Reishi tea (again, which Organo calls Ganoderma)[...], as well as super cheap bulk organic green tea.  Try this recipe -- 1 cup Reishi, mixed with 1 cup of Green Tea.  Put them together in a large cup or thermos, and enjoy.  You're getting the same stuff (more Reishi, actually, which is truly the good stuff) for less than half the cost.

The main benefit of this "tea"(a list of actual ingredients for this drink is apparently non-existent, so the viability of this "tea" is questionable) is the Ganoderma extract it apparently contains, as the taste leaves something to be desired.The distributor I got this tea from claims the teabags can be used 2 or more times, but I found that getting even one cup of decent tea out of the teabag was a challenge.If you're looking for a healthy, but boring "tea", this is definitely the tea for you!If you're looking for a healthy and fuller tasting tea, I would pass this one up.

This might seem like an absurd idea, chocolate-flavored vinegar, and I can reassure you that the uses described on this product page -- especially marinating meats -- are guaranteed to nauseate your gourmet family and guests. But there is an interesting use for this and for the other Xtreme balsamics ... in home-made ice cream!Vinegar-flavored ice creams are currently a flourishing fad in parts of Europe, especially in Spain. The idea is to streak thin veins of vinegar through an otherwise too simpering a flavor. Balsamic works very well with strawberry, which is normally too sweet for my taste. This chocolate balsamic works in only very specific flavor contexts: with medium dark chocolate, with raspberry, with orange or blood orange (ice cream, not sorbet). Of course, you can experiment in any way you like. If you never make ice cream, or if somebody gives you a bottle of this stuff for the holiday, you're on your own. The latter was what happened to me.

column9: My favorite green tea hands down

It seems very pure and clean to me, similar to Lipton Green Tea, Mandarin Orange, Premium Pyramid Tea Bags, 20-Count Boxes (Pack of 6) (the very good flavored version that I mix with this) but a bit finer. It will become a staple for you with lemon and honey (lime, orange peel, etc.)Green tea is also an extremely healthy drink with all the special polyphenol antioxidants that it contains.  It may even prevent Alzheimers disease.  (Black tea is dried which destroys a percentage of the antioxidants.) Now we only have Senseo Douwe Egberts Colombia Blend Coffee Pods, 16-Count Packages (Pack of 4) (with some Starbuck's cocoa powder or carmel sauce) in the afternoons a couple of times a week and our nerves are perfect.

Forget the old garlic you've been getting at the supermarket.That garlic comes from Mexico or China... and is dried out and old.When you order Casa de Fruta garlic, you get moist gloves with rich garlic aroma.In fact after I went to bed, My husband made some garlic butter for some bread; so much for sneaking a snack...I could smell it in our bedroom...!http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000Z8T6ES/ref=cm_cr_rev_prod_img

When I first found that fresh garlic was available on Amazon, I was stoked.  We go through LOTS of garlic at home, to the point where we'd be buying at least six large heads of garlic every week.  Super, I thought, three pounds of garlic delivered so I'll be stocked all the time!  The price for the size of the bag was very good, I thought.When I received the garlic, however, I was very disappointed in the quality.  I began using the garlic the very night I received it, so it was not sitting in my pantry for months.  Here is what I found:  Fully half the bag was either rotten, shriveled, or sprouting.  This is indicative of garlic that has been sitting around for some time and/or improperly stored.  When stored properly, fresh garlic remains fresh, firm, and crisp for weeks... or months.  Many of the heads in the bag were completely rotten all the way through.  Some were just light for their size and the cloves were wrinkled and shriveled.  An equal number were in an advanced stage of sprouting.  Those that were suitable for use were OK, but only just that.  These were not fresh heads of garlic.Very disappointed, I contacted Casa de Fruta via email.  After my second message, they were kind enough to ship a brand new bag immediately.  To their credit, the new bag of garlic arrived very quickly.  It was definitely better than the first, but I still lost about 10 heads of garlic to rot and shriveling; that's still a lot in a 3 pound bag, and what would have been a great deal for a full bag of fresh, crisp garlic turned out to be just a real disappointment and a bad deal for a bag of average-to-poor-to-unusable garlic.  For reference, I went through the entire second bag in less than a month, and it was stored in a cool, dry environment.  It was stored properly, in other words.So, at this point I don't know what to think.  I based my original purchase on the few - and all excellent - reviews and, indeed, I would have rated the garlic at 4 stars + had the second bag contained what I was expecting from the reviews.  That was not my experience, however.  It is possible, I suppose, that I was just twice unlucky.  Still, you'd think that the company would have made certain that the second bag sent, DUE to a customer complaint of quality no less, would have been totally primo.  I've got to go with the odds on this one then, and take my garlic business elsewhere.One final note:  Had it not been for courteous and timely response from the vendor, I would have rated this product at one star rather than two based on the quality.
Be prepared to use a lot of garlic; it's a large bag.  Mine came quickly, well-packed, delivered by the P.O.  It's very fresh, crisp and juicy. I will definitely buy it again.
love this garlic,  has a great flavor, and is much better than any garlic I've got from a grocery.

column10: I received these today, alot earlier than expected which was a good thing.The bottle is large with about 1/3 of it used for vitamins.It DOES have a child safety lid on it where you have to push down and then turn for it to open. First, understand I am a complete coffee fanatic...I even have several coffee plants growing in my home. I love a good cup of Jamaican Blue Mountain - I've actually visited the island and many of the plantations - and I'm willing to pay the high price for the best beans in the world. While these are okay, they aren't exactly the cream of the crop.Still, I want to start by complimenting the shipper. They arrived quickly, and if I'm to believe the "Roasted On" date on the package, they were roasted the day before I received them. The packaging was also top notch and my beans arrived in great condition.But that's about the end of the positives. For one thing, I always expect JBM to be somewhat large beans, uniformly dark and with a slightly glossy or oily appearance. The best tend to look almost "pampered". These beans weren't that...they looked like the small leftovers at the bottom of the barrel. The color was rather pale for JBM, and many of the individual beans were cracked and broken. I have to say, the beans just seemed unappealing in terms of appearance, and I've never seen that before from anything claiming to be pure JBM coffee.As for the taste, I'd rate it fair to good overall, but only fair compared to better brands of Jamaican Blue Mountain. The taste was very mild and again, somewhat stale tasting, and with an unusual almost fruity taste I haven't experienced before from JBM coffees. Perhaps this vendor doesn't sell much JBM, and so the remnants sit in their facility for many months longer than optimum, or possibly there were other varieties accidentally mixed in.To be clear, I wouldn't say they were terrible beans - certainly better than the JBM "blends" you see advertised, or anything you'll find at the local Starbucks. They're just not up to the standards I expect for a really fine Jamaican Blue Mountain coffee, especially considering they aren't exactly a bargain price.

column9: Gluten Free and SCD, yes, but NOT My Top Pick
column10: While these arrived fresh, freshness isn't the only hallmark of a quality product.  You can get the same results with a good food processor (i.e. a Kitchen Aid). This is NOT a fine, even grind.  If I sift the product, I find a lot of chunks.  I want a fine EVEN grind when using nut meal/flour (the terms are used interchangeably in the industry) as the main or only flour in my baked goods.Since this brand is easy to find in many supermarkets, I do recommend it for some uses.  It's good for folks who don't do mail order, those non-GF cooks looking to lower the carb count of their bread coatings, and those looking for an easy GF or a no-carb "breading" option, but only when a coarse coating is suitable. For instance I like fine coatings if I'm going to "pan fry" a white/light flesh fish fillet.When used as the main or only flour for baking, the batter will look lumpy and the finished product will taste a bit gritty. It won't perform well in some recipes because the chunkier nature of the grind will affect the way the batter handles moisture, which could result in a dense rather than light texture.  It could also yield products that fall severely upon cooling.In order words, disappointing outcomes might not be the recipe or your culinary technique, it could be your choice in ingredients!

I USE THIS PRODUCT TO BAKE COOKIES FOR MY HUSBAND.  HE HAS TO HAVE LOW SUGARS AND ALMOND MEAL FLOUR IS THE BEST FOR DIABETIC BAKING.  IT TAKES TIME TO WORK WITH IT BECAUSE OF THE CONSISTENCY, BUT THE FLAVOR IS GREAT.  THE PACKAGING KEEPS IT FRESH.  THIS IS THE SECOND BATCH I HAVE PURCHASED FROM BOB'S RED MILL.  I WILL DEFINITELY BUY FROM THEM AGAIN AND I HAVE RECOMMENDED BOB'S RED MILL TO SEVERAL OF MY FRIENDS WHO BAKE AS WELL.  THANK YOU.  C. CIACCIO

column9: Use it in all my Paleo recipes
column10: I've always been a fan of Bob's Red Mill flour ever since I've been cooking.  About six months ago, I switched to a "paleo" gluten-free (and mostly grain free) diet, and as such, I needed something to fill in the gaps where I historically would've been using wheat flour.  Along with Bob's coconut flour, I use this almond flour in many of my recipes.  Great stuff, constant quality, and super easy to order using subscribe and save!

I've started using this almond flour to make GAPS-friendly recipes, since grains are prohibited on the GAPS diet.I tried to use it to make cookie dough, and it didn't go so well because it completely changed the flavor and texture.  Also, I think this flour makes the resulting food heavier...which makes sense, anyway.  The gritty texture makes cookie dough less appealing to me.In other recipes, though, this works totally fine.  For instance, I made banana bread with this almond flour and it is still kind of heavy, but it tastes great.  I haven't tried it yet, but I suspect this flour would substitute especially well in crusts, instead of a graham cracker crust.Overall, this almond flour is not wheat flour--it tastes different, the texture is different, and it behaves a little different in recipes...so if you're just coming away from wheat flour, it isn't the same.  However, it is a decent substitute in many recipes, and I plan to continue using it.

column9: I love this product and the company
column10: I use several of their products and the only complaint was with the pizza mix and only because it makes a lot more dough than I was expecting.Anyway I swear by this product and the company.  I use it to make reduced gluten or no gluten desserts.  I make a killer almond cookie with this and when I use stevia instead of sugar I get people who can't believe they are eating healthier.  If I had to change something it would be to reduce the price but that is the nature of it it comes from almonds and not wheat.I recommend it to my friends and family.  I'm  getting ready to buy some more right after I finish this.

column9: Great Almond Flour for my cooking!
column10: Being on a grain free diet is hard, but being able to cook with almond flour makes it easier. I make my breakfast muffins and biscuits with this. Excellent product! Recommended!

I love this product!  I have deleted all processed flours and grains in my lifestyle.  I love this almond flour because it adds a great nutty flavor to all my baked goods and the density of it keeps me fuller for a longer period time than regular flours would.  No guilt feeling here when you use this flour!

I have tried other brands of Almond Flour, Bob's Red Mill Almond Flour is by far the best. I use this flour to make these low-carb, delicious blueberry muffins. Not just for those following a low-carb life-style, anyone who insist on great flavor.

I have found this almond flour to be the best for making gluten free treats. Last night I made pizza crust with almond flour and it went over quite nicely. Zucchini bread and banana bread made with almond flour are almost better than with wheat flour and it makes a nice coating on eggplant for parmigiana. This is an excellent product and Amazon has it for a very competitive price.

This almond flour has been my saving grace! I am on a very strict diet and this is the only flour I can have. Yes, its a little expensive, but its worth it. Its healthy and I have made the best muffins, cookies, breads and pancakes with it. I now have my husband and kids loving all my new goodies as well!!!
Love this stuff!  Buy it and bake with it.  Buy the George Stella cookbooks (low carb) for the best recipes using Almond meal.

Replacing half the flour in a basic muffin mix with these finely ground almonds is a great way to add flavor and nutrition while reducing startchy carbs. My signature muffin uses these almonds, a splash of almond extract, real white chocolate and raspberries. For a low carb version, I use poppyseed and these almonds replacing half the flour while sweetening the recipe with Splenda. Bob's Red Mill Almond Meal/Flour is also an incredible addition to Belgian waffles. The flavor marries well with pure maple syrup harvested near our inn, the Anton-Walsh House Bed & Breakfast Inn of Hurley, Wisconsin (just two blocks from the boarder with Ironwood, Michigan).Bob's Red Mill Almond Meal/Flour, 16-Ounce Packages (Pack of 4)

Am I using the same flour as everyone else? This stuff was a pain. The texture wasn't flourlike at all, it had huge clumps and the almond flour cookies I made (with an almond flour recipe) were HORRIBLE - grainy to the point that they would not even stay in a cookie shape, no matter how careful I was. Investigated after this and apparently Bob's Red Mill is known for this. I haven't really had issues with their other flours I've used (I'm on a gluten free diet like many people writing reviews for BRM products) so I think maybe they just don't grind the almonds fine enough? Not sure what exactly the issue is, but it is honestly unusable in recipes relying on lots of almond flour. Now I have 3 bags of it left and just mix a little in with other GF things I'm baking for a bit of added nutrition. If there's not too much in the flour mix, it doesn't affect the texture badly enough to ruin it, but you can still feel it a little. Blech. Who wants to buy a flour you have to grind fine yourself? I don't own a food processor, so it's not even an option for me. Might as well just make it myself at this price.

column9: If You Haven't Tried Almond Meal in Your Baked Goods . . .
column10: . . . you are missing out on a true baker's secret--magically moister, richer baked goodies. Plus, you'll be adding protein. Almond meal works great in bread machine breads. I use 1/2 cup as a substitute for the same amount of wheat flour.The downside is this stuff is pricey. NOW Vitamins has it for less, though Bob's is gourmet and elegant in the simplicity with which he crafts his foods. Trader Joe's used to carry almond meal but hasn't lately, at least at our local store.Wherever you purchase it, do give almond meal/flour a try. I think it's a bakers blessing and good for all.
This same product was almost $13 for a 16 oz. Bag.  This was less than $8  with no shipping with subscription.  Well worth it.

column9: Great product for low carb baking purchased at Amazon!
column10: I have used this product for the past year to bake low carb muffins and cakes. I also made pancakes with this product and they were very good. This product is very helpful to people like me who have diabetes and wish to keep their carbs low and avoid processed flours.

I purchased the almond flour with the intentions of making low carb pancakes, brownies and muffins. I also discovered it to be a great cheesecake crust alternative for those who are on a low carb diet. You mix the almond flour with your favorite sugar substitude (Splenda, Stevia or Truvia etc..), Ground cinnamon and butter (optional for flavor and moldable crust) and you have a very tasty graham cracker type of crust. I used about 1/2 cup of Almond flour which is equivalent to 8g Carbs 10g protien for the whole cheesecake pie crust. The price for the almond flour is not Cheap (about $10 per lb) when  compared  to other so-called low carb flour options such as those that are made out of flaxseed, coconut and wheat. I studied my options before buying and found the almond flour to be the one with the least carbs per serving.
My bf found out he had a gluten allergy and what do you know - gluten is in all his favorite foods. After a lot of research, I found this item and we both actually LOVE it!!

column9: Great product, fair price, Lightening fast delivery
column10: I love Bob's Red Mill products and my pantry is always stocked with their almond flour. This shipment came incredibly fast (less than 24 hours after I placed the order!!). It was very fresh and at a great price.

I love to cook and try new foods.  I have been trying to avoid wheat for dietary reasons.  I find the Almond meal to be a nice addition to my gluten free flours in baked goods and savory dishes.  It adds a nice texture and richness.
This flour is very fresh tasting and consistent in quality.  When I order anything from Bob's Red Mill, I know I am getting the best available product.

column4: The little things in life make all the difference
column10: Recently, I have decided to change my diet to minimize my gluten intake. This meant drastically changing the way I eat, which also meant attempting to eat gluten-free bread - which sometimes has a very distinct (sometimes, not so pleasant) texture.This almond flour has allowed me to enjoy baked goods again, while staying gluten free. Yay!The last 2 times I went grocery shopping, this product was all sold out - thanks to amazon, I can still obtain it. :)

This is really good stuff.  I recently decided to start using almond flour in place of regular flour and this tastes great.  It's a little heavier but has a buttery taste that I prefer to regular flour.  I recommend.

column9: Bob's Red Mill is the best!
column10: BRM Almond Flour is always the best and top of my list.  It is wonderful in many dishes and buying it in bulk on Amazon makes it at least $2 cheaper per bag...which adds up to a lot.  A great buy!

I use this for making marzipan (almond paste) which is so expensive to buy ready made. It is very easy to make. Instead of powdered sugar I use Xylitol which is a natural sweetener that tastes like sugar, but is a lot better for you, expecially if you're diabetic. You can buy it in powdered form under 'Jarrow Formulas Xyli-Pure Xylitol Powder, 16 oz', or a 5 lb bag of non powdered Xylitol (it comes in smaller amounts too).I recently found out on the Internet that if you have a Vita Mix blender (which I have), you can make your own powdered sugar from Xylitol to make marzipan. I've done it twice and it tasted exactly the same as marzipan made with ordinary powdered sugar. It is more expensive, but worth it if you are thinking about your health and weight!Xlear Xylosweet Bag, 5-PoundThe price of this Almond Meal/Flour is very good, I saw it in my local Richard's Whole Food Store for almost $11 a packet, that's without tax. If you subscribe, they send you 4 pks for $30.60, no tax and free shipping and have it delivered whenever you like by managing your subscriptions, or even cancel it if you wish. I've found that it keeps a very long time. You can use it for lots of recipes, like cakes and pastry, it's delicious and a bargain.

column9: Consistently high quality. Always fresh & flavorful.
column10: I've had this almond meal on auto-delivery for quite some time and I've always been pleased with the quality. We use it in baked goods, breading, breakfast cereal, etc.  I thought I'd save some money and grind my own once, but the mess and hassle definitely weren't worth the modest cost savings.  Now I always make sure I have a couple of bags on hand.

BRM 'gluten free' items still contain some sort of gluten cross contamination.  We started SCD/GAPS to deal with lingering health problems caused by eating a regular GF diet for our Celiacs.  I bought 2 different brands of almond flour, one made specifically for and by SCD and BRM.  We used up the other brand and started using the BRM and guess what?  ALL symptoms of Celiac started coming back!!  Doing an Internet search I did find out that many Celiac's not only react badly to BRM almond flour, but to many other of BRM GF items too.  Before SCD, we had stopped using any BRM GF baking products because we always got 'gluten sick ' from them.  We will NEVER use another  GF flour from BRM again because their food safety is just not strict enough.  I did get a prompt refund from BRM for the $125 I spent on the 25lb box of almond flour though.

ground almonds give many desserts that special something and because this ingredient is so precious, I don't dare to skimp fresh egg whites (15 to 30 cents per egg these days) with powdered egg whites.I found good recipes using almond flour in Nigella Lawson's How to be a Domestic Goddess and Marcella Hazan's Essentials of Italian Cooking.For the quasi petit fours Italian cookie, almond paste is required:Almond PasteRecipe #158696 ratingsMaking almond paste is so simple and to me it tastes fresher than any you can buyby Bergy1nine inch cake frosting click to change U.S./Metric measurement system or number of servingstime to make 15 min 15 min prepChange to: nine inch cake frosting US Metric8  ounces almonds, blanched and very finely ground (grind them twice)8  ounces icing sugar1  egg white  1. Grind your almonds.  2. In the second grinding add the sugar.  3. Gradually add your egg white working the mixture vigorously.  4. Use dough hook in mixer or knead on a pastry board.  5. The mixture should be firm& smooth when ready.  Financiers:1/3 cup (5 tablespoons) (85 grams) beurre noisette (will need 1/2 cup (113 grams) unsalted butter)1/4 cup (35 grams) all purpose flour1/2 cup (50 grams) almond flour (meal) or ground blanched almonds3/4 cup (90 grams) confectioners' (powdered or icing) sugar1/8 teaspoon salt3 large egg whites, lightly beaten1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extractFresh berries (optional)

I noticed no enhancement of flavor from substituting almond flour for some of the regular flour.  So many recipes call for grinding almonds that I am grateful to have this on hand but I looked apprehensively through the flour at the brown bits to see if they were bugs.  This product is expensive and requires storage in the refrigerator.

column9: 5/5 if you know what you to expect.
column10: Obviously, it's not real* wasabi. It's still hot, pale green, and taste good.The ingredients on the can have wasabi listed but it's last so obviously it's minimal at best.Haven't made sushi but I do make wasabi wings and it works great.Goes great with Mexican too so... whatever.
My dog loves her Tiny Tidbits Treats, we keep one in the car and one in the house for her.
This is the best natural canned dog food I've found that still has added vitamins and minerals. The dogs savor it!

column9: Perfect cold drink for a hot day...
column10: Yamamotoyama Iced Green Tea is great for a quick glass of iced tea.  You don't have to go through the hassle of making a whole pitcher, you can just make one glass at a time.  Very convenient.  Here's how I do it: I keep a bunch of glasses (actually beer mugs) in the freezer and some purified water in the refrigerator.  So, all I have to do is grab a frosty mug, pour in the powdered Yamamotoyama Green Tea powder from its individual packet (there are 20 in a box) and add cold water from the frig.  Stir and drink.  Ahhhhh!  Refreshing!

Price is wayyyyyy above retail!!! I love DRY sodas.  However, I think that you should probably be aware that you can buy these sodas from drysoda.com in the same quantity for $32 right now, and that isn't on sale!  There is also a place on the site to see if someone carries it in your area.  I was just a few clicks away from purchasing this here, and decided to do a quick check on the website which is where I will buy it until the price is equal here.  Just to be clear, if it was just the soda I would give it 5-stars, but because the price is essentially doubled, I am driving the point home that the pricing is outrageous and hopefully giving it 1-star will get people to read this.

Tongo Coconut Water, Tahitian Lime, 16-Ounce (Pack of 12)I have a house in Palm Desert where the temperature gets as high as 105 in the summer and I thought I would give this stuff a try since I was drinking so much gatorade.  I had tried coconut water before, but I never really liked the taste.  I heard good things about this brand so I am really happy to say that this stuff is DELICIOUS!!I love the flavor and I have to say it taste even better than gatorade.  What makes that impressive is that it has only natural ingredients and is naturally low in calories.I have been drinking one of these in the morning before I go outdoors, then while I work in the hot sun I down a few more.  I used to get headaches in the heat, but this stuff has cured those and I feel great all day long.  I also had my son try this during his soccer game and I could tell he had a lot more energy late in the game.Get some of this stuff.  You won't be sorry.  I am going to try the other flavors as well.

I like hot things and usually when items boast being hot, they're usually somewhere in the medium range. I have to say that this one is pretty hot for not being a specialty product meant to raise eyebrows. Flavor is pretty good; the meat in this brand (general Western's meat flavor not flavor type) is on the tangy side and texture more soft compared to Tillamook and other more traditional beef sticks, but it doesn't seem greasy. The sticks are also smaller which is OK with me. The casing may be "natural", but I'd say manufactured and not intestine which I tend to prefer.Overall, not my favorite stick or flavor, but the quality is good, price is fair, they warn that cajun is their "spiciest", and everyone has differing tastes; that's not their fault, so I they still get 5 from me. By the way, I followed with a purchase of the peppered bacon which I like better.
this is a very good cajun spice meat stick! Not so hot you don't enjoy the spice, but hot enough to tingle your ears!

I have found an A class beef stick that is not greasy and overly salty which is pretty hard with a beef stick. This does have a bite to it and I preferred the regular better but this is a close second.A good snack when you are out and about and don't have time to stop and eat. Toss a couple in my purse and I am good to go.Good quality, I don't feel like I am eating grinder trimmings.

Note: The amazon picture shows a box of "Senna Sunrise", but my box said "Laxatea" on it.I tried this tea for the first time last night, and if I could use one word to describe it - it would be lemony. It's not a terrible tasting tea, but it's not very appetizing, either. It's definitely drinkable. I imagine it would be a little more palatable to add sugar to it, but I'm not a fan of sweetening teas and prefer to drink them straight. It had some laxative effects by morning, but nothing too overpowering. This is definitely a very mild tea.

I am always looking for new salsa's to try just to eat or cook with and this one was a perfect blend of sweet and spicy.  The texture of the chunks of mango mixed with the salsa flavor and hint of lime is a great combo!

This particular product, for some reason, is not terribly easy to find, i.e., I never see it in craft stores.  So I was pleased to come across it.  It arrived in good condition, and with instructions for its care.  It's absolutely beautiful in arrangements, and I plan to purchase more from this vendor.

If i could give these preserves 0 stars I would.  I bought three jars of different kinds; blueberry, fig and raspberry.  They all tasted like variations of prune and nothing like the flavors they purported to be.  I threw them all away.

I love Diet Vernors and have been drinking it from cans and 2 liter plastic bottles for years. I assumed (bad assumption on my part) that like glass bottled Diet Coke, Diet Vernors in a glass bottle would be outstanding. Well, it isn't. I did a side by side comparison, and the longneck Diet Vernors, compared to a can of Diet Vernors, tasted flat and considerably less sweet. I'm guessing it's old (the date is in "code"), but I would hope Amazon isn't selling out of date products.

Tried one this morning, and I thought it was delightful!  Very festive and just perfect for cold weather.  The coffee flavor is not very strong, but the mint chocolate flavors were quite good.  I am not usually a mocha drinker, but I would recommend this one.  Also, you can find it for about half the money other places.
This peppermint mocha by Tassimo is excellent.  It is very flavorful and perfect for the holidays. Definitely one of their better products and a nice change from a regular latte or coffe drink.
Unless I'm reading something wrong on here than this product can be purchased for a significantly cheaper price by ordering directly from tassimo.com
This is a fall/winter favorite of mine!  I love making this in my Tassimo.  It's super easy to make and always tastes delicious!

column9: Pretty good, little bit of an aftertaste
column10: I'm not usually a big peppermint fan, but am a lover of the peppermint mochas that starbucks has seasonally. However, since the calories in those are so high, I got these to cut down on how many trips I made to the coffee shop - and on the cost.  Pretty darn good, and definitely much lower in calories, sugar, and fat in comparison to the originals. Still not as good as the original, but it helps cut the craving down :)  Good cost cutter, option, too, as long as you buy them either direct from the Tassimo company online, or from a place like BB&B (bed, bath...). The price here, if for only 1 package is ridiculous. Twentyfive? Ten is more of the standard pricing.  I believe BBB offers free ship online for single serve coffees like this, too.  Tassimo often does sales and always does free ship over 50 buckaroos.  If you sign up for emails from Tassimo, they often send out deals and sales on their stuff, too.There were a couple of cons, though. One is that they only offer the Peppermint Mocha seasonally, so that may be part of the high cost here on amazon right now.  The second downside is that there was a bit of a chemically aftertaste.  Nothing horrible, but definitely noticeable.

Five stars for Amazon; fast delivery, great packing, etc.  Standard Amazon service...The product itself... well, I really wanted to like this.  I really did.  But it's the same bitter coffee that the Tassimo came out with two years ago.  I had put my machine up in the closet for two years, hoping that maybe the coffees would taste better when I pulled it back down.  Nope.  The syrup is good, but the coffee itself is extremely bitter and it tastes burned -- even more burned than the 'green mermaid' coffee.  My machine goes back up on the closet shelf for another year... the concept is awesome, the machine is neat, but when the drinks taste like burned coffee beans, I just won't use it.I'm not giving up on you yet, Tassimo... but the K-Cups at work sure do taste a lot better than the stuff coming out of the Tassimo...

I was really excited for Tassimo to get a mocha line of coffees.  I love chocolate mixed with peppermint and had really high hopes for this blend.  It tasted like Gas-X mixed with coffee, and just like Gas-X it stayed with you the rest of the day . . . Not too festive for a holiday coffee.  I must say the regular mocha is delightful!  Note:  This is WAY cheaper on Tassimo.com, thus I don't feel so guilty throwing it out.

This is the third flavor that I've tried out in my Tassimo and I had high hopes for it since I REALLY enjoyed the regular Gevalia Mocha.  I was expecting more of an "Andes Candy" flavor, but unfortunately, the peppermint flavor here is a little too over the top/bitey and the chocolate is somewhat toned down/non-existent.  I might do some more experimenting with this though, since I have 7 more servings left.  I'll probably try something along the lines of brewing a Suchard Hot Chocolate disc in conjunction with the Peppermint Chocolate and espresso discs that comprise this flavor, in hopes that might take some of the edge off of the excessive peppermint.I am glad that Kraft is putting out seasonal flavors and want to support that endeavor, but I probably wouldn't buy this one again.  If you do like peppermint, you might want to give this a shot.

This is the worst tasting stuff I've ever experienced in a T-Disc.  It literally tastes like coffee flavored medicine.  It even leaves a bad medicine like  aftertaste in your mouth.  Very disappointed.  Won't ever buy again nor can I recommend it.

All dog owners have little tricks to train their dogs to go out and relieve themsevles , # 1 you get a cookie : # 2 you get BEGGIN' STRIP , the bacon for dogs .  As the years trot by and your dog is smart , the habit of cookie and Beggin strips don't die.
My dogs didn't care for these too much. They tend to get hard, and become very chewy, and they smell funny, like very artificial. Even my dogs turned their noses up.

i think i've tried all teeccino flavors and except for the chai one i pretty much LOVE them all.  the maya caffe doesnt taste like coffee but it has its own charm and it did help me to quit coffee. it has the same color and thickness like dark coffee and it gives the same warming feeling that coffee does. i add a little stevia and a little coconut cream...yum. i think the vanilla nut and chocolate mint and almond amaretto are a tiny bit better. overall its way more dramatic than tea :) and its a great way to start the day without the adrenals-exhausting-coffee-stress. also i prefer to use the  coffee drip machine over the french press. overall highly recommended :)

column9: Seller advertising product they don't have stocked.
column10: *Haven't gotten to try Teeccino* Placed order March 30th. Estimated to arrive April 5th-8th. Amazon emailed me April 6th that the seller (evitamins) had not notified them of shipping. Contacted seller. Seller stated item was out of stock and would be shipped when stock was replenished. Disappointed that seller wouldn't just say "Out of Stock" on Amazon. Don't know how long I'll be waiting for my order now. Boo. :(

We have had our youngest Pug on Earthborn since we got him (10 weeks.) We recently switched him to this to get him off the puppy food (which we recommend as well). We've always been very happy with Earthborn products. Our Pugs coats are so soft and I know it's because of this food. Our older Pug before was on a different brand and we recently put him on this now too and his coat transformed! :) The only reason I give this food 4 stars is because it gives our dogs HORRIBLE gas. Pugs are gaseous anyways, but this makes it sometimes seems lethal. We may be switching to another flavor of Earthborn because of this, but either way we are sticking with Earthborn!*update* after a couple weeks of daily stink episodes with the Pugs they have calmed down a lot and I feel as if the food is no longer effecting them in that way :) We did give them half their old food/half new food for most of that time so maybe that played a role too, so in other words... Earthborn is the best! I feel confident they are getting what they need in high quality and it shows!

Since we first got our dog, a Siberian Husky named River, she always have reactions to everything. She first had a reaction to the chicken in the puppy food. Salmon was good for a while but only a certain kind. We've always had her on Blue Buffalo and our other dogs as well but it was causing too many issues. We found this brand and slowly introduced it into her bland diet per the vet's instructions and no problems yet! She only poops about twice a day & our other 2 dogs (corgis) are about to be switched to it since they poop 4-5 times a day! On the plus side as well that it's cheaper than Blue Buffalo!

column9: Dog likes, what's not to like?
column10: My Westie was allergic when we first got her from OK Westie REscue.  She has always been on some fish type food, and she continues to do well on this.  No problems with it.  It is really terrific to buy and have it shipped to the house.

column9: Great holistic food if your dod can't have CHICKEN
column10: We adopted our 1.5 year old dog- Lady Pippy Waffles - from the local Humane Society last June 2010. We were told by lots of friends that WE HAVE TO find a holistic dog food because the dogs poops less, and its more solid- sorry for the details! When we first brought Lady home, she was on Science Diet. She had constant diarrhea. I finally did some research and learned that dogs can have a allergy to chicken- which caused the pooping problem- ugh. So we initially put her on another brand- which was great too, but about $15 more a bag. We have found that for the money- EARTHBORN was a great choice for Lady!  Be aware that when you open this bag of food, you will smell nothing but fish- but our dog loves, loves, LOVES IT!  Plus she only poops once a day, and has a gorgeous coat- (just not gorgeous when its all over my couch)!  Thanks!!!

I was super excited about receiving my gluten free communion crackers. Let me tell you. These do not taste like Jesus at all!! Not only that, but I ate these after molesting some alter boys this morning and I did not feel any better. I think when removing the gluten, they accidentally removed the Christ! 1/10 - would not buy again :(
It is difficult to say each one is the best, so that is why I always buy the combo:green and black olive paste.Just one word: YUUUUUUUUUUM!
This is the best Black Olive Paste I ever had.  It is thick and rich with flavor.  This is the only brand I buy!!

This is incredibly delicious and a break from tomato or cream based sauces. It's great on pasta, gnocchi, even vegetables or bread. I'm not much of a cook but all you need to do is heat something and put this on top and it tastes incredible. Very fresh tasting too, like it was just made. I'll order from this company again.

The 4.5 oz gel paste goes a LONG way! Colour does not dilute like water-based food colouring, and the sheen is not lost in any large amount of fondant. The gel paste stays true to colour and is very vibrant! Love Americolor!
this stuff is great - the health food store near my house sells out of it in less than a day - it is at the lydia's lovin foods level of goodness

Like others on here, I got my first bag of Lean Treats for our Shih Tzu, at the veterinarian and he loved them. He knows them as his "treats."  The bag says it is only available from veterinarians, but as I suspected everything is available on Amazon and at less than the $4 a bag the vet charges. A rattle of the bag gets him to come in the house when he is being stubborn.  He'll do anything for them.  I actually break them in half so I can give him a "treat" more often.  But these are relatively good for him....that is why they are "lean" treats.  I think it is amazing how he loves them, and clearly other dogs do too.  You can't go wrong giving your dog these.
lean treats were given to us by our vet. have used them scince & our dog really like them. would recommend !!

column9: Lean Treats are my dogs favorites!!
column10: I got a bag of Lean Treats for my dog at his last visit to his Vet and he loved them. He was hooked. The bag said available only from Veterinarians, not so, I found them on Amazon. I bought more and my dog is in gluttony heaven now. He actually shakes all over when I pick up the bag to give him one. Giving him his pills is no problem now since the treats are soft and a pill can be pushed into it and it's down his throat before he can taste his meds.
My dog absolutely loves these.  I don't have to feel guilty giving her one because they are low in calories.  I would buy these again.

column9: Needs more specific information in the description
column10: I try to buy organic products whenever possible; so I decided to try this. I usually do not use milk quickly enough to justify buying a gallon of fresh milk; so this sounded good. I cannot find it in any of the stores in my area and Amazon is easy to deal with so this seemed like a good choice. Organic Valley should be a bit more forthcoming with specifics about this product; since many of us may not be familiar with it. I have used a lot of other nonfat dry milk products, but this is quite different. Although the actual product description does not state that it is "non-instant", if you enlarge the picture, you can just barely read it on the front of the package. The mixing instructions on the package tell you that you can stir or shake to mix the milk, but your blender or an electric mixer are probably your best options. Stirring produces a very lumpy, undissolved mess. I called Organic Valley and spoke with a very complacent woman who informed me that she puts the dry milk and water in a jar and shakes it vigorously to mix it. She also informed me that since it is not an instant product, once it is mixed, you will need to stir or shake it again if it is not used immediately; because the mix will begin to settle. Once it is actually dissolved, the taste is wonderful: it tastes absolutely fresh.

Organic Valley Organic Nonfat Dry Milk Powder definitely sets the standard for other dry milks!  It does not have that "processed, cardboard" taste that supermarket milks have and the fact that it is organic only adds to the wholesome nature of this item.  I mainly use dry milk for baking and when I make yogurt, so a fresh taste is essential to the finished product.If you're considering purchasing dry milk, I would highly recommend that you try Organic Valley.

I do quite a bit of baking, and when a recipe calls for milk, I usually add dry milk powder to the dry ingredients and then add water for the liquid. Over the years, I've tried many different dry/instant milks. This is the best!The convenient pouch is resealable, and easy to open wide enough to insert a measuring cup. To me, that is preferable for measuring over a small pour spout. The milk powder itself is silky in texture, and dissolves quickly. It doesn't seeem to lump and clump like many do. The flavor is excellent, like all Organic Valley products.While I don't personally reconstitute dry milk for drinking by the glass, for those who do, this could be a good choice due to the ease in dissolving and the fine flavor.Because the seal is quite secure, it is also more shelf stable than most. This has earned an ongoing place in my pantry.

I add this to my kids milk for added protein and calcium.  It clumps together so you have to mix it up in a blender, but it tastes great and is worth the price to avoid hormones in non-organic milk. Sooooo much better than non-dairy creamer!  It's actual milk instead of "hydrodgenated coconut oil", also known as pure TRANS-FATS!!!  It tastes better, too!

column9: Good for baking (with a little trick)
column10: I use Organic Valley Nonfat Dry Milk Powder for baking bread regularly. However, there is one simple rule you have to follow every time you bake with it. You need to always mix it thoroughly with other dry ingredients before you mix in the wet ingredients. Otherwise, you will get little hard lumps of dry milk that will never dissolve no matter how long you work on it. The consistency of the lumps is almost like raw rice that has been soaked in water. So, regardless what you bake, just remember to mix the milk powder with the rest of the dry ingredients very well. Even a little mount of milk powder that's missed in the mixing will give you some hard lumps. Mixing it in advance with water or other wet ingredients is not a good answer either. That's what happened to me when I tried to reconstitute it to the equivalent of a cup of liquid milk when I used it for the first time (my recipe calls for liquid milk). I ended up throwing 3 tablespoon of it and started over. I can't imagine how some people can use it for drinking or in coffee without having to chew or swallow lumps all the time. I can understand it for shakes or smoothies. If you have tips of how to reconstitute it free of lump, please share it.
A wonderful organic milk powder.It mixes easily. Handy for cooking.Great for drinking too.

I also mix unsweetened dark chocolate powder with the dry milk before pouring in hot liquid (coffee).  Pouring the dry milk into hot liquid makes it clog together.  Before I realized that it would mix well if I scooped the milk in first, I ordered a little smoothie mixer and that is the best way to go, but it really is not needed as long as one remembers to put the milk in first, then stir in the hot liquid. And so on.Here's the skinny--take good water, pour in blender, plop in the powedered milk, blend for 2 seconds and enjoy!

It definitely doesn't dissolve well when you add it to hot water, and then being a non-instant product didn't help matters any.

column9: Great for coffee and strawberry Quik while camping
column10: We car camp with a tent and a bunch of coolers, so keeping food chilled is always an issue.  I am currently pregnant, and with a camping trip coming up, I was concerned about drinking the calcium I needed.  I came across this product and we gave it a try during our 5 day beach camp.  It was perfect!!  We used it as the creamer in our coffee, and I also brought a protein shaker bottle and strawberry Quik for a tasty drink that only needed water.  It was sooo nice to have this option!  It didn't need to be refrigerated, and packed very easily.My only complaint is that the powder sticks to the side of the pouch, so when you scoop the powder out, it tends to stick to your hands.  The pouch makes it easy to pack, but I will likely look for a hard sided container to store it in to make it easier to dispense.  The bag is only halfway full, too, so there's no avoiding sticking your hand in there unless you pour it out.This powdered milk is now a camping staple for us.  It tastes great, is organic, and gives us yummy beverage options.

This is unlike any dry milk I've ever used.  It's a super fine texture, so that when I add it to something it turns into glue.  I have always used dry milk in my coffee; unlike half and half it doesn't go bad, and unlike instant creamer it's not artificial.  But this stuff is terrible.  I wish it wasn't so expensive or I'd just toss the bag.

Like most people who routinely buy organic products, I'm accustomed to mark-ups in the 10% to 50% range. I usually think it's worth it to know what I'm ingesting. Thus, I would overlook the price of Organic Valley Organic Nonfat Dry Milk Powder were it not for the fact that getting the powder to dissolve in water is nearly impossible. Per the instructions on the package, I used cold (chilled) water. I tried shaking it vigorously - again, per package instructions - to no avail. "Put it in the fridge for a while so it can dissolve," I thought. Bad idea. When I took it out, the undissolved lumps of powder had formed a crust the exact consistency of Spackle on the surface of the water. "Ah, a whisk! That'll do the trick," was my next bright idea. No, the lumps of Spackle adhered to the wires of the whisk with a large mass of partially dissolved powder stuck accumulating in the center. I thought of taking a pitcher of water and milk powder to my local paint store and asking them to put it in the gadget that shakes the living heck out of paint, but that seemed like too much trouble and they might not appreciate my not buying any paint. I did get satisfactory results with an immersion blender, finally, so if you happen to have one on hand, by all means give Organic Valley Organic Nonfat Dry Milk Powder a try. By the way, if you do buy some and find a way to make it dissolve in water, please let me know. I look forward to hearing how you did it.P.S. Once it's mixed, the milk is good, but a little on the sweet side.

column4: A Research It Maven "Just the facts please"
column9: Bob's Red Mill is the BEST! But NutriCity is WORST source!
column10: Even better than Quaker or Mother's, these Bob's Red Mill Oats are the very best! They are thicker cut and you get 4 bags, but with the shipping from NutriCity this price is a Rip Off. If ordered directly from Bob's (as of this date) a four pack is $17.57 including shipping, and you get really FRESH oats from a trustworthy source - right from the mill!  Order TWO cases and save even more! Then throw them in the freezer for as long as you need, over a year is fine, and pull out fresh, tasty oats every time. (Bobsredmill site) We use oats every day so we order a LOT.Did you know that the grain we call "oats" is really the SEED of the oat plant? No wonder its so nutritious! After the inedible HULL is removed, the "groat" remains and is milled into all kinds of oats (steel cut or "Irish Oats," old fashioned rolled oats, quick oats, instant oatmeal, etc.) The great thing is that ALL the nutrition, fiber, and food value REMAINS no matter what STYLE of oats you choose!! Also, ground up oats can be substituted for up to one third of the FLOUR called for in baking recipies, so you can sneak in extra nutrition without anyone being able to tell the difference. Just put the oats, and an equal amount of the flour called for in the recipe, into a food processor and process till nearly smooth. Works great!Rolled oats is 50% soluble fiber and 50% insoluble fiber, having 8 grams of fiber per dry (uncooked) CUP! The soluble fiber floats around in your blood, reducing bad cholesterol and generally cleaning up, while the unsoluble fiber aids digestion and regularity. You just can't get a better buy in grains than OATS  - but dont use Nutricity!

column9: A Must Have for the Foodies Spice Cabinet
column10: When I first received my order of the Italian Dressing mix, I was a little wary. Here are my thoughts on the other two varieties that come with this set:*  French GardenAt first taste it seemed salter than the Italian version.  The chives not only tasted fresh but still retained their classic oval shape (meaning that they were not over-processed or ground to death).  The garlic and onions were strong, but not too.  I also picked up on the parsley and I thought I tasted a little tarragon.  I added this mix to a French style omelet (runny).  Very nice!  My fear of it being too salty was put to rest.  I next sprinkled it on some grilled eggplant and I was blown away!  It woke up the subtle flavors of the vegetable.  I will be trying this is other dishes to be sure.*  Napa GardenThis mix had a different texture than the others, probably due to the tomato powder which added a wonderful richness to the blend.  This one was not as salty as the other two.  The pepper gave it a little heat but I usually like more (which is easy to add, hard to take out). I tried this (along with some olive oil) with spinach angel-hair pasta.  That turn out to be a good choice.  The mix did not overwhelm the flavor of the pasta but added that extra kick.I highly recommend this variety pack.  All three will become staples in my spice cabinet.

column9: Brings salad up quite a few notches
column10: I have been on a diet for a while now, only eating oil and vinegar on my salads. I ordered this product thinking it would at least improve the taste a little. Well, now everyone in my family is hooked on this stuff. Even my picky husband loves it. My daughter loves to mix with olive oil and dip bread in it. All of the flavors are absolutely wonderful. You've got to give them a try.

I have been looking for a long time for a decent salad dressing. The store-bought dressings haven't done the trick (unhealthy oils, mysteriously long-named ingredients, odd to no taste, etc), the mixes we've tried haven't been much better, and I have yet to find a really terrific homemade dressing that is similar to what I can get in my favorite Italian restaurant. So, I was a bit leery when I saw these. But the price was right and so with a "sure can't hurt" attitude, we bought the Italian mix.Oh my! It is very tasty with just the right blend of spices and "zing" (not a hot and spicy zing, just an "awaken the tastebuds" zing). We all loved it and so were inspired to try the other varieties. There is no disappointment here! All 3 are simply delicious and have me wishing that, like a cow, I had more stomachs so I could eat more of the stuff ;o)  I find myself craving salads at all sorts of times and it makes a yummy marinade also.Seeing how our family recently found we need to go gluten-free, I contacted the company to ask about their GF status. The reply was that though the bottles are not yet labeled as such (they soon will be) they are most certainly gluten-free. So, one more thing we restricted diet people can have to enjoy. YAY!!It's great to be able to make up our dressings with the healthy oils we enjoy and to be able to understand every ingredient on the label. Our family appreciates that. Along with it being economical, I'd say you can't go wrong. Try them out. And if you don't like them, well, you can give them to me ;o)Bon Appetit!

I have the Italian Garden and have been using this on everything from: chicken salad, steaks, chicken & potatoes and even fish!! It is sooo awesome and works on everything....hardly any salt.....just some great flavor!! It is so "clean" and flavorful! I recommend this to EVERYone who wants to add flavor without alot of sodium and added "junk".

I had read about this on a web site for HCG because it's so hard to find ingredients for a salad dressing w/o sugars added. My husband usually uses packaged dry mix and really liked it instead of his regular mix so I can use it with or w/o oil and it tastes great!

Delicious!These are zesty and full of flavor.  They make a tasty dressing (see package for recipe) or just sprinkle on your salad and toss with oil and vinegar.  I'm enjoying my salads so much more with this.  Also delightful as a dry rub on meats.  Very favorable.  So glad I found out about them!This is a sugar and gluten free product.

I bought this dressing mix variery pack to use to add flavor to my salads while I was on a strict diet to lose weight. I like the flavors and the versatility of the mixes, as well as the fact that it has little to no calories. The containers are larger than the usual spice mixes and lasts a long time. I like these dressing mixes a lot and will buy it again!

I bought these mixes based on other reviews and I have to say it was a wise choice. I am using these dressing as spices for cooking vegetables. Last night I fried asparagus with the napa spice and the dish came out very tasty. I will probably buy them again.

I really wanted to like these dressings/marinades/rubs, but had to give upon them before I wasted a couple hundred in other ingredients trying to salvage the experiment.  Maybe they're good as rubs or marinades?  I made the various dressing mixes listed on the side of the bottles, but I didn't have the heart to put them on meat.I had two big problems:1) All of the dressing recipes are super, super, super vinegary.  Even if you cut back on the vinegar, you're still left with super, super vinegary.  If you're from South Carolina, this might be your thing.  I'm not, it isn't.2) They all smell and taste similar!  You know how every variety of Sam Adams tastes like, well... Sam Adams?  These mixes have the same issue.  If I had to guess, I'd say that "herb blend" that's the first ingredient on each bottle is the same blend - something proprietary that the makers spin off in different directions to make the different dressings.They are relatively healthy, without any scary fillers or sugar or whatnot, but Annie's, Wegman's and Brianna's make whole lines of relatively healthy dressings that actually taste good.  I'll be going back to those, or making my own herb mixes.
Thee are all so wonderful.  Sometimes I add a little oil and vinegar, sometimes if I want a creamier dressing I will use some vegenaise.  I love all the flavors and this will be our second order.

These are perfect seasoning for making your own dressing or marinades for fish or fowl.  I add a little lemon and mayo to any of them and have a nice creamy dressing.  You DO have to think outside of the box when using them, they are herbs to be used as you please you don't have to -just- follow the directions.  Get creative!  You will enjoy it!
Great ginger ale with a little ginger bite to it. The flavors of the honey and lime come through nicely, and the flavors are very clean. Highly recommended if you're a fan of ginger ale.

column9: You may not be used to the taste of real Ginger Ale
column10: Remember when they gave you Ginger Ale when you had stomach problems. I bought a bottle the other day and put it in the fridge. A friend came over and said she felt sick, I gave her a swallow and she felt better right away. I took a swig and it settled my stomach too.I hesitate to write this to make it sound like this stuff is just medicine or medicine tasting.  It taste great with a real refreshing shock of ginger flavor you just don't taste from the mainstream Ginger Ales anymore. The Honey Lime is an original and wonderful addition, I not only plan to buy more to eat with my next meal, I also plan to save some for when I feel a little upset.I think the Honey Lime Ginger Ale flavorings  will also help with a cold or a sore throat. It all taste real to me!

Every time I go on a cruise with Royal Caribbean, I, sort of, um, requisition a few extra of these tea bags to take home with me to Germany. But now I have found them on Amazon! Woot! I love this tea.
I'm not a huge tea fan but this is one of my favorites. I think the taste is very subtle and honey compliments it well. Next time I'll add some lemon slices or maybe an orange slice. Yummy!
I was first turned onto this tea on a caribbean cruise. I tried it and haven't looked back! It is delicious. I enjoy it hot and for iced tea. Both are very nice.

This is standard against which I compare all other green teas. Now if you like your breakfast green tea strong, this is not for you. This is quite light on the "green" flavor. I like the strong green tea flavor also, but for breakfast this is fine!I have this straight, with honey, or with honey and lemon. It is a perfect match with lemon and honey. I never liked honey in green tea until I tried it with this! When I want my vitamin C, I squeeze an entire lemon into this brew! It takes a little more honey, but tastes wonderful.

Lipton Green Tea, Orange Passionfruit & Jasmine flavor, can be hard to find in stores.  We were going to the one place in town that carried it, every month or so and buying every box on the shelf, and trying to hit sales.  Thanks to Amazon for helping us stock up at a good price.  This is a very pleasant way to consume green tea.  It is delicious.
Most stores I shop at didn't carry this flavor so when I purchased it here on Amazon I was in love again!

Due to the recent 30% off special for select Lipton tea here on Amazon, I have been stocking up like crazy. The Lipton Green Tea Orange Passionfruit & Jasmine is in my opinion one of the better tasting flavors from Lipton's green tea lineup. The flavor is strong but not overpowering which is good because I don't want to feel like I'm drinking a fruit juice. I am a little disappointed in the actual green tea taste because there really isn't that much to begin with. However, to counter that, I do drink green tea for health benefits and not for its taste! This tea, like most of the Liptons I buy, I always drink cold. I do like to drink a hot cup or so whenever I can after a greasy meal but cold tea is much better in my opinion.Also, this tea is very similar to the pyramid bag shaped Mandarin Orange green tea from Lipton as well.

To me, most green tea has a very strong, raw taste . . . like drinking liquid grass. But, this green tea with orange, passionfruit, and jasmine is very mild and pleasant. I prefer mine with just a little sweetener, such as honey. I'm also a coffee drinker, but when I'm feeling a bit out of sync, this green tea has a soothing, settling effect. I keep a few tea bags in my purse because I find restaurant coffee usually dissatisfying. Rather than paying $2.00 for a cup of something that I don't even enjoy, I just ask for a cup or small pot of hot or boiling water, and pluck my own tea bag in! My meal is so much more enjoyable . . . plus I save the cost of a bad tasting cup of coffee!

I have been looking all over, Amazon included, for a nice tea with Passion fruit taste.I found these in the store, and get the added benefit of Green Tea.Love the taste, much less expensive than the Paradise brand I purchased, and much better tasting than the Tazo.Now going to stock up, in case Lipton does a discontinued thing like companies tend to do.
Took mother-in-law to breakfast and had a cup of this tea. Came right home, looked on Amazon and there is was.  Love it!  Thank you Amazon
This tea changed my life, it finally helped me reduce my coffee intake.I ordered 6 packs yesterday!
This tea has a strange taste and is not enjoyable. If you are buying it because of the passionfruit flavor, look elsewhere because it is not present at all in this tea. Very cheap tasting.
Excellent tea - by far tastier than other green tea versions that I've tried. It became our absolute favorite, and when our guests try it they ask me where we purchased it.

column9: Taste good, but light on the green tea
column10: Great taste, but it seems rather light on the green tea.  I have to use a straight green tea bag along with a bag of the Orange Passion Green Tea to get the strength I'm looking for.  Good product and I  will continue to buy it, but if you like stronger green tea, be ready to supplement with a straight green tea bag.

column9: refreshing tea with a delicate flavor....
column10: I love to drink green tea after my first cup of coffee, when I want something warm but without a lot of caffeine, in addition green tea is supposed to be good for you and increase your metabolism.  I don't know if that is proven, but it couldn't hurt, right?  I have not bought flavored lipton tea before, and was surprised that they had a whole line of green teas.  This one so far is my favorite one.  It has a delicate flavor from orange, passionfruit and jasmine.  Though I normally drink this with no sweetener with honey would be lovely.  I have also used it to make iced tea, but since it brews light, I would probably add in a couple of regular lipton bags to get a darker brew and a more balanced taste for ice tea.Overall, a really nice tea for everyday.  Relaxing and tastes as good as it smells!

Been drinking this for years, and have given samples out to dozens of people, all of whom like it a lot. It smells great and tastes great.People who complain about the tea bag separating from the string are correct: the packaging quality is very poor, and surprising given how many decades Lipton has been making tea bags.The way to avoid the problem is to hold the tea bag with index finger and thumb at the point where the the tag is affixed, then gently pull the tag from the bag.  Next, when dunking the tea bag in the water, pull up on the tag gently, otherwise it will come off.  Better yet, don't dunk the bag at all. Just let it steep by itself for a couple of minutes and then remove it. Enjoy. Rinse and repeat.
They really got all the flavors right to accompany this green tea. It's slightly sweet, slightly spicy, aromatic, and just plain delicious! If you like fruit teas, I highly recommend this one!

I have been drinking this tea daily for years, and plan to continue. The orange and other flavors nicely mask the plain green-tea flavor, which otherwise tastes like river-water.Unfortunately, the strings are glued to the tea bags. Yes, I know that's hard to believe - the glue melts almost immediately upon contact with the hot water. You might be able to dunk the tea bag four or five times before it falls off, splashing hot tea onto the tablecloth.One can imagine the glee with which the Lipton executives toss actual pennies into the air, as they watch the laid-off staple plant workers shuffle off. One thing they are certainly not doing is drinking this tea.The packaging does not indicate what animal the glue is from, nor its nutritional value. Horses, cattle?

column9: Nice tea, poorly packaged- tea bags open at the top and let leaves out
column10: nice light tasting green tea.  Enjoyed it as part of a variety pack bought at my grocery store so ordered the same tea in bulk here.  However, the packaging of tea shipped by Amazon is inadequate and makes this tea nearly unusuable.  Each tea bag opens at the top when the tag/label string is pulled apart from the bag just before using the tea bag. The adhesive holding the top of the tea bags together is not strong enough to withstand even tiny, gentle pull from trying to "unstick" the tag and string from the bag.  Other than that the packaging is normal Lipton packaging (white paper outer envelope for each bag, thin cardboard box.  But this one defect is enough to make the tea unusuable (unless you like sifting it through your teeth as you drink) without resorting to self help such as personally stapling each tea bag closed after loosing the tag.  While the tea itself is ok and a nice light green tea for those who don't like the really strong kind, this is too much annoyance, I tossed these and will not reorder this brand of tea online, especially in bulk.  I am a lifelong tea drinker and have not experienced this problem with any other teas with anywhere near such frequency as I have with each box in this 6-pack of boxes of Lipton Green Tea.  The similar tea I purchased in a store had no problems.
