South Beach Living Fiber Fit Mocha Granola Bars are pretty much the best one's I've eaten in the healthy category. At least they actually taste delicious AND have fiber. However, for the vegans and vegetarians in the world out there, these Pure Bars are certainly edible and like I said, better than some I've had. For the other population that actually want a good tasting snack alternative, buy something else.

column9: He Likes It. He Likes It.
column10: After looking at the product wrapper, I expected a mass of nuts and chocolate when I ripped off the wrapper only to see a smooth, thin, sticky mass that somewhat resembles a chocolate brownie. There are no chocolate chunks to be seen, and the small bits of nuts can only be found within the pure natural chocolate almond bar which mostly consists of dates or a date puree.That being said, I actually like the taste and texture of this bar quite a bit. The chocolate flavor dominates and only the label indicates to me the predominance of date content, certainly not the taste. There is some moderate crunch to the smooth texture, and the eater's fingers will get a little sticky while eating this soft bar.The box of bars arrived at my house on a day of near 100 degree heat, a little warm but basically unharmed. The bar has 190 calories, 70 of which are from fat, so keep that in mind. Five grams of fiber and 7 grams of protein are an added bonus for these gluten free, vegan bars.

Love this product because it has a rich dark cocoa and not the standard overly sweet American chocolate most sweets have.  Its 70% protein and 5g Fiber, and is gluten free and has the U kosher symbol. 190 calories means this is not something you want to eat more than once a day as part of a whole healthy diet.Tastes like a French chocolate treat and I love how they made the dates and almonds blend into a delicious mini crunch. Not a heavy crunch but akin to a lovely moist grown up French brownie.  Will be buying these to keep on hand.

column9: I don't know what went wrong with these bars
column10: I would have loved to love these bars but I just couldn't. Everything about them sounded delicious but something was just off. I love almonds, dark chocolate, and the two together are great. Somehow these just didn't come together.

Since these are touted as a "healthy" snack, I didn't really expect them to be amazing.  Sometimes you're pleasantly surprised with items in the "healthy" and "organic" categories, but this one was kind of on the fence.  They tasted decent, but the chocolate flavor was subpar and left a weird aftertaste in my mouth.  Not bad if you're into these kinds of products, but for what it was, it's a little pricey and could use some improvement.

column9: TERRIFIC taste, wish they were smaller!
column10: I was expecting a chocolate tasting granola type of bar, and these are more like a super fudgy, soft chocolate brownie than anything. They have about twice as many calories as I allow for a snack though- 190 and I try to stick to 100. I felt like the bars were large, and could easily be halved and packaged seperately to fit with many weight loss programs. The thing I like the MOST about the bars though is the fact that they are gluten free and vegan. It is very difficult to find reasonable yummy snacks that fit in either of those catagories. It is especially hard to find gluten free baked goods that are tasty. So after I ate one, and my daughter ate one, and we liked them, my husband, who is NOT into health food at ALL, but is majorly into brownies, ate all the rest and loved them! So if they pleased him, that is saying a lot for the taste. Or perhaps I have just not baked him anything in far too long!
If gluten-free or vegan is important to you, this bar is delicious.  But it is mostly empty carbohydrates.  The bar is chewy and satisfying, but there is plenty of sugar.

column9: Gluten free, vegan and Kosher... doesn't get any cleaner.
column10: I will start off this review by stating that this product is gluten free, kosher and vegan.  For my unhealthy eat bagged and processed junk ways this little bar surprisingly hit all the right notes.  When you first open it, you will see that it is a smidgen smaller than a Snickers bar.  Yes... Yes... I do see the irony of including an unhealthy candybar in my review of a good for you alternative.  Now onto the flavor:  It is laced with crushed almonds throughout and has a very strong molasses taste. The bar is a tad sweet but in a natural way.  It isn't the same as diet products in respect to the flavor.  The chocolate almond flavor is very dark and looks like a tight moist brownie.  The smell is very reminiscent of a dark coffee.  From it's wrapper claims it is chock full of protein and a healthy alternative to all those other bars filled with preservatives and filler.  At the end of the day I not only loved the bar but so did my family.  The box was gone in 2 days.  No one else complained about the molasses flavored sweetness that would have me reaching for a drink after 3 bites.  The sweetness does satisfy a sweet tooth though!  Highly recommend to families and individuals that are looking for that healthy alternative that is PURE.. awesome find for those that have dietary restrictions.  For us I find them to be a bit steep in price considering our house of five goes through them at lightening speed.

column9: Adequate taste, serves the purpose, travels well
column10: The Pure Natural Chocolate Almond bars were average. They were dense and chewy like an undercooked brownie but with a fruity aftertaste. When I need nutrition on the go it serves the purpose quite well. I don't find myself craving them or having to hold myself back from attacking the box in the pantry however. As far carrying them around in the purse or in the backpace, they do that quite well as the dense texture keeps them in one piece and from getting banged up and broken. I don't like taking out the granola bar I packed in the morning to find it in a million pieces and having to shake the package into my mouth to eat it.I'm not sure I'll buy these in the future, but I won't have any issues finishing what I already have. They serve the purpose of a traveling snack pretty well with a middle of the road taste. I like the chocolate, not so much the fruity note. The almonds were good and a bit sparse.

I'm giving this product three stars by grading on a sort of curve. Or maybe it's more of an averaging. I hated these bars. Truly hated them. I don't think I've ever stopped eating something with chocolate in it before but I only managed to eat half of one bar.  On the other hand, the two people who tried them with me loved them. They said that the bar was moist and chewy and delicious. I agree they are moist and chewy. I think if this had been advertised as a protein bar or a healthy product I may not have had such high hopes and been disappointed so severely.  So, try them but don't think chocolate while you do. Think vitamins, think good for you...

I was surprised when eating these bars (which I did, happily), that they were much more fruity than you would have thought. I mean heck, these are chocolate almond bars, and yet they taste like dates (dates are listed as one of the first ingredients, for goodness sake!).Basically, if you like chewy, chocolatey, fruity-tasting brownie bars, you're in for a treat!

These bars are terrific for anyone who has IBD issues. My son has crohns and these are a life saver.  He is on a restricted diet, no wheat, corn, or GMO products and lots of protein.  They taste good too.  He usually eat 2 a day.  No stomach aches.  He is very active and surfs usually 3 days a week for two hours.  Lots of calories!  My other kids like them too, but all of us are used to not eating junk foods so if you are switching from Oreos, give it some time.

column9: Average Natural Bars with Stong Cooca
column10: First note that the bars themselves do not resemble what you see on the box or package -- that image is of chocolate and large almonds.  The bars themselves reminded me of no-bake cookies formed a rectangle with a deep, black color.  The almonds are pieces within the dense and surprisingly moist bar itself.While nutritionally this is good, in terms of taste the best I can say is that the cocoa is strong.  Beyond that this reminds me very much of the "natural" or "sugar free" bars and cookies that were just coming out two decades ago. This does not have that sickly sweet taste nor the unmistakable prune taste -- if I wanted prunes, I'd eat them -- but it is also not much of an improvement for two decades of development in the food industry.  Thus I could only honestly give this 3 out of 5 stars.You do however get 12 bars in a pack and compared to many granola or cereal bars out there, this is a lot for your money. My best advice is to try one before you buy an entire box.

column9: Like a Brownie without the guilt!
column10: This company makes several bars and the textures of them varies greatly. This one is like a cake brownie with a few almonds in it and it's delicious. I've got these on auto-delivery because it's a healthy snack I can use when I don't have time for a meal.

Disclaimer: A free sample of these bars were received from Amazon Vine in exchange for an honest review.The Pure Natural bars are gluten free protein snack bars. I sampled the Chocolate Almond flavor. I did not really care for the first bar but have since eaten a couple more and have raised my opinion to "okay." I don't eat protein bars generally, finding the ones that taste decent to be high in carbs or sugar or both-- if I'm going to eat something with that much carb or sugar I might as well "sin lustfully" and grab a Hershey bar.That being said, these bars are chewy with a fruity flavor. They do not taste very chocolatey, nor can you really taste, or even find, the almonds. However, they also do not have a strong bran or "dog food" taste as I find with many other protein bars.I wouldn't buy these on my own, and I'm not even sure if I will finish the package, but if you have gluten problems and you like protein bars, you may find you like these.

column9: A very healthy cereal bar from Pure!
column10: I was pretty happy with the taste of the cereal bar considering that it is so healthy and the fact that it uses natural ingredients. Most of the other cereal bars that taste good are pretty much loaded with sugar and not very good for your body. This is a great and healthy alternative when you have the afternoon snack craving at office or after you get back home.

I was really hoping the kids would take to these so I'd have a new product to add to their school lunches, but, they didn't care much for them at all.  (15, 11, and 5 years old)  The bars are dense and chewy with a few almonds tossed in. While they are supposed to be chocolate, they have a tangy, slightly sour taste that tends to be the first thing I notice.  The kids and I are gluten-sensitive, and on the box it clearly states that they are gluten free, but also that they are "produced in a facility that also processes soy, milk, egg, wheat, peanuts, sesame, tree nuts".  I'm extremely sensitive and often react to slight cross contamination, but I had no problem with these bars.  All in all, I might buy this flavor for myself as an occasional switch from my usual Larabar.

This did not taste like a chocolate bar at all. I can't describe how it tastes as I haven't encountered something like this before. I know that is is suppose to be better for you and it's all natural but honestly, I've had slim fast bars that tasted better than this. I'm glad I didn't have to pay for this as it went into the garbage.

I was looking for a less-unhealthy-than-usual breakfast or snack that I could carry with me and eat on the go or at my desk, and so I gave these a try.  I have nothing to compare them to as far as similar bars are concerned.  I am not a health fanatic - - the words "chocolate" and "almonds" appeal to me much more than any health claims.  I want the good stuff, and I want it now.  I like rich tasting foods, but dislike sweet foods.  As you've probably guessed by now, I will not be reviewing these bars based on grams of this or that or energy levels or any such, just taste.Before I ate my first Pure Naturals bar, I had no idea what to expect.  I found the dense texture a little surprising and the taste okay, nothing great but certainly not bad -- definitely not sweet.  Then the next day, I ate a bar for breakfast with a cup of tea.  After that I started craving them and have had one most mornings since then.  I find them a good alternative to other on-the-go breakfasts and very satisfying.  I really enjoy them now and would recommend that people give them a chance.I might add that I find a full bar good for a light breakfast, but a full bar is too much for an afternoon snack at my desk.  I cut them in half for a snack and save the second half for the next day.

Over the years I have eaten MANY "health" bars, fiber bars, protein bars, etc.  I usually eat a protein bar a day, and I am very used to the chalky texture and taste of protein bars and have learned to overcome them.  The Pure Natural Chocolate Almond bar is not a protein bar, but tastes almost as bad as that. Correction, it tastes, worse than a protein bar.  There is no real chocolate taste to it at all, and the protein chunks that are in it taste like these cheap almond pieces they used to shove into candy bars 30 years ago, way too small to offer any real taste.  Actually, they taste just like the nuts you get in brownies. I love almonds, but hated the taste of these. I forced myself to eat three of these bars so I could give them an accurate review, and that was extremely difficult.The selling point of Pure Bars are that they are made with natural, whole ingredients and are vegetarian and gluten-free.  As someone who is trying to avoid High Fructose Corn Syrup and added sugar, I like that, however it doesn't do me any good if I can't enjoy the product enough to consume it.  I know some reviews have claimed that these are "health bars" and that they have too much sugar, but they are not marketed as a "health bar."  Too many people confuse the ideas of "whole" and "natural" foods as "health" foods, which is entirely not the case. The idea is that these bars are for people who don't want additives and a lot of over-processing in their food, it's just unfortunately that they taste so bad.  If you're looking for a better-tasting alternative, I'd suggestion the -  Kashi Go Lean Crunchy Variety Bars (All Natural) - 24 ct. (meal Replacement Bars) or maybe the Clif Builders Bars.

I received this product through the vine program. I generally consume one or two protein bars per day, so I was excited to try ths product.  The excitement ended after the first bite.  It was dry, chalky, and not very chocolatey, not mention that I didn't detect any almonds in the bar.  It wasn't terrible, but also just wasn't very good.  If these bars were just stacked with proteins and vitamins, I might buy more. However, there are better tasting alternatives out there that have superior nutritional value.I would pass on these.

column9: Great if you love the taste of almonds and chocolate
column10: PROS- you get a generous package of 12 bars per box- very chocolatey flavor if you like chocolate- very strong almond flavor if you like almonds- very moist, chewy snack barCONS- the bar size is very small, so it's not a meal replacement; you would need to pair it with more food for an adequate meal- I personally prefer a crunchy snack or granola bar, and if you don't like a bar to have a moist, chewy texture, you might not like this barSUMMARYThis is a good value for the price. I personally dislike the strong almond flavor with the chocolate. Pecans or peanuts would be more flavorful, but if you love almonds with chocolate you might like this bar. I has a much stronger almond flavor than an Almond Joy candy bar, but without the coconut to offset it.
and has the right amount of protein to serve as an alternative meal or support to eat before or after a work-out. Taste is always an issue with protein bars but this one passes the test

column9: Didn't care of it too much
column10: I think this is one of those types of food products where you will either really like it or not care for it.I am a chocolate fan and I love chocolate and almonds, so I figured this was a natural fit for me.Upon opening the first bar it seems like any other bar of it's type. However, once that first bite was in my mouth it's evident it was not. The chocolate in these bards over powers the taste of anything else. Like I said, I'm a chocolate fan but this was just too potent of chocolate for my tastes.Since there were a dozen in the box I decided to let a few others try them. It was a mixed bag of results there too. One person took one bite and would have no more. One said they were okay with coffee. One person ate an entire bar before deeming it "not very good". The last person really liked them and said he would buy them in a store. So, basically 1 out of 5 people in my highly unscientific research liked them.I guess if you are a dark chocolate person these may be something you'll like. But if you're not stay clear of these.

I really like that these Pure Natural Bars are vegan and gluten free.  They have a good chocolate flavor and seven grams of protein.I'm currently pregnant and need to take snacks with me to keep my blood sugar steady and these work great for throwing in my purse.  They wouldn't hold up well in the car right now though with the heat we've been having.  The box that I received was a bit banged up and it was clear that some of the bars had melted a bit in transit.The only negative for me is the texture wasn't quite what I was expecting.  I thought the bars would have a candy bar type texture or maybe even a granola bar type texture but these are a bit more like a brownie bar.  I'm not crazy about the texture but overall these are a good snack to have on hand.

This is a pretty decent bar to snack on.  It has a sort of brownie-like consistency and taste.  The primary ingredient in this bar is dates which seems to be a pretty common one in the natural/vegan realm of sweats.  In turn, it has a pretty distinctive taste.  It is pretty tasty with a cocoa (not a rich chocolate) and almond flavor.  Quite moist which is nice.  My only complaint is that each bar is pretty small at 1.7 oz.  While golfing, I often eat bars like Odwalla or Cliff that are 2+ oz.On a sort of side note, it would be nice if Amazon posted the Nutritional Facts and Ingredients for all the food products they sell.

The choco/almond Pure Natural Bar is a good energy alternative for times when one can't sit down for a real meal. I work from 8am-3pm at one job then ride my bike to my second job, 3:30-8pm. These bars are perfect to toss in my bag and eat at 5 or 6pm. The taste is perfectly ok, although I wouldn't be sorry if it had an even more chocolatey flavor. It's nice and moist, which my old standby, powerbars are not... Each bar is filling and satisfies hunger pangs. I wish a single bar wasn't so calorie dense, but that's probably due to all the nutty goodness, which is what provides the sustaining energy. So as long as one doesn't eat them by twos and threes, it's probably all good.

As I unwrapped the wrapper to this bar, I was a bit surprised. The description of these bars describe them as "rich, dark cocoa with heart-healthy, crunchy almonds," and the packaging has images of almonds and chocolate. A look at the bar also reveals fruit, specifically dates.Having said that, I found the bars to be quite good. The dates added a nice touch to the chocolate and almonds, and as the bar is less than 200 calories and gluten free, one can't complain too much.  While these probably aren't the best bars in the market, they are definitely worth trying, just don't let the marketing of the bar fool you into expecting a decadent alternative to a candy bar. These bars have a healthy feel to them, which I found to be tasty.

The ingredients are simple and 100% organic, not "all natural", which means nothing. Enough chocolate and almonds and sweetness (from the dates), but doesn't taste like I'm eating a candy bar. And my body feels good afterwards, not like after eating a candy bar. Healthy and delicious!

column9: A nice healthy snack that is lacking something
column10: Pure Natural Bars Chocolate Almond is a nice snack tat's perfect for those who are into eating healthy.  Others need not apply.  I thought the bars tasted okay but they definitely are missing something.  I can't quite place it but it's pretty bland.  If you're a health food nut then you'll probably go gaga over them and find it utterly "divine".  I found them to be okay.

column9: Good, but need to change the package design
column10: I have tried most of energy bars and natural bars available in the US. And, this "Pure Natural Bars - Chocolate Almond" has one of the better taste in this category.It's not too sweet and has natural, yet complex taste.The biggest problem is the picture on the package. It gives you a wrong expectation of this bar. When I saw the photo, I expected Pure Natural Bars to be similar to my favorite Kind bars such as KIND PLUS, Cranberry Almond + Antioxidants, Gluten Free Bars (Pack of 12). While you can enjoy crunchiness of whole almonds and real chocolate to taste with Kind bars, you don't recognize individual taste of Almonds or chocolate with Pure Natural Bars. Pure Natural Bars are rather similar to Larabars such as [Larabar Fruit & Nut Food Bar, Lemon Bar, 1.8-Ounce Bars (Pack of 16), which I also quite like (not as much as Kind bars, though).As long as you know what you are getting, you'd like this bar.

At first these taste like a meal replacement bar... sort of bland and chewy. Then after the second bite, you realize that they're more like a less-sweet brownie, and you look forward to the next bite. They're not too chocolatey, which I really appreciate because I don't have too much of a sweet tooth. Like the peanut-raisin variety, I would recommend these as an afternoon snack to tide you over until dinner. And like the peanut -raisin, I'll be buying these in future.

column4: David L. Poremba "the past in review"
column10: I expected this bar to taste more chocolaty and not so bitter, although I sometimes indulge in high percentage dark chocolate. This bar is dense, like a brownie but is definately for the healthy, vegan chocolate lovers.

column9: Mealy But Good [Upgraded to Five Stars]
column10: The taste leaves nothing to be desired although the chocolate could be richer so why am I not giving this a full five stars? I didn't expect the soft `mealiness' of that first bite, it's like eating a very dense oatmeal when I'd expected a crunchier texture.Understand that this doesn't take away from the experience though and in the one place where it counts, cutting down on hunger and getting you to your next meal, it fits the bill.Recommended.[Update: I have to upgrade this to five stars. I've just finished the last bar in the box and I have to say it's delicious, filling, and even the mealiness I pointed out before simply becomes unnoticeable. One of the things that's changed my mind is how much my 20-month-old son loves eating this bar. It contains nothing that'll cause him grief and being as picky an eater as he is, the fact he munches down entire bars says something for the quality and taste of the Pure bars. Upgraded to Five Stars.]

The taste and texture of these bars vaguely remind me of brownies I've gotten out of vending machines in times past.Taste: Vaguely fruity, mainly sweetness with dates and hints of cherry (this comes from the almonds) and yes, chocolate.  The chocolate flavor is quite weak for a "chocolate" bar.Texture: About what you'd expect from a "health" bar; it's a solid mass with little identifiable texture.  It's about what I'd expect a baked good to be like if you left out the leavening.Appearance: Errr... it's a good thing this bar isn't in a clear package, as nobody would buy it.  The choice of dutched coccoa (which is quite dark when cooked) lends an appearance that suggests a huge amount of chocolate flavor that this bar simply does not provide.  It also makes the bar look... how do I put this... like it has already been eaten and "processed" by your digestive system.  To be sure, it tastes quite acceptable, but if I was formulating this bar, I'd add additional standard-process chocolate, which is lighter in color, and forgo the cost benefits of the flavor-enhanced dutched cocoa (which creates a rather dark-brown product.)I suppose if you are a Celiac kosher-keeping vegan boycotting HFCS and Sugar that is not having intense chocolate cravings this bar might be for you.  Otherwise, get your chocolate fix elsewhere.

I leave mine in the fridge. It's perfect for the summer.It is a bit soft and chewy on the inside without the stickiness to teeth. You could taste the almond flavor but not much. The picture doesn't really reflect the inside truthfully. The almond in reality is pretty small and not a lot.In all, it tastes really great and is NOT too sweet. It has the right amount of sweetness and thick chocolate flavor with a hint of almond.I really like it!

column9: Didn't like them, but that doesn't mean you won't
column10: I wanted to like these bars, I really did. It's nice that they're vegan, kosher and have lots of fiber, but the sad, sad thing is, I just don't like them and can't imagine myself eating them. If I had to eat them, I would. You know, if I was little and my mother made me, like parents used to make their kids swallow cod liver oil all those years ago. Well, these bars aren't that bad, but they don't taste very good, to me anyway. I see others have liked them and I suppose taste is subjective, so please take this review with a grain of salt.

If you're looking for a chocolate treat that's healthy, this bar is a great contender.  It's made of a dark chocolate and sweetened naturally with dates and organic agave nectar. I don't like plain dates, but I do like this bar. Two years ago, I learned my blood sugar was in the "diabetes" range so I've lost 30 pounds through healthy eating (1200 calories a day) of low-sugar, low-fat healthy foods and exercise and reversed the diabetes without medicine. Occasionally I want a taste of dark chocolate which is healthy for you--this bar meets that desire.I like the fact that this bar is sweetened naturally with no added sugar.  The natural sugar in this bar is 17g--one cup of milk is about 12g.  A cup of fruit juice is about 25g. So this bar is mid-range between milk and fruit juice.  A nutritionist said to think of sugar like poison for your body--your body burns sugar before it burns the fat so if you have too much fat, go light on sugar.  She recommended breakfast cereals that were under 8g of sugar, for example.  You might be satisfied with 1/2 of the bar (I was!) which would then be 8.5g of sugar and 1/2 the 190 calories or only 95 calories. I enjoyed the unusual texture for variety--and think it would be good cold, too.  You could keep some in the frig.The bar has 20% of daily fiber needs and 7g of protein.  As an alternative, I like Kashi's TLC Dark Mocha Almond Chewy Grandola Bars which are 6g of sugar and 130 calories with 1/2 the fat of these bars.  But you don't want crunchy bars all the time, so this Pure Natural Bar is a great alternative. It has a sorta brownie texture--or soft tootsie roll texture, kind of velvety. Family members sampled this bar,too, and liked it so it had wide appeal.  My Weight Watchers meeting tomorrow is going to be on snacks so I'm taking this box to the meeting to share with the group.

column9: Delicious - not too sweet - perfect chocolate taste!
column10: I am eating one of these Pure Natural Bars as I write this and I admit that aside from the occasional Lara bar, I do NOT eat any bars at all. I just don't really care for it. These were and still are delicious. They have the perfect level of sweetness, not too sweet which I couldn't tolerate and just nutty enough. I find they go excellent with a cup of Oolong tea and have been keeping me going in the afternoons. Love the taste and they seem really easy to digest to boot!

column9: Appearance is troubling, but quite good for the traveler
column10: Since airplane meals are monopoly priced with a 90% probability of nasty, these 'energy' bars have become something akin to an MRE for the coach traveler. The varieties are endless and variably convenient and satisfying. These are quite good by comparison. Far more chocolaty then most, they are a bit disturbing in appearance resulting in the 4 stars but certainly a good choice. If the child that might sit beside you were to ask "what are eating?" the answer could determine the balance of the flight because the child will have a predictable child-like perspective.

These bars are not intended to be as sweet as a Hostess snack cake. They are designed to give health-conscious folks a decent tasting snack that has more than chocolate and marshmallow in the ingredients. The flavor is not sugary-sweet, but the dark cocoa is definitely present and quite pleasing. By halfway through the bar, it's obvious that it's a health bar. That's not a bad thing for those of us into fitness. They're perfect. I eat one before a bike ride or a run and it seems to help with the 7g protien and 25g carbs.These are something I would buy even off the Vine program. I'm pretty sure I saw them at Trader Joe's, so I'm going to pick them up there. I recommend them as an additional source of protien and potassium while keeping the sugar in check.

I've tried a variety of healthy snack bars such as Clif Nectars & Larabar.  I felt this was was very tasty and filling (contains 5 grams of fiber).  I like that it also has 7 grams of protein in each bar, no gluten, natural ingredients (some organic).  These are also kosher (OU dairy) & vegan.  I like the texture of the small pieces of almond and find the dates give it a sweetness without being too overpowering.  I've used these as a quick breakfast or snack while traveling and felt energized for a while.  Highly recommend for the gym bag, eating at home, or as a quick pick-me-up on the go.Update: I finished up the box (had to hide them from others in the house I enjoyed them so much) but a little disappointed they are so pricey compared to other bars on the market.  Big difference between these and others is how much more healthy & filling these are, so it seems worth it, but wish they were a bit less per bar.

column9: You can really taste the protein
column10: Pure Natural Chocolate Almond bars take some getting used to. It is a heavy bar. Small but dense. It actually looks like a fudge bar but has more of a brownie texture. It isn't sweet but it isn't bland either but you can really taste the protein in it.The first two bars that I ate, I could not finish them. Eating half was filling enough. I wasn't sold on it from those first two bars.But by the third bar (if taken with tea), I actually started to like the bars. I had to get used to the texture mostly because the taste itself was something that I like (not overly sweet) and with the tea, it made a nice combo and it made a good snack to tide me over for dinner.After a week of eating a bar a day, I can comfortably give it 4-stars.

I love Lara Bars so I thought this would be a slam dunk for me. While I did appreciate the large chunks of almonds, the bar itself was too dense and chewy for my liking. The chocolate is also slightly bitter tasting. I had to make myself finish the whole bar. Not a winner in my book, but not the worst I've tried either. Definitely not something I'd go out of my way to purchase.

column9: Just what I was looking for.
column10: I received these Pure Naturals Bars free, as part of Amazon.com Vine program, to generate reviews for new products. I have been looking for a bar that is completely natural, no fructose, no chemicals and no fake chemical sugar sweeteners. These fit all of what I was looking for, the taste is good, the bars are a good size 1.7 ounces, and they are all natural. for vegetarians and Vegans; theses Bars are Vegan. These are definitely going to be my choice for a good carb protean Bar. They are 7 grams of protean, and have 5 grams of fiber. I Highly recommend Them.

One big complaint I have about protein bars is that most of the manufacturers want to give us something that tastes like a candy bar.  This Pure Natural Bar, Chocolate Almond is refreshing because it has a different consistency.  Sort of like a brownie, this bar has a nutty and slightly fruity flavor.  It is dense, but satisfying.  It didn't feel like a candy bar substitute, but a healthy snack.  Give it a try!

These bars are branded as "Chocolate Almond" but the first ingredient is dates. I'm not terribly fond of dates, so that was disappointing. I found the bar to be "okay" ~ I'd eat it if I were starving or needed food, but I wouldn't purchase this product.My son took one small bite and won't eat any more because they're not chocolatey enough. His mom also didn't feel they were chocolatey enough. The chocolate is more like an aftertaste than a primary flavor.I would have given these bars a 2, but because they truly are very healthy I couldn't in good conscious rate them any lower. Summary: Less dates, more chocolate.Don't believe the "Chocolate Almond" brand... think of them more like "Healthy Date Almond With A Hint Of Chocolate."

The flavor is okay for these bars.  They taste something like a chocolate brownie that isn't very sweet.It's great to see a product made from mostly healthy ingredients and not full of preservatives.I would prefer if it was sweetened with honey rather than agave and it would be healthier if the chocolate wasn't "dutched".One definite advantage, compared to many other protein bars, is that there is no chocolate coating to melt in the heat.  These are very portable and make no mess.Not a bad bar all in all.

Perhaps the best thing that I can say about the Pure Natural Bars is that they are okay, not great and certainly NOT a substitute for a brownie or treat.  It might be a healthier alternative, but you're going to sacrifice taste (the first tradeoff).  No... contrary to the packaging claim, your chocolate prayers have NOT been answered.  I like a good rich dark chocolate, and this just has a weak, bitter flavor.  It's a bad taste, it's just weak.All natural ingredients make these bars an overall safer alternative for people that must concern themselves with allergic reactions, but then the texture of them makes you think that you're eating a very dense paste (tradeoff number two).I don't mind the fact that they taste the way they do, and I'm not exactly looking for something that reminds me of bakery brownies.  But I get a little tired of healthy snack makers making claims that simply do not hold up with the first bite of their product.  It would be great if a snack bar existed that had it's own unique taste instead of trying to mimic the high calorie sinful stuff.  For example, I've tried a number of "burger substitutes"; forget them!  On the other hand, there are some fantastic "vegetable patties" that fit comfortably on a hamburger bun and provide a healthy, lower calorie alternative to the juicy, fatty hamburger that I remember so fondly.Forget trying to answer someone's chocolate prayers!  Just create a healthy, all natural, high fiber, low calorie snack bar that can be consumed and enjoyed.  Really... it shouldn't be that difficult, unless you're trying to make "substitutes" instead of "alternatives".

column9: If you like Dark Chocolate.  Brownie texture.
column10: Brownie texture with dark chocolate taste.I liked this and my wife did not.I like dark bittersweet chocolate nibbles.  I Usually buy 65% cacao.Dark chocolates are healthier than sweet.She likes sweet chocolate.  A sweet chocolate person may be disappointed.Brownie texture but does not taste as good as a brownie.  It's not a Brownie.Tastes fine for a healthy snack.  190 calories is in line for this type of 1.7 oz snack.The word delicious can't be used to describe this type of snack.  The word fine is meant as a positive.  Better than most health snacks I have tried.Very healthy ingredients.  Dates, Almonds, Organic Agave Nectar, Organic Rice, Dark Coco, Natural Flavors.  Gluten free, Vegan.There is no added sugar, nor high fructose syrup.No Trans fat .  Sat fat 1 G.A solid 4 star.

column9: Not bad for a vegan gluten free bar
column10: With a consistency like a Little Debbie Brownie and a taste like the no-Pudge brownies, these will not be for everyone. However, if you are on a restricted diet (no soy, no gluten, no dairy), these bars fit the bill. They are not overly sweet, although there are 25g of carbs in each bar. The main ingredient is dates, so that is what provides the majority of the texture. The bars soft and dense, sweetened with agave nectar with no other sugar added.  It does contain 5g of fiber and 7g of protein, but only has 10% iron and 4% calcium RDA.My biggest issue is the calorie impact: at 190 calories, I want something that has a little more flavor, especially if there is little added nutrition (these can't be used as meal replacement, just as an occasional snack). The wrapper says "Your chocolate prayers have been answered." I seriously doubt anyone eating this bar would agree with that statement.

column9: Taste Great, but Not a Health Food
column10: These bars really hit the spot: they have a good consistency, like a very thick brownie or fudge, without being overly or cloyingly sweet. The texture is just right, and rich enough to feel like a treat. The chocolate taste is pronounced (and really more of a 'dark chocolate' than any kind of milk chocolate), and the almonds - while not particularly numerous - are present, and add an extra crunch and flavour to the bar. If you're a die-hard, need-a-chocolate-bar kind of person, it's likely these won't satisfy your sweet-tooth cravings; for the rest of us, it's the right amount of sweetness.It's important to keep in mind that the bars aren't really 'health food,' though: they're not nutrient-dense enough to be a meal replacement, and likely won't fit easily into a stringent diet regimen. They're calorically dense, at 190 calories/bar: not very big, either. They'd be great to bring on a hike, long bicycle ride, or run, though, as they're compact, portable, and taste good. I wish they had more fiber (because really, these aren't very filling), but am glad they don't contain a laundry list of random chemicals/fillers, nor do the bars have any soy. The protein count is fairly good (7g), considering the Pure Natural bars aren't being sold as as a protein supplement.

column9: All Natural but Taste Only OK
column10: These bars are high in calories which is a good thing when hiking or performing some other strenuous exercise.  But they are not very high in flavor which is not such a good thing when eating them.  The bars are soft and have a brownie like texture.  The chocolate flavor is not pronounced, it is a dry cocoa flavor and texture.  Almond slivers are in the bars, there is a crunch every couple of bites, but the almond flavor is overpowered by the cocoa.  These are similar to other "health" bars in that they impart a chalky, dry texture.  No, my chocolate prayers were not answered by these bars.  The thing I liked about these is that they are not overly gooey and sweet.

column9: Should be called 'mashed up rice with chocolate and almond'
column10: Length:: 1:45 MinsDespite being called "Chocolate Almond Bars," one of the main ingredient in these bars by Pure is rice, and you can taste it -- the rice flavor overwhelms the chocolate.But these bars claim to be health food, so looks look at the nutrition facts.Each 48g bar has 190 calories with 70 calories from fat. The strikes me as a lot of calories for such a tiny bar. Let's compare it to another health food, Greek yogurt, specifically Chobani yogurt.A single 170g cup of Chobani non-fat Greek yogurt only has 140 calories, and no calories from fat. So the Pure bar has three times as many calories per gram than the yogurt. But wait, there's more!Pure touts that the bars contain 7g of protein. Compared to Chobani, it again comes up short -- the single serving of Chobani has 14g of protein (28% of your Daily Value). The Chobani also has 20% of your daily calcium value. And if you thought a benefit of the Pure bar is that it is gluten-free, so is the Chobani.I know that this review seems like it has morphed into a pitch for Chobani, but my point is to illustrate that there are healthier, lower caloric snack foods out there. And the Chobani tastes a heck of a lot better.

column9: Had a lot of Bars in my life.... these are simply THE BEST!
column10: I received these Bars as a part of the Amazon Vine Program.Here is what is GREAT about these Bars!1).  No Soy.  Thank you!  Every Bar out there has soy.  I cannot eat soy, these have no soy.2).  They taste great.  The chocolate is Cocoa.  Great for you... and they have a nice softness to them that make them a terrific mid-day snack.3).  7 Grams of Protein.  Nuf said.4).  Simple Ingredients.  The Ingredients are: Dates, Almonds, Organic Agave Nectar, Organice Rice Protein Concentrate, Cocoa (Dutched), Chia Seeds, Organic Agave fiber, Natural Flavors.  Tired of Bars filled with Junk?  Then these are for you.6).  OH, and the price?...... The price is right.  $16.98 for 12 Bars.  Do the math.  These are a really great deal..

column9: "For those of you who like this kind of thing, this is the kind of thing you will like."
column10: For those who really know nutrition, protein bars are a nightmare. Often filled with multiple sugar sources and nasty additives, protein bars run the gamut from truly healthy to downright bad for you. "Pure Naturals" Chocolate Almond Bar lands squarely in the second tier: Simple, semi-organic, some nutrition and reasonably tasty.NUTRITION: If you're looking for a lot of any one thing this ain't the bar for you. There's 7 grams of protein (albeit from organic rice protein instead of chemically extracted), which is nothing too spectacular but decent. 5 grams of fiber, again not bad. 10% of your iron and 320 mg of potassium but negligible on other nutrients. Sugars are 17 grams a bar; I've seen much worse. Chia seeds will give you a small amount of healthy fats and organic agave is the only sweetener. Downsides? The first two ingredients are not organic and they make up most of the bar. "Natural flavors" are used, never a good thing, and the cocoa is dutch processed which eliminates some antioxidant content. Other than that no real complaints. Nutrition grade: BALLERGENS: Made on shared equipment but labeled as gluten-free. No soy-derived ingredients that I could spot (watch out for those "natural flavors"). Obviously if you have a nut allergy you'll have to skip this line, but other than that the ingredient list is pretty straight-forward and clean.TASTE: This is easily the best tasting of the "Pure Naturals" series. It tastes like a gluten-free brownie, let's put it that way. Heat it up with a little coconut milk ice cream and you got a decent dessert. Not as yummy as the Zing Chocolate Coconut Bar, but better than a lot of the Larabars. Taste Grade: B/B-There you have it, hope that helps those of you desperate for a new bar that will work for your diet. Overall not bad tasting and decent ingredients. Happy snacking!FINAL GRADE: B/B-

I was pleasantly surprised by these bars.  Usually nutritional snack bars, particularly gluten-free vegan bars, are mediocre to terrible.  Pure Natural Chocolate Almond bars are delicious!  They consist primarily of dates, like chocolatey Fig Newtons.  The almonds provide a satisfying crunch.  The bars are 190 calories, 25g of carbs (unfortunately, 17g of those are sugars, which is why these bars get 4 stars instead of 5), 7g of protein, and 8g of fat (only 1g saturated).  The bars are filling as well - they could easily get you through from breakfast to lunch, or provide a good afternoon snack.  And because they're gluten-free, they won't bloat you.  If you're looking for a candy-bar-like 'nutrition' bar, look elsewhere. You won't find milk chocolate or drizzled caramel here.  But if you're looking for a delicious, much lower carb option than a Clif Bar, give these a try.

column9: Tasty for chocolate lovers, but more figgy
column10: I liked both the taste and texture or these bars, however, one non-chocolate lover in the house did not. It kind of reminded me of figs, and less so of chocolate, but I guess that is what Dutch chocolate tastes like. (Figs are NOT an ingredient.)  There is a special link between texture and chewing, and I found that I took smaller bites and chewed more with this product which left me with a very satisfied feeling. Overall, enjoyable...and good for you.  The inner box (the box pictured) didn't hold up that well in shipment, but it wasn't an issue since the bars are soft.  Just a hint: you will need to brush your teeth afterward to dislodge some of the almond chips.People with allergies should read the label before purchasing.  If that information isn't posted, post a comment and I'll update this review.A great snack bar for the purse or backpack for people on the go.  Highly recommended!

This has a smooth, moist, almost brownie-like taste and texture, not at all like other vegan bars, which are too often dry and gritty. The Pure Natural has a light chocolate center without an overly sweet, sugary taste. After my first bar, I immediately wanted to have another. My granddaughter should love this bar -- she requires a gluten-free diet -- but even if the gluten issue isn't relevant for you, Pure Natural is a good choice. I didn't give it 5 stars only because I'm not a big fan of almonds in my food (they're fine eaten separately), but I realize this won't matter to most people.

column9: Not So Much Chocolate---fruit and nut bar "Hint of chocolate"
column10: It does ~look~ like a chocolate bar if that is what they are meaning by chocolate.  Over all the bar is good but it should not claim that it is "chocolate" as it needs twice as much cocoa in it!  The hint of chocolate flavor is immediately overwhelmed by a very sweet date/agave flavor, which almost tasted like prunes to me(good thing I like them).  After the first bite I no longer tasted the chocolate.On the other hand my kids liked the bars and said they were yummy and would like to eat them again.  It was nice for them that there were no big nut pieces because they would have refused to eat them.  They chose to take pieces off of the bar that is super soft and roll it into balls-fun!I love that the bar is vegan and gluten-free.Bar: 8g fat, 25 carb, 17 sugars, and 7g protein.

The first thing I noticed about these chocolate almond bars is they arrived on a 90+ degree day and weren't melted! That answered any questions I had as to how well they would travel.The second thing I noticed was the ingredients list: Dates, almonds, organic agave nectar, organic rice protein concentrate, cocoa (dutched), chia seeds, organic agave fiber, and natural flavors.I was impressed. In case you don't know, agave is a sweetener that's low on the glycemic index (although dates may be pretty high -- sources differ). And chia seeds are high in EFAs. Each 1.7 oz. bar has 190 calories, with 7 grams of protein and 8 grams of fat, much of which is healthy fat from the almonds and chia seeds.What's most impressive is the taste and texture. They're chewy, but pleasantly so -- not tough like some protein bars tend to be. And the flavor and overall texture is like a really, really good chocolate brownie.In other words, these bars are great!

It is what it is. It's not a "chocolate bar" as the average American might think of. It is not a brownie. It is not a granola bar. It is a chewy bar composed of finely chopped almonds, dates, Dutch cocoa (which you can taste), Chia seeds, Fiber and sweetened with Agave Nectar.At 190 calories a bar, 8 grams of total fat, 25 grams of carbs, and 7 grams of protein, it makes for a healthful snack (or even breakfast). The fats are good ones, though.Our family was mixed in their reviews. My husband said he has tasted better bars at Sam's Club, I thought it was decent (though I wouldn't eat them regularly), my seven-year-old son loved them and was excited he would be eating the remaining ten bars, and my two-year-old daughter liked the bar as well.They are vegan (though we are not), and gluten-free. My son has a gluten sensitivity, so it is nice to have a snack he loves that would not aggrevate his body.Apparently these were founded by a lady who has a six-year-old vegetarian.Overall, they were good, but I don't know that they answer the claim on the box which reads, "Your chocolate prayers have been answered."

Marketers know that if they slap "pure" and "natural" on anything, there's a segment of consumer that's automatically going to snarf them up.  Well, at least the people behind these bars seem to be doing it without cynicism.  They are gluten-free, vegan and the box they come in is even 100% recycled.  What's more, they taste pretty good as far as healthy snack bars go.I passed them out around the office to get a wide range of opinions.  Everyone liked the taste, and the bars were compared favorably to Clif Bars.  To me, they have some of the same chalky, dry texture as Clif Bars, although to a lesser degree.  No, this isn't going to win head-to-head with a brownie, but it is soft and mildly sweet and certainly healthier.  I ate one as a desert after lunch today and it was quite satisfying.Why would you want something vegan-friendly and gluten-free if you're not a vegan or a sufferer of Celiac disease?  Well, from the research I've seen, gluten messes with the gut of even people without celiacs.  So probably good to avoid.  And the vegan aesthetic, when done right, is better for the planet as a whole, vegans and non-vegans alike.  Win-win.Ingredients: dates, almonds, agave nectar, rice protein concentrate, cocoa (dutched), chia seeds, agave fiber, natural flavors.  Dates and agave are two of the healthiest sweeteners; almonds are supposedly one of the best nuts in terms of heart health; chia seeds are reputed to be good for skin.I try to stay low-carb.  You will get 25g of carbs in a bar, probably from the rice protein concentrate.  The other positives about the ingredients probably outweigh this factor for most people, but it is something else to be aware of.  A lot of sins can be hidden under the name "natural flavors" too, but I'm willing to give Pure Naturals the benefit of the doubt.Overall, this is the best snack bar I've encountered in terms of both ingredients and taste.  Eat responsibly.

My first few bites were a bit chewy and dry.  I didn't enjoy it so much.  I suppose I was expecting more flavor.But ...After a few minutes and a drink of water later, I quite liked these bars.  They're a bit dense so I found they were filling when paired with a fruit.  Also, the chocolate in question is like a brownie and basically cocoa in flavor, not rich chocolate, which is what I was expecting.  As a result, the chocolate flavor is subtle, and I liked that because it makes this feel like a healthy option and it is not overpowering.  The almonds could have been more pronounced instead of being just sort of present here or there.  For a sweet tooth, not the option I'd go with, but if you like a bit of cocoa flavor and a snack option that's not going to kill your diet and is organic, this is a decent option.  Just make sure you have something to drink with it because it is chewy and a little dry.

My son is ultra-picky.  He tried Pure Natural Bars and said they were "not bad."  I asked him if he would eat it for a snack and he said no, but he would eat it if he was very hungry and there was nothing else to eat.I agree.  They are not bad.  Not great, either.  They're chewy, not too sweet (a good thing).  The almonds are there but not that noticeable.  I can say the same about the chocolate.  The texture makes me feel like I'm eating a bar of fiber.  Maybe that's why I'm not over the moon about it.

column9: I Liked it Okay, but it was a No-Go with my kids
column10: The wrapper forPure Natural Bars, Chocolate Almond, 1.7-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) shows a bar with whole almonds and chunks of dark chocolate, so it was quite the surprise to open the wrapper to find a soft, squishy brown bar with pieces of almonds throughout.  Looks aside, I didn't find the taste of this all natural bar with 7 grams of protein and 5 grams of fiber to taste all that bad.However, without being told the ingredients, my children immediately picked up that there was "prune-like" fruit mixed in this chocolate bars and they turned up their noises at both the taste and the texture. (And they are not picky eaters)  Turns out that the first ingredient listed for this chocolate bar is dates.And, although the ingredients seem allergy friendly (ingredients are: dates, almonds, organic agave nectar, organic rice protein concentrate, cocoa, chia seeds, organic agave fiber and natural flavors), the package is clearly marked that the product is made in a facility that processes milk, eggs, wheat and peanuts. I think my friends with highly allergic kids would not take the risk of trying this product because of that fact.All that being said, I think my husband and I will enjoy having these bars around for a quick on-the-go breakfast or snack.
Sorry, but Pure Naturals Chocolate Almond Bar did NOT answer my chocolate prayers. It was like eating 190 calories of cocoa, period. Thankfully, I had some leftover coffee in my mug to wash it down.

These are supposed to be healthy vegan nutrition chocolate bars. If they tasted really good then I would ignore the calories and fat content. But they taste mediocre at best with a gritty texture which I suspect are the ground up fiber or almonds. The box shows whole almonds but there are no whole almonds in these bars. They also don't really have that rich dark chocolate taste either. I usually eat Kellog's Fiber Plus bars which actually taste quite good and definitely taste better than these Pure Naturals bars.When comparing Calories, Fat, Protein, Fiber and Vitamins, it is about a draw between the Pure Naturals and the Kellog's Fiber Plus. The Kellog's Fiber Plus bar has fewer calories per bar 130 vs 190, fewer fat calories 35 vs 70, more fiber 9g vs 5g and more Vitamin E and Zinc. But the Kellog's Fiber Plus also has more Saturated fat 3g vs 1g and fewer Proteins 2g vs 7g.Another problem is that the Pure Natural bars are promoted as Gluten-Free, Vegan and Natural Ingredients. I'll give them the Natural but they are processed in a plant that also processes Wheat, Peanuts, Soy, Sesame so that negates the Gluten-Free statement. The only plus I can find to these bars is that they use only natural or organic ingredients.I definitely would not call either bar healthy but if you have to have a chocolate bar then they are better for you than your typical chocolate bar. I would recommend trying the Kellog's Fiber Plus first and if not to your liking then try the Pure Naturals bars. Will I eat them, sure but will I buy the Pure Natural bars, not likely as they are very costly compared to the Kellog's Fiber Plus.

This noodle dish is delicious, just a tiny bit spicy.  For a taste of Thai cooking, add a couple tablespoons of peanut butter to the sauce, blend well before adding to the noodles.  Great with chicken!

column9: Ginger Soy Soba Noodles are FANTASTIC!
column10: One of the thing I don't like about the Amazon review system is that it often lumps together reviews of similar products (which aren't really at all similar).  This is the case w/Annie Chun products.  On the Ginger Soy Soba Noodles page, there are 17 customer reviews, almost none of which refer to this specific product, but to another Annie Chun product/flavor.  That's too bad because customers should be able to see reviews just for that product.This review is for the Ginger Soy Soba noodle kit.  It was absolutely FANTASTIC and I'm ordering more.  The flavor is great - nice blend of soy & ginger (actual chunks of ginger too), the noodles are super tasty (and healthy - much more protein than a lot of Annie's other noodles), and preparation is very quick/easy.  As other reviewers have pointed out, the noodles are only 7" long so you don't have to break them to fit them in a medium saucepan.Note, there are not microwave instructions as the noodles need boiling for 3-4 minutes.  But, that's it.  Then you just mix in the sauce (and optional oil packet - you can use less of it to reduce fat).
Received item, but noticed that it one box within the package was a different variety than I ordered.  No big deal, just an observation
We loved the Soy Ginger Saba Noodles. Absolutely not too spicy...not hot at all. Our two year old gobbled them up.
Easy to make a meal out of this by adding some meat and veggies.  Easy and tastes good too.

column9: Unsatisfying flavor --- and too much work
column10: I've tried several of these Annie Chun noodle dishes and soups with noodles. I don't find any of them very good as compared with 'real' Asian food. Some aren't too bad when doctored with some soy sauce, hot sauce, or other sauce. And some aren't too bad for ease of preparation.This one isn't easily doctored, nor is it that fast/simple to make. Therefore I don't see any reason to keep in the pantry. If I don't feel like spending 20-30 minutes to make my own Asian food from scratch, I'll stick with better/easier ready-made products to keep on hand.

I bought this and a few other Annie Chun products on the recomendation of a Trader Joe's worker.  Annie's signature Soba noodles can be cooked to either an unappealing glue or still hard inside.  The sauce has an unpleasent odor, my fiancee would not even try it.  I went ahead and tried it but couldn't finish it.  I think I'm being generous with 2 Stars, seeing as how my dogs wouldn't eat it either.

column9: Kellog's changed Krusteaz recipe about Fall 2011.
column10: We used to eat these pancakes every week with fruit instead of syrup. We have introduced our friends to these. Amazing that such health and flavor could come from a complete pancake mix.Unfortunately it seems that Kellog's now owns Krusteaz and they changed the recipe approximately in Fall 2011. Here are some of the changes:- Sugar almost doubled.- Fat up by 33%.- Salt up by 8%.Hmm, so much for my tasty healthy alternative. Seems like there were plenty of to-sweet pancakes available on the market that appeal to children.The new recipe mix currently says "Improved Taste" on the package. I wish I could find a source for the old recipe and buy enough to last to the use-by date. There does not seem to be any way to ask Amazon sellers details like this about what they are selling.The new recipe is still the best tasting pancake mix that we can find, but how can you want that much sugar in something you are going to pour syrup over? We are looking for an alternative.

This is a really great pancake mix.  It was fresh and pefectly packaged.  It arrived intact and was shipped very quickly.I mix this with Krusteaz Blueberry Pancake Mix for a really super breakfast!  It's a really tasty pancake mix that's also very healthy.

column9: Pumpkin Pie in a Coffee Mug
column10: I think this coffee is an absolutely delicious eye opener.It fills the room with a mixed blend of fragrances of pumpkin, cinnamon, nutmeg and cloves.It's ingredients are all organic and a wonderful combination.It doesn't smell as wonderful in the bag as it does when heated. This is a savory way to start the day. Not just great for the holidays, but especially nice anytime during the cold weather. Highly recommended.

column9: Wonderful Medium Dark Roast Holiday Blend
column10: I almost never buy flavored coffees but took a chance because it was on sale.  A really excellent well balenced holiday blend.  As expected, I do not taste pumpkin, but I taste the nutmeg, cinamon and hint of cloves that make a great pumpkin pie.  The coffee is a medium dark roast (not Starbucks dark) that is a great match to the spices.  The pumpkin does not overpower the coffee, it compliments it.That said, coffee is a personal thing.  The reviewer who rated this 1 star rates K-cup instant coffee and tea 5 stars....I can't drink that awful stuff.  I agree with the majority here.  Really exceptional!

This pumpkin coffee arrived fresh and not overly flavored or sweet.  It's perfect with milk/creamer and sugar isn't necessary. My roommate, who has a sensitive stomach, is even able to drink this because it's "low acid" which was a nice surprise.  I'll definitely continue to purchase throughout the year and not just the fall season.

column9: Not a pumpkin-y as I would have hoped, but a great flavour
column10: I bought this coffee seeking fall flavors, but unfortunately, it just seemed there wasn't enough in this coffee! BUT the price for the amount of coffee you get is unbeatable and the flavor it still wonderful, just not as pumpkin-y as I would have hoped. Plus, it's organic and all that good stuff.

This is the second brand of pumpkin spice coffee that I've purchased and it is out of this world.  I feel like I'm having a warm piece of pumpkin pie. It's very rich and smooth and tastes the same cup after cup.

Just tried this Pumkin Spice Coffee.  Spouse said it left an after taste.  I couldn't taste the Pumkin -- the only reason to buy Pumkin Spice coffee.  Label says its Low Acidic -- that's a plus if the coffee was better.  Bean Coffee Engineer's have some work to do on this Pumkin Blend.PROBLEM:  We got use to GODAVIA, Pumkin Spice Coffee which is the VERY VERY BEST!  Unfortunately it is also $$$$$ VERY Pricey.

If you like medium or dark roast, this is not for you.  Only slight pumpkin spice flavoring and weak coffee taste.I will have to double up the scoops to achieve the flavor I want.  It is less acidic which is easier on a sensitive stomach.

column9: I seriously do not taste any kind of pumpkin or spice.
column10: I am so disappointed. I don't taste anything at all. I have to put my own spices in. I will stick w/ Green Mountain from now on.
I was looking for a replacement for my Dunkin donuts Pumpkin Spice. This not only does the job but very well may replace it. Excellent coffee. It is also Organic & made in USA!
This is yummy coffee but doesn't taste like pumpkin per se. Just a sweeter blend really. I do not think it is worth the money if pumpkin spice is what you are after

column9: good but more on the spice side than the pumkin
column10: We like this but it was not pumpkin enough but still great.  I would not buy the two pack if you are not sure.  We drank all of it but like the pumpkin from Gevalia better.

I have been looking for pumpkin spice coffee that really has a good flavor to it and bought this because of the reviews.  I opened the bag and was surprised to find no smell that hinted the presence of anything other than normal coffee. I made a pot of coffee and still, nothing in the flavor or smell to suggest it is anything other than normal coffee.The coffee itself is ok, but the product isn't at all as described. Given the reviews, I find myself wondering if a mistake of some kind happened during the busy holiday season, and I was sent plain coffee with a pumpkin spice sticker on it.
A subtle and smooth pumpkin taste!!  Very good coffee at a decent price. I recommend this coffee if you like a good seasonal flavor!!

I love this coffee! The flavor is smooth and low acidic. It is a rich flavor and it might not be as much pumpkin flavor as some others I've tasted, but it's so good I would get it again. The bags are huge so they last a long time!

The Bean Company has to be by far the best Pumpkin Spice coffee I have ever tried.. I have tried Gloria Jean's and others. Until now I thought Gloria Jean's was the best. This one tastes so much better.
Hardly any "pumkin pie" type taste.  It does have the flavor of some of the seasonings, lots of nutmeg.  Tastes very acidic.  I do not recommend. I'd return it if I could.
This one of the best flavored coffees I have ever had. Excellent with a little cocoa powder mixed in during the brew.

I was really surprised how good this coffee is. I bought it on a whim, then brewed a pot of it at work. It really has a delicious flavor. The pumkin spice flavor is really well balanced with the coffee. It's perfect for the holiday season!

Great coffee with no bitter aftertaste and delicious pumpkin flavor. I used it in an eggnog latte and it was a hit in our house!  The only negative is that it doesn't come with a way to reseal the bag i.e. a tin tie or sticker. I used the tin tie from another coffee bag and that worked just fine.If you like pumpkin and coffee you won't regret the purchase. While I did buy it during a lightening deal, I would buy again even at full price.

BAD smell when I opened the bag and even worse smell when brewing the stuff.  Not sure what the flavor is..some bad spice or chemical taste..family did not like it nor did our friends... all turned up noses..wish I  could return but...green mountain has an awesome pumpkin coffee, this was no comparison.

I'm a fan of flavored coffee and The Bean's pumpkin spice is the best I've tasted.  Subtle not overpowering.  I'm enjoying a cup of it right now along with a toasted cranberry-orange bagel with light cream cheese on this cool, crisp, autumn day. I love the low acid and high anti-oxidant content.  It's an added bonus. I didn't know the difference until I tasted it. This is a good one.

I had heard a little about this product from the local pet store, then tried a small bag for our 2 cats of about 3 and 6 years respectively. The female, younger one took to it right away, and the older male, who was unfortunately weaned on the junk cat food with all the corn meal and etc... in it, and would usually refuse a diet change, actually liked it too. The older male is overweight and we were trying to switch him to soft food on the doctor's request, but he totally refused it. He is a posh cat after all. He still consumes too many calories, the fatty, but at least I know he's eating good food. Of course, I know this product seems to cost more than most other feline food on the market, but I just can't see feeding our animals the lousy alternatives that are out there, marketed as being healthy. Why do commercials show cats eating a vegetarian diet which is mostly corn meal? Is that right? I'll stay with this for now, but stay tuned.I'm updating this review after 9 months of using this cat food for our two cats. I upgraded the stars from 4 to 5 as it really has been a good food for the two of them. Garfield still eats a little too much, but he's just a big cat who doesn't exercise much, let's face it. Our female cat will be 4 years old in a couple months and she's so healthy. She's tiny, but happy and agile. I tried the chicken version of Holistic Select, but Garfield seemd to miss this sardine version so we went back to this one. I've ordered the duck version and will update this once they try it.

I started buying this after I noticed my 1 year old cat was already starting to lose his "spunk" so I decided it was time to start buying him "real" cat food...not the garbage in the super markets. I found this at the pet store out of the other million choices, and I'm sure there are other brands that are just as good but this is the one I went with to try first and it was a great purchase. My cat has been on this for the past 8 months and he's now just has active as he was when he was a kitten and his coat has became sooo soft. Mainly, he loved the taste even more! I highly recommend this brand to all my friends and family for their animals!

I have done a lot of research to find the best food for my cat, and this is an excellent food.  That is also according to my holistic veterinarian.  They put probiotics on the kibble as the last step, which is very important to me.  The best thing is that my cat loved it immediately and I had to stop mixing it with the old food because she only would eat Holistic Select.

column9: Perfect Cat Food For Older Cats!
column10: This cat food was recommended by my vet because my 13 year old Cleo Cat was having trouble keeping any food down and was loosing weight.  It stopped her problems.  She doesn't eat as much as before since she seems to be more satisfied after eating which helps justify the added price.  It aids in digestion since the...ok sorry...smells are gone if ya know what I mean.  Had to add that so anyone experiencing problems with their cats can see there are a lot of benifits from this cat food.

I have a 4 year old male cat who has chronic urinary tract infections.  I feed him this dry food in combination with wet food (with water added to it) and Uri Ease.  The combination seems to keeps his UTI's under control.  If I switch to another type of dry food, his UTI gets worse.  The other cats seem to enjoy this food as well.  It's expensive but it seems to be the best solution for me.

Before I was educated about feline nutrition, I allowed my cats to become addicted to dry cat food. I always offered both canned and dry, but wish I would have fed them premium quality canned food and limited dry food. I have two 15 year old cats and two 5 year old cats. The only good quality dry foods they will eat are Wellness and Innova. Innova's manufacturer was recently purchased by Procter&Gamble. I began looking for a replacement. After once again offering several samples (from my local holistic pet store) Holistic Select was the only one (other than the usual Wellness and Innova) they would eat. For finicky cats, I recommend trying Holistic Select. It is a good quality food that is very palatable for finicky eaters.

My holistic vet recommended this, along with a few other brands. We tried them all, but my cats prefer this (especially the sardine version). The best part is their coats are so soft and clean and their eyes are so clear. AND (and I don't want to be rude, so I'll say this as delicately as I can) their waste is far less odorous than cats who eat the McDonalds junk found in most stores, which is a definite plus for me! The health benefits are so obvious - I highly recommend Holistic Select!

column9: Wonderful food - perfect for allergic kitties
column10: One of my cats is allergic to fish and beef. This formula is one of the few she can eat, and it has much better ingredients than the prescription diets available at the vet. Both of my kitties are very active, have soft shiny fur, and neither are fat. Dry food reduces tartar buildup on teeth, also.

Our cats thrive extremely well on this dry cat food.  They definitely have much less hair ball throw ups and their fur is great.  They are fit and not over weight.  This vendor ships extremely fast.  Is one of the top Amazon suppliers in our book!

Nature's Logic North Atlantic Sardine Oil Fatty Acid Supplement for Dogs and Cats (32-oz bottle)I always give my dog fish oil and brewers yeast tablets.  She always gets complimented on how her coat is so shiny and soft. This product had the best value I could find and my dog has no problems with the taste.  I mix it with her food.
Within a week of using this product my 2 dog's coats were both much fluffier and softer and snugglier. Expensive but worth it!

column9: This great stuff, and the big packages are convenient, but...
column10: ...the 16oz. boxes are less expensive per ounce.  At the moment, the 30 packages on this page are $0.20 per ounce, while the 16oz boxes are $0.18 per oz.  McCANN'S Steel Cut Irish Oatmeal, Quick & Easy, 16-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)  $0.02 per ounce isn't much, but it's 10% - $7.20 for the 12-30oz packages advertised on this page.
This sauce is by far the BEST! I happened upon it once and we were hooked. Now we buy it by the six pack and even give it as gifts.

column9: Sauce is great, Price is great & auto-shipping is Awesome
column10: we have large bbq's and everyone seems to love the sauce... its not just sauce... it has small chunks of good in it

I have been using Giovanni Body Wash (White Tea scent) for several years now. I have extremely sensitive skin, prone to acne, rashes and irritations when using most other soaps. I have wasted tons of money trying soap after soap hoping to find something that wouldn't irritate my skin, lathering well, while leaving me feeling clean. This soap has a really nice, soft scent, washes skin clean of dirt and oil and leaves no soap scum after rinsed off. This is the only soap I have found that does not cause break-outs/irritations and lathers well. I truely wish I could find a more econonmcal product that does the same job as this body wash but still haven't found one. So I try to find really good deals when buying this body wash to help off set the cost.Please note: this soap is a little drying.. so if you already have a dry skin conidtion this may not be the soap for you. I lived in a very warm humid climate when I started using this soap and did not notice the drying effect until I moved to a much cooler and dryer area. With that being said Giovanni also sells one of the best moisturizers I have ever used, it's their body butter (comes in the same scents as the body washes). This body butter works fantasticly! I am in the health care field and have to wash my hands many, many times a day. If I put some of the body butter on at night right before I go to sleep, my hands are moisturized all the next day without reapplying! I have tried many moisturizers that seems to work great until you wash your hands, then its like you never had any on in the first place... the body butter is not like this.

Ok, so I absolutely love the packaging and the nifty description on the back of the bottle, but when I'm paying .64/oz, I expect it to moisturize. Giovanni claims that their washes include "essential oil complex to soothe, smooth and regenerate skin's lost moisture" but the ingredients' list contains no such ingredient, unless they are referring to the "Essential Oil Fragrance" in which case they are blatantly lying because essential oils provide scent, not moisture. Even the dollar bottles of cheapo wash at Walmart contain some type of moisturizer, albeit petroleum. Sometimes I use St. Ives Whipped Silk body wash and it's definitely more moisturizing than Giovanni due to the sunflower oil. I've noticed even JASON's washes contain Sodium PCA to moisturize (although their stuff also has harsh sulfates, so I've never tried them). Or maybe Giovanni deliberately left out any moisturizers out so that we buy their lotions/body butters. Ha!While I sound like I hate the product, I really don't; I just wish it provided some moisture. The good: it looks and feels like a spa product, washes well and rinses cleanly, and smells good and not artificial perfumey like Herbal Essences and all that other junk. Also, it actually works well as a shampoo when in a pinch. In fact, I've taken to using it as shampoo as well since Giovanni keeps changing their shampoo formulas (and for the worse, it seems, judging from the new ingredients) and body washes tend to be more gentle than shampoos. I've tried Raspberry Winter, Lavender Vanilla Snow, Cassifluer White Tea, and D:tox (bar soap form) and they all smell awesome. True aromatherapy in a bottle.
Gave this to the nurses at Mom's rehab place. They were thrilled to have so many gourmet treats. Some liked the sweets, and some liked the salty. Everyone was really pleased. Great gift, good value.

column9: I really did not like taste of this coffee
column10: I really did not like taste of this coffee. I understand that taste is very individual and I don't want to discourage people from trying it, but I "really" did not like it. If you like taste of flavored coffee and drink it with milk, maybe it will be good for you. I drink my coffee black, not flavored and preferably strong, but I am trying to avoid caffeine. I will look for something else.

I absolutely love coffee but most of the time it makes me jittery. Over the years I've tried different Teeccino flavors and this one is BY FAR the best! It's closest to the taste of real coffee even though it's chocolate flavored, it's really smooth and light on the stomach, and the SMELL is so good when you first take it out of the packet! I love the "tee bags" they are making now because I can get the same brew every time-I steep mine for 3 minutes and dunk it 10-15 times, then add raw honey and cream. SO DELICIOUS!
For a person who loves but cannot drink coffee, Teeccino almost replaces my true love.  The Chocolate Teeccino is as good as desert!  It is very flavorabe and rich.

It smells wonderful. It doesn't actually taste like coffee, but it is a good substitute. I like the chocolateyness. If you haven't had a lot of caffeine recently, you can notice a little bit of an energy boost. It's nothing like a caffeine boost, but it's enough for me.

column9: A Very Satisfying Cup of "coffee"... Finally!
column10: I have been needing to give up coffee due to the acidity. I have tried several "low acid" coffees as well as made my own "Cold brew" coffee concentrate. Nothing was quite what I needed where flavor was concerned, and most were still upsetting my stomach. I had already given up the caffeine, so that was not an issue. When I saw the favorible reviews of the Teeccino products, I decided to give them a try. I sampled these "Tee Bags" first, as they came in a small box, so I figured if I did not like them, I wasn't out much.I cannot believe how much I LOVED this product! The Tee Bags make it super easy to prepare, and the aroma was great from the moment I tore open the little envelope. The flavor really is wonderful! Very rich and satisfying! I added a little flavored creamer to mine, just as I would with coffee and it was delicious. I am very surprised at just how much this tasted like coffee. It is my new favorite product. I highly recommend it to anyone having to give up coffee. I am looking forward to trying the "ground, brew your own" version, as well as the other flavors.

column9: Very smooth delicate flavor, great CHAI TEA
column10: I just bought my first box of this, being a sort of STASH CHAI addict, drinking the BLACK CHIA TEA, and the GREEN CHIA TEA, both of which are good. So, you like CHAI? great. The box lists the same spices for each box, but they are in different ratios, depending on the strenght of the backround tea. The black tea, uses ginger, then cinnamon, clove, allspice, nutmeg, and cardamon, in decreasing amounts of spice, as you decend down the spice list. (altho the company also uses spice oils, for the teas, for more flavor.) The green tea CHIA as more cinnamon in it, compaired to the black chia. NOW, for the WHITE CHIA. SPICES AS  FOLLOWS, its mostly CINNAMON, then ginger, allspice, clove, nutmeg, and cardamon. ALL real CHIA teas, use these spices, but they need to be balanced to the teas, and WHITE TEA, is very delicate tea, of course. ALso, since it is even less processed than GREEN TEA, its very easy to make it bitter.  (It has more antioxidants than green tea too.) SO, if you get this, and you want it to taste good, dont throw BOILING WATER on the tea bag(s). Let your water sit for a minute, until its around 190 degrees F.
