Amazon had a terrific deal on them for awhile, at something like $17.00 for twelve boxes, but now they've raised it to the same price as the other Carr flavors, $30.00, so they're no longer such a terrific bargain.Bummer.But I'm still buying them, not as frequently.

column9: Some of the best crackers made
column10: Carr's crackers are about as good as crackers get.  They're tasty, sized right and sturdy enough for dipping.

These are my all time favorite crackers. They're so delicious that they can actually be addictive. After you have eaten 2 or 3 a strong very good flavor starts to accumulate on your tongue. And you start to crave more of that great flavor. And then, the more crackers you eat, the more you crave another.  -The bad part is that these can be difficult to find. I first discovered these at local supermarkets about 10 years ago. But then, after a few years .They disappeared from all of my local stores. Then, about a year after they disappeared from local stores, Amazon started to carry them. But Amazon is often out of stock on these. Including a recent period when Amazon didn't have any for over a year. So if you want any. You have to grab them as soon as you see that any are  available.  -I was pleasantly surprised when Amazon recently made them available thru Subscribe and Save. Aside from the lower price and free delivery. Maybe that's an indication that Amazon now expects to always have these in stock.  -

****April 29, 2012These Cheez-Its from Sunshine Biscuits, which is owned by Kellogg's, are advertised on the box as being "Creamy & Mild."  If by creamy is meant that there's a texture that's creamy then this half of the "creamy and mild" claim is false.  These are crackers, and they've been intentionally baked so as to remove water.  They are crisp throughout.  They do not deform in response to sufficient pressure but rather they crack, which I think is why crackers are called that.  They are not a liquid in any sense; they are a quite dry solid.  And to me a texture that's described as creamy must be to some extent liquid, which these are not at all.  Brie is a creamy cheese, cheddar is not.Speaking of cheeses, these crackers contain three types.  The one listed first on the list of ingredients is white cheddar, followed by cheddar, and only then by mozzarella.And they are mild.  There is no burst of cheese or any other flavor when you pop a few in your mouth and crunch down.  So the second half of the "creamy and mild" claim is accurate.  I'm sure we're all different, but for me the biggest hit of flavor is just BEFORE I crunch down.  Try it: Just before you start chewing them, take a sniff through your mouth and nose and you'll smell a lovely odor of cheese.****You probably want to know why the manufacturer is called Sunshine Biscuits.  The company was founded by one Jacob L. Loose of Kansas City, Missouri, who with the profits it generated built and lived in what is now called the Loose Mansion, which is quite an extraordinary property on the south side of Armour Boulevard just east of Main Street, which you can Google.  It's a good three stories tall and comes equipped not just with walk-in closets but a walk-in safe, a carriage house, a kitchen bigger than a two-car garage, and more rooms than you can count.  No kidding.For several years the Loose Mansion was owned by my aunt Sue's not-for-profit educational enterprise, called The Teel Foundation, and during that time it was used for some of the scenes in the 1995 movie "Truman" starring Gary Sinise, and from which it, the foundation, benefitted because the movie crew left behind a really nice and really huge table that was used in scenes where Truman's cabinet met, so if you want to see that table you'll have to watch the movie.  And the reason I say I'm not kidding that it has more rooms than you can count is that Sue owned and operated her foundation from that mansion for over a year before she realized there were rooms she had never once entered.  This is a very big house.Anyway, Jacob, who also funded one of the finest parks in Kansas City, called Loose Park, was married to a woman named Sunshine, so now you know.****You also probably want to know just exactly how many of these Kellogg's Sunshine Cheez-IT Mozzarella Cheese, 13.7-Ounce (Pack of 4) by Cheez-It crackers you can buy for one share of Berkshire Hathaway stock.  I've read all the previous reviews of this product to date, and I see no mention whatsoever of any attempt even to ask this question, not to mention answering it, so let me fill in that hole for you, because as you know from so many of my own previous reviews on Amazon I do strive to be thorough.As of the close of business on the New York Stock Exchange on April 27, 2012, Berkshire Hathaway class A shares (ticker symbol BRKA) are worth $120,925.00 each.  That's right, it will cost you over $120,000 to buy just one share of Berkshire.  By comparison, one share of Kellogg's (ticker symbol K) at the April 27th close will cost you $50.35.I weighed ten of these crackers and arrived at 3/8 ounce.  I added ten more and arrived at 3/4 ounce, so we can be pretty sure each cracker weighs pretty close to 3/80ths of an ounce.  The inverse of 3/80 is 80/3, which means there are 26-2/3 crackers per ounce.  There being 13.7 ounces of crackers per box, we now know there are 365-1/3 crackers per box.Now we need to know the price of such a box, and here I get confused.  According to the Amazon page I'm looking at right now a pack of four of these boxes costs $29.97, which is $7.4925 per box, which seems like a lot to me.  When I just now used Google Goggles on the UPC bar code I was led to a store selling these for $2.88, which is the price, rounded up to $3, that I will use in the remaining calculations.$120,925 divided by $3 means you can buy 40,308 boxes (and have a dollar left over).  40,308 boxes times 365-1/3 crackers per box is the answer we've been so eagerly seeking.  For one share of Berkshire.A you will get nearly 15 million crackers.14,725,856 crackers, to be exact, will weigh 552,219.6 ounces, or 34,513.725 pounds, which is over 17 tons of crackers, not to mention the weight of the waxed paper liner and the box.That box is 9 inches tall by 6-1/4 inches wide by 2-3/8 inches deep, which means it occupies 133.59375 cubic inches of volume, which -- trust me on this -- means that 40,308 such boxes will occupy 3,116.259765625 cubic feet.  (Or don't trust me on this.  If you come up with an answer that's different by even a single digit anywhere, please do leave a comment.)If we assume a typical room whose floor-to-ceiling height is 95 inches, we can fit exactly 40 of these boxes laid flat in a tower, because 95 inches divided by 2-3/8 inches equals 40.  That tower will occupy 133.59375 times 40, or 5,343.75, cubic inches of volume, which is 3.09244791666 cubic feet, where the sixes repeat forever.  So the next obvious question is what the other two dimensions of the room must be to hold all 40,308 boxes.  Well, it's obvious to me.The number of 40-box towers necessary to make up 40,308 boxes is simply the latter divided by the former, which is 1,007.7 such towers.  The footprint of each tower being 56.25 square inches (9 inches times 6-1/4 inches), that number times 1,007.7 such towers is 56,683.125 square inches of floor space.  The square root of that number means if the room is square the walls will be just a touch over 238.08218118960519973573719117007586000668448380401921 inches, which with your permission I'm cavalierly going to round to 238.  238 inches divided by 12 inches per foot is 19.8333 feet, which I'm even more cavalierly going to round to 20 feet.To contain the number of $3 boxes of Kellogg's Sunshine Cheez-IT Mozzarella Cheese, 13.7-Ounce (Pack of 4) by Cheez-Its you can buy for one share of Berkshire Hathaway class A stock as of April 27, 2012, which is 40,308 boxes, you'll need a typical-height room that's 400 square feet in area.  Coincidentally, that's about the size of the two-car garage we mentioned earlier.  So, now you know.****If you've read this far you might be wondering about some of the conversion formulas I didn't show, so here's the complete set.To convert SQUARE INCHES to square feet, divide by 12 raised to the power of 2.576 --> 4.To convert SQUARE FEET to square inches, multiply by 12 raised to the power of 2.72 --> 10,368.To convert CUBIC INCHES to cubic feet, divide by 12 raised to the power of 3.5,343.75 --> 3.09244791666.To convert CUBIC FEET to cubic inches, multiply by 12 raised to the power of 3.3,116.259765625 --> 5,384,896.875.If you're wondering how I managed to derive 50 decimal places in that calculation of the square root of 56,683.125, I used a wonderfully useful program called Wolfram.  In case you're further interested, that particular answer is expressed by Wolfram to many THOUSANDS of digits, so aren't you glad I didn't show them all?Based on all the foregoing, I award this product 5 stars minus 1 for calling it creamy, which is, I'm pretty sure, equal to 4.****

Cheeze-It the creamy and mild Mozzarella baked snack crackers are wonderful and full of amazing flavor.  Very nice snack and is full of flavor that is so very satisfying. I would highly recommend this new flavor to anyone.

Mozzerella cheese is a favorite in our house, and we love the original flavor Cheez-its too, so I thought I'd give these a try. The box arrived in perfect  shape, so I was surprised to find about half of the crackers were either crushed or broken. The crackers have a nice Cheez-it crunch, but the flavor wasn't quite what I was expecting. They have a bit of a tangy, cheesy flavor; it's not bad, just different. (It reminds me a little of the White Cheddar flavor.) Good, authentic mozzarella cheese, to me, has a creamier and milder flavor. They might be good though, with different kinds of dip, or served with tomato soup. I like the idea that there are other varieties of Cheez-its available, but for now, I will probably stick with my favorite, the original.

I have been a fan of Cheez-It crackers for a long time. We almost always have the cheddar in our pantry and most recently the white cheddar which is very good as well. I was excited to try the mozzarella and I was not dissapointed! They have the same great crunch as the orginal but with a yummy mozzarella taste. I can't wait to see what they come out with next!

column9: Good flavor in this tasty treat
column10: I didn't realize Cheez-It had so many different flavors. I think it can be a slippery slope. For example, Doritos makes a bunch of flavors, but none are quite as good as two of their oldest flavors: Cool Ranch and Nacho Cheese. The other flavors are usually pretty good, but I tend to stop liking them as much before the bag is empty. What about the Mozzarella Cheez-Its? How do they stack up?Rather than just give you my impressions of the Mozzarella Cheez-It, I decided to share these with some coworkers. Here are the taste test results.Tester 1, Female, 60s: "Mmmmmm," she said after the first couple crackers. The words "good" and "tasty" came up and she remarked they have a totally different taste than the original Cheez-Its.Tester 2, Female, 30s: She got a funny look on her face and said, "Weird...I'm not sure...Not bad...Not as good as the original Cheez-Its." After a few more crackers she somewhat changed her tune and said they were quite tasty.Tester 3, Female, 40s: She didn't love them but thought they were "all right." She also preferred the original Cheez-It over the Mozzarella Cheez-Its.Tester 4, Female, 40s: She ate one carefully and started nodding. After a few more she commented that she preferred the Mozzarella over the original flavor. She liked the flavor a lot and said she'd definitely buy them.Tester 5, Female, 40s: She liked the smell of the crackers and also commented, "Mmmmmm," while raising her eyebrows. She liked the "buttery" flavor and commented she liked them better than the original Cheez-Its. She also eyed the nutritional information and approved of the zero sugars.Tester 6, Male, 50s: He enjoyed the "very nice mozzarella taste," and the "nice light flavor." He commented that he could eat "a lot more of these" and that he'd definitely buy them.Me, Male, 30s: I liked their aroma a lot. The box says "creamy and mild" and I'd agree. The first cracker's flavor really coated my palate like a sharp cheddar would but without that overpowering, strong taste. The texture of the cracker was enjoyable, too: very crisp. Also, the mild flavor of the Mozzarella Cheez-Its doesn't leave you with stank breath. I think they're on par with the original flavor Cheez-It which is not my favorite cracker snack, but I do eat them from time to time.Eating contest: Tester 2 and I had a contest to see who could fit more whole Cheez-Its in their mouth at once. Tester 2 fit 15 and I fit 22.  I bring this up because a serving size is 1 ounce or 25 crackers (150 calories, 7g of fat, 180mg sodium, 19g carbs). That should give you a visual of how large a serving size is.These crackers are a winner. They have a good flavor that isn't overpowering but also won't get boring. Some testers thought they'd be great in a party mix with other Cheez-It flavors.I received this box of crackers at no cost as a member of the Vine Program.

I'm sorry to say that I just did not enjoy these mozzarella cheese Cheez-It's. I like actual mozzarella cheese but the flavor powder on these crackers was just way too much for me. I could only eat two. The aftertaste was worse. I had to pop a peppermint to get the taste out of my mouth. A couple other people tried the crackers and weren't too impressed either.I like regular cheddar Cheez-It's, so I think I'll stick to those.

Cheez-IT crackers have been around since 1921, and I dare say that they have been a favorite of children ever since. I didn't know what to expect when I picked up this "new" Cheez-Its, mozzarella, but once I dug into them I found that I loved them. They are indeed quite smooth and delicious.If you like Cheez-IT crackers, then you will like these new mozzarella ones. I think that they are delicious!

column9: Good, but not as tasty as other Cheez-It products
column10: I absolutely adore Cheez-Its and eat about a box each week.  While these Mozzarella snacks are good, in my opinion the Four Cheese, Cheese-Duos, the Spicy, Baby Swiss, etc. are just a bit better.  Perhaps it's because Mozzarella is such a mild cheese that the cheesy flavor doesn't come through as well as it does in the other products.  I'm glad I tried them, but I won't buy again because I like the other Cheez-It products better.

These were good. I didn't have "regular" cheeze-its around to compare them too but if memory serves then these were "cheesier" and better. There are definitely some better flavors of cheez-its out nowadays but I can't imagine myself turning these things down at a party (or anywhere else).

While, we wouldn't have blind tasted picked out the idea of Mozzarella for these, the flavor is still cheesy and good. Everyone in my family enjoyed these. A light flavor that left us all fighting over the to the last bite. Definitely going on the grocery list.

I have never been a big fan of the original Cheez-Its although others in my household seem to love them. I really enjoyed this Mozzarella variety much more than the original flavor, although it was a bit strong and overwhelming.  For the general public, I would give these 4 stars. However, I changed my way of eating over 6 months ago and no longer eat foods with additives, preservatives, trans fat and other non-healthy ingredients (basically, most processed foods). If you fall into the category of being one who watches for this stuff as well, be aware these have enriched flour and a number of additives and ingredients you probably do not want in your snacks. I am happy to report there is no trans fat or high fructose corn syrup, which seems to be overwhelmingly prevalent in many processed foods today. Overall, I would eat these if I had to or really needed a snack and other options were not available.
It's hard to rate and review a Cheez-It.  If you like the white cheddar or monterey jack kind, then you'll like this one too.  These are just a little bit milder.

column9: A new twist on a classic!
column10: We love Cheez-Its and mozzarella is one of our favorite [hard to pick a favorite cheese!] so we were really excited to try mozzarella Cheez-Its!Thankfully, they did not disappoint, the flavor is a smooth mild cheese and with that great Cheez-It SNAP! We have purchased and enjoyed several boxes of this flavor, preferring it over the traditional Cheez-It flavor. Love the new flavors!

When I first opened up the box, I was chagrined to find that about half of the contents were broken crackers. Still, I'd ordered crackers through the postal service and some breakage is to be expected, right?The whole crackers were near the top, so I nabbed one gently between forefinger and middle finger and lifted it out of the box. Before my fingers cleared the packaging, the cracker had snapped in two.They're delicious - somehow creamy, despite having the pleasantly mealy texture of a good Cheez-It - but exceptionally fragile, making them unsuitable as a snack in a child's lunch or, frankly, the lunch of a fully grown adult with an unpadded lunch box. They're nice to eat out of hand and make a fantastic substitute for breadcrumbs when grilling up chicken or pork.

I love Cheez-ITs and have been eating them for as long as I can remember. White cheddar is a favorite of mine, and when I was on a diet, the Reduced Fat ones were just as tasty. Now for their latest flavor; mozzarella, I would have to say it is just okay. The flavor is mild and almost bland. Not to my liking and I would probably not purchase them.

column9: Mix up your cheese-it flavors now and then.
column10: I found these to have a good Mozzarella taste but they still retained that distinctive cheese-it cracker taste underneath which I liked. Everyone is going to have a different opinion on them so why not get a box and see for yourself? I did notice that MSG is listed in the ingredients. I don't believe that original cheese-its have it so that is something to keep in mind. Overall a good product that I like and will purchase in the future.I'd also like to note that mine were shipped smart post and I wouldn't recommend picking the cheapest shipping option when ordering. By the time the cheese-its got to me I'd say that only 1/3 of the box was whole crackers. The rest were broken down into a fine crumb mess. The box didn't look badly beat up, so I don't know what the post office does but it is definitely detrimental to the cheese-its.

I'm a fan of Cheez-Its.  However, I do prefer certain flavors over others.  For example, I personally don't like Baby Swiss flavor, but I do like this Mozzarella.First cracker, I found the taste of these Mozzarella Cheez-Its to be very mild.  It reminded me a little of the Baby Swiss, not in taste comparison but in that it's a very subtle cheese taste at first.  However, the more Mozzarella Cheez-Its I consumed, the more I tasted the Mozzarella flavor.  After a handful, I was in Mozzarella heaven.  It leaves a good after taste, too (unlike Baby Swiss).So, if you like Cheez-Its, and want to try a flavor that's not spicy, not tangy, and not 'in your face', then I recommend trying the milder, mellower Mozzarella cheese flavor.

column4: David G. Schwartz "I like reading more than w...
column10: We tried these out--both the kids and the adults couldn't get enough of them. They've got all of the cheesy goodness you'd normally associate with Cheez-Its, but with a slight, mozzarella twist. It's not exactly a pizza substitute, but this is good stuff.

I was never a fan of Cheez-Its. However, the Mozzarella Cheese Cheez-Its are an exception.I found these snacks to be very good. They're very tasty and most importantly they'renot very salty which was my main problem with the original Cheeze-It favor. While Iwouldn't buy the traditional flavor, I would definitely get these.

I'm not a huge fan of the original cheez-its, but these mozzarella cheez-its are wonderful.  They're made with both mozzarella and cheddar cheese, and you can definitely taste the cheddar.  But the mozzarella gives them a milder, butterier taste than a normal cheddar cracker.  They are also not too salty, which is often a problem with cheese crackers.At 150 calories for 25 crackers (a few handfuls), this is a great snack.  They take the edge of your hunger without filling you up with empty calories.They are a little greasy, so you'll want to have a napkin or a sink hand when you eat them.  The crackers in my box were almost all broken, which made it a little harder to eat them.  But those are relatively minor drawbacks, and this is certainly a product that I'll eat again.

The product description calls Kellogg's Sunshine Cheez-IT Mozzarella Cheese, a satisfying snack and claims that ..."regular snacking helps prevent overeating at mealtime and provides children with needed energy to keep their brains and bodies going throughout the day."Forget regular snacking.  With Cheez-IT Mozzarella it's munching mania.  The snack is like an overly salty bag of potato chips, and everybody knows about the (false) prospects of having "only" one.  "One more" is the mantra of Cheez-IT Mozzarella.  So incredibly addictive, it is a definite staple for the average American's couch potato stash.Taste wise, although billed as "100 percent real Mozzarella cheese," they have a chemical sting (you know, the one that Americans complain about, but secretly love).  However, the cheesy flavor is distinct, the texture of the cracker ... Cheez-IT ... all the way.  Keep them handy along with the other growing varieties of Cheez-IT crackers for the ultimate binge-snacking escape.Stacy Lytwyn, Marketing Guru/Motivational Speaker/JournalistAuthor: CONSUMMATE CONNECTICUT: DAY TRIPS WITH PANACHE

Kellogg's Sunshine Cheez-IT Mozzarella Cheese, 13.7-Ounce (Pack of 4)I sent for Kellogg's Sunshine Cheez-IT Mozzarella Cheese through my Vine offerings for review from Amazon. However, since the ingredients were not visible, I was unaware that the product contained MSG (monosodium glutamate) to which my entire family, me included, is allergic. So, I asked my neighbor if any of his household was allergic or sensitive to MSG-monosodium glutamate and he said no. So, they became my test group for the CHEEZ-IT with Mozzarella. Three boys high school and college age and their father, they reported as follows:21 year old: "Excellent Mozzarella flavoring. I liked it with ham added as a cracker snack."19 Year old: "Wow! Pete thanks, we all liked it and like my older bro I too made cracker and ham sandwiches of it!"12 year old: "it was good but a little too salty for me, so my brothers and dad ate most of it."Dad: "It was good and I joined the boys only I added an Italian ham to it, the spicy Capicola and it was great."There you have it, only one hitch, a suggestion to Kelloggs, RE: I read said that, more than 27% of people are sensitive to or allergic to MSG (monosodium glutamate), so any company or restaurant that uses it is automatically shutting off a sizable segment of their market.I agree, why cut out ANY of your market just to use a cheap substitute for spices'? I give it 3.5 stars which rounds out to four stars above, I took off 1.5 stars for the MSG added because it limits the marketability of the product and because we could not eat it.

We're a household of Cheez-It fans, so everyone was excited to try the new mozzarella flavor.  First of all, we were disappointed because many crackers had broken during shipping, so there were lots of crumbled bits scattered throughout the box.  However, the ones that remained were tangy and tasty.  They don't have quite the same texture as the regular cheddar flavor and do crumble a bit more easily.  However, this is a nice blend of salty and cheesy.  If you like the regular flavor and want to try something new, give these a try.

The CHEEZ-IT Mozzarella Cheese snack is totally yummy. My entire family loved these. We're also fans of the regular CHEEZ-IT's so I wasn't sure we'd like this new flavor. WE DID!!! They are mild but tasty. The CHEEZ-IT Mozzarella Cheese flavor is the only other flavor besides the original cheese our family will eat. GET THESE!!!

I have long been a fan of regular Cheeze-it's, and these are every bit as good, only with a wonderful cheesy mozzarella flavor. All the crunch and flavor you expect! I have to limit myself to a handful, then hide the box from myself so I don't eat the entire box!

It's not too hard to mess up Cheez-Its. Full disclosure--I only had a few due to my gluten-intolerance. But, my family easily polished off the box during the course of a weekend. They were tasty. Personally, I think I like this flavor to the regular Cheez-It flavor.

I really haven't found a cheez-it cracker that I do not like and the Mozzarella one's are no different. They are mild in flavor and kind of a little creamery tasting than most of the other cheez-its that I have tried. They are bursting with flavor as usual but without being overpowering. If you like Mozzarella cheese and you like cheez-its then I think you'll love this product.

I've always liked Cheez-Its, but the original cheddar version was always a bit sharp for me. This new Mozzarella brand has a smoother and ultimately more enjoyable flavor. Overall, I love it. I could eat a whole box of these in one sitting. I only wish they were healthier!

These Mozzarella Cheese-it's could be betterSure, They are cheesy, but they are not mozzarella cheesy. at least not to me. They tasted more like a white Cheddar and that was a major disappointmentSecond, they left a really bad aftertaste that reminded me of drinking diet soda and that was really unpleasant.I'd just stick with regular Cheezit's or the Hot & Spicy ones. These need improvement

The ingredients show cheddar cheese as the primary cheese in these crackers, and mozzarella is less than 2%. Therefore they taste more cheddar than anything else. Having said that, they were crunchy, cheesy, and every bit as good as other flavors. Friends and family members were equally impressed. Another hit for CHEEZ-IT.

My family loves Cheez-Its in general, so I was excited about the prospect of the mozzarella version. We were definitely not disappointed!The quality definitely fits with the Cheez-It brand name. It is a rich cracker with a good amount of flavor. The texture is the same as original Cheez-Its. My family enjoys these for both snacking purposes and cooking purposes.As for the mozzarella flavor - well, it does work. I'm not sure that I'd automatically think mozzarella if I were blind-folded and asked to identify the cheese. But, when I use it for cooking with a dish that works well with mozzarella but not some other cheese flavors, this product fits the flavor well.While I'm not sure that these are the snack crackers I'll automatically keep in the pantry, they are some that I will buy for specific cooking or snacking purposes. All in all, a pretty enjoyable product.

column9: ~~the more you eat the better they taste~~
column10: When I first tasted these I could only muster up an "okay".  Then I had a couple more and they tasted better.  After I had about 20 or so I realized that I really like them.  They are a completely different beast from the cheddar cheez-it's.  But they are quite good.  The taste is very light and it's a not an "in your face" kind of flavor.  If I hadn't tried the chedder jack flavor first I might even go so far as to say that they are my favorite next to the original flavor.  If they ever get on my Safeway's shelves I'll pick some up.

column9: Cheez-It crackers are a favorite with us
column10: Cheez-It crackers are a favorite in this house.  Everyone was eager to try the new Mozzarella flavor, so the box was open the minute it came in the door!  They did not disappoint, everyone likes them just as well as the other varieties we have tried.I will say, though, that this is where I find myself holding back from saying they are amazing.  They tasted pretty much like the other white varieties we've had, I couldn't taste any special difference in these being made with Mozzarella.  If I had been given a handful without seeing the box, I never would have known what flavor they were.  I prefer the original cheddar, that's my favorite.Still, my kids had to be limited to one serving, they love Cheez-It crackers in every variety!

I enjoyed this product.  After eating so many of the Cheddar flavor, it gets to be too much.  But, with this flavor, it was a milder and I could eat more than a few and not get sick of the flavor.  My family enjoyed it as well.  My wife, who isn't a big fan of the Cheddar, really liked the taste of these. Lighter and crispy.  I recommend this this product because it is a nice change from the Cheddar.

the mozzarella taste is mild but I can taste it. It still tastes like a cheez-it mostly and that is why I gave it five stars...because cheez-its are awesome. orginial is of course the best but this is still pretty good. If you like original cheez-its you will like this because of how much like an original cheez-it it tastes. They make a great alternative to the white cheez-its if white cheez-its are your bag.

Well being a junk food junkie this is an easy one to rate.  I loved this full flavor snack with real mozzarella taste.  This product didn't feel artificial like some other orange food.  I felt a little less guilty since it is not fried, but it was too easy to eat more than my fair share!

column9: An okay taste, from a delicious brand...
column10: I really love Cheez-ITs. I can sit down in front of the tv with a box and before I know it, it's half gone. But these were different. I don't know why, but I expected just a little more from this box, and yet it seemed to fall just short of hitting the nail directly on the head. Don't get me wrong, I still enjoyed them, but they left an odd after-taste in my mouth that I honestly wasn't that crazy about.Not much else to say, but I do hope that this review helped you in one way or the other.Enjoy.

column9: Really tasty but too many crumbs
column10: Like with every other flavor of Cheez-Its (or cheese crackers in general), I'm addicted. These are really tasty. Everyone in our house (including our 3yo son) liked them. The only problem was that half the box was crumbs, I assume from being tossed around during shipping...so that was a bummer.

This is a very mild and surprisingly flavorful selection from Cheez-It. I had this with a sandwich and they also go great with Tuna.Since the flavor is less 'cheesy' than the cheddar varieties, for instance these make perfect accompaniments for more flavorful foods. Still a healthy way to snack, and a 'different' approach to crackers with the mild flavor. Really enjoyed these!

column9: Review for Cheez-IT mozzarella cheese flavor
column10: I liked these Cheez-ITs. They taste like mozzarella cheese compared to the usual cheddar ones. They also don't get your fingers orange like the original flavor does.

I love Sunshine Cheez-It Crackers and always have a box on hand for snacking, so I was curious about their Mozzarella flavor.Well, about all I can say is they're good but can't hold a candle to regular ol' Cheez-Its.  The mozzarella flavor was just too light for me, making them taste more like plain old crackers instead of cheese flavored as I'd expected.They're not horrendous, just too lightly flavored for me.  So I'll be sticking with the oldie but goodie for now!

column9: Ok, but you should probably check them out at your local grocery
column10: First: purchasing crackers through the mail is a dicey proposition. These arrived and literally half the box was crumbs. So a small portion of the three stars above (which would be 2.5 if I could) comes from the fact that it was difficult to find a whole cracker in the box. (If this happens to you, do what we did: use them as crumb topping on a casserole).Second: At 5 dollars a box, they ring in at nearly twice the price of the same product at my local grocery...so you should probably check out your local grocery if you need to get your cheez-it fix.Now, on to the flavour--we didn't get creamy or mozzarella from these. They tasted fine...just not like the cheese whose name they wear. (The best flavours are original, the duoz with the smoked cheese flavour, and Swiss). There is too the problem of powdery residue on your fingers after snacking...a big plus of the original flavour is a total lack of this (and a much more cheesey flavour).

I have to say I was pleasantly surprised by the new Mozzrella Cheez-its. I had become rather tired of the old flavor, finding them to be a little on the dry side. But the new flavor is definitely worth trying - a product I would certainly purchase the next time I'm at the grocery store.The new mozzarella flavor is bold and distinct, and I found myself eating them with a glass of wine, something I would not have thought to do with the old flavor. And they went very well with a glass of white wine, though I'm sure they'd be every bit as good with red.My only disappointment was when I received the box of crackers - mostly crumbs. I'm not sure Amazon is used to dealing with fragile food items in their shipping, but hopefully Kellogg won't have the same issue when shipping to stores.This is definitely a product I would recommend. It's on my grocery list already and I can't wait to introduce it to my next book club.

column9: Something the whole family likes, but has MSG
column10: It's not easy for us to find items that everyone in the family likes.  We have one very picky eater, and another "sort of" picky eater.  One of them never liked Cheez-its ever (the regular kind) but was willing to try one of these. They all liked it!The mozarella flavor is mild, and not overwhelming. It makes for a perfect flavor enhancer to the standard Cheez-It cracker.Only problem is that it is seasoned with MSG (monosodium glutamate). This is something asthmatics are told to avoid, and with three asthmatics in the family, it can't be on our grocery list, unfortunately.We all enjoyed the flavor though, and think most other folks will too.

I like the MOZZARELLA flavored CHEEZ-ITS, but I can't really tell the difference between this flavor and the Cheez-It Baked Snack Crackers, White Cheddar, 13.7-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4) one.These seem to have a saltier flavor than the regular CHEEZ-IT, which is what I like, and there's a slight powdery texture to the squares. Also, they do have a somewhat milder cheese taste than the original. You can eat them with a sandwich or soup, or just out of the box by themselves.And since these are baked, they make a better alternative to chips, a serving size being 25 crackers, which I would estimate to be about one and one-half medium-sized hands full.

I was excited to try these out because I so love the regular ones.  I found that eating them by themselves isn't as good as eating them with a sandwich.  I think the mozzarella cheese is just a bit too strong for me without adding in something else.  The crunch was great as well. I wish Cheez-Its could be made a little less salty though.  Overall, a nice product but I probably wouldn't go out of my way to but this flavor.  The standard flavor still is best to me.
Taste great, though I think I prefer their cheddar for more zing. But mozzarella isn't known for sharpness.Packaging sealed tight for fresh product.

column9: A bit of an acquired taste
column10: I love the taste of Original Cheez-It's and find they make a nice tasty snack. I like the fact that they aren't messy when you eat them - there is no need to wipe your fingers after each piece. Before now I've not tried any other flavors of Cheez-It's and was curious about how the Mozzarella flavored Cheez-It's would taste especially since I like Mozzarella (and Cheez-It's!) I found them to be a bit of an acquired taste - good but not as good as the original flavor. I wasn't sure I'd like them when I tasted the first one, but once I got used to the taste I enjoyed them. The mozzarella flavor is good - subtle and not overwhelming. It is good but in the end I prefer the taste of original Cheez-It's.Mozzarella Flavored Cheez-It's taste good but I'm not sure I'd buy them.

If you're looking for a nice mild flavor in your Cheez-Its, you'll like this flavor.  I liked the smell when I opened the package and liked the taste - these crackers have a nice smooth taste with no weird aftertaste. I don't find the taste to be bland - it's just a very mild and light flavor (which makes it very easy to eat a lot of them in one sitting). I can see munching on these crackers by themselves or when you don't want the cracker to overwhelm other items that you're eating. If they were a bit lower in fat content (7gm for 25 crackers), they'd be perfect.

I enjoy CHEEZ-IT crackers. However, now instead of just the regular cheddar flavor, there are a wide variety of CHEEZ-IT flavors. Recently, I tried the new SUNSHINE CHEEZ-IT MOZZARELLA crackers. Mozzarella doesn't have a very strong taste, but it is distinct and can be tasted on these crackers. Personally, I think there are too many artificial cheddar cheese flavors out there and enjoy snacks that have a cheese flavor other than cheddar. I enjoyed these CHEEZ-IT MOZZARELLA crackers and will buy them in the future instead of the original flavored ones.

column9: Not my favorite Cheez It flavor
column10: I really didn't like these as much as I like the White Cheddar. These have a kind of mild, salty, cardboard kind of flavor. I expected more of a cheese flavor, but it was kind of a fake flavor to me. Now I know that there is not much of a flavor to Mozzarella, so I don't think they should have even tried to duplicate it. On the other hand, my 18 yr. old son thought they were pretty good, but he also likes Burger King and McDonalds too, so there ya go.

column9: Love Cheez-It's! Mozzarella My New Fav!
column10: In our household there is always some variation of Cheez-Its.Our household favorite has been the Cheez-It snack mix.But this mozzarella flavor just replaced that (maybe they will add this flavor to their mix!!?!?!)The flavor to me tastes just like mozzarella cheese, to me it was not a generic flavor.Very smooth flavor and no bitter or weird after taste.

Let me start by saying that I am now a big fan of these snackers. Don't get me wrong, I enjoy original Cheez-Its on occasion as well, but I often find them to be too greasy for me. The Mozzarella Cheez-Its, on the other hand, have a great smooth flavor without the greasy taste. For me, it is a snack for after I've had a hard day and want to relax, or when I really want a little something right before bed that won't weigh me down. I am pretty impressed with these, and will buy them in the future.

column9: It Won't Replace the Cheddar Cheez-it
column10: These are good, but not as good as I'd hoped. My daughter liked them quite a bit. Even better than regular Cheez-Its. She likes the mild mozzarella flavor, and, though, this may not be what Kellogg was going for, she felt that the milder flavor didn't make her breath stink as much as regular Cheez-Its.As for me, I didn't like the initial smell and taste. Kind of...I don't know...sour? Or too sharp or pungent. Once I ate them, the taste was very mild, and not at all like what they smelled like, so, that was a plus. But while these were a nice change, I find I still like Cheddar Cheez-It's best.

I was really looking forward to a nice mozzarella cheese taste. Instead I got a very bland tasting cracker that did not even have a hint of a mozzarella flavor in it. Then I looked at the list of ingredients to see if mozzarella cheese was even listed. It was--but so far down that the amount in these crackers is negligible, and certainly not enough to affect the taste.Bottom line: These crackers do not have an unpleasant taste, just a very bland nondescript taste. These are not something that I would recommend.

I am a serious cheese cracker eater - all brands, all flavors...this is a cheese household. These new Cheez-It Mozzarella flavor crackers are pretty good. They have a faint flavor at first, very light, almost no cheese flavor initially. The after taste as you swallow the crackers packs more of a flavor punch. I could discern the mozzarella flavor and it's very smooth, no bite like with the Cheddar version of Cheez-Its. We'll probably buy these again, but the better flavor is still the original.

Cheez-It Mozzarella has a lighter taste than the regular Cheez-It.  It's pretty good, but it doesn't really remind me of "Mozzarella" as I know it from Pizza and Sting Cheese.It is nothing special, but it is not bad either.  Come to think of it, that is the way I feel about regular Cheez-Its too.When I'm next in the mood for Cheez-Its again, I will probably get the regular version.

There is no doubt that Cheez-It has made some really classic crackers for all to enjoy. They have had a winning formula for the past several generation with great cheddar crackers that seemed timeless. When I heard they were going to make a mozzarella cheese cracker, I was very skeptical, and it didn't feel like anything that seemed like it was anything that extraordinary. I was right. The first taste of the new mozzarella Cheez-It crackers, reminded me of just how much they tasted like the classic Cheez-It crackers, and I was right. These Cheez-It crackers, taste like the classic cheddar taste of the classic crackers they have been known for definitely. In fact, they are actually made with a mixture of white cheddar cheese into the crackers. Not all mozzarella cheese. They taste alright, but not anything that was a wow factor. If you've loved Cheez-It crackers over the years, I suggest you give their new mozzarella cheese a try.Price: C+Taste: C+Overall: C+

These are delicious! I opened the box a little weary, not knowing if these would be good or not, ate one and did not stop eating them until I had made quite a dent in the box. They are so hard to put down! The box says they are creamy and mild and that is a perfect description for these. The cheese flavor is not as strong as the original which can be a nice change.I gave them 4 stars instead of 5 because I believe no matter how good any of these cheez-it flavors are, nothing will beat the original.

column9: Why does it taste so salty?
column10: I was excited when this product came in the mail. I love the original Cheez-it. It is dangerous for me to buy them because my snacking can easily get out of control with them. A 13.7 ounce box of Cheez-It was much bigger than I expected.The little crackers are crunchy and after you chew for a while they taste creamy but then very salty too. I checked the box, it only has 180mg of salt so why does it taste so salty. I checked the salt in the regular Cheez-it and it is 340 mg. I can't figure out. Why does a craker with much less sodium taste saltier than one that doesn't. I have to watch my sodium intake and sure enough, the next day my fingers were swollen and it was difficult to take off my ring.I had my husband taste it too and he thought the crackers tasted salty and sour.Occaisonally, I will brush off the salt all off the top of a cracker and offer it to my cockatiels. They tasted it and spit it out. Wise birds.Also, even though the box was packed with big air pillows, there was a lot crumbling in the last 1/3 of the box. Down there it was mostly crumbs.I would not buy it, I just don't like them.

column9: Mozzarella flavor is interesting, but not my favorite Cheez-Its
column10: Cheez-IT crackers are a great little snack - easy to eat, full of flavor and with a good shelf-life they are easy to keep on hand. Although I'd mostly stuck to the Cheez-It Baked Snack Crackers, Original, 13.7-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4) flavor, a sale at Kroger's Grocery Store last year had me experimenting with some of the other flavors. Although the Cheez It Baby Swiss Crackers, 13.7-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4), Cheez-It Baked Snack Crackers, Duoz, Sharp Cheddar & Parmesan, 13.7-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4), and Cheez-It Baked Snack Crackers, White Cheddar, 13.7-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4) flavors were good, my particular favorites were the Cheez-It Snack Mix, Baked Snack Assortment, 10.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 3) and Cheez-It Baked Snack Crackers, Italian Four Cheese, 13.7-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4) flavors.Now Kellogg's has added a new Mozzarella Cheez-Its flavor, and I couldn't resist trying them. I have to say they aren't bad, but they aren't even close to being my favorite flavor. I think one of my favorite parts of the Cheez-Its experience is the bold flavor in their crackers, and the Mozzarella flavor is a bit too mild to suit me. Like I said, they aren't bad, but I wouldn't say they are great.Of course, something like flavor is a really subjective thing. Other people may prefer the mild flavor of the Mozzarella Cheez-Its to the bolder tastes in their other offerings.In all honesty, after discovering the Italian Four Cheese flavor, no other Cheez-It really comes close for me, with the exception of the Snack Mix, which is really completely different from just a Cheez-It.Do I recommend the Mozzarella Cheez-Its? I think they are an interesting flavor and are worth trying yourself. Everyone's tastes are different, and although I prefer the other flavors, you might very well consider the Mozzarella your own favorite.

I found the Cheez-It Mozzarella Cheese crackers nothing special and just okay in flavor. For me they tasted somewhat sour, with a hint of cheese and the bare whisper of salt. My daughter says she likes them as she liked the crackers as they tasted a bit cheesy and salty.So there you have it: My taste buds were not awed by the flavor while my daughter loved the flavor.Recommend with caveats given.

I have always been a fan of CHEEZ-IT crackers.  The white cheddar has always been my favorite, especially the low fat ones, but these new mozzarella cheese crackers are really tasty too.  My husband likes to take these in his lunch, and he likes the kind with the jalepeno pepper flavor.  This is a great product and a new flavor that most all people enjoy.  Lets face it, if you like pizza, you like mozzarella chees.  We both would highly recommend them.

column9: PASS! - I'll stick with the original
column10: The good thing about a cheese like cheddar is that is packs a lot of flavor in it.  This translates well to secondary products like crackers.  Mozzarella - not so much.  Mozzarella is so mild that when you try to put it into a product like a cracker, it will inherently have a too mild flavor, so you'll need to enhance this somehow.  The easy thing would be to add salt, but Kellogg decided to use spices.  This makes the product taste closer to "Ranch dressing" more than cheese.The product is also marked as "Creamy & Mild".  True enough but just what the heck do they use to make a cracker taste "creamy"???  It is kind of weird to me.I'll stick with the original.

These Mozzarella flavored Cheez-it's are a bit more mild than the White Cheddar ones which are my usual choice. I'm not sure I'd pick out the flavor as a mozzarella cheese, the milder flavor was good, but not distinguishable or immediately identifiable as being like the cheese it's named after. Kind of a creamy aftertaste that reminds me of mozzarella. I think I'll prefer the Cheez-It's with a bit more of a flavor to them. I don't find anything bad or off about this flavor, but to me, there isn't anything special there either.There were a lot of crushed crackers in the box, more so than when I buy them from the store. As a snack, Cheez-It's are a favorite- they just always seem to hit the spot.

The new Cheez-It Mozzarella flavored crackers are great tasting. The crunch was transformed into a creamy cheese flavor as I greedily shoveled them into my mouth. I had to shovel them, because the crackers were broken into crumbs when I received them. This however in no way detracted from the flavor or deterred me from the swift completion of my appointed task. Wait, I think I missed one. Mmmmm

I enjoyed these Mozzarella Cheez-Its, but you can't beat the original. I have tried a number of the new flavored Cheez-Its, & there are some I like better than others. I probably would not buy this flavor again because I think some of the other flavors are better (Swiss or Smoked Cheddar).

I love cheez-Its from the get go but these mozzarella cheese ones are truly scrumptious.  They claim they are creamy...... and they really are creamy tasting.  From the first cracker in your mouth you think 'creamy'.  Sooo DELICIOUS!  There is 180 mg of sodium per each of 13 servings/box at 25 crackers per serving.  They do have 7 grams of fat/serving but no trans fats.  From a diabetic point of view, the 19 grams of carbohydrates and 150 calories/serving is a lot even with zero sugars and 3 grams of protein per serving.  I try to restrict my consumption to one or two serving each time I grab the box for a snack but I have to admit this is really hard to do.  They just taste so darn great!  If I have a complaint, the only one I have is that this product contains monosodium glutamate, MSG.  I am highly allergic to this well known neurotoxin and MUST be very careful with my intake of this dangerous chemical.  It is on the very bottom of the ingredients list so hopefully there is not a hugh amount of it in these crackers.  Since I just ate them, I'll know if there is too much MSG if I develop a headache and lock jaw type symptoms tomorrow.  Makes me wonder WHY put it into this delicious snack in the first place?  I do highly recommend this scrumptious treat if you can tolerate the MSG.  I'll have to limit my intake due to the MSG.

column9: Awesome, can't get them away from the kids!
column10: I always was under the impression that kids would prefer the regular version of Cheez-its, you know, the orange, cheddar kind.  Not so!  These were grabbed so very quickly that the box turned into a blur of red!  They say they're creamy, weird for an ad campaign for crackers, but they're really not kidding!  Creamy mozarella can be sensed throughout these little bursts of flavor, and once again, the kids just go nuts for them.  SO glad we tried these, definitely a "keeper" in this house.  They arrived fresh from amazon, unbroken, and packaged well.  Highly recommend!

My OLD favorite, was the "Original" flavor Cheeze-It, which had a strong cheddar flavor, and lots of crunch.My NEW favorite is the Mozzarella flavor Cheese-it, because it has a true mozzarella cheese taste, as well as that old time crunch that everybody in my family loves.We generally eat the Original flavor as a snack right out of the box, or along with soup (tomato soup, in particular).The Mozzarella flavor as a plain snack, right out of the box, was good, but we still prefer the original, (thus the 4 stars) but I used them in  the following ways as well:--topped a caesar salad with a few crackers (in place of croutons, and that worked great, taste-wise.-- topped off some tomato soup with a few crackers at the dinner table, and that didn't work quite as well, taste wise. --crushed approx. 2/3 cup  of these and used them as a bread crumb coating for a baked chicken breast parmesan, topped with tomato sauce. Very good, since the mozzarella flavor really came through.Nutritionally, and calorically, they are about the same as the original flavor.All in all, I'd say if you like the old, original Cheeze-It flavor, you'll enjoy the new mozzarella flavor too.

First of all, one must keep in mind that the regular flavor Cheez-IT isn't necessarily the best tasting snack food around.  These Mozzarella crackers cleverly offers a combination of acidity and creaminess.  The end result is a pretty good immitation of Mozzarella cheese flavor.  The overall impression is quite positive although the degree of saltiness is also high.  Mozzarella cheese isn't by itself of strong enough flavor so saltiness ends up being part of the overall flavor profile to promote general satisfaction.  I am ok with this product as the flavor is actually less artificial than the standard version Cheez-IT crackers.

column9: Insanely Addictive... and Awesome to Cook With!
column10: Cheez-Its are a guilty pleasure of mine, so I jumped at the chance to try this new flavor. What a flavor it is! Zesty, and really pronounced. Everyone in the house loved it!But getting them shipped to you might not be the best purchasing method, since our box was easily half crumbs. They tasted so good, though, that I didn't want to just toss them out. So I decided to tinker and crushed them up to use in place of Panko bread crumbs when making Parmesan Crusted Chicken breasts. YUM! That was such a success that I decided to use them in place of the bread crumb topping on homemade Mac & Cheese. Another winner!Unfortunately, my local commissary isn't carrying these yet. I'm pestering the manager, though. They're just that good.

I have always been a fan of Cheez-It so I was really excited to try out the new Mozzarella Cheese flavor and I have to say how happy that I have. It definitely has that cheese taste that is all baked into a tiny little cracker, which is one of my favorite qualities of Cheez-It's. But the mozzarella flavor has a smoother and more subtle yet creamier taste then the normal cheddar flavor and I can honestly see myself using this in salads and soups since it would compliment my food better then the normal crackers. But it also satisfies my snack factor so give it a try!

It seems to me that Cheez-It has always gone for bold flavors. These are not that at all. These aren't horrible; they taste like pretty mild-flavored Cheez-Its. I'm not sure exactly what they were going for here in choosing Mozzarella for their newest flavor. Such a mild cheese would be hard to impart into a cracker. And I don't think they've been successful here. While these taste good, they do not taste anything like Mozzarella. The mild taste might be an appeal to some who just want a slightly-cheesy cracker. But I think most Cheez-It fans will be underwhelmed and prefer the bolder flavors Cheez-It is known for.

column9: What does it bring to the table?
column10: I like Cheez-Its. I mean, I reeeaaaaally like them, so I never buy them because I don't actually need to eat any Cheez-Its. Seriously. They are a snack food that does not repay the calorie cost with sufficient nutrition, so I probably only eat them twice a year.But free Cheez-its, sent to me for review? This I had to try.I like crackers and I chowed through a few of these in search of an answer to the only question that matters, which is, do these taste  like mozzarella? Well, if mozzarella were dry, crispy, and charged with a faint chemical aftertaste, then I would say, sure. Kinda. I guess. But no, they do not taste like mozzarella in the way that regular Cheez-its taste like cheddar. I think this is because cheddar at its best is dry, sharp, and a little grainy. Mozzarella doesn't translate well into a cracker, as it's a melting cheese.

I received a cardboard box from Amazon that rattled. They sent the Cheez-ITs with no padding in the box! Upon opening the package, I saw crumbles with a few whole Cheez-ITs.They taste like salt, fat, sugar and mild cheese flavoring. Mozzarella cheese doesn't have much flavor, so it is logical that the Cheez-ITS don't have much flavor. So, why did my husband and I eat the whole box? Because they're salty, crunchy and loaded with fat. They don't taste great but they taste good. However, I think the original Cheez-ITS are superior in taste. I'd buy them over the Mozzarella flavor any day.

It's certainly a fun exercise trying to come up with spin-off products that are as popular or more popular than the original product. Such mainstays as Diet Coke and Honey Nut Cheerios are usually the only ones I can think of before I A.D.D. myself off to another topic.What was I talking about?Oh:  Mozzarella Cheez-Its.  I've been eating Cheez-Its since I was a kid, and it's usually better to not have a box around as it's hard for me to stop eating them.  "White Cheddar" Cheez-Its are, so far, the only spin-off product that I like as much as the original, and these new Mozzarella Cheez-Its come in a close second.  With a similar look and feel to the White Cheddar variety, they do indeed have a slightly more "creamy & mild" (as advertised on the box) taste, but, frankly, aren't too terribly different. The ingredients even show "white cheddar cheese" higher up on the list than mozzarella!No worries, though.  We don't buy this kind of product for its old-school Italiano cheese authenticity, nor, certainly, for its healthful benefits (btw, fat, salt and other bad things are similar to the other Cheez-It varieties). We buy it because we like the way it tastes, and those that like regular Cheez-Its and the White Cheddar variety as their guilty snack cracker pleasure won't be disappointed.

First of all I have to say I have yet to meet a Cheez-It cracker I did not like.The new Mozzarella Cheese flavor is no different. The Sunshine bakers manage to getthe flavor listed on the box into their crackers, and as usual they taste great.These crackers serve me as double duty. First of all as a satisfying snack, and alsoas a replacment when I am out of croutons for a salad. It does not matter whatflavor you use, the crackers are just the right size for salads. Or to float in abowl of tomato soup. The new mozzarella flavor crackers are perfect for this.

column9: I think the box I got was a dud
column10: I received a box of these via the Amazon Vine Program.I'll start by saying that I've always liked Cheez-It crackers, especially partial to the White Cheddar and to the Original.This Mozzarella flavor was not so good and frankly the crackers seemed stale. They were not as crunchy as I expect Cheez-It crackers to be and there were a lot of broken bits - at least 1/4 of the total weight was broken bits and crumbs.I certainly would not buy this flavor.

column9: Yet another flavor for fans of Cheez-IT crackers.
column10: How can you say anything bad about something that tastes so good? I've always had a taste for the "classic" Cheez-ITs, but these are a nice switch. Salty, crispy, cheesy -- doesn't that define one of our basic food groups?

column9: A Candidate for the DEA's Banned Substances List
column10: these new Cheez-Its with the Mozzarella flavor are incredibly addicting.  I went through the entire box in one sitting.  the taste is so much better than the original, bland product.  Highly recommended, only if you are not prone to addiction!

column9: Quite tasty but high in fat content
column10: As is unfortunately the case more often than not, if a food tastes really yummy then it's probably not very good for you. These crackers have a nice, creamy taste to them and they pack 7 grams of fat per serving. Yes, that is fewer grams than potato chips, but for a cracker I think that's pretty high in fat content. The taste, however, is very good and these would make a good snack if consumed in moderation. One concern for me was the state of the crackers I received. I tasted these as part of the Vine program and the box I received was very smashed up and the crackers were partially obliterated. If I were buying these crackers, I would have been upset about their smashed-up condition. Perhaps it would not be a good idea to buy these in bulk until you can verify that shipping of these crackers won't damage the product.

I have only one word to describe how wonderful this product is, and it is FANTABULOUS! I like this better than their other cheese-it product, because it does not have that cheesy taste. I find myself enjoying every bite I take. You won't be disappointed by buying a box of this great product.

column9: Nice addition to the Cheez-It family
column10: I have been eating Cheese Its for over 30 years and I usually stick to the original flavor kind.  I wasn't to keen on a mozzerella flavored chip but I figured someone in the house would eat them.  lol. I was surprised by the flavor of these.  I don't think it truely tastes like mozzerella cheese but I really like the taste of these.  I will be switching back and forth between these and the original flavor everyone has grown up on.  If you like Cheese Its....I suggest you try these because I was pleasantly surprised by the taste.  : )

The flavor of these mozzarella flavored Cheez-Its is more subtle than the regular Cheddar flavor. So if you're looking for a milder flavored cracker, these may be what you've been looking for. They still have the snap and crunch of the original, just a milder taste.

I have always enjoyed these mini bite sized snacks and along comes a new delicious Mozzarella cheese flavor. The box did not last long and was devoured quite quickly by  (the four of us)we already buy one or two boxes a week of Four Cheese and Cheddar Jack and will add this flavor to my list.A quick peek on their web-site reveals several other flavors not carried in our local supermarkets (too bad!)I did take away one star because the snacks were quite broken up but that could have been due to the shipping, however this is a great tasting product, finger licking addictive snack that I will buy again!

These were advertised as a pack of 4, but they were just one big box.  I am not sure getting the from Amazon is the best idea because they were pretty well smashed up by the time we got them.I really like the taste of them, but my wife said she will stick with the original flavor.  I really like them in chili.I will by these  again, but from the grocery store.

column9: My kids liked it, but my wife didn't
column10: I hadn't intended on getting this product through Vine, but I misclicked (hazards of responding to a Vine email on a smartphone). So I had my family taste-test it, as they are bigger fans of cheese than I am. The verdict was that my boys liked it, but my wife didn't like the particular flavor of cheese. When I say my boys liked it, wha tI mean is that's what they said in response to my question. Since then, however, they haven't clamored to have it again, whereas they continue to ask for pistachios for snacks.

column9: And old favorite with a new taste
column10: I have been a fan of Cheez-it crackers since my teen days when I enjoyed the cheddar cheese Cheez-its.  We used to sit in front of the TV with a bowl of Raspberry Apple Sauce and a box of Cheez-its.  Today I just received a new box, this one is Mozzarella Cheez-its, wow these are really a treat.  The flavor is much the same with a little subtle flavor of Mozzarella.Cheez-its, are made with 100% real cheese and you can taste it, the flavor is very fresh and creamy.I do not detect any MSG, although it is in there, and I find that the sour taste that was noted is not (to me) sour but a bit tangy, it gives it the zip you would expect in a nice cheesy snack cracker.  We all have different tastes and I find this one is a winner for mine.I love them.For the health conscious here are the nutritional facts:Serving size: 25 crackersServings per box: 13Total fat 7g  with no trans fatsPoly. Fats 3.5gMonio. Fats. 1.5Cholesterol: 0Sodium 180Total Carbs. 19gSugars 0Protein 3gAll in all I think this is a very nice baked flavorful crispy snack cracker.I am enjoying them very much, and I think you will also.My only problem now is to stop shoveling them into my mouth.Enjoy

column9: Fun flavor, but my wife says she can taste the MSG
column10: Up till now we've only had regular Cheez-It crackers in our home, so we thought the new Mozzarella-flavored crackers would be fun to try. In short: they're a hit. The kids really like them, and I guess that's what matters, as I don't get cheese-flavored crackers for me. The crackers do have a fun, mozzarella-like flavor. Nutritionally they have less Sodium and fat than regular Cheez-It crackers--a nice plus.I'm taking off one star for MSG. It's really down on the ingredients list, but my wife ate some crackers and--without having seen the ingredients list first--said they tasted like they were made with MSG (The regular crackers apparently do not contain MSG). If you're sensitive to the taste of MSG, it may be a bother to you too.

column9: Pretty good, not quite as good as the cheddar
column10: These are pretty similar to regular Cheez-Its, with the exception that they are a white/pale yellow color and they have a slight powdery seasoning sprinkled on them that is supposed to taste like mozzarella.  It actually tastes a little more like the flavoring they put on sour cream potato chips than mozzarella to me, but it's still good.  I do slightly prefer regular Cheez-Its or the white cheddar flavor to this mozzarella flavor, as does my daughter (9 years old).  My wife says she actually likes the mozzarella flavor much more than regular Cheez-Its, so clearly it's a matter of personal preference.

column9: Sunshine's Mozzarella Cheez-It tastes great but there is no way this should be priced over $5 per box
column10: In our household, we often purchase Cheez-It baked snack crackers and we often like to purchase various cheese flavors.My son absolutely loves Cheez-It's and often, we purchase the White Cheddar or original versions, but we noticed there was a new Mozzarella "Creamy & Mild" version that is available and is made with 100% real cheese.And for anyone who loves Mozzarella, the taste of these crackers are flavorful and as our 9-year-old would say "very yummy"!For those who are wondering about the nutrition facts, for 25 crackers, it's about 150 calories, cholesterol is 0mg and 0% and total fat is 11% with saturated fat at 8%.  Ingredients contains wheat, milk and soy.Now, purchasing Cheez-It are typically affordable but surprisingly a four-pack of a 13.7 ounce goes for nearly $30 and for a single box, they cost nearly $12.  For me, that is just insane...unless it's specially imported from Italy or if it was some huge family-sized package as big as family-sized cereal box, I can easily see how $12 is justified but for this small 13.7 ounce version to cost around $12 and a 4-pack for $30 just doesn't make sense (I am assuming that these third party sellers are factoring in huge shipping costs).JUDGMENT CALL:Sunshine's Cheez-It's are delicious and like other various flavors, next to our favorite of White Cheddar, Mozzarrella "Creamy & Mild" is going to be the version we will most likely purchase... but as long as you can purchase Cheez-It's for under $5, it's hard to justify these being sold for $12 or $30 for four 13.7 oz. boxes, these are costing more than Crunchmasters and other crackers that are sold at Trader Joes and even speciality crackers that I have purchased in Tokyo.Overall, Sunshine's Mozzarella Cheez-It's are wonderful!  Too bad I can't say so much about the price!

opened the shipping box right away. Noticed it was slightly crushed on the top. No packing to protect the box of crackers. About 1/3 were crushed. Sad about that.Love the flavor though. They taste a little different than the white cheddar which I also love. Great mild and creamy taste. I noticed one of the other reviewers suggested to put them in salads and soups. Will save the broken ones for that. Nice idea.Thanks for another great product. Will buy them and also try some of the other new flavors.

I didn't think these would have such a sour flavor. The first bite of one was fine, but after eating three or four, I couldn't handle how sour they are. My kids (5 and 2) really seem to enjoy them though. They're both asking for more. I also had a little bit of a strange feel in my mouth after eating them and a strong after taste. I guess they're not bad for a quick snack for the boys, but I won't be eating any more.

I had my doubts about a single serving cake bowl but this is the most ingenious dessert idea for people on the go. It is awsome because it is so easy to make. You just need a microwave. I bring them to work for a quick and hot sweet treat. But the greatest thing is that you don't have to worry about finishing off an entire pan of brownies. Just one satisfies my sweet tooth and I don't have all of the guilt from overeating. Unless of course you keep a cabinet full of these bowls...

This product is not only delicious-yummmmmmy! but it is so convenient and easy to prepare.  The different varieties are a delight also.  The Caramel cake and the others get a 5* rating.  I definetly will buy them again.

column9: Good for an individual hot serving
column10: I wasn't sure what to expect from this product.  It has a lot of packaging and I suspect one could do this basic thing at home with a box of cake mix and a jar of ice cream topping; but still, this is rather cool.All you do is open the package, put the powder in the bowl, add 1/4 cup water and mix it, and squeeze the sauce packet on top.  Put in microwave for 1 minute and 15 seconds.  That's it.  I have been adding nuts to mine before cooking and that works great.  What results is basic chocolate cake with a mild caramel sauce squiggled on it.  The warmth factor is what makes this so appealing; it really seems to add a nice and satisfying quality to it.  Also, while it's definitely sweet, it isn't as sweet as I was worried it would be.  You could choose to use less of the caramel sauce if you wanted, of course, or add other ingredients like I do; I'm going to try coconut and berries, but just a few nuts is really great.I don't think I would buy this again simply because I feel like the packaging is overkill and I do want to try replicating this process with a plain box of cake mix.  But it does taste good, and it works effectively and quickly.

I fell in love with these wonderful hot caramel-ly chocolate desserts the first time I ever made them. However, my local stores only carry this flavor in the mini size. Waaay too small to enjoy, so I was thrilled to find them on Amazon! They are yummy, yummy, yummy!!!

These are perfect to keep on the pantry for when you want something chocolate but don't want to bake larger tempting treats that stay around for days.  These always come out great.  Take a little time to play with how many seconds to microwave it.  I like mine a little runny in the middle and 1:06 is the key number for me.
These are a nice treat, but are very sweet.  One for just me is a lot to handle.  By the end of it, I am sick with sweet.That said, not bad for a microwave cake.

column9: Satisfies a craving but not the greatest...
column10: Both the cake and the caramel had a boxed, fake flavor.  We tried the lemon ones and thought they were awesome...this one not so much.  I think we still have one out in the garage a month later and I have several sugar-loving teenagers living here.  Unless you get this for $1 a piece like I did...I don't recommend.

My husband and I enjoy these cakes very much. If I make an entire cake mix or batch of cupcakes it never fails that 1/4 of it goes to waste since it is just the 2 of us. My husband was watching Ace of Cakes one night and then wanted cake, so I made one of these and in about a minute we were sharing the cake...no waste! I pick them up on sale and keep a couple in the pantry. The lemon cake is excellent too.

I have tried microwave cakes in the past and was always disappointed at the texture and consistancy of the end result, but not this time. The cake is almost as good as if you baked it in the oven only much quicker and easier. All you have to do is add water to the mix, stir together, squeeze the carmel from the packet onto the cake and put it in the microwave for approx. 1 min. and 15 seconds and you have a decent cake without the trouble, time and mess of making a full size cake mix.Try it, you'll be glad you did.
I would not buy them again, but if you are desperate for a dessert and don't have anything else prepared, it would probably satisfy your cravings.  Don't plan to serve it to guests though.

The Pelindaba organic lavender Rooibos tea is a delicious caffein free tea. It is a natural source of health promoting minerals,  has a high level of antioxidants AND it is low in tannins. If you have not tried Rooibos (South African "red bush") I suggest you try this tea. The hint of lavender infusion is delightful. You can also make a wash of the tea for acne problems.

column9: High Quality Cat Food- can't beat $26+Free Shipping!
column10: PROS:- High Quality Nutritious Cat food, Easily Digestable= less litterbox waste  Helps with Urinary & Constipation/Bowel/Allergy Related Issues, Human Grade Ingredients, Non Allergenic, No Fillers, Good Flavors- even for finicky cats. So even though it's a bit more to pay up front, it actually saves $$ in the long run in the form of healthier cats (most important), less food eaten & less litter used.CONS: Definitely a bit expensive but I bought it for $25.97 w/ Free Shipping through Petco on Amazon.com so I felt that was a very good value!! I will stock up when it is at that price for sure!TIP:- I actually WET THIS FOOD DOWN quite a bit, to a thick spaghetti sauce consistency. It's actually better for the cats b/c it increases their water intake which they desperately need since their thirst drive is so low. The food is highly nutritious & easily digestable, therefore helping stomach & bowel ailments improve. I  also have a cat w/ chronic acid reflux disease & one prone to urinary crystals & this helps keep those conditions under control. Also my sister's cat who was always snorty & snotty w/ allergies got completely better after being on this food, I believe due to no grain being used in this product. Just think how it will act on a cat's stomach! A lot of low quality cheap foods will just sit in the cat's stomach, not absorbing any nutrients into the body & then it just comes out as smelly poop!  Also, because they are getting less nutrients, the cats will EAT MORE therefore costing more $ in food, more litterbox waste cuz it goes right through them. I used to buy Science Diet thinking it was good for my pets but the ingredients are not species appropriate or high quality AT ALL. Veterinarians are generally extremely undereducated in animal nutrition, and they generally tout the food from the company that sponsors their schooling or otherwise they have a vested financial interest in. After having my cats be on medicines & "special vet diets" that did little to help, I switched to high quality cat foods, Wellness being one of them and my cats are thriving and some of them have gone off their meds completely. I HIGHLY recommended the Wellness brand, I have seen a HUGE difference in my own cats as well as the cats I rescue. PLEASE, PLEASE EDUCATE YOURSELF ON WHAT IS REALLY IN MOST PET FOOD AND YOU WILL SEE WHY WELLNESS IS AN EXCELLENT CHOICE.

column9: Fantastic Food for Good Cat Health
column10: The pet food industry can be one of the most infuriating as you start doing research and discovering what trash manufacturers (and the vets who get paid off by the manufacturers) push onto the unsuspecting public. For reference, don't ask your vet - do some Internet research at sites like, for example, [...]. What you'll find is that even the supposed "high-end" lines from basically every major supermarket label are horrible for your fuzzy friends. People who trust the marketing or trust their vets overpay and feed their cats foods that are full of carcinogens, cheap ingredients that are inappropriate for a cat's digestive system, and byproducts that provide nothing of value and are basically a way to make cheap profit off of literal garbage. It's a tragedy, as these same cats end up with shorter lifespans, kidney problems, UTIs, cancer, and a host of other issues, all of which could have been avoided by a high quality food.This is an A-Grade food. What you'll find here is very high protein content, many meats high on the list, flaxseed, good vitamins and antioxidants, and no grains, which is great as a cat is not an omnivore, it's a carnivore, and it simply does not need grains.What you will NOT find here is the kind of junk you'll see in things like Purina One and Science Diet - byproducts (aka beaks, feathers, bird feet), brewers rice (aka the waste product from making beer), wheat flour (a leading cause of pet allergies), corn gluten (a cheap waste of space), and things like "liver flavor" (because they don't want to pay for the real thing). I didn't just pull those ingredients out of the air - I was reading the ingredients list of Purina One. It's pathetic.Don't feed your cats trash. Pay a little more to feed them good food now, and they'll lead longer, healthier, more satisfied lives as a result. It's worth it.

My nine cats love Wellness Turkey and Salmon canned cat food. It is so moist and I feel like I am giving them something that is good for them. (one has had a UTI problem). I feel that the natural ingredients in it will be good for all of them and hopefully avoid any more UTI attacks. They love the taste. I haven't been using it that long, but I would recommend it to other cat owners.

column9: Excellent nutrition, well liked cat food.
column10: I switched to this cat food after our eldest cat was diagnosed with diabetes and required a change in diet to maintain his health. We got a serious crash course in cat nutrition and realized that cats should be fed this stuff all the time, not just when they're sick.This product is very low carbohydrate and high animal protein; perfect for a cat's required nutrient needs. I enjoy buying the Wellness brand as they hold high standards for what they put in their products and I feel comfortable supporting their company with my purchase.This can will last three days in a house with three cats. We feed this as a snack, more than a meal, but everyone seems satisfied with their share. All the cats are also fed dry food during the day, so if you only feed wet food this will not last you as long.

This is not exactly a small detail, just tell me what I am buying. HOW MANY CANS COME WITH THIS ORDER?!?!?! I don't care about the 'rainbow of veggies', I can look at the label myself. This is good stuff and my cats love it, but I'd like to know what I'm ordering....might as well get it from the store so I know what I'm getting.

column9: Seemed like a good food but caused urinary crystals twice
column10: I fed this flavor to my cat for over two and a half years (as a kitten he ate grain-free Innova), almost exclusively wet food. If he got hungry later I'd give him a tiny sprinkle of Wellness dry (salmon), but twice a day he got this food. He developed urinary crystals TWICE even though the food says it's designed to prevent this problem.I was a big believer in healthy, grain-free, wet food, "natural" cat food diets. Even when I was unemployed for a year, my cat continued to eat Wellness while I ate instant noodles. It was fine, I thought I was feeding him the best and pre-emptively striking against any preventable health problems. Well, he got urinary crystals on one occasion; I brought him to the vet, $1,000 later and he seemed fine. The vet cautioned me against returning to the same diet but I somehow thought it would be okay and that the diet wasn't to blame. Well, it was. A few months later he got the same problem.
