Another $1,000 later and boarding for four days, my vet (whom I've trusted with all my pets, dearly, for many years) told me that (1) the "natural pet food craze" was overblown and ridiculous, that he's fed a leading brand of standard grocery store cat food and has had cats live beyond 19 years; (2) the diet was the cause of my cat's troubles, and I had to change it.Well, now he's on prescription food that's even more expensive than the fancy stuff but with seemingly far less high-quality ingredients. But he hasn't had the problem come back, and from what I can tell, he's got the same energy levels and healthy coat as before, just minus the urinary troubles. The stray cats my family and I feed (six others) all get the junky grocery stuff like Friskies, Fancy Feast, and Purina, and they have never needed to go to the hospital. I know diet isn't the only factor but it is certainly the major one. I would rather have my cat eating food that doesn't send him to the hospital with a life-threatening condition, than one that makes me feel good about its "naturalness." Mind you, urinary crystals are severely painful and will kill your cat if not treated within hours. This food might work for many owners but I'm not taking the risk again.

My two kitties love this stuff and buying it by the case makes the cost reasonable to feed high quality food.My older girl sometimes needs it heated in the microwave or some extra water added so that she can eat it.  I also sometimes add a few pieces of kibble to the mix to give her more traction to lick it up.  This would happen with any wet food.I gave 4 stars because my latest purchase had many dented cans.  I hope this isn't a trend on amazon's part, but I thought it warranted noting.

My cats love this product, but this is the first time I ordered it online.  The Petco website was giving me error messages, so I went through Amazon.com.  It was shipped within a couple days of my order and arrived 5 days earlier than projected.  Excellent service!

column9: Wellness is the best I've found
column10: First, let me say that I watched my previous two cats die early on a diet of dry cat food - one from diabetes, one from kidney failure. I decided to do a lot of research I came to the conclusion that dry cat food keeps a cat in a constant state of dehydration. I own a pet sitting business and have displeased many cat owners with this information - feed only dry food and you can't get them enough water to prevent UTI, kidney/liver damage, diabetes and pre-mature death.I have raised my next cats on a diet of Wellness grain-free canned and the results have been amazing in all areas - their coat, their weight, their energy and their overall health. There is one caveat:  A diet of the best wet cat food doesn't do much to keep their teeth clean. I recommend a tablespoon of a dry dental food each day to combat tartar.

column9: Good deal, but not the same product
column10: We bought this because we have two cats and were trying to save some money.  Problem is, this is not the same as the 5.5 oz cans - this stuff is much more wet.  The cats didn't like it.  It is almost soupy.  We tried four of the cans and they were all the same.  We ended up taking it back to a Petco store and there was no problem with the return.  Otherwise we love the Wellness cat food OUR cats just don't like the consistency of the large cans.

column9: wellness adout turkey and salmon cat food
column10: The best cat food out there for your cat. A little more expensive than most, but the best. Cats seem to enjoy this food.

column9: My cat does not like this flavor
column10: My cat loves other flavors, but not this one. I don't know why.  My daughter says her cats won't eat this flavor either.

Don't bother try any others.  This one is tops!  My dog doesn't gobble it up in 30 seconds nor lose interest in it after 5 minutes because it loses taste.  Busy chews last about five to ten minutes of total enjoyment!  Only wish I could get the bigger 9 oz boxes and find them at grocery store.  There are about 15 chews in each of this size box.

Prior purchases were darker and had a lot more flavor.  My two Shih Tzu's just chewed on them for hours.  This purchase was bland and had no flavor.  Appears manufacturer was saving money by providing less color and flavor.  The final test was when the dogs looked, smelled and walked away.  Opened several more but the test was the same.

We have tried several different "chewables" for our dog, and we have found that she either eats them too quickly, or loses interest (as another reviewer mentioned). We tried her ont he Purina Chewnola, but she just started chewing off the granola layer and then hiding the rawhide part under furniture!With the heartyhides, she has YET to not finish one in a sitting, and will happily trot off with one in her mouth to work on for 10 minutes or so. Such a great treat to keep her busy, and it's basted in chicken flavor so that tail keeps wagging!Definitely recommended!

column9: Great for lunch boxes or snacks at the pool
column10: I bought these for the kids to eat whilst on their summer vacation.  They are ideal for putting in lunch boxes and taking along as snacks.  Ideal for playdates too as the chocolate in the chips isn't messy.

Our entire family enjoy the gripz chips deluxe.  It is a good size snack bag that can easily be split between two toddlers.  They have a nice crunchy texture and right amount of sweetness without being too hard or too sugary tasting.  Even in warm weather we haven't had these get messy.  These should still be considered a treat, the packets are .9 ounces (25g), 120 calories and 5g fat.
These are incredibly delicious! I just tried them for the first time and I am very impressed. They make an awesome snack.
I really love Daifuku, but I didn't know where I could get it nearby, so I ordered it online. The service is really efficient, and I got my order within a few days.

I wasn't sure what to expect.  They're a little like gummy cakes.  The flavor is very good.  They make a good addition to an a meal as a dessert especially when you want something on the lighter side.  They're not too sweet either.
I bought these and they were not the smarties brand, they actually do not say smarties anywhere on the box or the wrappers. Do not buy they are gross and not the real product they describe.

Dingo EZ Mini Bones are easy on my 12 year old Maltese's mouth and teeth.  He begs for one every night at 8:30-9:00 and eats the whole thing.  With regular Dingo mini bones he leaves half of the bone and they take a day or two and sometimes cause his mouth to bleed.  Max does not beg for them.  We used to buy these at Walmart but they no longer carry them and we could not find them locally so Amazon is the way to go for these.
Pops nice but can never get it to taste like movie theater popcorn. Doesn't even come close. Gave it a 2 star for popping not taste.
We've been using this in the popper at the office and I liked it enough to buy a jug for home too.

The school where I work has a "popcorn day" one Friday per month.  The popcorn is popped in a theater-type popper.  They use the Act II Buttery flavored oil and the Act II butter flavored salt.  I don't know how others who gave such poor reviews are popping their corn, but our popcorn is fabulous!  It is a huge hit at school, both with the kids and the adult staff.  We have families who buy enough for every member of the family for a movie and popcorn night.  Maybe others are not measuring it correctly, or are not using the right popper.  I don't know.  All I can say is I love this stuff!!  I smell it being popped all day and can't wait to eat it!!  It takes all my willpower to keep from eating a bag of it for lunch!If you use the Act II salt with the oil, be careful not to use too much of the salt.  It seems to be concentrated.  It doesn't take as much as you might think.If I could have these people send me their supply that they obviously don't know how to use, I'd be in heaven!I'm buying myself a theater-style popper for Christmas, just so I can have this popcorn more often than once a month!
This product has absolutely no taste whatsoever.  Makes the popcorn greasy and that's about it. Would rate it zero stars if I could.
The word "buttery" on the label is as close as this gets to flavoring popcorn. It is orange and gelatinous when cold. It heats up well and pops the corn nicely, but adds no discernable flavor.

I love popcorn, and this product is good except for the fact that it does not and will not give you the taste that you are looking for that you get from movie theaters. Even with the matching seasoning salt, it doesn't do the justice. But its ok,just not buttery at all.
Great popping oil.  The best.  I've used this for a years.  No other popcorn oil beats this. I would highly recommend.

I am not a tea connoisseur. I just started drinking herbalteas about a month ago. However, since then I have tried many and this is one of my favorite. At first I did not like the medicinal smell. But, the tea taste great. It is a spicy cinnamon licorice flavor, more than sarsaparilla. If you don't like anise(black licorice)taste, do not buy this tea. Instead try the Yogi tea Cocoa Spice. It is sweet and delicious. It's my favorite. The reason I drink Detox is because it does seem to have some detoxing benefits. Also, I feel extremely relaxed after drinking this tea. It really calms me, without making me tired. I am not sure what herb is doing this...but it is almost as good as a glass of wine! So far, I like Yogi tea better than any I have tried. It is worth the extra cost for a great tea.

The taste of this tea will take some getting used to - it's a bit peppery and warm, and you can taste a tiny bit of licorice in it. Sounds disgusting, I know, but it isn't bad - just...odd. I've heard that it helps with recovery from colds and mild illnesses, though I haven't tried it for that purpose myself. As for the "detox" effects, they're extremely mild and you likely won't notice any physical difference (except for increased energy, perhaps).

column9: So good. The next best thing to thin mints
column10: I put these in the freezer and they taste just like the girls scoots  thin mints. Their cheap and you can by they all year round.
Worked great in the cotton candy machine our 30 something kids got as their "toy" for Christmas.  It fluffed up immediately and tasted terrific.

column9: Not recommended by the manufacturer but works anyway!
column10: Although Sugar Floss is not recommended for use in the Nostalgia Electrics Hard Candy/Sugar free Cotton Candy machine, we didn't find out until both were already purchased. We tried using it anyway, and if you let the machine heat up well before using it, it will make delicious amusement park style cotton candy. We used one teaspoon at a time, so the sugar will last us years, but it is yummy!
THE KIDS LUV IT!!! THE KIDS MAKE COTTON CANDY WHEN THERE FRIENDS COME OVER AND ITS FAST AND EZ GREAT BUY!!!

I love the 34 degree cracked peppercorn, wheat, and other varieties so I thought I would try the caramel, cinnamon, and graham as an alternative to cookies or regular graham crackers. True - you can have a lot of these crackers for little calories/carbs, but the flavor is bland. In terms of satisfaction, they don't quite cut it for me as a snack unless I put peanut butter or something on them. They would probably be good as part of a fruit and cheese dessert platter, along with some peanut butter, fruit spread, honey, or cream cheese.

column4: evilalita "I'm sciencing as fast as I can!"
column10: The crackers were VERY DELICIOUS.  I have tried all of the savory 34 degrees cracker flavors and Rosemary is the best--hands down.  This caramel flavor is tasty.  I don't know how they do it--it is thin and flaky in texture like a thin rice cracker, but it tastes like creamy caramel.  The only reason this didn't get 5 stars was how it arrived--most of the cookies in the box were crumbled, which would probably make a good ice cream topping.  Still, I would have preferred if they arrived intact.
Thank you for the chocolate covered Pomegranate seeds.  Not only are they delicious, but they are the REAL thing (containing ONLY Pomegranate seeds).  Delivery was exactly as mentioned.
Dark chocolate and pomegranate seeds. Exactly what I was looking for. I heard both are good for you so together makes a perfect snack. Very good.

This is the best cat food that I've found. It's made of whole chunks (not that yucky pate style), so that you actually can SEE what's in it! Our cat LOVES it. It has pretty much what it says in the title - there is no 'hidden' beef in every can, unless it says so on the front (we don't feed beef, only seafood or poultry, which are more natural to animals this size, and in protest to the treatment of cows). There is also a full list of vitamins and minerals (meets the AAFCO requirements). Overall, THIS IS IT! :)

I opened a can of this for my cats dinner and was totally disgusted.  I expected big chunks of sardines with shrimp and crab like the label says.  What I got was some sardines in a thick jelly with one shrimp.  I did not see any crab meat at all.  One cat ate most of it and one would have very little to do with it.  Not worth keeping at all.  This will go in the trash.
This cat food was not appealing in texture or smell to my cats.Ended up giving it to our outdoor cats! would not recommend

I have 3 indoor cats and 2 of them liked it, the other one wouldn't even taste it. The 2 outdoor cats eat anything I feed them. Of course it's mostly sardine but you can see the crab meat and bits of shrimp. This flavor does have a strong scent, likely the reason the one cat wouldn't try it. Still you are getting a lot of meat as the filler is only a small amount of a gelatin substance to hold it all together. All of my cats like the other flavors of this brand so I may stick w/ the flavors that do not contain sardines. I still think this brand is a great value compared w/ the ingredients in other canned cat food.

column9: It's hydrogenated and is best avoided
column10: In principle I like lard.  It's rich in mono-unsaturated fat, and the dangers of saturated fat have been greatly overstated and over-hyped -- it may not in fact be harmful at all.  This comes in a neat, tidy package and doesn't need refrigeration, but the problem is that it's been hydrogenated in order to have a nice, firm, even consistency, and hydrogenation can't help but add some trans-fats -- something nobody should be eating at all (barring a few found naturally in fat from ruminant animals, which are very different in structure from those found in hydrogenated fats, and seem to be beneficial to eat).I suspect that the levels of trans-fats here aren't way high -- the hydrogenation is probably just enough to make a firm, consistent product -- but I'd rather avoid them entirely.

This lard is the BEST lard that you could EVER... wait... hold on a second... you can write up a review for lard?  Wow.  Really?  Isn't that kind of weird?  I mean... it's lard.  Internet lard.  What else do you really want to know?  Okay, fine, how about... probably you should avoid eating it directly from the package.  There.  Review for lard completed.  Have a nice day.

column4: Heather L. Parisi "Robert and Heather Parisi"
column9: NOWHERE ON DIAL OR ARMOUR'S WEBSITE CAN YOU FIND THAT THEY MAKE THIS STUFF!
column10: IN A NUTSHELL: FEW NATURAL FOODS COULD BE WORSE FOR YOU THAN LARD!WHAT IS WORSE?  --- Hydrogenated LARD, which is loaded with TRANS FATTY ACIDS - CHOLESTEROL - SATURATED FAT - AGRICULTURAL CHEMICALS - HORMONES ETC. AND that's what this product is.SOME INTERESTING STUFF: WHERE IS THE LARD ON THEIR WEBSITE?Dial, the soap people, own Armour, and Armour makes this Hydrogenated, "All Natural" Lard. However, though Armour owns up to making many less than healthy edibles, on their website, there is NO mention of Lard as one of their many products.If you have to use Lard, this is a long established brand that resturants use, and though "hydrogenated", this is a good product as hydrogenated Lard goes.Nevertheless, I wince when I leave a resturant, and while walking through their parking lot find myself staring at huge tubs of empty lard containers lying around the dumpsters. Funny, but I'd swear they weren't there before I ate.BOTTOM LINE:This is not just lard, but Hydrogenated Lard, which should be stricken from the human diet if at all possible. If that is not possible, Armour has been a reliable brand that has been making lard forever, though they don't want to admit it apparently [WONDER WHY?].It does, however, make me wonder what is in Dial soap?![I AM NOT AFFILIATED WITH ANY PRODUCT OR COMPANY]

column4: Mr. T. Keeling "Timmy the Tiger Thompson"
column9: GOD BLESS LARD, AND GOD BLESS YOU MY CHILDREN
column10: Amazing lard, how sweet the taste,That saved a wretch like me....I once was thin but now am fat,Was fit, but now, I slouch.T'was lard that taught...my heart to fear.And lard, my stomach recieved.How precious did that lard appear...the hour I first consumed.Through many dangers, toils and snares...we have already come.T'was lard that brought us safe thus far...and lard will lead us home.The Lord has promised good to me...His word my hope secures.He will my shield and portion be...as long as lard endures.When we've been here ten thousand years...bright shining as the sun.We've no less days to sing lard's praise...then when we've first begun."Amazing Lard, how sweet the taste,That saved a wretch like me....I once was thin but now am fat,Was fit, but now, I slouch.

This is my favorite flavor of the Ike and Mike.  Mmmmm Lemonade . Great stuff, but watch out! It will pull the fillings right out of your head!  And let's face it... if this stuff is a favorite meal, you've got plenty of  fillings. But hey, that makes it an adventure just to eat 'em. Try micro-waving them for about 5 seconds or so and they are softer and a little less chewy. The order arrived in a flash to my door step and ordering was easy.
I ordered this candy for my grandson, we were unable to find it in any store, he swears that this is the best candy ever made.

I bought some of these in PA;  not available in my state yet, however i will get them as soon as available.  Much tastier than the usual grocery store chips; a little more salt than i usually like, but that is a matter of taste. It's a winner.

column9: At $4.96 best deal on a great product
column10: If you can get $49 worth of products and free shipping from Vitacost, this costs you about $1.53 per lb, which is a terrific deal. Be aware that Vitacost won't let you know if the item is back ordered; you'll have to call and ask if your order arrives short. This can go in your freezer for several months so buy in bulk when you can!It's a great product for GF baking (try Elizabeth Barbone's baking book for easy and tasty recipes) and less costly to use than a GF mix. It's a bit grainy, which is actually a plus in some cookies. I made Ginger Snaps from the above book with it and they were great. Any cookie leftovers (yeah, right!) can be used to make crusts for cream pies and cheesecakes.I haven't noticed any grainy texture in finished baked items like muffins. The graininess actually makes it a favorite in my homemade GF breading mix, adding a nice dimension to fried and baked breaded chicken, cube steaks, etc. Add a little grated strong cheese to your rice flour breading for a flavor boost.

I normally drink the starbucks brand of bottled coffee so my comparison is based off that. The Illy isn't as sweet as starbucks and for me that was the only drawback. I found the strength to be just perfect and the flavor was pretty good as well. If it was only a little bit sweeter then it would have been perfect but I like my coffee sweet. It should be a dessert really.

I really wanted to love Illy Issimo caffe expresso style drink.  However, I simply did not.  The expresso used in the product is strong, but still does not have the richness of an expresso received fresh at a cafe. The smell of the expresso is overwhelming.  I also did not like the taste of this expresso.I guess it is a good product if you want expresso, but cannot leave your home or office.  It is only 50 calories per cup, so it is excellent for dieters. Hoever, I will not drink this product ever again.

Coffee drinkers tastes are wide and varied, like all coffee drinkers, I like my coffee a certain way, strong, black, with a touch a sweetness. This canned coffee drink is strong, black, but too sweet for me. I liked that it was more like coffee rather than a cream drink with some coffee mixed in, but the sweetness of it killed it for me. It wasn't terrible to the point of "I can't drink this" but it also wasn't so good that I would go out and buy it. I do love iced coffee though and I would consider buying an unsweetened version. I never let the coffee shop put the sweetener in my coffee, I want to do it myself to my taste and feel the same with a bottled or canned coffee such as this. I could tell there was a good expresso coffee flavor to this drink and would definitely like to try a plain version I could make to my own taste.

I came home from a hot morning in the Arizona sun and opened my illy issimo coffee drink nice and cold from the fridge. I found the expresso taste strong but refreshing and the amount of sweetness just right. Great Product.

This is a great pre-made and sweetened iced coffee.  Not bitter, no metallic aftertaste from the can, and not too sweet, though it is very strong as an espresso based drink should be.My wife poured her share into a glass and added a splash of creamer and that was also very good.Summary: Recommended as a quality iced coffee perfect for those hot summer days.

column9: I thought it was perfect - a little sweet without being too sweet
column10: I drank this cold and could not be more pleased. The coffee was high quality arabica - I always notice when coffee is arabica or robusta. It was sweet without being too sweet - how'd they do that? I mean, you can't compare this to the major bottled coffee brand for that reason alone. You can keep this in the fridge at work and offer it to people without looking like you're pushing calories along with caffeine.For a long time, I'd stock highly sweetened coffee beverages in the fridge at work.  Then I noticed that people stopped consuming them, and it happened around the same time that I lost interest in that level of sweetness.  I recommend this drink for those that prefer a lower level of sugar and for old school arabica coffee types.

column9: Woah - now this is coffee drink tastes like coffee
column10: And if that's what you're looking for then this should be your cup of... coffee. Seriously, this can only contains four ingredients: coffee, sugar, potassium bicarbonate and potassium citrate. I don't know what those last two are, but I can tell you that there's plenty of coffee in here and only a dash of sugar. Unlike other iced coffee drinks in a can that I've had this one is hardly sweetened and definitely doesn't have any cream in it. The label describes it as an "espresso style coffee drink" and they're not messing around. I had trouble getting this down because I like a lot of cream and sugar in my coffee, but if you like your coffee black this is the can you've been looking for.

column9: illy issimo - Caffe In A Can!
column10: I have tried different illy brand products and have always enjoyed their products. The new illy brand "issimo" line which translates loosely to "extremely" or "remarkably" pretty much lives up to it's moniker. At 6.8 oz. and only 45 calories, it is a nice pick me up in the AM. I only enjoy cold coffee products in the summertime when it's hot so I wouldn't be a year round drinker of issimo but I liked the flavor and especially the sweetness of the product. It isn't at all sweet, thick and doesn't have an overly "canned" quality to it which I found nice. I still preferred the cann cappucinno over the caffe, however.  Issimo is a light product that doesn't leave you feeling bloated or heavy. At just under $2.00 a can, it's not the cheapest coffee beverage out there but it's certainly more cost effective than your local, upscale coffee shop.

Although it has a bit of added sugar, this canned espresso is quite bitter. I tried it over ice and it definitely gave me that espresso jolt. Not as good as a fresh-brewed iced espresso -- even one from Starbucks -- but a decent substitute if you're in a hurry and need that coffee hit.

I love my coffee--in any way shape or form. I especially love to add espresso shots to a regular cup of coffee. But one thing I've never done is have espresso over ice.This product had sugar added (beet sugar) so it is NOT made for purists and a web search did not give me the info I wanted as to how much caffeine this product has.What it does have is an excellent flavor that was unexpected from a canned product and a convenience that I find gratifying.Take the warning on the back of the can seriously--do NOT shake this product before using, it actually isn't necessary (I shook it a little to see why there was a warning and it frothed all over the place when I opened it).- if you don't have issues other than not wanting milk in your iced espresso have no fear, if there was milk in it I couldn't tell.Delicious, flavorful, not overly bitter -just enough to give a kick, convenient.I will definitely buy more of this product! At a 1.92 per nearly a 7oz can - and with a 20% off coupon when you buy from Amazon, this is a pretty good deal for the convenience of it all!

Not the greatest canned coffee ever made...it had a very bitter taste to it to me.  I wasnt' thrilled at the amount of "in your face" flavor it had, even for an espresso style drink.  I guess I would rather have had that hot vs. cold.  At only 50 calories a can, it can be used as a pick me up on a hot day and you'll be going until nightime ;)Much preferred the "flavored" variety, but if you like Italian blend, espresso style coffee, it's worth trying.

This coffee was delicious! When I got it out of the fridge I had the urge to shake it as with other canned coffees, but this one says to not shake it so I just popped it open and took a delicious sip. The can is the perfect size and was very portable. The coffee had a sharp taste to it that really gave me a jolt of energy. I will be stocking these in my fridge from now on. Well worth the cost for the convenience and taste.

The illy issimo Coffee Drink is simple and delicious.  The taste is bold and flavorful, although perhaps not as strong as Starbucks.  Note that the Caffè drink comes in sugar-free (unsweetened) for those on low-carb diets, but the "Beet" sweetener in here is medium, not too sugary, and does not overpower the drink.

Obvious yes, given that this is an 'Italian Espresso'style coffee drink."It isn't too bad!"  VERY high praise from my husband, seeing as he doesn't even like coffee.But I do, and while this had a richer flavor than I was expecting, I am not a huge fan of the aftertaste.I am no espresso connoisseur, in fact that only espresso I have ever had is Starbucks, so I don't have a whole lot to compare it to, but I do like strong coffee.  A slightly bitter taste is actually something I enjoy, as opposed to overly sweetened coffee that seem to be the rage.  This little can (6.8 FL OZ) certainly has that.  It has a surprisingly bitter taste with just the right amount of sweetness.  At 50 calories a can, it's relatively diet friendly too.But there, at least for me, was something of a strange film in my mouth.  Not a big deal, but at almost $2 per can ($22.93 for 12) I expect to like it much more than I did.  If I was running errands and really wanted some iced coffee, I might consider this, but at home I will stick with my own brew.

column9: Surprised to find good coffee in a can!!
column10: As a devout drinker of good, fresh roasted/ground/drip brewed, strong coffee, I approached this can of ILLYissimo espresso with much skepticism and profoundly low expectations. The experience of drinking it caught me by complete surprise as it is entirely acceptable as a cold/cool glass of coffee on the run!Described by another reviewer as "muddy water in a can", I can only infer that strong coffee is not to that person's liking. This IS a strong formulation and does not suffer from the burnt taste or bitter aftertaste that many other canned coffee beverages have. It is sweetened, but mildly so and used beet sugar to do this.  Too many other canned coffee beverages are overly sweetened thereby destroying any vestige of honest coffee flavor.Made in Denmark and distributed by Coca-Cola, it is a pleasure to find an alternative to either sickeningly sweet or simply bad coffee in cans or bottles.Rich, satisfying and easily portable, I plan to have a pack of these in my desk drawer (or in the refrigerator) at work for those days when brewing hot coffee isn't right - but a smooth and satisfying 6.8 ounces of the 'real thing' chilled would really hit the spot.

Illy Issimo Coffee Drink is really good. I especially like it iced in this hot weather. It gives me a nice caffine boost. During the low part of my day (early Afternoon) it is a nice pic me up! It also tastes pretty good.If you like a deep rich coffee you will love it.Try it iced.

column9: Not bad. Sorta watery.  Quite sweet.
column10: It's not bad.  I had this on my way into work.  Great way to get some caffiene in ya before work!  It only has 4 ingredients: Coffee, sugar, and the other two I assume are preservatives or something.  It tasted almost creamy, although there is no cream in it!  It was sweeter - more sweet than anything else.  The coffee flavor is on the watery side.  It tasted like one of those cold Starbucks drinks you can buy, only not as creamy.  I thought it was good enough - but I'd never buy them.  My preference for a cold coffee-style drink is those excellent Starbucks bottle things!!!

I'm a big coffee drinker, and I loved illy issimo Cappuccino.  However, I did not enjoy this coffee drink.  It taste bitter, and is not refreshing.  I prefer Starbucks coffee cans better.  This one did not do it for me.  I still rate the cappuccino version highly.

column9: If you like your coffee black
column10: I don't mind straight coffee on occasion but this tasted like a strong americano to me but a little more bitter. I wasn't a fan. I prefer my coffee to have some sweetness and cream. I also think the price is on the high side. You can get the large starbucks cans on sale for 1.50 a can at your local grocery store.

column9: Not much flavor and very bland.
column10: This drink barely passes for a coffee drink. It is very light in flavor with minimal coffee essence, despite the first ingredient being coffee. It has very little flavor and still less of what I would call espresso. It also has a somewhat odd after taste, sort of bitter and seltzer-like. It left me more thirsty than when I finished it.Overall not very good.

column9: Not overly bitter like most espresso, but...
column10: Let's face it, espresso is not for the casual coffee drinker.  It's highly concentrated, and generally tastes terribly bitter.  But I thought I'd give this illy drink a whirl anyway. It does seem a bit tame for espresso -- which is a good thing if you're not an aficionado; but for those who love espresso, this will likely be too dilute. I think illy's canned cappuccino drink tastes much better.  But I guess if you're a serious coffee drinker, having an espresso on the go like this would be a good thing.  I think the price is relatively fair considering the cost of packaging, manufacturing, distribution, et al, but at the end of the day, I still think it's far too steep a price for canned coffee.  Overall, it's just ok.

While the Illy ssimo Coffee drink does taste like espresso, it feels blurred by an aftertaste, perhaps from the beet sugar, its minimal other ingredients, or just the long time it spends in a can on its way from Denmark.  I'm glad I tried it and it at least tastes like a coffee product compared to their cappuccino in a can, it won't replace iced coffee for me, when I want coffee on a hot day.

I enjoyed every bit of this smooth and lightly sweetened coffee beverage. For a vew calories, it delivered great taste and a nice little caffeine jolt to get me through the afternoon. This definitely goes on my shopping list!

I can understand a latte in a can or even a flavored coffee drink in a can but just coffee and sweetner in can?  There just does not seem to be a good reason for this product.  It's not hard to make coffee and if you like it sweetened (which I don't), then there is sugar or sweetner.People might say it's for "on the go" or travel but see above for the first, and if I were camping I would used instant or concentrated coffee.  I just don't get the purpose of this?As for taste, just okay and of course I hate that it is sweetened.

column9: I am not a coffee drinker
column10: But my daughter is and she said 'well it's not great, but it's coffee in a can so what can you expect'.  I took a sip and it's really a meh! product...not as bad as it could be but also not as good as it could be either.

column9: Not for me if you like straight Espresso  you might like this
column10: okay here is my disclaimer -I like my coffee sweet and with cream --my first taste yuck!but I said I would review this so took a second sipBitter tasteslight powdery feellight carbinationA strong coffee aromaI was hoping for something better

What can you expect from coffee in a can? I certainly did not have very high expectations. However, when I first tasted this illy coffee, I was surprised by its strong coffee flavor. I do like my coffee strong. Unlike some other reviewers, I did not find the taste bitter. Generally, I do not put sugar in my coffee, or anything else for that matter. So I did notice the sugary taste.After trying the illy at room temperature, I decided that it would be fair to compare it with my usual hot coffee, so I poured the remaining liquid into a coffee cup and plopped it into the microwave. When heated, it was better than at room temperature. Good coffee taste, but still too sweet.This coffee drink has 10 grams of sugar per can. That is almost as much sugar as there is in a tablespoon of granulated sugar, which comes in at 13 grams. I would never put that much sugar in a single cup of coffee. Some people may like it though.

column9: Good espresso flavor, low sugar, caffeine kick
column10: I got one can of Illy issimo coffee drink free from the Amazon Vine program, in exchange for writing a review about it.I like strong, dark coffee, but avoid most canned coffee beverages because of the sugar and carbs. We drink French roast coffee at home, brewed very strong, so most coffees at restaurants and in cans taste weak to me.This little can of espresso was a pleasant surprise - it only contains 50 calories and 12 carbs. It had a strong coffee flavor but I didn't detect any bitterness or aftertaste like some reviewers reported. It also had a nice little caffeine kick, probably because the coffee is strong.Of all the canned coffee beverages I've tried, this one is my favorite.

I really like coffee and I really like cold coffee drinks. So how was this one? Basically this tastes a lot like McDonald's coffee with some milk and sugar. It was drinkable but not something I would spend money on. It did seem to have a lot of caffeine, even I felt this one. If you really like the coffee at Micky D's, go for this. If not, I would suggest passing.

For a wanna-be Italian coffee produced in Denmark and distributed by Coca-Cola, this is much better than expected.  It really does have a smooth, rich espresso flavor.It is sweetened, but fortunately real sugar is used, so there is no strange aftertaste, and there is not enough sugar to mask the delicious coffee flavor.  Of course, refined sugar is never healthy, and there are 10 grams of sugar per can, but this would still make a nice occasional treat on a long road trip, and I could foresee myself having one again.Now, make no mistake, you will never get the best coffee flavor from a can, but this still beats most of the fresh-brewed coffee served in most convenience stores or offices, and you have the convenience of popping one in your cooler or handbag to enjoy at your convenience.In conclusion, it's not the best, but for what it is, I'm impressed.

column9: Kind of shocked to like this!
column10: Not exactly the highest possible praise, but as something of a coffee snob, I was surprised to find this so palatable.  And really, if you need a caffeine hit, isn't it better to down something that didn't have to be formulated inside of a lab?  Five Hour Energy Drinks, I'm talking to *you*.What's in the can?  Coffee, beet sugar, potassium carbonate and potassium citrate.  Those last two you can buy in the vitamin/supplement aisle of your drugstore, and they do have natural antacid properties - I don't think they are used here as preservatives, but rather to tone down coffee's natural acidity.  I get good balance in the flavor of the coffee, so it's easy to enjoy without the addition of milk - great for me as a lactose-intolerant coffee drinker.  If you happen to already cold-brew in the fridge at home for lower acid, you'll appreciate the difference.  On the other hand, if you're a huge fan of bright, acid-y Central American coffees as opposed to the deeper Sumatrans and Suwalesis, then for you this might be a deficit.I'd keep this around in warm weather to offer iced to guests.  It's true that you can probably brew a better cup, if you start with good beans, but I think the convenience here is worth the price, particularly if you don't normally brew much coffee. Roasted beans kept in storage go stale - FAST.For decades, Illy has enjoyed a reputation for reliable, if not exceptional quality, and I'd sooner have one of these than a Starbucks canned or a McCafe any day. (Even if they did partner with Coca Cola for this latest Issimo line, says the coffee snob.)

Illy Caffe is a lot like the premade iced tea, it's okay but not special.The taste is fine, it's coffee and sugar, pour it over ice and you have iced coffee.  I get coffee drinks, the cappuccino by Illy is really good, or the starbucks, but this is very plain and at roughly two dollars a can it's not any cheaper than a small coffee out somewhere. The can is small, the calorie count is 50, the taste really standard. Anyone with some instant coffee, sugar, and ice could make this easily. I don't even see it as being a matter of giving up taste for convenience, as it's not a "fancy" drink.

I don't pretend to have the most discerning palate in the world when it comes to coffee.  I might even have to admit that I don't know what's good.  I do, however, know what's bad.  And this is bad.  The flavor is way too strong and overpowering, is very bitter has a strong stale quality to it, and doesn't really have any kind of dynamism or complexity.  It's kind of like the dregs of a pot of Folger's that's been sitting out all day, and I'm not saying that because I drank it cold.I quite liked the illy issimo Coffee Drink, Cappuccino, 8.45-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12), I wouldn't mind recommending it.  But this was awful.  Oh well.  Nothing ventured, nothing gained, right?

column4: Shana "That's my opinion- I could be wrong!"
column10: Very deep and tasty Caffe drink. It's got just a hint of sweetness and a hint of chocolate taste. Not too much fat and less sugar than most drinks of this type. Even my husband who doesn't like coffee likes it. It reminds me of a Starbucks double shot, but less sweet and it has less cream. I'd definitely buy these and try them again.

There are times when making iced coffee or even getting premium iced coffee from a coffee shop is not a possibility, and for those times, having some cans of illy issimo caffe would be great.  The caffeine--plus a little sugar--really hit the spot.  It isn't a big serving, but the benefit of that is that it's only 50 Kcal a can!The downside?  $2. for 6.8 oz. is a lot.  So while I will buy this drink from time to time when I stop into a deli for something to allay my thirst and caffeine deprivation, I don't think I'd stock up for home use, because making iced coffee by the quart, and keeping it in the fridge, isn't that onerous.

Never before had I tried black coffee with sugar - until I tried the illy issimo.This is just plain black coffee with sugar.  Some people may not like the taste of it, since most of are used to having either black coffee or black coffee with cream and sugar, but black coffee with sugar - hmm.Overall, I did like the taste of it.  If you are planning to buy this, I would suggest trying a single can before doing a bulk order

I usually have four or more cups of strong black coffee every day, and I like to pick up a Starbucks DoubleShot Espresso Drink 12 ct if I am starting my day away from my coffee pot, so I have tried this kind of drink before. If you don't like the "burnt coffeepot" taste of espresso, then don't get this product. I put this on par with Starbuck's product of the same type. Would I go out of my way to get this product instead of Starbucks? No, I would not. In my area, this product is significantly more expensive than Starbuck's. So, I would get this product if it is available for less $$, which at retail, usually isn't less $$.

This drink is really good. It contains no cream. Just coffee and a touch of sugar. It isn't overly sweetened at all. It is perfect. The coffee flavor is bold with a slight acidity. At only 50 calories, this coffee drink could easily be a daily habit.I only gave it 4 out of 5 stars because it seemed weird to me drinking coffee from a can. I'm not so much a can person. And these cans are pretty small.

As I sit here and taste this for the first time I wonder what it is that I like so much and what it is that makes me not like it.  The coffee flavor is really there, so it can hold up to the ice you will no doubt use to make this truly iced coffee.It is a bit bitter, it needs to be smoothed with some milk or non dairy milk product to give it the nice smooth flavor of iced coffee.  The sugar content is fairly low for this kind of product so is the calorie count, 50 cals. per 6.8 fluid ounces. The only thing "for me" is the caffeine is a little high, and is openly stated on the back label, to be: 155 mg/per 6.8 fl. oz.I do like this product as long as I can add some "milk" to smooth it out a little.As far as I can see, this is a pure product and is made well.I would drink this again.

column9: Has a good taste but maybe too much added sugar
column10: I enjoy my coffee but I normally add only a touch of sugar, if any at all to my coffee. When I do add sugar, I would put no more than a 1/2 teaspoon of sugar in my cup of coffee. I also will generally choose a dark roast coffee, like French Roast or Sumatra.This illy Caffe coffee drink is an Italian Roast coffee. It has a decent taste in my opinion. I was expecting some sort of "canned" taste but didn't sense that at all while I was drinking it. But I did experience an aftertaste that I can only describe as somewhat metallic.I usually drink the dark roast coffees but was surprised to find that this had a really  nicely balanced coffee taste without the pronounced bitterness usually associated with the bigger, bolder dark roasts to which I'm accustomed.It was the added sugar that I don't really care for. The serving size is 6.8 fluid ounces and that contains 10g of sugar. A teaspoon of sugar is approximately 4 g which means this 6.8 oz can of coffee has the equivalent of 2.5 teaspoons of sugar. Even if I did put sugar in a cup of coffee, I'd only put in a single teaspoon. So for me it was way too sweet. Knowing that many people do sweeten their coffee, I'd say that many people would not find this as overly sweet as I did. You'd probably like it if you sweeten your coffee.I find it convenient to be able to have with you on trips or travels, a good quality cup of coffee. This tastes much better to me than your typical gas station swill that is passed on as coffee. So for trips or commutes it would be a great choice. Just be careful if you are diabetic or have sugar restrictions because there is quite a bit of sugar in a serving. Other than that it tastes pretty good to me.

If you're a coffee lover like me, you'll be thrilled with this Expresso from Illy.  I poured it over some shaved ice on a superhot day in Chicago and savored the rich taste.  And, as a plus, I didn't have to brew a pot of coffee to get my coffee kick. The low calorie count didn't make a dent in my calories for the day so I celebrated with some chocolate sorbet!  A real winner.

In a nutshell this is a 6.8oz Italian Espresso style drink, made in Denmark, by the Coco-Cola company, sweetened with 10g of sugar, comes in a small can and has 50 calories.I don't usually drink coffee from a can so this was an interesting trial. I tried this two ways, first as a straight espresso. But since I don't drink my coffee room temperature, I heated it up in a microwave. Straight up, I'd say this was a little weak, and the 10g of sugar doesn't do anything for it. If I drink it black, 10g of sugar takes a little of the bite away; if I drink it sweetened, it's not sweet enough. It's a like a matter of trying to please everyone but not making anyone happy.Next, I tried it as a latte and added some milk and heated it up. I usually drink my latte without sugar but since this already had a little and not enough at that, I sweetened it a little more. As a latte it was actually not bad.The taste is a little bland (not talking about strength but flavor) but I'm accustomed to making my own coffee from different beans so I wouldn't mark it down that much. It says it's 100% Arabica but that doesn't really tell you much since the most common bean grown is C. arabica. Is it the dregs swept from around the world or is it the finest hand picked? Coffee taste itself is very subjective so all I'm saying here is that the taste is not very specific to a region that I can tell. I really have to give kudos for Coca-Cola for trying to make a canned presentation out of a product whose taste is so personal and difficult to please.It doesn't have any caffeine information on the can but I wonder if they juiced it up because it gave me a buzz that I only usually get when I drink extra concentrated coffee.I would think that cans like this are meant to be drunk cold from the fridge or from a cooler and unfortunately I didn't think to save some of it to drink with ice or cold. But overall I think it's an OK substitute for someone who needs his coffee fix when there is absolutely no cafe around and it's not too bad for a situation like that.

column9: This Illi Issimo Drink Packs A Strange Combination Of Sweet And Bitter
column10: Through the years, I've tried just about every pre-made coffee beverage imaginable. I am a coffee lover and enthusiast, so I'm married to the idea of buying a can or bottle of a delicious coffee based product that I'll live happily ever after with. My experiences, however, have yet to yield bliss. Some are just fine, but nothing has ever made me say "Wow! I'd like to drink this all the time!" I had heard some positive things about the illy issimo brand, so given the opportunity--I sampled both their Caffe and their Cappuccino.Caffe (2 1/2 stars) is, in their own words, an Italian Espresso Style Coffee Drink. At first, I thought this drink had a strong and pronounced coffee flavor. But something is slightly off. The more I drank, it seemed too sweet and too bitter at once, which is a strange and not altogether pleasant combination. As it is essentially comparable to drinking an iced espresso, it may not be as palatable as some of their other creations. But, it's not really something that I would sample again. And at an approximate cost of $2.00 per can (only 6.8 ounce), this serves more as a caffeine boost than a refreshing beverage. Made with real Arabica coffee, I was also intrigued by the "Do Not Shake" warning which left me with the unappetizing visual of the particulate matter that must still be in the liquid drink (fine for Turkish coffee, not so appealing for something in a can).Cappucino (3 1/2 stars) is, in their own words, an Espresso Style Coffee Drink with Lowfat Milk and Cocoa. So, at 8.45 ounces this is a slightly bigger drink. As some of the harshness is buffered by the milk and cocoa combination, this one easily had a more pleasant taste. Still, a bit sweet for my liking but better overall. I'm still not blown away and I won't be a regular purchaser of this, or any illi issimo brand drinks, but I didn't dislike this one. Nice enough once in a while, but not inspiring enough to purchase a case. I guess I'll remain a fresh made kind of coffee drinker! KGHarris, 6/12.

column9: for a canned coffee, it's okay
column10: My first choice for a coffee is never a can. I much prefer perked, homemade, hot coffee. Being of English/German background, Espresso was never a standard drink in our home. All that being said, this coffee was okay for a canned drink. There is no cream in it, so the color is dark. It is much less sweet than the Cappuccino version put out by illy, as so I liked it better than the Cappuccino.I did not taste the metal aftertaste in the Caffe/Espresso drink that I detected in the Cappuccino version, so that is a good thing.After drinking 1/2 a can straight to get the full flavor, I added a hint of half and half cream (I know, not traditional, but I'm not Italian) and I liked it better than without. This is a quick fix for a caffeine boost if you are in a hurry.The can is smaller than the Cappuccino, having 6.8 oz, 50 calories and 100% Natural Arabica.  One can would be more than enough for me in one day. Don't shake the can before serving.

I really wish I knew what was up with this country and sweeteners.  These days you can barely get a cup of coffee somewhere without someone dumping sugar into it without asking.  So along comes Illy's ready-to-drink "espresso-style" coffee and I imagine I should have guessed that it would be sweetened.  I didn't.  It was an unpleasant shock,not only because I hate sugar in my coffee, but because you have to check the ingredient list to find the sugar. Okay, fair enough, you should look at the ingredient list on everything you put in your mouth, but it should also say "pre-sweetened" on the front of the can. I'm just sayin'.All that aside, and making an honest attempt to evaluate the stuff in spite of the sugar, I'd have to say that it's a good, smooth, tasty brew.  I've always liked Illy coffee and this brewed stuff isn't half bad for something that comes out of a can.  I think I'd prefer it from a glass bottle, but what are the odds of that happening? As it is, the flavor of the can isn't a huge problem, but it sure doesn't add anything to the experience.Tiny can doesn't go very far either.  Presumably the reason why Illy has produced a ready-to-drink brew is for people who want to grab a can out of the fridge and swig it down.  If they're going to heat it... well no, I don't even want to think about that.  Ugh. So it's meant to be drunk cold.  Twelve ounces would have made more sense in that case.  This isn't a tiny cup of hot espresso we're talking about, it's a cold beverage. If Illy is going to bow down to the Sugar Gods of America, they can darn well do a bit of homage to the Gods of Conspicuous Consumption, too.  But $2 for less than 7 ounces of coffee?  Thanks but no thanks as Sarah Palin famously remarked.  @2 for a 12 oz can is still a bit high, but more acceptable overall.So kudos to Illy for using sugar instead of HFCS, but points off for using any sweetener at all.  Good flavor and body, but cans just don't lend themselves to a good coffee-drinking experience.  Cans are too small and the price is too high.  Buy a tin of Illy and brew your own.  It'll taste better and you'll save money.

column9: Only for those who enjoy the darker, richer side of coffee!
column10: The Illy Issimo Caffe drink is dark, rich and smooth.  If you love your coffee beans dark, or drink your coffee black you will adore this drink. A wonderful cold 6.8 oz Caffe Italian espresso drink that is made from All natural with 100% percent Arabica coffee and sweetened with beet sugar. This is an acquired taste, and only for those who enjoy the darker, richer side of coffee.

This is a strong iced coffee drink in a small can.  The coffee is light to moderate in acidity, clean tasting,with a medium level of bitterness, quite strong and quite rich.  There is no milk or cream in it.  There is a little sugar which gives the drink a moderate level of sweetness that is good and appropriate.  Drinking it straight, the taste is a little too lean and austere.  I prefer iced coffee to have a little dairy for roundness and body.  Coffee of this strength alone leaves too dry a taste and lacking in richness.  That aside, I added a small scoop of vanilla ice cream to this drink and it tasted very nice.  It has all the missing parts filled in as far as I am concerned.  Most bottled ice coffee drinks with cream are too sweet.  This one isn't.  It just needs a bit of roundness from the ice cream (half-and-half will do similarly).  Overall, it is an ok drink.  From a can though, if you have no access to milk or cream, this drink may be a bit too strong and too dry to have broad appeal.

column9: Surprised This Had Sugar And Calories In It......
column10: My impression of this coffee is it is probably of very high quality and also very strong.  I was surprised to see sugar had been added to the product and that the can contained 50 calories as I had assumed it was almost pure coffee.  I had to add a bit of skimmed milk with the ice cubes to make an enjoyable iced coffee for my taste buds.

column9: Issimo's "Caffé" style iced coffee:  A Critical Review.
column10: Iced coffee, if you're a regular coffee drinker, is an acquired taste.Even discriminating coffee drinkers won't drink any coffee...cough...cough... Starbucks... cough.  But, this iced coffee is not bad.After tasting it, I can say that "Caffe" tastes like a spoonful of Breyer's coffee ice cream but with a slight bitter aftertaste.Although I still weigh in on the side of "hot" coffee, especially Chock Full O' Nuts brand, Issimo's "Caffe" is not that bad for iced coffee.4 stars.

column9: Not too sweet -- Good taste, even right from the can
column10: The first thing I did was Shake The Can. Then I saw the "Do Not Shake" warning but I opened the can anyway and nothing happened. I suspect the DNS is in reference to the Potassium Bicarbonate (fizz-producer?) that lurks within the ingredients. There WAS a nice little "kick" to this -- perhaps from the Potassium Bicarbonate.The initial taste produced an "aaah!" reaction. This is a nice full-bodied coffee, straight from the can, or iced (if consumed shortly after being iced). As a coffee purist who grew up with my Italian Nonna and her old-fashioned espresso pots, it would have been anathema for me to put this in a cup and Nuke it. But I suspect the flavor would not be diminished by doing so.Is this a real Espresso experience? The name says it all - "Italian espresso STYLE Coffee drink". Although it stands out over and above your regular strong coffee, I would say it is a mild but memorable brew, compared to the espresso that your local Barista brews for you -- and compared to mild-mannered Nonna Lucia's "stand-your-hair-on-end" potent brew.The sweetness factor is not cloying. The coffee (made with the better Arabica Beans)is too rich to be chugged. It IS meant to be savored.I'm happy with Illy issimos' Caffe -- take it with you to work - on a car ride -- it would also be a nice addition to any backpack or travel-case, as the can is a nice compact size.  Add it to your favorite cofee liquer-based drink(s), or even smoothies.  Price is a consideration -- my budget will not allow this on a regular basis, but as a treat, as I do consider it a quality product.Bravo Illy -- Viva Italia.

column9: Not too sweet, with some bite to it - good stuff
column10: "illy issimo" Caffè was a pleasant surprise to me after trying a similar illy product, illy issimo Coffee Drink, Cappucino, 8.45-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12).Where the cappuccino was a bit weak and bland for my taste, this Caffè had a reasonable amount of roasted coffee flavor and a bit of bite to it.  Like the other illy products I've tried the Caffè is only moderately sweetened.So if your preferred coffee drink is McDonald's or Dunkin Donuts iced coffee, this product is probably not going to appeal to you.  But if you'd like to try a premade coffee drink that's not overly sweet and actually has a bit of roast coffee flavor, illy issimo Caffè may be worth a try.

column9: Bold coffee with just enough sweetness.
column10: I usually like my coffee hot with just a little half & half.  With it getting warm outside, I sometimes brew my coffee and put it over ice.  I usually add a bit of sugar to it when it's cold.  With that said, I like this coffee it is strong with just a touch of sweetness.  The ingredients are Coffee, Sugar, Potassium Bicarbonate, Potassium Citrate.I would drink this on mornings that I didn't feel like hot coffee.

Seriously, there's a 'do not shake' warning on the can and it's there for good reason - the contents are under pressure so... you shake it at your own risk.As a coffee drinker, I can't say that I'm impressed by this canned Espresso to the point that I'd stop making my own but I suppose that's not the point of the 'illy'. No canned coffee can challenge the flavor and aroma of a freshly brewed cup but when that is not possible, here comes the 'illy' and... it's passable.If comparing canned coffees to canned coffees, the 'illy' espresso is okay as in 'decent' and probably preferable to most other canned brands but to call it 'espresso' is a bit of a stretch. It's got 'sugar' for starters, 50 calories worth of it and I don't know too many espresso drinkers that would tolerate sugar in their espresso drink. And it's not espresso-strong. It's a little stronger than the normally bland canned coffee but maybe only half-way between regular coffee and espresso. As for the taste, this is supposed to be made of 'Arabica' and maybe it is but it tastes more like instant coffee to me. Maybe Arabica-based, cold instant coffee.So... if stranded on an island or anywhere a decent cup of real coffee is not an option or you aren't in the mood or don't have the time to make your own, the 'illy espresso' is an option and at least as good, possibly better than alternative canned or bottled coffees. In other words, "It's Okay" (3 stars) if used as directed and your expectations are reasonably low.________________________________Note: Should this be chilled before use? Ice espresso is an abomination but, again, just because it says 'espresso' on the can it doesn't necessarily make it so.

column9: A very nice beverage but it could be stronger for me
column10: Length:: 1:50 MinsI thought that a video review of this beverage might but fun.  I liked the drink but it really didn't have that strong, rich, coffee flavor that I was looking for.  The ingredients were pretty simple: coffee; sugar; potassium bicarbonate; and potassium citrate.  I am not sure if I would buy this on my own but it is something different and I liked the taste.

I've tried Illy cappuccino and it was tasty, creamy and a bit sweet. Having Illy espresso in the fridge to try I was ready for refreshment and some kick in taste and energy. This coffee drink went down the drain after 2-3 sips. I love lattes and I could drink hot fresh espresso, but this was just unbearable. VERY bitter, despite of having sugar it (and I don't sweeten tea and coffe). Also there is 50 calories in the can, not 45 (small difference), but fot many that count calories might matter.Anyway I wouldn't recommend Issimo espresso, unless you love very very bitter coffee.

column9: Eh. Only okay for coffee, not worth the price.
column10: After having and loving the illy issimo Coffee Drink, Cappucino, 8.45-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12), I expected to like this. However, it tastes like mediocre, slightly bitter espresso that was watered down and poured into a can. It says it was sweetened with beet sugar, but I didn't taste any sweetness to it, nor did my husband. I couldn't even finish one can, and then I offered it to my husband; he couldn't finish it either.We love fresh brewed coffee, and we've become coffee snobs recently, not caring for Starbucks and other chain coffees like we used to. I expected this brand to measure up to those expectations, especially after the cappuccino did, but it fell miserably short.

Illy issimo caffè Italian espresso style coffee drink is a 6.8 fl. oz. (200 ml) blast of sweetened caffeine in a can.1930s Italy under the rule of Mussolini greatly contributed to the development of modern coffee culture, improved coffee-making, and new types of coffee-making equipment. The Horn of Africa (where coffee originated) was under Italian colonization and companies such as illy and Bialetti were founded.In that tradition, this drink is now made in Denmark under the issimo brand from illy and distributed in the U.S. by Coca-Cola.This canned cappuccino has a slightly bitter dark roast coffee taste with the right amount of sugar and a pleasant mouthfeel. It's not as good as freshly made espresso but it's not bad at all. I do prefer the illy issimo cappucino as a treat.

column9: Strong and bitter for my taste
column10: I tried both the illy issimo Caffe drink and the cappucino drink.  I loved the cappucino and would gladly buy it any day.  However, I was very disappointed in the caffe drink.  I found it too strong, with a bitter edge. The level of sweetness seemed just right, but it couldn't cut the bitterness.  The ingredients are simple, containing coffee and sugar, along with ingredients that I think are supposed to take the bitterness off - potassium bicarbonate and potassium citrate - but they don't seem to work well enough.I tasted it three times (yes, Mom!) but poured the rest down the drain.  I would not reach for this again, but I love their cappucino and I would gladly try other products by illy.

This little can packs a lot of flavor; it is strong and just enough taste of bitterness in it. You can smell a bit of aroma even if it is cold.  You can enjoy it direct from the can or chill it with ice.  It has 155 grams of caffein and gives me a shorst burst of energy when I need it.  Product of Denmark.Only 10 grams of sugar. But then again, it is just an itsy bitsy can.

I had heard of this brand of coffees, but had never tried one, until now.  I did not know what to expect, but I think I thought it would be like one of those iced coffee drinks.It's not, at least not to me.  First of all, on the can it says not to shake it.  Iam not sure why.  I had put the can in my refrigerator to chill it for several hours.Each can is 6.8 fl ounces, which is one serving, has 50 calories, total carbs-12 grams, sugars-10 grams, and 155 milligrams of caffeine.  On the caffeine scale I have no idea how high that caffeine level is on a scale from low to high, but by my taste buds I would say it ranges on the higher side due to the STRONG coffee taste that this has, at least to me.I did not find this Caffe Italian Expresso Style Coffee Drink to be sweet at all.  All I tasted was a STRONG coffee flavor, no other flavor was pronounced.That may be because it's an expresso type drink.  Expresso is always a stronger coffee.I do know this, and that is I couldn't drink more than a few sips of this drink out of the can, just the way it is.It's just way too strong for me, but I think if I put it into a taller glass, add some ice and some flavored liquid creamer, it would taste much better to me.For those of you who love STRONG coffee beverages, you may just love this one!To me it packs a real coffee punch for a can of this size!

column9: Okay Coffee. It has good flavour, but is weak for my taste
column10: I usually have very low expectations for these kind of canned coffee, but this one was better than I thought. It has a sweet coffee taste, reminding of real espresso. However, it felt more like americano than espresso (meaning it is more diluted with water than necessary). It still packs enough caffeine, and if you do not want to go the "5 hour energy" route in urgent needs (like driving early in the morning), it would be a good alternative.I would recommend it cold, so keeping in the car might not be an option. Nevertheless, it's good enough for the product category (canned coffee).

column4: Kilgore Gagarin "Those who believe in telekin...
column10: My wife ran across this specific brand in Japan last year and said it was every bit as good as the canned Starbucks Espresso competitor and a lot cheaper (check prices). I refrigerated my sample and split it with my wife, and as daily AM quadruple espresso drinkers, this hit the spot. She usually has her espresso with sweetener, and I like mine bitter and black. We found this to be a pleasant in-between sweetness that we both liked. Neither of us added anything. Cold, unshaken, right out of the can.My rule when I get free stuff to review: Would I buy this with my own money? My answer: yes. We're going on an upcoming vacation in the wilds of Northern Wisconsin and I'm getting a case of this, as well as a case of illy issimo Coffee Drink, Cappuccino which I've also reviewed. This product and the Illy cappuccino are spot on for a couple of espresso caffeine addicts.

column9: Good coffee - arabica is the best, nice flavor, convenient
column10: As you can tell from my user name, I'm a bit of a coffee lover and have been for years however, I despise crummy coffee, instant coffee, coffee fillers, artifical flavorings etc...I like rich, dark arabica coffee served strong and black.Typically I grind my own (organic) beans using a vintage mill and french press but there are times when it's not possible to make a decent cup of coffee. This fits the bill perfectly. A nice balance, not weak but not overpowering, solid arabic rather than the inferior robusta and all the convenience. Kosher (important) and relatively free from preservatives etc... I wish there was an organic option but aside from that, I was very impressed by the flavor.

column9: Strong coffee beverage with a little sweetness
column10: I like to have a few cold canned coffee beverages on hand, as I prefer them to most energy drinks. Unfortunately finding one that isn't filled with sweeteners has become very difficult.  Living in the Seattle area I was already familiar with illy for their coffee beans that are used in some of my favorite coffee houses. So being given the chance to try some of their canned coffee beverages was something I was looking forward to.After spending the night in the fridge, I opened the illy issimo Caffè without shaking it as noted on the can and poured it into a glass. (*See customer images) The color was very nice, it looked like a strong cup of coffee. The smell was good too and although I knew it was sweetened it wasn't coming across too much. The coffee was strong, very smooth and thankfully not too sweet. I was able to enjoy the entire can in one sitting.Overall illy issimo has a great product and for once I've found one that isn't too sweet for me to enjoy. Plus now that I have been introduced to their canned coffee line I am looking forward to trying this one next: illy issimo Caffè (No Sugar)

column9: A little too strong for me
column10: Illy coffee is not new to me. I have been buying their illy, Ground Espresso Coffe, Fine Grind (Dark Roast, Black Band), 8.8-Ounce Tins (Pack of 2). I will admit I bought it more than a few years ago. After awhile my taste changed and I liked drinks with more of a cream flavor to them.Illy makes a lot of great drinks. I buy them when I run out to the drugstore as a pick me up or a treat for myself. They are pricey but they do give you a quick jolt of the caffeine for pick up. I have not tried the caffe' can locally. I made sure it was very chilled in my fridge and like all my other cold coffee drinks, drank it with a straw. I had a hard time getting this down. It was my first drink of the day and being a caffeine junkie, thought it would be easier to swallow, it was not. Understand it is an espresso drink that has no cream to it so it is very bold tasting, almost bitter to me. I tried to suck it down and had to take small sips it was so strong. I did finish it though.I can't say I would buy this again since it is not to my liking. I now like my cold coffee drinks to have a cream added to them or a flavor. This drink is very bold and strong. If you are not familiar with how strong it is, you might not even be able to keep it down.Size wise I compare it to Starbucks double shots drinks but without the cream. I drink a ton of Starbucks cold coffee beverages since they carry them in bulk where I live. However, it might compare size wise but again, no cream. Illy also only has 50 calories if calories are a factor for you. I like to drink cold coffee with lower calories in case I drink two a day but can't say this is one I would factor in because of the low calories.Glad I tried it but can't say I would buy it again. If I were on a road trip and this was the only coffee sold at a gas station I might buy it as a pick me up. A regular drink, not for me, Illy has much better drinks out there in my opinion.

Although no canned coffee will come close to fresh brewed, within their own category there is a broad spectrum of quality.  The illy issimo Coffee Drink falls in the upper end.  It is labeled Italian Espresso Style Coffee Drink, and as such has a strong, somewhat bitter flavor. This is balanced by the added sugar which makes the drink moderately sweet.  More preferable than the cloyingly sweet taste that proliferates in canned coffee drinks.  If you are looking for a brisk pick-me-up, the illy issimo does the trick.

column9: I liked it; I still prefer black, hot coffee, but this could be an occasional switch
column10: I have tried a variety of chilled coffee/espresso drinks, and while I like them individually, I have yet to find any drink that I would go out of my way to try repeatedly. Maybe this didn't amaze me, but I liked that it was an adult coffee drink.I drink black coffee with no sugar - and I drink a lot of it. The good thing about this brand is, like another reviewer said, the coffee is the star. I tried it right after a cup of my normal hot coffee, and it did not pale in comparison.I drank the Caffe chilled and it was not bitter or over-sweet like so many of these drinks. I normally drink high-end coffee, and this tasted pretty legit in comparison. So I think quality ingredients were used.It's a little stronger than my normal coffee - which it should be, since it's an espresso drink.Another review thought the sugar overwhelmed the flavor. It's funny - I didn't get that at all. It IS a little sweet (and sugar is the second listed ingredient), but it wasn't something I noticed that much.Bottom line - good ingredients + adult taste = solid quality.If you're a black/hot coffee fan like me this probably won't change your habits, but for a hot day this might be a good switch.

column9: Sugar Overwhelms Rich Espresso Coffee Flavor
column10: If you generally prefer black coffee (as I do), you will probably find that the sugar (10g) overwhelms the rich espresso coffee flavor of this ILLY ISSIMO "Caffè" drink.  That's too bad, because the coffee itself tastes delicious.  Apparently this canned espresso drink is designed to deliver a quick caffeine/sugar "pick me up" jolt.I think that the product is intended to be consumed straight from the can, at room temperature.  The can includes a "do not shake" warning, but has no instructions for chilling or warming the contents.  Because I don't care for iced coffee, I tried the product only (1) at room temperature straight from the aluminum can, and (2) after warming in a microwave-safe cup.  It tasted about the same both ways.This "Italian espresso-style coffee drink" certainly did not convert me to canned coffee drinks, especially ones with 50 calories in each 6.8 fl. oz. can.  I drink a lot of coffee, and prefer to brew it myself from freshly ground whole coffee beans.  However, because ILLY ISSIMO "Caffè" tastes like it's made with high-quality coffee, I award it 3.5 stars, rounded up to 4 stars.

I love coffee, and this drink didn't disappoint.  Just pour over ice for a nice, refreshing Americano-style coffee drink.This is not an unsweetened drink; one can contains the equivalent of about 2 1/2 tsp. sugar, which is not too excessive in this day and age of sugar addiction.Recommended for a quick, refreshing coffee pick-up.  Would be 5 stars if they'd used Splenda or Stevia instead of sugar.

I use decaf illy coffee for my morning cup of coffee and love it. It costs a little more, but is very worth it. As far as the espresso drink...not for me. I tend to like lattes or cappuccinos--something with more milk/cream. This was too strong for me. My son tried it however, and loved it. If you like espresso in general, then I think you will love this product.

column4: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
column10: I like strong coffee - have a Keurig for my daily brews, and stop by Starbucks every couple of days.  So I thought I'd give this a try - I'm tired of the generic energy drink taste. This tastes like a medium roast Espresso, with the same after-taste. It has only 50 calories, although I'd prefer no calories. I did not pour over ice - drank from the can right out of the fridge. That's plenty cold, easier to carry, and I can keep a can in my pack when on the road.  You can also keep the can in the freezer for about a couple of hour before sticking in a backpack, so it will be ice cold several hours later.At 6.8 oz, the can is thicker than a Red Bull can (8.4 oz), and a tad bit shorter.  Definitely worth a try!

I found the 6.8 ounce illy issimo Coffee Drink, Caffe to have a very good, rich and well balanced coffee taste. That biting, bracing espresso "hit" is there in spades.  The caffeine is eye opening and the serving size provides just enough for a little buzz. These drinks are not overly sweet, they have a great balance of flavors.

This was pretty good. It had a little too strong of a coffee flavor for me so I added some milk to mine. I served it cold over ice. I love iced coffee drinks. The can was pretty small so it only has 12 carbs so that was good for me. The caffeine count must be pretty high though because I became quite jittery from it. The combination of sugar and caffeine does quite a job on me personally.I did like it and would try it again but I did like the illy issimo Coffee Drink, Cappucino, 8.45-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12) better.

I'm usually not a fan of canned coffee drinks, but wanted to try this since I love Illy espresso beans. While the canned version can't compare to a properly pulled shot of espresso, this is a pretty tasty alternative. Good flavor without the odd after-taste I've experienced with other canned coffee drinks.I tried it right out of the can (room temp) and over ice. I found it more enjoyable straight from the can.My only complaint is that it's a bit on the sweet side. I never add sugar to my coffee so I'm sensitive to any level of sweetness. Others may find the sweetness level to be fine.But, even with the sweetness, I would certainly get this again. It provides for a tasty afternoon pickup.

Wow, a little 50 calorie can of espresso and sugar. Serve cold and this is a delicious little shot of espresso. It does have sugar in it, but it is not overly sweet and the sugar helps offset the taste of the espresso. This Caffe is not too bitter or too sweet. It tastes good and really gave my afternoon a kick in the pants.

This was an enjoyable and refreshing treat on a hot summer day.  I poured the coffee over ice to enjoy it colder and it was very good.  It has a strong, bold coffee flavor, not bitter, and is slightly sweetened but not very sweet.  You could always add more sweetener to suit your taste, but I personally didn't find it necessary.  At only 50 calories a can this is a nice light drink.

column9: Do you like iced coffee? This is for you!
column10: If you really liked coffee or want an alternative for a hot day, this is it. Refrigerate it and/or pour over ice and it is ideal for that hot day relaxing. It is sweetened, but me personally like a bit more sugar. It tastes just like coffee and is not overly strong. I like the fact that it is a single seving can, so I don't have to make an entire pot off coffee. It is easy enough to put in the refrigerator and grab when needed, or take to go while on the run.

This illy issimo Caffe Coffee Drink has a strong coffee flavor that would normally be a plus since I like "bold" coffee, but the very bitter aftertaste is too much to make this enjoyable. Just to be sure it wasn't me, my coffee loving daughter also tried it and while she liked it more than I did, she said it is not a drink she would seek out again.This just misses the mark for us.CFH

I found this coffee really tasty.  It is difficult to catch a good Italian espresso that doesn't have an aftertaste, and for me, this coffee was rich and smooth with no burned taste.  It only has 10 grams of sugar which is a little over 2 teaspoons, not bad compared to other high calorie coffees.  The description in this page says it has 45 calories, but the can clearly says 50 calories.  I personally enjoyed it and found it pleasant to my taste buds.

column9: Rich coffee taste with the convenience of a can
column10: The illy issimo Coffee Caffè drink had a nice, clean, rich flavor, both at room temperature and poured over ice.  I liked it over ice the best.  There is just the right balance of coffee and enough sugar to make it appealing but not so much that it overpowers the drink or leaves an aftertaste.  The convenience of popping open a can for a great tasting caffeine fix is appealing.  And a good jolt of caffeine it is:  155 mg. per 6.8 ounce serving.  (The size of the can.)  Compare that to 48 mg. per 16.9 ounces of caffeine in Coke Zero.The ingredient list is pretty simple: Coffee, sugar, potassium bicarbonate, potassium citrate.If you're looking for a quick, bold, full-bodied, Italian espresso-style coffee drink, look no further.  This is a good one.

I always expect these cans of coffee to be very creamy and sugary no matter what is written on the label; a contrast to how I drink my hot coffee.Instead, this one is cold black coffee lightly sweetened - they did a pretty good job on the sugar level.It is worlds better than most of the other cold coffees without cream that I have had, most of which have been out of 2 liter plastic bottles in Japan, which are always extremely disappointing.  I can't give it a 5 because I don't love it, but I suspect that it is the best of its type one can get; you can sense that the quality is there.  It doesn't suffer too much from being cold because it doesn't seem watered down, like most usually do.

I poured me a can of this drink into a glass to enjoy the flavor.  My first reaction was its bitterness (it's espresso afterall) followed by a sweet but not too sweet aftertaste.
