It was enough to burn my tongue and lips and cause me to stop eating them, even though they tasted good.

I'm a big cashew fan, but was unimpressed by this product. The nuts were fresh, but the seasoning was a bit too heavy-handed - they are very salty and the pepper has more of a bite than I liked.The seasoning gets stronger the lower you get in the can due to it falling off the upper ones and coating the lower ones. While tolerable when first opened, the seasoning becomes way too overpowering once you get half-way down in the can. I found myself putting the nuts in a dish and rolling them around a bit to dislodge some of the seasoning.If you're on a sodium restricted diet (or just want to cut down on sodium) you definitely want to pass on this.If they would dial back the salt by 50% and the pepper by 75%, it would be a great product. As it is right now, however, I'll have to give it only 2 stars.

Everyone in the house loved these nuts, including my fussy hubby.The flavouring is excellent and might I add, addicting!! We had to hide them from the aforementioned husband.......and the best of all, this is healthy w/ omegas and a decent salt..not all salt is bad for you.So much better than chips,candy and so many other snack foods kids andthose who are not health conscious eat.

column9: Strong flavor, with room for improvement...
column10: The first thing you'll notice about these peppered cashew nuts is the packaging -- the large green plastic jar seems like overkill, but flipping it over, one finds that it's made of 7th-generation recycled plastic, so I suppose it's relatively eco-friendly (no indication of where it was manufactured; most likely in China)  So, we peel back the outer plastic wrapper (which also acts as a safety seal) and open the container, then check out the nuts.I have to say, the flavoring was much more thickly applied than I'd anticipated, with an almost pasty mix of pepper, salt and spices embedded on all the nuts. The second surprise is that the nuts are much moister than I'd have thought -- I prefer really crisp, dry-roasted nuts, and these were almost damp with the flavoring ingredients. Visually, there's quite a bit of black pepper in each bite, but it doesn't have as much kick as you'd expect. The pepper flavor, like that of the cashews themselves, is overshadowed by the rest of the seasonings -- the dominant tastes are of salt and dried onions, and the cashew umami is obscured to a remarkable degree.  Also, the salt doesn't taste very "sea salty", as it is competing with sugar, peanut oil and citric acid (which adds a nice lime-y tang, but also is buried in the mix...)  A much lighter seasoning might be better, one that concentrates on the flavors in this order: sea salt, dry-roast umami, citrus tang.  The other flavors -- onion, oil, sugar -- are just in the way.The final surprise came after I screwed the lid back on, set the jar aside and then came back for another sample. The lid popped right off, the jar slid out of my hand and almost spilled out onto the floor. Had I forgot to fasten it on properly?  Noooo... not quite. It turns out the screw-top lid  doesn't really fit very well onto the container. It screws on, alright, but it pops off quite easily, with slight force ranging from a short tug to just picking up the jar. Another half-turn worth of grooves would probably solve this defect. Also, it would be nice if the product info -- ingredients, nutrition value, etc. -- didn't peel off the container along with the safety seal.In sum, this is an okay snack food, but it could be much better. Mostly, a more subtle, less wham-bam approach to seasoning would help.Ingredients:Roasted cashews (with peanut or cottonseed oil), sea salt, peanut oil, black pepper, maltodextrin, sugar, granulated onion, citric acid, spice, natural flavor

column9: tasty alternate to peanuts or almonds
column10: These cashews are another nice addition to Emerald's line of nut snacks.  As someone who's addicted to peanuts and nuts for snacking (I usually have 2-3 containers open at any given time), I'm always looking for some variety, such as these with their salt+pepper seasoning reminiscent, in some ways, more of chips than nuts.The cashews themselves are high quality, large and meaty.Note the description is accurate, they liberally use both salt and pepper, so the sodium level in these is more than twice that of the similar cannister of Emerald almonds, and the pepper flavor is distinct.  Avoid if you dislike pepper or are on a salt-restricted diet.

A few years ago I gave a dinner party that had all the gay spontaneity of an open grave. Unbeknownst to me, each and every couple I had invited was on the outs with the others, but only in a quiet, teeth-gritted sort of way.The food, however, was a smashing success, especially some spicy pecans that I threw together as I walked in the door about a half hour before my guests. I have never replicated the success of that first batch, but these cashews come close.They have a good balance of sweet (the cashews themselves), salty, and peppery flavor. The pepper is not overpowering and strikes me as just right.The nice thing about the snack is that a few satisfy. I tend to to eat way too many plain cashews when I buy them lightly salted. A very few of these make a nice nibble, and would go great with sake or a martini.

I will admit that I am very fond of cashews. I have to resist the temptations to pick through a bowl of mixed nuts and snag the cashews for myself.These cashews are salty but also peppery.  The peppery flavor means I can only munch a few of these at a time. This is a good thing. They are different. I would serve these at a party and a few make a good snack before dinner.

column9: tasty but a little too strong
column10: You can only eat a few of these at a time--very strong salt and pepper.

It's very difficult to review a food item, because taste is so tremendously subjective.  I liked the combination of sea salt and pepper; the nuts were salty without being too salty, and the pepper was just enough to be noticeable without being overpowering.  My wife thought that the sea salt and pepper would be better on a chip or something crunchier, and that the texture of the nut was jarring in combination with the seasoning.  In general, I think these are tasty nuts, and while I don't think I'd be inclined to eat these regularly, I enjoyed them.  Cashew purists who are looking for a pure expression of cashew flavor (which I love myself) are advised to stick with good old regular roasted cashews, however.
These nuts seem fresher than most other brands. I don't know if they're packaged more airtightly than most, or harvested  more recently than others. Perhaps both.

column9: they're salty, they're peppery and they're delicious!
column10: I just cracked into the can of sea salt and pepper cashews and they are exactly what I expected.  Large cashews (not pieces), with a generous coating of salt and pepper.  They are salty, so if you are watching sodium or don't like a salty taste this probably wouldn't be for you, but when I want some salt, I want some salt.  The pepper was just enough to give them a bite without being overwhelming.  The valued added seasoning of onion/sugar combo was fine, I really couldn't tell that they were in there- I just know that I liked the taste and the size of the cashews.  Also, I like that the lid holds one serving size.  Short of portioning out your own snack bag this is a clever idea so that you don't overeat (if you don't want to).  Overall, a nice snack product.  I would definitely consider buying these when I buy flavored cashews again.

I think there are a lot of folks that will NOT like these cashews, as they are not faint.  Imagine `salt `n pepper' potatoes chips and replace the potato flavor with cashews.  It is intense, but I am addicted.  These strongly flavored cashews are truly `over-the-top' in flavor and the citric acid and granulated onion only intensify the flavor.  There really isn't anything especially nutritious about these cashews other than nuts are good for your heart, but I'd think the salt would cancel that out.  This is one of those `love it or leave it' food products and I just happen to really, really like these.

I have never thought about using salt and pepper on cashews or any other nut but I have to admit it is quite unique. I am from Texas and am rather fond of "hot". This snack has a bite to it and can stand up to any Tex-Mex jalopeno or Cajun cayenne. Since cashews are a good source for protein and a much better choice than a sugary treat, the added kick of pepper and the mixture with sea salt makes it all the more healthier. I like the canister size and shape as it fits well in the drink holder in your car for easy reach. I would recommend this product to anyone who enjoys a bit of spice to their life. Now, how about peanuts with salt & pepper?

These sea salt and pepper cashews are addictive. The seasoning makes them even more addictive than if they were just plain. Just as in Emerald's cocoa-dusted almonds, the seasoning is not overpowering. It's done just right. It's just enough to kick it up just that one extra notch. You'll be craving a drink to go with them, though. And I wouldn't recommend eating the dregs of the canister, either. The seasoning all settles down at the bottom, and if you try to eat it, it will rip your taste buds out.

I have to admit that when I first tried Emerald's Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews I didn't like them. Emerald has great cashews and I initially thought that the true quality of the cashews could not be detected because of the seasonings (besides the sea salt and pepper I could really taste onion). However, like Emerald's plain cashews, the sea salt and pepper ones are addicting and once I got used to the seasonings, I couldn't put them down. My one real complaint is that they are a bit too salty, especially when you get to the end of the can where the salt tends to settle. The cashews come in a container designed to fit into a car's cup holder and the lid holds 1.5 ounce serving of nuts which is the FDA daily recommendation for good heart health. The cashews have no trans fats, are high in protein and are a good source of iron and zinc. Although they are seasoned, there are only 160 calories per serving which is the same number of calories as a handful of regular cashews.Emerald's Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews are addicting and delicious.

column9: Nice, distinctive tasting treat for cashew lovers...
column10: Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews is a pleasant treat for cashew lovers. The saltiness of the product is a little intense at times, but the taste of sea salt (as opposed to ordinary table salt) combined with some nicely-flavored ground pepper does give Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews a fairly distinctive flavor... and a good one, to boot. Recommended.

column9: They are Okay Nothing to Scream about.
column10: First off the pepper flavoring is nice not too much. Just the right amount of spice.The saltiness was a turn off for me. I thought there was too much salty flavor to them. However they are good in like a salad or something. To eat on their own not so good. They do have the nice pepper flavor just  overall I thought they were a tad bit to salty for my liking . I have had other flavors of this brand I got before at a Local Grocery.This flavor here is gonna be like the crystal pepsi probably short lived. Not very good at all. Tone down on the salt and they'll be fine.
The nuts and flavouring would satisfy the palate of any lover of nuts. The product is very high quality for the price, and the nuts were rich and fresh in flavour.

I love nuts as a snack. They're good for you, high in protein (and other nutrients), and they just taste good. (Yes, they also contain fat, but if you don't overdo it, that shouldn't be of much concern.)So, after years of eating plain old nuts, I was delighted to try these Salt & Pepper Cashews. I was looking forward to trying something different, and these really have a unique flavor.They're salty, which is a nice compliment to the slightly sweet taste of the cashew, but the pepper is the real star here. It adds a perfect spicy/savory note, which wraps itself around that sweet/salty nuttiness for a real taste treat.Not too high in calories (my canister said 100 calories per serving), they should please most nut-lovers looking for something new.Enjoy!

Initially the first few cashews were lightly salted and had a definite kick with the pepper that was different but still enjoyable. As you continue to munch out of the container, the salt and pepper are much heavier and totally masks the cashew flavor. I normally don't use much added salt although I do like spicy foods. I decided to rinse them off, let them air dry and then they were tasty. Mine were not oily or any of the other quality complaints I read in other reviews. I've tried other Emerald products with varying quality issues that somewhat reflect other reviewers' complaints. Amazon will replace a faulty product within 30 days which gives peace of mind and wallet when purchasing them here.

column9: Very tasty, a few at a time.
column10: My children and husband and I LOVE nuts! I was worried these would be too strong for the children, but the 6 year old liked it, but didn't want another. The 4 year old ate an entire handful, and said he'd like more, but only with water, and the 3 year old ate about ten before she said, "These are REALLY pepper-ish!"I really enjoyed the strong taste - reminded me of beef jerky or something. But I could only eat a few - the taste is QUITE strong, but a very good taste! So, if you'd like some nuts that will hang around the house for a few days, these are great! Very fresh, good texture, and delicious, and you can't down the entire box in one sitting for sure.Sra. GoseAuthor of Spanish Fun Activity Calendar

I like the product; Emerald is always tasty, from what I've experienced. But as a casual enjoyer of cashews, and nuts in general, it's hard to say if the sea salt and pepper really add anything to the experience. If you love cashews and eat enough that you're craving something a little different, give this a try.

column9: Nice twist on an old favorite
column10: I really like Emerald's packaging for their nuts -- it fits nicely in your hand. All the easier to indulge in over-eating! It's nice to throw in my daughter's backpack for a snack on the go.As far as the salt and pepper cashews go, the adults in the house loved them but not a big hit with the kids. The pepper was too much for them. I loved the pepper but thought there was too much salt. This product claims to be a healthy snack, but I think it would be healthier with about half the salt. Don't get me wrong, they taste great as is, I just won't eat as much at one time since I'm concerned about too much salt in my diet. For me it's a guilty pleasure!

Both my husband and I are cashew lovers, so I was looking forward to these nuts.I thought the cashews were very tasty. I am not a pepper lover,  and I thought the pepper taste was fairly strong. My husband, who loves pepper, thought just the opposite - that the salt was dominant.All in all, we both recommend the nuts. They were tasty, satisfied both the urge for something sweet and salty, and they came in an attractive container.The only drawback is there is a slight aftertaste to the cashews, but I still think you should give them a try.

column9: Cashew Taste Masked by Too Much Pepper
column10: I love cashews and I love unhealthy amounts of salt.  Combined, salted cashews are my favorite snack, but the overabundance of pepper totally ruins the taste for me.  I would give this 2.5 stars if I could just because they are cashews.There is simply too much salt and pepper.  If you are need to monitor your sodium intake, you do not like pepper or you do not like spicy foods, then you should avoid these Salt and Pepper Cashews.  I never knew what heartburn felt like, that is until I ate these.  I think I have now experienced it for the first time.

These are absolutely delicious! I wasn't sure what salt and pepper cashews would taste like but I really love them. There is a salt, pepper, onion and lightly sweet flavor to them. The combination is really great. None of the flavors are over powering. Each flavor really adds something to the taste. I will definitely buy these in the future. The whole family really enjoyed them.

column9: If they eliminate the pepper, I'd recommend this product.higher.,
column10: Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper CashewI sampled a canister of Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews and like the sea salt, but they should lose the pepper, IMHO, I couldn't finish the canister. If they eliminate the pepper, I'd recommend this product.Gunner June, 2008If they eliminate the pepper, I'd recommend this product higher.

column9: Too salty and peppery for me
column10: I personally would give these a one-star rating because I thought they were awful. A friend, however, really liked them. I was disappointed after trying the cocoa flavored nuts by the same company (loved them!). These were way too salty and too peppery for my taste and left an unpleasant aftertaste.

Nuts are good for you, at least that's what I keep hearing. Cashews, I dare say, are a bit high on the fat side, but the taste is great. I like the Emerald products, not just the cashews, which are great, but also the almonds and mixed nuts. Unlike other brands, these cashews are all plump and fresh, not those sad little cashews that are used as filler. I like the salt and pepper flavor, which is delicious and just strong enough to deter one from eating too many in one sitting. These are premium nuts.

Last month, I tried some salted almonds, and while I really liked them, they were a bit too salty for me. I found myself wiping off some of the salt.These salt and pepper cashews sounded intriguing--after all, who puts pepper on nuts. So I tried a canister. And the pepper REALLY works. It makes the cashews just delicately spicy and ... well peppery. Would I buy these or give them as a gift? Absolutely.

These were much too salty for me.  I was disappointed as I love pepper but the salt and perhaps other spices overwhelmed the taste of the cashews.  My husband, on the other hand, thought they were delicious which is why I'm giving them 3 stars instead of one.  After three handfuls I had had enough.

First, let me say that I like cashews and was a littly leary of the "Salt & Pepper" labeling. I had almost made up my mind that I wasn't going to like them before I even tasted them, because who could improve on the taste of lightly salted cashews? But I was pleasantly surprised to find out that I did actually like them and that they were quite good in fact. I think it was the "Salt & Pepper" labeling that put me off. Made me think of eating vegetables or eggs for some reason. In my humble opinion, they should be labeled something like "Light Peppery Seasoning" or something like that. The black pepper flavoring is quite light and enhances the cashew taste as does the light salting. I do feel this is a matter of personal taste though as my daughter tried them and wasn't too impressed. I asked her how she would rate them on a scale of 1 to 5 and she said 3. Not bad, but not exceptionally good either. I can't say that they are exceptionally good either, but I would definetly buy them again as I enjoyed the flavor which is slightly spicy but not overpowering.

Contrary to what the Emerald folks might say, it's tough to get tired of "plain old cashews."  But you can get excited about cashews with more pizzazz and what's what Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews delivers.There's a lot to like about this snack food as long as you are aware of your/its limitations.  Yes, it's 160 calories per serving, but read the nutrition label!  A serving is defined as approximately 10 nuts!But the sea salt and pepper does provide a better kick than usual snacks and the absence of trans fat and the high protein content make them a healthful choice over a lot of other snacks... as long as you consume them in moderation.  Delicious moderation, but moderation nonetheless!

I do like cashews & pepper though I restrict my salt intake.  Obviously, salted cashews will have considerable sodium & fat--they come with the territory, but if you're seriously considering this product to purchase, then the taste/cost are paramount.  I think the cost is fairly reasonable for this relatively expensive nut (much more than peanuts) and the taste is quite good--not as good as their cocoa almonds (Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds, 11oz Canister (Pack of 4)), but pretty good.  I had to force myself not to consume the packaging (as well as the contents) on the 1st sitting.  Yum.  Enjoy!p.s. "you are what you eat" but "sometimes you feel like a nut, sometimes you don't!"

even though i love cashews, these were just too salty.  the pepper taste was great and they did taste good, but for hours after i ate them, i was so thirsty.  i don't think these would be enjoyable to most people.

column9: Not bad...but not quite what I thought it would be
column10: Emerald knows what they're doing.  So, the 3 out of 5 stars isn't a criticism.  It's mostly due to the fact that I wasn't expecting the unusual taste.The cashews are large and the seasoning is bold.  The one thing that I prompted me to look at the ingredient list is that they actually taste very TART which was not expected due to the citric acid that's included.The product is good but I could do without the "tangi-ness".  So these stayed around the house much longer than the dark-chocolate dusted almonds made by the same company.

I've tried other Emerald products but I think this one is my favorite. The Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashew is great - i love the added pepper, a non traditional flavoring (for me) on nuts.  I took it to work and had it for snack.  Delicious!

My experience.  When I ate these as the first food of the day the salt(not so much the pepper) was almost unbearable.  When I ate this after eating smothing else the salt was very tolerable.  These would be good with an ice cold beer.There seemed to be an equal amount of flavoring on eat nut.  Mostly the nuts were whole, but there were a few pieces.  The plastic container is substantial but the top is not airtight.  The unit price is around seven-fifty a pound.I enjoyed them but would not go out of my way to get them.

column9: A unique nut that bites back
column10: The Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper cashew is a break from the normal salted cashew.The back pepper adds a Cajun flavor to the obsequious cashew. The result is a unique flavor that makes other cashews seem bland by comparison. It makes me want to taste a cashew without any salt at all. The black pepper adds enough flavor that I think the salt may be unnecessary.

as another reviewer stated, my family also tested Emeralds Macona Almonds and loved them. So I was excited to try these cashews as cashews are my favorite nut.  Sadly, this product is a big time disappointment. Like many companies, Emerald is now trying the "if "blank" sells well, then "blank" with crazy added seasonings will be better".  When it's not true-it takes the simple and delicious cashew and douses it with so much seasoning that the cashew itself can no longer even be tasted.  If you like cashews then skip this product and stick with this companies simply roasted cashews instead.

Emerald's Sea Salt and Pepper cashews are moderately spiced and benefit from not being oily or heavy.  In addition to salt and a slightly spicy dose of pepper, the cashews are coated with traces of sweetness and onion.  These cashews are great to have on hand as a snack, to accompany cocktails, or to add flavor to a stir fry or vegetable dish.So why a rating of four instead of five stars?  I prefer snacks to be packaged in glass containers instead of the plastic Emerald uses (however, chances of damage in shipment are next to zero in plastic packaging, so I see their reasons).  In addition, the nuts might benefit from slightly less onion flavor.  However, these are minor gripes, and mainly a matter of personal taste.Emerald's salt and pepper cashews taste great, can be used in a variety of ways, and are a great snack to have on hand.  Recommended.

My first taste of these cashews and I felt they were too spicy from the pepper. Yet I kept craving more. My family, who like a lot of spice, loved them. They were eaten up pretty quick. I would purchase this item. I also liked the canister. Most nuts are stored in the round containers that take up a lot of space in my pantry. This would store much easier.

column9: Sea Salt and Pepper with a Hint of Cashews
column10: I love cashews and I would give just plain old unsalted cashews five stars, so it takes a lot to get a snack that's naturally five stars for me down to two stars, and that something is lots and lots of pepper.There's certainly more than a hint of pepper on these cashews.  There's actually so much that I can hardly tell I am eating cashews at all.  So, if you feel compelled to eat cashews for health reasons, like you need the fat that you'd get by sitting down in front of your favorite TV show and wolfing down a tin of 'em, and you don't want to taste them too much, I would recommend this product.  Otherwise, this is just overkill.
These nuts aren't bad, but are VERY salty. The pepper isn't too strong, and adds a different flavor to them. Probably would not purchase them in the future.

I never thought of putting pepper on nuts.  These yummy cashews were salted with sea salt and pepper, and were they ever good!  The pepper really adds some zest to the taste.  I ate almost the whole canister in one sitting.  These cashews were just that good.
Just got this and it was excellent. The salt/pepper combo adds a great flavor to the cashews.

These are the most unique nuts I've ever tasted. The product description says "light" salt and pepper, but that is not my experience. Quite salty, quite peppery, quite intense flavor. I liked them, being a lover of salty things, but a couple people I shared them with found the flavor overpowering. The container is very cool and portable, so it's great for work or sports events.

We opened and tried these cashews, and they were soon gone!  The predominant flavors of the sea salt and black pepper complement each other well.  The sea salt presents a more rounded and subtle salt sensation than ordinary table salt, and the onion, spice and natural flavor listed on the ingredients list no doubt to the excellent finish.If you eat the contents of a whole container in one sitting, as we did, you may find them a bit to salty.  This is not noticeable when eating just a few.

I received this product from Amazon Vine and I love them!  I would buy this anytime I saw them for sale!  They are so good!  The pepper adds some spice so if you don't like spicy, it won't be to your liking but I very much enjoyed this product.  Buy It!

column4: Raquel S. "Avid Amazon Fan and Kindle User"
column9: It's All About The Pepper; It Just Sneaks Up On You
column10: Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews is all about the pepper. The sea salt is nice, but it's a bit too light on these cashews. But the pepper....ahhh....the pepper.  It tastes soooo good, then the heat sneaks up on you for a good tongue curling, throat clenching burn.My husband adamantly told me to give this product a bad review. Why? Because Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews are ADDICTING to him. He can't stay away from them and doesn't know to eat these in moderation. LOL!Peppercorn's punchy taste is usually a turn-off for me. But for these Emerald cashews, it works. I've tasted other salt & pepper cashew combinations, but I like Emerald's version best. Maybe it's because of the sea salt (yummy!), or perhaps it's the quality of the cashews. Whichever it is, it won me over despite the fact I'm not a huge peppercorn fan. However, the pepper eventually does get to me. I find a small handful is more than enough at any one time.Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews. The verdict: Deliciously good peppery treat with a delicious heat that sneaks up on you. It's all about the pepper with these cashews. Keep a cold drink nearby.

column9: Spicy Cashews are Tasty and Addictive, but a bit too Salty
column10: These are good, excellent flavor, quite fresh out of the package, but a little too salty for my taste.  Not much to add, except to note that once you taste a few of these pepper and salt coated cashews, you want more of them. I like them a lot. My friends seem to like them also, but with one complaint that the salt content was too high. Everyone else (5 people) thought they were excellent as is, and would be better if they only had a good cold beer to go with them. One person thought that there was too much pepper for such a mild tasting nut (cashews). I just caught one of my friends redhanded with their fingers in the nut jar going for more.

These were a five star hit in our house. As mentioned by others, this product is not "flavored" with a hint of anything...it is generously seasoned with a decent sea salt and a (to my mouth) quality pepper. I'd say the nut holds its own for 1/3 of the taste. For us, that worked really well. This was probably the biggest hit of any nut product we've ever had. If you want pure nut and no seasoning, you'd want to run screaming from this product. You need to be a serious salt/pepper fan for it to work. It took 1 day for us to consume this 10 oz can. Not proud of that fact, but it is a measure of how much we liked them.I dislike the temporary nature of the nutritional information. I don't think it should peel off as soon as you open the product. Otherwise, I'd definitely seek out and purchase this product...it's a winner.

I was not sure about the pepper factor with this product but decided to try it out.  The pepper seasoning was actually pretty good and a different twist on the usual cashew snack.  They went way overboard with the salt, however.  This really detracted from the overall quality.  If you are a big fan of very salty items, this is your snack.  If you normally prefer moderate, low, or no salt seasoning then you should pass on this one. ( Or build up some muscle mass by shake-shake-shaking the salt off as much as possible.  :)

column9: For Committed Salt And Pepper Lovers Only
column10: The cashews used in this product are high quality and delicious like all the nuts sold by Emerald.  The handy green canister has the same functional design as the other snack products from this company I have tried.  But for my taste buds at least the salt and pepper seasoning is way way too strong. Cashews have a delicious flavor that doesn't need any enhancement or at least that's this reviewer's opinion.  I  realize some people will love this flavor (one of my family members who tried them thinks they are great) but the taste just isn't for me.

These Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews have a great flavor and are not overly oily like other nuts I've tried. They are NOT, however, for people with a low tolerance for black pepper, as there is plenty of it, clinging right to the nuts. You will notice an aftertaste of pepper that stays with you for a while. The sea salt is not overpowering, and tastes better than ordinary salt. For those who are game, this is a quality product; Iwill be seeking out other Emerald nuts to try in the future.

column9: Wow!  These are flat out great!
column10: These are tasty.  The cashews are fresh and sweet, and the pepper is understated and spicy.  The combination of salt and pepper work very very well with the sweetness of the cashew.I tried these with a beer, and with lemonade, and for a snack before dinner.  They stand up well to a complex beer.  I also had one or two with a good Cabernet Sauvignon, and I am sneaking a handful right now.As a guy who prefers sweet to salty, these are addicting and really fine.  I heartily recommend them.  I intend to buy them.  They are gone!

column9: Cashews With A Zoom And A Zing!
column10: Emerald Sea Salt And Pepper Cashews add zesty sea salt and pepper to cashew nuts, resulting in a high-protein snack with a zoom and a zing. These are great for people who like their nuts spicy but not too much so, though the pepper can burn your mouth. Overall, if you like real salt from the ocean, and you also like cashews, you'll LOVE this new snack from Emerald.

As always, Emerald provides fresh tasting, crisp nuts (we're especially fond of their almonds).  Now, comes the "but" regarding these Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews - someone had a heavy hand with the pepper.  For us, they're really hot, too spicey to be eaten by the handful and even in smaller quantities we find ourselves reaching for something to drink. They are also tasty, definitely a different flavor for cashews.  Perhaps a cocktail buffet would be a good place for them where people will just  use a spoon to serve themselves several.  But, (there's that word again) - we didn't find them appropriate for snacking or nibbling while watching TV.

I was pleasantly surprised by this product. I like salt and pepper flavors in general, but this one has a bit garlic and onion flavor to it that I liked a lot.The pepper isn't too hot, but it gives it a nice kick. The pepper flavor doesn't compare with freshly ground pepper, naturally, but it's pretty good for a commercially made product.It's a tiny bit too salty for my taste, but I know that tends to be personal preference that's different for everybody.The nuts are well roasted and crunchy. They're also a really nice size--too often I see tiny nuts that don't have much flavor. These nuts are tasty.I would get these again. These would be an interesting snack to serve to guests.
It's not that salt and pepper are a bad idea but too much is really bad.  These cashews are almost in the inedible range.  I can not recommend these at all and I really like cashews.

column9: Love cashews, but these are overly salted and peppered
column10: I love cashews and I've loved other Emerald cashews I've tried....but these are just too darned salty (and I love salt). The pepper further adds to the problem. There's just not a lot of cashew taste, because the sea salt and the pepper overpower the taste of the nuts.I would not purchase these in the store - especially since our local Kroger sells other similar Emerald brands for $6.99 for the 10 oz cannister. That's just too much money for a mouthful of salt.

I like black pepper. When I cook, I grind my own and use as much as is called for by the recipe. On those recipes that I consider "keepers" and decide to tweak, one of the most freqent changes I make is to add more pepper. I tell you all this so you will understand that I'm not a Casper Milquetoast who can't tolerate anything spicier than corn flakes. I am fond of spicy foods, and when I order them in restaurants I do NOT tell the waiter, "Mild, please".The idea of putting pepper on nuts is, I think, a good one and could work well. But there is just too much pepper in these. And not a little too much, a LOT too much.The nuts themselves seem fine. Nice and fresh with good texture. I think the amount of salt is good, but that's difficult to determine with taste buds overwhelmed by pepper.If Emerald would use a quarter to a half as much pepper, I think this could be a winner.

column9: Excellent nuts ruined by an intolerable seasoning.
column10: I was sincerely looking forward to enjoying this product and reviewing it, however, it's hard to sing the praises of anything when the roof of your mouth is on fire.Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews is a good idea gone terribly wrong. The nuts are wonderful. I plan on soaking off the seasoning and using them in a chicken recipe. But there is no possability I could eat them as the manufacturer has served them up.To be sure that this was not some oversensitivity on my part, I offered the cannister to a friend -- casually and without comment. He ate two or three and begged me for a beverage to clear his mouth, saying he thought he must be "allergic" to something in them, because they "made his mouth burn."I'm just baffled that the seasoning is this unpleasantly strong yet sold in a cannister that suggests a mild freshness. I truly regret that I could not give Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews a higher rating.

When I first opened the canister the smell of pepper was burst forth.  At the first taste, first the salt and then the pepper flavors completely overwhelmed the cashew flavor.  Finally a hint of cashew came through. When  other family members tried these their reactions were similar - too much seasoning and too little cashew.Those who are fans of cashews will  probably be disappointed that there is so little cashew flavor but those who like salt and especially those who like pepper will be pleased.  It just seems to me that there is no need to use cashews in this product, peanuts would do just fine since the salt and pepper flavors completely dominate this product.

After having the privilege to test Emerald's Marcona Almonds, I was very much looking forward to testing their Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews.  In fact, when the box came in the mail, I raced to open it so I could try out these little gems.Unfortunately, what I expected to be a favorable experience turned out to be terrible.My first taste of these nuts was like having orange pith (the white part between the peel and the orange) fried in oil, doused in a vat of salt and sugar and dipped in black pepper.  There is virtually no cashew flavor left in these little nuts.I love cashews.  I have eaten them raw and roasted in many ways for years.  This experience with Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews was an assault on my taste buds.The salt with citric acid combination is terrible.  When you combine it with the maltodextrin AND sugar, the cashew flavor is corrupted beyond recognition.  Then adding the black pepper makes it even worse.  A handful of these *nuts* is like dumping a salt shaker in your mouth.  It is almost repulsive.The nuts themselves are pretty greasy as well.I am very sorry that these cashews were treated this way.I would have preferred the graceful simplicity of simple roasted cashews with a DUSTING of sea salt and black pepper over them- nothing more.  The sugar and maltodextrin ruin this mix- and the addition of citric acid makes the finish quite bitter.  I do not like these at all.If you love sweet things and don't mind bitterness and a mouth full of salt, you might enjoy these.  However, if you love cashews and prefer the seasonings to COMPLIMENT them instead of overpower them, pass on these.

As part of the Vine Voice program, I received a canister of these nuts.I love cashews...that said, Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews are greasy and too salty and have no discernible cashew flavor, as those ingredients overpower the flavor of cashew. I would not purchase this product, as it contains sugar and maltodextrin.By the author of the award winning book, Harmonious Environment: Beautify, Detoxify and Energize Your Life, Your Home and Your Planet

These cashews are as fresh as they can be.  That's a big plus.A slight minus, though, is the overwhelming flavor of the seat salt and pepper.  I can only eat a handful before the spices make me stop.That could be a good thing, though, as the nuts last longer.  Or it could be a bad thing because I've still got the munchies.I think I'll probably stick with the plain old salted cashews from Emerald.  You can't buy better ones unless you're visiting the actual farm where they grow.

I love these cashews - they are saltier than regular salted nuts, and the pepper adds enough of a flavorful zing to make them interesting but not too hot. The problem is (and maybe it's only a problem for me!) I want to eat huge amounts! It is very difficult to just eat the "one serving" portion of these, and they are very high in fat and calories. Consider yourself warned.

column9: Emerald - Sea Salt & Pepper Cashew, 10 ounces.
column10: Personally, I enjoyed both the Marcona Almonds and the Cocoa Roast Almonds better. But I have to admit this particular choice is okay, especially the way the pepper tends to bring out the distinctive flavor. Two things to consider, try to remember to keep a napkin handy + you might want a beverage to wash it down with. Maybe not my personal first choice, but decent.

column9: Perfect Mix of Salt and Pepper
column10: I guess the title might remind some of a band, but this stuff is much better.  Too often snack foods avoid pepper, or when they do use it, they overwhelm the taste of the pepper with the salt.  This product is an exception.  The tang of the sea salt mixes well the large grained black pepper.  Emerald also uses large high quality cashews for the mix and not cheap smaller nuts that they can disguise with seasoning.  I love cashews in any event, but this product is simply the best seasoned nuts I have enjoyed for some time.

... this is a five-star taste treat for sure!Had only tasted a couple of these once before, and found them quite interesting. Cashews are a personal favorite, and have been for years. Normally don't go in for anything but lightly salted or plain cashews, and personal preference over time has ruled out the dry roasted, chocolate covered or honey roasted varieties.That being said, expected that black pepper and cashews could go together but must say that these these turned out to be a surprising taste treat. The nuts were high quality and had a fresh taste which combined surprisingly well with the pepper and sea salt. These are only 160 calories per serving, which is the same as a handful of regular cashews. They are a good source of iron and zinc, and have no trans fat.Must also note that Emerald's "On the Go" canister" is an excellent variation from the standard packaging, featuring a handy lid that seems about right to measure a single portion.Ingredients: roasted cashews, sea salt, peanut oil, black pepper, others.Serving size: 1 ounce (about 1/4 cup)Servings per container: 10Calories per serving: 160Calories from fat: 120Trans Fat: 0gPros: good sized cashews, lightly salted and a nice balance with the pepper, combined with an excellent natural buttery cashew taste. No trans fat.Cons: oil and sodium... but it's that sea salt that makes them great.Bottom Line: If you want some really flavorsome cashews, Emerald does a tremendous job with these. Will order more of them for sure...For those who prefer their cashews plain, try Emerald Nuts Cashew Halves & Pieces, 10-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 4) or Emerald Nuts Whole Cashews, 10-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 4), both of which have outstanding natural buttery cashew taste, and are packaged in the same handy canister.Warning: any of these can be habit-forming!

I LOVE cashews but I thought that these were pretty horrible.  Well, maybe horrible is too strong of a word.How about I just try to share with you what tastes I experienced and you can judge for yourself whether you want to give them a try or not:The package design is superb, a plastic container with a screw top that also fits perfectly in your car's cup-holder.  The nuts were nice and crunchy but although I like spicy things, these tasted overly peppery to me.  After you get through that, you get hit with an onion/garlic taste that lingers.  I probably should have done it beforehand, but when I tasted this I HAD to check the ingredients.  Yes, they did indeed not only pepper the cashews, they also added onion powder.Sooo... If the thought of eating crunchy cashews seasoned with black pepper, onion powder and salt sound like it might be up your alley, then by all means give these a try.  Somebody out there must like these, right?

When you're in the mood for something savory, these really fit the bill. You get the richness of cashews contrasted with the bite of black pepper. It's a unique combination, and I give them five stars.
These are great for on the go.... the family grabbed them on the way out and everyone was smiling while munching! Will order again .. Note: these are salt and pepper ..so expect the flavor!

column9: Sea Salt and Pepper - a nice change of pace
column10: I buy Emerald nuts of all kinds on a regular basis.  I tried these and found that the normal cashew taste was present with a very strong presence of salt and prettty spicy pepper.  I did not detect that much of an aftertaste. Consistency was pretty much normal for cashews.  I highly recommend - as an occasional alternative to the "normal" brand.  The novelty factor for a product with this much "zing" is pretty high.  What tastes really good with the first handful... could pretty well go south after too long.I believe that this product makes for a pretty good desk ornament - your visitors will grab one handful, rave about what a trendsetter you are, then leave you without demolishing the whole container (which happens to me regularly with their honey roasted almonds).One thing that worries me is that so many folks leaving reviews have complained about the aftertaste and consistency. I guess I will have to buy a few more containers to check on the quality control!!!All the best,Jay

Recently I had the opportunity to try and review the Emerald Salted almonds.  I gave them an overwhelmingly good review, although I had some qualms about the packaging.  The flavor was excellent.Now I have sampled the Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews. Granted people react to seasonings (salt and pepper) in  very different ways, but  the combination of salt and pepper on the cashews was not a taste bud delight.  The combination of both flavors added to the natural goodness of the cashews was disappointing.  Perhaps it would be popular in a party mix, but eaten out of the can the spices were a little too strong and distracting.  I like the idea of sea salt as opposed to normal table salt, but the pepper was not a bonus.  Edible, but not delicious...

Since I had liked the Emerald Marcona Almonds, 11.5oz Canister (Pack of 4) better than I thought I would and since I like cashews anyway, I was sure that I would like Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashew, 10oz Canister (Pack of 4).  What I didn't anticipate was how much I would LOVE them!Salt & Pepper makes an entertaining movie crime fighting duo, and in hair color it sounds a little better than "going gray", but as a flavor it did not appeal to me...until now.  I had planned to ration them out by the lid full per day, but the whole ten ounces was gone in a couple of hours.  I guess I should consider myself lucky that Amazon only sent me one canister to sample!  Some might consider the flavor a bit strong, especially if they enjoy the bare cashew taste, which is all but obliterated here.(sigh)Yet another temptation I must learn to resist!Note: I'm simply going to have to take their word for it that the "Twist-on lid locks in freshness" because mine didn't last long enough to test the claim.

Oh yum yum yum. Double plus tasty. A pow! of pepper followed by a strong left hook of salty nutty knockout.  These nuts be good.So the subtle taste of cashews is lost.  So there is also some sugar and maltodextrin in the mix.  But if you like the taste of black pepper and are looking for a bold (i.e. super strong, maybe even a burning aftertaste) experience from just a few nuts then this is it.  Good for just having a small handfull, or will be good sprinkled on an otherwise bland bed of lettice.  The light canister is egonomic, but won't be accepted by recycling programs as the plastic is index 7.

column9: Really good nuts overpowerd by the seasoning
column10: I was looking forward to trying these Salt & Pepper Cashews as I love cashews. I am disappointed though. The seasoning just overpowers the nut. It makes you want to drink something, right now! The pepper sneaks up and gets you too! I'd expect that in a chili flavored snack, I think this should be more subtle.  It's too bad as the actual quality of the nuts is good. Whole and half pieces in good shape, not too many broken pieces.I found something of interest as I read the label. It contains peanut oil. If you're allergic to peanuts but not all nuts, you need to avoid this too. Another note on the label. When you open the package you tear away the upper part of the wrapper. That takes away the top part of the nutrition label with some important information. It would have been nice to have lowered the information so it survived the opening of the package.

I love cashews and was looking forward to trying these. Unfortunately to my palate they have way too much salt and pepper. The bitterness of the salt overdose gives way to the bitterness and bite of the black pepper. The cashew flavor was completely overwhelmed as well as the pleasant subtle flavors of the onion and garlic. :P

Sea salt, pepper, cashews---are any three words, together, more capable of evoking images of love and desire? Emerald knows just how to combine them. These cashews are so delicious I can, while eating them, close my eyes and feel I'm lounging on a divan in a pasha's fragrant tent, fanned by eunuchs as a breathtakingly beautiful member of the royal family whispers seductive parables in my ear!Open a canister, close your eyes, and see where you're transported!

Emerald's Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews come in a sturdy, ergonomically designed, green-colored plastic container with an ample twist on lid that both facilitates serving and preserves the freshness of the product. The well designed and clearly written label, however, came askew and wrinkled as it is printed in a plastic paper-like material that seems to easily slip around the two large indentations on both sides of the container.The cashews themselves were of an excellent quality, with superb size, texture and freshness. The flavor experience, on the other hand, is open to interpretation. I have never used much salt in my diet so I found them salty and the pepper aftertaste marred the cashew flavor to the point of masking it. In other words, I could pretty much only taste salt and pepper with a hint of cashew. Other nuts, such as peanuts and almonds, bear seasoning better than cashews therefore the flavor concept might work better if understated. Because of my particular lack of exposure to salt I double checked my opinion with several family members and friends and without any input on my part they all pretty much agreed with me: the seasoning combo was too much for the cashews, albeit they seemed great to eat while drinking beer.They have 270 mg of sodium and 2.5g of saturated fat. The ingredients, however, are all natural and they provide a high iron, potassium and fiber content, as well as being cholesterol free.

Yes these are sea salt and pepper cashews, however they are SO salty that neither me or my husband could handle eating them. The sea salt did have a nice flavor to it (not regular old plain salt taste). However it just was really hard to eat and then we were both thirsty for long after eating a couple of handfuls.We are both black pepper lovers and we loved the black pepper taste.If only these had perhaps 1/3 the amount of sea salt with this same amount (or more) of black pepper then they would rank a 5 star rating.The nuts themselves are excellent.I have tried other nut products from this company and loved them.

column9: Love the Cashews, but a little Salty
column10: I like the Emerald brand nuts. The canister is very convenient and easy to take along. I was a bit leery about the salt and pepper flavor. It wasn't as bad as I thought. I was mainly concerned that the pepper would be too strong. I actually found the salt to be a bit overwhelming. As I got closer to the bottom of the canister, the salt taste became stronger and the nuts at the bottom were very salty-almost inedible. If you love cashews this is a nice change from just salted as the pepper gives the nut a little "kick."

These were really good cashews.  The flavor is great, though it was important to pay a bit of attention when eating as occasionaly one nut will have a insane amount of pepper, but over all a really great taste. The nuts were fresh and not too salty, which is a problem with a lot of nuts.  The container was also very nice and convenient to use.

I love cashews, and I love black pepper flavored potato chips, so when I saw these, I knew I had to try them.  At first taste, I wasn't sure what to make of them.  The pepper taste was strong, almost overpowering the cashew flavor.  But I soon found myself enjoying the flavor, even craving them.  This is certainly not a flavor for everyone, but if you prefer savory flavors to some of the sweeter nut varieties out there, give these a try.  And I have to once again comment that I love the canister these come in.  They fit well in a car cup-holder, and I can just pop the canister in my messenger for a between-class snack, without worrying that the container will pop open, scattering nuts everywhere.

I love cashews but wasn't so sure how I was going to like them with pepper added.  At first, I thought they were just okay.  I ate a few and then put them away.  A short while later, I found myself wanting a few more and this seemed to just keep happening.  The pepper makes for an interesting flavor, and when combined with the sea salt - well, they became strangely addictive.  I recommend anyone who likes cashews to give them a try!  The only reason I gave them 4 stars, though, was that some of the cashews were overwhelmed with salt.

column9: Although wary, I actually enjoyed these!
column10: I have to admit I wouldn't normally throw pepper on my cashews but I liked the combination. There are other flavors as well (a hint of garlic, I think) so the label be slightly misleading. This product is definitely worth trying. My teen loved it too and it disappeared quickly in our house.If you like unique flavor combinations and are willing to kick things up a notch, give this product a try. Odds are, you won't regret it, if the preferences of several teens, 2 adults and one bird (who flew down and ate a couple of dropped pieces - we were outside) gives you something to go on.Some other details that might be of interest: not too salty, large sized cashews, nicely roasted. There. That should do it :) Enjoy!

These reminded me of seasoned nuts I've purchased at the Indian grocery in the past, but ten times better. The cashews themselves are fresh and large with a good rich cashew taste. The pepper and salt add a wonderful flavor and the result is a very pleasant snack with a great aftertaste that kept me going back for more and more. Yes, they were a tad salty (especially the last 1/4 of the canister) but to me that was the only drawback. I can see how, if someone did NOT like spicy or peppery foods, they might be "too bold" as others have said, but come on, they are salt and PEPPER flavor...what do you expect?I plan to get some more in the near future...my canister is empty!

When I got these nuts I expected what the description said,sea salt and a 'hint' of pepper.Instead I got a salty,hot assault on my taste buds.There is no taste of cashew left.All you get is an overpowering hot,peppery mess.I would never buy these and do not recommend that you buy them either,unless all you want is heat.Then I recommend you stick your tongue in your car's cigarette lighter.The resulting taste is about the same.

I love cashews but often steer clear of anything I haven't tried (yep creature of habit) however, when 'Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews' came up for review I figured - what the heck - might as well give them a try.  The pepper is just enough to add an enticing spiciness to the nuts without overpowering them and the seasalt is perfect.I figured I'd snack on a few and save the rest for later, well I'd eat a few close it up and minutes later open the container right back up to nab a 'few' more.Will this replace my standard flavors - no, but I definitely won't overlook them and assume they aren't going to be to my liking anymore - I now know better.Of course my husband is laughing at me because he's been eating salt and pepper potato chips for about the past year and I refused to even try them.

After enjoying the Emerald Marcona Alomonds, I was really looking forward to the cashews. I love cashews and thought the Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper would be great.  However, it was evident with my first handful that there was way too much salt and pepper for my taste.  Maybe that was a good thing because it slowed down the momentum of how I usually eat cashews. Each time I had more, I had to wet a paper towel to soak up the excess seasoning.I quite imagine that for recipes that call for cashews, the pre-seasoning would probably be a welcomed addition.

I've been partial to Emerald's products so my favorable reaction to this one comes as no surprise to me.  However, I would warn that this may not be to everyone's taste - at least at first.  The sea salt definitely has more kick than the usual salted nuts and the pepper gives it a decided bite.  For those whose taste in nuts tend more towards sweeter concoctions, this may be a bit much.  But for those who like dark beer, strong coffee, and snacks with attitude, this is a welcome treat.

I was not expecting to like these, but was surprised to discover I had absent-mindedly eaten almost half the container while working at my desk for a couple of hours after first opening the package. I took the container to the kitchen where it managed to last a few more days.These are an interesting variation on the traditional salted cashews. I would not buy them instead of traditional cashews, but would be happy to have them as an occasional change of pace. One star off because the onion leaves a mild aftertaste.

These are still fattening and overpriced, but the sea salt and pepper keep the eating experience slow. Instead of munching on a whole can of fattening cashews without much flavor, you eat the nuts slowly. And they are very salty (and peppery as well). So they are still fattening but they are slowly fattening you for the feast.

As a health nut, there's nothing like picking up fresh food that's tasty and nutritious.  During breaks or on the run, Emerald's Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews are a zesty change from drab, empty-calorie snacks.Nutrition wise:  It adds a healthy dose of protein, iron, zinc, and good lipids (fats) to the nut mix.  For kids, it's a low-sugar alternative to everyday peanut butter.The designer canister fits snugly in your car beverage container, and the nifty lid is perfect for portion control. With four canisters and 10 oz. in each, you get about a month's worth of rewards--if you can control yourself.

These are a pretty good snack.  But, there's nothing extremely out of the ordinary.  After trying the cocoa covered almonds (simply delicious), I had high hopes for these babies.Don't get me wrong. They are pretty good.  But, I had some jalapeno flavored peanuts a week or so ago that were delicious.  Black pepper while it gives these a little kick is not enough for a real spice lover.  It does kind of sneak up on you after you've had a few though.BTW, the nuts are also flavored with sugar, citric acid (adds a touch of tartness, I think) onion, "spice" and "natural flavor" in addition to the sea salt and black pepper.  You can definitely taste the sugar, onion and the citric acid (kind of a citrus twang- not a lot, just a hint)  That's something I would have liked to have known before purchasing.  But the taste that comes through is the sea salt and black pepper.  Actually quite a bit of black pepper. After trying them over again, I don't like them as much as at first.If you're looking for real cashew flavor with just a hint of spiciness, these are OK- not bad at all. But, not stellar either.BTW, the lid that is a serving size is a GREAT idea for those trying to control their snack portions, which is really hard to do with something as addictive as cashews.

I think these would have been better without the pepper -- or maybe just a little less pepper.  It creates a very overpowering taste.  I can only eat 2 or 3 at a time.The cashews themselves are soft and delicious.  The packaging is nice -- resealable and recyclable.So if you like salty nuts, you may like this.  I prefer my nuts lightly salted and with just a little pepper.

So far I have tried all of Emerald's products and love them. In fact, I buy a case of their almonds every month to mix into my home-ground peanut butter.These are a little too peppery for the peanut butter recipe, but they are super for a taste-intense treat once a day.Who would have thought that pepper would work on cashews, but it does. And it's gooood!Try it.

column9: A Gift for My Worst Enemy!
column10: Ok, when you start screwing with the original delicious flavor of cashews, then you are experimenting randomly.  These do not taste good!  Plain and simple.  Pepper belongs on eggs only and NOT on cashews.  There is a tangy citrisy flavor that doesn't make it either.I honestly say, I tried a handful, husband tried a handful and we said, NO WAY!  The claim is SEA Salt, whatever that is;  I know I wouldn't drink sea water, so why would I like SEA Salt.  The cashews are hot and spicy and overall, the heavy seasonings take away the original flavor, and without original flavor you have something completely different.Cashews generally are a good source of snacks and these have no transfat which is good.  It's a good thing I have a few enemies in my lifetime, because they will deserve these!....Rizzo

There is a LOT of flavor on these nuts.  At first all I tasted was the Sea Salt, then the Black Pepper kicked in.  The flavor of the nut itself is very hidden.The label on the can has the following information:Nutrition Facts:Total Fat 13g (Saturated Fat 2.5g; Polyunsaturated Fat 2.5g; Monounsaturated Fat 8g)Sodium 270mgPotassium 140mgTotal Carbohydrate 8g (Dietary Fiber 2g; Sugars 2g)Protein 4gIngredients: Roasted Cashews (cashews, peanut and/or cottonseed oil), Sea Salt, Peanut Oil, Black Pepper, Maltodextrin, Sugar, Granualated Onion, Citric Acid, Spice, Natural Flavor.Allery Information: This product is processed on equipment that also processes other tree nuts or peanuts.  May contain tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, milk, soy, or sesame seeds.

I like nuts.I eat pistachios and cashews and walnuts and pecans and macadamia nuts all of the time.After all this time, I know what I like and what I don't.At first, these cashews didn't grab me.Sure, they are a good quality nut and are crunchy and "fresh."But the spicing was not something I was used to.  I usually like my nuts plain or lightly salted.  The seasoning here seemed a bit extreme.However, by the time I reached the "bottom of the barrel," these nuts had grown on me and I have to say they are pretty darn good.  The spicing really suits the cashews.  If you like salty, peppery nuts with a very strong onion aftertaste, then you will really enjoy this offering from Emerald. They also make some Cocoa Roasted Almonds that I just have to try.  But if you like your nuts fairly plain, I would steer clear of the strong flavor these nuts offer and instead get something like Emerald Nuts Whole Cashews, 4.5-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 12).Overall recommended if you are a little adventurous with your nuts.  :')

column4: Jean  Yates "jean, jewelry designer, book and...
column9: Grab this can of fantastic cashews and don't let go!
column10: Your friends and family may envy you...when you show them these incredible cashews spiced up slightly (do not worry--your mouth is not set on fire!) by the sea salt and the pepper. My only advice is, unless you don't want to have any left by the end of an hour or so, DON'T share. I know that is not nice of me to say, but these cashews are so phenomenally delicious, you will end up with an empty green pencil holder (one idea I had for what to do with the can after my can of nuts was empty because of my family eating all of the nuts) and just a fleeting memory of your incredible delicious Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews by Emerald. Yes! It can hurt to love something this much! I should have hid these!!! Wow! Five stars for these cashews!

column9: Cashews are very fresh, but much too salty, sea salt questionable
column10: I'm a big fan of Emerald nuts, just check out my other reviews.  However, I was slightly disappointed in these cashews.  While they're very fresh, there was much too much seasoning, especially going overboard (haha, get it?) with the sea salt.  Furthermore, I question whether real sea salt was used, which typically has larger grain sizes than table salt.  It looks just like regular table salt.However, there is a saving grace for these nuts, and it prevented me from dishing out just 3 stars.  What to do with overly salty, peppery cashews?  Stir fry some chopped chicken breasts, and make Chinese chicken & cashews with bell peppers.  Don't bother adding salt to the chicken- just add in these cashews, and you're good to go!

column9: Pesky Little Prickly Pepper Picked for Palate Pop
column10: I am writing this review fully acknowledging that tastes are matters of personal preference, whether in music or in food. That being said, I have to come out and say I just don't like these cashews, which are practically encrusted with salt and pepper.In our family we don't salt and pepper our food liberally, so maybe my wife and I were particularly sensitive to the salt-and-pepper blast of these cashews. Again, it's a matter of taste: if you love salt and pepper, you might like these.To write a fair review, I decided to wash the seasonings off the cashews under tap water to taste the bare nut underneath. I was surprised to find that the salt and pepper didn't just rinse off. Something was making it adhere to the cashews. So I soaked and rinsed and rubbed with my fingers a little more and finally got all the seasoning off the 5 or 6 cashews I had in my hand.Once I got all the seasoning off (or so I thought), I noticed something else that surprised me: the cashews were still greasy. This wasn't intended to be a whole-day affair, so I just popped two in my mouth. The first thing I noticed was that the cashew retained a slightly crisp, roasted character even after the drenching. That was the good news. Then I dropped the remaining cashews in my mouth, and a few seconds later came the bad news: I started tasting that pesky little prickly pepper picked for palate pop, poking its way through an otherwise tasty though plain roasted cashew.If you'd like a simpler review, my wife, a no-nonsense woman, ate just a couple and said, "I hate these. Do they have those Emerald almonds with the cocoa back in stock yet?"

column4: N. Ferguson "Two, Daisy, Hannah, and Kitten"
column9: granulated onion and sugar + pepper = icky taste,  doesn't make any sense to call these "sea salt and pepper" flavor
column10: I love cashews, was VERY hungry when I opened the container, and was ready to scarf down a handful of these!Unfortunately, they are nothing like "sea salt and pepper" flavor. This is one of those weird combos of ingredients that end up tasting very artificial.  In fact, the coating of sugar, granulated onion, and salt even has a strange texture that feels sort of plastic-y on the tongue and does not seem to dissolve.  The ingredient list is ridiculously long for a product marketed to appear simple and natural.  Why was all the artificial and processed junk added, when the basics of cashews, salt, and pepper could have been so tasty?If these had truly been as advertised I'm sure I would have eaten half the container. :)  Instead, I was only able to eat 3-4 nuts, then closed up the container.  When I find time I'll try rinsing them off with hot water in a colander so that they don't have to go to waste.On a positive note, the packaging is nice-- reseals easily and is convenient.

column9: Should be called "onion and salt cashews"
column10: These cashews are awful...no, wait, awful isn't strong enough word.  Disgusting, yep, that's it.  They're disgusting.  Eating these cashews is like going to your cupboard, grabbing a container of onion salt, and eating a spoonful of it.  If that is appealing to you, then buy these cashews.  Remember to give your significant other a sloppy wet onion kiss when you're done.
They took a great nut-and ruined it by putting too much salt & pepper on it.  Usually one nut leads to another -- for those on a diet, try this nut, it will curb your desire for seconds.

column9: Tasty Cashews Somewhere Under All That Seasoning!
column10: I'm a big fan of Emerald nut products, especially their almonds, but I have to say I'm not nuts about Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews.  Cashews are generally tasty enough so all they need is a little roasting with a sprinkling of sea salt to heighten their flavor.  In this case, the poor cashews don't stand much of a chance against all the salt and, especially pepper--not to mention the granulated onion.  Where cashews are concerned, less would definitely be more!

I like salted cashews to begin with...and I just discovered that a good sprinkling of pepper makes them even better.  The taste is great. All that fruity sweetness in a cashew is brought out by the pepper. These nuts have plenty of salt and enough paper to leave the tiniest burn on the tongue.  The peppery flavor enhances the taste of the cashew and heat is just the right intensity. If you have an ultra-sensitve or immature palette and cannot abide anything spicy, you may want to give these a miss. But if like a little bite in your bite, you'll gobble these goodies down. Serve them with beer, alongside a sandwich plate, or tossed on top of any salad. They'll add a little crunch and terrific flavor.  I liked the Cocoa-poweder dusted almonds that Emerald recently introduced. They are subtle, unusual and delicate. These cashews, on the other hand, are bold...all that salt and pepper pack a lot of flavor into every nut.  The taste is so intense that one handful is very satisfying...good news for us who like to watch our calories.

Honestly I love cashews however these are a bit too strong for my liking. As others have said, too much salt and way too much pepper! Still the nuts are crunchy and fresh although I can taste some suger on them.The pepper leaves a hot aftertaste in my mouth that lasts for several minutes. I ate a 4th of the can then had to get something to drinkIf you like pepper then these are for you. If not then maybe you should get something else instead...

column9: Charlie Cashew Sez: "I Coulda Been a Contender"
column10: Like Marlon Brando in "On the Waterfront," these lovely cashews could have been a solid winner, if they had at least half the salt. Instead they remind me of the time I put a cup of salt into the cookie batch instead of sugar. There's quite a bit of pepper too, and it's nice if you like things peppery now and then, and most of us do.The best one can do is try to shake or paper towel some of the salt off (unfortunately this takes the pepper off as well) and sprinkle the nuts on a simple salad with just oil and vinegar for dressing, or perhaps nibble them along with some very plain veggies, like celery sticks. Serving size is listed as 1 oz. (1/4 cup) which gives you 160 calories, 4 grams of protein, and 270 mg of the dreaded sodium.Like other Emerald nuts that I have really liked, Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews would have been delicious and a 5 star item with much less salt, so they are a disappointment. Perhaps Emerald can change their recipe a little to give us "menos sal y mas pimienta." The sturdy container has many "post nut" uses, with a label that comes off easily, a lid that screws on tightly with ease, and a shape that fits the palm of your hand, as well as the cup holder in your car.

I love cashews, so I was intrigued by this product. However I found it very disappointing: there is way too much salt on the nuts, which covers the flavor instead of highlighting the natural sweetness of the cashews.Also, they could have chosen a more environment friendly packaging, like recyclable see-through plastic, which is also less likely to leach into the foods contained within.

I love Cashew nuts and spicy foods, so I thought this would be a good combination.  Unfortunately, the nuts were too salty for my taste.  I have tried other snacks with Sea Salt that I found enjoyable, but I cannot recommend this product.  I will wash the seasonings off of these Cashews and  add them to a spicy soup.

column9: Purchase only if you have more willpower than me
column10: This is the easiest review I have ever written. I am in love with a nut (my spouse is too...and both of us really like these cashews).I like cashews plain or salted...I like salt & pepper potato chips. So I couldn't say no to this product when I saw it on Amazon (I have yet to see it in my local grocery which is probably a good thing). From the first taste, I really was in snack heaven. I very easily could have eaten the entire canister. They are lightly salted & lightly peppered with just a hint of onion. There is very little pepper-burn that some aggressive chips can have. If you stick to the serving size (difficult) they're only 120 calories. Fantastic.I don't give many five star reviews, there's always room for improvement. At 4.75 a canister, I guess these could be cheaper...but that's comparable to lower quality grocery store cashews & they taste much better.They're also available at a slightly higher price point (per ounce) in 2 oz. packs. If you DON'T have more will power than me, I would suggest buying them that way to avoid overindulgence...but who am I to talk? I'm having a little baggie of them for breakfast right now!

column9: Should Be Called Onion, Sea Salt, & Pepper Cashews
column10: This is the second type of nuts that I have tried from Emerald with the other being the Cocoa Roast Almonds.  While the almonds were a sweet and salty snack, these are salty and spicy.  As with the Almonds, the lid measures a 1/4 cup serving of nuts.  After eating these for a few days, here are my impressions.As you can tell from the headline, these didn't turn out to be quite what I was expecting.  Granulated onion is listed on the ingredients along with "spices", but the onion flavor comes through rather strongly with the salt and the pepper.  While the taste grew on my pretty quickly, I found that these made me very thirsty.  Compared to the 25 mg of sodium in the Cocoa Roast Almonds, these cashews clock in at 270 mg.  The almonds also win with 210 mg of potassium versus only 140 mg in the cashews.In the end, though, the taste is what is going to make or break this product for most people.  What you need to know is that the flavor of these cashews is very strong, and it doesn't come from the cashews themselves.  If a strong salt, pepper, and onion flavor is what you are looking for in a snack, this will be right up your alley.  For me personally, they are something that I wouldn't turn down if someone offered them to me.  However, I probably won't go out of my way to buy more of them.  Finally as with all nuts you have to be disciplined because the serving size is small for the calories you get.
Holy cow... way too much salt and pepper... There is nothing good about this seasoning.  It completely wipes out the taste of the nut.
These are really great nuts.One thing though, they have too much salt and pepper.Just use a strainer and shake them for a few minutes.

Wow!  Someone likes Salt and Pepper way too much over at Emerald.  I got a coupon for it so I thought I would try it.  Didn't like them - I will go back to buying Planters Salt-n-Pepper.  The Planters has just the right mix of seasonings.

These cashews have a good texture, solid with the right amount of crunch and softness for a cashew. The extra salt and loads of pepper give my very weak taste buds something to experience. I am a cancer survivor who has lost much of my taste buds going through radiation and chemo so these nuts are enjoyable and not too hot at all for me.

Nobody likes salt more than me.  And I love cashews.  So it really means something when I tell you these are too salty.  Sorry.  I was ready to love them but it just didn't happen that way.  Seriously, I'm someone who finished a bag of pretzels and then pours the remaining salt and crumbs right down my throat.  I like salty.  But I could only eat a few of these cashews before feeling like I was baking in a kiln.

column9: WAY too much seasoning, both pepper and salt!!
column10: I tried to like these, but they were just COVERED with salt and mostly pepper, way, way, too much.  I ended up using them in stir-fry and didn't have to add any salt and pepper to the dish!!  I don't recommend them at all unless you REALLY like lots of seasoning (and I THOUGHT I liked salt!).

column9: Like cashews? Bet you can't eat just one!
column10: Had only tasted a couple of these once before, and found them quite interesting. But if you're going to do a taste test the right way, you really need to get a canister of these for yourself: Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashew, 10oz Canister. Cashews are a personal favorite, and have been for years. Normally don't go in for anything but lightly salted or plain cashews, and personal preference over time has ruled out the dry roasted, chocolate covered or honey roasted varieties.That being said, expected that black pepper and cashews could go together but must say that these these turned out to be a surprising taste treat. The nuts were high quality and had a fresh taste which combined surprisingly well with the pepper and sea salt. These are only 160 calories per serving, which is the same as a handful of regular cashews. They are a good source of iron and zinc, and have no trans fat.Must also note that Emerald's "On the Go" canister" is an excellent variation from the standard packaging, featuring a handy lid that seems about right to measure a single portion.You can also get the same thing in a different packaging here: Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashew, 2-Ounce Bags (Pack of 24).Ingredients: roasted cashews, sea salt, peanut oil, black pepper, others.Serving size: 1 ounce (about 1/4 cup)Servings per container: 10Calories per serving: 160Calories from fat: 120Trans Fat: 0gPros: good sized cashews, lightly salted and a nice balance with the pepper, combined with an excellent natural buttery cashew taste. No trans fat.Cons: oil and sodium... but it's that sea salt that makes them great.Bottom Line: If you want some really flavorsome cashews, Emerald does a tremendous job with these. Will order more of them for sure...For those who prefer their cashews plain, try Emerald Nuts Cashew Halves & Pieces, 4.5-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 12) or Emerald Nuts Whole Cashews, 10-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 4), both of which have outstanding natural buttery cashew taste, and are packaged in the same or similar handy canisters.Warning: any of these can be habit-forming!

column9: Only if you really enjoy processed foods
column10: I enjoy cashews and thought these would be a tasty variation. I eagerly bit into my first one and was replused by the oily taste. Since I always make my kids take 3 bites of everything, I kept chewing. It didn't get any better. Soon a salty taste mixed in with the oil, followed by the flavor of stale dimestore pepper - the kind grandmas keep in a tin in their cupboard for years because no one uses it. After completing the first tortureous bite, I ate 2 more nuts just to be sure they were not some acquired taste or novelty I may be missing out on. They were not.
