Took a good brushing and rinsing with Listerine to burn the flavor out of my mouth.I gave them 2 stars because I eat a lot of fresh foods and an above average amount of raw foods. Some one more used to a processed food flavor might find them more desirable than I did.

column4: Carbonadam "Ladies and gentleman, I hope that...
column10: As a nut the Cashew is one of my favorites. The pepper flavor was interesting and added a unique flavor to this already great nut. The salt was a bit much. Salt tastes good but i would cut the salt by 75% here. It was very overpowering and required water almost immediately.

column9: Not just salt and pepper! Onion and Mystery Spice Too!
column10: These are very strongly seasoned, with not only salt and pepper, but also sugar, granulated onion, citric acid, and mystery "spice." (I've uploaded a photo of the label above).I find them unpleasant for two reasons -- 1) they're just FAR too strongly seasoned and 2) I do not enjoy the pepper/onion/mystery-spice combination.  I can definitely taste the onion and citric acid (provides a bit of tartness), and cannot quite put my finger on the mystery spice.The nuts themselves are reasonably sized, most are whole or halves, with some broken pieces.  I've uploaded a photo above so you can see them.But ugh.  The taste is just not for me, and there is too much of it.  I think the rare person who really likes the salt/pepper/onion/mystery-spice flavor might enjoy these, as at least one reviewer has, but I'll pass in the future -- and I *LOVE* cashews in general.  The might be good to cook with, adding to a dish with no prior seasoning to add cashew and spice flavor!

column9: Simple but delicious combo, unless you don't like pepper.
column10: I've noticed in the last few years the tendency of companies to try to dress up normal every day products by adding something new: Lime Coke, Vanilla Coke, vitamin coke, Lemon Coke, you get the idea. Sometimes it just gets ridiculous.Anyway, I like cashews, though I don't eat them too often compared to almonds and peanuts. I usually avoid salty snacks, but find the sea salt and pepper a good combination and the container is a nice size and design. I could see these being especially good with/ after a couple of beers.

I love cashews, and the idea of these yummy nuts with a dash of sea salt and pepper sounded inspired. However, the result is way too salty. If there was one-tenth the amount of salt, I might have tasted the pepper and -- even better -- the nuts.Another problem is the twist-on lid. It doesn't stay secure, which means the nuts are going to get stale, and maybe spill.

I love salted cashew nuts spiced up with cayenne pepper, but this product is way too salty and hot. Cayenne pepper powder and salt lumps were found at the bottom of the canister. The product description says, it has "a hint of pepper," but this is an understatement. I have to say this is not one of the best Emerald products.1. Cashew Party Bag - 5 lbs.2. Whole Cashews, Rstd/Salted 8 oz.3. Snacking Sensations-Almond Brothers Gourmet Nut Tray4. Pecan Paradise-Almond Brothers Gourmet Pecan Tray5. Everybody's Pistachios-SALT + Pepper

column9: Too salty, a little too oily and overpriced!
column10: I found these cashews too salty and peppery for my taste. There is also a hint of onion flavor with some citric acid to give them a slightly sour taste. Some cashews were almost completely encrusted with coarse salt making them almost bitter in taste. I found it hard to have more than 2-3 cashews at one time. Combining a handful of these cashews with a cocktail is a sure way to get heartburn!The price is also on the higher side. I prefer the store branded lightly salted and far less oily tinned cashews you can get at any grocery store to these.

column9: Strong Kick Takes Away From Natural Taste of Cashews
column10: Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews are advertised as an alternative to "plain old cashews".  And while the combination of salt and pepper create an interesting flavor and an almost elegant alternative to most snack junk food, I am a big fan of the natural taste of cashews and think this product is essential a "fix" to an unbroken staple of American snacks.If someone does not enjoy the natural taste of cashews, however, then this product does present a clear change and certainly an upgrade.  The salt and pepper combine for an irresistible, slightly hot combination that's hard to put down (if you have plenty to drink, of course).Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews come packaged in the kind of handy plastic cylinder with a sturdy lid that my grandma would wash and use to store sewing supplies.  Even more appealing is that the canister fits perfectly in a car's cup holder, and the lid is designed to hold exactly one 160 calories serving.

column9: Too salty and peppery for my taste
column10: The Sea Salt and Pepper cashews from Emerald were okay.  They weren't as delicious as the almonds I reviewed the last time around.  I felt that thesalt and black pepper were just too overpowering for my palate. If they toned down the seasoning, then you might have something.  That's my only complaint with the product, otherwise they were good.  The cashews were nice and fresh and I love the sea salt flavor.If only they would ease up on the salt and pepper.  I would mildly recommend this product.

The new Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews are a bartender's best friend.  Every bar in town should have a dish of these prominently displayed for their customers to enjoy--and in return many cocktails will be served.  These cashews are not for the faint of heart.  I love salty snacks--especially those salt & sour potato chips--and cashews are my favorite nut, so I was very interested in trying Emerald's new brand.  The natural sea salt is great--but the "hint" of pepper is overpowering.  It was way too much seasoning for me.  Eat too many of these and you'll need a few cocktails or glasses of water.  I think I'll stick with my regular old tired boring cashews from now on.  But I'm sure some folks might really like the pepper seasoning--like bartenders looking to serve a lot of drinks.

I was quite excited to try these nuts and equally disappointed upon putting them in my mouth.  They're greasy, not crispy and dry as I'd expected.  This is a bummer both from a mouth-feel perspective (the nuts just don't feel right!) and from a sticky-smelly-mess-in-your-hands perspective as well.I've had some wonderful sweet nuts and also savory nuts that are baked just right.  These nuts, however, taste soggy, oily.  And given how much I love both cashews and pepper... what a shame! :-(

column9: A strangely exotic treat that grows on you... but bring water!
column10: Okay, it's almost impossible to screw up cashews.  So, that'll net three stars right there.  The idea behind these seasonings had me worried, though.  It was so obvious that someone must've been avoiding it for a reason.  After enjoying them, I'm not sure why this wasn't done a long time ago.  In short, the snack works.  I had seen the Emerald Robert Goulet ad and knew that the company was being run by mad geniuses, but I could never find the brand.  Until now.  A quick breakdown...THE BAD:They really lay on the "sea salt."  And I find the idea of "sea salt" vaguely pretentious.  It all tastes like salt to this Philistine.  Anyway, there's a lot of it here.  Make sure you have cocktails (these go very well with martinis, gin & tonics, or scotch), sodas, or water to mitigate the mouth-puckering amount of salt.THE GOOD:Great container... for one person.  Easily fits into a car or movie theater cup-holder.  (Of course, the squatter Planter's containers double as nut bowls, but then, they're useless on the go.)  If you're on your own, you can pretty much "drink" the snack out of the container.  If you just lick the seasonings off the nut before biting in, as a friend of mine did, you won't get a fair idea of why they're good.  The flavors -- salt, pepper, and the buttery cashew taste -- only work when you've chewed them together.  At that point, food chemistry takes over and the mix takes on a sophisticated zing.Overall, an oddball snack with an air of hoity-toity, cocktail-hour sophistication.  This is the eccentric, world-traveler uncle of snacks.  A wacky-yet-bland idea that works best after you've melded the flavors for a few bites.  And I commend Emerald on one other point.  Nuts are my favorite snack, and I tend to stick to the traditional brands -- Planter's, Diamond, Mauna Loa.  These were of an equal quality -- large, not broken into pieces (mostly), faintly sweet, and very fresh.PS --Since writing this review, I found a similar product at World Market.  The Emerald brand is far superior.

column9: Too Salty and Too Peppery Cashews
column10: Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews were quite a disappointment.  The cashews are rather small and a bit broken up (which could have been from the shipping) although they seem to be of good quality.  The problem with this product, however, is that it goes way overboard on the salt and pepper spices.  They nuts are too salty and too peppery and just not very enjoyable.  And they get even more salty and more peppery, thus less pleasant, the further down the container you go.I love cashews, but these are ruined by the spices.

column9: How could they do this to cashews?
column10: I love cashews, but Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews have too much pepper on them for me.  They look dirty, taste peppery, and leave a burning sensation in my mouth.  The pepper takes over completely and there is very little actual cashew-taste.Emerald has some good products, like the Emerald Marcona Almonds, but this time I think they are trying too hard to be different.  I am definitely disappointed and would not buy this product.PS.  I rinsed them off and they tasted fine.  (Hardly an endorsement.)

I have the feeling that people are either going to love this or hate it.  For me, I hated it.  The salt and pepper combo is extremely aggressive.  The chunks of salt are so large that sometimes they make a {crunch} when you bite down on a particularly large one.  The pepper is also large flakes and there is a lot of it.After just a few of these I felt a bit sick to my stomach and now even the thought of them makes me a little queasy.  I have loved the Emerald product line up until this one.  I do give them respect for taking chances but I think they went too aggressive on this one.

I enjoy a variety of nuts for snacks and cooking. This is definitely more the snack-variety.  I liked that the nuts tasted very fresh and had a pleasant aroma when I opened the canister. The canister itself is very convenient and wide enough to reach into for the snack without scraping your knuckles on a rough plastic rim.  The pepper flavor is significant, but not overpowering. A good balance.  However, I like salty snacks, but found this to be a little too salty, even at the risk of drowning out the flavor of the cashew.  If you like VERY salty, these are good, but if you like mildly salty, steer clear.  I can't even imagine how the ones on the bottom of the canister would taste.

My first impression of these cashews was that they are very salty.  Sea salt has a stronger flavor than traditional salt and it comes through in spades in these.  So, those who don't like or want too much salt may not want to try these.  Also, true cashew lovers may not appreciate them since the salt and pepper seasoning *almost* overpowers the nuts.  That I said, after the initial startlement, I found I liked them very much.I don't usually care for cashews since they are softer than other nuts I prefer.  But the extra spicy aspect the pepper gives these (and I admit to loving salt) make them a nice change.  I needed a large glass of ice water, but I did enjoy eating them!  I would buy them again, though not in bulk as offered through Amazon.  They are too strong for regular snacking.  However, if they ever offer a mixed nut selection I wouldn't hesitate if these were included.  Recommended to those who like salty treats, and those looking for something different.

Wow... VERY peppery! I love cashews, and I love salted cashews, so "Salt and Pepper" Cashews sounded intriguing... unfortunately, this product has too much pepper for me. The pepper overpowered the taste of the cashews. I would never buy these. I'll stick with good old salted cashews.

column9: Way too much pepper (and salt and sugar and onion, oh my!)
column10: First off, let's start with the product description for these cashews that appears on the product page: "Lightly roasted with natural sea salt and a hint of pepper - Value added seasoning for the consumer who is tired of plain old cashews." From reading that description, one would assume that these cashews have "a hint of pepper." That is not the case. These cashews are LOADED with pepper. When I first opened the container and saw these nuts, it looked like someone had wet them and dredged them in black pepper. And believe me...You can taste the pepper; and it stays with you. Very, very spicy. Too much so for me. I also agree with other reviewers who have said the nuts are too salty. WAY too salty, with 270mg of sodium in a single 1 oz. serving. Now, back to the "value added seasoning" description...Nowhere in the product description does it mention that these nuts have SUGAR added to them. Sugar? With salt and pepper? Add that to the "granulated onion" that also appears on the list of ingredients and maybe you can understand what I mean when I say that there's just a bit too much going on here flavorwise. You can't even taste the nuts!! I love cashews. And I love seasoned cashews. But these just don't make the grade. I think my biggest complaint is definitely the amount of pepper that are on these. It's WAY more than a "hint." Stay away from these nuts unless you want to make your taste buds very, very angry and give yourself some major heartburn.

After trying Emerald's Sea Salt & Pepper cashews, my household reached a general consensus. We would rather NOT have pepper on our cashews. While there were varying levels of dislike throughout the house, nobody really liked them. My sister thought they were disgusting. My dad, who LOVES cashews, will hardly touch them. I thought they were alright, but they're not something I'd want to eat a lot of.The pepper definitely adds a zest to the cashews. Whether that's good or bad... I guess it depends on your personal preference. If you love nuts & cashews, and you're tired of the same old thing, I'd suggest giving them a try. While I'd rather pass on the pepper, I did like the fact that they used sea salt, which is better for you (nutritionally) than regular old salt.I cautiously recommend this product to anyone who likes a bold flavor.

After Emerald's disappointing cocoa-powder covered almonds, I expected these to be better. If anything, they're slightly worse.Pepper seems a complementary taste for cashews. But there's too much pepper, and way too much salt. They smother the cashew taste. Though the cashews are of good quality (off-brands can be Really Lousy), their texture isn't quite as crisp as I'd like. (Granted, cashews aren't particularly crisp to begin with.)The cannister is nice -- ergonomic and sturdy. I can see buying this product simply to get the cannister to hold plain nuts or other snacks. (Lead balls, too.)Most nuts are sold "plain", with only a bit of garnishment (salt or mild spices), and for a good reason -- nuts taste good by themselves. They don't need enhancement. If Diamond (the "synomymous with walnuts" company that makes Emerald products) is trying to enhance their profits by "enhancing" their products, they're not doing it very well. I'd rather have a can of Planter's, thank you.

column9: Spicy Flavor Almost Totally Hides the Taste of the Cashews: Good for a Snack with Beer
column10: If you didn't like the taste of cashews, you probably wouldn't eat them. But this product seems designed for people who don't like the flavor of the nuts.Your mouth is hit with lots of saltiness first, quickly followed by warmth from the pepper. You can get the same experience by sprinkling some salt and pepper on your hand and licking the spices.No one could eat very many of these without a beer or other beverage that complements the saltiness and pepper.The package shows lots of perfect cashews, but my package contained more broken pieces and halves than complete cashews. The package needed to be filled more completely to avoid breakage in shipment. These don't look good enough to serve to guests.Stick to regular cashews!

My hubby loves salt and pepper anything and I had purchased other brands of Salt & Pepper Cashews in the past. He said that the Emerald were better at first: crunchier and had a more pronounced freshly-ground pepper taste. He said that they were much less salty than other brands he had tried.Update:Unfortunately, after eating them a few times, he told me that the pepper taste was becoming overwhelming and he adores freshly ground pepper, he must eat about 5 times the amount I do on food. Maybe it was just that he was eating too much at once?I did notice that he went back to the Archer Farms brand that I had in the pantry, so I don't know if he'll be finishing the Emerald brand or not.If anything changes, I'll update my review again.I like the fact that the lid fits securely and they seem to stay fresh for a long time.

Firm, Crisp, Perfectly Salted with hint of Pepper...A little on the stronger side for people who dont like spicy....But I am the Spice Queen and these are absolutely Purrrrrfect for me. Infact they go really well with Drinks...thanks to the pepper in them.If ur about flavor and taste..this one is for u.It has become a regular feature for when friends come over...besides these are quite economical.I have a thing for nuts anyways and who doesnt love cashews....Get them u wont regret it.

column9: Good nuts roasted and seasoned just right
column10: These cashews are of a nice size and are very tender and flavorful.  The sea salt and pepper used to season them is a great touch.  I thought they were delicious and ate the whole can within three days!  I gave some to my mom and she found them too peppery.  I'm not a fan of spicy food and won't even buy medium salsa yet I didn't think the cashews were overly hot.  I would recommend these to anyone except those who are acutely sensitive to pepper in any amount and if you were you wouldn't be considering buying these anyway right?

column9: Maybe too much pepper, but a good flavorful snack
column10: I think it's important to note that the "pepper" here is ground black pepper - not a spicy pepper like jalapeños - something I didn't realize when I ordered these cashews.  But, no problem, I actually like black pepper.  And I think the combination works very well here, except that there's a bit too much pepper being used - the amount could probably be cut almost in half.  And the pepper is pretty strong, like freshly ground pepper, so it gives a good strong taste, but not so much that you don't taste the cashew.  I thought it kind of overwhelmed the flavor of the sea salt but as I shared some around the office others thought the product was a bit too salty (I'm something of a salt-aholic).  Nonetheless, everyone agreed that they're good enough to be slightly addicting.As with the other Emerald nuts, the cap makes a great measuring cup for a serving - if you can limit yourself to a single serving.  It's maybe not my first choice among the many excellent Emerald products, but a good snack for anyone who likes pepper.

Emerald's Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews are top quality roasted nuts seasoned with a generous amount of black pepper and sea salt. What that means is the flavor here is very strong and spicy, and for those, like myself, who like strong flavored snacks, these are very good. However, you won't be able to eat more than a few at a time. The flavor is that strong. Of course, maybe that's better than a snack you continuously pop into your mouth until you've devoured the entire container. Some may say that the salt and pepper overpower the nut flavor here. I disagree, though the heat from the pepper definitely lingers. I'm going to give a thumbs up on this tasty product, but with a strong warning that if you don't like things hot and spicy, you won't like these. There probably is a smidge more salt and pepper than necessary, the only reason I'm not giving it the full 5 stars, so perhaps Emerald could take note of that and lighten the amount just a bit.As for the nutritional information:Calories - 160 per serving (120 from Fat), Total Fat 13g (saturated fat 2.5g, trans fat 0, polyunsaturated fat 2.5g, monounsaturated fat 8g), Cholesterol 0mg, Sodium 270mg, Potassium 140mg, Total Carbohydrate 8g, Dietary Fiber 2g, Sugars 2g, Protein 4g, Calcium 2%, Iron 25%.Ingredients: Roasted Cashews (cashews, peanut and/or cottonseed oil), Sea Salt, Peanut Oil, Black Pepper, Maltodextrin, Sugar, Granulated Onion, Citric Acid, Spice, Natural Flavor.Allergy Info: This product is processed on equipment that also processes other tree nuts or peanuts. May contain tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, milk, soy, or sesame seeds.

First of all, I'm a cashew lover, so I figured I'd like these nuts. What I didn't expect was how much I'd like the sea-salt pepper combo. There's a slight 'twang' after eating a handful of these, and they are great with a cold beer or soda. Each nut is big and bold, no little pieces in this jar. The packaging is great; good for taking along on trips. The twist lid is easy on and off. If you enjoy spice, go for these, the pepper does give a little extra kick.

column9: Not for the Faint of Heart
column10: If you're the kind of person who lets the waiter grind the pepper mill until he pulls a muscle.....these might be for you. If you're the kind of person who likes a little popcorn with their salt.....these might be for you. Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews are not for the faint of heart. This is a strongly seasoned snack. Lots of salt and lots of pepper. I really liked them, but I can see where they wouldn't be to some people's taste, and for God's sake! if you're on a sodium restricted diet, don't even be in the same room with these!

I was a little bit leery of trying out cashews with pepper on them, but I was very pleasantly suprised.  The black pepper complements the cashews well and kicks up the taste a notch.  As with all the Emerald canister products, the quality is excellent, the canister is fashioned to fit in a car cup holder and the top is a handy measuring cup for a serving. I really enjoyed them.

column9: Fantastic - but you'd better love pepper!
column10: The combination of salt, pepper and cashew does work. I really wasn't sure what I was going to think of these but was intrigued at the idea of the pepper.  The first thing you taste is a lot of salt.  And then you taste a LOT of pepper, and I do mean a lot.  In fact, even though I love black pepper, my reaction to the first couple of nibbles was not very positive.  I put it aside and tried it again awhile later and found that the taste had "grown" on me.  I now can say honestly that I love these and could see myself choosing them over plain cashews on occasion.  My 10-year-old daughter, who likes spicy food but usually does not like a lot of black pepper, says these are "awesome."  I definitely would buy again.

These are very tasty cashews. My husband's quotes are..."Amazing", "bleep those are good" and "Can we get more?" I wasn't sure about sea salt and pepper on cashews, but I think it is a good combination, too. The pepper slows me down on how fast I eat these, which makes me enjoy the flavor and taste more. While not an issue for my family, this product contains maltodextrin, which is sometimes made from wheat. As we are fans of wasabi peas, we have previously tried Emerald Wasabi Bold Peanuts, 12-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 12), but we like this flavor much better. I will buy this product again.

Given that Salt & Pepper is my favorite potato chip flavor (specifically Kettle Brand Krinkle Cut for those who might be interested) and I love cashews, I was looking forward to trying these. Alas, once again, Emerald has managed to just miss the mark.I like only enough salt in my food to enhance the taste, and the fact of the matter is that cashews are flavorful enough that not a whole lot is necessary. These nuts--which are nice and crisp and unbroken, no problem there--could easily lose 75% of their added salt and they'd be great, especially given that the black pepper used is of pretty good quality and kinda kicks in after everything has been eaten...if you can refrain from gulping your beverage of choice to slake the salt-induced thirst, that is. There's also some onion powder added, which would be a good thing if it were only discernible. But it's not because of the salt.The lion's share of the nutritional data peeled off when I opened the canister, so I'm not able to provide them (I think I can be forgiven for not rifling through the garbage). Cashews are relatively low in fat for nuts, but they're not a low-cal food by any stretch of the imagination, plus these are roasted in peanut oil as well. I personally think nuts, plain or flavored, are a great source of nutrition but only if I can actually taste them.In my experience, the single ingredient most common to mass-produced foods is salt, which seems a shame to me, especially since its misuse is so unhealthful. It's a lot easier to add salt to a dish than remove it, so if you're interested in actually tasting your food (and I think even simple, inexpensive food should and can be wonderful), let the manufacturers know. This product could easily be delicious if whoever formulated it would put a bit more finesse into it.

HOLY GUACAMOLE!!!  Never thought I'd say this, but MAN I LOVE HAVIN' THESE NUTS IN MY MOUTH!!!  As if cashews weren't already perfect enough, the Emerald guys decided that "nope; they need to be better"!  They've gone and packed a whole bunch more flavor into an affordable can of already scrumpcious cashews.  I'll admit every now & again you'll get a cashew so salty that your face'll contort into one of those stupid salt overload kinda faces, but those are few & far between.  The pepper adds a great flavor & a little heat at the tip of your tongue, it's literally unlike anything I've tasted on a cashew before, AWESOME!!!  Seriously, it was like god touched my mouth while eating these suckers.  Oh well, he giveth & he taketh away.  In the time it's taken me to write this review half of my stash is gone :(.  If you're looking for something semi-healthy this is for you.  Pimp My Cashew Baby!!!Now if only we could get some Wasabi flavored cashews (Hint! Hint! Emerald)
I love Cashews, but this product SUCKED! It had too much Pepper. I washed them off and put them in the toaster oven to freshen them up. Now they are semi descent.

I love cashews but wanted to get several different opinions so I brought this in to be enjoyed by all of my coworkers.It didn't last three minutes.Personally, I loved them.  The picture shows some cashews lightly covered in pepper but when you open this up there is no light covoring.  These things are three times as smothered in salt and pepper than the picture depicts.  The taste was fantastic!  It added a lot of flavor to cashews and brought them to an entire new level.  They do have an after-taste, but it is a good aftertaste so you can enjoy them longer than they last in your mouth.Now this is all opinion, but I hope you can trust this lover of cashews.  How quickly they disappeared amongst coworkers should be further testament to their tastiness.  One of them even hunted me down asking for more.If you love cashews, at least give these a shot.  I haven't found anybody yet who didn't enjoy them.

The product description currently states that these nuts have "a hint of pepper."  Don't you believe it.  There's at least as much pepper on these as there is salt, and there's too much of both.  I can't taste anything but the pepper when I eat them, and they're so salty that I'm thirsty afterwards.  This is a terrible product, and the company needs to seriously scale back their seasonings.

column9: WOW -- I never expected the taste on this!
column10: Do you like cashews? You've never had them like this! I have never met a nut I didn't like, so of course I volunteered to try this new product. I looked at the container and thought, hey yeah, cashew snacks -- gotta be good, right?  Well not only are these GOOD, they are completely and utterly sublime. The blend of sea salt and pepper adds just the right spice to the cashew. I could eat this snack all night! It will add a little zip to an otherwise ho hum dish of nuts at a reception or party! I am currently trying to figure out how I could use them in another recipe -- say for instance, a chinese rice and cashew chicken entree????  YUM! Get some today!
Sooo much pepper and heavy salt - reminds me of "Adams" trick food gags (garlic candy, hot pepper chewing gum, etc. ). Can't eat as is - seriously , these are fresh nuts - just over seasoned.

I picked these up at the grocery store the other day just to try them out, and boy, are they super-salty!  I can only have a couple before I have to chug a glass of water.  The pepper taste is fine but they really need to cut down on the amount of salt used.  :(

column4: James W. Cowan "Every night and every morn,"
column10: Too much, not enough, needs this and that.  This was the surprise I wasn't expecting, and I almost put them back on the shelf.  The reason I am here is to look for other nuts with the salt and pepper (and onion).  I was hoping you had peanuts with the same additions.  You have a winner here, try it with other nuts.
Not terrible. The seasoning is a bit  overpowering, a little too much onion. Cashew is a mild flavor to begin with so the seasoning was a little too much.

Found these by accident in the grocery store and fell in love. they aren't Planters but that is what makes them special. Yes,depending on the batch, the pepper can be a bit much, but that is a saving grace.  The spiciness limits intake to one serving (a capful) or you might end up eating the entire canister in one setting.  Talk about being "rich" for the system. My sister, who has no tolerance for spicy foods, actually loves them. She plans to add a couple cans to her Hurricane kit.For the past month, I have not been able to find the nuts.  Knowing that Amazon has a supply is simply great and at a cheaper price (including shipping).  Needless to say, I will be ordering a "few" cans.

I ordered the cashews and the first order I received was great...could have used more pepper, but that's just my taste. I thought they were fantastic, so I decided to autoship them. My very first autoship order was HORRIBLE!  Way, WAY overseasoned.  I didn't mind the extra pepper, but they were so salty they were inedible.  Unfortunately, I was hoping the problem was limited to only one container, so I opened them all, and they were all inedible.  I was very disappointed, so I cancelled my autoship. I see no reason to keep paying for something and you're rolling the dice on the quality.

column9: Warning: These nuts contain genetically modified ingredients.
column10: This product contains genetically modified cottonseed oil. There is no excuse for a premium nut company to be using GMO oils in its products. I'm finding it more and more difficult to find nuts that don't have GMO oils. And now Emerald has sold out too!
My new favorite snack.  While visiting my son in Richmond, had the opportunity to try these.  They are delicious.  Love them.

I got a chance to taste these cashews at my trainer's house a couple of months ago. Normally I have much better manners than to finish off an entire can of snacks offered to me at someone's home, but these cashews were fantastic. They are large, creamy and buttery cashews sprinkled (okay showered) in a luscious coating of high quality sea salt and pepper. Definitely not a treat for "blander" palettes (unless you shake off the excess)...but for someone like me for whom there can never be too much pepper, these nuts are the holy grail of snacks. The excess coating is great to season seafood and makes a terrific cashew encrusted Tilapia...just yummy.

I love cashews and I love pepper. The first time I bought these I thought they were great. Then a friend gave a canister to me as a gift and they had tried Sea Salt& Pepper cashews and they were not sure they liked them. I was surprised by their comment and then tried some of the cashews from their canister and immediately noted that they were much saltier than the cashews I had tried previously. I later tried the cashews they had given me as a gift and those too were much too salty! I thought at that time maybe it was just a "bad batch". I had almost decided to not buy any more but then gave them one more try and once again found them delicious and not too salty! I have bought more since then and some are too salty and others are not! I plan on letting Emerald (Diamond Foods) know about the inconsistency because when they are not too salty they are REALLY good!!!Update: 7/12/2012. Diamond Foods responded promptly to my complaint that the product is inconsistent by sending me a coupon for $5.99. But unfortunately the product continues to be very inconsistent. The last few packages I have bought have been way too salty--so sadly I will not purchase any more! Once again--if you are lucky enough to get a good package they are great!

column9: Too Much of a good thing
column10: Great concept but just way too much pepper. The combination would be perfect and this product would rate 5 stars if they just held back on the pepper by 50%.

column9: Flavorful; nice kick from the pepper
column10: I received a package of these in a birthday gift basket. I love cashews. I love salt. And I love pepper. So I expected them to be good, and I wasn't disappointed. The pepper gives the cashews a nice kick without being overpowering or too spicy. (Note that I like spicy food, so my palate may not match yours!) Definitely a nice change of pace from normal cashews seasoned only with salt.

column9: I do not like cashews, BUT I LOVE THESE!!
column10: I was introduced to Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews on a recent fishing trip. Someone asked if I wanted some, and I declined... "Thanks, but I don't like cashews..." I was then encouraged to try these, because they were "amazing". So I did, and I agree! I could NOT stop eating these! Ordinarily, the only nut I like are peanuts. However, these were SO awesome that I recently found myself shelling out for them in the local grocery. I took them home to my wife, who was also skeptical, and she loved them as well.Here's the deal: if you are sensitive to or do not like things that are extra salty or peppery, DO NOT buy these. You won't like them. They are not "lightly" treated -- they are heavily salted and peppered, which is (in my opinion) what makes them so great. The salt/pepper does not bother me at all, but I still make sure to have something to drink nearby!These cashews were priced at like $5-6 in my local grocery per 10oz container, so they are not cheap. But the Amazon pricing on the 4-pack is a good deal, and I'll definitely be coming back for more in the future!

I ordered these cashews at the same time I was ordering several packages of the dry roasted almonds (which are exceptionally good!).The major quibble I have with the cashews is that they do not last. They are addictive and possibly the best cashews I have ever had.The same item(s) are available at WalMart online but cost about $2.00 per unit more when using their home shipping option...whichis the point since they are not carried in most WalMart stored.

Who would have thought that these would be so freakin' great!  Once I start I have an empty can in no time!My only problem is I haven't been able to find them locally OR on Emeralds website!  I only have 2 food stores left to check . . . wish me luck!

I have purchased this particular item several times (10-12 canisters)and have been somewhat disappointed in at least half of these purchases.  I don't know how the process is done when adding the salt and pepper, but on most of the containers I have purchased, the salt and pepper did not stick to the cashew - hence, just another cashew!  I have waited for months in between purchases to see if the next canister is better - sometimes yes, normally no.  I don't know if I will continue to take a chance on purchasing these really good cashews (when S&P adhere to cashew)as they are rather expensive and I am tired of not getting what I pay for.
This are large great tasting lightly salted. I really enjoy them and they arent over powering.

These are fantastic. Despite many of the other reviews, they are a little too salty for my preference, but I don't tend to salt food anyway. As far as the pepper, I think the mix is perfect. You still get the cashew flavor coming through, but if you are used to more bland food, I can see how the pepper may seem to be too much. But if I didn't like pepper that much, I wouldn't be interested in this product anyway. My only complaint is that most of the stores in my area don't carry it. I'll be ordering through Amazon.

This product was very good! i am not sure what people were referring to when they claim "the heat was turned up in this"....maybe these folks are super sensitive to spice. I found the flavors to meld wonderfully together, a fresh tast combination! i am desi and have aquired a taste for heat, so to me, these were not in the least bit spicy...they were, in fact, tasty...salt with a bit of a pepper flavor. i loved them and couldnt keep my hands out of them! i also got rave reviews for them when they were presented as part of the appetizers for a party i had. dont be shy about trying them...they are realllyyyy good!

column9: Sea Salt and Pepper tastes like:  SEA SALT AND PEPPER
column10: I was surprised to see all the people complaining about the taste.  I thought these nuts were really good.  I enjoy mixing them with raisins.  The combo of textures and tastes when mixed with raisins is really good.  Yes, these nuts will make you thirst so have some water handy.

I am not one to play the race card, but when it comes to tea I stand firmly on my Britishness.  Tetley's British Blend is real tea, not the pallid, anemic apology for tea that skulks in silly little bags (twee bags) with strings and tags and staples and other absurd paraphernalia attached, in a vain attempt to disguise the uselessness of trying to extract any vestige of taste from the contents.  These are round, robust bags that sit purposefully at the base of the cup and mean business.  They contain real tea with real taste.  Make sure the water is boiling hot when you pour it on, give the bag a minute to soak - encourage it with a little squeezing - then add a drop of low-fat milk or a slice of lemon and enjoy a true cuppa, taking time to sneer at the poor, deluded fools around you, sipping at their pathetic rosehip infusions or vanilla flavored Lobsang Souchang Rama Gupta, or whatever it is.The shelf life is long enough for you to buy it in bulk, and Amazon's price is good, so treat yourself to a proper cuppa.  Coffee can only start your day.  Tea can make it.

Product:  Tetley British BlendSome quick terminology: a "Breakfast" tea is usually a blend of "black" teas that have been matured/fermented (until the leaves turn nearly black in color) to give an infusion that's a rich ruby color and an above-average caffine content.  Assam usually makes up the core of the blend. "English" style breakfast is a bit of a bastardized term that originally referred to a blend that was optimized for being brewed in soft water which, if you're fortunate (like I am) is the best for making tea ... soft means very pure, with negligable dissolved solids. As a general rule, if breweries like the water, it will make great tea.Ok, back to the Tetley.  My wife and I go through a lot of tea, and "Breakfast" style tea is our favorite.  Tetley's British Blend (henceforth "Tetley-BB") a very nice breakfast style blend that's also very convenient and economical.  The flow though bags are sturdy, fine woven, and infuse very well.  My only tiny nit is that if you're brewing a large pot requiring more than just one bag, you have to give it a brief stir to seperate the bags, or they'll tend to cling togethber and not infuse fully ... a problem not shared by pyramid bags.Flavor and appearance wise, the Tetley-BB brews up a bright ruby red, with good body, modest floral notes, good caffine, and a healthy tannic edge.  I like tannic tea, because I find it edgy and appetizing, rather than watery and insipid.  However, in this blend's case, the tea throws quite a bit of tannin ... enough to be noticeably staining, so you'll need to periodically scour your mugs, to remove tannin buildup.There are better teas out there, and plenty of comparable ones ("PG Tips" Pyramid Bags spring to mind) but in addition to good value, good and consistently bold floral flavor, and convenience, this one also offers relatively easy availability.Recommended.

I have looked long and hard for a great affordable everyday tea. Between us my wife and I drink about 2 1/2 to 3 liters of tea daily. This tea can be found for 4-5 cents per tea bag and holds more than other teas such as Lipton. For me a good tea should be able to sustain a long brew time to get the most flavor without an excessive tannin taste. I can brew the amount above for 5 1/2 minutes with only 3 teabags. 4 bags would suit others. We put the tea in an airpot and it tastes good all day. Just try that with Lipton "tea dust". It has been stocked in our local grocery stores over the last couple of years and I buy several boxes at a time. I bought 12 boxes from Amazon though because it was cheaper and tea keeps for months if not a year or more. I hope this tea catches on. Only 4 stars as there are other better tasting teas, such as Empress from Fairmont Hotels or a good pure Assam, but as noted this is a great economical everyday tea.

column9: D E L I C I O U S LY.......D I F F E R E N T.......A......R E A L....B A R G A I N.....!.!.!.!.!
column10: Some tea, ("herbal" teas), say they are different.  They are.  To my admittedly middle-class, (but striving to go upward!) tastes, herbal tea is awful.  "Regular", bagged American tea is not far behind, (but at least is palatable.)  I count myself very, very fortunate, though, to have sampled the delightful, tasty, wonderous delights of loose, pure Jasmine Tea, Fortum and Mason's delightful "Royal Blend Tea", F&M's "Queen Mary Tea", and the wonderous "English Blend" tea, put out by several manufacturers, including the now sadly deceased, (it was far too good a company to judge its wares 'defunct'), Jackson's of Picadilly.  ALL these "fancy" teas were wonderous, and wonderously different from the "ordinary" tea one usually finds on supermarket shelves.  Alas -- all these "extraordinary" teas had extra-ordinarily high prices -- which, sadly, keep on climbing.Tetley's British Blend Tea is a very happy medium!  Not quite as tasty as my favourite, pure Jasmine tea, Tetley's British Blend is still, wonderously, delightfully, and quite tastily, different and delicious!  It has a nice, full, rich flavoUr, as in NO (other?)supermarket tea I have ever found!  It is a "hidden treasure" in the supermarket -- and here in Amazon's grocery, as well.  I like to think of it like me -- a person of modest means who is working hard to try to find a way to enjoy the best things in life, for myself and those whom I love.  I would daresay that this "Tetley's British Blend Tea", (so neatly and conveniently placed into round, but otherwise, deceptively "ordinary" tea bags), is, indeed, "the tea of the American Dream"! : )To make the best tea, I've found that one should boil the water.  A lot.  THEN LET THE WATER RST FOR A FEW HOURS.  When the water is cold, let the water come to a boil again....but J U S T to a boil.(If you lack the time for this, then just bring the water JUST to a boil the first time.)  Mmmmmm...absolutely first-rate!!!!P.S.:  I do hope that Amazon is able to sell this wonderous tea forever, and that the "only 3 left" does not betoken either Amazon'sslow sales on this (hidden!) treasure....or, (worse!) Tetley's decision not to manufacture it any more(!)?  If either is the case, and no more can be had by the usual channels, either on Amazon or in the supermarket.....watch Ebay....and watch the prices soar for the remaining boxes!Please keep making this tea, (Tetley), and selling this tea, (Amazon), forever!In the meantime, I'm going to end this review, and buy some right now!
They right amount of tea in the bag for a true cuppa tea, british style. Wait for it on sale. I decided might as well spend the money and get a good tea you enjoy.
This British Blend is as near as we have been able to find to good British tea.....since we are British, we know about that!!!

column9: Finally!!  A good cup of tea in the USA!
column10: I found this recently at Walmart and have practically bought them out!  It is the only worthwhile tea to drink in this country.  I am convinced that the only reason the US prefers coffee is due to the poor quality of tea available here.  Anyway, if you're used to the strong, milky cuppa that is popular in the UK, this is all you need.
I love this tea.  It's just like what I used to get when I lived in Canada. It has great flavor.  I'll continue to purchase this from Amazon.  Thanks Amazon for the fast shipping.
This is tea as it should be.  Not like some of our US cheap stuff.

column9: This is what tea should taste like
column10: I drink a lot of tea, usually 2-3 liters a day. Of all the teas I have tried, Tetley British Blend and Twinings English Breakfast are my two favorites. If I had to pick one tea, it would definitely be Tetley British Blend.If you like a strong but smooth tasting tea without bitterness or a twang, Tetley BB is a tea to try. The little round tea bags are great with no bleed through. It is good for hot/iced tea, sweet or unsweetened. To me, Tetley tea BB is the perfect tasting tea. It is what tea should taste like. In my opinion, you will not find a better quality everyday tea for the price.Also, one case of Twinings Breakfast Blend, 120 tea bags, is about the same price as one case of Tetley, which is 480 tea bags. So Tetley is by far the better deal.

Tetley Tea's British Blend is our family's favorite; so much so that we have it on a subscription service through Amazon.com.  So many other teas are weak tasting, but this product tastes robust and delicious even when you add ice to the drink.  It really is a great tea.

column4: By The Grace of God Go I
column9: LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE This Tea! Cannot be without it!
column10: I take this tea with me everywhere I go in zip lock plastic bags, just in case I cannot purchase it on trips. It is the ONLY tea I will use now. I used to buy Stash and Yogi other nice lines of tea (pricier too!) but I am so in love with this, I will never buy another brand. I pray they don't stop making it. All other brands of tea now give me terrible heartburn. This one soothes my tummy and makes me a very happy woman :-) I typically purchase by the multiple boxes, such as at least 4-6 boxes at a time. I live in a very rural area and it's difficult to get out to "the store", meaning the ONE WalMart within 45 miles! LOL. Otherwise, I do all of my shopping for items like this online, which is much easier. Thanks, Tetley and thanks Amazon, for being there for me in a crunch when I was almost out of tea!

Tetley Tea by far is one of the better British Teas out there for those that do not wish to afford the expense of Twinnings. It is great to see that you can buy one of the biggest selling teas in the British Isles over here across the pond however for those that live close by to a Walmart, go and check their shelves first. Online it is $3.18 for 80 count, in my local store it is only $2.75 for 80 count and I dont have to subscribe to get a cheaper price and I dont have to wait for it to be delivered. I first missed all the good things from home but since Lays have started Salt and Vinegar "Crisps" and I can find Tetley Tea on the shelves of Walmart along with Chocolate Digestives, all I need now is to find a place that sells Crumpets and I will be in heaven.
I have tried many different black teas over the years. I've been drinking this kind for a few years now and it's by far my favorite. Strong, but not too bitter.

I was thrilled when I saw Amazon sells this product.  It is very hard to find in my area so I purchased five boxes.  I live near the Canadian border and was raised in Canada so became used to British tea.  I normally drink Red Rose (Canadian) and have since I was a child.  Now it is so difficult going across the border to get the tea so I tried and finally found one that satisfied my taste in this Tetley product.  If you are a tea drinker I think this one is so full of flavor and so close to the Canadian Red Rose you will enjoy it as I do.I noticed Amazon also sells the Canadian Red Rose but they are out of it, when it returns I will order a full supply for myself. Or may even try crossing the border again to go shopping in Canada.

column9: You'll never have tea so good in your life!
column10: When I lived in England, I used to buy this type of Tetley tea. Of all the English teas, this was my favorite. English tea is strong and mellow, whereas American tea is weak and bitter. British Tetley was the best English tea. It is nothing like American Tetley tea. Completely different. Buying this British Tetley from Amazon is no more expensive than buying regular American tea at the grocery store, postage notwithstanding. I order case after case; never get tired of it. Serve it, after steeping it in fully boiled (not just heated or warmed) water, with milk and sugar, the English way!
This is the best tasting tea I have found out of at least 30. Also has the added benifit of helping my digestive system work more properly.

It smells like tea, that's the first thing. As soon as you open the box, it permeates your breathing passages. A really nice touch is the serrated lid so that you can tear off the lid and the side top flaps to get a nice container that fits perfectly in the kitchen drawer under the counter where my kettle is. But the main thing is that you get a decent cuppa, not some "titty" tea - as they would say in old England!Tetley British Blend Premium Black, 80-Count Tea Bags (Pack of 6)

Generally, I'm a coffee drinker, but my family likes tea occasionally. My daughter is very fond of British teas. This one brews up very bold with just a ton of flavor. Most teas I won't add anything to them. This one I need to add a bit of milk or sugar to because the flavor is so strong.It's excellent iced, and one of the more affordable teas we drink.

So being from the U.S., I'm much more used to iced than hot and, honestly, that's how I prefer it, year round. I enjoy hot tea on occasion but at work I usually only have time to lug around a large lidded cup with room temp tea (I think I need not add the word "regretfully" there).As others point out, Lipton tea is lackluster at best. PG Tips is pretty easy to get over here now and usually isn't unreasonably priced. Yorkshire Gold may have an edge on PG in aroma and flavor, but only slightly - and it always costs more and has to be tracked down. I've seen Red Rose but have never tried it; ditto Twinings.What I can say is this: neither Lipton, Tips or YG ever lent themselves to enjoyable "cold brewed" tea - merely drinkable, sometimes barely, even for me, who is used to it. Which is why Lipton's big Cold Brew bags are doubly disappointing. They SHOULD make good cool/cold tea but don't. Neither do Tips or YG.Tetley, however, DOES.I had never seen Tetely until a month ago when the spouse couldn't find Tips and brought home Tetley in its colorfully glossy but subdued box. Opened it up...nice fragrance. What's this -- round bags vs pyramids or regular old squares? Intriguing. Sadly, I never got around to doing anything more with that first box than taking it to work, where it sat unused for about four weeks.It's very dry winter weather here right now so yesterday, mid-morning, I was parched. Dropped 2 Tetley rounds into the bottom of my 18 oz plastic cup, poured on frigid tap water and let it sit for awhile (don't be disgusted yet, hear me out). After maybe 20 minutes, I shook the cup, swirled it around and sipped. Wow! EXCELLENT flavor, even cool! Tips, YG nor Lipton Cold Brew had any flavor when I'd prepped them in just this fashion. Tetley cool wasn't just drinkable, but was enjoyable!I know this means of tea drinking is heresy if not sacrilege to many here, but the fact that Tetley gives so much flavor when made this way - whereas the other big brands don't - has to say a lot about its quality.Now all I have to do is buy a second box for home and try it hot, with a side-by-side comparison against Tips. I'm suspecting Tetley will come out on top. Plus, it's cheaper off the shelf.

I agreed with all these rave reviews. BUT, maybe 6-8 months ago they changed this tea and ruined it. It is pathetic as lipton or any regular tea. I like a bold flavor with cream "british style" I, even, tried 2 tea bags and  it still did not taste the same. I have used this tea for years and am exremely picky about my tea. Having tea, is a big part of our family day. I have change to british PG TIPS tea or Irish Breakfast tea. It is not the same- but, they are pretty good.
I love good, old-fashioned black english breakfast tea.  Tetley fills the bill.  Good hot or cold for ice tea.

Haven't tried this batch, but Tetleyis the best for me.  Like it w/o thebag strings., and it's strength.Wish Amazon could get straight ondeliveries here in Hoodsport.Somehow Amazon and the USPS can'tget together as to how to make aquick smooth shipment and quickdelivery.Also, I would like Amazon to cleanup my bankcard numbers they use.They keep trying to use an old,outdated one instead of thecurrent one.  We will survivebut it is a pain in the backside.  Well, you asked for it!.

Hey if my 18 year old cat will eat it, and I don't have to drive to Petsmart, then I'm a fan!Note: if your cat is a nibbler not a wolfer, give smaller portions several times a day. At first I was dumping out half a can and she would leave it and it dries out quickly. Then she wouldn't touch it. A sprinkle of water and 10 seconds in the microwave did the trick....but now I give her 1/4 can 4 times a day.

This is my favorite "soda" (coke) on the planet. Fanta Pineapple is great,and its hard to find, soooooooo.......However, as good as this is just about everybody has a similar pineappledrink in a 2 liter bottle these days. Just go to a Mexican grocery and theygot this stuff hanging from the rafters like a pinata. But if you can affordto ship 3 gallon packages of this stuff around the country, then have at it.Kookaracha ya'll! LOLWell wouldnt you know, 2 days after posting this I made a beer run and guesswhat I found on the shelves of the local chain convenience store? Glad to seethem widen the distribution...and at $1.59 I'll drink this stuff all day long!

I like this tea, but I wouldn't say this is the best tasting tea.  I have had teavana chai teas and they is amazing, but pricey.  I would say you get what you pay for with this tea.  I will finish the tea but will never buy this flavor again.

This tea tastes fresh! It has quickly become one of my favorites and I drink it almost daily. If you let it steep too long, it can definitely become too strong - but otherwise I really like the balance of flavors. You don't need to add anything to this tea, but it is good with a bit of milk and sugar or just sugar.It smells really good. Anytime someone comes to our house when we've recently made a pot of this tea they comment on the nice aroma. I've even gotten comments from people who don't like tea.If you like tea, give this a shot and you won't be disappointed. I'll be getting a second bag soon.

This tea is my absolute favorite, I drink at least one cup every day. It's soothing at night and a delicious treat in the morning. I like the balance of the chai flavor, not too overpowering like some teas. I also feel good about my purchase because it is both fair-trade and organic. The 16-oz bag is huge, much more than I expected. All in all, I could not be more pleased. I will definitely buy again!!

column9: excellent chai- FRESH!. great price for value.
column10: smell: divine. QUality: excellent. I drink this in the mornings with some milk and honey or simply with 1 sugar at work. The smell alone draws "oohs" and "aaahs" from co-workers. Taste is great, not as strong as some other chai's I have had. to the bag itself I add more cloves. at home I add some fresh ginger to the after dinner tea drink. This is one of my daily teas. Gypsy tea makes excellent teas. This made me a believer after hearing about the company. Getting some mint next. just need to find the pound bags. The price savings at a lb are incredible.
This tea arrived fresh and well packaged. It is absolutely delicious and worth every cent! I will be sure to order from here again!!! completely and absolutely satisfied!

Zhena's Gypsy tea is BY FAR the BEST tea on the market.  I have tried almost all of their tea flavors and LOVE them all.  My favorite way to drink tea is loose leaf though I have purchased BOTH their loose leaf teas and tea bags (so I can take Zhena's with me wherever I go) from Zhena's.  I highly recommend Zhena's Organic teas to certified tea lovers, such as myself, and those who are just trying tea for the first time.  You WON'T be disappointed.  Thank you Zhena's.

This black coconut chai tea is the best, beats white chai tea by a million percent.  It has a deep bold flavor & great body.  Have 2 huge mugs every morning & never tire of it.  I add a little mint tea sometimes & that just makes it better.

Of course!!  What did you expect?  Nothing has changed and it was perfect to begin with.  Do yourself a favor and buy some!  Buy some nice horseradish while you're at it - go ahead!  Be a mensch!  Why would I lie?

column9: good product but tooo expensive here
column10: 2 bags of these in Asian supermarket are only 1/4 of what they listed here.Love the products though.

column9: A Great  Flavor Adventure! (but no price bargain)
column10: These are absolutely great to eat!  The peanuts are unusually crisp and crunchy, and are delightfully spicy with the flavor of the hot red chili shards and (more exotic) Szechuan peppercorns which make your mouth tingle. The chunks of chili and little Szechuan peppercorns mixed with the peanuts are also crispy crunchy, and very potent.  I think the salt must be infused into the peanuts somehow, not sprinkled on, because I found no grains of salt.  The spices from a bag (after I sorted out the peanuts) weighed about 4 grams.My 5-star rating is based entirely on the product, not the price.  I can get these peanuts for $1.59/bag at an Asian grocery store here in Sacramento.  To send some to a friend as a gift using Amazon, with shipping costs I paid $17.92 which is $4.48/bag for four bags.If you want to try these peanuts, first see if you can find them in a local Asian market before you order from Amazon at the price I paid.
Peanuts and roasted red chilli peppers.  Definitely spicy, but not unbearable.  Great flavor.  I highly recommend, you won't be disappointed.
I did not like peanuts in a can or bag before but this one is really delicious .Will buy / order it again.
Such a ridiculous price for a 7.5 OZ pack of peanuts.It's only $1.99 for a 3.88 OZ pack in Asian markets.
These are very crunchy and the ap iciness is perfect. However, don't buy them here. Find an Asian market. The price here is ridiculous.

column9: Good nuts, but way too expensive
column10: Very good peanuts if you like the taste of Szechuan peppercorns.  They had a very strong peppercorn flavor and also a nice amount of flavor and heat from the chili peppers.  These nuts also have much more crunch than American roasted peanuts.  I like it, but some people think the Asian nuts are too hard.  My only real problem with this product is the price.  If you have an Asian market anywhere near where you live, you can buy these for less than 1/2 of what I paid for them -- and I bought them from Amazon at clearance sale price.
It tastes great and very spicy!!! But how many bags 4x 3.5 oz or 2x 3.5oz? Either way, the price is outrages.

I bought these candy rocks for decorating a dinosaur cake. They were so perfect! I used the larger jelly dinosaur eggs as large rocks near the dinosaurs, and the small rocks looked so real around a water area. They also taste great! I would use these again for sure if I make a cake with that kind of look again.

column4: A Research It Maven "Just the facts please"
column9: Dieting? Organic, low sodium, tasty, fat free chicken broth!
column10: Great product to have on hand at an excellent per can price! Really good right out of the can for a hot drink, but also tastes wonderful in any recipe. Lower sodium than others and nicely herb flavored. Highly recommended.

column9: Great broth at a great price
column10: This is one of the very few broths that doesn't have MSG as a hidden ingredient. Sometimes they hide it as yeast extract. They can even hide it in the "natural flavor" category. This is just broth, the way it should be.
Health Valley Chicken Broth is simply the best canned chicken broth available. If you want any better you have to put a chicken in a pot and make your own.

Health Valley chicken broth has been a favorite for years, ranking way above competing products. Last year the only market in our area that carried it removed it from their inventory.  Fortunately, Amazon came to our rescue and we are grateful.
I have ordered this product many times earlier, but the last shipment contained dented cans - almost every can was dented.  Either seriously or simply bent.  Not acceptable.

Very simple to prepare and very satisfying.  Strong lemongrass and ginger-like scent (guessing it's rhizome), but light on coconut flavor.  It's spicy, but not overwhelmingly so.  I also recommend adding more coconut milk in the preparation.The can says "serves 2", but it's a full meal for 1 served with rice noodles and toppings (veggies and/or meat).  It's perfect for those Thai noodle soup cravings!Ingredients as noted on the can: fish 40%, coconut milk 30%, red curry paste 10%, rhizome 10%, sugar 4%, salt 3%, spices 2%, msg 1%
i love it :) add a coconut milk with it and water make it more yumy

Worth every penny - fresh and well packed from Maine to Seattle in one day.  Packed in 2 pound "netted" packages surrounded with "blue ice" packages for refrigeration. All in a sturdy styrofoam container and boxed. Out of my 4 pound order, only 3 of the clams were broken and had to be thrown away. All the others were fresh and "closed". Cleaning and cooking instuctions included. Maine steamed clams are one of the most tender varieties - not chewy like little necks or other varieties.  Steam 10 minutes, take beard off neck, dip in butter and arrive in Heaven.

I was concerned when I got these because I don't know that much about clams but had a really amazing recipe I wanted to try. I was happily surprised after doing some research and finding out that they were okay and how to eat them. We had the most amazing dinner in the world. I will absolutely order from them again!

column9: My cats love this, and I love what it does for them
column10: Started mixing this in with my furry persons' regular commercial brand, hoping they wouldn't notice too much and still eat it. No problems there! They loved it from bite one, and now are at the point where their former dry food has been entirely phased out and they're just eating Indigo Moon as their dry food (I'd come across Indigo Moon at a local furry-person store).Within two weeks of starting to feed them Indigo Moon, both my cats' fur have become thicker, shinier, and softer with almost no shedding (whereas before, there had been plenty of shedding - even the dandruff problem with one of them has cleared up) and they also seem to have increased energy (both are five years old).Many dry foods promise "100% nutrition" results, but this one delivered even better than I'd hoped for. My cats look even more gorgeous and seem healthier. This is a keeper, especially at its price, which ran about ten dollars less than the other premium feline brands where I purchased it.

These taste great but they are more like crushed candy pieces.  I thought they would be more like sugary sprinkles (like the red and green kind that people put on cookies).  They were a little bit harder to get them to stick on the glass. So it depends on your taste.

column4: Bonnie Jo Davis "Loves to read and review books."
column10: I am addicted to this tea.  I only drink unsweetened tea and other than bottled Lipton tea there isn't much choice in the grocery aisles.  I stumbled across Sweet Leaf Lemon & Lime and it's unsweetened.  It has a very crisp, lemon and lime flavor that is so refreshing.  I love it!

column9: No sugar for double the price!
column10: This product cost more than double the cost of other flavors of tea from the same company that have sugar. Why does it cost MORE if there are fewer ingredients?!
I really like the taste of this product and feel like it is helping me feel healthier.  I enjoy putting it in my green smoothies.

This is quality sprouted flax. Tastes great, is one of the best things you can eat, has added super berries, and lasts for two years without the need for refrigeration. Wow! Also I didn't realize that the outer shell is removed with sprouting, so that makes it a lot more palatable actually. Well worth the price, I'm glad this company goes to the trouble of sprouting them.
I thought the other 2 spreads these people make were great, but this one is even better--they are all wonderful in the morning on english muffins.
Where's the chocolate? When I could study the list of ingredients, I couldn't find any cocoa or chocolate. Not bad as a cake icing.
Taste great.  Like a potato chip only in ring form.  Nice to order onlne instead of having relatives send them from Ireland.

column9: Expensive!  For $16 / lb buy a steak or go out!
