They are not overpowering with the amount of sugar other wafers have but yet are so delicious. I can't wait to try them once again.

These little wafers are yummy! My kids love them and they're a good treat to have around the house for something small. Pour them into a bowl when you have company-- you won't have any left! I like them with tea. As another reviewer stated, they're not quite as sweet as what I'm used to, but they're creamier. Yum!
I just love this little snack.  It is a very light and creamy wafer.  I usually buy it at Cost Plus but lately they are always out.  I am glad I can still find it online.

i grew up in italy and loved these wafer cookies... i had almost forgot how good they were. then i decided to order some just to refresh my memories and ended up eating 4 out of the 8 bags in less than a 24 hour period (i did have some help). everybody that tried them asked me where i got them.i bought the hazelnut ones and i think that hazelnut is such a better choice to combine with chocolate and cookies than peanuts like they do here in the states. i wanted my friends to try different flavors so i ordered tiramisu, vanilla and lemon.....i see they have an option to deliver them ever month or two but i think they should deliver them weekly. lol.

I have to say I was looking forward to getting my favorite cookie, without paying the local $4.89 per package.  I always buy from Amazon whenever the price is right, and they have what I want.  The packages of wafers came as expected, however when I got them, one package had it's seam split and wafers throughout the box and they were less then fresh.  The other packages appeared to have gotten excessively warm as the wafers had slid off of each other, causing a "slanted' wafer.  Not the upright wafer cookie I expected.  All in all, I will take a second look before I buy eatable items from Amazon.
The whole point of a cookie is for it to taste good!  This product tastes little better than wood.  Sorry I wasted my money.  Do NOT buy.  Save your money -- they are not worth the calories!
This is a very nice red miso from Japan, not too strong, just right balance of taste and flavors.  Goes well in seaweed soups.  I will order again.

I love hint water so when I saw they offered hint fizz I had to try it. It is the worst thing I have ever tasted. Straight soda water with absolutely no HINT of watermelon. I wrote to the company regarding any form of customer satisfaction guarantee and as of now I have not heard from them.  This has been 2 weeks now.

I really wanted to enjoy these flax crackers. I like the fact they are organic, raw (dehydrated at low temp), etc. They are a healthy snack food, although they are difficult to eat without plenty of liquids (they kinda congeal/clump in mouth, making it hard to swallow). That having been said, they are simply overpriced. If you have a dehydrator tray or some ingenuity, you can save 90% (a pound of organic flax is about 2$). I prefer the Foods Alive brand instead, if one absolutely must buy pre-made flax crackers (Their mexican flavored are very good, and do not contain liquid aminos (soy), like this brand does, for those who avoid it)

These wafer crisps are very healthy, with a nice flavor. Don't buy them expecting anything sweet. And don't expect anything like a potato chip, which usually have added sugar. Flax Snax go great with raw almonds and walnuts, as an example of how to combine them with something else for an extraordinarily healthy snack (as long as you don't eat too much).

I had a previous review saying it was not strong enough. But then I read the instructions. After pouring the almost boiling water over, it needs to brew for a full FIVE Minutes. I was used to black teas that brew up quite strong in a minute or so...Also, I had gone back to the Co-op and tried some of the more expensive oolongs but didn't find their flavor or strength to be any better than this.
This tea is OK with a mild flavor.  There are "stems" in the tea I received but this doesn't disrupt the flavor.  The price is exceptional making the tea a good buy.

Compared to the Numi Oolong loose leaf teas, this one is about half the price.  The loose tea is comprised of almost all leaves, with just a sprinkle of sprigs.  In the mouth, the tea is mild with slight roasted quality, quite harmonious but not very distinctive.  It is a pleasant but definitely lacking character, especially when you compared it to the Numi Iron Goddess or Bao Hai Oolong varietals.  Nice for the money, but I think I would rather pay twice as much for a better Oolong.

column9: Can Not Beat this Price for Wulong
column10: Before trying this tea I had only had oolong from a tea bag. I found this to be a nice full leaf tea. The first cup I made was a bit "earthy" for my taste but since I am dieting and I wanted something affordable enough to make at least 3 cups a day. I did some research.I found that some recommended improving the flavor with "waking up" the leaves by pouring a small bit of hot water on them and then draining it off and adding fresh water for steeping. I also read that Oprah likes to spice hers up with a mix of cinnamon, allspice and cloves. Wow both those tips really made all the difference for me. I love this tea made that way and I love the price. I may try a small amount of a more expensive brand just to compare but for the price this combo is going to be hard to beat.

Bought this for my dad, who loves the plum tea.  Its impossible to find in the stores, so he was happy.  Delicious mild white tea with a scent that will make you close your eyes and sigh.  Shipping was fast, price was right.  We are all thrilled with this purchase.

Salada's Asian Plum is my favorite white tea flavor, hands down, over all other brands/flavorings in white teas that I have tried. It has just the right amount of sweetness, and just enough caffeine to get me going without giving me the shakes.  It's smooth, not bitter, and very satisfying.

I like the tea product but the advertisement is misleading. It states 2-count  (pack of 6) but it should read 20 count ( pack of 6).The price is higher than other sources for a pack of 6 but lower than others for a 2 count (thinking it was 2 packs of 6).Please correct this in the ad.

This is my favorite tea bag tea, it has the best taste as is...just add hot water, no milk, cream or sweetner of any kind is needed! I wish I could buy it when I do my grocery shopping, but lacking that getting it here is good. I have friends in Plano, Tx that can buy it in stores there and ship it to me which is nice! Just an FYI  if you know anyone in Tx.

column9: Looked high and low for this tea
column10: I love this tea! It has a light crisp taste with a hint of plum flavor and it smells fantastic! I started drinking it years ago when I lived in Nashville, but after moving to Michigan I had a super hard time finding it. I found it on walrmart's website but its a much better deal here on amazon. I haven't found a tea that matches it in taste and bargain. My boyfriend hates tea, but now he can't get enough of this!
The flavor is wonderful & the tea leaves a silky coating in your mouth that is strange, but quite pleasant.
this tea is really good. you don't need to add sugar or sweetener to this tea, and the smell is really good. i drink this at night.
this stuff is delicious, used with a simple syrup, (no high fructose, glucose etc.)very good!!!!
I am very pleased with this purchase. I have made tea everyday since it arrived. I will order again when I need more.

column9: Arrived slower than expected, more tea than expected
column10: Although I was initially upset with how slowly the order processed, I was impressed that one order gets you 200 bags of tea rather than the anticipated 100. A (slow) steal!

column9: Best Soy Sauce on the market!
column10: I buy this by the case because it's so hard to find! The touch of fruit flavor is the best!

column9: SIXTY SIX PERCENT SUGAR Very Little Nutritional Value
column10: First, with a Name like, "Floridas's Natural" I thought maybe they were made with fruit from, I don't know, FLORIDA!!!  Wrong! they are made in China. Aside from that, imagine a giant gummi bear run over by a steam roller.  These are not fruit leather, they are traslucent, molded strips of evaporated fruit juice that have 0% daily fiber, are 66% sugar by weight and have almost no nutritional value.

column9: Healthy & Delicious! Only 8 grams of Sugar
column10: I stumbled on this fruit snack at our local grocery store. Our children take snacks to school everyday and I'm always looking for something healthy and low in sugar and carbs for them.  This was one of my lucky finds! Here's a quick comparison against another one of our HEALTHIEST regular snack purchases:Stretch Island Fruit Leather.One flavor per box. 8 strips to a box, 9 grams sugar and 12 grams of carbs. For roughly $3. an 8 count box.Stretch Island has a grainier leathery texture and my kids like them.Florida Natural Fruit StiksAssorted flavors, 12 stiks per bag, 8 grams sugar and 10 grams carbs.  For roughly $3. a bag.Florida Natural has a slick, chewy candy texture that reminds me of Laffy Taffy.  I absolutely love the taste and taffy-like chewiness!As you can see, compared to the very healthy Stretch Island Fruit Leather - these Florida Naturals come out cheaper due to greater quantity, less sugar, less carbs and more assortment.So they are my FAVORITE fruit snack choice. :)

Very yummy treat! My 3 yr old son and I both enjoy these fruit strips!  They are very tasteful and sweet which fixes my sweet tooth craving at times. The sticks are very chewy so may not be ideal for younger children unless they suck on them. It takes a lot of chewing to get these down but doesnt bother my son or I. I highly recommend this product over most fruit snacks that have high fructose, food colorings, and other artifical flavoring. The price can't be beat either!

These are SO good.  They taste just like fruit leather.  I don't think there's a whole lot of health benefits to eating these but they aren't high in sugar or made with any corn syrup.  They are a healthier alternative for a sweet tooth :)

column9: Addicted to Florida's Naturals Fruit Products
column10: I absolutely love these fruit pockets as well as the sticks.  It's a quick snack that satisfies that sweet tooth.  And it's a great way to get a little kick if you're running low on energy and need that extra little push.

Inedible.  I purchased this to hand out for Halloween.  Luckily, we sampled it first.  It is so hard as to be almost unchewable.  Might as well serve Jolly Rancher (TM) sticks!  I was also disappointed that it is made in China.  Not that Florida is local.  But still.  I did not want to give out trinkets because I hoped to avoid made in China crap.  I failed.

I thought these would be like fruit leathers or fruit roll-ups or any fruit snack...but they are the consistency of a hard jolly rancher that has melted. Very thick, very sticky, and so chewy is hurts my jaw at times. Wouldn't buy again.
My kids loves these little chewy fruit treats.  They take them everyday for a snack or in their lunch!

column9: More like candy than a fruit snack
column10: These are very sticky and seem more like candy than a fruit snack.  I also didn't realize they were made in China when I bought them.  Overall they are ok but I am not likely to purchase again.
Much better than the "fruit snacks" I used to eat, which have almost NO fruit in them. A bit chewy because of their thickness, but I haven't lost a filling yet!

These things are great. Bag contains equal distribution of Blueberry, Orange, and Strawberry flavors. Not much of a fan of the Blueberry, but Orange and Strawberry are very good.Amazon is *really* high on this though, at least compared to local prices. My local HEB has been selling these 3/$8 for months. Maybe when and if HEB raises the price, I'll check back to see if Amazon can beat it. I'm addicted to them now.

Some folks are complaining that it's too expensive for JUST erythritol.  But this is organic erythritol fermented from cane sugar.  The Emerald Forest brand mentioned elsewhere in these reviews is not organic and certainly therefore derived from corn, which is cheaper. What's the big deal, you ask?  Well, I clicked on the Emerald Forest brand 44 lb. bag, and it's manufactured by Cargill--the big pharmaceutical and agri-business giant.  The corn they use is most likely genetically engineered. (Think Monsanto)It's worth it to me for health reasons to use the Zero, although I do sympathize with others who feel it's pricey.

column9: Depends what you use it for
column10: This stuff is a pretty good sugar substitute, but it really depends on what you use it for.If you are planning on using it in baked goods, I'd suggest that you not. The "sugar" has a slightly cooling effect when you taste it (it's hard to explain).  I tried to make cookies with it just to see how they would turn out, and they had that weird sensationy taste to them.This "sensation" (taste isn't the right word) is not very noticeable if you use it in small amounts, such as on cereal, on fruit, in smoothies (AMAZING)...and I'd imagine in coffee (I don't drink it, so I don't know).Organic Zero is sweet, and for the most part, it tastes--and even looks--like sugar (it's basically a sugar alcohol). Again, I would recommend it in small quantities, but not for baking purposes.$20ish dollars is an EXTREMELY good price for two packages. I bought some at my local co-op and ended up paying about $15 for one bag.If you're into artificial sweetners, I'd say it's worth a try--it doesn't have scary things related to it like aspartame and nutrisweet do.

I'm going to ride on the previous reviewer's comments - with the exception that I use it for baking, but use 1/2 Zero and 1/2 original sugar requirements.  I don't notice any cooling and it makes the baked items easier for me to handle (less insulin, I'm a diabetic).So far I've made pumpkin spice cookies, banana nut bread and gingerbread cookies this way and it tastes fine in all of them.

I am diabetic and have been waiting for a product like this. No nasty aftertaste at all! Try it on grapefruit, I even made some Koolade using half Splenda and half Zero. It was really refreshing.  I am anxious to bake with it, though its a bit pricey to use in larger quantities as yet.  I'm Hoping the price will go down some.  Not as sweet as sugar, but it has all the same texture and crunch. Try it, I think you will be suprised.

I bought this for my husband because I don't like him using the pink packets, and this seemed a healthier alternative.  I bought this at Whole Foods, but I think I'll buy it from Amazon from now on because it's almost half the price.I tasted this before dumping it in his coffee, and it tastes wonderful.  One of the other reviewers mentioned a "cooling" sensation - it does taste like you're eating something cold, even though it's room temperature.  It's kind of like mint in that way, but not mint-flavored.  I put a little in my own coffee (usually I prefer coffee black, but I'm testing it for this review) and it didn't give the nasty aftertaste that "pink" (saccharine), "blue" (nutrisweet), or even "yellow" (splenda) gives.  I also don't have a headache, which I get from "yellow", but then I didn't put much in my coffee - maybe a teaspoonfull.I'm nervous about health issues, but since this is made from fermented cane sugar, I can't think of any health issues that this would have, as opposed to saccharine.  I looked it up in Wikipedia, and the article on "erythritol" is informative and nerve-calming.  You should read the article if you're curious, but apparently erythritol (which this product is) is safe, has almost no side effects (like gas or bloating) unless taken in HUGE quantities, and is even safe for your teeth.  It also mentions the "cooling effect".

column9: Spendy, but non-corn source is worth it.

With any substance that might be used by a large number of people, it would be commendable if health promoting bodies and manufacturers collaborated to produce reliable statistics on rates of adverse effects and consumer acceptability, as well as proposed benefits. In the absence of this we have to go on a combination of patchy data and anecdotes. This review will seek not to duplicate needlessly information from other reviews.Amazon reviewers often note surprise at quantity needed; it's important  to distinguish bulk sweeteners such as sugars itself, and the "sugar alcohols" xanthitol, erythritol etc versus highly potent sweeteners such as aspartame, stevia, and so on.I'd confirm that erythritol works well for me in porridge and cereal, though I do not normally need them very sweet, so the quantity I use may be comparatively small. At that level I have not noticed any worsening gastro-intestinal problems.Contrary to what some have suggested, Erythritol DOES occur naturally in small amounts in regularly eaten fruits but that only assures us that it is not highly toxic. The gastro-intestinal problems presumably linked to non-absorbtion seem to be dose-related and perhaps also individuals vary in sensitivity.If we consider the very substantial health risks of diabetes and "morbid" obesity, then it seems that at least in these groups of people the benefits outweigh the disadvantages. It's worth a try! For the general population the disadvantages including cost put it probably on at best an equal footing to other minimal calorie sweeteners.Current producers for retail include: Now Foods, Wholesome Sweeteners, and Emerald ForestNOW Foods Erythritol Natural Sweetener, 1 lbEmerald Forest 5lb Erythritol SweetenerEmerald Forest Erythritol, Single Serve Packets, 100-Count Single Serve Packets (Pack of 3)Wholesome Sweeteners Zero, 12-Ounce Bag (Pack of 2)

column9: A new study reveals that this may be beneficial for your health...
column10: Recent article from WebMD about this sweetener.....-----------------------An artificial sweetener that's been shown to help people shed unwanted pounds may also lower blood pressure and cholesterol levels in people with mild or borderline high blood pressure, Chinese researchers report.The sugar substitute is called oligofructose, or OFS. It's used to replace fat or sugar and reduce the calories of foods like ice cream, dairy products, and baked goods. OFS has about 30% to 50% of the sweetness of table sugar, according to the FDA.The study involved 96 adults, ages 32 to 63, with mild or borderline hypertension. That means their systolic blood pressure reading (top number) was 120 to 139 and/or their diastolic (bottom number) reading was 80 to 89.The condition, also referred to as prehypertension, is a warning sign you may get high blood pressure -- a risk factor for heart attack and stroke -- in the future.OFS Supplements Lower Blood Pressure, CholesterolIn the study, reported at the annual meeting of the American Heart Association (AHA), participants were given either 20 grams of OFS or a placebo daily for 12 weeks."Beneficial changes in both blood pressure and cholesterol were observed in the OFS group," says researcher Dan Qu, MD, PhD, of Changhai Hospital in Shanghai, China.By the end of the 12-week period:  * Systolic blood pressure dropped an average of 6.9 points in the OFS group, compared with 3.5 in the placebo group.  * Diastolic blood pressure decreased an average of 7.3 points in the OFS group vs. 2.3 in the placebo group.  * Levels of total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein (LDL or "bad" cholesterol), and triglycerides also dropped more in participants given OFS than in those who took placebo tablets.Surprisingly, people in both groups dropped an equal amount of weight, Qu says."OFS supplements lead to reduction in blood pressure and improvements in lipid metabolism in [people with] prehypertension," he says."Further research is needed to see if taking the supplements for a period of time would decrease the [risk] of heart attacks and stroke," Qu says.Asked to comment on the findings, AHA spokeswoman Alice Lichtenstein, DSc, a nutritionist at Tufts University, tells WebMD that "the study is very interesting. But we need further study before we can make recommendations about whether people should take OFS supplements."

It has a good flavor, and if you are like me and order chipotle items off of menus when you are out, you most likely would like this sauce at home as I do.There are 110 calories per 2 Tbsp.  100 of those calories come from the 11g of fat. (Soybean oil is the main ingredient  So this is not a diet condiment, but how many are?  No different than most mayo you get.  If you want less fat, you should use salsa type toppings on your tacos.If you like chipotle flavor, this is a good sauce for your tacos and other foods.  I like it and will get it again.

This sauce really was yummy - it does have a little kick to it, though. I prefer it to the other flavors that Taco Bell also offers. My only complaint is that it was expired the day it arrived. We ate it with our fajitas that night, but I had to throw the rest of it away.

I tried two of the Taco Bell sauces: the Spicy Ranchero and the Chipotle. Both are tasty and reminiscent of the Southwest Sauce served in Subway stores. (A personal favorite.)I tried the Chipotle in a beef taco and the Ranchero with chicken. In neither case was the flavor overpowering. They were just nice flavor additions, a little extra zing, to an otherwise good meal.Of the two sauces, though, I gotta say I like the Chipotle best. The spiciness lingers longer. But not in a "get me some water now!" way. Just a nice added zing.Overall, I think they are both flavorful. Worth having around for the occasional Mexican treat.

On rare occasion, we do stop off at Taco Bell. That was why I decided to give this Chipotle Sauce a try. We tried it on sliced cucumber -- not so good. We tried it on some roast beef -- not so good.I am sure that this sauce will be loved in another home, but not mine. That "smoke" flavor was overpowering, and the taste was just heavy in an unpleasant way.Sorry bo be so critical, but our reaction was negative. We did consider mixing it with mayo or sour cream, but realized that we were only trying to dilute something we already didn't like.

I don't eat things like this but hubby LOVES anything hot or with pepper flavor.  He tried this as soon as it came today.  He spread a little bit on the sandwich he was in the middle of eating.  He says it's good!  Not super hot but has a good pepper flavor.  He says we'd buy it again and he could see putting it on salad, on burgers, dipping fries or veggies in it.  Guess we'll be buying it again soon!

column9: Not my favorite - perhaps best used in beef dishes.
column10: I had the opportunity to sample and evaluate 3 different flavors of Taco Bell's bottled sauces. These were the Jalapeno, Chipotle and Spicey Ranchero flavors. Of the 3, I personally liked the Jalapeno flavor the most with the Spicey Ranchero coming in a close second. The flavors are bold so a little sauce goes a long way.I approached this evaluation from the standpoint that these sauces are condiments, like ketchup or mustard, and not just sauces that you might put on your tacos and burritos. That said, I tasted each flavor on fish sticks with pleasant results. The only sauce I did NOT like on them was the Chipotle sauce, which I feel might be better suited to dishes that include beef. The Jalapeno and Spicy Ranchero both work really well with fish (and would be great for fish tacos) as well as chicken. Used as a condiment, these sauces can add a new flavor experience to everything from deli sandwiches to casseroles. I added about 2 tbsp of the Spicey Ranchero to a batch of left over rice along with some cheese and a bit of sour cream to make a great side dish. A lot of recipes that call for mayo might be livened up or rejuvenated with a measure of your favorite sauce.

It's no secret that I like spicy food. When I reviewed Taco Bell's Home Originals Bold & Creamy Jalapeno Sauce a little while back, I noticed two little words on the label that really got me hopeful: Home Originals. Will there be more flavors in this line?Yes! Bold and Creamy Chipotle sauce is even more flavorful. Chipotle peppers are fiery chili pepper made by smoking jalapeno peppers. The smokiness adds a depth that's just hard to beat. If you like creamy hot sauces, you will love this on all those fall meals: tail gate parties, hot dogs, fries, rice and grilled veggies. It's zippy with out being overwhelming and tasty without being  tongue numbing. As always, it's great on all you Mexican food faves. I know this will be a stock item in my fridge.

The Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is very bold and flavorful! I tried it with chicken wings, tacos, and a salad, and it made each dish extremely tasty. I am so glad I sampled this new sauce. It will be a staple condiment.

Clearly, this sauce provides an alternative to traditional non-franchised sauces.  It's a runny salad dressing that has some tang and a lot of calories. Whereas adults will find the taste, color, and texture largely unappealing, children may like it based on their experiences with Taco Bell.  This sauce is not "hot" by any measure and not even close to any real Mexican sauces. I consider myself a fan of real Mexican food having lived in San Diego for 13 years.  This sauce is garbage compared to what any small restaurant or even street vendor on the border can produce.As with any processed food, the nutritional value is horrible and I doubt I will use it again.  In 2 TBSP, which is not a lot, you will consume 110 calories, 300mg sodium, and 11g of fat.  Who eats this stuff? These nutritional facts do not seem apparent on the Amazon product page.Bottom line- if you your eating habits are garbage, this sauce fits right in.  If you try and eat healthy, stay away. You will find very little return in terms of taste versus nutrition.

I was sort of looking for a product like this and luckily for me, this one became available.The actual Taco Bell Restaurants used to have a taco salad that I liked and, unexplainably, they discontinued it -- but by incorporating the ingredients that they formerly used and by topping the salad with this dressing, it tastes much the same to me.Over and above that, if you're tired of the same old Italian or Ranch dressing on your green salad this will bump it up a notch. It's especially good if you include sliced boiled eggs in your salads. You can also use this dressing (a small amount) to infuse an entirely new flavor into your home-made coleslaw.Everyone in the household who tried this product liked it so you're not going to be stuck with something unwanted if you give it a try.Recommended.

column9: Much better than their spicy ranchero sauce
column10: Taco Bell's Chipotle sauce is much better than their ranchero sauce which had a burnt taste that I didn't like at all.  This sauce hits the taste buds with a sharp creamy pepper, vinegar, and smokey barbecue taste, and leaves a smooth barbecue and vegetable aftertaste with it.  I know the thought of vinegar and barbecue sauce on mexican foods sounds strange but it actually compliments tacos quite well.  It's a little too strong for dishes with plenty of flavor already like fajitas, and it might also be too much for a dipping sauce, but it adds a nice kick to tacos, nachos, burritos, and even cheese pizza.If you don't like the kick of vinegar or prefer milder salsas or sour cream flavors, this is not the complimentary sauce for you, but in the ranks of chipotle in general, its definitely worth a try.

Taco Bell has always been a tasty treat, but not a very healthy snack choice. The Chipotle Sauce by Taco Bell is definitley tasty. I tried it on a homemade taco and it was great. I also tried it on a turkey sandwich and it added a much-needed zing. However it also added about 11g fat and 110 calories. That's like adding half a McDonald's Quarter Pounder to your taco in terms of fat content. [...]That being said, I wouldn't eat this sauce every day. I would try it once in a while on an otherwise bland food choice, and probably on a workout day. It's truly bursting with flavor, so if you're not on a diet it's a nice change of pace.

column9: Not as good as the other Taco Bell sauces
column10: This sauce is ok.  It is no where near as good as the other Taco Bell sauces.  It has a mild taste and is quite ok on whatever you want to put it on.  If I could have tried this one before the other two I might have given it a higher rating.  That being said, if you like a mild Chipotle taste you will like this sauce.  It is pretty good on french fries.  I have tried it on several things and once again it does add a decent taste, there just isn't a zing there.  One thing as with the other Taco Bell sauces, a little goes a long way.

This chipotle sauce is nothing too exciting to write home about. It doesn't taste bad, it just isn't anything super special, I "have to have" kind of sauce.I enjoy it; the sauce is creamy - not as creamy as the Jalepeño, whose flavour I enjoy more - and it is flavourful. I use it on sandwiches, wraps, and pita pockets.I have nothing bad to say, but I don't want to seem like I'm trying to spice up my review or give a false impression that I'd go out and buy this as often as I can.I may or may not buy it again, but then again, I'm not the biggest chipotle fan; I just wanted to try it and see how it tasted. Not bad, but again: I prefer the jalepeño,probably 'cause I love the taste of jalepeño a lot. I've tasted at least one other chipotle sauce, and this one isn't quite as good as that one, but, again, it's not bad, just not "the best."

column9: Adding A Nice Zing To A Meal
column10: I'm not a huge Mexican food buff; if I find myself in a Mexican restaurant with someone else, I can find something appealing, and if I'm in the home of someone who's serving Mexican food I can enjoy it, but never in my life have I requested a Mexican meal or a visit to a Mexican restaurant.  The only exception is if I want fast food at a VERY low price and I'm tired of the same old burger-and-fries routine; then Taco Bell might come into the running, if I'm going to be passing one anyway.The reason I bring this up is that I used this Taco Bell chipotle sauce on foods that might not necessarily be what you'd have in mind: a variety of sandwiches (it goes especially well with turkey and chicken) as well as bacon and eggs, meals which would not pack much of a kick without this sauce.  With that you might think that the sauce would overpower the rest of the food, but it didn't.  It was really a perfect complement: spicy, but not with enough of a kick to dominate the meal or make my eyes burn and mouth water, and with that smoky chipotle flavor, rich and full-bodied.This is how it tastes on foods that pack minimal spicy kick on their own.  I guess it might end up getting lost in a meal with other spices and peppers and whatnot.  It may well work fine in such a dish, or it may not.  For my purposes I was very pleased with this product.

column9: Taste is great but Nutrition Facts prove hazzardous
column10: I like Taco Bell. That may explain why I really like the taste of this Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce. It is good right from the bottle, two drips per chip, as a corn chip dip. Make nachos with a plate of chips, ladled with ground beef and onion mix, then pour on the Chipotle Sauce. What an appetizer; but unfortunately at the same calorie, fat, sodium, levels as most fancy restaurant dishes, or those huge multi-meat bacon cheese burgers. So for those who do not have to count calories or healthy nutrition, it's tasty. Spicy and flavorful without being HOT, at least to my liking, as I enjoy a bit of heat.If you're not a Mexican fast-food fan, you might find this product a bit unsophisticated. In that case, if the supreme high-priced Tex-Mex restaurants are your cup of tea, then skip this product. But if you want to spice up the celery, carrots and green peppers on your ball game night snack food tray, this may be as good as Taco Bell delivering to your door.Good also as a high calorie taco salad dressing. Unfortunately, I can't tell you if it is good on a taco because I ran the bottle dry before I got to trying it on a real taco.If only they could reproduce the taste with heart healthy nutrition levels.Oh well, I'll bet it's good on a cheeseburger.

column4: D.M. (Lover of all things Heart) "laugh a lot...
column10: This Chipotle Sauce is very tasty, and it can be used with many different things. However I loved it the most with vegetarian meat (I'm a vegetarian, living healthy and all *grins*), and this sauce is amazing in a veggie sandwich, or with cooked vegetarian meat. However this sauce is very fattening, hence why I took one star out, it contains 11 grams of fat in 2 tbsp. So one needs to be careful to have it in very small portions, or make sure to have a good workout session after indulging in a good hearty meal containing this sauce.Overall I love this Chipotle sauce, very tasty.

I enjoy trying new flavors, especially sauces and sandwich dressings.  I once inadvertently discovered that a certain flavor of a certain brand of salad dressing is pure heaven on a roast beef sandwich, and now I won't eat roast beef without it.When I saw that Taco Bell had come out with a new line of sandwich dressings, I figured it couldn't hurt to try.  As an Amazon Vine customer, I was able to get two free bottles, so I chose Taco Bell Bold & Creamy Chipotle sauce and Bold & Creamy Jalapeño sauce.  The idea of trying them on a sandwich made my mouth water.I had a guest who wanted to try the Chipotle sauce.  OK by me; I figured I'd keep the Jalapeño for myself.  He took one bite, on a ham and cheese sandwich, and pronounced it, "Flavored mayonnaise".  I remember thinking it couldn't be that bad, but it didn't bode well that he didn't finish the sandwich.A week or so later, I got some take-out chicken fingers and figured they'd be good to try the sauce with.  Since the Chipotle was already opened, I poured some on a plate used it to dip my chicken fingers in.  I dipped it in.  I tried one, two, three chicken fingers.  My friend was wrong.  It didn't taste like flavored mayonnaise.  It tasted like generic, store brand flavored mayonnaise.  Like real Chipotle, it had a mildly smoky, bacon flavor.  But beyond cheap - it was very, very cheap tasting.This brings us to today.  I had a friend over, and I made some frozen chicken (General Taos's Chicken, if you must know).  As the chicken was frozen and rather bland, I figured it was time to try the Jalapeño sauce.  I put some out in a dish and we tried it, dipping our chicken into it.  Yecch!  This time, it tasted like generic, Jalapeño flavored store brand flavored mayonnaise.  It wasn't very spicy, as I would expect Jalapeño to be.  It also wasn't terribly flavorful and, on the whole, it reminded me of the Chipotle sauce, just a little more spicy and maybe a little more boring and cheap tasting.  I wanted to be as fair as possible, so I gamely continued on for another few pieces.  When I realized it had ruined my dinner and I'd had enough, I'd had enough.Shortly before starting this review, I dumped the two half-empty bottles of sauce into my garbage can.  From now on, when I think of sandwich sauces, well, "Yo no quiero Taco Bell".Not recommended.

I've tried using this on chicken and hamburgers and really liked it. It's a nice change from ketchup and BBQ sauces. The Chipotle has a spicy tang but it's overwhelming. It's probably even milder than the spicy sauces in an actual Taco Bell restaurant. It actually has a slightly sweet taste. It is a bit salty and creamy for those who are health conscious, but I find that even a small bit provides a lot of flavor and can be spread quite far over your meal. The bottle seems a bit smaller than you might expect, but other than that I'd recommend this.

column9: I really do like this dressing
column10: Tangy, zesty, spicy, but not too much.  It turns any left over vegetables into a salad.  Is great on any type of salad and I've used it as a sandwich spread.  Really a very nice flavor.  I'll be buying more.

I'm going to resist the urge to say it's not hot enough, because I don't care; some things are very hot, and good or bad, and some things are milder, and good or bad. It's not all that hot, but if that were the primary criterion, I'd go eat a pepper. If the basic flavor is all right, you can always add peppers with no harm done.I had tried the Taco Bell Jalapeño Sauce and liked it quite a bit, more as an ingredient than straight. I do not think this is as good. It does have a bit of smoke flavor, and that's pleasant, but I find it has a noticeable artificial taste that was missing from the jalapeño sauce. It's almost a rubber-like taste (not texture--that's fine), and I'm not sure how much it would have to be diluted to make it go away. We tried it straight on tacos, and while my husband said it was good enough, it still tasted a bit like a tire to me. I'm not sure whether this means I am a delicate and sensitive flower, or that he is an oblivious lout with no sense of nuance. I will allow that I might have been looking for it after taking a taste directly from the bottle--not the best idea I've ever had.I'll work with it some more to see if I can find a dish it goes with well; it's not a total loss, and we'll finish the bottle--eventually.

This product is very good.  The connection with Taco Bell adds a familiarity.  The packaging is excellent as is the color of the product.  The color and the taste are consistent, which is good.  The flavor is very balanced in body, mouth feel, acidity and spiciness.  It has a genuine peppery flavor with just enough temperature but not too hot.  The only thing that needs to be changed is that it is way too salty.  I added a little to way under seasoned food and it was just right.  Otherwise, adding it to food of normal degree of seasoning would be too salty.  It is a shame because the taste is so good.  You want to use a fair amount but that would make the food too salty.  Less salt will let the nice flavors come off better.  Salt helps to bring up flavor except if there is too much.  Then it obscures and overpowers the intrinsic flavor of the product itself and ultimately the dish that it is being added to.

This sauce had the consistancy of salad dressing. The taste was a bit smoky, with a hint of spice. Very mild flavored; the flavor could get lost if combined with another sauce. It was just OK, I'm not sure if I'd buy it.
Mexican spices are so good on many foods...this chipolte sauce has a great flavor, unlike other hot sauces...not very hot, quite mild, but intense... I have put it on everything, not just tacos...

If the new Taco Bell sauce reminds you of a salad dressing when you see it, it's with good reason, it's tastes just like a spicy salad dressing. I was a little surprised, I expected more of a sauce like a taco sauce but it's completely the same texture as salad dressing. It's not bad in a wrap, I use Ranch dressing in my wraps anyway but you probably wouldn't want this on your taco or Mexican food.

Today's lunch: steak tips with carmelized onion. Sliced yellow carrots with white beans, spinach, and garlic. AND...Oven roasted sweet potato fries with TACO BELL CHIPOTLE SAUCE.  Delicious!Never mind the first two items on the menu (they were good, too!:>) This review is about the Chipotle sauce.Now, I'd planned to use it on the steak tips, but decided to try a sweet/hot combo with the sweet potato fries. It was GREAT!  Just the right amount of heat, and cheese flavor which brought out the sweetness of the fries.To complete this review, I scrambled a few eggs, added drained, diced tomato, and some CHIPOTLE sauce. Again, great results.This sauce seems to take on a new flavor depending what you pair it with.  My next plan is to try it on chicken wraps.I'm sure it will be just as good as with the two recipes I've tried so far.Quick and convenient, it's worth a try!

I must admit that I am NOT a fan of Taco Bell. That is, unless I'm hungover. But since I'm not 99% of the time, I was reluctant to try this sauce. But, honestly, it's quite spicy and goes GREAT with chicken! I used it to cool some chicken breasts and they were quite flavorful. I also used this to top a Mexican salad, which also tasted nice. The sauce is very hearty and robust and gives off some good heat. I was thinking I wouldn't like it, but I must say that I look forward to picking it up at the grocery store!

This Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is pretty good, especially if you're a huge taco Bell fan and want to recreate the taste at home.The Chipotle flavor is pretty mild as chipotle goes, but it does have a little kick to it. This flavor is definitely spicer than the Jalapeno Taco Bell sauce flavor. We liked it on (another fast food chain's!) chicken pieces!It's also good as a taco salad topping instead of dressing. We love to make our own taco salads, and none of us are fans of most bottled dressing, and this was actually nice.Also try the milder Taco Bell Jalapeno sauce.

Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is fabulous on tacos and burritos.  It's wonderful on sandwiches and salads, too.  Anywhere you'd enjoy a little bit of "kick" with your meal, a pour of Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is the answer.You can even mix it into other sauces for a bolder flavor.  Maybe adding it to bechamel when making macaroni and cheese or to alfredo sauce over pasta would be a mouth-watering adventure.  The uses for this sauce is limited only by your imagination.

column9: Smoky with a bit of a kick ...
column10: I jumped at the opportunity to try out this sauce -- I'm a big fan of Taco Bell and I love chipotle mustard on sandwiches, so I figured this would be some good stuff.I wasn't disappointed.  It has that distinctive chipotle taste in a sauce that is slightly thicker than creamy ranch dressing.  So far, I've used it on southwest chicken salad (romaine topped with grilled chicken, black beans, corn, diced red bell pepper, jack cheese, and some chopped fresh tomato).  It compliments those flavors well.  Because it's so thick, you don't need to use a lot to get the flavor spread around.  I've also used it on sandwiches (turkey with provolone, roast beef with cheddar, ham with swiss), and it's very nice.  Adds a slightly spicy touch without being overpowering.Will I purchase again?  I think so.  Not sure I'd be able to use 6 bottles of the stuff, but a bottle or so once in awhile seems probable.

I really wasn't sure what to expect when I got this, but I was pleasantly surprised. I made some taco salads and these worked great. Tastes good and pours well. Has a nice open and close top which makes it convenient.Probably the only downside is the limited use of the product. What can one use Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce on?Will I buy it again? Probably, but only if my budget allows it, as it seems cheaper to just mix salsa and sour cream together to make the same thing.

column9: This one is a bit spicy. Tastes a bit heavy.
column10: My family and friends tried this. Unfortunately no one seems to agree to buy this again. This is too spicy for most of kids. Some complained it tastes a bit artificial and less natural. Others claim is is a bit too heavy. Of course, each one has its taste, and we are a small sample, but even so our small feedback is not that positive on this one.

There's not a lot to say here. I like Chipotle sauce, and I like Taco Bell, so the sauce is great. I once listed Taco Bell among my 5 favorite restaurants in the United States on Facebook, which prompted some serious questioning of my taste buds, but I suspect that I'm not the only one who loves to munch on their various burrito concoctions.I like the salsa that they sell, and the Chipotle sauce is excellent, too. Oh, it's not really hot; pretty mild. Enjoy!

column9: Never got to taste it-kids stole it
column10: My kids got ahold of this and took it all before I ever got the chance to taste it. They took it to their apartment. I had to take their word for it when they told it was "awesome sauce." They say they put it on everything. So you'll have to take their word for it. But I never got to try it.

I enjoyed the Taco Bell Bold and Creamy Chipotle sauce.  It tastes and smells good--and different--and doesn't have too much heat.  I used it as a dip for potato chips, and I'm looking forward to using it on tacos next time we have them.  I think the chips tempered the sauce's heat.

Overall, we were very pleasantly surprised by both the texture and taste of this stuff. This chipoltle is mixed in a creamy rather distinctive Red pepper and Paprika base and while that would have been enough sweetness for my palate, they do unfortunately add sugar. At least there is no corn syrup which is an absolute no-no.It's great on burgers, cheese steak hoagies, etc, as the smoky undertone with the zip of roasted jalapeno works well with meat and some cheeses.We are yet to see it on any store shelves around here but if we do we will definitely buy a bottle from time to time to snazz things up when the mood strikes.

Taco Bell has outdone themselves this time.  This chipotle sauce is just right.  The sauce itself resembles French dressing, but milder.  The pureed chipotle pepper is a mild but pleasant chile, so they blend perfectly.  The oil used is soybean oil.  There's just a tinge of garlic flavor, as well as red bell pepper, to even things out.It contains 110 calories per serving size (two tablespoons), 300 mg. sodium, and the daily value of vitamin A is four percent.This sauce would be great on a salad or a sandwich.  It is also recommended for tacos, but I require more of a tomato-based salsa on my tacos.  To each his own.Yes, I will make this a permanent staple in my home.  Not too hot, not too intrusive.  Yet not dull.  Pleasantly pleasing would be the words to best describe it.

We love all things spicy and Mexican but this sauce is not worth it. It is very mild and has little chipotle flavor. It looks like Thousand Island dressing but adds no flavor. Empty and flavorless calories. My recommendation (if you want a kick to your sauce) is the Frontera brand. Now that one has flavor and spice!

To start off the review, I'm going to admit that I've eaten at Taco Bell only a handful of times in my life. Because of that, I'm not sure if this sauce is supposed to replicate a sauce that the restaurants use. Also, I don't know what chipotle sauce is supposed to taste like.Now that the disclaimer is out of the way, the back of the bottle suggests that it's "a perfect finishing touch for your tacos, Mexican salads, and sandwich wraps". I tried this sauce with frozen burritos and I also tried it as a dipping sauce for french fries.Overall, I think it tastes pretty good. Another reviewer said that it's mild but I'd say it definitely has a kick to it. If I had to try to explain the taste, I'd say that it reminds me of ranch dressing with some spice added to it. If you're looking to try a "new" sauce for your tacos, I would check this one out.

column9: Creamy and Mild - if you like that
column10: About what you might expect from Taco Bell sauce. It's middle-of-the-road in terms of spice and texture. Not too spicy - which was fine for me. The texture was very creamy which might not appeal to everyone. It was workable but nothing terribly exciting. In other words, it got the job done by adding some flavor without getting in the way. It you like your sauces with a bit more bite and more texture, you might want to look elsewhere. Otherwise, this won't disappoint.

column9: Great Chipotle sauce, not so salty.
column10: This sauce works well as a sauce for Mexican and Tex-Mex recipes. It has subtle heat and smokey chipotle flavor. It will suit those who prefer hotter food, but won't be too overpowering for those who don't.Another great plus is that it is not overly salty. Many processed sauces are, but this one is not.

I eat at Taco Bell all the time, and this tastes exactly the same as the Taco Bell sauce included in food sold at Taco Bell.I'm not a huge fan of Chipotle Sauce, but for what it is, it's the best I've had.Definitely glad I have it for whenever I make burritos from home :)

column9: I'm From New Jersey, what do I know about Chipotle?
column10: I'm from New Jersey, so I have no idea what authentic Chipotle is supposed to taste like. I have had Chipotle sauce on my sandwich at Subway and I like it better than Taco Bell's Chipotle sauce. I find that the Taco Bell sauce has  a bit of a strong smoke flavor, while the Subway sauce has more of a kick to it. I have also had the Kraft Sandwich shop Chipotle Mayo and have found that to have an artificial chemical taste, the Taco Bell sauce does not have as much of a chemical taste (it does have some) as it does a smokey taste. It is almost like adding a bacon flavor to whatever you put it on. In fact someone tried it on their tacos that I served (just like the picture on the label suggests), and that was exactly what they said, it tasted like bacon on their tacos. Now, I guess bacon on tacos isn't a bad taste, but some may not prefer the flavor. I have been using the sauce on my turkey sandwiches at lunch and it is not bad for that. The sauce has a consistency of Ranch dressing and in fact is in the same shaped bottle as salad dressing. I often get it mixed up with the other dressings in the refrigerator, that may be something that the manufacturer may want to do is change the bottle to something more unique so that it stands out a bit more and is not overlooked with the salad dressings, especially Thousand Island. I agree with the label, the taste is "Bold & Creamy". It is also slightly sour and acidic, though not overly. I do not find it to have much heat, though it does have some. Those who tend to like hot foods will find this sauce to be incredibly disappointing in that respect. I guess Taco Bell had to appeal to the common denominator, which is ok. As other reviewers have pointed out, this is not the healthiest sauce, it adds fat and calories. I don't have the bottle in front of me, but I remember 2 tablespoons of sauce had more calories than a full glass of Coke and a pretty hefty amount of fat, so use this sauce sparingly. Overall, I think this sauce is quite average, it tastes like a mainstream commercially prepared sauce, it is prepared with common ingredients found in in many other products, it contains preservatives, and there is really nothing unique about it.

After trying both the Chipotle as well as the Spicy Ranchero sauces I was very happy that Taco Bell decided to branch out their at home selection.When using this sauce with the Taco Belle taco seasoning you get a taco that is pretty close to the flavor that you would get if you went to the restaurant but it's not quite there.Honestly this can be much better though for a few reasons. First you can use your own fresh ingrediants, you don't have to leave the house (just order it here or get during your normal grocery shopping), and lastly, you don't have to deal with the fast food experience; lines, rude cashiers, people that don't wash their hands, and you can save a little money.All in all this is a great way to get a Taco Bell fix in your own kitchen. And if I had to choose one over the other I would easily pick the Chipotle sauce, Mmmm.

column9: Just what I wanted!  The perfect amount of spice
column10: I have seriously been looking for a product JUST like this for a while now in the grocery store when I spotted it here on Amazon.  I wanted a spicy, creamy dipping sauce for fries or to put on chicken sandwiches, etc.  I actually made my own with mayo and taco seasoning...but it was NOWHERE as good as this stuff is!  It's just perfectly flavored -- spicy enough for me (if you don't like spicy food, you won't like this, but it's not extremely spicy).  Creamy and yummy.  The only drawback?  Pretty high in fat (similar to regular mayo or salad dressing).  I use pretty small amounts of it, so that's ok with me...but it would be awesome if they could make a light version.
I use this sauce for pretty much everything mexican, and on my sandwiches as well it is really good I give it 5 stars.

Like most food products this will either fit your tastes or it won't. It has a nice smokey chipotle taste, a little bit of a kick but not all that hot. Very creamy but a slight texture of granularity can be felt, just like they ground up real chipotle peppers.  I like it.

I love spicy food, and chipotle is usually one of my favorites, so I thought this sauce from Taco Bell would be great. It was okay at best. It adds a little flavor to foods like quesadillas and burritos, but it just didn't wow me. It doesn't have much kick at all. I haven't tried it as a dressing for taco salad yet, and that may be a better way to use it as it has the texture of a salad dressing.For the price ($20 for 6 bottles??), if I felt I had to have another bottle I'd shop locally rather than order it.

The biggest reason a person would buy a Taco bell sauce is because they like the taste of their food & want to be able to do it themselves. Not with this product you won't. While it does taste ok, putting it on something at home won't give you that Taco bell taste. Still, all in all it isn't bad, but there are probably other brands of similar type sauces I would buy.

column9: I already ordered more of this sauce
column10: I use this sauce for some dishes that could some zip. Love to dip grilled cheese sandwiches in it and chips and veggies of all kinds.  Adds some zip to taco salad and tacos. Good on baked potato. I am just starting,

column4: Tracy Foote "College Savings Plan Author, Pho...
column10: This sauce was just average for my family. Everyone reached for the other flavor (the jalapeno one). For both flavors, the preference was to use it to spice up some chicken tacos or chicken sandwich. Between the two, if you are serving beef (ground or shredded or a hamburger) -- then this one, the Chipotle, is the better choice. The sauce is very creamy, so if you like mayonaise type sauces, you will probably like this. No one in my house found it very spicy, so you have no worries if you don't like spicy food.

Taco Bell chipotle sauce has just enough "zing" to it to be interesting, but not overly hot.  It's great on taco salads, hamburgers, as a dipping sauce for hot wings, or anyplace you like a creamy, zesty sauce.  Taco Bell makes some pretty decent products, and this one will be at the top of my "favorites" list.  I love chipotle flavored anything, and this does not disappoint!

column9: What You Would Expect From Taco Bell
column10: Taco Bell has built their reputation as a Mexican fast food restraunt, that is as successful in the Mid West as it in California.  This means that they make a product that is no thrills and bland enough that everyone will like it.  If you want authentic Mexican food Taco Bell is not for you.  Most Mexican food is very spicy and often has a little kick, I have seen Mexicans that use Tapatio hot sauce on hamburgers, rice and soups and Tapatio packs a kick.  The Chipotle sauce is nice and bland which is how most people like their food but it really does not pack the kick that a typical authentic Chipotle sauce has.  I tried it on tacos which was not good at all and nachos which actually was pretty good.  If Taco Bell is your choice for burritos and tacos than you will like the Chipotle Sauce.

What do I think about the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce?  Well, it wasn't terrible.  It had a mild chipotle taste with a taco bell take, which I prefer over spicier toppings.  However, It isn't something that I think I'll be picking up on every shopping trip.  The container is a nice size that should be fine for a few family dinners before running out.  If you are looking for a new sauce, I suggest trying this one. Taste is so subjective a thing that you just might like it!

column9: Singed Phoenix's Review: Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce
column10: Not really much to say except it can be best considered sour cream with a kick. I mix it in with my nachos along with chipotle flavored Tabasco sauce to give it a tangy boost. As for taste, if you had a Baja flavored chalupa from Taco Bell, imagine the Baja flavoring having a badass cousin who rides in on Vespa. One of my friends used it for a salad dressing for his taco salad, but I was more horrified than interested at that point. Like I said, it has the consistency of sour cream.In summation, I love it for my nachos, especially now for football season. However, the bottle is small and you're lucky to get 10 servings from a bottle.

I used the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce in an enchilada casserole as part of the sauce. It gave a mellow smoky flavor to the dish, with just the slightest bit of kick. Planning on trying it as a condiment, as well. Tasting it straight out of the bottle, it did have just a touch of a metallic taste, but when added to the recipe I made, the metallic flavor was absent.We eat a lot of Southwestern food, so I am happy to have a new product to experiment with.

These sauces are light and have a spicy edge.  They mix well with meats, Mexican food, veggies, and some of them are good in salads.  They are liquid, so blend well with other foods. Jalapeno is the lightest, Spicy Ranchero is like the original Taco Bell Hot Sauce Flavor the most. It goes well as a salad dressing if applied sparingly.  The Chipotle one is the most mellow one, all with a bite.  I will definitely buy again.Taco Bell has outdone themselves.

column9: Not bad, but not something I'd rush out and buy....
column10: I absolutely love Taco Bell, so I was excited to try their new Chipotle Sauce on my home-made Mexican food. I was a little disappointed by the taste, which is smokier than I would like, and not very spicy at all. It's a decent product, but after the initial test-run, the bottle has been sitting in the fridge, untouched, through many a Mexican meal.
It's not what i expected. I love Taco Bell, but i'm not the creamy Chipotle type of guy. I love spicy food, just not spicy and creamy together. All in all, it was just okay.
This was a big hit when I made turkey sandwiches for my son and his friends. It's a little too spicy for my taste, but the kids loved it.

column9: Slightly smoky and creamy is more like it
column10: Taco Bell recently introduced a new line of three "Bold & Creamy" sauces for the home market. Each is based on soybean oil, water, vinegar, buttermilk,  and a few other standard ingredients. The Bold and Creamy Chipotle Sauce adds chipotle chile pepper puree, chipotle chili pepper, extractives of paprika, and natural smoke flavor to the basic recipe.As with the other two sauces, I tried the Chipotle Sauce first on regular Taco Bell tacos, both crunchy and soft. As with the others, I still prefer a traditional taco sauce on my tacos. It is also a fairly mild sauce to those of us who first experienced Mexican food before there were chain taco places. There is a slight-though-perceptible heat that lingers for maybe a minute if you don't drink or eat something else immediately. There is  a mild smoke flavor, which would be expected given the ingredients.I tried it with some plain tortilla chips. The chipotle and smoke flavors come through clearly when there is little in the way of competing tastes. Still, I'd rather have a traditional chunky salsa with my chips. I can't see myself using this sauce again on tacos, but I do think it might be good on a hamburger or as a dipping sauce for onion rings. I plan to try it on both after the current heat wave has passed. When it's this hot (95º - 105º), I try to avoid any cooking that adds to the heat load the air conditioning is managing. I'll update this review after I've tried these items with the Bold and Creamy Chipotle Sauce.One note: the "Best if Used By" date on the bottle I received was only about six weeks after I received it. This seems kind of short to me for a room temperature bottled product that's refrigerated after opening. Perhaps it was from an older lot, but it's something to bear in mind if you're thinking of ordering in bulk or taking advantage of a sale.

As a vegetarian, I'm always looking for a way to add zing to food.  Luckily, I added the chipotle sauce from Taco Bell to my meal, and it was delicious.  You only need a small amount to get a lot of flavor.I cooked 1/2 cup of Morningstar crumbles and 1/2 cup of Rotel tomatoes in a skillet till the liquid was cooked.  Then I removed from skillet, added 2 tblsp. chipotle sauce, added daiya non-dairy cheddar cheese and put in a tortilla wrap.Goes great with a side of refried beans, black beans, or Mexican corn.  Low in calorie, healthy, and filling.  I definitely recommend.  The only thing that would make it better is if the product were vegan.

I was pleasantly surprised by the taste of the Chipotle Sauce.  It is kind-of like a spicy mayonnaise.  I used this sauce in tuna salad, on sandwiches and as a salad dressing.Similar to mayo, almost all of the calories come from fat.  I think it is tastier than mayo and has a nice amount of spice.  You can taste the pepper in the sauce but it doesn't leave your mouth burning.  It's a good balance of flavors.

To give you an insight into how bold this sauce is, I recently bought some Kraft Chipotle Mayonnaise and the mayo was much spicier than this sauce. I like the taco sauce that you get in the restaurants and thought this would be similar, but it's a far cry from the packets. The smokiness is a little too fake and the aftertaste is off-putting. I know some may consider this a small thing to complain about, but the mouth of the bottle is the size of a salad dressing bottle, so you have to be careful when pouring or it gets all over. That is not something many people necessarily want, especially since the recommended two tablespoon serving size is 110 calories and 11 grams of fat.

I ordered this up because I often get the southwest chipotle sauce at a certain national sandwich shop. I thought it might be great to have this flavor at home. The Taco Bell version had the spice, but not the flavor I was looking for. In addition to trying the sauce on my favorite turkey sandwich I also tried it on a tossed salad which was good. At the end of the day, I'm glad I tried it and I certainly didn't think it was so bad I should throw away the unused quantity. That said, it just wasn't what I was hoping for and I'm not sure I'd order it again.

column9: BBQ sauce flavor overwhelms, Mexican spice minimal
column10: From the look of it, Taco Bell's new "Bold and Creamy" Chipotle sauce looks like it may be a spicy-cheesy concoction fans of quick-serve Mexican food would enjoy. This is deceiving. The pastel orange color masks its true nature: it is essentially a remixed BBQ sauce. The BBQ-inspired taste is so strong that it actually drowns out the chili pepper, garlic, and other spices Taco Bell blended with its chipotle recipe.This product is made to be used with tacos hard and soft. That being said, the reviewer tried it with a ham and cheese sandwich as well as a taco. It made no difference either way. The BBQ flavor will make itself fans or critics based solely on how the consumer feels about the southern staple's fusion into Mexican food.The packaging is clean looking and attractive. The Taco Bell logo is at the top, with an appetizingly loaded hard taco taking up a good 60 percent of the label. My sole gripe is that while the name (chipotle) refers to smoke-dried jalapeno peppers, the sauce has no kick to it. Taco Bell ought to do more market research on consumer preferences for "bold" being synonymous with hotness in this style of cuisine. Fans of old school Mexican-American food should pass on the disappointingly one-dimensional Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce, 8-Ounce (Pack of 6).

I enjoyed this Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce.  Even though the Chipotle flavor wasn't very strong, I did enjoy the flavor and the moderate zip (not quite a real "hot") that it provided the tacos, burritos and nachos that I tried it on. Like the other Taco Bell sauces that I have tried (Jalapeno Sauce and Ranchero Sauce), I didn't enjoy it as a dip with tortilla chips and found it had a bit of an aftertaste.  However, I thought it complimented the mix of bean, meat, cheese and tomato etc. in other Mexican style foods very well.  It's not overly smokey like some chipotle products and the heat level is somewhere slightly below the average medium salsa.  It's a good replacement for sour cream in Mexican style foods if you want to try something different, and although I won't use it every time, I do plan on keeping some in the fridge.

column9: Great Bold Taste That Packs a Punch!
column10: What's not to love about this nifty little product from Taco Bell. While the bottle is a bit on the small side for the pricepoint, the product more than makes up for it by packing a really tasty punch. I've used this sauce on both tacos and hamburgers and I have to say that it has not disappointed in either case. If you like spicy sauces and you're looking to add a little kick to your burgers and tacos without going too far overboard, give this chipotle sauce a try.

I absolutely love this stuff!!!  It would be wonderful on just about anything - grilled chicken, hamburger patties, steak, burritos.  It has an amazing taste, not hot at all.  It's a little high in fat at 11g. per serving.  But, if you're doing low carb there's only 3g. per serving.  My only problem is the serving size - 2 TBS.  There's no way I can just eat 2 TBS!  That's like trying to eat just one chip!  Can't be done.  I hope this becomes available in larger sizes.  A bucket size would be wonderful!!!  This stuff is that good.  Buy it!

This spread has a decent smokey flavor of Chipotle, but it isn't super spicy. I really liked the flavor, actually. It advertises as something to use on wraps, tacos, and Mexican salads, but I wouldn't suggest it for a salad dressing. It is essentially a flavored mayo or sandwich spread, so the base is thick like a mayo. I think it would be excellent on a sandwich, wrap, or even a taco or burrito, but it would probably be too heavy for a salad dressing.Since this spread has enough spice on its own, I tried it on a prociutto and provolone wrap with sprouts. It gave it that great tang and zip without overpowering the sandwich. It was tasty and definitely added something to the sandwich. I am excited to try the other flavors put out by the Taco Bell line!

column9: Not What I Expected, But Good
column10: I love the taste of chipotle, and have used the dried pepper most often in marinades, rubs, and chile. When I tried this sauce, it was different than I expected. Picture a creamy dressing like Ranch with the smoky taste of chipotle peppers and other seasonings.At first I couldn't figure out how to use it. The bottle depicts it being used on a taco, but I prefer fresh salsas for that purpose. But I've used it in several meals with great success: as a condiment for broiled meats; as a dressing on sandwiches; and to add an "adult" flavor to the chicken nuggets I was forced to eat when my kids wanted them for lunch! I think it would also make a good dipping sauce for fresh vegetables, chicken fingers, maybe fried zucchini...? It's the kind of sauce you'd want to use in small amounts on the side, rather than pouring it over a whole salad or even a whole taco.A worthwhile addition to your stock of condiments.
Loved it! A topping for tacos, burritos, and a quick snack topping on a tortilla chip! A great prtable snack item.

This sauce is spicy, and very tasty - with a hint of smokiness flavor. I used it as a dip for veggies and it was a hit, my son and his friends used it on sandwiches and they raved about it.  This is very tasty, and I think it would be delicious on pork or chicken.  Something I will buy again.

You know when you are making a burrito and you want something saucy...not justsalsa?  This arrived in time to make it to my burrito night tonight, it was ok,not bad...not as flavorful as I had hoped it would be...I ended up putting salsaon it ALSO...so that should tell you.  People who like a LITTLE zing might enjoythis but if you like spicy or a bit of heat...I would suggest you try something else.

Taco Bell's sauce is indeed yummier!! We used it in our burgers, sandwiches and some meat dishes. The key is that the main things, the protein, still have to be seasoned and cooked right. Then add the sauce on top of it before serving.Obviously, this does not replace anything that should make the steak/beef tasty. Use it like a ketchup, and not too much. Then the flavors will pop and taste well!

This is a product without a clear purpose.  Do you use it as a taco sauce?  Salad dressing?  Marinade?  Condiment?I used it on tacos and the results were---ehhh.The chipotle imparts a smoky, earthy flavor which doesn't pair to badly with ground beef, but it also has some chemically-tasting unpleasant undertones.  Regular taco sauce and sour cream both proved superior.I wouldn't recommend this unless you're a real chipotle fan or just bored out of your gourd with traditional Mexican condiments.

I am a big fan of the sauces from Taco Bell and assumed this was like them, but it isn't.  Not to say the sauce isn't good, its just not what I expected or had a taste for.  The flavor is not really chipotle, but somewhat dry and bland.  Not hot at all if you are looking for spice.  So far we have only tried on tacos and won't be buying another bottle.  It was different and worth trying, but again not typical Taco Bell.

I ordered the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce through Amazon Vine.  We put the sauce on Taco Bell tacos and burritos.  I thought the sauce was good.  It tasted strong with a lot of spices.  It was thicker than the sauce in the restaurant.  It was thin but it must have many spices in it.  My wife thought it was ok but found it to have a smoky flavor.  I thought it was a tangy flavor.John Navarra

This sauce was surprisingly good and delicious on fajitas. It is strong but compliments meats and fish very nicely. The ingredients include soybean oil, whey, vinegar, buttermilk, sugar and egg yolks, with less than 2 percent chipotle chile pepper puree.

If you're a foodie, or a chipotle nut, this sauce probably isn't for you. If you like to occasionally throw some different flavor on your food this is really good stuff to have around. I put it on some fish tacos and I thought the flavor was similar to that of On The Borders chipotle fish tacos.

I first tried chipotle sauce on a sandwich at subway and liked it.  I will say it has an acquired taste.  It's not hot hot-just a tad spicey.  When I saw this offered on VINE, I thought i'd try it.This taste great.  I've used it on burritos that I have bought at taco bell.  I also have used it as a salad dressing.  Just get some lettuce, slice up a tomato, add some mexican cheese, black olives and pour some of this sauce on it and you got a taco bell-like salad!  It's pretty good on veggie burgers, too!If you like mexican and want to add some zest to mexican food, burgers, sandwich wraps or a salad, give it try for something different!

I used this on a London broil I had grilled, and it complemented the meat well.  Many will wonder how hot it is.  Tough question, since I really like peppers of all kinds, but I would call it pretty mild.  Your taste may vary!

I can't say I would've purchased this in the store, but having received it to taste (and test out) at home was certainly worthwhile. Surprisingly flavorful with a slight kick at the end, this sauce makes a great accompaniment to chicken sandwiches, salads, even chili. Yum yum.

column9: Tricky to meld with my summertime harvest
column10: This Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is a robust sauce with strong chipotle flavor and a creamy consistency. Ingredients include soybean oil, whey, vinegar, buttermilk, sugar and egg yolks, with less than 2 percent chipotle chile pepper puree.I had some confused idea based on the packaging that this was a chipotle sauce mainly for salads. It's a bit too flavored and strong with chipotle flavor to go well with my typical summer salads consisting of arugula, lettuce, tomatoes, feta cheese, anchovies and nuts, with the produce items hand-grown and picked. If I subtracted the anchovies, the sauce harmonized better, but still, this definitely is not an all-purpose flavoring. I think there may be too many warring ingredients for a theme to come through for this sauce.So I switched to adding it to homemade tacos consisting of queso fresco or Monterey jack cheese with chopped onions, homegrown grape tomatoes on fresh tortillas from the nearby tortilleria. Much better results. I'm a fan of strong flavors, but it's tricky to figure out the best use for a premade chipotle sauce.I notice Allrecipes has recommendations for enchiladas, turkey wraps, chicken in chipotle sauce and chipotle sweet potatoes, so these may be the best way to go.

column9: Good flavor but doesn't stand out
column10: I like Taco Bell so I was anxious to try this sauce.  It's ok but also typical of a lot of sauces.  The flavor is good and the consistency is creamy but it's not as hot as I'd expected.  Taco Bell isn't associated with healthy food so not surprisingly there are 11g of fat in each serving.  The calorie count isn't too high (110) but the calories from fat are 100.  If you're looking for very hot or less fat (or both) there are a lot of better alternatives on the market.

we tried the product on tacos and on taco salad, and it did not impress. Too many artificial ingredients make it taste dull and not fresh. Oddly bacon-like. I prefer plain salsa, green chilies, fresh guacamole, or sour cream (I substitute Greek yogurt; just as creamy, but less fat). For the chipotle flavor, I will try a home-made from scratch sauce.

When I tried it on a salad the taste overpowered the salad and was too spicy. When tried on tacos the effect was greatly diminished and resulted in a passable substitute for a carry out meal from Taco Bell. I wouldn't give up going down to my local restaurant for this at home substitute.

column9: A little too smokey for my taste!
column10: We used this sauce on tacos and as a dipping sauce. Though I am a big fan of Mexican food, I found the smokiness of the sauce to be overwhelming to the rest of the food. I could not taste the rest of the food. I would imagine, however, that if diluted in sour cream, the smokiness would serve as a compliment to chicken. I have to admit that I experiment a lot with dressings, sauces, spices, etc of different brands, and it's possible that the strength of "chipotle" flavored ingredients is simply not appealing to me. If you do try this, I'd use only a bit, to test the waters-the flavor and smell went right up my nose.

This sauce is good. It's creamy, mildly spicy, and it has a nice flavor. I tried this with garden salad and it tastes good. It goes well with tacos, burritos and fajitas as well. I also tried Taco Bell's Jalapeno sauce and I liked this better than chipotle sauce. Jalapeno sauce has much better taste, but that is a personal choice. I would recommend trying both and stick to the one you like.1. Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce, 8-Ounce (Pack of 6)2. Taco Bell Bold & Creamy, Spicy Ranchero Sauce,  8-Ounce (Pack of 6)

"A perfect finishing touch for your, tacos, Mexican salads, and sandwich wraps." - from the labelThe Food Police will undoubtedly squeal when confronted by Taco Bell's "Home Originals" BOLD & CREAMY CHIPOTLE SAUCE. Is the home not sacred? Do the fast-food purveyors of unhealthy meals have to invade Man's last refuge? That provocation in itself makes the condiment endearing to me in addition to the fact that it's a striking radioactive-orange color (especially after being dispensed from the plastic squeeze bottle that will probably persist in a landfill until the Sun goes supernova - another endearing goad of the politically correct).For the chipotle experience, I've heretofore relied on Kraft Sandwich Shop Mayo Chipotle, 12-Ounce Squeeze Bottles (Pack of 6)). Compared to this, the Taco Bell offering has a bit more intense smoky chipotle bite to it, and there's an undertone of cheese to the flavor perhaps imparted by the dried buttermilk in the ingredients. In any case, I've so far tried this sauce on chicken, beef, cheese sandwiches, eggs, and tater tots and licked drips off my fingers. To the extent used, I prefer it to the Kraft product and would preferentially buy it.Nutritionally, this product contains (per 2 Tbsp serving) 110 calories, 11g total fat, 1.5g saturated fat, and 300mg sodium - all of which means that my health and nutrition-conscious wife will likely leave it all for me; I won't have to share.

column9: Tastes like a mixture of Taco Bell's taco sauce and bottled ranch dressing
column10: There isn't anything too objectionable in this, according to the ingredients list at Taco Bell's official site.  It's got eggs, wheat, and soy in it (so, if you're allergic, avoid this), along with vinegar, sugar, molasses, and both saturated and unsaturated fat, propylene glycol, and some preservatives.  One of them, Calcium Disodium EDTA, has caused some environmental concern based on what it breaks down into, but it's fairly common in food products, and if you're eating Taco Bell, I am guessing you're not all that worried about it.If you are a fan of creamy salad dressings, you might like this on something like a chicken taco or a southwestern salad.  I'm not a fan, and I did not like the taste of this.

Taco Bell's Chipotle sauce is the texture of a weak ranch dressing. Possibly due to this texture, the flavor vaguely reminds me of ranch dressing with some Mexican spices added. It isn't very spicy hot. On a scale of 1 to 10 with 10 being the hottest thing I've eaten, I'd put this sauce around 3. It is about as spicy as a typical packaged taco seasoning from a kit.I tried the sauce seperately, on a bit of taco meat, and buried in a taco. I can't say that it ever tasted good, but it wasn't too bad when it was only providing a hint of flavor to the taco. I'd much rather have salsa or any of the great liquid hot sauces available online or at the supermarket.According to the label, it has 110 calories and 11g of fat in a 2-Tbsp serving. The top ingredient is soybean oil. It says "contain milk, egg" in the allergen section of the label.

I added the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce to BBQ chicken, soft taco shells along with sauteed onions, lettuce and tomatoes. It bought out great flavor with an extra kick. I agree with the previous review that the caloric intake is high at 110 which 100 is Fat Calories for just 2 tbspa. Just like anything else use in moderation to add extra spice to my meals.Not only does the spice enhance your meal but there is a distinct smoky flavor also. So for those of you who do not have a grill this is a excellent alternative as a baste or even a marinade. I loved that it was thick and not "runny" I would definitively use this product again.Enjoy!

Tasted kind of like old Ranch dressing.  Boring and fairly unoffensive.  Unmemorable.  Creamy? Yes. Bold? Not so much.I'm not really sure where this item fits into your condiment selections.  Salad dressing? Not really.  Salsa? No.  On tacos?  Maybe soft tacos...?  Creamy tacos?  That doesn't really fit either.  Might do alright on a hamburger.  I wasn't able to try that out before the item expired.  Not spicy enough to replace salsa or tabasco.  I can't recommend this.
