Better than the Ranchero sauce, but not by much.  If you do not like things too spicy or too hot, but with a little kick of flavor, these dressings might be the ones for you.  I am not a big fan of heat, but I found myself reaching for the Tabasco when I made a burrito with this, but it worked just fine in a taco with a lot of lettuce and tomato.

I love chipotle.  And I love Mexican food.  What I have my doubts about sometimes is pre-fab food bought on the shelf (in other words, anything other than the basics....canned chilis, fresh salsa, and canned beans --or when I'm feeling especially motivated, dried beans I can prepare myself).  But the promise of chipotle flavor was enough to get me to give this a try.I like it!  I first tried it on Taco Bell's own food....a couple of Tacos Supreme.  But I've also used it with the best tortilla chips around.  The chipotle flavor is evident, but it's not overwhelming.  Which is good, because too much chipotle also can be way too hot.I personally would not use this everytime I craved either chipotle or cheese, because I like making my own stuff and because the 300 grams of sodium is too much for me (health wise, not taste wise).  But as a once-in-a-while, easy alternative, this is a condiment worth having on hand.

column9: Not as spicy as I expected.  Great taste bud sensation
column10: I was intrigued with this product from Taco Bell.  So glad I tried it.  I used it on chips and any thing else I could find.  It just was so good to the taste buds.  Not too spicy.It offered a nice compliment to what snack chip I chose and to the ground beef as well.If you like this type of condiment and taste you can't go wrong.  And it's from Taco Bell.Your taste buds will savor it.

My family liked this taco sauce and said to give it 5 stars.  I made a hamburger dish with it, with hamburger, rice, this sauce, and crumbled corn chips.  It was quickly gobbled up.The picture on the bottle of this sauce, is that of a taco.  I guess that means it was intended for use on a taco.  However, I made a taco hamburger skillet dish.  I'm sure there are probably lots of recipes somewhere in which you could use this sauce, or you can just create you own, such as I did.  Mine was really simple indeed, but loved by my family.I am used to taco sauce being red, but this is a brownish-orangy, so I guess that makes it unique!  As long as my family liked it, and I didn't have to throw it out (which I didn't), I guess it is good.

This creamy sauce is ok but not great.  It tasted oily, more like emulsified soybean oil with spices and chipotle flavor.  It does taste OK on tacos and taco salad though, but I don't recommend it as a dip, it doesn't blend well.  I have to point out that I received this sauce on Oct 4th and the bottle said: "Best if used by 29Sep2011".  Might be a reason why this sauce does not have the best flavor.

This sauce tastes pretty good! It's creamy, spicy (but not overly so), and has a nice flavor that pairs well with burritos and other Mexican-style foods. That said, I think it's a little bit overpriced for what it is. The bottle is quite small. 8 fluid ounces is the two-thirds the size of a soda can, so the amount of sauce you get really isn't very much at all. They make the bottle wide and skinny so that it has the appearance of capacity. The concave curves on the side further deceive the eye. So in summary, what we have here is a tasty sauce offered for a high price. I would recommend perhaps looking for a single bottle at your local supermarket before committing to an entire six-pack, to see if the flavor is worth the cost for you.

column9: Not what I was hoping for
column10: I tried the Taco Bell Chipotle sauce on my tacos the other night and did not like the flavor at all.  Previously I had tried the Jalapeno sauce and enjoyed it for being different from my regular taco sauce.  Not something I would use a lot but maybe every once it a while.  The chipotle sauce, on the other hand, tasted like a ranch style dressing with a bit of smoke flavor added it.  I was hoping for more of a real chipotle flavor like I've tasted from other sauces like the Tabasco Chipotle sauce.  I doubt I will use this sauce again.

I'm not a hot hot pepper addict (I can tolerate an 8 or 9 out of ten, but prefer somewhere around a 7), but I am pretty addicted to the flavor of hot sauces, and put them on almost everything. My favorites are chipotle Tabasco and sriracha, but years ago I fell in love with a sauce from a San Jose restaurant that looks a lot like this, so I had high hopes.My first impression was that this just tastes like mildly chipotle-flavored ranch dressing, and given that buttermilk is the first or one of the first ingredients, I guess that makes sense. It's about the same consistency as ranch dressing, too. I've had this over black eyed peas and on a burrito.The chipotle flavor is not strong, and not very spicy -- maybe a five -- so I'm still tempted to add some chipotle Tabasco to augment this. But really, if I'm going to do that, I might as well just mix some ranch dressing and Tabasco, since I'm already stocking those.And yes, as others have noted, this is mostly not a food product, but a chemical concoction you couldn't make at home. It tastes as much like artificial flavoring as it does like anything else. Buuuut, it does taste good, and if you (or your kids) like the chipotle flavor but aren't very heat tolerant, this could be a good option.

I have to say, well done Taco Bell. This sauce is quite delicious. It has a tangy, bold flavor that good as an addition to tacos, burritos, nachos, as well as other non traditional items, such as salads and sandwiches. I would definitely recommend it and I look forward to trying it out on other items as well as trying other Taco Bell sauce flavors.

A delectable sauce with Mexican flair.  Mildly spicy with excellent taste.  My family used it with different dishes, including salads. The 8-ounce bottle did not have a chance in my home, as it was quickly and joyfully consumed within two weeks.
This was pretty good and goes easily on many things such as hamburgers and hotdogs etc and wouldn't make a terrible salad dressing either. Its not necessarily healthy however.

column9: A Creamy Delicious Sauce Great For Dipping
column10: Yeah, Taco Bell isn't exactly associated with healthy living. While it may say Taco Bell on the label the sauces are actually manufactured by Kraft Foods. They pay Taco Bell to slap their name on the label and voila you get a more recognizable brand. The sauce is pretty typical. It's tangy, creamy with a little spice to it. Great for dipping. Try it out if your a fan of the flavor.

column9: Good stuff but way too expensive
column10: I really like this stuff but, on the web it's way too expensive.  It's $1.50/bottle at Walmart.  I use it as a cheap tikka masala sauce.

column9: Doesnt know what it wants to be
column10: Well, honestly i didnt know what chipotle was before i got this. But i like sauces and so i just decided to give this a try...but unfortunately this product hasnt left a good impression of chipotle in me.The flavor is some weird mix between spicy and sweet. Your initial taste is of sweetness and then your left with a spicy aftertaste. I had liked the mild sweetness initially. Its also got a smoky flavor in the spicy aftertaste similar to BBQ sauces. But the taste overall is just weak and undistinguishable (unless you put a big chunk in there).On top of the weak taste, it gives you a fair amount fat/calories per serving(110 calories and 11g fat for 2 tablespoons) for a sauce. Personally, i say stay away from this.

I really enjoyed this sauce on my occasional home-made attempts to mimic some forms of Mexican style food.  I always call for Subway's Chipotle sauce on subs, and this sauce is almost the same.  I really like this chipotle sauce because the taste is much brighter than other chipotle sauces.

This sauce really delivers what it says on the label!  It is both bold AND creamy; spicy enough to make salads and sandwiches interesting without inducing tears.  It's thick and creamy enough to be an ideal salad dressing or the complement to a stacked sandwich.  This will be a repeat buy item for us.

We tried this Taco Bell brand Chipotle sauce on burritos, and it did add flavor, but to me was not spicey enough. I like hot stuff, and this was good, but would'nt consider this spicy at all. Try this sauce, you may like it. It did add good flavor to our meal.

column9: Strange taste for tacos but ok for dip???
column10: This sauce didn't do it for our family.  The texture is nice and thick.  The sauce has a nice aroma.  The problem for me was that it tastes like bacon and thousand island dressing.  No one liked it on the tacos, but the kids loved it as a vegie platter dip.  Go figure.

I tried three of Taco Bell's sauces (creamy jalepeno, chipotle, spicy ranchero) and have reviewed them all on Amazon. This was my least favorite.  The flavor is very strong and overwhelmed food items like traditional beef tacos and fish tacos for me.  However, if you are a true lover of "chipotle flavor" you may have a different opinion.  I could taste the vinegar used in this sauce which is a flavor I do not enjoy which is why I do not like jarred salsas either.I did some further experimenting and baked some cheese enchiladas.  After they came out of the oven I drizzled some sauce over the final product and enjoyed the flavor combination.  I also think it would be good in a cheese ball as the smokiness and bold flavors would add a spark to the traditional cheese ball.

This sauce is okay, but nothing to write home about.  In the past, my experience with chipotle was on a sub at Subway, which I absolutely loved.  Ever since then, I've been trying to find a close match.  If I'm buying Chipotle sauce in the future, I'll try other brands to see if I can match Subway's perfection.  If there are no other brands, I'll probably pass on buying any type of chipotle sauce.

This sauce reminds me of the Samurai sauce that you get in the European Friteries. It is a very flavorful but little on the heavier side. My only downside to using this sauce is the high fat content. If you use this in moderation, you will like to blast of flavor that it adds. Spice lovers would rejoice using this sauce on their dishes.
Not too spicy, not too bland.  I love this stuff on a sandwich.  This sauce really makes sandwiches taste much better than using mayo or mustard.  Its a nice change from boring sandwiches for lunch.

The taste reminded me of the salad dressing that fast food restaurants use for taco salads, which isn't necessarily a bad thing but it's not that great either. For the standard use on burritos, tacos, and misc Mexican food, I didn't care for the taste. However, it worked well w/ hamburgers and as a additional sauce on top of a sushi roll.It's definitely a product that will have varying opinions on the taste, so it's not something I would put on food automatically. I would just leave it on the side if anyone wanted.

This is one of the milder of the Taco Bell sauces which I have tried, so not too spice, but not completely wimpy either.  It has a great chipotle flavor and nice texture.  Not as thick as mayo, but more like a salad dressing.  Aside from the obvious uses with Mexican food, I have found this works best as a hamburger topping. It is also a nice sandwich spread (but it will tend to run off the sandwich).  This is my new hamburger topping of choice!

column4: Krishna M. Sadasivam "pcweenies dot com carto...
column10: Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce has a creamy texture, packed with a tangy taste that's perfect for tacos, chip dip, Chinese fried rice, pizza (yes, pizza) and even sandwiches. It's flavorful and spicy, but not in a hot way. The bottle is easy to open and the sauce itself has a thick consistency. It pours well out of the bottle. I'm sold on the taste and plan to buy more once this bottle is over. Highly recommended.

column9: A good option for change of taste
column10: I love tacos.  I love chipotle sauce. I thought this would be the perfect combination of both.  While the sauce was good, it was spicier than I expected and it's creamier texture wasn't quite what I really like.  It was nice for a change in taste, but not something I would use all the time since I'm not a "spicy" person.  I personally will stick with my taco sauce, but if you like spicy and want a creamy texture on your next taco then you will enjoy this product by Taco Bell.

This sauce looks like an orange tinted thousands islands salad dressing and tastes similar as well. There is a hint of horseradish that smells stronger than it tastes.  The sauce is more tangy than hot. It is fairly thick and after refrigerating the last quarter of the sauce doesn't flow out very easily even when the bottle is shaken.  The bottle will give you maybe 6 servings.If you like orange colored food and the taste of thousand island dressing you will like this sauce.

column9: Mighty tasty with a little kick but not overly spicy
column10: This is a very tasty (and by no means low fat or low calorie) sauce.  I've mostly used it as a dressing for salads (both green salads and things like taco salads), but I've also tried it on burritos and tacos.  A little goes a pretty long way in terms of adding enough flavor, but it's not too overpowering if you like to pour it on, as well.  It's a little bit spicy, giving a bit of a lingering tingle to my mouth, but not so spicy that it's painful (I'm a little bit of a spice wimp, so if you're super into very spicy foods, this is probably too mild for you).

Chipotle is one of my favorite flavors in the world.  I cook with them all the time, make chipotle sauces and marinades, and chipotle mustards.  Because I usually make my own sauces and dips, I had pretty low expectations regarding this "Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce."My low expectations were met.The chipotle flavor is stronger than I was expecting, and the taste wasn't bad at all.  Neither was it good.  It has a distinct fast food flavor. This is basically a bottled version of the sauce fast food restaurants might put on their "chipotle burgers" or maybe a "chipotle dip" to each with French fries.  Which is exactly what I used it for.If you are craving that fast food taste at home, then this might be right up your alley.  Me, I would rather just whip together a tin of canned chipotles and some mayonnaise to get roughly the same effect, and probably better.

This is the stuff they put in the baja gordita (I think).  It has the consistency of Mayo, but it has a little spice to it.  Now, if anyone has had the "hot" or "fire" sauce at Taco Bell, then you understand that they are not known for making things very hot at all, and this is exactly the same.  It is just slightly spicy, but not very hot at all.  I am currently using it on almost everything I eat, from eggs to hamburgers and, of course, tacos!

column9: Yummy! So many ways to use it.
column10: I've always ordered chipotle sauce on my sandwiches when I eat out but never could duplicate those sandwiches at home. I tried a chipotle mayo that's on the market, but it wasn't the same. And then I received a sample of this. This is exactly what I was looking for. It's got the same kick as the sauce at a major sandwich chain that I love. I tried this on more than just my sub sandwiches though. It's yummy on quesedillas, fajitas, and tacos. Plus, it's good for dipping veggies and fries. I'll definitely be buying more of this when my bottle runs out.

Yum a bit of Taco Bell right in my own home! Around my house we LOVE spicy and this really hits the spot whether it be a breakfast burrito, nachos or whatever we may fix, my children LOVE to put it on everything! Has a bit of a zing to it and I am so glad I got to try it! I am wanting to try the other sauces now as well!Great addition to eggs in the morning, or any kind of wrap/burrito/chimichanga you are making. If you make some kind of mexican meatloaf this would be a wonderful addition, would give it a definite kick!!!If you like spicy things, this is for YOU!

My family likes Taco Bell and we like this Chipotle Sauce okay. We eat Mexican-ish style dishes quite a bit at home, so it's nice to have a bottled sauce for a little extra kick. I do like the chipotle flavor in this particular sauce, but of course, not everyone has the same tastes. I also liked that it comes in a squeeze bottle with a flip lid with a small hole, rather than having to try to pour it out of the larger opening. That makes it convenient for adding just the amount you want. It can be used as a salad dressing, if you like thick dressings... or as a dipping sauce for tortilla chips, or on tacos, burritos, what-have-you.

I love Taco Bell products! This sauce is really good and goes well with many different things. I added some to our Taco night and it was a hit. If you like Chipotle, then you really need to try this sauce! It's good to add or to cook with!

column9: It Tastes Like Spicy Catalina Dressing
column10: I guess if I had no other taco sauce to flavor up a taco, I'd be okay reaching for this bottle, but it wouldn't be my top choice at all.  As a taco sauce, it tastes too much like Catalina salad dressing, but spicier, which makes me think I might have liked this better, had it been presented to me as a salad dressing instead of a taco sauce.  I don't love it, I don't hate it, but I wouldn't buy it for my Tex-Mex dining pleasure.

column9: Not as spicy as I thought it would be but still very good
column10: Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce isn't quite as spicy as I thought it would be but it is still creamy and tasty and a little goes a long way.The taste is almost like a barbeque sauce with a bit of spice to it. Weirdly, I liked it with my chicken salad. Instead of putting it on the salad like a dressing, I used it as a dip. It was really good.I also used it with a steak and egg burrito that I made with leftover steak. The creamy texture worked well against the bell pepper that was part of the burrito filling. I also liked it with the baked chicken for another dinner. Like the salad, I used it as a dip rather than drizzling the sauce on it.All in all, it is a simple sauce. Not quite the taste that I expected, but still very good in surprising ways. I will definitely be getting it as an alternative to salad dressing and dip. I wouldn't use it all the time but it is nice to have as an alternate to ketchup or salad dressing.

Chipotle is one of my favorite flavors, and this Taco Bell Chipotle sauce does not disappoint.  The sauce is more the consistency of mayo rather than the runny hot sauce consistency of other chipotle sauces I've tried, which made it a tad milder, and also helped keep it on the food instead of running off.  Obviously, it goes great on tex-mex food, but I also put it on a whopper and loved it.  How about getting this sauce in the restaurants?

This is a good, classic chipotle flavor sauce. It has the thickness of a creamy salad dressing and delivers the chipotle flavor. I used it on a grilled chicken sandwich with avocado and cheddar cheese and this worked great. I could also see using on burgers, tacos, maybe even as a salad dressing. Taco Bell did a good job with this sauce.

column9: I tried to like this, but I just couldn't like it
column10: It had this sharp taste to it that didn't agree with me somehow.  I tried it more than once to see if I could like it, but it had more of a bitter taste to it.  It could use some sweetness and some other spices.  I am not an expert on that.

I used this sauce on some chicken fajitas and quesadillas I made and they were DELICIOUS! I also used it as a dip for some other stuff...it is so yummy! It is a little spicy because of the chipotle but I like spice! It is a good substitute for ketchup too. It isn't too thick but it is very creamy, the consistency of a ranch dressing but the flavor is so much better. I really loved it!

I am a HUGE chipotle fan and this sauce did not disappoint!  Truly delicious and goes well with fish tacos, chicken tacos, burritos, or salad.  The only downside is that I wish they made it healthier.  They could have easily made it lighter... too bad as I won't get it eat it as often as I'd like (or drink the bottle).

Taco Bell Chipotle SauceRich and creamy, extraordinarily tasty! :) Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is an extremely versatile sauce, whether served on tacos, with oven-warmed tortilla chips, or just as a dip for hard boiled eggs, cheese sticks or vegies.Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is sure to be a hit, no matter how you serve it.Even Dad loves Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce, and he can be a really picky eater. Best to pick up a few extra bottles, just in case! 'nuf said! :) Highly Recommended! --Katharena Eiermann, 2011

Pretty versatile sauce, I have used it on tacos obviously, but it is also a good chip dipping sauce and mixed it with ranch dressing and put it on a salad.  It really gave it a BBQ Ranch dressing flavor that became pretty addictive.  It's pretty spicy but not overwhelming and left me with a tart after taste.  I believe it is that same sauce that taco bell uses on their quesadillas.

I know it's Taco Bell, so it's got to taste like the chain's sauce. But I keep dreaming of the Subway sandwiches' chipotle sauce, which I like better. Taco Bells' has a tangy ketchup hint, that makes it a bit more like Miracle Whip to a Mayo aficionado. Nothing offensive or odd about it and it tastes good.Taco Bells chipotle sauce is great on a sandwich.

The thing with Taco Bell products is that though they are not really "Mexican" they are always a tasty delight and this no exception.I love the intense Chipotle taste, a hint of Garlic (not over done) just just hot enough to please, and it goes with just about anything.In my opinion it tastes best at room temperature or even warmed up rather than cold "out-of-the fridge" which seems to inhibit the taste somewhat though in my opinion salsas always taste better warm or even hot!This won't disappoint at all and I just loved it!

I was really interested in trying this product one I saw it.  I usually like the taco bell products that come out at the store.  They make some decent products that are available in the grocery stores.  This one is a new chipolte sauce and Sounded great as a way to spice up your meals.  I added some of this to tacos and also to some hamburgers.  It added a good flavor and a nice change to the meals.  The sauce wasnt as spicy as i would like but overall it tasted good though.  I would recommend if you want a little something different to add to your meals though.

column9: Ok but nothing to write home about.
column10: This might be ok for "taco night" for dinner but other than that this is nothing to write home about. I've tasted other chipotle sauces that are much better than this. This definitely needs some work if they want people to buy this on a regular basis. Why some reviewers are raving and giving this 5 star reviews I have no idea why they would praise something like this.

Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce is tasty, lending a smoky zing to whatever you happen to use it with.  The list of ingredients, however, is quite extensive, so don't anticipate that what comes out of the bottle is anything remotely akin to healthy.  Good for an occasional foray into the decandent and fatty world of fast-food-type condiments.

column9: Awesome! Not just about the chipotle.
column10: The additional spices, especially the hickory really add something special to this sauce. As with the Jalapeño sauce we've  used this on burgers, sandwiches, and Mexican meals at home. As much as we like the Jalapeño, this one tops it because of the awesome hickory note balancing the heat of the Chipotle. Two thumbs up and a big hit with our family.

A nice change of taste for a Taco.  I put a little sauce in with some canned roast beef, warmed it up and put in  a corn tortilla  just like I would for a taco with ground beef.  It had a delicious taste reminiscent of something I tasted in Mexico years ago.  I love the  smoked pepper chipotle taste but not having to make the sauce.  Much easier to buy this tasty condiment instead.  I bet it would be good with chicken or fish tacos too.

This flavor of this sauce is very reminiscent of the Taco Bell sauce packets, which I love.  These "creamy" versions take that familiar flavor and add a cream base, which is very similar to salad dressing.  I actually dressed some salad with it and it was pretty amazing!  Unfortunately, the bottle is too small to make that an economical choice, and this is intended instead as a "finishing sauce."  For example, adding it to tacos or burgers for a little extra kick.  If you like spicy food, this will not be enough, but it adds a little heat.I'm not sure that I would buy this over the translucent sauce, but it is very good.  If you like Taco Bell sauce and want something more substantive, I think you will enjoy these creamy sauces.  I've tried the Spicy Ranchero and the Chipotle, and the former has a more polished flavor, with the latter (this one) just a bit off.  They go best with greens, as they are too heavy when paired with just meat.

There really wasn't a lot of heat in this one for me, although I do like things hotter than most folks. I don't have Mexican food (or chips) in the house or eat it on regular occasions so I haven't been able to sample try this product out on them. I did try it as a condiment to my ever-so-boring turkey and it was OK, but I prefer the spicy mustards instead. I did try some today in a salad and that was OK, but not one I'd recommend or use again. The product has an oily texture/taste to it, and if I was going to go for something so fatty I think I'd prefer it to be a sour cream base instead of oil base.If you aren't worried about fat and calories and eat a lot of Mexican food products this might suit, but otherwise I'd give it a pass. There's not enough flavor to make it worth the added calories for me.

column9: Lacks expected heat and ends up unexciting
column10: Not a bad sauce but there does seem to be something I cannot quite pinpoint that seems to be missing in spice.  It is unexpectedly mild for a chipotle-based condiment giving the impression that it is a bit dull.  Spice is a matter of taste perhaps but I suspect this will be less than most would expect.  It may solve the problem of disguising leftovers once in a while but it is certainly nothing to get excited about.
This is a great tasting product.It can be used on more than just Mexican food. Tried it on hot dogs, and it was great. Not too spicy.Give it a try.

The taste is decent, but it's all from fat and chemicals.We tried this on tacos, fajitas, and grilled poultry. It's true, the sauce does bring something to the meal, but at what cost? The flavor is from fat and chemicals.

column9: Processed Taste, Almost All Fat, Too Strong Smoke Taste
column10: In my personal opinion, this is basically an overly processed fatty salad dressing made from a soybean oil base. I love Mexican food generally and salads, but was put off by the label showing such a high fat content (11 grams for just a couple tablespoons) and also the chemical preservatives listed on the label that I cannot pronounce.  I tasted a wee bit on my finger and was kind of shocked by that strong "natural smoke flavor" and the vinegary, salty and bitter taste on my tongue. I noticed a little chili heat, which I like.  Since I was making homemade tostadas with fresh chopped lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, onions, guacamole, pico, sour cream and beans on a corn tortilla, I thought this would be the perfect compliment. All I can say is that for me it is not worth the dietary failings of the product as I don't like the strong smoke taste, even once tossed with alot of fresh ingredients, and it is high in fat and preserved.  I would much rather spice up my fresh guacamole with cayenne/chili and know that the fat I am getting is a more healthful type.  I will not be buying this product.

I received this product through the Vine program.  As described, this is a creamy chipotle sauce that has a pronounced flavor without being hot.  While a bit high on fat at 11 grams for a serving (two tablespoons), the flavor is strong enough that you can reduce the amount used to control the fat content.This sauce works well for wraps where you do not need a lot of sauce to carry the flavor.  It does not work as well in salads in that the tendency is to use more than a serving portion and that really can drive up the fat content of your salad(although the flavor is good)!Over all, I would recommend this product and only suggest a little self control in the portion size.

My first thought was that the Taco Bell sauce would be good as a dip.  Since my garden is now producing cucumbers at a scary rate, I tried the sauce as a cucumber salad dressing as soon as I opened the bottle. It worked very well. The sauce is smooth, has some sharpness to it, but is not overly spicy. After the cucumber experiment, I placed the opened bottle in the refrigerator. I will try it again as a salad dressing when the tomatoes in the garden turn red, Right now they are still green.  They will probably turn all at once, so I will have to figure out ways to consume them.My impression of the Taco Bell sauce after refrigeration was that it has almost the same consistency as mayonnaise, This gave me another idea. I usually make tuna salad by mixing mayonnaise, hot sauce, and a few spices into the tuna.  This time I mixed in only the Taco Bell sauce.  Incidentally, the sauce has half the calories per tablespoon compared to the mayonnaise.  The tuna salad turned out well. It was very similar to my mayonnaise-based version.I was pleasantly surprised by my initial experiments with the sauce.  I have tried both the Chipotle and Jalapeno versions. They both work equally well.  That is, I find it hard to tell the differences in taste. The one negative is that they contain artificial coloring and flavoring.  They lose a star on that account.

The only thing chipotle about this sauce is in the name. Don't get me wrong, it's pretty darned tasty. It's thick and spoogy, which isn't everyone's thing, and I needed a bit of hot sauce to really add zing to my fajita, but it's good stuff.

Yes, this sauce is not good for you, that's kinda to be expected when Taco Bell is on the label.That said, I've previously been disappointed with Taco Bells jars of taco sauce as they were not even close to being the taco sauce you got at the restaurants, so I wasn't sure if this Chipotle sauce would reflect any actual flavors I taste in the food I get from Taco Bell.I'm happy to report, however, that it does bring on the Taco Bell taste, it actually reminds me very much of the cheesey sauce they use in their Cheesey Bean and Rice burritos, only with a little more spiciness to it.  I was very happy about that, I love that sauce, and I love just a bit of bite to my food too.  Its gone good on the burritos and sandwich wraps I've tried it on, so thus far I'm a fan.Now if they'd only market a squeeze bottle of their fantastic Baja sauce, I'd gain back the 10 lbs I lost last year in about a month!
This sauce is very tasty!  My husband loves it too - it's slightly spicy, creamy, and delicious!

This Taco Bell Chipotle sauce is quite enjoyable and has the tangy yet not very spicy taste you would expect. I have used it on burritos and as a dip. There is no question that if you like the flavor of Chipotle sauce you will enjoy this. But it is high in calories which I expected and did not mind for you do not need a lot too enjoy the flavor.Yet two tablespoons of this sauce contains 100 calories from fat and a total of 110 calories per serving size. The serving size is the aforementioned two tablespoons. It taste great just be aware of its high fat content and calories. When serving size is measured by the spoon full you know the calories are high. And even so, I would get this product again.

column9: Mild, smoky, creamy spice.  Good, not amazing.
column10: I liked this, but not enough to be a frequent purchase.  This is not a particularly spicy sauce, was flavorful but mild, so lacked real heat.  The consistency was thick and creamy, non-greasy.  Worth ocassional variety.  I do not eat Taco Bell enough to compare this to a menu item.

column9: Adding some spice into my life!
column10: What a surprise this was! I have a love affair with chipotle sauce, so I was really looking forward to trying out Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce and I have to say how much I enjoyed it! I tried it on some tacos we made for dinner last night and it really spiced them up! Changed the flavor and really brought out the ground beef we were using, they were so good that hubby asked if we could try it as a sandwich spread for lunch today. So how was that sandwich? As a spread I have to warn you not to add too much for it does make the bread a little soggy if you make your lunch the night before, but it really adds a flavor boost to your food. The flavor is a spicy and very slightly smoked bold chipotle taste. If I was ranking it between Taco Bell sauce packets I would have to say this is ranked between Hot & Fire. If you're a Mild type person then I would personally stay away from this sauce for it was not mild at all.Can't wait to try it on many different things, up next is a chicken salad with corn salsa! Mmm we expect many great things out of our bottle!

This product is tasty, spicy, and carries a nice kick. I was surprised, as I expected something more bland coming from Taco Bell, but this was full up good.I have found it makes an excellent dressing for a taco salad. It also makes an excellent filling for an omelet, turning a plain omelet into a Mexican treat. I can also imagine it would be good inside a home made cassadia.In any case, I will definitely be keeping this as a staple in the refrigerator.

column9: it will make your tacos taste completely different
column10: I think the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is worth getting as it will make your tacos taste completely different.  This sauce has a nice blend of both spicy and creamy tastes.  It wouldn't hurt to try more than one flavor too, as these sauces will make you re-think what a taco should taste like.  I also like how the bottle has a less messy squeeze-top cap.  The sauce will also be great for other things too; I can't wait to try this sauce on wraps and toasted grinders.

Taco Bell's Bold & Creamy Chipotle Sauce is perfectly described in its name. This is a thick sauce with a strong smoky flavor and although it is quite spicy, there is little heat. I first used it to spice up black beans being served as a side dish for tacos. The beans are so bland, they always need something, and this sauce was the perfect addition.The sauce also worked beautifully with falafels - again, just the right amount of spice and it gave the pita bread sandwich stuffed with lettuce, tomato, cucumber and falafel balls a needed jolt. Finally, I used the sauce on a veggie burger and it also worked beautifully there, too. I was pleased with the results each time I used it, and found the sauce very versatile.The only negative is it not low on calories - two tablespoons have 110 calories and 100 of those are fat calories - so I use it sparingly. That said, it is sufficiently spiced so that a little goes a long way.

My husband is a huge Mexican food fan, so I let him try this first. He liked it, said it was spicy, but not too much for him. He liked the flavor, and said it reminded him of the sauce they give with chicken fingers at Zaxby's. He said it would be great on a Taco salad, or even to eat with veggies on a snack tray for a party. So I tried it myself. I don't like spicy/hot foods, and this was not overpoweringly spicy. Just enough. I think it would be a good sauce to mix with a bit of sour cream and cheese for a dip, too. So Taco Bell, we love you. You did it again.

column9: My whole family liked this product.
column10: My whole family liked this product.  It has a smoky chipotle flavor that (when tasted alone) leaves a slight burn on the back of your throat.  We used it on tacos and the sauce gave them a very distinct taste that we all enjoyed (no burn :) ).  My husband is incredibly picky and said he liked it and would eat it again. The Kid thought it would even taste good on a salad.  I'm thinking it might also be good as a marinade.I would definitely recommend it the next time you want to add something a bit different to your meal.

If you are a resident of the American Southwest, you probably would have eaten in a Taco Bell restaurant. It serves Americanized Mexican food - tacos, burritos, quesadillas, nachos, etc. They are delicious, especially with their small packets of sauces.  I eat there occasionally, but frankly, I don't remember tasting this sauce in the restaurant.  It is thick and creamy, with a hint of chipotle chili pepper, but it is too sour for my taste.  It reminds me of a salad dressing but it doesn't go well with salad.  I don't like it with my tacos or burritos either.  The sauce overpowers the food by masking its favor, instead of enhancing it.  I doubt that I will buy this sauce again.

I'm addicted to Taco Bell.I need a recovery program.Instead I got the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce so I can Taco Bell it up at home.And Taco Bell it up I have!I use this on grilled chicken, hamburger and anything that is in any way bland.I dip my fries in it.I dip my cukes in it.I might marry it and make babies with it.What?I said MIGHT.Seriously, I love this stuff. You will too!

My 18 yr old son thinks Taco Bell is ok and said this sauce is very much like what you get when you go to Taco Bell. My wife thought it too spicy, but she is not a fan of spicy foods. I thought it was ok - a bit like 1,000 island dressing with a slight kick - not quite as sweet. It also reminded me a bit of the dip you get when you go to Outback and get their bloomin onions.It did not 'wow' any of us, we'll use it until it is gone, but no plans to buy more. Since other reviewers have gone to great lengths to list the ingredients, nutitional information, etc I will not duplicate their work.This is glueten free, so that is a +

On a pure taste basis, this sauce gets 5 stars. (I am not going to address the nutritional aspect. Read the nutritional label and you can see that this is not "clean eating" or health food. But if you want healthy food, you're probably not reaching for something that says Taco Bell, anyway.)I love spicy food, and I found that this sauce has a nice zip to it. For sensitive tongues, it may even be too spicy if too much is used. It's nice and creamy with that smokey chipotle flavor coming through the spice.This sauce works well on tacos, sandwiches (although a bit runny), and nachos or layered taco dips.

column9: Great tasting, but way too fatty!
column10: The taste is great, but the fat content on this suggests that it might as well have been 90% mayonaisse. Use it spartingly!

column4: Sam Hendricks "Author of Fantasy Football Gui...
column9: Great sauce just like at Taco Bell
column10: Bold and spicy are good descriptors for this brightly colored chipotle sauce. It reminds me of the sauces at Taco Bell and thus does a great job of emulating them. I have used it on tacos, burittos and fajitas. Just spicy enough to be noticable but not too over the top.Sam Hendricks, author Fantasy Football Tips Fantasy Football Tips: 201 Ways to Win Through Player Rankings, Cheat Sheets and Better Drafting and Fantasy Baseball for Beginners Fantasy Baseball for Beginners: The Ultimate "How-to" Guide

This sauce is very orange and just a bit spicy.  It adds a nice flavor to the sandwiches I often put in my lunchbox or the quesadillas I make at home.  Not low in fat, but adding a bit to a tuna or ham sandwich can't be that bad for my health, can it?

Tasting a dab of this on a fingertip wasn't too pleasing: it felt too rich, too fake, and too underspiced (basically thousand island dressing with a slight aftertaste of chipotle).So I tried adding it to some food, and in most cases I couldn't even tell it was in there - with the exception that my burrito made orange drips on the plate.I'm sure I could get more of a taste profile (and more orange drips) if I added a LOT more of the sauce to my food...but that would boost the calorie count unacceptably. All in all, Taco Bell might do well to change the name from "Bold & Creamy" to "Bland & Fatty."

The Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is our favorite at Taco Bell and so happy that Taco Bell is sharing their sauces with the public.  It is tangy but not so spicy.  The bottle doesn't last long enough for us!  We will be purchasing more of Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce along with the Creamy Ranchero one.  This is a good buy!

I really like the Baja Chicken sandwich from Quizno's, so when I saw this Chipotle sauce I thought "I could make my own Baja Chicken sandwiches!" and I got it. Naturally, I never did manage to make that particular sandwich, but I did enjoy the entire bottle of sauce on pulled pork sandwiches. The sauce wasn't spicy at all, which was a little disappointing, but had a nice creamy, smoky flavor.I liked this sauce, but I would probably try to find a different, spicier, Chipotle sauce before trying this one again. Though if offered this sauce, I wouldn't turn it down. If you like mild, then this is probably a good sauce for you.

column9: Not a Taco Bell fan--but this is good on all sorts of things!
column10: First, let me say that I am "not" a Taco Bell fan.That said, my review sort of started off with a negative slant.  I wasn't thrilled about trying a product from a restaurant that I didn't care to eat at.The first thing I tried this on was eggs in a breakfast burrito.  Wow--it was good!  Enough spice to pep it up, but not enough to send you running for a glass of milk.  The chipotle flavor really made the burrito special.I tried it on grilled chicken--again, it was just enough to give it some flavor, but not overpowering.The flavors in this are robust, not-too-spicy, smokey...I have since tried it on beef, with the same result.It's been in the house now for 3 days, and has been used more than any other "sauce" in the 'fridge.  I can see it won't last long.  It'd be great on sandwiches, too.So, coming from a non-Taco-Bell person, this Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is really good!  I will definitely purchase this again.

column9: Spicy Complement to  Salads, Eggs & Wraps
column10: I tried Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce on a traditional salad, scrambled eggs, and a turkey wrap.  On the salad, the sauce completely dominated because of its spicy flavor.  I wasn't able to distinguish clearly the other ingredients of the salad.  I like spice, but I prefer salads with a more gentle dressing.  I enjoy both creamy and oil/vinegar dressings.  The Taco Bell product is the creamy variety.I tried it on scrambled eggs which gave the eggs an Eggs Ranchero kick.  Not bad if you can take the spice that early in the morning.  I used a little and it went a long way on flavor (and spiciness).  Would I use the sauce on eggs again?  Maybe.The best results occurred when I used the sauce on a turkey wrap.  The wrap contained white meat turkey, iceberg lettuce and tomatoes.  Since turkey is rather a bland meat, the Taco Bell dressing put some zing in the sandwich, making it far more enjoyable than a wrap with mayonnaise or mustard.I know many people have sensitive palates when it comes to spice.  For those folks, I would suggest steering clear of this product.  But for those who enjoy spice, I would heartily recommend it.

column9: A taste treat that adds some spice to your meal
column10: According to Wikipedia, chipotle comes from a word that means smoked chilli pepper. It is a smoke dried jalapeno that tends to be brown and shriveled.I enjoyed getting my sample of Taco Bell Bold and Creamy Chipotle sauce.I bring a sandwich to work on most days and the basic meats are generally mild. The sauce added to the sandwich is nice to spice it up.  I tried a small amount of this sauce to my chicken breast and then to my turkey sandwich and found it added a nice taste that was different.I also found this was a pleasant addition to my dinner salad.Where the sauce stood out was when added to a barbeque. I have added it to hamburgers and Italian sauggage patties. In a small amount the taste was delicious. I didn't need pickels or cheese because this taste was totally different and enjoyable.I recommend this product.

column9: very strong with a powdery taste
column10: Having tried all of the Taco Bell bottled sauces, I have to say this is my least favorite. The chipotle flavor is very powdery, almost chalky, and the overall taste is extremely strong. You don't have to use much of it, literally 1-2 drops on a taco is all you would need, but I found it unpleasant. The other flavors are smooth and well balanced, but the chipotle flavor just doesn't cut it. The consistency of the sauce is good and it lasts a good long time in the fridge, and the 8-oz bottle goes a lot farther than you think it will.

It's a very nice perk that a senior citizen can buy any item & receive a free small drink,  but when I asked the counter clerk to substitute a limeade ...obviously, I would pay the difference ... she said that the limeade would still remain at the full price of $1.89. I asked her if the limeade was labor intensive & she said "not at all." So my question is: Why? ... A suggestion: Just charge the 30 cent difference ...or, even an extra 89 cents is fair if the ingredients cost more ... but the full price is an 'insult' to the customer.The sales clerk apologized & said that "It didn't make sense to her, either!"

The Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce, 8-Ounce (Pack of 6) sounds spicy, but thankfully it's not, so it makes a great light taste for meals. Personally, I found it a bit too creamy, but it seems to be the same as the sauce at the restaurant.

I rarely ever go to Taco Bell, so I wouldn't recognize this as a Taco Bell product.  I make sandwich wraps with lettuce, turkey, cucumber, red onion, etc. etc. and this is the sauce I use inside the sandwich wrap.  I have made tacos and burritos and this is a good additive.With other sandwiches, I also use the Taco Bell Chipolte Sauce.  It is orangish and in color and has a slight spicy tangy flavor.  The texture is more like a salad dressing and can be used for that too.  I like this!  ....Rizzo

This is a wonderful product, and I am not one who dines at Taco Bell. I used to eat there when I was younger in college, but have not in years, so I was pleased to try this product and find that it was great!First, I like that the bottle is not so huge because the taste will stay fresh instead of getting stale from lack of use. I have many dressings and toppings etc. in my 'fridge, so it's nice to have a smaller bottle.Second, the taste is excellent. I love the creamy texture, and it has just a little "heat" from the chipolte flavoring to be interesting but not too hot.I used this on a home made taco salad, but I also used it as a sauce on a noodle dish I made that was like a south of the border spaghetti - grandchildren like noodles, so we made noodles and taco flavored meat and this sauce with a few veggies thrown in and had a Mexican style noodle dinner that they loved!So I highly recommend this product!

Creamy and tasty with a nice chipotle flavor.  Not very spicy hot.  In fact, very mild.  Probably best described as tangy.  I wasn't sure how I was going to use this when I got it, but I found the perfect use for it.  It really jazzes up plain baked chicken.  I am not much of a fan of baked chicken, but my family eats it a lot and this sauce turns plain chicken into chipotle chicken.  I imagine that it would go good on tacos too to give them a little extra flavor, although have not tried it yet on tacos.  I know it would be great on chicken tacos; not sure if it would be as good on beef tacos.  I tried this sauce on fish too, but that would be a thumbs down for me.  Not a good compliment for fish.  This sauce is something different if you are tired of salsa all the time on your tacos.  If you like chipotle flavor, you'll no doubt like this.  Certainly not a "bold" flavor; just a nice, mild, tasty and very creamy sauce.  I can't imagine anyone not liking this sauce, but if you are looking for something really spicy, look elsewhere.
This sauce is good, but I expected it to be hotter than it is. It is pretty mild when you compare it to other chipotle sauces, like Subways. If you like mild, this sauce is good for you.

I honestly wasn't expecting much from a Taco Bell branded sauce, but this has a surprisingly good taste - just the right mix of spicy and sweet.  This sauce also makes a great dipping sauce for chicken tenders, as well as a taco or tostado topping.  I confess, I don't have much experience with other Chipotle sauces to compare it to, but I really do like it.

The smokey flavor and vinegar come through strongly and really give it tang, but with no tomato it's kind of a hollow, thin flavor that hints at BBQ but doesn't really deliver or stay with you. It's not particulary hot either.I tried it on hard and soft shell tacos, as well as on pork and chicken cutlets. It works best on simply seasoned meat - just salt and pepper - where it's not competing with other strong flavors.The texture is like a thick salad dressing and it's marketed as a finishing sauce for tacos and Mexican salads. It doesn't spread or mix as well as a Thousand Island or Russian  dressing so I wouldn't use it for salads that are mostly lettuce.It would probably make an interesting Reuben sandwich.

On first taste, bacon seems to be the most dominant flavor..followed by smokiness.  It is somewhat bold but not hot, as I would consider it. Advertised as chipotle sauce, you would think it would be quite spicy. The flavor is strong enough to hold up when I used it for sauce on the boneless skinless chicken I was cooking. Really did make a good tasty sauce!  Also put on hamburgers after they were cooked..just not very good at all.  Maybe if you mixed it in yr ground beef before cooking, it would really enhance yr burgers w/that bacony smokiness..I will try that next, enjoy!

In order to get some valid feedback, I offered this new sauce to four teenage boys who love eating at Taco Bell.  Not one of them liked it. Their comments ranged from "Too smoky", "Tastes like French dressing that went bad" to "It leaves an aftertaste". I was quite surprised by their responses. In order to fairly evaluate the product, I added it to my own turkey and cheese sandwich wrap. (It is not a low-cal condiment.) I'm sorry to say...I agree wholeheartedly with the boys. Perhaps this product is better suited for just tacos and not sandwiches or salads. Unfortunately, I was not impressed with this product.

column9: It's hard to believe that something that tastes so good has Taco Bell on the label!
column10: Taco Bell isn't exactly the pinnacle of flavor, and I didn't have high hopes over the potential flavor this sauce was going to deliver, but WOW, it is actually delicious, adding another dimension to already good food!It has some heat to it, but not excessively, still in the "mild" range, but with subtle smoky overtones, completely appropriate for a chipotle sauce.  We sampled it on seasoned shredded meat (pork & beef) soft tacos with angel hair cabbage, sour cream, and cheese.  The tacos were well flavored with mild heat on their own...adding this sauce actually kicked them up a notch from good to WOW.On a lark, we tried a flour tortilla with raw shredded cabbage inside, about the blandest imaginable "wrap", and added a few drops of this sauce.  Even that tasted great!We've sampled several flavors of the bold & creamy line, and this one is by far the best flavor.  Whether its tacos, burritos, flautas, or even a plain jane burger...this sauce rises to the challenge.  I highly recommend it!

"Tex-Mex remoulade" is the best way to describe this delicious sauce. You can use it as a taco sauce, but it also makes a great spread for a sandwich or wrap, or a condiment for fish or meat. It would probably make a good salad dressing, although I haven't tried that yet.

column9: Don't read the nutrition label - just enjoy
column10: OK, who else has a stash of Taco Bell sauces in their fridge?  Just me?  Wow, I hope not.  You people are just too embarrassed to admit it.  :)  Well, as a former college student, I have learned to love Taco Bell, mostly for their cheapy "Mexican" food.  But it turns out they can make some nummy sauces, too!  We had this on burritos (homemade!) the other night, and it really tastes good!  And looking at the nutrition info explains it all.  Two tablespoons has 11 grams of fat and 300 milligrams of sodium.  And somehow 4% of the daily value for vitamin A snuck in there.This has a little bit of a bite, but it's not spicy.  There is a good smoked chipotle flavor to it.  I really like it and would buy more.  But in the interest of my blood pressure, maybe not all the time.

This is just fat, pure fat, made from soy bean oil.  And, it's too hot for me.  If you don't care how many calories you pour over your food, and that those calories are all fat calories, you won't care that this is so incredibly high in both.I don't like hot stuff.  A little bit of tang is a good thing, but all I tasted in this is hot.  I really didn't taste the flavor at all.This is a pass for me.

column9: Delicioous - and not only on tacos
column10: It only takes a spoonful of this flavourful sauce to give a wonderful zest to chicken, meat, and omelettes (just to mention the three uses I tried.) I'd highly recommend TacoBell Chipotle as a superb condiment with great versatility.
It's not a bad sauce over all.it has a nice flavor,its has spice but its not bad at all.highly recommended.tasted good with the taco,with salad and chicken nuggets lol..good stuff

I was sent one bottle of Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce to review for the Amazon Vine Program. Here's my take on it:Listed as a "Home Originals" bold and creamy chipotle sauce for use on tacos, Mexican salads, and sandwich wraps or as a dip, I first tried it out on Doritos, then on a taco. It's creamy, more a cross between mayonnaise and sour cream, but I'd hardly call it bold. Yes, there's a slight chipotle taste and a bit of bite, but otherwise, it's pretty bland. I'm, no doubt, prejudiced, because I regularly make my own chipotle crema sauce which is extraordinarily good and easy. So, I was expecting a sauce with a bit more chipotle taste. The inclusion of buttermilk in the sauce imparts a slight cheese taste, not a good thing, and it's not at all smoky as chipotle should be. Also, it has a very bright color that seems enhanced.If you're a reader of labels, know that each two tablespoon serving contains 110 calories, 11g total fat, 1.5g saturated fat, and 300mg sodium.I was happy to try this sauce but will probably stick with my home made version which is decidedly more flavorful and robust.

column9: Add a Smoky Zest to Your Food
column10: I used this on tacos and quesadillas. Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce added a smoky, zesty flavor to both while not being too hot. It has a richer, more decadent flavor than salsa with more calories, but what the heck! I'm a firm believer in splurging every once in while.If you want to live a little bit, try this sauce and put a little zing in your life.

column9: A sauce that is easy to like.
column10: The most distinctive qualities of this sauce are its rich orange color and creaminess. The sauce has a slight hot flavor, and a smokey flavor.  The hotness is provided by that most famous of spicey molecules, "capsaicin."  Capsaicin is what makes peppers naturally not.  At any rate, the good folks in Iowa who work tirelessly to put corn and pork on the table, might consider this sauce to be adventuresome or "out there."  However, folks from the San Francisco Bay area, where practically every block contains a Thai restaurant, a Chinese restaurant, or a Korean restaurant, will find this sauce to be bland or tame.  The most subtle feature of this sauce are the little red specks and green specks that are suspended in the orange creamy stuff.  I urge every person who (by habit, choice, or necessity) uses canned beans as a frequent component of their diet, to try the TACO BELL CHIPOTLE SAUCE on the beans.  Once you do this, you will likely view canned beans in a new light, and a more positive light.  To summarize, the CHIPOTLE SAUCE has a hot flavor and also a smokey flavor, which makes it a more interesting product than Taco Bell's JALAPENO SAUCE, which really only has a hot flavor, and not much of any other flavor.

The Taco Bell chipolte sauce provides a nice change of pace from the usual mayo and sandwich spreads.  It is pleasant on tacos and adds a little tang to otherwise undoctored mac and cheese.  There is the characteristic smokey chipolte warmth but I would not describe the flavor as either bold or creamy.  However there is some  flavor which distinguishes it from the usual dumbed down cuisine.  The sauce has a somewhat runny salad dressing consistency and care should be taken lest you douse your food with it.  It also has an odd light orange color. It tastes like weak ranch dressing with chipoltes added.This sauce adds a little verve to routine dishes.  It is unlikely to please a sophisticated palate or anyone who really enjoys the heat. If you are looking for something to add a little flair without upsetting the apple cart,you can't go wrongwith this sauce.

The best reason to buy this is because you've had it at Taco Bell and loved it.  Obviously, since it's from a fast food restaurant, it's hard to take this product too seriously, or analyze it too much.Of course, all the chipotle sauce or chipotle-inflected salsa I've had tends to be BROWN, but this stuff is ORANGE. It might be more like outer-space chipotle paste!It's fatty, with a milky mild mayo-ish texture and mouthfeel, and with just a hint of signature chipotle spicyness.  This is not the extra kickin hot sauce and isn't meant to be.  It is, however, a quick alternative to add to your tacos, burritos, beans and rice or even a chicken sandwich, when you are weary of the same-ol' same ol'.  Just don't add too much, as 11g of fat in 2 tbsp is a lot for a topping.

If you a fan of sour cream like myself, This product puts a welcome spin on bold taste. It's likes sour cream with a chipotle kick! It goes great with tacos of course and even Burgers for a little south of the border flair. Feeling adventurous one day, I tried it out on a grilled chicken recipe, complete with spanish rice and bell peppers! Can you say YUUUUUUUUUUM! My pantry now has at least two bottles of this at all times. What are you waiting for?

This creamy sauce is pretty good. Is it a culinary masterpiece? No, but as with most things at the grocery that come in a plastic bottle, it's good enough for the day-to-day meal. This chipotle sauce has a lot of flavor. It's got a decent amount of heat, but the creamy factor keeps it in check. It has a noticeable garlic taste, but the chipotle is more noticeable.I've tried this sauce on just about everything, and it has been a nice change of pace. Naturally, this sauce spices up Mexican dishes nicely, especially ones with lots of fresh tomatoes. However, I have also enjoyed it on hamburgers, hot dogs, sandwiches, and chicken. The best way I can describe this item is "spicy salad dressing." If you like to dump creamy salad dressing on random foods, which I do, then this sauce will add some fun to your dinners. And caloriewise, it's about what you'd expect from creamy dressing, 110 calories per 2 tablespoons.

My husband's thoughts on this sauce: "Too strong without enough sweet, pungent with a fake aftertaste. Don't need to buy it for me again." He likes chipotle flavors more than I do so I wanted to share his opinion. I tried the sauce with some refried beans and didn't find it as unpalatable as he did. It tasted like bottled chipotle sauce, rather fast food like, a little bit of a fake taste to it, but not overwhelmingly so. And when used with other strong flavors it would be strong enough to be an accent. It is definitely not low in fat so be aware of that. It has a small kick but not much, fine for almost any but the wimpiest heat levels.

A rich, creamy sauce that goes well with near anything. I've used it in avocado-chicken salads, tacos, burgers, just about everything. It might be just a tad too strong for some people, but it doesn't have very much heat otherwise, think Medium on the scale of flame.I personally always ask for a scoop of lava sauce at taco bell, and I usually order off of their Volcano menu, and to me, this is God's second gift to mankind. A great tasting, smooth sauce that is a great alternate condiment for the spicy lovers in the house. Highly recommended.

column9: Really good!  Much better than I expected
column10: I was pleasantly surprised by Taco Bell's Ranchero sauce, so decided on a whim to give this a shot.  Lo and behold, we all liked this sauce even better.  It works better as a dipping sauce than does the Ranchero, and was really good with some quesadillas we prepared.  It also has the smokiness which I would expect from some with "Chipotle" in the name, and enhances a chicken taco without overwhelming anything.If you are looking for raw heat, this isn't going to do the job for you.  Our heat-crazed teenager simply mixes in one of his pepper-extract sauces and that appears to make him happy.  I was actually expecting this to be a bit more hot than it was, but it would appear that Taco Bell is trying to keep the boldness, as it were, under some control.Would I buy it again?  I liked the Ranchero sauce enough, but didn't see it becoming a staple in our house.  However, I can see myself replacing the increasingly empty bottle of the Chipotle sauce.  Well done.

column9: Well, they got half of it right ...
column10: The makers of Taco Bell Home Originals Bold and Creamy Chiptole Sauce did get the "creamy" part right - though there is no cream anywhere to be found in this bottle, just copious amounts of soybean oil.  This is why this sauce has a whopping 110 calories per 2 tablespoon serving, on par with most regular salad dressings.Unfortunately (or more unfortunately) the "bold" part of the name is an extreme misrepresentation.  Oh, there is some chipotle puree way down on the ingredient list (listed under the label "contains less than 2% of"), but it only lends a hint of chipotle flavor to the sauce.  It's more akin to mayonnaise with a few dashes of pepper added than to a real chipotle sauce - nothing "bold" here at all.As it does have a somewhat pleasant (though overwhelmingly bland) taste, I'll give this Taco Bell sauce a bit of credit.  But I suspect that it would be much better and healthier with a bit less oil and a lot more kick.Note - since people have varying responses to spicy foods, I'll let you know that when I'm at a Taco Bell the "Fire" sauce is my usual choice, and I consider "Medium" and "Mild" to be about as spicy as ketchup.  Perhaps those more sensitive than I to spicy heat will have a better opinion of this sauce than I do.

I like chipotle sauce and thought this sauce from Taco Bell was adequate.I like my sauce and condiments to run towards being spicy and or hot and this one was okay if just a litle bit bland.The bottle was a bit big and I did have to make room in my fridge for it. The top was fine and easy pour but due to the opening I tended to put a bit too much on the food I was eating and had to wipe off the excess.Grade: C+

I love anything chipotle, and this did not disappoint! The Taco Bell Chipotle sauce is a salad-dressing-creamy type sauce.With leftover taco meat, we made taco salads. This made a delicious dressing! Just the right amount of spicy without real heat. Even though it essentially has a salad-dressing base, it poured and tasted like a creamy sauce. Mixed with a little Ranch dressing it would make a nice Chipotle Ranch salad dressing.This would make a tasty dipper for chicken, on burgers, fried mushrooms, you name it! I sent it on a wrap sandwich for my husband's lunch as well.Nutrition info: It does have sugar and maltodextrin listed in the ingredients, and 2 T. is the serving size. If you are watching your fat, 2 T. will set you back 11 grams. It will also count as 3 carbs, 1 of which is from sugar.This is tasty enough that I would definitely buy it.

column4: Sir Charles Panther "Life is hard.  It's hard...
column10: I tried the sister product, the Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce in August, and wrote a review for it.  Overall, this is a slightly better product, with better color and a better taste making the small difference.As with the jalapeno sauce, this product appears to be trying to cover too many bases.  It's "sauce," which means it could go into anything, in cooking or in serving, so it seems to be landing as both a cooking ingredient and as a table condiment.  And it could go on anything from your breakfast eggs to your mac `n cheez for dinner, which makes it a table condiment for breakfast, lunch, dinner, any time.  And its "bold," the American euphemism for something that's not really spicy, is marginally beyond the typical bland and boring that most Americans rely upon.  It's got the tiniest tinge of spice, but isn't powerful in the least; the taste of this product does not qualify as "bold."  Now, the taste of Cheez-It Hot & Spicy; they got "bold" with that one.The bottle's copy says the same as the jalapeno sauce, that it's perfect with "tacos, Mexican salads and sandwich wraps."  In our house it went on pork roast, couscous, green beans, Brussels sprouts, meatloaf, and french fries.  My kids (13 and 15) both liked the sauce and declared it was definitely better than the jalapeno sauce.The basis of this sauce is a mayo/buttermilk dressing-type mixture.  I don't know, but it strikes me that all of the Taco Bell sauces start with the same plain base, and the respective flavors are just dumped in at the factory.  The sauce is not chunky in the slightest, and squeezes right out of the bottle.The pluses in this product are the color and taste.  Where the jalapeno sauce faltered because of an unappetizing color of mayonnaise-off-white with mysterious green flecks, this one's smoky-creamy orange color is far more appealing.  It looks better in the packaging, and it looks much better on the plate and on the food.  The taste also is better. Jalapeno is a very distinctive taste, and those who know it and seek it out want that hard burst of powerful, earthy jalapeno punch, the chipotle taste is one that is more subtle, not nearly as strong, and as such works much better in this sauce.  The taste of this product is slightly smoky, with a good tang--not bold, mind you, and not even close to spicy.The sauce is just a bit too runny, though.  Yeah, it's in a squeeze bottle and it's got to have the right consistency to actually flow out of the packaging, but at the same time, it's a bit too runny when it gets on the plate.  Taco Bell needs to thicken it up just a little bit more to get it to the right consistency.This sauce is not bad; it does not taste bad.  It just doesn't deliver on what I'm looking for when it comes to spicy.  If I were starving on a desert island, I'd slurp this stuff out of the bottle and call it the Food of the Gods.Bottom line: "Creamy" this sauce is, but "bold" it is not.  Our family knows hot and spicy, and a lame American "bold" doesn't cut it for us.  If we want Scoville-graded heat with our food, we'll go for the Sriracha, Crystal, Cholula, etc.  If we want creamy, we'll go for the all-American ranch dressing or straight-up mayo, and we'll leave this product on the shelf.

This is okay, but it's nothing special. I tried it on a taco and it doesn't add a lot of flavor. I did not find it hot at all, and I do not like hot food, so that worked for me. It did seem a little weak and I expected more from a chipotle sauce. I prefer other sauces or even ketchup to this one.

column9: Decent flavor for a quick fix
column10: I am typically a huge fan of all things chipotle - the smoky heat, the warm, earthy flavor - I use the spice in a lot of my cooking.  I thought Taco Bell's Bold and Creamy Chipotle would be an easy, ready-made way to enjoy that flavor.I've tried the sauce on salad and in burritos thus far.  The heat is there, and you do get the chipotle flavor, but along with it is a distinctly fake/preservative-ridden taste that I found unappealing.  In the salad especially, without many other strong flavors to mask it, that artificial taste was particularly offputting.  In the burrito, it blended in better with the beans and rice and left more of the heat/smokiness.Two tablespoons leaves you with 110 calories and a whopping 11 grams of fat.For a quick chipotle fix, this is just OK. I'll be sticking with my own spices.

column9: Okay but not what I hoped for
column10: I was excited to see these Taco Bell brand sauces because I was hoping they'd be like the Baja sauce I loved on the grilled stuffed burritos and whatever is in the chicken quesadillas. This sauce wasn't it, but it's still okay. Don't think I'd buy it, though.

I love Taco Bell, but this sauce is not right....it says "natural smokey flavor" on the ingredients, which comes across as a heavy dose of that Liquid Smoke that some BBQers use...way too much for the flavor.  Left an afterbite and worse, the chipotle flavoring felt powdery, like it wasn't mixed in well.  Kind of like a grit in it....

column9: Great flavor - not the healthiest option
column10: This Taco Bell Chipotle sauce is quite tasty. I tried it in homemade burritos, and it was a great-tasting addition. It's a creamy sauce with just the right amount of spicy kick. It also works well just as a dip for tortilla chips.The downside - as with most creamy dressing-type condiments - is the amount of fat content. Two tablespoons of this sauce contain 110 calories, 100 of which are from fat. There are eleven grams of fat in each serving. A shot or two of this sauce once in awhile is fine. But the way some folks like to liberally douse their salads with dressing, this isn't the best choice for that kind of thing.But in moderation, this sauce is a great way to dress up your Mexican-style cooking. The flavor is distinct without being overpowering.
I tried this sauce on a wrap and pitched the rest of the bottle. All I could taste was salt (300 mg of sodium in two tablespoons). Ken's Boom-Boom sauce has a better taste.
This sauce really tastes like a mix of Taco Bell hot sauce with a ranch/creamy sauce.  Not healthy, and not very tasty.  There are definitely better sauces out there.

column9: Not JUST LIKE Taco Bell but Still Really Good
column10: Let me be upfront and say, the products marketed by Brand Name restaurants (ie Taco Bell, O'Charley's) never taste exactly the same as they do when dining in.  I don't know if that's just me or maybe it's because the food prepared isn't identical to theirs or whatever.That said - the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce may not taste exactly as it does on Taco Bell's food items but it's still very, very good.Whether it's a splash on a taco or globbed onto a turkey sandwich in place of mayonnaise or drizzled atop a salad, this Chipotle sauce offers a real kick and livens up an otherwise boring dish.Yes, as other reviewers have pointed out, it's fattening.  But does anything that taste good not have lots of calories?There are so many uses for Chipotle sauce and Taco Bell's is definitely one of the top tasting brands on the market.  It may not be JUST LIKE Taco Bell's in-store sauce, but it's good nonetheless so if you like Chipotle, this one you want to give a try.

column9: Best taco sauce I ever had.
column10: 5 stars out of 5!To me this is the king of kings in Taco Sauce land. So grab your royal scepter, place thyn crown upon thou cranium, sit in thyn gold plated and jewel encrusted throne, for tonight my friends, you dine with the best.I love this taco sauce, and have been addicted to it for about a year now. Though it isn't for everyone, of my family I am the only one who really likes this stuff, everyone else is like "meh" or "it was ok".It gives a slightly smokey bbq like flavor to the taco, with a little spicy hit. Not terribly spicy, though I am the kind of guy who is very used to hot sauces, I go through a LOT of Tabasco sauce each year. I can literally drink a whole bottle of tabasco if I wanted *though I don't because I know the next morning I will be extremely sorry I did*. Though I don't buy this sauce to make my taco "hotter" rather I buy it because I love the flavor. The only con I can find, is I wish it were a little cheaper, and in a much larger bottle. I would be extremely happy if it was in ketchup sized bottles for say 5 bucks each. I go through a lot of this stuff.I should also note here that the other 2 flavors in this line of sauce *Spicy ranch and Jalapeno" are not nearly as good. Jalapeno I can enjoy on hotdogs, but the ranch flavor isn't good on anything in my opinion.I prefer this chipotle sauce in soft shell tacos, and until I find something I like better, I'll keep buying this stuff. I will say that Eric Cartman has the right idea, could use some Choptle-away from Billy Mays. Overdoing it with this sauce can cause some painful bathroom visits, usually in the morning functioning as your own natural alarm clock. And I should also note that the smell coming out is horrendous pending on how much you had. The smell is soo bad even from your flatulence I could see it ending marriages, so guys always check your wife or girl friend agro meters before daring to partake of this forbidden but illustrious and decadent delicacy!Why would anyone eat something that does this to them, Kyle might ask..... but in the words of Cartman who said it best.."Dude. Have you had chipotle? It's really good."

OK.  I admit it.  I am a total sucker for anything that has the word "chipotle" in it.  This is no exception.  This is a pretty good sauce that goes well with more than your standard taco bell fare.  I have used it on steak and chicken.  Tastes great!  I have used it as a dip for cold veggies, tasted good!  I might be a bit biased but this was really good stuff.Pros:1. Tangy and tasty.  Has a nice "chipotle" kick to it.2. Versatile.  I found it went with many, many things.3.  You don't need much to get the kick.Cons:1. I am pretty sure this is a slippery slope to the ingestion of some very unhealthy food.  (Not the sauces fault!)Great stuff.  I plan on ordering  more.  The only reason I am rating 4 instead of 5 stars is the moderately high calorie and sodium content.

I used this sauce on some chicken and it turned out well. I'm not one for spicy products, so that was the only drawback for me. The consistency was very good as was the flavor. The heat was probably mild for most people, for me it was a little too much. I had to cut it with some sour cream... but that did work. Worth a try for sure.

column9: You've definitely had bolder chipotle sauce, but this will do in a pinch and makes a decent substitute for ketchup, mayo, etc.
column10: Bit late to the party with this review, but I wanted to wait until I'd finished the bottle to offer a little praise. This is all-around decent sauce with just the right amount of bite to it. Were I given this in a restaurant, I'd likely complain that it was far too mild for my tastes, but for home use, where people of varying palettes are likely to use it, I prefer these kinds of squeeze sauces dialed down just a touch, so I can use them in a variety of dishes and they won't overpower. I used this in chicken wraps, on hard-shell tacos (of course!), as a substitute for ketchup in and on just about everything (including cheeseburgers AND french fries!) and even as a salad dressing on a basic garden salad, and it added just the right kick to all of them. Not the hard kick you'd get from something more legitimate or hand-crafted, but a nice kick nonetheless. It's pretty thick to use as salad dressing, actually, but you'll figure it out. I'm guessing it would also sub nicely for mayo on sandwiches and the like. The bottle resided in my fridge for a few months at least, and never went off. Not sure if that's a good sign--I've had dressings and sauces go bad in a much shorter period--but as I don't sauce things up on a regular basis, it was good to meet a bottle that actually kept for a while.

I do not expect miracles from Taco Bell and this certainly is not a miracle.it is bland, with a hint of spice.  Might be better titles "Chipotle Sauce For People Who Do Not Like Spicy Food".The closest I can come is to say it tastes like generic ranch dressing with a hint of Chipotle flavor.  I think you could safely give this to a five year old without fear of burning anything.it's not bad, makes a decent dipping sauce for chicken nuggets but don't expect any real "zing" to your cooking with thisI'll admit my wife took one sniff and declined but she hates *anything* even vaguely hot and while this is not very hot at all, you do get a hint of spice in it.With green peppers a "1" and Habaneros a "10", this is about a "1.1" on the heat sscale.  It's not bad but it's not great and if you expect real spice and heat, try elsewhere on Amazon.(May I suggest TABASCO brand Chipotle Pepper Sauce 5oz. for a real Chipotle experience?)Or if you want to go full gonzo: HOT SAUCE FROM HELL, DEVIL'S REVENGE, HABANERO, from Ass Kickin'

This is a great sauce to use on sandwiches to give them a little extra kick.  Love it with grilled chicken, lettuce, and tomato.  I would thin it a bit to use on a salad, but it's just right with a sandwich.  Could get creative with it.  Meatloaf, maybe?

column9: Tasty sauce, great on a veggie burger
column10: I admit I don't often visit Taco Bell. However, I have enjoyed their bean burritos in the past, as I am a vegetarian and I appreciate that they offer several items on the value menu that I can eat. I like this sauce, and it's good on a veggie burger. I think it might work well with roasted vegetables, as a vegetable dip, but I haven't tried that just yet. Tasty!
Pretty tasty.  I was expecting the ingredient list to be a lot worse with many names I couldn't pronounce, but it's not too bad until you get toward the end of the list!

column9: A little too sweet, but still comestible
column10: These Taco Bell condiments are pretty good, considering what they are: more-or-less standard, corn syrup-sweetened and preservative-laden sauces that go down easy - not too spicy for most folks, and a tad on the sweet side. Not nearly spicy enough and a bit too sweet for me, though. (However, I will admit to dipping cold grilled chicken in this stuff, and eating it rather gleefully...)

Decided to try this on a regular sandwich... Threw it on some wheat break with salami, bologna and mayonnaise, just for kicks.WOW!! It turned out to be far better than expected. I'm not sure if mixing with the mayo is what really brought out the flavor, but you must try it with cold cuts.Outstanding!!

There's nothing really bad about this sauce but it's nothing I find myself craving either.  It's reasonably spicy and seems to have a variety of uses but I still don't find myself using it much.  I tried it on tacos, burgers, etc and it's fine but not great.

First off let me say that I lovvvvvveeee Taco Bell.  To find there sauce now on the grocery counter is a major plus in my book and a smart move on their part.
