column10: My 16 year old daughter is the queen of energy drinks.  I thought that she would be the perfect person to try this drink.  Unfortunately, she only took a sip and gave it back to me.  She said that it had almost no carbonation and tasted like grapefruit.  I decided that I would have to try it too.  Unfortunately, I had to agree with her on this one.  Although the carbonation part did not bother me (I am not fond of carbonated drinks), it did taste kind of like grapefruit...only it was sort of an "off" grapefruit and left a bit of a nasty after taste.  I am not sure that I would buy it again.

This product has a very good taste, not like many of the other energy drinks.  It tastes like berries and is smooth, not tart, at least to me.  I had 2 four ounce glasses during the day.  I didn't notice a huge spike in energy, but I didn't need an afternoon nap either.  It didn't make me jittery etc. and I slept well at night.  I wish it came in a diet drink, no calories.  I would recommend this for the taste.

column9: Taste is better than some energy drinks I've tried - and it's got the usual ingredients for boosting energy
column10: I've tried several different kinds of energy drink - and can't stand the taste of most of them. This one's not bad.  It's got a bit of a fruit-punchy flavor with only a mildly bitter aftertaste from the energy ingredients.  In fact I like it better than most I've tried, with the exception of the Arizona Az Energy drinks, which are more fruity with less bitter afterwards. It does have a lot of sugar, though: 260 calories from high fructose corn syrup and various fruit juice concentrates.  I'll try anything once, and in a pinch I'd try this one again, but next time I think I'll try the sugar free variety.

Wow, I was surprised that this can goes for nearly $28.00 for a case of 12!!  Is it worth the cost?The drink is full of amino acids which are helpful, but it is also full of sugar and caffeine, which are not.There are all sorts of warnings for children and pregnant women not drinking this stuff.  Not sure if that's real or just a tantalizing bit of danger (read: promotion & marketing ploy) to get you to buy it.Taste:  Doesn't have an after-taste like some energy drinks do. I did notice a bit of perk, but that's probably due to the sugar and caffeine.Recommendations:  Probably save your money.  Eat your chow boys and girls.  It's the protein in your meals, not the sugar, that gives lasting energy and a high metabolism.[I got this free on the Amazon Vine program.]

Having enjoyed No Fear's Sugar-Free energy drinks for quite some time now and being offered the Super Energy Supplement via the Vine Program, I decided to give it a shot.  What I got was a can of generic energy drink with the standard generic citrus-like, lightly carbonated taste and a bizarre but brief aftertaste that I can best explain as tasting like the smell of old cigarette ashes.I had a sausage, egg, and cheese croissant on the morning that I consumed this drink, to give you an idea of what was in my stomach when I drank it.  I had stayed up fairly late the night before and really needed a bit of a kick.  Instead of my usual coffee, I opted for the No Fear instead.  Initially the taste isn't bad, but as I've already mentioned, there's a very, very brief and nasty aftertaste after each sip.  I drank the No Fear on my way to work after eating my breakfast and finished the entire can (all 260 calories of it) in a twenty-five minute period.Once I arrived at work, I allowed thirty minutes to pass before expecting any results.  I got none.  In fact, I was just as tired after drinking the No Fear as I was before drinking it.  This sort of surprised me, though, as the sugar-free version of this drink always gives me a good kick for a few hours.Overall, I think I'll stick with the sugar-free No Fear and only grab one of these if I'm in need of an energy drink and no Monster drinks are available.

column4: Michael A. Saxton "Dark Lord of the Sith"
column10: The No Fear energy supplement is pretty much a standard energy drink, much like Monster, Venom, and the others. The flavor itself is one that you have to get used to, just like many of the other ones of this style. It's not terrible (doesn't taste like medicine) but it's not fruit punch either. I reacted to this the way I typically react to energy drinks so I'll describe it in general terms. I am the type who is sensitive to caffeine and herbal energy blends. As such, a can like this is one I will nurse throughout the day. You need to know your limits. Some people can pound them like a bottle of beer at a party. I am not one of them. If I drink this stuff too fast it drives my heart rate up and makes me bounce off the walls, then I'm burned out when it wears off. Sipped slowly throughout the day, I don't have a problem and I can sustain the "wake-up" all day and into the evening.Again, be aware, too much of this stuff can be harmful. If you have anxiety problems and you pound this, it can make matters worse. Same with high blood pressure or any of that. Also, this particular one is not sugar free, so you're talking added calories. If you're watching your carb intake or your weight, go for one of the sugar free ones.

column9: Not my favorite but it does work
column10: Well, The smell was not as bad as Redbull but I still had to hold my breath while I drank it. I have no idea what flavor it is supposed to be but it is tolerable.The definite pros are that it did work well. Each can has two servings, I downed them both after a particularly grueling workout. I'm happy to report that I did feel renewed and my energy levels lifted and kept me going for the rest of the day.I would use this product again - however I might add I would prefer a Full Throttle for better flavor. Also what is it with the Soy? Why is soy in this drink? To what end? So I suppose I should add that those with Soy allergies will/should take a pass on this.

column9: More energy or just a sugar high?
column10: This did give me more energy, but it was very short lived and had me wondering if it was just a sugar high because this one can packs in 66 g of sugar!  Total calories per can are 260 and total carbs 68g.  Add in the fact that the second ingredient is high fructose corn syrup and that it contains soy and it's a guarantee I won't pick up another can.  Gaining short lived energy isn't worth it to me to put that kind of garbage and empty calories into my body.

I have little experience with energy supplements, so I can only review, not compare.The first aspect of any consumable is its taste.  On first gulp, one is doubtful, but as you proceed it becomes quite palatable, although not something you would probably drink for the pleasure of it.  You will find yourself trying to guess what the flavors are.  My guess: grape, cranberry, and orange.  It has a very pleasing astringent effect which I like, somewhat like Coke, but more so.As to its energizing effect, I can say that it is not like the fabled NZT, but I am still awake and ready to take on my tax preparation, which would usually sap my energy for at least a few days.A note of caution however.  The label says it contains 130 calories.  But if you look above that you will note that it says that a can contains two servings.  So double the calories.  Being carbonated, it is unlikely you will drink half and store the other half.  If one were to drink 260 calories of Coke or Pepsi, you might feel the same energizing effect, with a better taste.  It does however have a nice dose of several vitamins, especially B.Enough said, you be the judge.

column9: Tastes Better Than Most Energy Drinks
column10: Most energy drinks don't live up to the buzz.  They taste awful and the energy boost neverequals the hype.  So it was with some trepidation that I tried No Fear Super energy Supplement.  One large can contains two servings so I split it with a friend.  He thought it tasted like a strong strawberry soda but didn't notice any energy boost.  I would describe the flavor as a grapefruit.It was pretty good, excellent for an energy drink with only a slight and short lasting metallic afertaste.  I too noticed no discernable difference in my energy. I am a heavy coffee drinker however my friend does not imbibe so I can't attribute the lack of effect to caffeine resistance..  So if you are looking for a change of pace flavorwise, this might satisfy.  However, if you are seeking a shot of energy, stick with coffee or coke.

This energy drink tastes OK. As for the energy kick, I didn't feel any, though I remained alert. So, overall, extra money, extra calories and some questionable ingredients. For me, I prefer Coca Cola. However, if someone is curious about this drink, it might work for him/her, as for taste and possible buzz.

A single can of this super energy drink is good for 2 servings.  Each serving has 130 calories, which means if you drink this all at once you will have twice as many calories.  Some of the active ingredients listed are: caffeine, taurine, L-carnotone and arginine.  There is plenty of corn syrup in this drink.  It is bubbly drink with ginseng and grape flavor and my can had beverage in reddish color.  This drink will definitely keep you up, but I am not sure that calorie count is worth it.

I started out with half of the can because the can is labeled as two servings.After about 20 minutes I went back and finished the other half.This taste is not terrible. Its actually drinkable but it is very sweet (I never put sugar in my tea or coffee).You can smell and taste the "vitamins". To me the smell is a little worse than the taste but overall not bad.As for the caffeine you can tell there is some. There was a slight energy boost.No jittery feeling. But not enough caffeine to stand up to others.Also, too much sugar for me.

A Decent Energy DrinkNo Fear Super Energy Supplement.  I am not so sure what is so super about it, but it is a nice energy drink.The color is a dark red and you have a medium level of carbonation, not too bubbly that it burns going down, but not so flat that is has no bite.The predominant flavor is grape, backed with some tropical flavors like guava, mango maybe some passion fruit.  I suppose the best way to describe the flavor is a grape based tropical flavor; very pleasant, nothing funky and no bad aftertaste.They describe the drink as 2 servings in the can.230 calories total.174 mg caffeine totalThe only sweetener I could read on the label was high fructose corn syrup.A warning on the can said it contained soy, for those with soy allergies, not sure where the soy is from as I couldn't identify any soy based ingredients on the label.The buzz is good.  Doesn't come on too strong or give the shakes, tapers off after couple hours I didn't notice any big crash.Suffice to say an average energy drink.  Nothing special, I tend to imagine this is a drink designed to sell to the market that "No Fear" appeals to.  Not a bad drink, not my favorite either.  Only real reason to stick with it is if you are a big fan of the taste in my opinion.  But it is worth giving a try.

I enjoyed the taste of No Fear, but I can't say that it gave me any more energy than the other energy drinks on the market today.  Since I do, occasionally, indulge in a few energy drinks from time to time, I can say it delivered as much energy as other supplement brands. The four stars were mainly for the taste.

column9: Sweet pink grapefruit juice flavor, great energy boost
column10: The flavor of this energy drink is really good, kind of like a sweet pink grapefruit juice. If you like a drink that tastes more like fruit juice instead of a flavor like Red Bull, you will like this. Although there are added vitamins, Taurine, L-Carnitine, L-Arginine, etc, I didn't notice any "vitamin-y" aftertaste. I thought it gave me a good all-day energy boost with no negative side effects like jitters or nervousness. I generally liked most things about it, but thought it was just a bit too sweet. A little less sugar would have made me give it 5 stars. Other than that, I would try this again.

I really liked the taste of this drink - it reminded me of a cherry soda. There was no aftertaste and it did seem to give me more energy to get through the part of the day that just drags on.  I also thought it worked fairly quickly.  I was a bit surprised to discover that each can actually contains 2 servings, at approximately 130 calories each, so it's definitely not a diet-friendly drink. Although I think the drink did provide more of a boost than a diet soda, for me, it's just not worth the extra calories on a regular basis.  That said, I would drink it again and I would recommend the drink to people who are looking for energy drinks or don't mind the calories (and sugar).

column9: Eh. Not bad, but not a fan.
column10: A little too fragrant and intense for my taste. Somewhere between strawberry soda and grapefruit juice. Leaves kind of a bitter taste in my mouth for an hour after drinking it which makes me feel as if I'm thirstier than before I drank it.Note that this is a TWO-serving can with each serving having about as much caffeine as a cup of coffee.Also - take my lackluster opinion with a grain of salt - I think energy beverages are a bit childish to begin with. This was the first one I ever tried.If you want juice, drink juice. If you want coffee, drink coffee. If you want soda, well, you get the idea. Or maybe you just need a nap.UPDATE:Bumping up a star. Saved half the can for my 19-year-old daughter and she loved it, so we'll split the difference. I give it 2, she gives it 4 or more.

column9: An energy drink, not a health supplement ... don't be confused!
column10: I appreciate the can labeling for stating nutritional facts and that there are two servings per can.  Like most people will probably do, I drank the entire thing minus a couple of sips.The drink labels itself as a "super-energy supplement".  The word "supplement" in and of itself has health benefits implied.  There are no specific health benefits to this drink and it shouldn't be consumed or bought with that in mind.  The ingredients labeled across the top - especially L-Carnitine has received press over the past few years as a fat dissolver, muscle builder.  Unfortunately, L-Carnitine interferes with Thyroid hormones (Synthroid, etc) and can make them less effective.  You won't see warnings about that on the can but it's something worth being aware of.The amount of caffeine (per serving) in this drink is about the same as a cup of coffee or a Red Bull Energy Drink, 8.4-Ounce Cans, 4-Count (Pack of 6).  I prefer my coffee with my occasional Red Bull because I love the taste of that.This drink has an appealing looking can and catchy name "No Fear".  This branding has made it's way into some of the MMA circles too (Uriah Faber).  The taste of this drink is citrus-like and has a predominant grapefruit taste to it.  It is sour to the taste buds and actually defies the 66 grams of sugar that it contains (33 per serving - 2 in a can).I got the kind of kick a Mountain Dew gives - too much sugar, too much stimulant.  3 stars for an overhyped, pricey energy drink billed as a supplement.  At least a Red Bull states what it is and doesn't pretend to be anything it's not.Coffee and an occasional Red Bull suit me just fine.

A boost in the energy department is always welcome, whether it's for an early morning wakeup call or a mid-day pickup, and for those who don't care for coffee there are a wide range of energy drink options available. No Fear's entry into the cut-throat arena is a tasty one that I'd definitely try again.The flavor is a blend of fruits, which I thought tasted like peach with a hint of grape, while my wife took a sip and proclaimed, "Definitely pineapple!" Whatever any given drinker gets out of the fruit blend, it's definitely a better taste than the average energy drink and has a much more pleasant flavor than Rockstar or Monster.On the ingredient and nutrition front, No Fear has a lot less Vitamin B6 and B12 than other varieties, with most of the energy instead coming from the taurine, caffeine, and sugar.  A full can gave me a bit less of an energy jolt than a shot of Five Hour Energy, but it also didn't make me jittery at all. If you like the sugary energy drinks but want a better flavor than the rest of the competitors, definitely give No Fear a try.

column9: Tastes good and provides a quick pick, however also contains a lot of sugar
column10: The taste is good and it has enough caffeine (174mg per can) and taurine (2000mg per can) to provide a good long lasting pick-up. It also has some trace vitamins added, which although nice, still don't make this a healthy beverage by any means. It would be nice if the Amazon product page listed the full ingredients for this product and as things stand now (and have for the past week or so), the short sentence that does serve as a product description lists this as being sugar free which it is not. They do make a sugar free version of this product and it looks like they simply used the same product page for both. I did chuckle a bit because right above the sugar free description is a large legal disclaimer saying the actual ingredients as listed on the can may be different from those listed on the website.It does contain a large amount of sugar (OK technically high fructose corn syrup). The sugar will keep me from buying this paticular version in the future as I have no issues bombing my body with too much caffeine, taurine, and B vitamins but I have to draw the line somewhere. If you have no issue with the sugar content then this is a good choice as it taste good an is effective. I am hopeful someone will take the time to correct the "sugar free" error and then expand on the product description on the main page.Servings: 2Calories: 130 Per serving or 260 per canSugar: 33 grams per serving (66g in the can)Caffeine: 87mg per serving (174mg if you drink the can)Taurine: 1000mg servingInositol: 100 mg servingginseng: 50 mgguarana: 50 mggrape seed extract: 25mgL-carnatine: 25mgL-Arginine: 10 mgAlso has Vitamins C, B6, B12, folic acid, selenium, and zinc ranging from 10%-100% of RDA per serving.

This is the  first energy drink I've tried.  The 16 ounce can has 2 servings at 130 calories each - so - it's a great candy bar snack substitute.No Fear Super Energy Supplement is very delicious, perfect afternoon pick me up. It's lightly carbonated, tastes fruity and there's no added sugar.I'm really tired of coffee by noon and No Fear is a refreshing change.Vitamin C, B6, B12, Selenium and Taurine are a few of the ingredients I wouldn't get in my coffee!Thumbs up to No Fear, Super Energy Supplement.

column9: It's pretty good, and it works a little better than most other energy drinks...
column10: I have a very high tolerance for energy drinks, so I was pleased that this one gave me a noticeable boost in my energy level. I deliberately waited until a morning when I when to bed ultra-late and got up ultra-early, to see how well it would work, and I was pleased. I wasn't bouncing off the walls or anything, but I didn't have any issues with sleepiness and my energy was consistent. Focus also wasn't a problem.Energy drinks tend to have a characteristic sort of 'herbal' taste to them, and this one is no exception, but I actually enjoyed the flavor. It's flavored with grape juice and more generic 'fruit juice' (per the label), and it tastes good- sort of like a carbonated fruit punch. There IS an aftertaste, but it's really mild and brief.I don't normally use or recommend energy drinks, but I enjoyed this one and it worked.

Let me admit straight off that I have never used an energy drink before and this was my first attempt.  I was very happy with the results and felt a noticeable a little boost in energy but the sweetness of the drink prevented me from rating it five stars.The taste of this drink reminded me of a cherry soda.  It was easy to drink the whole 16 ozs and I felt an increased alertness and little boost of energy for the next 4 hours.  Not being familiar with energy drinks, I was afraid of how it would taste and any after effects but this drink dispelled both of these worries.I will be purchasing this energy drink again since it did provided a boost in energy without any bad after effects.

This No Fear Super Energy Supplement drink has a crisp, fruity taste, like Pomegranate.  Each 16 ounce can is supposed to have 2 servings in it, but once the tab is pulled, you have to drink this beverage or lose the fizz.  Each can has your daily recommended vitamin C, Vitamin B6 and Vitamin B12.The price is prohibitive.  If you think you need this particular product, and have prime shipping, you will pay close to $2.50 per can, which is probably higher than retail.  If you are paying for shipping, it will cost more than that.

column9: Great tasting and a good kick, without making me shaky
column10: I've been drinking No Fear for around about 6-7 years now.  I've tried numerous other energy drinks (during a long period when No Fear was unavailable as they changed distributors), and nothing has ever even come close in flavor and kick.Like all energy drinks, it probably is an acquired taste for most, but after a couple cans you'll be hooked.  Energy drinks are highly personal, but for me, I've always gotten a solid, long-lasting kick from No Fear, without the shakiness, nervous energy and inability to concentrate I've experienced with other drinks.Currently you'll probably only find this stuff on the shelves in Arizona as they expand their distribution, so a case of 12 might be quite a leap for a new drinker.  I'd suggest trying several cans over a few days before you decide if you like the stuff!  On the off chance that you don't want to finish your case, send it my way!

column9: New No Fear Super Energy Supplement Is Worth A Try !
column10: This is a new, nice energy supplement drink that can please folks wanting a quick Energy Pick-Up.  It comes in 16 oz. cans containing Arginine, Taurine, and L-Carnitine. The taste is interesting and the product does seem to pick you up.  It contains a HUGE array of desirable supplements, from Sugars, to Folic Acid, To Vitamin B12, Caffeine, and much, much more !!  It's fairly priced, equivalent to products in its class.  If you want a "pick-me-up" in the afternoon, this would probably fit your needs !!

column9: A distant runner up to Monster
column10: Not a fan of No Fear. It has a very sweet & fruity soda flavor with an unpleasant aftertaste. It left me feeling dehydrated and cotton-mouthed instead of refreshed and energized.Energy drinks for me are few and far between. I will continue to stick with Monster on the occasions I pick one up though.

column9: No Fear of the Supplement, Some Fear of the Price
column10: I got a single can of this as a sample from the Amazon Vine program.  I've never been one to drink energy drinks as I have always feared they would be overstimulating, so I don't have a lot of experience with them.  I split the drink with my son, since one can has two servings.  We both knew right away that we liked the taste.  To me it tastes like a delicious fruit punch. I was waiting for a jolt after drinking it, but none came.  I looked on the can and saw that it has less caffeine than a cup of coffee, and I read somewhere that taurine is supposed to regulate blood sugar, so that was a plus.  It's really hard to read the ingredients and supplement facts, and it took me a while to figure out that its name was No Fear.  I am an allergic person, and morning mucus is often a problem for me.  I was pleasantly surprised to find that after drinking it I was spitting up a lot of mucus.  In a little while my bronchials and head were clear, and I felt calm yet alert.  I think the price is kind of high, but I was thinking I might be able to stop buying Mucinex and use this product instead.  Putting it in a can almost forces you to drink 2 servings at once unless you have a good stopper for the can.  A bottle with a screw top would be better.  Nevertheless, I'm giving it 5 five stars because it makes me feel good, and that's what it's all about.

I'm a coffee drinker and I also use the 5 hour energy shots so I didn't expect to get a big energy rush from this as I've built up tolerance to caffeine and vitamin B. However this drink did give me a boost that was very smooth and without jitters. The ingredients are basically identical to other drinks of this sort but what surprised me was the taste. While not great it was pretty good and had minimal aftertaste. That sets it apart from other energy drinks I've tried, and I've tried just about all of them. If you like this type of product then this is definitely worth a look. I checked the label and there wasn't any specific flavor listed so I guess there's only the one.

In the cutthroat market of energy drinks, you would think someone would come along and have a lower price. I am not a coffee drinker, I prefer an energy drink when I wake up. The "No Fear" energy drink is like all the other products out there. The taste was not that bad and had the same ingredients as other brands. As far as the product it did its job and I liked the taste. However, the price is just like everything else out there with no bulk discount. I am able to get AMP or NOS at 2 for $3 at most gas stations in my area, I will stick with them. I would consider buying this, but not at the current price.

column9: Great taste - wrong description on page
column10: This energy drink is very good tasting, IMO.  It's extremely sweet...extremely, which I happen to like.  It tastes like a mixed berry drink to me, and it goes down nice and smooth.  There's no overly harsh taste from caffeine or carbonation like I've gotten from other drinks.  For me, it's something that I would enjoy in the afternoon but not early in the morning, though, so it isn't my choice for an early morning pick-me-up.  Since I drink caffeine in the morning and not in the afternoon, I "like" but don't "love" this stuff.As for the description on Amazon, it's incorrect at the time of this review.  I'd never had No Fear before and wasn't familiar with it, but the good reviews enticed me to try it.  What also enticed me was Amazon's description that it's sugar free.  While there is a sugar free version (which I noticed after ordering this), this one definitely is not - there are 66 grams of sugar per can.  That's not a cut against the product at all, but had I known that, I wouldn't have ordered this version.If you like sugary drinks and are looking for a sweet energy drink, this is very good stuff and worth giving a try.******************The nutrition facts weren't available when I bought mine, so here's a listing:Serving size:  8 ozServings per container:  2The following are the amount per serving:- Calories = 130- Carbs = 34g- Sugars = 33g- Vitamin C = 100% DV (DV = "Daily Value")- Vitamin B6 = 100% DV- Folic Acid = 10% DV- Vitamin B12. = 100% DV- Zinc = 10% DV- Selenium = 10% DV- Sodium = 4% DV- Potassium = 1% DVProprietary Blend- Taurine = 1000mg- Inositol = 100mg- Caffeine = 87mg- Panax ginseng Root Extract = 50mg- Guarana Seed Extract = 50mg- Grape Seed Extract = 25mg- L-Camitine = 25mg- L-Arginin = 25mg

column9: Great stuff and someone bought the company and is supposedly reproducing it!
column10: A company called Shadow Beverages and Snacks bought No Fear and is reproducing them.  They only kept the Red & Blue.  There appears to be a Berry Lemonade one.

I never liked any other energy drink like this before, and I've tried alot! I used to get these all the time before work to drink before the 2pm crash! Like others I can't get it around my area anywhere anymore! I believe it was originally by Sobe, bought by Pepsi, replaced by Pepsi's new n-r-g drink and now distributed by Shadow bev.(don't quote but pretty sure :) As long as Amazon carries this, I will continue to buy a few cases at a time because this is my 2nd case and they sold out fast the last time! KEEP IT STOCKED AMAZON PLEASE!!!

No Fear used to be my coffee, but tastier and without the ex-lax effect. Out of all the much worse energy drinks out there (Rock Star and it's billion different flavors, Red Bull you can feel the kidney stones going down your throat practically, Full Throttle's dry and dehydrating drinks and Monster just doesn't count as an energy drink) No Fear was taken off the shelves. The Mother Load I may be able to understand, because that may have been a heart attack in a can. The regular red can, the sugar free and the orange dragon fruit had what every other energy drink out there lacks: delicious taste. There's something else about it, and I don't know how they did it but it also doesn't make you crash. When caffeine wears off it wears you out, but No Fear surprisingly didn't give you that effect. I encourage stores to put this product back on the shelves and No Fear to freaking keep producing these perfect replacements for coffee!
i am a big fan of no fear.i only wish shadow beverage whould make it avalable in my area.thnx amazon

Unfortunately, after the Sobe/No-Fear split and purchase by Pepsi, Pepsi discontinued manufacture of No-Fear. The greatest energy drink out there.Thank you Amazon for stocking up!One con, though: I've gotten 3 cases since I found No-Fear here. The last one had a popped can, which soaked the cardboard base and began to mold. I personally don't care (aside from the one can loss), but, maybe some better handling would limit this possibility.Other than that, friggin amazing drink, at a great price, with quick shipping!

I've been hooked on this drink since 2005, when I lived in DC I used to get giant boxes shipped to me and now I'm being told by all my local gas stations that Pepsico has discontinued it in the United States.... anyone know if this is true? Amazon is the last place left I can find it anywhere, and if I could I'd buy'em all!

These energy drinks are the best!!!! Me and my husband LOVE them!!! We used to drink at least one a piece everyday, but you can't find them in the stores anymore..WHY!!!! They have a GREAT taste and you don't crash with these like other energy drinks. I wish they would bring them back to my local stores. It is a lot of trouble to have to order them online, but since that is the only way to get them...I have to.

I should state up front that I *like* energy drinks. I consume far too many of them. However, this "No Fear" was the absolute bitterest-tasting drink I've ever had in my life, and I actually had to spit out my first sip and dump the rest of the contents of the can down the drain. It tasted HORRIBLE. On the up-side, I really thought the design of the can was awesome, with the skull-and-bones universal sign for "poison" as a logo.

My husband loves energy drinks.  He is the person I buy them for.  But he wasn't really a fan of this one.  Since most of them have relatively similar ingredients, he's most concerned about taste, and he thought this one wasn't that great.  We won't be buying it.

Sobe drinks can be pretty good stuff...just in case you didn't know this was a Sobe product, it is.The tastes, it's all relative.  Some don't like the taste of energy drinks, some find it ok, but they always taste similar even if they use some flavor addition from one to the next.  To me, I find it strangely distantly similar to licorice...I don't know.The bad, in my own contention of course, seeing those new commercials about sugar being sugar and your body can't tell the difference...this product contains high fructose corn syrup (at least it did as of this review or when I received it).Product details:Nutrition Information: Carbonated Water, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Citric Acid, Taurine, Grape Juice Concentrate (Color), Sodium Citrate, Natural Flavor, Inositol, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C), Caffeine, Caramel Color, Fruit Extract (Color), Monopotassium Phosphate, Creatine Monohydrate, Grape Seed Extract, L-Carnitine, Panax Ginseng Root Extract, L-Arginine Hydrochloride, Zinc L-Methionine, Soy Protein Isolate and Rice Flour, Guarana (Paullinia Cupana) Seed Extract, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride Selenium, Folic Acid, CyanocobalaminThis product is 16 oz and the serving size is half that...so double the nutrition data in the pic I provided if you drink the whole can.

This product has that 'energy drink taste' that we've all now become accustomed to. However, I didn't personally prefer it. It has an overly grapefruit flavor. For background, I prefer RedBull, over Monster. That should let you know if our taste preferences align

column9: Good Taste For An Energy Drink
column10: The No Fear Super Energy Drink actually had a good fruity flavor and no bitter/gross after  taste.I have tried several energy drinks that were hard to swallow and or left a horrible after taste and urge me not to purchase that kind again.It is a large 16oz. I could feel I was a little more energized  shortly after drinking it, that stuck with me most the day.

column9: Get your fix, the right way.
column10: Have you ever woken up wondering what it feels like to be backhanded by a deranged platypus? Yearned for a the feeling of a quick splash to the face of highly potent acid? Hoped to travel through your own body's veins on a makeshift tiny raft? No Fear, Super Energy Supplement, won't answer any of these questions or curiosities. But it will give you similar desires.I'm not sure if No Fear, Super Energy Supplement, changes my brain chemistry, but whatever it does to me I can't trade for any sensation in the world. After drinking it, I become aware that the only way I can remain happy is to find more No Fear, Super Energy Supplement.I happily lap the substance off one of my shoulders, as is easy to do when one is mostly submerged in a bathtub full of No Fear, Super Energy Supplement, and contemplate the universe's most trivial absurdities.By all means, I recommend this beverage; just beware the comedown.

Now this drink has real flavor, rather then just a differnt slant on sweetness.I thought it tasted like mango, chased with peach & maybe a bit of raspberry twist.No Fear has a lighter, cleaner fruitly flavor then many energy drinks,and is very enjoyable going down.I was surprised to notice a definable boost of energythat far outlasted by about 2-3 hours the Lo-Carb Monster drink I'm used to.It was a good feeling all the way, and no let-down.Oh but here's the down side, I'm going to mention 3 of the biggest differencesbetween No Fear and Lo-Carb Monster.No Fear;Calories - 130Total carb - 34 gSugars - 33gMonster;Calories - 10Total carb - 3gSugars - 3gIn all fairness I'm sure Monster has less bad stuff because it's low-carb,still no matter how you slice it, it has less bad stuff.I really enjoyed the taste, and LOVED the energy of No Fear.I can't figure how the drink can taste lighter, and yet have more sugar, but it does.If you're someone who's not concerned about extra calories you should give No Fear a try.It delivers a powerful engery boost.

I love this product.  After one can, I'm sold.  I might opt to try the sugar free since the carb content is 30+ per serving and each can has 2 servings.  That's a bit much for one can.  The reason why I'm sold? I was dead tired and this woke me up and got me moving early in the morning. I had nothing else in my stomach and it did not cause a stomach ache.I personally did not detect an after taste and thought the drink was refreshing and light tasting.  Yes, it's sweet, it's going to be it has tons of sugar. I also noted a huge sodium content. I mention that in case you wish to know.  I personally only drink Energy drinks in extreme emergencies and so I don't mind the carb and sodium content in this product but I might if I drank them more frequently.In closing, it has a nice flavor and does the job you expect an energy drink to do.

column9: Great if Packaged Correctly - Awesome Energy Drink
column10: Have been getting this for a while and when local stores had trouble getting it, I turned to Amazon.With Prime shipping, this is a great deal and an awesome product.The only issue I have occasionally, is if this is incorrectly packaged at the warehouse, it will arrive damaged.It ships in a 12 can case, but the warehouse has a habit of packing on its side which can result in damage.To date 30% of my shipments have arrived damaged BUT, customer service has been awesome resolving issues!!!  My hat is off to those folks!!!

This brand of energy drink tastes good and really gives you a jolt of energy.  I didn't have jitters afterwards and I noticed a difference in focus.  I have problems with some of them making me jittery but this one really worked with no side effects.

column9: Good but not great energy drink
column10: The "No Fear" energy drink had a good flavor that tasted like a combination of citris and apple. While the flavor was okay and the drink did wake me up without causing me to be jittery, it was lacking something. Perhaps a little more carbination would have helped. I didn't like this drink as well as "Rockstar" or "Monster", but if you are looking for something different to try, "No Fear" is a good alternative.

Energy drinks are pretty common these days and tend to contain the same main ingredients (sugar, caffine, taurine) so it really comes down to how they taste and do they give you a kick.  On the taste side this one has a kind of light fruity taste that I found pretty refreshing.  It did not taste very "energy drinky".  On the kick side I really didn't notice much, certainly no more that the average Red Bull or Monster - but your mileage may vary.  I'd recommend trying it for the taste and you may end up liking it.

column9: No Fear Super Energy Supplement Works, if You Can Get Past the Taste
column10: Everyone could use a boost in energy from time to time and with the abundance of energy drinks and pills available, that added boost isn't very far away. No Fear Super Energy Supplement is one such energy beverage that is readily available and prepared to add a little bounce in your step, increasing alertness and filling the body with vitamins, minerals, and other ingredients known for their energy- enhancing qualities.Energy drinks often have an odd taste and No Fear is no different. However, it isn't as bad as some other energy drinks I have sampled over the years and I must agree with others who claim that it has a taste similar to that of Red Bull. The flavor is berry- like, but with added herbs and other things that are somewhat difficult to describe. The taste is certainly not something I would seek out, but it isn't terrible and I found that it left the palate in a short time. There was no nasty aftertaste, so once you got past the few seconds of unpleasantness, there was nothing left to remind you of the so- so flavor you just experienced.As for the energy component, No Fear is about as good as any other energy drink and I found that it did succeed at making me feel a little more alert and ready to get up and go. I sampled this drink for the first time when it was getting late- around 10pm- and I was starting to feel a little drowsy. Normally, I rely on caffeine to get me through these moments, but this time, I reached for No Fear instead and I found that I did feel wider awake and ready for a second wind.Energy drinks have their usefulness and No Fear is good at boosting energy so you can go about your day. It isn't the best energy drink I have ever tried and certainly not the best tasting. But the flavor isn't bad and it does make a difference when you need to eliminate sluggishness and keep yourself alert and ready for action.

column9: The only thing setting it apart is the skull
column10: I have had my fair share of energy drinks...from the old fave, Red Bull to the more sinisterly painted Monster energy drink. The basic ingredients in these drinks are the same with differences in amount. And of course let's not forget the packaging. That is where the drinks differ. While Red Bull has a more subdued packaging, Monster drinks looks like something radioactive that a Marvel Superhero would drink before "hulking" out. No fear continues the trend by featuring a skull with wings which would make an awesome tattoo if you were to get one.The taste isn't bad but at the same time, it doesn't taste significantly different to set it apart from the other drinks on the market.

column4: M. Jobbagy "Follow Your Bliss - Joseph Cambell"
column9: Better than sucking sugar from a straw
column10: As far as energy drinks go, this wasn't so bad. I don't think you can find one that actually tastes good, but that's mainly because of the energy ingredients. I have had far worse, and this one didn't give me the jitters or shakes as some will, and did provide a decent energy boost.A lot of people seem to really love this one over others, for me, it's better than most, but not something I will regularly consume. A few diet cokes usually have enough caffeine to 'pick me up', and tastes MUCH better....

column9: Low fiz taste makes No Fear a good buy
column10: This lightly carbinated energy drink, that has a tropical fruit flavor and smell, brings a crips drink that would be great in hot weather. There is virtually no aftertatse. It is better on the inside of the can than out, dinged for weird art graphics and hard to read red print on black base can. But, if you're looking for a nice ebergy drink to get you through those last hard hours, it is a good buy.

column9: I will stick with 5-hour Energy Drinks
column10: I usually drink a 5-hour Energy drink5-Hour Energy Extra Strength (24 Bottles Grape) when I first get up so that I can quickly get in to my morning P90X routine. I put one on my nightstand before going to bed and quickly drink it down in the morning. I don't much care for the taste (though I don't exactly hate it) but I like the effect of energy drinks on my exercise performance, and that is why I decided to give this No Fear drink a try. I was disappointed and will stick with 5-Hour Energy. Here are my thoughts:1 - Calories: At 260 calories a can, there is a 65X difference. It does not fit in with my nutrition goals.2 - Taste: It's a little sweeter than a Red Bull. I don't much like Red Bull though and the flavor of No Fear was not an improvement over 5-Hour Energy.3 - Size: This is a BIG can yet it has roughly the same amount of caffeine, taurine, etc as 5-Hour Energy. Why drink this massive can of fluid when a small shot will do? If I REALLY enjoyed the taste, I might feel otherwise.4 - Energy Boost: I found the effect of No Fear to be similar to that of 5-Hour Energy.Bottom line: 5-Hour Energy works better for me.

No Fear,Super Energy Supplement is your typical energy drink, and in my opinion tastes very similar to Red Bull. I tend to find all energy drinks taste the same though. Drinking the whole can at once also provides about the same "pick me up" as drinking 2 cans of Red Bull. If you're a fan of energy drinks, you'll probably like "No Fear,Super Energy Supplement". If you hate the taste of products such as Red Bull, you probably won't.

column4: Christina Paul "Live like you MEAN it!!"
column10: I am a rather casual consumer of energy drinks.  I have had my fair share of them to get me through the day as needed. My very favourite drink got pulled off of the market for no other reason than because of its controversial name.  "No Fear Energy Drink" has an eye catching can design and what's inside had a decent berry taste.  Many drinks are either sickeningly sweet or have funky aftertaste due to the taurine and other ingredients. No Fear was better than a good many better selling energy drinks.  As for its properties:  it really was rather mediocre as far as how much of an energy 'boost' that it gave.

column9: Best tasting energy drink I've ever had
column10: I'll have an energy drink on occassion but am not addicted to them as some of my friends are. With No Fear, Super Energy I would definitely consider drinking them on a regular basis. Most energy drinks taste like cough syrup to me but this one has a pleasant fruit taste. It was more like drinking fruit punch with a little kick. I didn't feel a zinging energy boost but I did manage to stay up later that evening after drinking the supplement at about 2:00 in the afternoon. I would recommend this for anyone who dislikes the taste of energy drinks like Monster or Red Bull and only need a slight energy burst but if you need a super boost of energy pass on No Fear.

`No Fear, Super Energy' is a big claim when there are so many energy drinks out there.  For about less than three bucks a can, it competitive in price, but I have to be honest.  The taste was bad.  It was like a chemical peach flavor without much fizz.  I am sensitive to caffeine and Taurine, but really did not feel much of a boost.  If you like your vitamins, there is plenty of Vitamin C, B6 and B12.  The calorie intake is 260 a can!  I think I will stick to Red Bull or RockStar, even if they cost a little more.

column9: 2 Servings Per Container - No Energy Boost for Me
column10: I've not tried a bunch of energy drinks, but have used Celsius products Celsius Green Tea, Raspberry Acai, Value Pack, 4 ct.in the past, and drink Optimum Nutrition Essential Amino Energy, Fruit Fusion, 30-Count before workouts; with great success in boosting my energy levels using both products.When given the opportunity to try out 1 can of No Fear 'Super Energy' Supplement via the Amazon Vine Reviewers program, I jumped at the chance.What I like about this drink:1. It tastes good.  Kind of like Squirt soda or a sweet grapefruit juice.2. There are TWO servings per can.3. One serving has 100% of your daily recommended Vitamin C, B-12, and B-6.4. It contains Grape Seed Extract, which is believed to boost your immune system.5. Contains some Zinc and Potassium to help with recovery after a workout.What I don't like about this drink:1. The calories - but I hear there's a sugar-free version.  Not sure how that would affect the taste though.2. NO ENERGY BOOST for me.  None. I do drink coffee and perhaps that means my tolerance is higher?3. 34g of carbs per serving.  Again, the sugar-free version might be worth a try for some.4. Two servings in one can may be deceiving to some who would not read the can to see that they'll get 2x's the calories, caffeine, etc... by drinking the whole can.5. Expensive!For me, there are better options out there for energy drink supplements.  My recommendation is to give it a try if you don't mind the sugar and calories in this one, and see if it works for you.

column9: Shareable size, but flavor is meh and no kick?
column10: This large (16oz) two-serving can is big enough to share, and has some ingredients not found in my usual energy drink (Redbull) such as L-Carnitine.  But I found the flavor lackluster, the calorie count high, and somehow I didn't get the bit of a buzz that I normally get from an equivalent amount of Redbull.I've had Redbull in many conditions and combinations and always enjoy it (and always notice a bit of a perk, if not an outright buzz).  There wasn't any similar effect that I noticed from drinking a serving of this NoFear on an empty stomach.  Redbull hardly tastes natural, but this stuff tastes...weird, like flat RC Cola mixed with something.Comparing labels, the NoFear claims slightly higher caffeine content (87g vs 80g) than an 8.4oz Redbull, but also has more calories/carbs.  For a class of product that's already heavy on sugar, adding even more doesn't seem wise.It comes down to that I didn't think "that was tasty!", nor did I feel energized. Flavor preferences are personal, and I'm sure some people will get a caffeine jolt from NoFear, but for my tastes, Not Recommended.

column4: Scary Gertrude,  the Bad Sheriff for Life "Li...
column10: No Fear has soy in it.The initial flavor in this was not too bad.  I don't know that I have ever liked one on the first try - even my favorite sugar free Red Bull.  The initial flavor wasn't too terrible, but then it had a sour aftertaste.  It has a seriously chemical flavor to it and a slippery, kind of oily, feel to it - kind of like pouring gasoline in kool-aid.The problem for me was the excess carbonation.  Take a drink, burp.  Take a drink, burp.  Not something to drink in polite company.Then there is the sugar and the serving size.  I don't know why manufacturers say that 16 oz is 2 servings.  Maybe so that we think there are 130 calories?  There aren't.  There are 260 calories. That's more than my morning omelet.In any case, I wouldn't buy a case of any energy drink without trying one first.

We have cans of the blue Rockstar in this house. We don't drink energy drinks everyday anymore. I did not care for the taste at all. I'd rather just drink a bottle of Mt. Dew. or 2, in replacement of the caffeine. I am not a fan of any sour, and this to me, was sour tasting.

I couldnt make up my mind about this drink...at first  I was thirsty and kept drinking it. It has a  tremendous aftertaste, kind of like aspartine only harsher  The drink is extremely astringent, makes you pucker u. It has  a bit of a citris taste but BITTER like eating dill pickles or alum.  It has a hint of ca I dont know if it is my imagination or what but I think I actually felt a lift from this product.  At first I thought it might be caffeine but that was only 87 grams. It does have quite a bit of sugar (33 grams) and carbohydrates so it is not something i can have all the time

column9: Why would anyone drink 66 grams of sugar in one can?
column10: I'm so glad I read the label before drinking this! I did taste it though, it's HORRIBLE and spit it in the sink, the aftertaste is hard to get rid of even if you don't swallow it. This can has a whopping 66 grams of sugar which would have put me in a sugar coma for a day, hardly something that would give anyone long term energy just a big fat sugar crash. It doesn't even taste good, so why would anyone put this crap in their body? It has lots of caffeine and 260 empty calories per can. There are supposedly two servings per can so if you down this whole can know that you double all the amounts on the label. There is no good reason to consume this stuff.

From the product description: "A brand new taste"- relative to an earlier version? To me it tasted an awful lot like sugar-free grapefruit juice. "Toughest can on the shelf"? I disproved that immediately, while trying to remove the bubble wrap form the single can Vine offered, the knife went a millimeter too deep and made a nice scratch in the can, which immediately burst. I slapped into a containment glass, but it is the Vine's way of rarely offering enough of a food or beverage for the reviewer to form an honest and well considered opinion.OK, ok, I know that's not what they meant by "toughest drink", but I was unaware that was a quality anyone would ever seek in an energy drink.As it stands, I am not very well acquainted with this style of beverage anyway, while I saw them mainly as hangover cures, I guess many regular users see them as an important part of their intake of vitamins and minerals. And Taurine and the other raft of fairly obscure supplements. And often caffeine, although my label was somewhat damaged and I couldn't quite make out the rather extensive list of ingredients. I suspect this is of little interest to the average user in any case.I happened to be pretty beat the day it arrived, and didn't even want to stop for a Five Hour Energy- my usually dependable source of a brief respite from fatigue- so it was a perfect time to try it out. Any "lift" or burst of energy was not readily apparent, although it did help chase away the blahs for a little while. I still went to bed early.

Normally, Energy drinks do not do much for me. Actually, most of them either make me sleepier, or leave me with an odd feeling in the stomach and do nothing to improve my energy. I find that most of the powdered or small bottles of Vitamin-B filled energy drink-mix or "shots" tend to work better, extending my energy for a longer amount of time. Nothing too amazing, but if I don't feel like I am going to make it through a whole work day, I can take one of those and last through the shift and then some.Then I tried No Fear, "Super Energy Supplement" - and I experienced something I had never experienced before! I was not bouncing off the walls, but I went from awfully tired (feeling like I wouldn't last more than half hour before falling asleep) to having plenty of energy for hours and hours and hours! I did not feel too tired to get up and go do work - in fact, I felt like I was full of energy and could do whatever I wanted without worry of tiring myself out! Also, the energy lasted me for quite a long time! Seems to last a good 15 to 18 hours! I drank one just after midnight as I got to work tired, and was still plenty awake and full of energy at 6 PM (18 hours later) trying to get to sleep for the next work day!I found this odd, and figured it may have been a fluke. Considering I have never had such success with energy drinks, I had to perform some tests and compared days where I was not tired to days that I was tired and tried a No Fear drink. I have more energy when tired and using a No Fear than most days when I am fully awake! No Fear helps me go from very tired to being able to perform on one of my better days. I have to say, No Fear works great! No doubt about it - it tastes great, works great, and I am very happy to have found it!I am also very happy about the flavor. I would have to describe the flavor as a grapefruit-soda type flavor. My best description would be "Squirt, but with actual grapefruit flavoring" - because you don't taste much actual grapefruit in those other sodas. I love Squirt and grapefruit flavor, so No Fear's flavor was nothing less than AWESOME! And, I did not get that odd feeling in my belly that I tend to get with most other energy drinks!If you are wondering if No Fear is for you, I would recommend giving it a go. I normally have little to no benefit from energy drinks, and this one really worked! The flavor is great, and I did not experience a lack of energy when it wore off. I seem to have different results than most, but I think it is still worth giving a try!

column9: One of the worst drinks for you
column10: Curious about what your drinking? The second ingredient should be enough to scare you away. After HFCS began to be widely introduced into the food supply 30-odd years ago, obesity rates skyrocketed. And because the sweetener is so ubiquitous, many blame HFCS for playing a major role in our national obesity epidemic. As a result, some shoppers equate HFCS with "toxic waste.It would be helpful if Amazon was responsible and posted Ingredients just like every shopper can look at when your shopping in a grocery store!Carbonated Water, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Citric Acid, Taurine, Natural Flavor, Sodium Citrate, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C), Inositol, Caffeine, Monopotassium Phosphate, Gum Arabic, Grape Seed Extract, L-Carnitine, Glycerol Ester of Wood Rosin, Panax Ginseng Root Extract, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, L-Arginine Hydrochloride, Zinc Methionine Sulfite, Guarana (Paullinia Capurian) Seed Extract, Caramel Color, Selenium Complexed with Amino Acids and Polypeptides, Beta Carotene (Color), Folic Acid, Cyanocobalamin.

I liked the taste of the No Fear energy drink.  I didn't experience any kind of after-taste.  As for any kind of "energy" boost...I don't know.  If I felt any kind of energy boost, it was slight.  But, to be honest and fair, I've tried other brands of energy drinks and I can't say I ever feel any kind of boost.All-in-all, this is a delicious drink and ranks right up there with any of the other drinks on the market.

Does it taste good?  Yes and it better had to be as it packs about 66 grams of sugar per can!  You get your energy blend, vitamins, minerals and other good stuff, but I wish they would consider cutting down on sugar.  While I realize that each can gives you TWO servings (33g per serving,) it is a can, so it would be inconvenient to keep it open while it gets stale and loses the fizz.  If sugar does not bother you, I suppose this is a great choice for you and as with most energy drinks, be careful not to overdose!
I tried Rockstar and Monster and they weren't good tasting. This is a sweet Red Bull kind of drink - like a cherry cola flavor. The can is huge and is two servings. Medium sized kick.

This new flavor of No Fear energy taste quite good. The energy benefit is touted as the best... However, I didn't find it any more energizing than any of the other brands on the market. Personally, I prefer Monster Low Carb.

column9: I LIKED IT SO WELL I BOUGHT THE COMPANY!
column10: Not really:)I absolutely love the taste of this energy drink, though! But does it give you energy? Yep. But I would only use it to do certain things or at certain times of the day. By that, I mean I wouldn't use a whole can of this stuff as pre-workout drink if I was planning on having a massive iron pounding workout. Off the top of my head, I think is roughly 175mg of caffeine in a whole can. It takes about twice that much caffeine for me a big and heavy workout day to give that "in the zone" iron punishing feeling. The best uses I've had with No Fear is drinking a half can in the morning for excellent pick-me-up and taking on days when all I plan to do at the gym is cardio or biceps. Small workouts. For those it works great and I get a good clean energy from it. No jitters. No stomach problems. In fact, I will usually drink half on the way to gym and save the other half while I'm doing cardio.I suppose the downside to No Fear, as with most energy drinks, is that it has quite a bit of sugar and calories. And it's slightly pricey. For me, the calories and sugar are mostly a non-issue since I have a fairly high metabolism rate and mostly watch what I eat(except on the weekends ;) A 16 ounce can has 260 calories and 66 grams of sugar. Not real good for some people. I'm not sensitive to caffeine, at all, so a half of a can may work wonders for some people. I think what really helps provide a good dose of energy(aside from the caffeine) with this stuff is it having 2 grams of Taurine in a can. Add in 200% of B12 and it all comes together to give a rather nice hit. I've tried numerous energy drinks over the years and most I haven't been impressed with either because of taste or lack of energy. The taste of this stuff is very good. Has a nice citrusy afterbite to it. Goes down smooth. The best energy drink I've tried is Knockout Punch. By test I mean taste, price and energy.... that stuff has 320+ mg of caffeine in a can... potent stuff.But you really can't go wrong with No Fear. It's a close 2nd to Knockout Punch Energy Drink. With No Fear you're going to get at excellent tasting energy that is going to give you a good kick in the seat of your shorts if you use it for the right purpose. Just don't drink a can 30 minutes before you workout and think you're going to train like Ronnie Coleman in his prime. I primarily use this a wake me up get me going morning coffee substitute. I hate coffee... but I like this stuff so much I bought a 12 pack after trying a free sample. I'm a stickler for high quality health supplements, so if I buy a case of something you can bet it's good stuff. I give it an 8.5 out of 10 or a 4.25 out of 5.If it would have had a whopping load of caffeine in it it would have gotten at least a 4.5 from me. The Knockout Punch I mentioned eariler I haven't reviewed yet, but I would give it a solid 4.5 stars out of 5, in comparison. With it's only really downsides being too much sugar and calories for some people. To be honest, even being in great shape, I don't need all of the excess junk calories and sugars I get. I don't really complain about that stuff, usually, but I know it's a concern for many people, which is why I always try to point that out in a review.

Energy drinks are one of those things that you love or you hate. Some companies get the flavors right while others miss the boat entirely. No Fear gets it right. Very drinkable and smooth. No major crash afterwards. Those familiar with these types of drinks will not get the "shakes" either. Again, you either buy the conspiracy hype regarding these things being bad for you, or you're an adult who can read a label and know exactly what you are going to get. Personally, I have been enjoying these style drinks in moderation for years. Since this particular brand can be hard to find in some areas, you might as well get it here on Amazon.  No Fear here!

This has a really nice flavor and is not  too carbonated but it did absolutely nothing to my energy level! This is the first time I have tried a product like this. I tried it because I work nights and wanted a little energy boost to help get me through  til quitting time!  I think a little extra caffiene will work and be less expensive.

column9: Yucky Tasting and High in Sugar, Carbs and Calories
column10: I prefer Monster or Rockstar energy drinks, but I am always trying new one's because I like variety. The first thing that I noticed when I got this can was the amount of sugar, carbs and calories in this can. It is ridiculous! 260 calories, 66 gm of Sugar and 68 carbs per can. There is supposedly 2 servings per can, but who drinks just half a can? Plus, in can form it is hard to save.Now for the taste: in my opinion this tasted like sour passion fruit. It was nasty! I wasn't able to drink more than two sips because I found it so repulsive. I realize that people's taste buds are different and some people may love the taste, but I hated it. I recommend trying 16 Pack - Monster Rehab - Tea + Lemonade + Energy - 15.5oz. if you want a great tasting drink that is low in carbs, sugar and calories.

I'm a fan of most energy drinks, but No Fear's Super Energy is not impressive.Each can contains two servings, each serving being 130 calories and 33 grams of sugar, and only 90 milligrams of caffeine. For me that is a lot of empty calories and not a whole lot of "energy" to be honest with you.Taste wise it's actually quite pleasant. Drink it super chilled or iced and it's refreshing.Energy wise, it's not even close to my standard Celsius or GURU  that I drink.If you're not too concerned about calories and want something a bit different than coffee in the morning, give it a shot.If you're wanting some energy and not a bunch of sugar, I'd recommend taking a look at the two products mentioned above.

Received a sample can of this through the Amazon Vine program. I tested it on the morning of my first day with a new job and it certainly provided a boost. Because it was a new job, I hardly slept the night before. In the morning I felt dead tired, so I drank down the can of No Fear. Suddenly, I was ready to face the day. The effect was better than coffee.With all of the above in mind, No Fear Super Energy Supplement is certainly worth a try for those folks looking for something to help keep them awake and alert. No Fear tastes pretty good, and the energy boost effects kick in almost immediately upon drinking it.

column9: Great flavor and no after taste with decent energy
column10: These are expensive per can but testing it out was a pleasant surprise as I liked the fruit juice taste and there was no after taste and it went down smooth. It would be great for mixed drinks too for parties but I just used it as a supplement to lunch and I didn't want to nap around 3 pm when my energy usually dips. Very impressed that I didn't feel jittery or nauseated after drinking it either. I MUCH prefer this one over Red Bull.

column9: Pumps Energy, Taste Could Be Improved
column10: Take it from someone who has never taken an energy drink, never downed an energy "shot". I am a total newbie to the burst of energy you're supposed to get with these new fad drinks. So here is what happened when I tried this product.I waited until I was dragged down and tired. Side bar: I am fit and active, and am rarely tired. Continuing, the day I was dragged down, I drank 1/2 of the can and had to stop because the flavor repulsed me. I forced myself to drink it so I could see if it worked or not. After about five minutes of downing 1/2 of it, I definitely felt a surge of energy. I got to my feet and continued my day with the energy I like to have all the time. I did not notice that the effect died off; I seemed to feel fine the rest of the day (approx from noon to bedtime).So I think this product does what it says. I just wish it tasted better. It was unpalatable to me, but sometimes, medicine doesn't taste as delicious as we wished it did.

column9: Didn't like the taste or the calories
column10: No Fear comes in a 16 oz can. The can contains two servings (total 260 calories per can).I don't know of many people who would drink half of this can and then store the rest for later or share it.This stuff tasted sweeter than regular soda and probably is. It also has a bitter taste almost like grapefruit.It was bad it just wasn't good to me. The first two ingredients were Carbonated water and High fructose corn syrup.There is way too much sugar in this for me. I didn't really feel an energy kick. I would not use it again.

column9: Did not seem all that different from other brands
column10: I will state up front that I do not drink energy drinks frequently.  I like to use them for a big pick-me-up when I really need it.  Therefore, I don't really have a brand loyalty and will usually just drink whatever is on sale or looks most interesting that day.This drink was like most others - a little too sweet and with a flavor I could not exactly place.  The taste was okay, nothing to get excited over, so I was hoping for a big energy boost.  What I got was the normal sort of kick I get from most energy drinks - not really a burst of energy, but feeling slightly more alert and on-the-ball.  The effects just wore off gradually, so at least there was no crash like I have experienced with some.The price is pretty comparable to other such drinks, so there is really no savings to entice me to purchase this brand over any other.  I can't say that I would turn down one if it was offered to me, but I don't think I would go out of my way to seek it out either.

column9: I don't have the energy to get another.
column10: Where red bull is your standard, and for good reason, there are always going to be other attempts at achieving their success. Make it bigger. Creepy can to appeal to the kids. Illusion of a hard core drink without the so-called "kick".It's just "eh". Energy drinks never really taste too great.  So this has it's cough syrup flavored carbonation with extra water to make it big. At least with Red Bull, they have the formula down to give it their "wings".  But No Fear, I fear is too weird.  I don't get it.  I was given one can, so I can only rate my one short experience with it as non-effective, and not worth the unpleasant taste.  I won't be going out of my way to buy one.  But, if I wanted a couple energy drinks, and they were the only ones available, I guess I would get them.  But there really is no point.
drink was ok I guess, didnt taste all that great, not sweet enough for energy drink. didnt notice alot of energy effect.

The No-Fear, Super Energy Supplement is...well, a super-sugary energy drink.  I normally drink diet energy drinks, either Monster or Red Bull, so maybe that was what made this seem so darned sweet to me.Did I feel a significant jolt of energy after consuming it?  No, not so much, especially given that it's a 16 oz can.I prefer Monster to the No-Fear in the "large size energy drink" department.I wish I could write a longer review here, but there's not much to say.  I received this drink for free to test, so I don't know what it costs.  The only reason I'd consider buying No Fear is if it had a substantial price advantage vs. Red Bull or Monster.

column9: I didn't enjoy the taste at all.
column10: No Fear, Super Energy Supplement is not all that its cracked up to be.  I was stoked to try it out because I really enjoy energy drinks.  I didn't care for the juice taste and it was too sweet.  The "juice" taste was too overwhelming for my taste buds and it made me feel loggy instead of refreshed.  You can taste the HFCS in the drink and it taints the product in my book. The sticky sweet taste ruins what could have been a really good energy supplement.  The crash I had afterwards was even worse.If you are looking for a good energy drink I advise you to look elsewhere.  I do not recommend No Fear.

This drink is so "super energy" it's almost frightening.  Several members of my family tasted it and the consensus was that it might, indeed, give you a boost but the taste...some even compared it to grapefruit juice...was  definitely not good.

column9: Leaves an aftertaste I do not care for.
column10: My preferences for energy drinks is the regular and lo carb Monster. I do like Red Bull but you are paying for the name. This No Fear drink is infused with grape juice, which makes it to sweet for my taste buds. Of course it is loaded with HFCS. If you are a person that likes the juice energy drinks then you may like this drink.The energy drink had a bad aftertaste, which is the reason I would not recommend it to friends or family.I gave it three stars because it is still drinkable unlike Full Throttle.I did not get any kind of energy boost but that is because 1 can no longer does much for me. Have this after a large coffee and you will the buzz

column9: Too many calories and too strong a taste...
column10: I was looking forward to trying NO FEAR ENERGY DRINK because I definitely could benefit from a daily energy drink, and this one was recommended by a friend. But I found it much too strong, and grimaced after the first sip.As a person who loves to eat lemons whole, I've never avoided strong, fruity flavors, but NO FEAR ENERGY DRINK has a pronounced pineapple taste (with a touch of grapefruit and grape), and pineapple in particular has never appealed to me.I had to force myself to drink half a can, which I discovered later, is 130 calories. The entire 160 ounce can is 260 calories, containing a whopping 66 grams of sugar. That's considerably more calories than I use up in a workout.On a positive note, an 8 ounce serving does fulfill 100% of the daily requirement for vitamins C, B6 and B12, and 10% for folic acid, zinc and selenium. It also contains soy, and traces of sodium and potassium.Additional elements in the drink are difficult to determine from the can, as the print on it is not only small - it is too thick to be readable. I was able to find out however that the primary ingredients are high fructose corn syrup and carbonated water. It also contains l-carnitine, which has definite health benefits (I take it daily for hyperthyroidism), as well as grape seed extract, targine and argine. It appears to have few preservatives.I did not notice any difference in my energy level the hour after drinking it. But five minutes afterwards, I experienced a bout of frequent burping.Personally, I would not drink NO FEAR ENERGY drink again. But taste is subjective, and people who like the flavor and do not mind all the calories might enjoy it. My inclination, however, is to stick with my favorite drink, glaceau vitamin water zero (acai blueberry or mixed berry) which is delicious, nutritious and calorie- free, and leaves me feeling clear-headed and motivated.

column4: Wendi Barker "Wendi's Book Corner & What Wend...
column9: Great Taste in This 2 Servings Per Can of No Fear Energy Drink
column10: I really loved the taste of this energy drink, which has two servings per can.  It is 130 calories per serving, so an entire can will be 260 calories.It has a light, slightly fruity taste, which I really enjoyed.  After drinking other energy drinks, I've always experienced that kick in energy, but I did NOT get that with this one.  That said, I did feel good and didn't crash from it later.I will certainly get No Fear Super Energy again.

....even though this was in the fridge for me, my husband grabbed it before I could get to it!  This is typical of him, eating and drinking things I intended to consume; but here is what he had to say about it:  fruity, smooth, no weird after taste like many energy drinks contain.  Did not notice any caffeine buzz or "energy" but very good as a beverage.  Would he drink another? Sure, but probably would go for something else with less calories, less sugar, and more of a kick.I have to note that before I placed this in the fridge to chill, I noticed that the entire can contains no more caffeine than a large strong coffee.  The sugar content is high, and for those who want to spare themselves extra calories will not be impressed with that here, but my guess is the that this appeals to a crowd who doesn't (yet) have to worry about caloric intake.

The flavor if the No Fear energy drink is just fair not great. I personally would have preferred a sugar-free version. I dont drink a product with so much sugar in it. I did notice having a fair amount of energy after drinking this.

This energy drink has a pretty tasty berry flavor. Personally, while I love energy drinks, I don't generally drink the ones with sugar. My personal favorite is Monster Absolute Zero. This No Fear drink has about 66 grams of sugar in one 16 ounce can. I can't justify drinking that on anything approaching a regular basis no matter how much I like the taste. If I see a sugar-free No Fear, I will try it. For me, my choice will continue to be Monster Absolute Zero or diet Rockstar. If you don't mind the crazy amount of sugar and you like berry-flavored drinks, than this No Fear is a good choice.

This stuff is really good. I've never tried it so I've been drinking it in small doses at first. I really love the taste. It's a very berry fruit flavor, my favorite. It keeps my energy up without making me feel hyper and crazy or feeling like my heart is going to give out. This is a good drink, I completely recommend it.

Although the selection said Pack of 12 16 ounce cans, I only recieved one can, which is a bit misleading--but this was strictly for purposes of review and not a regular purchase. The product is good. I had to work an extra long shift and took this product about half way through when I felt myself flagging. Within a short time I was back up to speed and stayed that way through a very busy shift. The taste isn't spectacular, but not unpleasant either. I recommend this if you are going to be super busy and need that quick pick-me-up.

column9: Really, how many sugar, carb packed energy drinks does this world need
column10: 66g of sugar in the form of High Fructose Corn Syrup. 260 calories (in the form of sugar carbs). 174mg caffeine. A smattering of vitamins. Yes it will keep you awake. And yes you will inevitably crash from it. (I did.) It does taste better than red bull and about the same as Rock Star. But seriously, 2 of these day as some people reported seems to be putting you on track for health problems. And why in the world does an energy drink need a skull on the front? I downed my can before doing an MMA session. The guys in my class were not extra intimidated when they saw the skull. (Bummer.) I did not have any greater than usual work out ability. Time did not slow down. UFC fighters and BJJ black belts did not run away in fear.This really isnt a bad drink, I was just hoping for something different or better or healthier than EVERY OTHER energy drink out there. Instead it just seems to be trying to cash in on some sort of bad a$$ mystique. While pumping you full of carbonated water, HFC and citric acid. (Also contains Soy?!?)  I'm going to stick with black coffee, green tea, yerba mate, exercise and multivitamins for my caffeine, energy and supplement needs.

column9: A good taste frozen, but over 60g of sugar?
column10: I have tried a large variety of these drinks and taste-wise this one ranks up there with being good, but the ingredients and after effects just bring it way down.I tried this one frozen (slightly thawed) and it actually mushed well. The after taste was not bad and in this form the syrup did not get that bad feel in your mouth like some of these do. But the ingredient list is outrageous with so many bad things and the highest volume of sugar I have seen in one of these drinks (over 65g). The syrup is high fructose corn, and the preservatives and colors just make it worse.I know this drink is sought after as referenced in so many reviews here, but the sugar content and syrup definitely left a bad feeling in my stomach...will not be drinking it again. The cost is too high for this much bad stuff and I could feel it (in a bad way).

column4: Jason P. Pumphrey "the movie & music man"
column9: tastes terrible and made my heart jittery!
column10: Wow, this drink not only tastes terrible, it made my heart really jittery.I can handle caffiene good enough, but this stuff was just too much for me, I'll NEVER drink this stuff again!

column9: Big on sugar, low on ... everything else
column10: Go to any grocery store, gas station or nutrition shop, and you will no doubt be overwhelmed with the panoply of energy drinks on the shelves. There is clearly money to be made here, so every company under the sun has their own brand, replete with flashy packaging and a mad-scientist assortment of ingredients. No Fear Super Energy Supplement drink is just such a drink. The cool black can with the menacing skull and bold lettering are alluring, likely to attract many. Tread cautiously, dear energy drink consumers.The aforementioned flashy labeling atop the can highlights ingredients such as Taurine, Arginine and L-Carnitine, which are all great components of a good energy drink, but the quantity included in this beverage are so minimal that their impact is likely negligible. And caffeine? 85mg per serving. Slightly higher than a cup of green tea. Basically, every ingredient falls far short of being able to have any real impact -- other than the sugar. But, I'll let the nutritional panel speak for itself:Serving Size: 8 fl oz (240ml)Servings Per Container: 2Amount Per Serving:Calories: 130Total Carb.: 34g (11%)Sugars: 33gVitamin C: 60mg (100%)Vitamin B6: 2mg (100%)Folic Acid: 40mcg (10%)Vitamin B12: 6mcg (100%)Zinc: 1.5mcg (10%)Selenium: 7mcg (10%)Sodium: 100mg (4%)Potassium: 20mg (1%)Proprietary Blend: 1.35gTaurine: 1000mgInnositol: 100mgCaffeine: 87mgPanex ginseng Root Extract: 50mgGuarana (Paullinia Cupana) Seed Extract: 25mgGrape Seed Extract: 25mgL-Carnitine: 25mgL-Arginine: 10mgIngredients: Carbonated Water, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Citric Acid, Taurine, Grape Juice Concentrate (Color), Sodium Citrate, Natural Flavor (Contains Soy), Inositol, Ascorbic Acid, Caffeine, Caramel Color, Fruit Juice Concentrate (Color), Monopotassium Phosphate, Grape Seed Extract, L-Carnitine, L-Arginine Hydrochloride, Zinc Methionine Sulfate, Panax Ginseng Root Extract, Guarana (Paullina Cupana) Seed Extractive, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Potassium Sorbate, Selenium Complex with Amino Acids and Polypeptides, Folic Acid, Cyanocobalamin.Well, if that list isn't compelling enough to get you to rush out and slam a few of these, maybe the taste will! The flavor is something akin to a slightly un-ripened fruit blend, with a metallic, vitamin aftertaste. If you aren't yet drooling, then perhaps the energy rush will get your head swirling. Speaking of ... .For an "energy supplement," there was nary a buzz derived from this beverage.
