I experienced an ever-so-slight perk, likely due to the sugar content, rather than the blend of B-Vitamins, amino acids and caffeine, which was quickly followed by a large crash, again, likely due to the sugar (66g in the entire can, may I remind you!).Bottom line:  No Fear Super Energy drink is essentially nothing more than colored sugar (well, high fructose corn syrup, specifically) water. You're honestly better off drinking a good old 12 ounce can of Mountain Dew, which has better flavor, a bigger energy boost, lower caloric impact and cheaper cost. Fear the No Fear.

I really liked this energy drink. It had a great taste and a nice kick to it, that actually energized me. The only thing that I was disappointed about was that I only got one in the pack, and not 12...but that's okay, I'll just have to pick some up!

If you like No Fear, you will like this.  It has a refreshing citrus taste and is not over carbonated like some of the other energy drinks. You get more energy then from a soda, but not enough to make you feel jittery or have a big crash.  It's not as much energy as compared to a Red Bull.  It tastes like Mt.Dew, but not as sweet.

Of all the energy drinks out there this one if by far the best and my favorite. unlike other drinks it doesn't rely on being super sweet to give you energy and It actually tastes good. Just be careful not to drink it too fast lol its got quite a kick when it hits you. Great for all nighters and gamming.

Unfortunately No Fear Super Energy drink is longer being made because No Fear is out of business. However, this is still the best tasting energy drink ever produced. The taste is cherry-like, but like nothing else comes close to how smooth and delicious it really is. It beats all the other stuff on the market ... past or present.

For a few years now No Fear has been the best energy drink available. It has had the best results for me. The flavor is much better than any other energy drink i've tried. Some other products leave you looking to wash your mouth out after drinking, but not No Fear. It has been discontinued in my area and Amazon.com is the only place i can get it these days.
Typical energy drink with herbs and stuff that really don't work. Didn't like the taste.  Cool looking can is the only favorable thing I can say about it.

The  "No Fear super energy supplement" tastes like virtually identical to every generic Red Bull knock off energy drink I've tasted in the last two years. If you've ever ordered an energy drink from a television network website because it had the logo of your favorite TV show then you've drank something VERY similar to this. In fact, I wouldn't be surprised if the company that makes "No Fear" sells this exact beverage under different names to anyone who wants an "energy drink" with their company logo on it.The drink isn't bad, it's just boring and completely unoriginal. If your are a fan of energy drinks like I am then you won't find anything new here when you open a can of No Fear.

Taste: OK - fairly sweetAftertaste: BadEnergy Boost: Maybe a little? Certainly nothing worth the...Calories: Yikes! 260 in the can. Of course, the can is supposed to contain 2 servings, something that never seems to work well in this packaging (non-resealable aluminum can). For that matter, even 130 calories is more than I'd be happy with.Bottom line: Not for me. I think I'll just keep taking my B Complex vitamin with a cup of green tea when that desire for a nap hits me at around 2:00 pm.

I've never been a fan of energy drinks. I think they cause more problems than they solve. This one is no exception.While it does what it's supposed to do - amp you up for a half hour, followed by a debilitating crash - the flavor is absolutely objectionable. The drink goes down hard like cough medicine did when you were a kid. Picture your first swig of booze. You were expecting one thing, and well, you remember, right? Yeah, it's like that.I wouldn't recommend energy drinks to anyone, but if I did, I wouldn't recommend this one.

the color is somewhere between purple and brownthe taste? some citrus, a lot of sweetthe energy? didn't feel any after drinking a few sips, but then, after looking at the label and caffeine content...well, let's just say that i didn't finish this drink

column9: You'll have more energy than....the average housecat!
column10: NO FEAR, as energy supplements go, is okay. Based on one can, it seemed to provide enough caffeine to fuel my typical Saturday, although a busy workday would have been a better test. (Alas, the Vine program only provides one can, so I couldn't compare.)It has a nice, fruity flavor, with little aftertaste. The carbonation seemed a little weak, which gives it a sort of "watered-down" feel.Like other energy drinks, NO FEAR contains taurine, an essential amino acid for felines which they get from their carnivorous diets. (In cats, a deficiency can cause blindness.) As for its health benefits in humans, the jury is still out. I'm not convinced it has any particular benefit, except that listing it as an ingredient probably increases sales.I only mention that because NO FEAR and other emergy-drink products tout themselves as "health" drinks, but that's not necessarilly true. If you buy NO FEAR, do so because of its caffeine content. NO FEAR contains about 83 mgs of caffeine per 8 ounces, which is more than Pepsi Max (69 mg) but less than a typical cup of coffee (110 mg) or black tea. NO FEAR is certainly an option if you don't like the taste of coffee or you just prefer cold, fizzy drinks.But maybe an extra dose of taurine in the morning will hone your catlike reflexes and allow you to attack your day like a leopard taking down a gazelle!Right before your six-hour nap.

The first thing I do when Iam trying or thinking about trying a new product is look at the ingredients, at least I can do that in a store, where I can see the product up close.  Online you may get the general idea, which is open to interpretation.I've never had an energy drink before, or any energy product besides 5 hour energy.  With that, which I have only tried that once, was if I drank the whole bottle, tho it is small it may have given me energy, but I didn't feel very good, until it wore off.This product, No Fear, which I had to turn the can around to even see what it was called, it's a 16 ounce can, which is supposed to be 2 servings.  On the front of the can it says super energy supplement.I took a few sips.  It tastes like grapefruit, so the taste isn't bad.  It's kind of refreshing.Then I read the ingredients on the back of the can.  What I saw amazed me!!Calorie wise it's 130 calories, but what really surprised me is the amount of carbohydrates, it's 34 grams, but the sugar is 33 grams, and both of those are for ONE serving!I wonder if the real energy you are getting is because of all of the sugar that is in this product!The caffeine level is 87 mg's, so I don't know how much that computes to when you are considering the amount of caffeine, what differentiates a high caffeine level versus a low caffeine level.  I suspect that this drink is on the higher end of the spectrum as far as the caffeine level.I just wonder if the can shows it's for 2 servings, what if you don't want to drink the whole can at once, which is 16 ounces?  If you saved the other half of the can, just like soda, which first has fizz when you open the can, if you have some left over it won't have the fizz.Iam really not sure who would want to drink this product or why, but for me, just the amount of carbohydrates and sugars would make this a drink I could never consider drinking.At least for me, this is NOT a healthy drink!  Maybe if your main concern is having more energy it may not matter to you, but at what cost?I would be curious to see how someone would feel who had drank this whole can of No Fear.What they should fear is getting diabetes, especially if they drank this on a regular basis!
This stuff works.  It doesnt taste to bad and will keep you going.  It does not have the aftertaste some of the other drinks have.

Does it give energy? yes.Does it have more caffeine than Mt. Dew? Yes (83 v 54)Does it have substances of questionable value and safety? Yes (Arginine, L-carnitine, Taurine, Inositol, and several ingredients conveniently blurred to be difficult to read)Does it taste like crap? Yes (Unless you like carbonated grapefruit)Does it leave your fingers numb when it wears off? Yes (Seriously about 12 hours after drinking my fingers went numb and the room went spinning... talk about "hitting the wall" or "crashing.")Must be an energy drink... eat an apple (it's healthier and will keep you awake much better).

column9: WAY TOO SWEET AND TASTE TERRIBLE!
column10: I have tried many "energy drinks" and try to use them sparingly, but with everyone's overloaded schedules these days, it's easy to see why people buckle under for some "magic" pick me up sometimes. This particular drink is one of, if not the worst I've ever tried! It's so sweet that you will wince while swallowing this stuff. It also has a terrible taste(whatever flavor it is?)that will not leave you wanting more, but will leave a "I can't wait until it's over" sensation. If you want a good one that doesn't effect your stomach(like me, if I drink three cups of coffe, my stomach is wrenched!) try Celcius, it's very low carb and doesn't make you run out of gas. Like all of these drinks, it's easy to become addicted to them, use only when you just need a boost and not just because you like to ZING! ha-ha! ....Oh yeah and you all know the "magic" is caffeine... right? ;-b

column9: Nice energy boost, followed by a hard sugar crash
column10: The text on this can of No Fear Super Energy Supplement is very blurred, like the red ink doesn't line up with the rest of the print on the can, so I didn't try too hard to read it before I started drinking it.  I was a little more than halfway through the can when I realized that there are two servings per can--does anyone save half a can for later?  If you can figure out a way to do that it's probably a good idea, since each serving will give you 33 grams of sugar in the form of high fructose corn syrup.  I could have eaten a candy bar and come out ahead.All that sugar, plus 87 mg of caffeine (per serving) did give my skull wings, right before the sugar crash that followed.The flavor is far too sweet for my tastes, with kind of a weird fruit flavor.  It felt like the inside of my mouth was coated with syrup, like I'd been drinking cough syrup.  Come to think of it, this would probably make a great flavor for kids' cough syrup.It wouldn't work as a kids' drink, though.  The label warns: "Not recommended for children, pregnant women or people sensitive to caffeine."  Those who are allergic should know that it also contains soy.If you're looking for a sugar boost but couldn't possibly eat another bag of Skittles, this is for you.  If all you want is the "proprietary blend" containing taurine, inositol, caffeine, ginseng root extract, grape seed extract, l-carnitine, and l-arginine, you might want to check out the sugar free version.

column9: one should not consume anything that shares the universal logo for poison
column10: I thought this product was going to put me through the roof in a whirlwind of hyper activity. It did not. I didn't even get a boost of energy during or right after drinking it. I am not a caffine or energy drink user. I have 1 cup of coffee every morning and that is it so I figured this might really have an impact on me. It has not. It did not taste very good and made the corners of my mouth sticky. Also, one should not consume anything that shares the universal logo for poison.On the plus side it does have a very large can, so while it may not taste great, at least you get a lot of it.

My son, who is a medic in the United States Army, really enjoys his No Fear Energy Drinks. He has been a fan since his freshman year of college. As none of the store in our area sell this product, we have had to order it for him. He spent a year in Afghanistan and I had to send what I ordered or was lucky enough to find stocked in stores over 40 miles from where we live!

column4: Lonnie E. Holder "The Review's the Thing"
column9: Do We Really Need Another Energy Drink or Any Energy Drinks at All?
column10: I have drunk energy drinks in the past, though they were coffee flavored rather than fruit flavored.  They seemed to help wake me up in the morning and give me enough of an energy boost to help me kick off my day.  I usually substituted these drinks for breakfast, so the calories were not an issue.  I was unsure of what this energy drink would do for, or to me.Initially, I was unable to identify the flavor.  I kept sipping to try to figure it out.  The next thing I knew, the drink was gone.  It was about that time that I figured out the flavor was grapefruit.  Before I go on, be aware that there are less expensive ways of getting a grapefruit flavored drink.  For example, you could drink Ocean Spray's grapefruit drinks, which include several varieties.  Crystal Light also makes a grapefruit drink.  Lots of options exist that do not contain the caffeine of this energy supplement.  Of course, where is the fun in that?I drank the whole, 230-calorie can.  Of course, that is supposed to be two servings.  Did I feel more energetic?  Actually, no.  I felt a bit light-headed rather than energetic.  I even felt a little sleepy, perhaps because of all the calories.  All that caffeine also seemed to require a number of trips to the restroom, and my mouth felt dry.  I guess there is more evidence that caffeine is a diuretic.Do we really need yet another energy drink?  I wonder whether some of the "energy" effect is related to the belief that an energy drink will wake you up.  This drink did not seem to give me more energy.  Just the opposite, it made me feel tired.  The flavor was okay, but there are less expensive ways to drink a grapefruit flavored drink.  Maybe an easier way to get energy is to get plenty of rest and to get some exercise.  Something to consider.Good luck!

Seriously, the only thing you have to fear is the taste of No Fear. It was nasty. Further, after drinking it (with a funny look on my face the whole time), I didn't notice a whole lot of energy. Really, I did not enjoy this and did not get much a boost out of it. I'm a fan of energy drinks. I like them. I just didn't like this.

This was really good. I don't like soft drinks that are too sweet and my son (16) does.  My son really likes Monsters Monster Energy Drink, 16-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24); sweet, but sour. I prefer energy drinks more like Jamba Jamba Strawberry Banana, All Natural Energy Drink, 12 - 8.4 oz cans that is more fruit drink than soft drink. I am deducting a star because we were told by Amazon that we would get a pack of 12, but we only received one can. I didn't want to share. I really liked it and it didn't give me a headache.  I liked the aftertaste and my son, the know-it-all of energy drinks, said most had a juice in it.  Well, if I had known it was grapefruit, I probably would not have liked it simply because I have a bias against grapefruit.  But I tasted it first and I liked it. The Punk wants more!

column9: How about a nice Hawaiin Punch?
column10: No Fear tastes like Hawaiin Punch. Not impressed. I like Green Monster. That one tastes weird but I have a craving for it. Did I get a burst of energy? No. It didn't burst through my energy slump from 7 to 9 PM. Fell asleep watching TV. Again.I went online to find further information about this product. No Fear is a spin off of Sobe. Sobe name is derived from South Beach in Florida. They also make clothes. Skateboarding, surfing and Extreme Sports gear. Wetsuits. Their website focused on models for wetsuits. Couldn't get to the information on No Fear. There are actually websites/blogs that only feature reviews of energy drinks. I didn't look at them, to be perfectly Sinatra. Sobe was bought out by Pepsi in 2000. I am a Coca-Cola person. But whatever. I won't hold that against them. I heard that McDonald's bought out Chipottle. There was some truth to that, but more like both chains were owned by the same parent company.Coca Cola > PepsiStarbucks > McDonaldsPeets > StarbucksChipottle > Taco BellIn N Out > McDonaldsBut, you know. Sometimes you're in the mood for a McDouble or a McRib. This is starting to remind me of Samuel Jackson and John Travolta in Pulp Fiction. Segue to Jim Carey in Yes Man. Because there is a really funny scene involving Red Bull and Zooey Deschanel! Which brings us right back to--The Bottom Line is Green Monster > No Fear!PS: They said it was a pack of 12 cans for review but they only send you one. Cheapskates.

column9: I gave this to my 12 yr old to try
column10: He said he liked the taste of it, but it kept him up half the night.  I guess it did what it claimed then!  He has not asked for me to buy more though.

I drank this beverage during that part of the afternoon when my energy level desperately needs a boost. Only after consuming a third of this 16 oz. drink I felt more alert, energetic and a tad jittery. The drink is lightly carbonated, and fruity with a raspberry-like aftertaste. It's similar to Red Bull but the flavor is not as sharp and heavy, which kinda belies the intimidating skull, wings and dark décor of the can. `No Fear' contains 130 calories and if you're calorie conscious you don't need to drink the entire can for its effects to be felt.Like most energy drinks, this ought to be consumed if you're looking for a jolt of energy, not necessarily for the flavor. But it's tasty and it certainly wakes you up!

column9: Not bad...has some ups and downs
column10: The Bad: The taste is a version of 'grape,' that is more like bitter, low-class red wine. Tart in an unpleasant way.It comes in 16-oz cans, with "two servings" per can. Since it's carbonated, you either have to drink the whole can over an extended period, save it and hope it doesn't go flat, share it, or drink it fairly quickly like any normal soda - and get a lot of caffeine and sugar in a pretty short time. Drinks like this should come in smaller cans.The Good: It will perk you right up, which is the point.Doesn't give the jitters like some of these drinks tend to. I drank the full can - two servings - but it didn't make my heart palpitate or anything.I drink several cups of coffee a day, and occasionally drink energy drinks like this as well. Despite my caffeine intake, a caffeinated soda like Diet Coke will still keep me up at night. Notably, this drink did NOT keep me up.

column9: A Large Canned Energy Drink With a Good Taste
column10: I don't drink very many energy drinks. I've taken NODOZ on occasion and have had a few 5-hour energy drinks, and some caffeine candy, but that's about it. Therefore, I wasn't sure what to expect when I tried a can of NO FEAR SUPER ENERGY SUPPLEMENT. The drink tastes surprisingly good. It's not as sweet as a 5-hour energy drink, but NO FEAR doesn't have a bad taste. It tastes like a soda and reminded me slightly of Mountain Dew.I made sure to try my can of NO FEAR late in the afternoon after I had a long day. I felt tired and didn't have much energy and was thinking of taking a nap. The drink gave me a boost, but unlike 5-hour energy, the kick in my energy level didn't happen immediately. It was a gradual boost over about a 45-minute period. The tiredness didn't wear off until several hours later.I'm still not a fan of energy drinks and will continue to limit my consumption of them. However, in the future if I feel I need a pick-me-up, I'll look for a can of NO FEAR instead of just relying upon 5-hour energy boosters. If you're looking for an immediate boost, you'll want to drink something different, but if you're looking for a more gradual pick-me-up, you might want to try NO FEAR.

column4: Sir Charles Panther "Life is hard.  It's hard...
column9: Nice Scent and Taste, in Intimidatingly Heavy-Duty Packaging
column10: I'll admit this up front: I'm not an energy drink consumer.  I've never had a 5 Hour Energy, nor a Red Bull (even mixed in with something else), nor a Monster, etc.  This was my first-ever energy drink.Don't shake.  This is a carbonated beverage.Given my energy drink virginity and the can's color scheme and artwork, I expected something the color and consistency of an unholy mix of blood and motor oil, smelling of saddle leather and diesel exhaust, and tasting like fire and going down like acid.  I mean, really, black and red, with a scarred, angry skull?  Who exactly is the target demographic, resentful Goths and sociopaths?  Bikers?  Posers who want to look badass?  The product description here says it's the "toughest can on the shelf by far."  What does that mean, that the can is specially structurally reinforced, so that it's, like, hard to open?  Or am I supposed to somehow believe that I'm the toughest by far because I am able to keep it down?  Or does their "tough" mean they've packed this stuff with so much mega-engineered super-energy power that they're toying with the very elements of time and existence?  I'm having a hard time reconciling the product inside with the can and text outside.So, I was very pleased to find it was not what I expected.  Poured from the can, the beverage is light and flows as any water-based liquid, with no gloppy, syrupy viscosity.  The color is a clear reddish, with a tinge of pink, no cola-brown.  The scent is quite nice, distinctly fruity, with more than a hint of berry.And the taste.  Thankfully, it didn't taste like something packed with sugar and caffeine.  It didn't taste like a product that would come out of a black can with a winged skull on it.  The drink's appearance and taste match nicely, with the taste being distinctly fruity/berry, with a pleasant and light dry fruity aftertaste.  I thankfully did not get any of that funky industrial-artificial chemical flavoring taste.I opened the can and tasted it at first at a cool room temperature, and it was passable, not at all nasty like some drinks can get when they warm in the slightest.  It is much, much better over ice.  The carbonation is light, nothing compared to a Coke or Pepsi, and it fits the taste nicely.I ran it past a core consumer target, my 16-year-old daughter.  I did not tell her what it was, and she liked both the scent and taste.  She mentioned she tasted a little bit of peach.  She was surprised that it was an energy drink, and without prompting said it tasted unlike any energy drink she's ever had, better than both Red Bull and Monster.And the "nutrition" stats: 130 calories and 87mg of caffeine, 34g carbs, and with plenty of sodium and potassium, etc.  All this is interesting, until you see that this is for an 8-ounce serving; the can contains two servings, so double everything.  Also interesting is reading on the can: "Not recommended for children, pregnant women or people sensitive to caffeine," and, "This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease."  I'm not too sure what to make of these statements, but I know for a fact I've never read it on any of my beloved Diet Dr. Pepper.There is 2000mg of taurine, also known by its handy nickname 2-aminoethanesulfonic acid, in every can.  That's ten times the amount of anything else in the can, so I have to infer it's supposed to be a good thing.  The Interweb has a lot to say about taurine, essentially that it's naturally occurring and a needed thing for humans.  My quick survey has the usual daily intake at somewhere between 40 and 200, so this can is dropping a good ten times that on you.  I guess the logic is that a little is good so a lot is better, but that usually is not the case when it comes to the fine-tuning of body chemistry.  One source says, "the influence of high taurine doses on [crucial physiological] processes is uncertain."  Another source says, "...a 2003 study by the European Food Safety Authority found no adverse effects for up to 1,000mg of taurine per kilogram of body weight per day."  So, that means at 220 pounds you can slop up 100,000mg/day, 50 count `em 50 cans of this product.  So there you go, definitive ambiguity.As for super energy, I drank my pint of No Fear at about 4:30pm after a morning coaching high school rugby practice, then straight to marching in a St. Patrick's parade, then home to loading/unloading rugby gear, laundering jerseys, storing gear and supplies and parking a full trailer by hand.  After 30 minutes I did feel considerably more energetic, and had a slight headache.  Are the two related?  Maybe, but then again, maybe not.  No convulsions, no heart attack, no trembling hands, slurred speech, or eruptive bleeding from my eyes.Bottom line: After decades of drinking diet soda, this just isn't my kind of drink, and I'm unlikely to purchase it, if anything because of it caloric content.  That being said, I did like its taste, and don't have a problem recommending it to folks who like energy drinks.

The selling point for this energy drink over others is that it has a "brand new taste." I suppose if one wants something different from the taurine/B complex flavors of the Red Bull and Monster, then it definitely does taste different, and sweeter and fruitier. Others report grape juice flavor; I also think there's some watermelon flavor in there too. It certainly doesn't taste bad, and I don't detect any chemical or other aftertaste. I still do prefer my classic energy drinks, but I have no regrets about trying this one out.The bottom line is, if you need a kick and don't like Red Bull and Monster, and coffee's not your thing either, you might want to give No Fear a try.

This is a berry flavored beverage that actually tastes like a berry drink. Most of the energy drinks have a chemically after taste and the flavors are weak and don't mask it well. The new taste that the advertisements are talking about is backed up by reality in this case. I shared it (it is a big can) with some of my friends who drink a lot of energy drinks including Monster and No Fear and they were also surprised by the flavor. Good news: the can shows only 1 carb per serving and lists no sugars. Not sure about that, but it's better than some competitors that have the equivalent of a dozen donuts worth of sugar!A huge down side is that a can of this has about 260 calories, which makes it one of the higher calorie energy drinks out there.Also, the caffeine in this drink is appx 87 mg per serving (2x each can) which is lower than some of the other energy drinks. So if you are going for caffeine for energy this one wont work. Admittedly, they are going for supplement energy from Creatine, Guarana, L-Carnitine and Taurine and you really ought to know what works for you before you start buying cases of this stuff.Overall, a much better flavor which will likely become a favorite for energy drinkers.

column9: Unique Flavor That I Surprisingly Liked
column10: The No Fear energy drink, like almost every energy drink out there, does very little to decribe it's flavor.  I can say that this is somewhat grapefruit flavored, which I wasn't expecting.  The flavor though is smoother than actual grapefruit and gave the drink a nice refreshing taste.  I think most people would be surprised by this flavor & the pink color of the drink after seeing the black can with the skull logo.  The taste is odd at first but by the time I had a few drinks, I was enjoying it.As for the contents, the sugar & sodium levels are as expected.  But, the vitamin & supplement content was a little more diverese than most drinks.  I really felt that I got a good blend of extras - besides just caffeine, sugar, and vitamin B's.  This also contained Vitamin C, Zinc, Selenium, Potassium, Grape Seed extract, L-Carnite, L-Arginie, and more.  It did feel like a super energy drink, as the can promoted.For the same price, other drinks don't take this extra step.  Considering the extras & flavor, I was pleasantly surprised!

column9: Good flavor, but not the greatest ingredients
column10: THE CAN: The can itself says it's a "Super Energy, Supplement". Nothing about which flavor it is or is not. Sounds like they are trying to market to those that are addicted to 5 Hour Energy, Liquid Energy Berry, 2-Ounce (12 Pack) shots and the like.SMELL: Yes, I wanted to know how it smelled before I drank it. It completely smelled like I was about to drink a grapefruit drink. I'm personally okay with that but know others may not be too excited and wonder if it would have a bitter bite to it like grapefruit.TASTE: I was pleasantly surprised! Drinking the other brands there is always this "bite" that makes them sometimes hard to drink. This has the best flavor of them all!! And it did NOT taste like grapefruit, but sort of a fruit punch flavor.COST: Currently at $2.33 per can on Amazon (includes shipping), I guess the prices is average. But for about the same price I could get a grande house coffee with an extra shot of espresso from the overpriced Starbucks. I would still get a boost from Starbucks AND with less ingredients going into my body.INGREDIENTS: First three ingredients are: Water, High Fructose Corn Syrup, Citric Acid.Really? The cheapest and one of the worst product to put in your body is, HFCS.An easy Google search on the health dangers of HFCS will reveal that HFCS is related to health problems as weight gain, dental cavities, poor nutrition, and increased triglyceride levels, which can boost your heart attack risk. No thanks!The print on the can was very difficult to read, so I couldn't really tell you what other ingredients are in this thing. It does have an allergen warning of "Contains Soy".ENERGY BOOST: I'm use to having one(1) cup of coffee a day at that. So when I drank this I was wired within 15 minutes. It definitely had the boost!!OVERALL: Still nothing replaces healthy eating, exercise and a good night's rest for living a high energy life. But since we don't always get that, a supplement such as this drink does come in handy.It taste great and gives a good boost, but at the cost of damaging ingredients.

column9: Does the job, but doesn't stand out as better than other energy drinks
column10: "What's not to like about an energy drink that comes in a black can with a cracked skull with wings and the words "NO FEAR" emblazoned across the top, right? Well...It tastes sort of like carbonated strawberry or grape, a slight pucker-inducing dull fruity taste. Not bad, just not delicious. It's sort of par for the course when it comes to energy drinks. If you like Monster, Amp or Red Bull, this should be just fine. If you drink your coffee black, this will be a huge improvement unless you just love that mud-like taste.As far as energy, this has about the same effect on me as the Monster and Amp line of energy drinks: it gives me a subtle energy boost, and that's a good thing. Red Bull leaves me feeling wired and edgy and I don't want to waste the extra kick by sitting around vibrating, feeling restless and hating how my skin feels like it's crawling. The caffeine in a can of this is on the low end of an average cup of coffee, but it's also loaded up with taurine, l-carnitine and arginine, as well as things like vitamins B and C--things that seem to have some other potential health benefits other than just getting me through an afternoon energy slump (assuming there's enough of those things in there to be useful).Overall, I give this 3 stars. It does the job, doesn't taste unpleasant or leave a nasty after-taste, and falls within the price range I'm accustomed to with other similar energy drinks. It doesn't stand out as being better than other energy drinks I've tried, though, but would have earned an extra star if it tasted a bit better.

column4: Ursula K. Raphael "AstraDaemon of The Zombiep...
column10: Tasted great without any bad after taste; drank it in the afternoon, when I felt my most sluggish & it did give a boost without making me feel jittery.I was surprised to see this had soy in it!I liked this better than the "Rip It" energy drinks.

column9: All that sugar and no real boost for me.
column10: Not sure why I didn't get any real boost from this.  To me, it really isn't anything more than glorified Mountain Dew.  With 33g of sugar per serving (2 servings per can) and 130 calories each, it should at least give you enough energy to offset the calorie and sugar intake it provides.

column9: Kept me awake without the jitters
column10: I was surprised at the taste of the No Fear,Super Energy Supplement, 16-Ounce Can. It was nice and fruity, and didn't have that chemical almost-citrus taste that most energy drinks seem to have.Because I had evening plans, I drank the No Fear in the early afternoon. The can is two servings, but I did down the whole can.  It wasn't sugar-free, so I thought that the "rush" I'd get would be a sugar high, followed by a crash.  However, I drank the No Fear around 2pm, yawned a small bit through the afternoon, and stayed up a few hours past my usual bedtime. I slept well and had no problem waking up the following morning.I was pretty happy with the No Fear, and would get it again - probably even over another brand.

column9: Tastes good, not like a vitamin
column10: This energy drink tastes like fizzy grape juice.  Not fake grape soda, or that other energy drink "b vitamin" flavor, but balanced, grape-juice sweetened soda that goes down very easy.If you want an energy drink, that doesn't taste like one, and are ok with sugary sodas, you should try this.What it is:- Great tasting.  Grape juice-based soda with a nice purple color.  No vitamin flavors that I notice.- Not a diet drink.  Sweetened with plenty of sugar.- Caffeinated. About two strong cups of coffee worth (130 mg I believe) in a can.What it is not:- Not: a huge boost of B Vitamins.  B Vitamins work great, but they don't taste particularly good.  Think red bull flavor.- Not diet.  A whopping 66 g sugar in a can.  This is the same, per serving, as any other sugar-sweetened soda.  Tastes good.  Blood sugar spike.Overall:  A good product if this is what you want.  I personally try to avoid such sugary drinks, but for those that like them, this one tastes great.

No Fear Super Energy is mostly made up of high fructose corn syrup - it's the #2 item on the ingredient list after carbonated water. Each 16oz can contains 66 grams of sugar (and 260 calories)! Yes, there are some other ingredients which may increase your energy, but most of the energy will undoubtedly be due to the HFCS.Each can is said to contain 2 servings, but since it's a carbonated beverage, it's not really going to keep well. The flavor is like carbonated cherry cough medicine.

column9: Not bad.  Not bad at all.  In fact, pretty good.
column10: Let me preface this review by saying that I'm not a big "energy drink" person because I don't want to drink a lot of high fructose corn syrup, preferring instead a slimmer waistline.  That being said, I drank "No Fear" for an added pick-up that my usual dose of coffee wasn't providing due to a lack of sleep.  First of all, the drink was fizzy and tasty, with a hint of fruit, so it went down easily, unlike a few other energy drinks I've sampled.  Second, a half can (8 oz.) was about 128 calories, which wasn't objectionable.  Would buy it again if the need arose.

column4: Chris Swanson "I'm just this guy, you know?"
column9: Ok taste, no noticible energy boost
column10: Well, there's this. No Fear energy drink. It has a taste that's vaguely like fruit punch, which was ok. Not terribly great. But let's face it: you don't want this for the taste. You want the kidney-vibrating energy boost. Well, you might want to look elsewhere because I didn't notice one.Now it's not like I'm some energy drink drinker; far from it. This is the first one I've had in about a year or so. I do drink lots of Diet Coke, but that's about it, and frankly I get the same amount of "boost" from the caffeine in that as I did from this, plus it's a lot cheaper.So can I recommend this? Well, taste-wise it's ok, but I'm sure you can get the taste and the energy boost elsewhere for less money.

Granted, No Fear is better tasting than most of these types of energy drinks.  It's fruity like a popular canned punch and there is enough in this can to split between two adults.However, regular coffeehouse drinkers may be a little disappointed if they don't feel the same rush they get from an espresso shot, though this also contains a significant level of caffeine.  Also, to try to put it mildly: If coffee tends to "run through you," don't be surprised if this has a similar effect.Despite the impressive list of supplements, this is not a health drink, by any means. It cannot overcome the fact that High Fructose Corn Syrup (after carbonated water) is second on its list of ingredients- it's a GMO food additive that dehydrates the body, for starters.At 66 grams of sugar in one can, it's like drinking fruit flavored soda with vitamins added. This may seem effective short-term if you're mostly interested in a tasty energy boost and you prefer this type of method to obtain your sugar intake.Unfortunately, the nutritional supplements cannot counteract the other ingredients, especially if you need increased energy long-term.

column9: Have no fear super energy is here!!
column10: Surprisingly I had never tried No Fear energy drinks but when I got offered this product on the Amazon Vine newsletter I figured id give it a try. I'm so glad I did, I'm also happy to see it offered on Amazon.com. This drink is right up there with some of the best ive ever tasted. Great taste and no mentionable crash aftrrward the calories are reasonable for an energy drink however keep in mind it is 130 calories per serving and this bad boy contains two. It also has 34g of carbs 33g of sugar 1000mg of Taurine 87 Mg of caffeine 25 Mg of L-Carnitine and 10mg of L-Arginine. The price may seem high but its actually about the same as most others. For around $28.00 you get 12 16oz energy drinks it equals about $2.33 a piece so like I said not bad. I recommend this drink for anything from helping you wake up in the morning, to working out or even a mid day pick up but probably not if your trying to loose weight. This drink will for sure help you show No Fear!!!

I found ONE in the store this weekend after going without for MONTHS so I was so excited to think maybe it was brought back! I eagerly drove around to TEN different stores and gas stations looking for more... but nobody had it. All they have is the sugar free which is disgusting (sorry, but it is).So I thought maybe I'd find it on-line.... and was excited to see Amazon has it... but then sad to see it is discontinued.I'm begging Pepsico to bring it BACK!!!  This is the ONLY good tasting energy drink on the market.I get my house clean when I drink one of these!(and I'm a 49 year old lady... not any young teeny bopper).Update: THANK YOU AMAZON!  I am so excited that I could order it! I may have to get a couple more cases... Thanks again!

Sometimes it comes a little banged up, but I don't care! No beverage on the market tastes anything like it. Every thing is cherry this or orange that, this is No Fear and it tastes like No Fear!This is the best!

column9: All I have to say is Hell Yeah!!!!
column10: I have been searching the web for months looking to order No Fear with no luck at all! Amazon finally sells this stuff! I am clueless as to why in the world Pepsi would buy this product from Sobe and then discontinue it?!?!?!? It is without a doubt the best energy drink ever made! Doesn't taste like cough syrup or liquid candy like all the others and it doesn't make you bug out of your mind! The perfect taste with the perfect amount of energy!
