Amazon: We want No Fear back!!! Don't ever stop selling it! They say out of stock, could that mean the end of No Fear from amazon?? Everybody get together to get it back on Amazon!
This is by far the best drink ever produced. Please put them back on the shelves. Dont get no better.

Love me some Sobe No Fear! Unfortunately it's getting harder and harder to find. The taste is what sold me on it way back when I started drinking energy drinks at work. Sort of a sour fruit punch taste that isn't ridiculously sweet. Put it on ice and it's not bad with a meal either.

column9: No Fear here , go for it !
column10: No fear of funky chemical taste here.I find this is a great tasteing product, more juice like than any of the others I have tried.It doesn't get me too wired out and I can enjoy it with lunch as a boost for the afternoon.I used to be able to get it at alot of stores , but it seems Pepsi bought them and are more interested in pushing the "popular" drinks. I found it on Amazon and have been ordering it here since. If you do the 3-5 day shipping it's free, it's the most cost effective way to go.
i have tried several different energy drinks,and NO FEAR is by far my favorite! i have never been a coffee drinker, NO FEAR IS my morning coffee! AMAZON is THE PLACE!!!

No Fear is a superior taste, and clean energy. I've been hooked on it since 2006. It's getting extremely difficult to find, but luckily I was able to pick up a 12 pack from Amazon. They need to mass produce this stuff again, because its hands down the best energy drink available.

column9: Not bad for a big can energy drink
column10: I am a bit of an energy drink addict.  I got hooked on them when I lived in Japan, where "genki drinks" are ubiquitous and sold in little bottles containing a shot of vitamins to get you through the day.  Because of that, I prefer the 5-Hour Energy brand that gives you the energy shot without all the fluff and soda water.I have tried a few of these big can styles, like Monster and Rockstar. They usually taste foul and I find it difficult to finish off a whole can.  But, I am always up something new, so I gave this "No Fear Super Energy Supplement" a try. I was surprised that not only did it not taste bad, it actually tasted good!  This is the first of the big can style energy drinks that I would actually drink for the taste.  It tastes somewhat like a Cherry Cola, with a hint of that vitamin after taste.As far as the energy boost goes, I can't say that I really felt it.  Usually, after I drink a "5-Hour" drink I can feel the tiredness wiped away from my eyes and an actual physical effect.  With this "No Fear" drink, it was refreshing like any cold drink but I didn't get that sense of waking up.This one can contains two servings, so it is a lot of calories to pack in just to get a small energy boost.  That is one of the things I dislike about the big can energy drinks.  In the future, I will stick with the "5-Hour" energy boosters which give you all the goodness and vitamins without the excess of soda water.

column9: Remember When a Skull on the Label Meant DON'T Drink the Contents?
column10: Not anymore, apparently.  Offhand, the only other place I can remember seeing skulls on the labels of beverages is in the Rotgut Industry.  But this is hardly the first case of counter intuitive marketing in energy drinks: Monster Energy Drink cans have claw marks slashed through their label, Venom Energy Drink cans have a poisonous snake on their label, and Cocaine Energy Drink - As Strong As 3 Red Bulls and Zombie Blood Energy Potion Pack pretty much speak for themselves.(What next?  This Will Kill You brand energy drinks?)Which is a bit ironic since No Fear brand energy drinks could argue that they are a little bit more healthy (or a little bit less UNhealthy) than the average energy drink because they contain grape juice concentrate.  How much is unclear, but from the label we can know that there is less grape juice concentrate than the taurine (1000mg) but more than the inositol (100mg).  Oh, it is hardly what I would call genuine "Soda Juice": IZZE Fortified Sparkling Juice, essn Sparkling Juice, or The Switch Carbonated Juice, but this probably explains the different and IMHO surprisingly good taste.Note: Also available in No Fear, Sugar Free, 16-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12).

I live in Minnesota and love the NO FEAR ENERGY DRINK. I would drink 1 sometimes 2 a day they have a great taste and I did not crash from them. Sometime ago they stopped selling them around here for an unknown reason but through some searching found them on sale on Amazon. I just ordered my first order and received them yesterday AWSOME. I hope some day they bring them back in stores around here.

column9: Buy it for taste above performance
column10: It's always a bit of a gamble with an unfamiliar energy drink - generally I worry that it taste bad and/or give me the shakes. Thankfully the hefty-sized "No Fear" 16-ounce can that I was sent through Amazon Vine had neither. In fact the taste was remarkably nice; kind of like a sweeter redbull and I had no searing chemical after-taste at all. I actually enjoyed the drink from the first opening to the last drop and felt great afterwards.I then went onto to do my very simple workout routine consisting of a couple of miles on the treadmill and some free weights and had no issues, but in all honesty I didn't feel anymore energized or hydrated than normal. One can (which was all that was supplied) and a single workout may not be a sufficient amount of data to be able to say for sure how radical this energy drink could impact my daily exercise regimen though. The ingredients listed consists of the normal fair for this kind of product with taurine being the usual suspect. At 260 cals a can I thought that acceptable given the size of the can too.I felt fine and enjoyed the workout for what it was and felt the drink was nice enough to purchase a full pack of 12 cans. At around fifty cents a can this is very good value for money too, especially given the giant size of the cans.

I will admit to some slight apprehension the first time I popped open a can of NO FEAR and cautiously took my first sip. Perhaps it was the intimidating black finish and winged skull trimmed in red and silver. Anyway, it was good! Not as sweet as I had worried it would b. It has a mild Apple-Pear, fruit punch flavor followed by slight bite at the back of the throat. No real off flavors or hints of the supplemental ingredients within. No tingly rush followed by heart palpitations either, thank goodness.NO FEAR does contain sugar -- 33g in each of its two 8 oz. servings. By comparison Coca-Cola Classic has about 26 per 8 oz. serving, Mountain Dew has 31. So this is not an energy drink for those looking to avoid sugar, try 5-hour Energy for that. High Fructose Corn Syrup is the most abundant ingredient after carbonated water. NO FEAR contains a number of vitamins and minerals in addition to its proprietary blend of energy promoting ingredients, but I suspect that they are so over-processed that their health value is questionable.I do like the flavor though, and it did give me an energy boost and kept me alert and clear while working at my desk for a few hours. Perhaps if I had chugged both servings at once the effects would be more noticeable. On a side note, it also makes a decent mixer in adult beverages, a la Red Bull. I don't think I'll be getting it again though. The ingredient soup is just a little too scary. Its not for me, but I can see others enjoying it. 4 stars for flavor and energy enhancement, 2 stars for health value. I've yet to try the sugar-free version so cannot comment about that.~ Kort

column9: Unable to finish the can, Highly artificial, Medicinal flavor
column10: I work long hours. Coffee and soda don't agree with me, so I'm always on the lookout for alternative sources of energy. No Fear Energy Drink may work very well--if you can stomach the flavor. It tastes like cherry medicine. If this is what I have to drink to keep up the pace after 10-12 hours, I'd rather stay sluggish. Better to stick with Red Bull or another variety carbonated energy drink.

column9: No Fear Energy Drink. Why did they take the fear away?
column10: I can only be happy that Aamazon.com is out there to bring what they have taken from us. Of all the Energy drinks out there, No fear is the top of the line for taste. If one wants a variation of taste, No fear is there.Why this product was taken off the market is totally beyond belief. How many really good products come along, Only to get the axe? No Fear, No Fear, No Fear, Oh how I wish it would come back.!!!!!!!!!!

I love sobe No Fear, and was lucky enough to find these at a local store the other day in 12 packs, needless to say I stocked up. It might be worth mentioning that these are not sobe they are now canned by a different company but I could not tell a difference in taste. Hopefully they will come out soon to order online, until then I will enjoy my find.[...]This is the site listed on the can, Sobe had their logo above the No Fear logo when they were bottling it.

I don't usually like "energy supplements" because most of them have me vibrating like a tuning fork. No Fear definitely delivers on the energy portion of the program, but not in such a huge burst I felt as if I was going to have a heart-attack if I stood up too fast. The taste? Well, it has one. It's sort of citrus between lemon and grapefruit. While I likely am not the target audience, I could see reaching for a cold one of these on a day when I need a boost instead of coffee.

That was pretty much the consensus at our house. It was a bit too sweet and did not have enough carbonation. For the amount of calories that are in this can I would expect it to taste amazing but it did not.

column9: A great drink for those who don't like sour
column10: This is my favorite energy drink. I was sad when they stopped making Adrenaline Rush, but happy to see it was basically just renamed and repackaged in No Fear.It doesn't have that sour/tart taste that I think other energy drinks have. For me, they taste like cough syrup- especially if you don't finish the can before it's no longer cold. This drink stays sweet without coating your mouth.They don't sell it anywhere in the area I recently moved to and I was bummed. I purchased pretty much every energy drink the stores carried, hoping to find something similar or that would work and there just wasn't anything like No Fear. Thankfully, Amazon has saved my mornings.

I've drank No Fear since it's creation. I'm VERY sad to see it go, and have only recently noticed the distributors locally seize to carry it. It had great flavor, and a sufficient energy kick. It wasn't that bad for you compared to Monster products. It's sad to see it go.

No Fear Super Energy Supplement 16 ounce cans are 260 calories, with a great tropical taste with no bad aftertaste.  It's low in carbonation, not over-carbonated like some sodas...it didn't cause jitters or provide the `instant up' energy drink feeling, but it did seem to make focus a little easier and accomplishing daily tasks.  Not a big fan of the tropical taste personally, but at a reasonable price and with the need for an energy drink, this one would do the trick - would recommend to others to try, especially if they like tropical flavors and want a good energy drink!
This energy drink is the best . It's the only one that j will drink. Thanks to amazon I can have my daily can. Amazon is the only place I can find it thank you amazon.

Ordered this for my oldest son who is 21 an drinks Monster or Red Bull. His comments were that the taste of this was awful, and although he did feel an increased level of energy, he'd never buy this but would stick with Monster or Red Bull. I think that about sums it up - if a drink doesn't taste good to you, you're not going to buy it.

The actual product is flavorful and goes down "easy"; on a like-for-like basis, I would probably rate this as the best energy drink I have tried (versus the usual suspects ... Monster, etc).  However, I am basing this assumption on my experience of drinking a flat product.  The can was damaged and bloated on top; the shipping box was completely undamaged.  So I wouldn't hesistate recommending trying out the drink from your local convenience store, but I would be wary of online orders based on my experience (who knows, probably is an isolated incident, but could be a packaging issue related to the new product).  Give it a shot!

Down here in Houston, Texas, No Fear was sold too, up until a few years ago.  I don't know the reason, and from I've read, it stopped selling in other parts of the U.S. too.  Anyways, thank God I found it here in Amazon, which is amazing.  I ordered several cases of them, enough for the rest of the year.  The taste is good, since I never liked Monster nor any other one, except maybe Red Bull.  The shipping was FAST!  This drink can be used to mix it up with vodka: makes a hell of a drink.  Highly recommend it!
I did not care for the taste of this product at all -- I was expecting something similar to Red Bull.  The taste of this was just kind of funky to me...

column9: The best and most Hard to find Drink on the market.
column10: This is by far the greatest energy drink ever made. Perfect balance between flavor, energy boost and price. 16oz for only 2.33/can USD is fantastic. I can't find it in my area anymore and if I'd go out of my way to buy it online, you know it is worth it.

column9: Great flavor for an energy drink
column10: I give this 4 instead of 5 stars because there are some other energy drinks out there that deliver the energy better than this. This is not a complete let down and the flavor is pretty good considering, but there are still other drinks more *stimulating*

When energy drinks first hit the market, Red Bull dominated. I tried it then and occasionally try it again. As a Kid I had better tasting cough medicine, which was foul! My son said he'd found a better drink and handed me a can of No Fear. Well, I didn't spit it out, as I have the panther p*** called Red Bull.Later I tried it over ice. Not only was it better, it was good! I still don't fully enjoy it out of the can, but over ice, it is a superior flavor. If I can get it, I prefer it to Pepsi or Coke and NO other energy drink is worth drinking, in my book. It has gotten VERY difficult to find in CA. But, here on Amazon, I can order it at a price, including shipping, that equals the price in the store (when I can find a store that still carries it).

column4: Marshall Carter "Ornery Gamer, Fiend Club Member"
column9: Nice energy boost, but tons of the sweet stuff.
column10: No Fear has never been my favorite energy drink, but I'd go to it from time to time because it delivered the energy, thanks largely to the over 180mg of caffeine per can (2 servings...yeah...right). No Fear disappeared and is harder to find now, but here it is, brought by a different bottler and with a different can design, but tasting very much like No Fear always has (despite the claim that it's brand new). I was never a fan of the taste (kind of a tropical fruit, mango taste), as it just seemed cloying and syrupy (not surprising with the amount of sugar in this), but there's no denying the energy boost it gives. Since there's no accounting for taste, take that with a grain of salt (most people seem to prefer the taste over Red Bull). If you're looking for an energy drink that delivers, you can do worse.

This energy doesn't excel in any area compared to other energy drinks, and the promised "new taste" wasn't all that exciting, but it wasn't unpleasant, either. It gives a good boost to your energy levels for a few hours.All in all, this is a drink to add to the long list of new drinks on the market, and I'd buy it if there was a good deal on it.

column9: Didn't care for the taste, but the energy was okay
column10: The No Fear energy drink has a mango flavor.  I wasn't a fan of it, and would definitely prefer Monster or Amp as far as taste goes.  I drank the can I received one morning to give me some energy, and it did the job.  Sometimes I drink energy drinks for the flavor, but I would definitely not do so with this product -- I decided not to finish the can because it did not appeal to me at all.  I would choose a different, better tasting brand over this, if I had the choice in the future.

column9: Taste was pretty good, oomph was YES!!
column10: While I wasn't super crazy about the taste of the No Fear super energy drink ~ to me, it kind of tasted like medicine ~ I loved the boost it gave me almost instantly!  And it lasted for several hours ~ so YES, this was a definent go to for me when I need a quick energy boost!!

column9: Not my favorite, but it has its good points
column10: I didn't particularly care for this energy drink - the taste was almost cough syrupy (HOWEVER, I will say that a lot of the energy drinks taste like that to me)The energy boost was ok, I did feel more awake and energized. Also, I didn't notice a big "letdown" like some of the drinks have.So all-in-all, No Fear is a good drink - just not my favorite. My son, however, loves this brand.

column9: it's alright, but I prefer Monster
column10: I prefer the taste of Monster over this.  Amazon only sent me one can to try so I didn't exactly acquire the taste of this.

column4: Adam Ellis "I Believe In A Better Way..."
column10: I drink energy drinks fairly regularly, so I'm familiar with the particular flavors associated with them, and it's common for a citrus flavor to be added to offset the taste of some of the ingredients.  On this product, they appear to have decided to try a grapefruit flavor.  It was not a good decision.

I shared this with my fellow programmer across the hall. We both liked the taste and were surprised how good it was. We both also noted that we didn't feel any boost or increase in energy after we drank it. I always feel a good boost with 5 Hour Energy, Monster, Red Bull, and RockStar, but nothing with this one. It does have great taste. Maybe you could drink two or three and get a boost that way. I don't think I liked it enough to try that.

column9: Not the best taste and left me jittery
column10: Over the years I've probably tried almost every energy drink (and energy shot) out there at least once, from Monster to Venom to Rockstar to the ubiquitous Red Bull along with a bevy of "natural" energy drinks (FRS, Genesis Pure, etc.). This No Fear drink looks a lot more "hardcore" than the other ones, with a mostly black can dominated by a winged skull. On the inside, though the ingredients are mostly the same. The flavor is also similar - slightly fruity with a hint of carbonation and an aftertaste of vitamins. But I have to say this one falls pretty low on the taste scale for me. It also has a pretty powerful smell that I didn't care for. But taste alone doesn't kill an energy drink as long as it works. Unfortunately this one didn't give me energy as much as it just made me feel jittery and a little antsy. And 30 minutes after drinking it I got a headache. It's not the worst energy drink I've tried but it's definitely not one I look forward to trying again.
The flavor of the No Fear, Super Energy drink was good and it gave me a lot of energy.  Great for an afternoon pick me up.  I got my housework done in record time.  Whoot!

This energy drink is very different from the norm. It actually tastes like something you can identify, in my opinion a cross between orange and grapefruit juices. As with all energy drinks it has the requisite amount of caffeine and taurine for the energy boost we all enjoy. With the Amazon price at about the same as a case of Monsters from my local supermarket, I'll be ordering a case or two of this from Amazon.

I tried out the "NO FEAR SUPER ENERGY SUPPLEMENT" on a 7 hour road trip recently.  I think it helped to keep me focused which, for me is HUGE because I am sleepy when I drive.  So, for that I think it worked great.  Tastes a little fruit punchy to me.  Try it if you are looking for  energy and clear thinking.  I'll definitely buy it again.

I can confidently say that this drink works quite well. I drank a can at around 10:00 at night, and it kept me up until 2:30 am. The flavor is pretty good, though not that unusual from most energy drinks I've had.

column9: What Flavor is this supposed to be?
column10: After my first few gulps I thought it tasted decent.  However, after half a can it started to take on a strange and somewhat unpleasant taste.  I still couldn't tell you what the flavor was.  Some sort of "fruit punch".  It does do what it says it is supposed to do which is give you an energy pick up.  I have tried a bunch of different energy drinks from various companies and they are all pretty similar.  Lots of caffeine, Vit B, guarana, and similar ingredients.  There effectiveness depends on individuals' resistance to these stimulants.  I drink several cups of coffee and/or energy drinks a day so the effects are there but minimal compared to my wife who is smaller and will only have an occasional cup of tea or coffee.  She drinks one of these and is bouncing off the walls.  For me it comes down to taste and I am not a fan of this flavor.  I would also choose a no- or low-calories version.

column9: Not the biggest boost, but tastes great
column10: I have to get to work pretty early, so I need something to get me started. I'm not crazy about coffee, so I've been trying to find an energy drink that agrees with me. This brand is the first I've found that both wakes me up and doesn't have that off-putting chemical aftertaste. It doesn't give me as much energy as some of the other brands I've tried, but it tastes better. It's a nice compromise between flavor and kick. However, if you're looking for a more powerful boost, look at some other brands -- but they'll probably taste worse than this.

column9: At just over two bucks per can of tasty energy boost, this is a good buy if you're an energy drink fan!
column10: I'm not one that, honestly, drinks a slew of energy drinks on a regular basis. I've had a few Five Hour Energy shots during my six hour drives up the East Coast, and now I've tried No Fear's Super Energy Supplement on the same long drive... Outside of that, I am a fan of Red Bull, but only when it's been paired with a favorite 56 herb and spice alcoholic digestif... Outside of those few uses, I typically stick to coffee for my energy jolt, but if I was in the market for something similar to, but not as cloyingly sweet as, fruit punch with a kick, I'd go with this product.The No Fear Super Energy Supplement has a sweet, fruity flavor to it with a bit of a tart and tangy bite. The fruit flavor is also not overpowering, and is different from most of the other standard fruit punch flavored drinks you're likely to come across. It has a hint of passionfruit taste to it, with a little bit of a citrus undertone. The energy boost that I felt while sipping it on my drive also didn't particularly surge, but was more of a subtle feeling of waking up, without any caffeine overload or shakiness that I could detect. And, with a can this large, you can sip on this throughout your day, as long as you have a way of keeping the can cold enough to suit your tastes.Red Bull might do a great job of giving you a much-needed energy boost, but I have to say that I always felt it tasted like medicine. No Fear's energy supplement drink has a pleasant taste that isn't too sweet, and it's more cost-effective for the quantity you're getting than Red Bull is. As for Five Hour Energy, that stuff was NOT pleasant to drink, so I just shot it, and gulped it all at once, trying to avoid as much contact with my taste buds as possible. Given a choice, No Fear's energy drink wins my vote, for price-point, flavor, and effectiveness.Good stuff!

Most energy drinks I have tried are not very good taste wise, but this No Fear drink tastes great. The energy that it provides is on par with other name brand energy drinks like Monster or Rock star. For those out there who love these drinks, you should give it a try, best tasting one yet.

The vast majority of my rating for this one comes down to taste. It's a carbonated drink that tastes a bit like a fruity soda, but the sweetness is a little smoother and nicer than soda typically is.The big drawback here is that a 16-ounce can contains 260 calories of sugar. After some thought about how I wanted to consume this once I realized how much sugar was involved, I saved it for a day when I knew I'd be walking for several hours so that I could just drink it when I knew my body had plenty of use for the sugar. I wouldn't recommend it as a drink to have sitting down at a desk or something like that, because that's a lot of sugar to be consuming if you're not doing anything at that moment to burn through it. The company does make a sugar free version No Fear, Sugar Free, 16-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12), though I haven't tasted that, so that's an option to try for those times when you want an energy drink but you won't be moving around much.

NO FEARENERGY DRINKI have tasted many an energy drink in my day and while some have tasted good at least none have worked for me. For some reason these so drinks do not keep me up or give me that boost or whatever. Still that doesn't mean that I can't enjoy the taste of said products. When it comes to this one it is a bit sweet but overall it tastes pretty good. It is the usual 16 oz can full of energy and taste for most people. I would recommend this to people that are fans of energy drinks.

As far as energy drinks go, this one has a flavor I enjoyed. Most energy drinks taste awful but this one has a nice flavor without the chemical, vitamin taste that some energy drinks have. I usually avoid energy drinks for this very reason but this one I would drink again.The drink also gave me a boost to get my day going. I was very tired the day I drank this and it helped me to get the day going. It kept me going for quite awhile until the early afternoon. I would say it did it's job!The two drawbacks to the energy drink are the price and also the amount of calories in the can. The can contains two servings but I don't know many people who drink half of a can. That brings the calories in the can to a total of 260, 130 if you drink half of a can or one serving. That is quite a bit if you count calories. The price is a bit much for my budget. I would be more inclined to keep this on hand if the price were lower.The bottom line-the flavor is good, the drink gives you energy at a high cost of calories and cash.

The NO FEAR 16oz Super Energy Supplement tastes great, with no aftertaste, and definitely gives an energy boost. I drink of lot of coke, but definitely felt different after guzzling this beverage on a Saturday morning. It carried me through my brisk morning run, and kept me going while I played with the kids and did yard work.Bottom line, this drink works, and if energy drinks are your thing, definitely worth the money.

Of all the energy drinks i've had this ranks as about average. I for one didn't like the flavor of this one. Which made it a bit difficult to finish. I still think Monster makes one of the best tasting energy drinks i've had so far.

column9: Dorky name but taste is better than most
column10: I've been an avid red bull drinker for a few years, but no more than 1 every few days.  Drank it a lot during finals.  Had monster, rock star ect but those are a lot more sugar.If you don't mind the 260 calories per can and the super dose of caffeine, it's pretty much the same as the others but the taste is more of a refreshing grape.  It's definitely more drinkable than the others but as the name implies, it takes all of it to an extreme, sugar, caffeine ect.  My gf and I split the can and liked it and will most likely buy it if we feel the need like a road trip or whatnot.

I really like the concept of energy drinks--chug some ounces and get a boost of stamina to continue the day (or night). Most of them offend my taste buds! Absolutely cannot stand the taste of a few of the better known energy drinks.  The taste of No Fear,Super Energy Supplement, 16-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12) was great, not even sure how to describe it. More of a juice taste than a fake alcohol taste like a few I've tried.While the drink has a great taste and there is more of it than many energy boosters, I can't say I saw a huge difference in my energy levels. I spent last week looking after three kids under six and could really have used a shot of energy, but didn't see any difference (unless my levels were so depleted that only a good night's sleep would have sufficed to raise them again) in energy, stamina, or being less tired.The can has two servings at 130 calories per serving or 260 per can so unless you stay active, you'll probably pack the pounds on if you guzzle this in place of something else!So to sum it up--great taste, not so great on the energy levels!

I have a slight fear of energy drinks ... I tend to not like the taste and the effects on my workouts are often questionable.On the first fear, this one has you covered. I truly liked the taste, and will be buying more. The taste is light, refreshing, and with absolutely no chemical taste as some others have. Even without the energy boost, I'd drink this. (pardon the pun, but as to taste, there is "no fear.")Energy? "no fear" there either. This does give a slight lift ... as good as other energy drinks I have tried, without any noticed drawbacks. Just watch the calories, as you should do with any similar drink.

column9: Unusual flavor with a pretty good boost!
column10: I've tried a few of the energy drinks. Some are pretty good, some are Yuk! Some worked while a lot didn't. Now this one, it works. It gave me a good kick in the backside to get me going and tasted pretty good too. It did have an unusual flavor that I can't really describe, other than to say it was something different and I liked it. I only had one can of it to try and its kinda hard to be more specific from just that. I've looked for it in the stores around here where I live in Colorado but haven't found any yet. At $28 for a 12 pack, that's really high for me and way out of my price range. There's several energy drinks out on the market now and a lot of them are priced far below these. If they bring the price down then I'd think about buying some more to try out.  Over all, this one gave me a good lift to get me going. It did give me a small dose of the jitters and my hands a minor case of the shakes for a little while at first. Or as some people would say, a slight case of the tremors. But that calmed down after a little while and I got a lot more done around here than I usually do. I suppose that jittery feeling and shaking hands, or tremors, would go away if you used this regularly and got used to it. I don't have any problem with recommending this No Fear, Super Energy Supplement. Except for people that have High Blood Pressure. This could cause your Blood Pressure to go up from a little to a lot. So be sure to check it a few times when you first use this or any other stimulant.

column9: It doesn't taste as awful as other energy drinks.
column10: I don't regularly drink energy drinks but occasionally on the weekends when I don't want to fall asleep at eight o'clock I'll try one.  This No Fear energy drink didn't taste as bad as some of the ones I've tried and it did actually give me energy so I guess it worked.  I still didn't think it tasted great and it left me feeling a bit jittery and wired.  I also get tired of the large amount of liquid I have to consume and much prefer the smaller quantity of a five hour energy supplement.  This isn't terrible in a must have situation but it isn't the first thing I would grab if given other options.

column9: Offers a different taste than other energy drinks
column10: I'm a good ol' fashioned Red Bull or Monster type with my energy drinks, so I decided to give this one a try through Amazon's Vine Voice program.TASTE:It took me a few sips to get used to the taste - it tasted like grapefruit, but it wasn't overpoweringly bitter...there was just enough of the additional ingredients to take off the edge. There was also no metallic aftertaste, which I've come to expect from energy drinks.SUPPLEMENT FACTS:This is a 2-serving 16 ounce can, so by drinking the whole can, we're getting 260 calories, 200mg of sodium and 66g of sugars.For comparison, a 2-serving 16 ounce Monster Energy drink is 200 calories, 360 mg of sodium and 54g of sugars.ANY EXTRA ENERGY?I passed on my morning coffee to try out this drink and it did make me more alert for about 2 hours, about the same as 2 cups of coffee usually do for me. I didn't feel any kind of crash later on from drinking this.WEBSITE INFORMATION?The address on the No Fear can took me to the No Fear website which offered information on their clothing line, but nothing about the drink itself.To compare, the website listed on the Monster Energy can provided ingredient listings for each of their energy drinks.WHAT'S MY VERDICT?While I did enjoy this drink because of its unique taste, the high calories and high sugar count will probably keep me from buying more.When I crave an energy drink, I usually go for Monster Lo-carb Energy because it gives me the pep I want, but only has 20 calories per can.

column9: I said 2, he said 4 - average of 3
column10: I'm not a fan of energy drinks but I thought I would give this a try.  We only received one can to sample and review so I took the first sip and passed it on to my man who promptly drained the rest of it.  I didn't care for the taste, but that is what has always been an energy drink turnoff to me - I can't even choke down a red bull.  My man, however, thought it was quite good.  The unfortunate part was that he chugged it about 8pm and was up until about 3am.  At about that time he was out cold until about 5pm the next day.So if you like energy drinks - this is apparently a high power drink with low calories so those of you who are attempting to lose weight - this won't break the caloric bank. It can't hurt to give it a try, though availability may be an issue as they haven't shown up on the market shelves around here yet.

I needed to mow my lawn but was exhausted from work this week, a perfect time to try this No Fear Energy drink. I only drank half before and then half in between, but I definitely felt a boost. The flavor is Fruit Punch with an emphasis on Berry flavor. It is more tart than sweet but far better than some other energy drinks. I only had a single can to test, so I cannot say if the effects and flavor is constant between cans, but I would definitely consider buying more to find out.

Normally, I do not care for the taste of energy drinks. Their gruesome typical taste, along with the shakes or sugar crash they normally give me, are just two of the reasons I avoid energy drinks. I do have a teenage son who loves them, however. When I had the opportunity to try the No Fear product, I thought he and I could both see how we liked it.When it arrived I chilled it first, and then tentatively took a sip of it. Usually I get an immediate reaction of distaste to energy drinks, but I have to admit that I liked this one. I took half the can and put it over ice and it was good enough that I would buy this and drink it as a refreshing beverage.  The teen liked it too. We were both pretty surprised that this didn't have the usual shudderific energy drink taste!The only thing neither of us noticed however, was any increase in energy. No thermogenic effect, or increased heart rate or anything of the sort. As a drink though, we enjoyed it.

This seems like a cross between a regular soda and an energy drink.  Some of energy drinks do taste awful.  The "No Fear" drink taste a lot better but still have the taste of the Taurine type of drinks.  You cannot really compare this with Red Bull or 5-Hour as it is more like in the same league as "Monster".I don't find a lot of difference with other products.  Because of the volume, this caters to those who want to also quench their thirst and not only for the energy boost.  In terms of energy boost, I find a bottle of Gatorade just as good.

I think what is missing is the "pumpkin" flavor.  With this in mind, if I read the flavor name again, it is "Pumpkin Spice" not "Pumpkin AND Spice".  This is a lot of money to just pour down the drain.  I intend to do some experiments using pumpkin to see what I can yield.  Someone who has used this before MUST have a good recipe to share....  If I find anything, I will post it.As for the starbucks pumpkin spice latte, they use a "Sauce".  The ingredients of which are unknown.The closest recipe I have found (per the claim of the recipe, anyways), is this: [...]It appears that there is much effort to duplicate this seasonal Starbucks favorite, as any modest internet search will reveal.  Each recipe seems to be wildly different, several claim to be the exact copy of the Starbucks version of this seasonal favorite.  The recipe above actually calls for this Torani pumpkin spice syrup.  However, I am not sure that the author of the recipe actually tried the syrup themselves.  My first attempt was to follow the recipe exactly, using 2 shots of espresso.  WAYYYYYY too sweet. Several reviewers of this recipe do point out the fact that following the recipe would cost nearly as much as the starbucks version with questionable results.I have experimented with several different variations of the recipe and achieved something that is at least drinkable by using:2 Shots espresso (I use Lavazza Crema e Aroma, found on Amazon in 2.2lb bags)2 pumps vanilla (I substituted vanilla syrup for vanilla extract as called for in the recipe)3 pumps pumpkin spice syrupcopious amounts of powdered pumpkin pie spice (To taste)Frothed milk (heated to ~180deg F)Combine all ingredients to fill a 20 oz cup.  Used frothed milk as a topping or whipped cream.This is the "Drinkable" combination I have found.  The "pumpkin" flavor still seems to be missing, and it certainly isn't close to Starbucks.I hope to find the time to create my own "sauce" using the torani syrup, vanilla syrup (from starbucks), pumpkin pie spice (powdered), canned pumpkin puree.  The recipe posted above also states to use canned pumpkin.  My fear is that I will end up gulping down chunks of pumpkin puree :p - I don't see how the pumpkin puree will dissolve gracefully into the coffee.  Also, I have an espresso maker.  The recipe calls for "strong coffee" as most people don't have access to their own Super Automatic espresso maker.  I would rather find a recipe that stays true to a real latte, and which does not attempt to "hack" day old coffee in a stove top pot.As for my rating, I will give it a "neutral" 3 stars for now, as I do not believe the poor result is necessarily the fault of the syrup itself.  I believe the syrup is intended to be 1 part of a recipe, not a complete solution to a specific drink.  If I find a good recipe the uses the syrup, I will adjust my rating accordingly.As for me, I took this on more as an "adventure" to see what I could come up with.  I am not using Starbucks espresso, so I know my result will never be the same.  I do like the Starbucks version.  If you are trying to save money, you will likely be disappointed.  Enjoy the occasional Starbucks Pumpkin Latte while it is in season, in moderation, as a seasonal "pick me up".  It's not intended to be an every day thing.  Realize that there is no discernable pumpkin flavor in this, and maybe you will look at how you can use it differently.

This isn't at all what I had hoped for. I absolutely love pretty much everything "pumpkin flavored," but this missed the mark. I was hoping for a flavor similar to Starbucks Pumpkin Spice Latte, but this isn't even close and I've honestly produced better flavor just using sugar, cinnamon, allspice, and cloves in my latte. I appreciate other coffee shops' pumpkin lattes, so if this had tasted good, I could have gotten over the fact that it was different from Starbucks', but I just plain don't like it. I think the spice is too heavy--I'm not sure exactly what spices were used in creating this, but based on pumpkin dessert recipes I've made it seems like maybe there is too much allspice? I have a feeling this is going to wind up down the kitchen sink drain :/
Not really a good flavor if you are looking for something close to Starbucks. Way to heavy on the Pumpkin flavor, not sweet enough maybe?

Excellent! Crunchy, 100% beef nuggets -- a healthy alternative to those biscuits and treats with no nutritional value. My dogs LOVE them!

My dogs love them but they are loaded with junk and come from another country. these went in the trash once i read that. I buy USA only and not loaded with junk like caramel coloring or anything thats a preservative. stay away from these. not good for your dogs.
My dogs love these treats.  They gobble them up.  I like that they are made in the US.  The company also has very nice, helpful customer service employees.

What a waste of $$ buying things I think my dogs would love to chew on. They didnt give these bully things a 2nd look after sniffing for the 1st time I put it in their play area... Welp I am surely gonna stick to DINGO's maybe a little pricy but at least they are going to EAT IT!

column9: Perfect fix for a chocolate craving
column10: I am a big fan of Japanese candies, and Choco Baby is one of my favorites. Choco Babies are basically milk chocolate chips but in a small cylinder shape (think along the line of tic tacs in terms of size and shape) and smoother in texture than your average chocolate chip. It's the perfect size for the burst of chocolate flavor you need when you're craving chocolate. There's no interference from candy shells or nuts inside. It's just pure, simple, good-tasting chocolate. The size of the bits is excellent for portion control, and comes with a cute container with recloseable lid. I think the chocolate tastes better than other commercial brands such as Hershey's. Despite not having a visible shell around the chocolate, these hold up pretty well not melting in your hand for quite a while. I don't think chocolate fans would be disappointed in giving this a try.

column9: Yummy-ness in a tiny pellet.  M&Ms are passe'

I guess if you want to keep raking in the money you have to fudge and mislead folk.  That's what SmokeHouse has done by adding 'USA' to their name.  I can say this without fear because the packages I have sitting on the kitchen table in front of me clearly say that this is a "Product of China."You know, the China where they feel free to add melamine to products for human babies (2008), and dogs and cats (2007 and 2010) -- all so that the protein levels register higher than they normally would :(I am so disappointed. I bought these specifically because they were made in the USA and I assumed they would be safe.  They were so hard I could barely break them and my dog wasn't chewing them well.  He started choking on a piece while eating it and that was the end of that.  These are terrible and dangerous.  The pieces are so sharp I became concerned about him cutting an intestine or something.  Now I make my own chicken treats.  It's pretty easy and I know exactly what is in them.

column9: Made In America, with a STRING going through them
column10: I bought these because they are made in America and my dogs are worth it.  What I don't like about them is that there is a thick string, or maybe just a thick vain of some kind, going through each piece. A much smaller issues is that these are very hard, even hard to break by hand.  We have been using a pliers to break the pieces up before serving and then a scissors to cut the string part!  A dog could choke to death with these.My biggest problem is that I am looking for an alternative USA raised chicken solution for treats.

Have been buying this product for some time now - saw complaints about made in USA or not so I called the company. I spent about 30 minutes on the phone with a woman there who was weary of this complaint but very nice. I told her we love our pets, have learned to trust almost no one anymore and they were hurting themselves by selling products from China.As she explained,the confusion comes from the following: the "Made in USA" labeled chicken breast strips - what I have been using for my golden retriever puppy (who ABSOLUTELY loves them - really a healthy nutritious chew toy that lasts about 3 minutes - maybe 10 minutes for a little dog - when he sees it, he goes nuts - has never choked on them or had any negative effects I can see) is, as it says on the bag, Made in USA - they are processed in the USA and come from chicken raised in the USA.Smokehouse DOES sell another chicken product that does NOT say made in the USA on the package and this product DOES come from China.Buy whichever one you want.As to the complaints about not being able to cut them up easily - this IS absolutely true - so, if you want tiny bits of treat to use for reward based training, this is definitely NOT the product you want. I use other natural treats for this purpose (Merricks lamb lung is terrific for this use and my dog loves this product just as well - a one pound bag goes a long way - very easy to break up in whatever sizes you want in seconds)Finally, this product (chicken breast strips) has ONE ingredient: chicken. It is made in the USA from chicken grown in the USA. Because it is dried, it lasts forever, does not need refrigeration, makes no mess when fed to your dog, dogs love it - what else do you want for a treat?

My two medium size dogs love these treats and the thickness is great for their teeth.  lt is also very UNTRUE for any review to state this product in not made in the USA. It absolutley states that very clearly on the packaging and I have also verified this with the manufacturer.  No made in China here.

I bought the product because it was made in the USA.  I have 2 small dogs and was used to breaking them up and giving them pieces as the breast strips are too large for their mouths. These are so hard, neither my husband or myself can break them up.  Will not order again.  Amazon verified purchase.

column9: Crap- So hard couldnt cut with a meat clever

This stuff was so hard if you tried to snap in half it crumbles away a big portion of the piece.I finally put it on a cutting board and when I tried to cut with a meat clever I got scared the knife was gonna slip sideways.  The pieces still crumbled.  I mean we are talking serious dry.This product is touted as quality and american.  This product is much more expensive yet is the worst I've ever purchased.  It is like it was outdated.Do not buy this product.  It is poor value

We have three dogs and I try to find healthy treats from the USA. Smokehouse also has chicken strips from China that are much cheaper but I'd rather give them less treats from the US than spend less and give them more treats from China. These are pricey but the dogs all love them.

If your dog is the kind with a cast iron gut who chows down on road kill with nary a problem and you have an extremely limited budget, this may not be the treat for your dog. For my own case, I have a Border Collie with a sensitive stomach and my budget for dog treats is modest. These are a great treat made here in the USA as the previous reviewer noted, avoiding the potential problems of Chinese made goods making the news recently. Feeding one of these 2-3 times per week gets that excited, eyes bugging out, reaction one would expect from a treat while providing an all natural, high protein component to your dogs diet, while remaining very affordable. As with any treat, overindulgence can upset the proper balance of your dogs diet, but even 2-3 in one day have not upset my dogs gut. In my opinion, this is almost as good as cooking for your dog yourself.

Just to clarify, Smokehouse makes these in the US and also in China.  The ones made in China will cost less than the ones made in the US. The ones made in the US clearly states it on the front of the bag.  For those of you that got bags from China, you should check to make sure you ordered the right bag and if so, return it for a refund if they mistakenly sent you the wrong bag. These treats are great. All natural, so they're healthy.

column9: Smokehouse delivers great product - not all from USA
column10: We're very happy with the Smokehouse products we've ordered. The quality is top-notch. The Natural Chicken Breast Strips are our dog's favorite. He devours them. He gets a little gassy, sometimes, from them but overall he responds well to the treats.Warning: Not all Smokehouse products are made in the USA. We've found that they are clearly labeled. You can't find the Made In the USA strips in any of the pet stores I've visited, so I regularly order these on line. Great product!

They look just like chicken tenderloins.  I say that because in my heart of hearts I sometimes wonder if our dog treats really come from the animals they say they do?  They call it chicken so that we, the consumers are happy to buy them because we eat chicken too, but what if they said they came from some other kind of avian source?  Anyways, I digress.  My dogs love these, they have no digestion issues from them whatsoever.  I would only feed them, at most, 1 per day.  It is a good value to buy them in the big bag, the smaller bags cost more at my local pet store.

column9: Very happy with "Made in the USA"

column9: If you want your dog to die.....

column9: Treat caused ulcers in my dog's GI tract
column10: I should have known when I touched these strips.They are rock solid hard.Anyways I gave it to my dog for the first time, and it caused minor tearing and ulcers in her GI tract. I first noticed little blood in her stool, and dog was visibly unwell.I brought her to the vet immediately before they closed for the day, and did xrays, stool test, and all that.Ended up with a $1600 vet bill, but at least a recovering dog that shouldn't have any long term health problems.The treat basically was so hard the sharp edges was causing minor tearing the GI tract. My dog is a chewer too and she never swallows anything whole, and I was watching her as she ate.I had given her bully sticks, raw hide before (about once or twice a week), and she had no problems.It couldn't have been anything else either because she hasn't eaten anything else other than her dog food (Ziwipeak) in the past 3 days. Ziwipeak isn't a kibble diet either. It is jerky like meat which is very soft. No signs of anything else (like plastic or metal toys, etc) on her x-ray either. So yes, it is these Chickenstrips.Anyhow, I took a new one out of the packaging, and attempted to cut it with a pair of scissors.The strip was so hard my scissors wouldn't cut through, especially where the vein/tendon/muscle fiber (or whatever that is) is.I probably will need a penknife or a small saw to do the job.So yea I learned my lesson, and should have listened to what another reviewer said earlier.I took my chances because this product had so many 5 star feedback, and I made my dog go through unnecessary and avoidable pains and hardship. And also landed myself with a $1600 vet bill (sigh...)Definitely wouldn't advice this to anyone. If you have a really big dog like a Mastiff or a Pit Bull, I can see how this is probably OK because the dog itself is big, so this treat is really small compared in size. I have a 10 pound dog, so yea. I still wouldn't recommend anyone risking any chances, well unless you think a few thousand dollars in vet bills is nothing and don't mind your dog going through all that pain.From now on if I am giving any chicken treats, its gonna be freezed dried or I will just boil or steam some boneless chicken myself.Lesson learned. An expensive, painful, and totally avoidable one.I am so regretful for what I have done to my dog -_-

I bought the smokehouse chicken breast strips because they were made in the U.S.A. Love that its made in the USAFirst bag arrived and chicken was dried and crumbly.Replacement bag arrived and was better but still dried out.

Has a natural strawberry taste that is nicely blended with the granola.  Only slightly sweet (a plus for me).  I started ordering from Amazon since my local grocery was not reliable in regularly stocking this.

Of course I picked up the strawberry, because when it comes to health food I make sure to pick a flavor I enjoy such as strawberry. It's big, but not too much of a loss if you wind up not liking them (which I doubt will happen).

column9: The worse part is how addictive they are!

I bought them on a a trip down south at Super Target and when I returned I seriously went to every store looking for them with no success. I wish it was available because I would buy them every week.
