Please do not waste your money. This Fly trap is absolutely useless. I bought two of  this product for the kitchen, we always BBQ and go in and out by the Pool and fly's get in the House. We have started to make jokes about his product not ONE Fly so far has gone on both of them since i hang it up 2 weeks ago :) Terrible Product!

Placed around the house for several days, setup a fly attracting trap in vicinity. literally watched the flies avoid this trap. after 2 days I was excited to see one lil'bugger land on the surface, only to be disappointed when I approached to examine and he flew away! the paper is tacky when the pressure of a human finger is applied, but for most small flies it is hardly a trap.

I've been nurturing a plant at work and it was doing so well I decided to repot to a larger pot. I must have gotten some funky soil because as soon as I repotted, we were being overrun by a large colony of small flies. I was swatting them and getting bug guts on my hand so frequently I stopped bothering with the "gross!" exclamations. The fact that in the city of San Francisco, you have to compost just aggravated the situation.I bought one of these nitfy traps and set it by my plant and voila! Instead of my hands getting the daily dose of bug guts, the trap is now lined with the tiny suckers! It's been a few months and the trap is pretty much covered (the gross part) and I need to order another one. Not sure how well this will work on larger inserts but it works really well on these tiny, annoying flies.
The only thing this item trapped was a few fruit flies.  It didn't work at all as a fly trap.  I wouldn't recommend it.

column9: THIS ITEM IS EXCELLENT TO KILL INSECTS
column10: I am so happy with this Item. I had too many flies that were disturbing in my kitchen. I put the product near the window and it works fantastically

column9: We have so many flies in the house.  Have had this product for 3 weeks and it has only stuck 1 fly thus far.
column10: We have so many flies in the house.  Have had this product for 3 weeks and it has only stuck 1 fly thus far.

I wish I'd read the reviews before making this purchase. It's basically a cardsotck box that is sticky all over the OUTSIDE. Those pink-ish things that look like entrances "into" the trap? They're just pictures. There *is no* inside of the trap. All the flies will be stuck to the OUTSIDE. It's basically fly paper, just horribly, horribly HORRIBLY overpriced.Do yourself a favor and just get fly paper or fly strips. Same yuck factor, but much cheaper.

column9: Doesn't work!! Don't waste your money!!
column10: Worst product I have gotten in long time. Would rate it as no star if I could.  Simply did not catch a single fly or bug of any sort.  Went to the hardware store and bought the old-fashioned spiral fly paper which was very effective.  Had an unuasual influx of flys in the house this fall and needed to do something.

I had an infestation of fruitflies, they were literally everywhere flying around me in my  kitchen, so I bought this product hoping to at least get rid of a few. But after 2 weeks, only 1 fly had stuck... I was going around with a notepad and squishing the buggers myself with a success rate of 2-3 a day so clearly this product was useless! I even dabbed to red wine and banana to the top of the column after 1 week because they were really attracted to any red wine I had in a glass... but still it did nothing to get them stuck. And then I actually saw a second fly land on it once, and I watched as it flapped it's wings frantically and within 30 secs it had unstuck itself!!!! This product was a total waste of money!

If I could rate this fly trap lower than one star, I would.  I think flies have come from miles away just to come in and laugh at this thing.  I'd have more success taking the flies into a vat of scalding water than getting a fly to randomly run into this box of ridiculousness.WASTE OF $$!

bought this awhile ago, decided to review it now.  this thing sucks.  there has been flies caught on this, but took over a year to get maybe, 10 or so tiny microscopic flies.  no regular flies that you can see with your eyes.  i still have it up, only cause it catches flies a few times a year.  maybe i should let those little things fly around, or i could get a real fly trap, that actually works. :)

Used this fly sticky tape trap in the garage where we had a knat fly problem. We also had some fruit fly type  bugs flying around also. Our neghbor has a big fig tree that isn't pruned of taken care of and all the figs stay on the tree and rot till they dry. Smells really bad and attracts the flys that go into our garage because of its proximity to our garage. We put these up and only caught about 3 to four on each one. We had better results with the sticky traps that unravel. These caught much more knats.

Like others have said, hanging this up is useless. You have to lie it down in an area where the flies like to land. I have caught dozens and dozens of flies with this, however I have noticed that some of these traps are stickier than others. The flies in my house also seem to have figured out how to basically "walk" down the trap until they get to the end, where they can get unstuck and fly off. Maybe 25% of the flies escape, and the others are trapped. I actually have taken to pressing the flies into the trap once they land, to try to keep them from escaping, but this is disturbing and I'd rather not have to do that. The Catchmaster Window glue trap is really superior to this product by comparison (but is currently unavailable...).

Okay so I have a little garden in my back yard that attracts a lot of flies and I have been looking for a way to combat them once they are in the house. I wasn't sure if they still made Fly Paper but when I saw this after searching in the great Amazon I was excited. From the moment I opened the box I was dismayed and I seriously cannot decide if this is a joke or not. The packaging says the box has stunning 3-d images to draw in the flies, these images are perhaps the funniest drawing's I have ever seen being called 3-d...this product has not caught a single fly they simply ignore it and fly everywhere but at the stunningly realistic 3-d images anyone got a better idea?DO NOT BUY THIS UNLESS PLAYING A joke on someone

This is nothing more than a cardboard box with a little dry adhesive on the outside. It does nothing to attract flies and the adhesive is not gluey enough to trap them if they do happen to land on it. Save your money.

I'm fairly certain that once caught, the flies are supposed stay stuck. Not so much with this trap. It's become part of our daily routine to compare how many flies there are on it in morning with how few are left in the afternoon. About 50% of them escape from it.

This product does not work at all. I hang it in the kitchen for 5 days but no fly has been attracted!It doesn't worth the time and money to return it. But please, buyer beware, I strongly suggest you go find some other item.

Having used traditional fly rolls in the past, I was dubious when my hubby opened up the box and showed me this little stand-alone cardboard fly trap. We were desperate, though, as we had a full-on gnat invasion in our kitchen. We put it in a few places on the counter before settling on one near the coffee pot where the gnats seemed to love to gather. At first they seemed to ignore it, but over the next few days, more and more were finding their way onto the trap. At one point we gave up counting--there were dozens. This product is great for ridding yourself of those pesky gnats. I love that it is poison-free and that it can stand on the countertop if you want it to, as our very tall ceilings would make a hanging strip less than useful. But for those wishing to hang it, there's a little hanger included as well. I can't make a claim about larger flies, we didn't catch any of those--there were none around. And I think there would be better choices for outdoors than this product. But for the $$ this little fly trap did the job we asked it to do, and you can't beat that!

Well I received the item and placed it in the same area where we had put fly paper before-we had far fewer victims than with the regular fly paper and it looks like it doesn't really catch "the big ones" like the fly paper did. However, for the price it is decent and looks more attractive than the regular strip of fly paper.
This sly trap is attractive to look at, works well, and has no odor. I recommend it!

I bought a few of these after my apartment was infested with fruit flies. After only a few hours, the trap had "attracted" many flies and within a few days they were practically gone. This may not be a long term  solution, but if flies are driving you crazy, consider buying this. One  caution- the surface is very sticky, so try to avoid touching it.
Bought at my local Hardware Store.  I was having a terrible fly problem, and it only trapped one (1) fly (it's been over a year now, still hanging, still just the same one fly.DON'T BUY THIS PRODUCT!

For something that was supposed to attract them, The flys couldn't have cared less. In about a months time it caught maybe 10 flies which sure were only a miniscule fraction of those in the kitchen! Was a waste of money.

I don't really think that the design of the cardboard box makes one bit of difference to the flies. House or fruit flies. Flies land on pretty much anything. With sufficient time flies flying around randomly and landing randomly around the house. Eventually they'll land on the fly trap.Perhaps after the first few have landed and died on the trap the rest will be attracted to the scent of the dead flies? Directly out of the box, I don't think there is anything on it that is an attractant.

Well, I purchased 3 as they were inexpensive and I figured for the shipping, I might as well. I have two up in to different areas of my small apartment and after 24 hours, nothing. I've managed to kill some flies but that was only by me swatting at them.

column9: Doesn't work. I have 4 different types of traps, and this is the only one that is empty.
column10: Even the cheap 'ribbon' traps have caught many dozens of flies in the few days I've had them, and the liquid bait traps (Rescue, and Victor's Fly Magnet) have caught hundreds in a few days, but this thing remains empty (the best seems to be the Rescue trap, I call "the stinker", because it reeks, but it works). This trap is in the same space as the other traps, and there are hundreds of flies out there. Just does not work. While it is an "indoor" trap, the directions say that it can be used outdoors if protected by weather, which it is.

column9: Regular fly ribbon worked way better ...
column10: In the time I spent waiting for my order of these fly traps to arrive, I went out and bought regular fly ribbon for the bad fly problem (not sure what kind of flies - slightly bigger than fruit flies) I was having. In the at least week that I've had one of these fly traps up, I've caught zero flies with this fly trap and have caught probably over 100 flies with the regular fly ribbon. At one point, I even saw a fly on this fly trap and thought it was caught, but now it's gone. I even have pictures to prove it.

column9: still waiting to catch a fly
column10: With hundreds of common house flies all about for 24 hours and not a single one caught I resorted to a fly swatter and killed 50 or so in 1-2 hours with my old fly swatter. This fly trap appears useless.

After a summer grill party where the door was kept open all day/ food was out on the countertops, we developed a horrible fly infestation in our home.  My husband bought this trap and it did not work, not one fly was caught.  I ended up putting a tiny smear of honey on one side and that actually worked, the next day I counted over 30 flies on the thing.  But by itself, it does nothing to 'attract' flies.

I bought this tea last year directly from Chartreuse and have been doling it out on special occasions. I've tried other lemon/rooibus mixes, but this one has just the right balance--refreshing both hot and cold. I can understand why people drink it all day, and I'm going to start! I'm so glad Amazon is carrying it now!

I consider myself something of a tea conneisseur and I'm generally a big fan of green tea.  This is some of the best tasting tea out there.  I've been happy with every variety I've gotten from Chartreuse, and every time I make some my whole house smells great!

I get these for those 1 hour car trips or day excursions with my kids (5 and 9 yrs old).  They love these and they are a healthy alternative to other snacks that are out there.  I also keep some of these in my office for the same reasons.  When I need to work late, sometimes I need something to hold me over for a while until I can go home and eat a proper meal, and this is better than those fatty snacks in the vending machine!

These are great little snacks, tender and yummy! Will definitely buy them again. Great cranberry flavor, but they do contain a little sugar, so if you are very carb restricted, you might want the ones with no fruit.

I can't speak highly enough for this product. It tastes incredible and I really like that it is all natural, straight from the Lakota peoples on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation. I plan on ordering a lot more - well worth the price!
These bites beat the living daylights out of jerky.  They are chewy bites with the perfect combination of sweet and salty. A perfect Primal/Paleo friendly snack for the desk/car/gym bag.

column9: Looks like dog treats... Tastes like AWESOME!
column10: I'm always on the lookout for good jerky in my area, so I was excited to try these Tanka Bites. The ingredients look like pemmican (except, sadly, minus the fat), which I've wanted to try but can't find locally. These flavor is pretty good -- savory and a little sweet -- and they're not super tough or overly chewy. The texture is a little bit plasticy, though. The dried, sweetened cranberries might not make it Whole 30 approved, but it's definitely a convenient primal snack.

column9: Taste Great but Pricey; Great Gluten Free Option
column10: These buffalo jerky bites taste great, but they are expensive, especially when you consider the cranberries (which add a nice flavor, but are at the end of the day filler). If price isn't a concern, then there's no real negative for this product.This jerky is also a great option for those who on a gluten free diet. It's difficult to find gluten free jerky because many products include soy sauce and other unfriendly flavorings. This product doesn't contain any wheat or ingredients that contain wheat.

I was disappointed with the taste and texture of these Tanka Buffalo Cranberry Bites.  I have followed the Paleo diet for over a year now and am accustomed to grass fed buffalo.  I'm not sure what happened with these.  Not tasty.

We decided to try this for our backpacking trip to Glacier National Park this year.  This is the best jerky that I have ever had.  It is moist and soft.  Also it has no MSG, nitrates, just spices, bison and cranberries.  It tastes so good!!!
Surprisingly tasty. Meaty and fruity but not too sweet. They are very low fat, but the protein keeps them somewhat satiating.
Great tasting jerky. Healthy snack with great taste. Texture a little different but good. Love the buffalo and cranberry combination. Will definitely buy again.

These are great, the ingredients are such that I don't mind feeding it to my kids and it tastes amazing.  The only problem is that it's hard on the wallet especially because it's easy to eat them all very quickly.  I think the pack of 6 three ounce packages lasted us 2 days, if that.  But that's kind of a testament to it's greatness.

My daughter is studying Native Americans at school.  I ordered Tanka Bites to share with her grade level.  They were a huge hit and 2nd graders are tough critics.  The children also enjoyed the product information on the packaging.  I chose this product because it was a Native American company. However, I will buy more (& have already ordered) because it is really good.  The Tanka Bites are a nice texture, easy to chew.  The cranberry adds a nice burst of flavor.  I am looking forward to trying the spicy pepper blend.  I do NOT like jerky products and seldom eat meat.  Interestingly enough, I have found myself wishing, on more than one occasion, that I had another bag of Tanka Bites on hand for a quick snack.  You know it is a good product when you can't wait to re-order!

These are a great bite-size, healthy snack option for you & your kids. They are gluten-free, nitrite-free, dairy-free & soy-free: a good choice if you follow a Paleo lifestyle (note: there is minimal sugar added to the cranberries). I recommend these for a fast yummy treat when you are in a hurry & on-the-go.  Busy lifestyle does not have to equate to crappy food.  Be prepared with healthy snacks.
tastes great at first.. then the after taste starts...yyuuukk. I think it is the cranberries. My friend spit it out.

I sent brisket to my sister who had all her grandchildren for a summer visit. She got the brisket and served it and her grandchildren went crazy over it! You know how hard it is to find things kids will eat and they devoured it because it was so tender and delicious.

I received this as gift and thought it was great. I usually like the fatty part of most briskets and will drown the leaner side in bbq sauce to make the dry parts edible for me but this brisket was tender all the way through! It had a nice smokey flavor, fresh texture and came vacuum sealed. You don't even need sauce for it but be sure to invite some friends over because its too much to eat on your own. I would not have bought it on my own but will probably buy it for myself down the line again.

Awesome product, i dont even have to use monster anymore. it also has less sugar. it keeps me alert and focused for school and is good for you. it also has vitamins. the seller is just as good. i got my product right away.

I had looked all over for a place to purchase these flatbread crackers.  I could not find them locally so I went to Amazon.  I was so excited to find them.  Placed an order for 6 boxes.  When I received them, I opened the first box and all the crackers were crumbs.  Second box, the same.  After opening all six boxes, I found that I only had about 6 of the flatbread crackers that were whole.  I would never order them again.

My family is trying to eat healthy and we discovered this product when a friend broght it over.  They have a crisp texture, tasty seasoning and are very low in both fat and sodium.  They're great as a snack but can compliment any topping.  We like them with dips and vegetables but they go well with soft, spreadable cheeses as well.  For entertaining, they're a little different from what you normally get served.
USE TO GET THEM AT cOSTCO, THEY DISCONTUED CARRING THEM.  THESE WERE ALL BROCKEN WHEN I RECEIVED THEM, ALSO MUCH MOR EXPENSIVE, GUESS I LEARNED MY LESSON

The store where I had originally purchased the crackers no longer carry them.  I was pleasantly surprised to find them on Amazon.  Received them right away in excellent condition.  The crackers are my favorites by far and I highly recommend them.  They are well worth it!

I've been reading the reviews of various fruit juices in addition to my usual orange and thought I'd try some odd combinations out.  Organic banana-strawberry-orange?  Yes!  Delicious.  I'm trying to eat more bananas anyway the more I learn about their incredible health benefits.  Ditto strawberries.  Sometimes I add a little peach schnapps to the juice for a little lift.  Not 100% organic but rather orgasmic!  Glass bottles make juices taste fresher, imho.

column9: Really cute, But not the best chocolate.
column10: I purchased several bags of these to use as prizes for a mad hatter themed baby shower that I hosted, They were really cute and a big hit among the guests but I did taste a piece of the chocolate and it wasn't even worth eating. For the effect though I would purchase these again.

This candy will make the perfect gift for the flamingo collector on your list. The service was fast and friendly so how can you go wrong? The package arrived quickly and everything was in good condition. Why not treat the flamingo lover you know to a special treat made just for them?
These favorite chocolate treats are especially good designed as "flamingo droppings."  Great tasting, fun packaging. Made a nice gift for caring neighbors.
This is a wonderful and fun gift for the flamingo lover. Comes nicely packaged with a neat 'flamingo' label.

column9: A fun gift for a flamingo lover
column10: My wife collects flamingos, and she loved this. It made a perfect stocking stuffer, and I loved the look on her face when she got them. I don't know what they taste like, as she hasn't eaten them. But they made a cute fun gift.

column4: M.S. Pierce "Up Against it and Coasting"
column10: I had been expecting White Chocolate Flamingo Droppings, the kind favored by *les nobles qui sait* in Nice and Monaco. I have used those for years as both an alleviate and an ironic potpourri for would-be long-term guests, and I have never been disappointed. Imagine my dismay, then, when I received (by breathless messenger) this item, clearly intended to be *eaten*.  Shudder.

column9: Excellent Teas, and the best Tea Pot Ever
column10: I have quickly become a fan of this tea company.  I have never seen a loose leaf tea brewer that works as well!!  I really is wonderful.  The teas in this collection all taste wonderful.  I recommend this as the perfect gift for the tea afficianado in your life.
great teas.  i love the brewer/dispenser.not a big fan of mango melange though, but all others were great!

column9: I wish I could give more then 5 stars
column10: This is the best idea ever. I have many pots for loose tea and make tea every day. I have used "bags" to put loose tea in and balls to hold loose tea or a pot with a filter in the middle, I've used a small filter that sits on top of my cup but nothing works near as well, and is as convenient as this pot. You put the loose tea and boiling water in the pot and after it has steeped you place the pot on top of your cup, the tea drips into the cup because the rim of the cup presses it's valve.It is the simplest way to make loose tea that I know of. A uniquie gift idea. I plan on getting one for all my tea drinking friends. Christmas shopping is going to be easy this year.

This was on my daughter's wish last fall for her birthday, so I bought it for her.  Her husband & I loved it so much that I got it for him for Christmas, and my own husband surprised me with it.  We all love it and still use it daily.  The teas from Adagio are wonderful, but it's the pot that is truly extraordinary.  I highly recommend this for any tea drinker and it makes a really excellent gift.
So easy to use and clean. The sample teas were very flavorful. Am ordering this for my sisters as gifts. Any tea lover would appreciate this little gem !

I love that there is no pouring required for this product. There is no mess will spillage or with loose tea leaves. Its great for a quick cup of tea or for a group. I also enjoyed the sampler because i could try out the different types. Cleaning the tea leaves out required filling the pot with water and swishing it around instead of having a tea filter to dump the leaves in one swoop. That is the only set back to this great product.

column9: My cats love it. It's good for them, but it's a bit pricey
column10: I feed my cats a raw-food diet. I feed this to them like treats. I sprinkle it on their regular food and they love it. You can safely feed this to your cats as their regular food (as long as you add water), but it's too pricey for me to feed it 100%. Apart from the price, I highly recommend this product.

column9: Finally raw food for my pet
column10: Fresh food contains enzymns that cooked food does not and I was concerned that my cat did not have food that provided such nutrients but all that is changed now.
Pop Rocks weren't introduced to the public until 1975... By that time you are a 20 yr old adult if born in 1955... What's the point?

column9: Don't waste your time with the small bottles!!! :)
column10: I recently moved to Pittsburgh PA from upstate NY. "Dino" is a staple food in my home town.  Although they have the small bottles of slathering sauce at the local store I like to make a great big crock pot full of bbq pulled pork using the Slathering Sauce. Needless to say my Pittsburgh Co-workers were quite impressed!
With the texture of halavah and a wonderful honey and almond taste, Jijona is absolute heaven.

My kids and I enjoyed this granola. It had a nice fresh taste (unless some of the stale tasting ones we have had). The chocolate chucks were a bonus for my daughter who normally doesn't eat granola. I put it over homemade ice cream and they gobbled it up. I ate it as cereal with milk and enjoyed it. I have been happy with every Back to Nature product I have purchased and this is no exception. I would buy it again.

column9: Love it ! Enough chocolate for my taste, too much for my wife's
column10: Hi love these granola, I lightly fill the bowl with cold milk, let it just sit long enough to have the milk color and then drink it and scoop the granola out. Delicious !My wife thinks it's too sweet though.

I'm kind of so-so when it comes to granola. Don't really care for it as a cereal or snack, but do enjoy it mixed into ice cream. My favorite has been a brand I get at Trader Joe's - not too sweet, and not  gritty or "flat" tasting like some of the lower-end brands.Well, there's a new winner when it comes to granola. This is fantastic - loads of really good chocolate plus excellent granola taste. Crunchy, but not so hard that it feels like it's going to break a tooth. The first granola that I enjoyed right out of the bag as-is -- no need to mix it in with ice cream or yogurt. This stuff is great!!

column9: It's Granola with Chocolate... Who Doesn't Love Chocolate!
column10: Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is a tasty and fairly healthy snack.  It comes in a sturdy 12-ounce pouch, with a strong Ziploc-like seal you can use to keep it fresh.  The Granola pieces are nice and crunchy and taste very fresh.  The chocolate pieces are not so much mixed into the granola chucks as they are just separate Chicklet-like chocolate pieces (there appears to be little bits of chocolate in some of the granola chunks, though).  The mix of granola and chocolate is quite addictive.  The crunchy texture and nutty taste of the granola goes well with the smooth texture and sweet taste of the chocolate.The all natural ingredients are things you'll be able to understand, there's nothing foreign here.  As far as nutritional value it concerned, a serving is half a cup and has lots of fiber, 220 calories and a decent amount of fat.  It's no rice cake, but it tastes a lot better, and there are far worse choices out there.All in all... Perfect for the office, in the car, or while watching TV - it's a tasty snack.

column9: Good snack, or yogurt topping, or...whatever you want it to be
column10: I really wasn't sure how I was supposed to eat the granola chunks when I first received the package, because they were more like the granola that you add to yogurt - in small pieces.  But there were also pieces that were too big to be topping.  So I used them both as finger food and a yogurt topping.  I find that alone, it's a little too sweet, and as a yogurt topping, it's nothing special.  However, it's not a bad snack, because it uses some good ingredients and the dark chocolate helps add extra taste.  In other words, this is a light, fun, and tasty snack that won't put you back too  many fat calories, and provides some nutritious benefits as well.  Just don't expect something that redefines granola as a snack.

On first bite, I found this granola to lack much sweetness.  Then again, I am comparing it to those sugary cereals that people who are looking into this product are probably trying to avoid.  Adding some milk, I found that the cereal was very nicely balanced and has a very healthy taste.  That means that I felt good after eating it and not weighed down.  As for the technical nutritional facts, the ingredients and stats are listed here (a nice thing about Amazon).  The absence of high fructose corn syrup and the basic natural ingredients are quite reassuring, but, as with all granolas I've seen, portion control will be needed to keep the calorie count down (220 per half cup).  I found the texture quite good for cereal, crumbly bits and all, which is how I eat it.  It may be a bit messy for casual consumption by hand.Overall, this is really basic.  It would be quite inexpensive and easy to make this yourself.  That is not a bad thing, though.  It means that when convenience is at a premium, this product carries the benefits and comforts of something homemade.  If the price doesn't scare you, I would heartily recommend it.

This is a tasty snack that seems to fit the "natural" category,  in that it has no artificial flavors or preservatives, hydrogenated oils or high fructose corn syrup.  The oats combined with the dark chocolate is good, but it's dry and needs a glass of milk to go with it.

First things first, this granola is TASTY. Straight out of the pouch. And for me, that's a BIG bonus since that's how I eat my granola probably 97% of the time. And honestly, I don't really eat granola because it's good for you---I eat it because it tastes good and is *somewhat* healthy (i.e. it's better to snack on this than chocolate cake, LOL).I was also looking forward to more clusters, since the description says "Crunchy Clusters"--but it was mostly oat pieces and chocolate chunks, which makes it quite hard to eat straight from the bag without a spoon or making a complete mess (I actually took to just dumping it straight into my mouth).All that said, I would buy this again. I received this item as part of the Vine program, so I had no idea how much it cost. One true test of an item is to think how much you would pay for it, and THEN check to see what it sells for. After I tasted it, I thought I'd probably pay $3 to $4 a bag--well, at Amazon's current price, it works out to $3.60/pouch so it was dead on.

column9: Tasty and Delicious Just Wished Did Not Have Extra "Sugar" Hidden As Carbs
column10: I am a big fan of granola, but unfortunately not a big fan of fat, which is traditionally what one gets with granola.  For those concerned about taste, I would say this is a great product and if rating on taste alone I would give this "Back to Nature" product 5 Stars.  However, once again we have a product that "looks" seemingly healthy and fun, but is loaded with added carbohydrates, aka "sugar" and that is what brings the score on this product down.  You think companies would work with today;s busy professionals and re-establish trust, by offering products that are truly truly healthy and not just slipping them in under the FDA or surgeon general guide lines of what is deemed good health or nutrition.  I am  very health conscious so always reading labels for ingredients.  Furthermore I have to keep my sugar intake in check during this "look better naked" summer months.  Great treat, but for those looking to shed the extra pounds of fat or get leaner during the summer save this for the winter months or during your bulking phase.

column9: Excellent taste, texture, and good for us!
column10: Welcome to the new Kraft - while you might not think that a major company like Kraft is in tune with health and wellness, well think again. This new Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is delightful, tastes great, has real chunks of chocolate and is loaded with 28 grams of whole grains. If you love granola you have got to try this product - although I do have to wonder about the copy on the back which talks about feeling warm sand beneath my feet, but the re-closable Ziplock bag more than makes up for it.

There really isn't much to review for this product--in my opinion--because the product title and details pretty much tell you everything.This packet contains nothin' but granola and dark chocolate bits.  'Nough said.If you like dark chocolate and granola, this one's for you.  I guess the only "gripes" I have is that I didn't initially know it was dark chocolate because the title and the big letters on the bag only say chocolate.  But, c'est la vie.  I prefer dark chocolate anyway.And, I guess from years of being subjected to sugary granola often found in McDonald's yogurts and grocery cereals, I wasn't expecting the oaty taste I found in here, which is, I presume, what granola is supposed to taste like!Good stuff.  I'm eating it as I compose this review!

column9: Crunchy granola, dark chocalate chunks. What's not to like?
column10: I happen to like granola and I LOVE dark chocolate, so this snack hits the spot. If you are concerned about your health, the granola has a high fiber content (4 G per half cup serving) and the dark chocolate is high in anti-oxidants. The sugar content (13G) is higher that I'd like, but, after all, this IS a snack.

First, the nutrition facts:Serving size: 1/2 cupServings per container: about 7Calories: 220Fat: 6gSodium 5mgCarbohydrates: 37g (Dietary Fiber 4g, Sugars 13g, Other carbs 20g)Protein: 5gThis granola is really very tasty. The chocolate chunks add a nice flavor and texture, and the granola is very crunchy. It comes in a plastic zip-seal bag.With so much chocolate and sugars, this is by no means a "health food", but it's a great snack that at least has some nutrients, unlike candy bars for instance. And it tastes just as good, if not better.Disclosure: Although I was not paid for this review, I received one pouch of this product for free.

column9: Too sweet, even for a treat!
column10: This granola was WAY to sweet, WAY WAY WAY too sweet, and it was lacking nutty goodness I expect in a granola.The dark chocolate used in the granola was very good, I found myself picking out the bits, as the sugary coated oats was just too much for me.Well, not JUST sugar, it really was evaporated cane juice (AKA a sugar), Brown rice syrup (AKA another sugar) and molasses (AKA another sugar) on top of the SUGAR and DEXTROSE already in the chocolate pieces.I think my pancreas is in shock. Why so much sugar?And why are the only ingredients (other than the sugars) basically oats and chocolate? How about some nuts?This is basically dried oatmeal and chocolate bits held together with SUGAR.I like a sweet treat, but this is overboard. I would think using 1/2 or less of the sugar in this would have left it tasting naturally sweet. And the addition of SOMETHING, anything other than plain oats would have been a welcome addition for the tastebuds.Nope, for a wholesome snack this didn't do it for me. If I could describe it in two words it would be : SUGARY BLANDNESS.

column9: Little dark chocolate bits melt on your tongue. Yum!
column10: There are 3 main styles of granola:1) Hard and crunchy (aka the broken-up granola bar), good for single-hand snacking and on-the-go snacking.  Firm and won't fall apart in your hands.2) Chewy (broken up cookie/dense cake type), good for snacking but can be sticky and messy. Usually need more than one hand to eat this.3) Crumbly, mainly good for cereal, shot-glass style snacking or sprinkling over yogurt and ice cream.This product is the 3rd type: small crisp crumbly clusters the size of large popcorn, but also a lot of little bits in the bag.  The little bits account for a little over 1/3 of the product in the bag. (See uploaded photo)Taste:The product is a not too sweet granola with small thin chocolate bits evenly distributed in it.  The small chocolate bits melt nicely on your tongue and there is no excessive chewing of large hard chocolate chunks or worse, chocolate sprinkles, powders or coating on the granola. Simple granola + chocolate bits in the right size. The chocolate is a decent but not spectacular dark semi-sweet chocolate that isn't crunchy but melts on contact with your tongue.Packaging:The bag is resealable, but the tear-off strip was messy and ineffective. I had to use scissors.You could easily make something just like this at home, but this product's main selling point is the size and consistency of the chocolate bits.  Also, packaged granola is convenient.Good for those who like sweet breakfasts and snacks and for those who like chocolate with their granola but don't like the hard chunks of chocolate they usually have.  It would also make a semi-healthy snack for kids (who don't mind dark chocolate) using the jello-cup method. I would not recommend this for on-the-go snacking because it is rather crumbly and the chocolate melts easily. I would also not recommend this for milk chocolate lovers. For those who live in the warmer parts of the country and for the upcoming summer months, the chocolate might melt during transport.Granola is to oats what a Caramel Latte is to milk: a very tasty spin on something healthy by making it less so, but in the end it is still made from something healthy and better than candy or cola.

column9: Tasty product with a great ingredient list
column10: First, a disclaimer.  I am strange in the fact that I like cereal as a bedtime snack.  That way, in my diet riddled mind, I am getting some quality nutrition for the calories I am eating (as opposed to , say, ice cream).  With that off of my chest, this is a great cereal.One quarter to one half of a cup of this granola with some milk and I am totally satisfied.  The chocolate taste proved totally enjoyable - even though I had my doubts about how chocolate and cold milk would get that whole "melt in your mouth" thing going.  Somehow, Back to Nature pulls it off.The ingredient list is also very good.  No preservatives, colors or flavors.  The first ingredient is rolled oats and the second is semi-sweet chocolate.  That information alone will give you a sense of the predominant flavors.

I ordered this granola last week and was really looking forward to trying it.  I can't have dairy, so before I placed my order, I checked its product page both on Amazon and on Back to Nature's own website for any milk, butter, etc. listed in the ingredients.  Everything cleared (yay!), so I went ahead and ordered it.While waiting for the granola to arrive, I perused the reviews on this page just to see what others thought about it.  For the most part, it sounded delicious and that everyone had enjoyed it.  But at least one person had listed "skim milk" among the ingredients, and upon reading this, my alarm bells went off.  Surely Back to Nature's own website would list the correct ingredients of their product, right?  Upon receiving my granola yesterday, I immediately flipped to the back of the package -- and wouldn't you know it, clearly listed (as part of the chocolate chunks) is nonfat milk.I don't know if Vine Voices were given a beta product, or perhaps Back to Nature changed their recipe and wanted to get rid of their backstock.  Which information source are we supposed to believe, the product packaging or the company website?  This mislabeling won't be an issue for most people, but it is a risk for those who are lactose intolerant or who otherwise don't consume dairy.Mislabeled or not, I wasn't willing to chance it, so I skipped eating the chocolate pieces but still ate the plain oat clusters.  It was very sweet and oaty, like a decadent "dessert-type" granola -- similar to Quaker Chewy bars, except not as moist.  I ate a few handfuls out of the bag but found it too dry; it was much more palatable eaten in a bowl with soymilk over it.  I do think it would be nice in an oatmeal cookie mix or over yogurt.  Although this granola has a pleasant flavor, mouthfeel, and crunch, I have tasted better and would rate this fairly average.Looking down into my bag when I was done with the oat clusters, I noticed that the chocolate pieces are all very tiny, flat, brick-shaped flakes -- instead of asymmetrical, craggly, varyingly-sized chunks.  I don't know why I was expecting the latter, but obviously it wasn't a big deal since I didn't eat them. :)Overall, this is a nice-tasting average granola.  You wouldn't be doing yourself a disservice by purchasing this -- it's tasty -- but there is better granola out there.  If you can't have dairy, you may want to opt for another variety/flavor just to be safe.

you will love this stuff.  It has all the dark semi sweet chocolate pieces that you could want in a granola.  However, in warm weather, which we are having now, the chocolate melted in the bag. So, into the refrigerator to chill out.The clusters of oats are small and held together by the sweeteners. It is sweet but not overly sweet, the bitter chocolate blends it out.It's great as a ice cream topping or a yogurt mix in.If you eat it straight out of the bag, your hands will be a chocolate mess.Enjoy it, but keep a paper towel nearby.

column9: Delicious - Chocolate and not too sweet
column10: This granola is wonderful.  It has a nice dark chocolate flavor but is not too sweet.  A great start to your day if you love chocolate.  I have mine with some soy milk and love it.  The granola is crunchy, but not so hard you feel it will break your teeth.  There are no nuts in the granola which is nice for those who don't like them.  I would highly recommend this cereal.  Also a great snack without milk.

Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is a combination of very dark chocolate and crunchy granola.  At 220 calories per one-half cup, it cannot be considered low-calorie.  It has a saturated fat content of 2g, 5mg sodium,13g sugar, and dietary fiber of 4g. I find that storing this product in the refrigerator keeps the chocolate at just the right consistency.  This is an extremely good-tasting combination and makes for a great snack.  The dark chocolate has just the right sweetness.  Others have remarked about the granola being crumbly and not very many clusters.  However, it is granola, and granola is quite crumbly.  Immediately upon opening and tasting Chocolate Delight Granola, I instantly fell in love with the crunch and flavor mix.  If you love dark chocolate, this item is for you.  The granola mixed in gives it a wonderful touch. Highly recommend it as a snack.  Very good!

Good grief this stuff is like crack.  It is supposed to be cereal, but I eat it like candy. This is a great size bag to just put in your purse or backpack to snack on when you want something tasty but not too filling.  The chocolate in it can really make it taste like dessert.  I'm going to order more and make cookies with it.  Great product.

column4: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
column9: Nutrition Info here...Great Dark Chocolate flavor..
column10: Granola has a healthy reputation but the truth is that it is usually chock full of calories, fat, sodium, and sugar.This granola is not as sweet as many (Our favorite is Whole Foods Almond Crunch, which is as addictive as crack, but has tons of sugar and fat)  Although it doesn't look like that much chocolate, you can taste it in every bite.This granola is surprisingly healthy - no palm oil, hydrogenated fats, etc.  Some saturated fat, I presume from the chocolate.  All the ingredients are identifiableHere are the numbers compared to Cheerios (Which I consider the healthiest cereal this side of organic free range sawdust)First I have to adjust the serving size to get a fair comparison.  Cheerios uses a 28g serving size with 100 calories while BTN GranolaGoing with 50 gm servings for both,BTN = 220 calories, Cheerios = 179Calories from fat: BTN = 23%, Cheerios = 15%Carb calories from sugar: BTN = 35%, Cheerios = 5%Protein: BTN = 5g, Cheerios = 5gSodium: BTN=5 mg, Cheerios = 339mg!Dietary fiber: BTN = 4 g, Cheerios = 7gOverall, it's quite healthy and tasty.  I recommend it.  Four stars though as I would have preferred a bit stronger flavor (more vanilla perhaps?)My ratings: 1star: Avoid! / 2star: Some merit but I can't recommend  / 3star: Decent, recommended / 4star: Highly recommended  / 5 star: Nearly perfect!If you have found this review to be helpful, please let me know!

I'd say this a fair to good ice cream topping - chocolate with some fresh raspberries mixed in.  It only really gets 3 stars for two reasons.  First, some of the chocolate chunks had melted, maybe a packaging issue, maybe a chocolate selection issue, but still.  Second, it's extremely dry and granular.  Not a big granola eater, all I saw I could do with it would be mix it with oatmeal or ice cream.  It's ok, I believe I prefer granola to be in slightly larger chunks.

This is good stuff.  I almost want to say it is more of an "adult" granola but, who doesn't like like chocolate.  The reason I say this is that it isn't that sweet which is really nice.  The chocolate is a semi-sweet and the granola is lightly sweetened.  It is somewhat hard to eat because the pieces don't clump together (probably because there isn't a lot of added sugar).  I tried eating it while walking on a golf course and it was tough.  The granola is almost airy when chewing.  I would probably be good eating like cereal.  I usually put granola in my yogurt but, wouldn't do that with this chocolate chip one.  Overall, pretty good stuff but, hard to eat on the go.

This granola is fantastic.  It's crunchy, there's a lot of chocolate chunks in it, and it's healthy - what more can I ask for?  I eat this granola with yogurt for breakfast or afternoon snack. If I'm looking for a little chocolate fix at night, I don't feel bad about snacking on something this good for me!

column9: Very good tasting, healthy granola snack
column10: This granola is surprisingly good, and healthy too.  It comes in a resealable zip-lock package, and it consists of chunks AND BITS of granola and dark chocolate.  It is crunchy and delicious.  Back to Nature makes this granola with no artificial preservatives, flavors or colors.  It is an excellent source of whole grain.  The packaging describes it as crunchy clusters of whole grain rolled oats and dark chocolate chunk, sweetened with natural ingredients, and this is a fairly accurate description.  They say "chunks", but it's more like chunks and some smaller bits.  It's something you would dump into a bowl and eat by hand out of a bowl.  I found it difficult to control just by pulling handfuls out of the bag and holding it in my hand.Serving size is one-half cup, and one serving contains 220 calories, 50 of those calories are from fat.  Here are some stats from the label's "% Daily Value": 9% total fat, 10% saturated fat, 5% potassium, 12% total carbs, 16% dietary fiber, sugars 13g, other carbs 20g, protein 5g.Calcium 2%, Iron 10%, Phosphorus 15%, Magnesium 15%, Zinc 10%, Copper 15%.Ingredients: whole grain rolled oats, semi-sweet chocolate chunks (chocolate, sugar, dextrose, cocoa butter, soy lecithin,, vanilla extract, nonfat milk), evaporated cane juice, brown rice syrup, brown rice flour, expeller pressed safflower oil, molassess, vitamin E (a natural vitamin to help preserve flavor), natural flavor.Contains soy, milk.Manufactured on equipment that processes wheat.I cannot guarantee you that they won't change the product or the product label at any point, but this is what's on the label of my sample package.Overall Rating:  Delicious, healthy snack food!

Honestly, I expected the worst with this product. I thought that I wouldn't like it. And then the package arrived. There looked to be only a small portion of dark chocolate mixed into the granola.Then I took some in my mouth.And the taste was amazing. The dark chocolate taste explodes about halfway through chewing the granola. And it is very satisfy. If you are a fan on dark chocolate, and want a healthier snack then just a plain bar, try this product. you won't regret it.

Dieters beware, this stuff contains more calories per gram than a Hershey's dark chocolate bar. But if that's not a concern, this granola is delicious, like eating a crumbled chocolate chip cookie.  My kids love it, and even argued over the last crumbs in the bag.  I like the crunchy texture and I didn't think it was too sweet.  It's very good mixed about 1:3 with Special K or other unsweetened cereal.  It would also be good as an ice cream topping or yogurt mix-in, but it's just too rich to eat by itself as cereal or snack.

column9: Is it a snack or a breakfast?
column10: I thought this was okay - the chocolate was interesting and not overly sweet.  Granola can be pretty high in fat -- this was moderately so -- definitely not diet food. The idea of chocolate for breakfast doesn't really appeal to me so I would be more inclined to eat this as a snack but as a snack, I would expect it to be in bigger chunks -- this is just going to leave a bunch of small crumbles at the bottom of the bag or a bowl if you serve it as a snack.As for those in our house who do like chocolate for breakfast -- they're not granola eaters so it's hard to know just who the target market for this would be.  It doesn't look like it's anyone in our house.

column9: Chocolate Granola huh? An oxymoronic goodness ...
column10: At first these two ingredients really do not go together. Granola is often thought of as a healthy food and chocolate - well, not so much.The taste is not really one or the other - but a good break if you feel like something mildly sweet and somewhat solid. A rare craving - but if you have it - then it is good stuff.The chocolate is tasty and seems to have just enough to make you want more. Not too much to drown out the granola ...

I confess I do not eat this granola from a bowl with milk, I keep it stored in an airtight container and use a shot glass to scoop out an ounce at a time for snacking.  Very easy to toss back using the shot glass and my fingers stay clean.  It is very good and has no bad ingredients.

Not too crunchy and not overly sweet, but it is sweet. I like that the bag has a zip lock top to take it on the go. It is high in calories (220 for half a cup) but that's granola for you. Took it to the park with a large group of kids 5-10 yrs old and they went wild for this granola. I wish I had brought small cups to put it in since it has more of a cereal consistancy to it.

I got this today, and it couldn't have come at a better time.  Every once in awhile I get a craving for chocolate, and today was that day.  I tore open the bag, and grabbed a handful.The granola itself is slightly sweet, with just a hint of saltiness.  Exactly how I like my granola, but the chocolate was the real surprise!  It was rich and melted in my mouth.  Not really the sweetness of milk chocolate, but not the bitterness of dark chocolate either, but a very nice in between.You get six 12 ounce packages for $21.57 or about $3.60 a bag.  That seems to be about the price for natural, organic cereals, so this is an average deal.  That said, I would certainly buy this for my family as a snack.  For me, it's too crunchy and the clusters are just a tad too big for a morning cereal.

Very addictive stuff.  The day I bought this I almost finished off an entire bag in one sitting.  Whole grains, no artificial badness, luscious chocolate chunks, good stuff!  Unlike other reviewers, I didn't find it overly sweet or chocolatey; I thought the granola and chocolate had a nice balance.  And I didn't feel "heavy" after eating it- I just felt happy!  One complaint: why not organic?  It's not cheap, and being organic seems like a no-brainer.  Otherwise I would have given it 5 stars.

This is a tasty product, however, it's got a tad too much sugar (and consequently calories) for my taste.  If I'm trying to eat healthy, I really do try to avoid eating things with a lot of added sugar.  Now, if I'm going to have a chocolate chip cookie, so be it.  I expect the sugar and carbs.  But, if I'm aiming to eat some granola, then I might just prefer it to be high in fiber, some added protein and a minimal amount of added sugar or otherwise useless carbs.The taste was good...don't get me wrong.  But, don't think this is some health food sorta thing cause it's not really that!

column9: Not too crunchy, not too sweet
column10: This is a nice combination of not too sweet and not too crunchy. I was hoping to find a granola that had a little interest without boring me to death, and one which has some good healthy aspects to it.I love the touch of chocolate...it adds flavor without going overboard and I believe that chocolate is good for you !!! I like it !!

column9: perfect balance of sweet and crunch
column10: Loved this! Surprisingly the chocolate bits are not overwhelmingly sweet like most other granola mixes. The crunch and chocolate flavor blend in a perfect mix. Great with my yogurt for a healthy mid day pick-me-up.

column9: Tasty chocolate, but not much else.
column10: I found the actual granola part to be rather bland, though I did enjoy the crunchy texture. The chocolate part is delicious in contrast to the granola. They are little chunks of good quality dark chocolate. I eat it because I have it, but it's not something I would seek to purchase.The ingredients are mostly natural and consist of whole grains for extra fiber and nutrients. However, as with most granolas, there is a notable amount of fat (6g per 50g serving) and sugar (14g) and calories (210).INGREDIENTS: WHOLE GRAIN ROLLED OATS, EVAPORATED CANE JUICE, SEMI-SWEET CHOCOLATE CHIPS (SUGAR, CHOCOLATE LIQUEUR, DEXTROSE, COCOA BUTTER, SOY LECITHIN), BROWN RICE FLOUR, BROWN RICE SYRUP, EXPELLER PRESSED SAFFLOWER OIL, MOLASSES, VITAMIN E (A NATURAL VITAMIN TO HELP PRESERVE FLAVOR), NATURAL FLAVOR.

Very chocolaty.  My daughter loved this and consistently asks for it for her mid-afternoon snack she goes directly for the chocolate pieces! I like it because I can get my chocolate fix and feel fuller faster because of the oatmeal and grains it contains.  I can actually eat the recommended serving size of 1/2 cup and feel satisfied.

This product is an alternative to eating granola bars. The only downside is that portion control is easy with a granola bar, whereas once you start eating this product out of the bag it is difficult not only to stop, but also to gauge how much you have eaten unless you first scoop out what you want, put it onto a plate, and weigh it on a food scale-- which I doubt most people will do.This is very tasty, and is about the same calories as a granola bar for a similar portion. While some of the pieces are chunks, other pieces are single granola flakes or chips, though this did not really bother me.Much as I like this, since it is not superior in taste to the chocolate chip granola bars that I eat, and since it is just too easy to eat a large portion, for now I will stick with my granola bars. But if portion control is not a concern, then this is a great snack.

The back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola was better tasting than I had expected. The dark chocolate is delicious and the granola is good tasting too. It is a bit difficult to eat out of the bag because it is broken up fairly small. This is a good thing for younger kids, but as an adult I would like bigger clumps. It is a bit on the dry side, but what granola product isn't. There seems to be a nice mix of the granola to chocolate. I found a couple of large clumps of chocolate and claimed them as mine before anybody else in the house could get them. ;) It makes a nice, quick, snack. It would be nice to take on the go, but I wouldn't take it along if it was too warm because the chocolate would probably melt and make a mess. My 10 year old came along and grabbed a handful and a few minutes later came back and asked if they could have some more, so this passes the kid test with me.

While I am enjoying eating the pouch of Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola that I received, I doubt I would order this product again.  The flavor of the chocolate pieces is not as intense as I would like (in terms of my chocolate consumption, I typically eat dark chocolate) and the granola itself is nothing extraordinary.  It's a little drier than many other granolas I've had -- not a bad thing once you put it in a bowl with some milk, but it makes snacking on it out of the bag a little more difficult since the granola pieces are so small.If I could rate this using half stars, I would probably give it 3 1/2.  Since that's not possible, I'll bump up my rating to 4 stars.

column9: Dark Chocolate and Granola - a winning Combo.
column10: I like Granola, I like Chocolate but I have never mixed the two.  Until now.  I have found out that I also like Chocolate Granola. This is a crunchy granola with dark chocolate that is great as a snack right out of the bag or with milk as a breakfast cereal.  The chocolate seems to be a high quality dark (semi-sweet) chocolate that is a nice contrast to the sweet granola.  There is just enough chocolate flavor but it is not overwhelming.

Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is a surprisingly good product.The granola portion is similar to some of the better granola products that I have had before - slightly crunchy, a bit chewy but not overly so, with a mild but pleasant taste of oats.  And though I wasn't sure that the taste of dark chocolate would go well with the granola, it does actually combine with the oats to make a great tasting snack food.  One interesting thing in the ingredients is the lack of honey - apparently Back to Nature uses cane juice instead.  I can't say that I notice any difference in taste because of this difference.The other thing that I noticed is that while not a "low-fat" food, it is lower in fat calories than similar products from other companies, such as Bear Naked All-Natural Granola, Fruit and Nut, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6) and Udi's Original Granola, 13-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6).  On the down side, this back to Nature product has a bit more sugar per serving than the other two products.While agreeing with other's criticism that the small bits make Chocolate Delight Granola a bit messy to eat by hand, it is still a great option as a snack food.  Even my wife (not a chocoholic) gives this product the thumbs-up.  Two thumbs up for me.

I have tried Back to Nature products before and always been a little bit underwhelmed, but this product is pretty good.  The granola is not too sweet, which is perfect, and the dark chocolate chunks are great.I was also pleased by the amount of fiber and whole grains, though the product is also higher in fat (6g) and calories (220 per 1/2 cup).  Another plus, I could pronounce all of the ingredients.Unfortunately, the bag contained mostly crumbles, so it may have been better eaten with a spoon than by hand.  I'm not sure if putting the snack in a box would have been any better at maintaining the larger clusters of snack or not.  (After all, my Kashi Go Lean Crunch cereal has nice clusters on the top and a bunch of tiny crumbles otherwise.)I could see taking this snack on a trip, as the bag size is not overwhelming and has a reclosable zipper top.

column9: Wow - I Could Actually Like This!
column10: Finally a snack that "appears" healthy that I can get into!Although I find the chocolate not to be to my liking (it seems to be dark chocolate), it does add a strong enough flavor as to reduce the blandness of the granola.Don't be fooled however by the packaging.  While it may contain natural products, it's high in fat content, carbohydrates, sugars, etc. (1/2 cup equally about 4 points in the Weight Watchers program)If your not concerned about the health content but products use to produce, then this is a great product!

I think this is a great product. The granola is toasty, lightly sweetened  and does not have the raw oat flavor that many do. The dark chocolate chunks are good quality and there are plenty of them so you really get a big chocolate flavor in every bite. It is great from the bag, with milk or yogurt and was also fabulous in my favorite granola cookie recipe.1/2 cup serving:220 caloriesfat 6gcholesterol 0mgsodium 5mgpotassium 160mgcarbohydrate 37gfiber 4gsugars 13gprotein 5g

column4: Nicki Heskin "Editor, Early Childhood and Bre...
column10: This is a fine product.  I think if it had more complexity of flavors, it might be worth the price.  But if this was something more than just an occasional treat, I'd recommend going to a health food store and buying bulk plain whole grain granola and adding dark chocolate chunks.That said, it is good.  The chocolate is tasty, with the granola and alone.  The kids like it, but I don't really want to give it to them because they get messy fingers from the chocolate.Instead of the little pieces of chocolate and the loose granola, I think this would have been better and less messy as clusters.  By the end of the bag, it was so broken up it needed to be eaten with a spoon.I wouldn't exactly call this "healthy" just because of the nature of granola and chocolate, but it is refreshing not to have it filled with junk and preservatives.  Back to Nature products are generally reliable about that.  I think it alternate flavors, I might be more enamored with this product.

column9: Yummy with a bit of sinful delight!
column10: Ordered these because I mistakenly thought they were granola "bars" but am pleasantly surprised with this "plain" old granola.  What saves this from being just "plain" old granola is the semi-sweet dark chocolate chunks.  If you enjoy dark chocolate then you will love the taste that combines with the granola clusters.I love to munch on it while watching television.  My 6 year old also loves having a little baggie as a healthy snack.  Very tasty, high quality steel cut oats that is sweetened with only natural ingredients.For any individuals with allergies the product contains soy and milk and is manufactured on equipment that processes wheat.Highly recommend this product and even more so because it provides 28g of whole grain in a 1/2 cup serving.  Awesome!

The dark chocolate chips are a perfect match to the light and crunchy granola. This leads to "just right" flavor out of the bag as a standalone snack. It also makes for a perfect topping for vanilla ice cream. This is big hit in my household. 5g of protein per 1/2 cup serving is a plus.

Back To Nature's Chocolate Delight Granola is so chocolatey it was almost too much for me. I definitely prefer it as a snack, not a breakfast food, it was just too sweet for breakfast. The good thing is, the sweetness and the chocolate meant I didn't need a very big serving to satisfy my sweet tooth. I tried it both as a traditional cereal with milk as well as out of hand as a snack. I think I enjoyed having a handful for a snack the best. It's your basic granola of sweetened oat clusters plus chunks of semi-sweet chocolate. The cereal must have a dusting of cocoa on it too since the milk turned kind of chocolatey when poured over it.Marketed as delicious, simple and wholesome (which it may well be) one should not get the idea that it's either low fat or low calorie. A 1/2 cup serving is 220 calories and 6 grams of total fat (2 grams of saturated fat) and mostly sweetened with "evaporated cane juice" (um, that's essentially sugar with a euphemistic name and some trace minerals) so it still needs to remain in the "treat" category.

The taste of this granola is so delicious, by itself, in some milk or , (my favorite), over ice cream! The oats are light and crunchy. The dark chocolate is in perfect balance to the granola. It gives a nice sweet taste, without being too overwhelmingly sweet.Back to Nature has it right, it is a delight to eat, and I will happily do so!

This is not a complicated granola:  Whole grain rolled oats & dark chocolate.  The chocolate is little bitty chunks and since dark chocolate is the latest "health food" you don't feel too guilty.  Its mostly oats.  Its pleasantly sweet, not overpowering.  No preservatives, no hydrogenated oils, and no high fructose corn syrup.  Good snack.

column4: Lisa M. Hendey "Mom, Blogger, Podcaster, Author"
column9: So Tasty but a Bit Messy
column10: I really enjoyed the taste and texture of the Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola.  The granola clusters are good and not overly sweet and the chocolate is more a hint than an overpowering ingredient.  I'm not sure that I would eat this for breakfast (it feels a bit decadent with 1/2 cup for 200 calories), but it's the perfect treat for an afternoon snack or in place of desert.  If your watching calories, carefully measure your portions as this is so tasty that it'd be easy to eat the whole bag in one sitting.The only fault I found with this product was that some of the chocolate in the sample I received was melted and stuck to the sides of the bag, making it a bit messy if you're an "eat from the bag" granola consumer like my husband.A tasty treat - would definitely recommend!

Plain and simple, this is pretty generic tasting granola. I've had tons of different types/brands of granola and this one ranks right in the middle of the pack.The chocolate isn't sweet, which is perfect. Milk chocolate in granola just doesn't stand up to the hearty/nutty taste of the oats and grains. The chocolate came melted in my bag (go figure...), so I just tossed it in the freezer and the chocolate pieces firmed right up.Overall this is a pretty tasty treat just that for the price I'll stick to my plain granola and adding my own dark or semi sweat chocolate pieces to it. Tastes the same if not better then this.Pros:No additives/preservatives.Quality ingredients.Chocolate isn't super sweet (which I think is a pro, some might see it as a con).Cons:Price.Is pretty generic tasting, nothing extraordinary.High in calories, but what granola isn't?

The Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is delicious.Texture: Crunchy and yet breaks down immediately as you chew - you don't feel like you'll ruin your dental work or that your jaw is going to be sore after a bowl.Sweetness: The granola itself is lightly sweetened without any fructose or high fructose corn syrup. They used cane juice, brown rice syrup, and molasses as sweeteners.Chocolate Chunks: I love chocolate and can be a little picky about it. This is very good quality chocolate. This surprised me. It is not too sweet and has just a touch of nutty bitterness to make the flavor linger without being offensive to those who like a more mellow chocolate.The only reason I gave this 4 stars is for the folks who don't like the chocolate to be so strong. The flavor really lingers. I love that. Some folks may not. And, some may not see it as breakfast food. Even so it will make an awesome snack.

I received this granola through the Amazon Vine program, and I'm very glad that I chose it.  As soon as I popped the bag open, and took a whiff of the content, I could tell that this granola was very fresh and going to be delicious.  I was certainly right; the first thing I did was pour some into my hand.  The rolled granola held together tightly and there were large chunks of chocolate mixed in.  I put the handful in my mouth and ate it dry, very good!  The granola has a very natural taste it, and was absolutely delicious.  The sweetness of the chocolate enhanced it and made for a very pleasant experience.  Next I poured some into a cup with some nice cold milk and took a spoonful, again delicious.  This granola can be eaten as a snack, a cereal or a dessert, amazingly versatile and just as tasty to boot.

column9: Is it a snack or breakfast cereal?
column10: When I ordered this from Amazon the description said "heavenly snack" so I had it sent to the office instead of home (the kids might make short work of it at home and I'd never see it).  But rather than being like "clusters" of granola it looks more like the Sweet Home brand of granola CEREAL we buy from the grocery store - except for those chocolate chunks.  But I tried it and it's pretty good, except there's so many little pieces and try as I might, it ended up getting all over my desk and lap.  The taste is fine but it's a bit messy, so I figured it must not be a snack.I took it home and tried it for breakfast.  It's not bad but I'm not used to eating cereal with chunks of chocolate (and I'm a big chocolate fan, dark chocolate, too - I even love chocolate chip bagels).  My 6 year old daughter, who loves granola cereal and almost always has it for breakfast, took one look at the chocolate chunks and declined.So I'm not quite sure what this product is: snack or cereal.  It's too messy for a snack but the chocolate is a bit much for cereal (to my taste anyway).  Calories are higher than the Sweet Home brand of cereal we usually buy (220 vs 200 for a half cup serving - the Sweet Home brand uses honey and almonds) but calories from fat were lower (50 compared to 60).  It's okay but I'll stick with the grocery store brand.

BACK TO NATURE CHOCOLATE DELIGHT GRANOLA is most definitely a tasty treat.  Containing whole grain rolled oats and dark chocolate chunks, CHOCOLATE DELIGHT GRANOLA is an extremely pleasing blend of crunchy and sweet.  This cereal is chock full of chocolaty goodness and will satisfy any chocolate-lover's sweet tooth.  The crunch holds up extremely well, even in milk.  I had a bowl (at the recommended serving size) this morning for breakfast, and found it to be quite filling, as well as delicious.I also gave a bowl of CHOCOLATE DELIGHT GRANOLA to my 4 year old daughter.  "Mommy," she said, "this tastes like chocolate chip cookies!  Chocolate chip cookies cereal!"  She dove right in, and finished the entire bowl.  High praise coming from a picky eater.  And I have the comfort of knowing that it is made from all natural ingredients and doesn't contain artificial flavors, trans fat, preservatives, hydrogenated oils, cholesterol, or high fructose corn syrup.  BACK TO NATURE CHOCOLATE DELIGHT GRANOLA is also an excellent source of whole grains and fiber, something we could all use more of.I have to say, I agree with what it says on the bag.  BACK TO NATURE CHOCOLATE DELIGHT GRANOLA is simple ingredients, simply delicious, and simply good.  Surprisingly so.

column9: chewy and totally chocolate -- dark chocolate
column10: Its not too sweet, doesn't have nuts (I'm trying to avoid nuts while I am nursing)  and its chocolate heaven.  Really good dark chocolate chunks, and not messed up with cinnamon etc which I don't care for if you have really good chocolate.  Its pretty filling, and really satisfying at the suggested serving size of 1/2 cup.

With granola, it's usually a trade-off between taste and health, and Back to Nature Chocolate Delight is no exception, delivering only moderately on both counts.By using different kinds of sugars, the ingredient label looks better, but added up, it's still a lot of sugar.  With 13g of sugar per 50g (1/2 cup), this granola is almost one-fourth sugar:  evaporated cane juice, brown rice syrup, molasses, sugar, and dextrose.  Back to Nature isn't the worst in this regard, but if you want to minimize your sugar intake (and everyone should, of course), be aware of what you're eating.The fat content is also moderate for a granola, 6g in the form of safflower oil.The taste is okay; I didn't find it to be outstanding.  And the granola pieces are extremely hard and overly crunchy (which I didn't like).  However, my eight-year-old daughter loved this granola and would be delighted if I got it all the time (the chocolate chips, though not particularly tasty, in my opinion, were a big hit with her).This granola is worth trying if it sounds like it might suit your preferences, but try to get a single pack of it from a local store to try before committing to a big multipack.

column9: Good but too sweet for cereal
column10: I have always loved granola cereal and I have always loved chocolate so putting the two together seemed like a dream!  I have to admit, I like this but it is much too sweet for my breakfast desires.  Granola alone is sweet so adding chocolate would obviously make it even sweeter.  However, I was surprised at just how sweet it was.  I could not eat it as cereal.  Instead, I used a handful to manage the occasional sweet urge.  While good, I am not sure it is worth the price.  It would be cheaper and equally as good to add chocolate chips to plain granola if desired.  While I enjoyed this as a sweet snack, I will not be purchasing it in the future.

Overall, I like the way this granola tastes. It has a good ratio of granola-to-chocolate, and the chocolate tastes good. It doesn't taste cheap, and it's not too sweet.Unfortunately it melts pretty quickly to the touch, so this can be a messy to eat with your hands. (It's worth pointing out that the bag was in a hot car before I tried some, but I still had this problem even after it cooled to room temperature.)The granola itself is a bit dry, unlike more honey coated brands, and the pieces don't stick together that well. So, after the big chunks are gone, you're left with lots of tiny bits that are messy to pick up. I suppose this wouldn't be a problem if you like your granola in cereal or yogurt, instead of trail mix.Even though it's healthy, I wouldn't recommend this product (or any granola) for mindless snacking. Just 1/2 a cup contains 220 calories, which in my opinion is a lot for a snack. On the plus side, it's great for a hiking food or a quick pick-me-up.

column9: They should call it Brownie Granola
column10: The chocolate in it is that good.  Most of the time when you get granola or trail mix with chocolate, it is cheap-tasting milk chocolate bits.  Along with that, the chocolate is decent sized, no mini morsels, nice little chunks of dark chocolate.  The granola is pretty good, too.  It gets a little lost in the taste of the chocolate.  Its great the way it is, but I would love it if they made this with almonds or nuts of some sort in it and it would be the ultimate snack.  This is going to go by the handful, no yogurt topping for this stuff.  Although, ice cream would be amazing...yum

I'm a big proponent of eating chocolate for breakfast...or any other time.  Let's face it, chocolate is sooo delicious and has some health benefits too.  It's a mystery why there aren't more chocolate filled breakfast cereals.  Well thankfully, Back to Nature Chocolate Delights Granola fits the bill to a T, whatever that means.This cereal has the exact balance of granola, chocolate and sugar that I've always dreamed of.  Plus, you won't find any yucky corn syrup.  The ingredients are all top notch (though I would have preferred more molasses and less evaporated cane sugar).  The chocolate chunks are outstanding.  They are the perfect shape and size and melt in your mouth, not in the bowl.  This is the first chocolate cereals I've seen that doesn't turn your milk brown!  I was blown away.As I said, the cereal is balanced, so it's not too sweet for breakfast.  It will likely appeal to the more refined adult chocolate lover as well as any kid.  I had only two gripes - (1) the granola is a little too loose with little pieces to eat easily straight out of the bag.  (2) it has a moderate to high sog factor when left in milk.

After trying Back to Nature's cereal and being completely satisfied, I decided to see what their snack food held in store for me.Now I know: it's a bunch of chocolate and granola goodness!First Impressions:The bag was taunting me from the get-go, the transparent leaf showed all the oats and chocolate - like it was just waiting for me to start eating!On the back, there's the mission statement of Back to Nature - they make a point to mention that this snack doesn't have any artificial preservatives, colors or flavors.Appearance and Nutrition:There was no shortage of chocolate chunks or granola in the bag. According to the Nutrition Facts, there were seven servings...I had to work very hard to limit myself to just one serving for the review! I was quite pleased to see the bag was reseal-able - nothing like a longer shelf life for those future snack fests!In one serving there are about 220 calories. No trans fat, 2g of saturated fat, no cholesterol, and the sodium comes in quite low at 5mg. If you need carbohydrates, there's 37g per serving, so look no further.Taste:Back to Nature has done it again...this is absolutely DELECTABLE. Amazon sells these in 6-packs and the price is right! The chocolate chunks are very sweet and tasty, and the granola is a perfect match.My sweet tooth and his 31 neighbors agree - if you're looking for snacks without the additives, Back to Nature is the way to go.Enjoy!

column9: Good trail snack or TV snack
column10: My girlfriend complained that the packaging didn't open the way it should have and she needed to use a scissors, but other than that, we both enjoyed the fresh-tasting snack made with natural ingredients. The mix is of course loaded with carbs, which could be a good thing (trail) or bad (TV) depending. The taste and amount of the semi-sweet chocolate chips is probably what sets this apart from other granoloa snacks, so if you like the idea of chocolate in your crunchy granola, then get it. Oh..it's also great mixed with yogurt, keeping its crunch throughout.

column4: Mary Jo Sminkey "15 years of Amazon Reviews!"
column9: Maybe not the healthiest snack....but sure tastes great!
column10: I am definitely a chocolate lover, and fond of granola as a cereal so thought I'd try a bag of this, even though it isn't necessarily meant as a cereal. I think it would be a bit hard to eat as a snack, as the granola is fairly crumbly and not in large chunks. The chocolate as well is separate from the granola so hard to just eat from the bag. As a cereal, it tastes amazing! I probably would have liked a little *less* chocolate just so I didn't feel so much like I was eating candy, but I can't fault the taste at all, it really had a great blend of granola crunch, a bit of sweetness, and that semi-sweet chocolate taste that blended perfectly. Definitely not something I would eat everyday, but for a mid-day snack with milk, I really loved it.

column9: Tasty and with good quality ingredients.
column10: I do have a soft spot for chocolate, but I like something a little more sophisticated than, say cocoa puffs, not to mention a little more nutritious.  I've tried Special K Chocolatey Delight, which I liked, but I have this habit of occasionally checking the nutrition facts. I found out why they call it "chocolatey" rather than "chocolate."  The bits in the Special K are mostly sugar and partially hydrogenated oil.  That cereal is also sweetened with high fructose corn syrup and preserved with BHT.  It has some other added vitamins, but I don't really understand the benefit of adding those to cereal vs. just taking a supplement if needed, or better yet eating more foods that contain them naturally.In comparison, I see that this granola has "real" chocolate chunks, is sweetened with evaporated cane juice and brown rice syrup, contains no trans-fatty acids, and uses only vitamin E as a preservative.  It also has 4g fiber per serving, vs. 1g.  That doesn't magically turn it into health food, in fact this granola has more total sugar and fat per serving that the Special K, but given the choice between the two it still clearly wins on ingredient quality.As for the taste, I like it.  It's simple, without too much going on, and it's sweet enough to satisfy the sweet tooth without going overboard.
