The amount of chocolate is just about right as well; enough to find some in most every bite.Overall I'd say it's a pretty good choice to stifle a morning chocolate craving as long as you stick to a reasonably sized serving.  I'll almost certainly be getting some more, especially if I find it on sale.

Given the "Back to Nature" brand and the marketing material printed all over this package, you would think you were eating health food.  Unfortunately, that is not the case.  Sure, it has lots of whole grains and no artificial ingredients, but this is a high calorie, high fat food.  Admittedly, it is incredibly yummy, and my wife and I struggled to stay out of the bag.  Since my wife has a nut allergy, we were happy to find that this granola is free of nuts and is NOT produced in a facility that also processes nuts.  If taste were the only criteria, this granola would get 5 stars.  However, as granola, I believe it ought to be a little healthier.  In my mind, this is a great alternative to junk food, but it isn't for the extremely health conscious consumer.

"Quaker" is to granola is what "Kleenex" is to facial tissue. Quaker granola tastes so good that it's almost impossible to stop eating it. In the marketplace, it's the 800-pound gorilla of granolas."Back to Nature" granola is, by comparison, bland. It doesn't taste bad, it just isn't very exciting. The (good-tasting) chocolate bits don't help. If anything, they distract from the taste of the granola.And it's expensive. If you want chocolate on your granola, just throw some bittersweet morsels on it.I can imagine a cartoon commercial for this product, with tie-dyed teens chanting its praises. ("CHOC-late-bits granola -- yum yum yum") What's next -- sugar-frosted acid flakes?

I would caution anyone ordering this to realize that the chocolate melts in warm temperatures.  Mine arrived in a chocolate coated bag.  I put it in the fridge to try to solidify it a bit, but it wasn't a big improvement.  Makes it hard to eat out of the bag.  I really didn't want a chocolate flavored cereal, so I was planning on enjoying this as an eat out of the bag snack, but the melted chocolate makes it messy.  The chunks are an okay size for that, but it would probably work better as a cereal since the chocolate melted.When I purchase granola, I usually look for ones with either almonds or pecans.  This has neither. The only solids listed in the ingredients are whole grain rolled oats and chocolate chunks (first 2 ingredients). The rest of the ingredients are predominately sweeteners.  A serving is 1/2 cup and that has 220 calories, 50 of which are from fat.  There are 4g of fiber, 13g of sugar, 20g of other carbohydrates, and 5g of protein.  Just because something is "natural" doesn't mean it is good for you.

column9: Tasty and crunchy but could be improved.
column10: I can't really add too much to the other reviews; I received the product yesterday, and immediately tore into the bag.  From the first mouthful, it was clear this is a tasty product.  As someone who likes granola anyway, and who is a chocoholic (especially dark chocolate), it was a winner.  The only real complaint (and it's a minor one) is the fact that it's too crumbly.  As someone else noted, bigger chunks would be an improvement.  It was a bit difficult to scoop out without dropping some (although my cats liked to pounce on the pieces as they hit the floor).  Given this, it probably is better served being added to yogurt or sprinkled on fruit.  All in all, this is a really good product.

column9: Tasty & Crunchy with a good balance of chocolate to cereal but a bit crumbly
column10: Like most Back to Nature products, this is every bit as tasty as it sounds from the description.  The Granola has a nice crunch to it and the dark chocolate tastes rich and decadent. I'd give it five stars if the product weren't so darn crumbly.  Other reviewers have stated that would have liked to see this product produced more as crunchy large clusters and I agree with them.  Over half the bag was reduced to single oat pieces and crumbles of chocolate buy the time it reached me.  That may be a result of the packaging choice to put it in a pouch rather than a box.  it's hard to tell.Even so, the crumbly nature didn't alter my enjoyment of the product too much.  It goes nicely into vanilla yogurt as a stir -in and works equally well straight out of the bag as a snack.  My husband told me he thought the molasses used as a sweetener stood out a bit too much but I didn't think so.  The product is a little on the sweet side but certainly not as sweet as most cereals available today.Highly recommended item but buy with Auto-ship to get the best possible price.

column9: Good taste, but needs more clumps
column10: I love the granola taste and the touch of chocolate is just right.  It would have been nice if it came out in clumps but at least the bag we received was evenly distributed.  That is nice for cereal but not ideal for granola.But that is a minor issue easily solved by pouring out what I wanted into a bowl rather than eating from the bag.  Doing the latter gets kind of messy.

When I saw all those chocolate chunks in Back To Natures Granola I got a little too excited.  I love me some chocolate and when it is in granola I can only imagine the orgasmic experience in my mouth.  I am sad to report that no orgasmic experience was to be had.  Upon first bite I noticed a great crunch but the flavor of the granola by itself almost had a raw taste to it, like a raw flour/oat taste and it was very off putting. Not at all sweet and that could be a plus for someone who is trying to not eat too much sugar but I need my granola to have some sort of sweetness to it which this granola did not have.  I had some of the chocolate in the mix and that by itself was very delicious but not worth the cost of the granola, will just get a chocolate bar.  I much prefer the Love Crunch Granola By Natures Path, that is absolutly scrumptious and has the perfect amount of chocolate flavor and pieces along with freeze dried berries, plus it is all organic.  So if you are looking for a nice flavorful granola that has nice chocolate goodness look elsewhere because you will not get that with this granola.

I normally don't buy these products...but when I do, unfortunately I don't know when to stop consuming them.I love chocolate, but not granola.  However, the combination makes for an interesting taste.  The sweetness of the chocolate is offset by the granola.The way this product comes, are you supposed to eat it out of the bag as a snack, or put it in a bowl like cereal?  Here is where a chocolate/granola bar would be better. With the bag, you open it, and eat and eat until you ate too much.  A wrapped bar is a finite portion.Would I buy this again? I wish I didn't have to buy a 6 pack.  One pouch would suffice..for both my wallet and my waist.

column9: Excellent granola, love the chocolate instead of raisins!
column10: I'm picky about granola and don't like when there are too many flavors going on (with lots of added nuts, raisins, dates, cranberries, etc) so I really loved this granola which is plain with just chocolate pieces.  Not too sweet and I also like the fact that the granola has plenty of clusters (also don't like "loose" granola.  No "junk" ingredients which is very important to me.  I would recommend this cereal even for snacking-good to keep in the car for when you don't have time to eat and are needing a little something to tie you over until lunch or dinner.  Good product!

column9: A look at the ingredients -- I'll stick with muesli
column10: I'm a muesli eater who tries a granola every once in a while to see if I've changed my mind and decided I like it any better. Like other granolas, this one did not convince me to switch. My basic gripe about granolas is that they get that crunchiness from sugars. That's true here as well, although the sugars have fancier names -- plus you have chocolate added.The ingredients of this product are as follows: whole grain rolled oats, semi-sweet chocolate chunks (chocolate, sugar, dextrose, cocoa butter, etc), evaporated cane juice, brown rice syrup, brown rice flour, expeller pressed safflower oil, molasses, vitamin E (to preserve flavor), natural flavor.I'm not a health nut, but since I really enjoy muesli more anyway, I guess I still don't see much of a reason to switch to granola. I'm glad I tried this product, but it seemed pretty much like a typical granola to me.If you want a chocolaty granola, this could be a great product for you.

column9: Not bad... but it's mostly just granola... I expected more
column10: When I saw this yummy sounding chocolate granola, I thought it sounded great!  Well, it is just that, chocolate granola that is!  Nothing fancy, but it's still tasty. I guess I was disappointed nonetheless though... I was expecting a bit more creativity I suppose.

This will be a short review, because there's not much to say.  All there is to say, is this: Back To Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is pretty tasty and made a good munching treat.The chocolate bits in it aren't high quality confection, but they're better than, say, the waxy chocolate bits you might normally get in a grocery-aisle chocolate chip granola bar. The wheat and such comes in small, flaky bits (I might have preferred slightly larger nuggets), and it's very dusty, so keep a dry towel on hand.  I also appreciated that it came in a resealable bag, so I could just keep in in a drawer at my work desk without needing a separate container.

If you like granola and dark chocolate, you'll love this.  It doesn't say on the package if it's a cereal or snack.  I just ate it as a snack.  When I received and opened it I noticed something else in the bag.  I just assumed it was a coupon or pamphlet about the product.  I ignored it and left it in there.  After a couple of days and several handfuls I pulled it out.  To my dismay it was the top part of the bag from another package!  It looks like someone ripped open a package of back to Nature and just threw their trash into this one.  Q.C. at this plant is obviously needed!Good taste, but what else will you find in your bag?

Yes, it's tasty.  Yes it's convenient to eat.  And as it's filling, you don't need to ingest a lot of calories just to satisfy that quick craving.  But in all honesty, take a look at the ingredients list and you'll find a few recognizable components and a lot of what I'll term "chemistry class" ingredients.  That kind of contracticts the image of the Back to Nature concept.Still all in all, if you like processed granola, this is very tasty.  I'm just not sure that you're gaining anything (or losing any inches) by making a product like this part of your regular diet.

column9: Granola the entire Family Will Eat Yeah!!!!!
column10: This granola has a great chocolate taste.  Although not organic, there are no freaky ingredients. No artificial preservatives,flavors, or colors.  Whole grain too.  Absolutely no high fructose corn syrup.  Finally a granola that appeals to those who do not care for dried fruit or nuts.  I like all types of granola.  This is the only granola my family was willing to try, liking it from the very start.Your family will enjoy snacking on this.

column9: My wife's favorite, but second place for me
column10: First off, I must say that my wife absolutely feel in LOVE with this granola. I almost didn't get to have a taste of our first bag before it was gone! She would easily rate it 5 stars, but needless to say I have my own opinion.Being a bit of a chocolate granola snob, I have to compare the flavor and texture of this granola to that of KASHI COCOA BEACH GRANOLA and Cascadian Farm Cereal, Dark Chocolate Almond, Organic, 13.25-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10), my long-time favorite. I have enjoyed all three as both a snack and a meal, usually with milk.Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is more enjoyable than the Kashi as both a snack or as a meal. The flavor of the Kashi can be a bit too generic, and this granola just tastes healthier and more natural. As a snack, my only complaint is the amount of small bits that are hard to snack on. Perhaps my wife got all the large morsels before she let me have a taste, but I do feel there should be more uniformity for best enjoyment. This is not as important in a bowl, of course.I enjoyed a medium sized bowl with milk, but this is where the Cascadian Farms granola takes it a step further. I ALWAYS want a second bowl of Cascadian Farms because it just tastes so good, but here I didn't find myself going back for more. While this does lead me to rate this granola just below my personal favorite, it might be a positive point as others trying to lose weight (such as myself) are less likely to give in to the urge for "just one more bowl".

column9: A so-so granola that'll please those who enjoy chocolate chips
column10: Back To Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is an okay granola cereal.  But it didn't have anything that really struck a chord with me,  It's a rather ordinary granola with some chocolate chips thrown in.  Nothing less, nothing more.  On the plus side it wasn't stale and it has a fresh taste to it.  If you're a big granola connoisseur then you'll enjoy it,  The casual granola eater wont be so pleased.

I enjoy granola and trail mix products, but I found this very hard to chew and hard on the teeth. About halfway through the bag I decided to use it as a cereal and it was good that way. I wouldnt buy it for that use though, too expensive. Very hard to chew dry!

column9: Sure has a lot of chocolate
column10: Some products these days have you wondering where's the chocolate, but not this one. I can say that it has plenty of chocolate chunks mixed in with the granola. I used it as cereal. I did like the taste, but it got pretty soft in the milk, except for those plentiful chocolate chunks. When mixed with milk you need something with the granola they used to perk it up and that's where the chocolate comes in.

I've been eating this granola with vanilla soy milk.It's absolutely delicious!Just sweet engough with the wonderful dark chocolate in it, I don't feel like I'm eating a healthy breakfast, even though I am.I will definately be purchasing this granola.  Loved it.

Sometimes a food doesn't have to be complicated to be good.When I saw this granola only had sweetened oats and chocolate chunks, my first thought was "that sounds boring."  But after I got the first handful in my mouth, I changed my mind completely.  Two tastes bouncing off each other perfectly, with the added bonus of no artificial ingredients.  A great healthy snack.

My title says it all.  I thoroughly enjoyed this "Chocolate Delight" granola -- as did my wife and my oldest daughter.  It's not too sweet (a problem with many granola products) and the small chunks of dark chocolate were perfect.  I have to admit -- my sample bag didn't last very long!  (The last portion topped my dish of vanilla ice cream last night!)Very highly recommended!!!

column4: M. Jobbagy "Follow Your Bliss - Joseph Cambell"
column10: I liked this product, for a couple of reasons.One is it's all natural. We get no preservatives, or corn syrup processed in any of it's many incarnations. We get oats, and chocolate. And who doesn't think chocolate should be one of the major food groups?? It's dark chocolate to boot, so not full of sugar and sweeteners that we don't need.The other reason I like it is that it isn't too sweet. It's definitely not a cheap bag of 'trailmix' from those major stores that's full of candy, dried sugar covered fruit mixed in with some nuts and oats perhaps. The only sweeteners I could find on the label were molasses, evaporated cane juice, and brown rice syrup. The semi sweet dark chocolate has some sugar in it, but that's ok, sugar is natural, as long as you don't make it one of the primary ingredients.A nice healthy and tasty snack food, that's what you'll find here. I don't think the kids will be too disappointed in the taste, it does have chocolate after all.

I don't usually use a lot of milk in my cereal because I don't want to waste it (it goes to the cat--I know, bad cat owner!) I haven't drained the milk from a bowl of cereal since I outgrew Cookie Crisp (mmm. Cookie Crisp)...this was so good I drank it all.First the con and the reason for the four instead of five star review: price. 12 oz. for 3.60 (plus shipping on Amazon) or 3.79 in my grocery is out of line. Comparable products offer 17 or 18 oz. for the same or a slightly lower price. So Kraft (and yes, it's a Kraft product) lower the price to get another star.The rest is all pro. The mouth feel is perfect; as the uploader of the customer photo states, not big bad chunks. Nice and crunchy in cold milk. The flavour is fantastic. DARK chocolate...not milk. Yum. Plus just the right amount of little choc pieces. Others criticised the Summer Berry Blend variety for being too sweet (others too tart,) but I found it and this just right on the sweetness scale.4g of fiber, low sodium, 5g of protein...and a couple vitamins all natural. No HFCS, no Sucralose or Aspartame so your liver and brain don't need to fear it either!Notice I didn't mention the calories...220 in a "serving" welll, a 1/2 cup serving size is a wee bit unrealistic. I measured it out and it's about five bites. A cup was good for a light breakfast...so 440 calories about the same as a bagel...not for weight watchers--but an excellent treat!

column9: Quite possibly my new favorite food
column10: Who doesn't love granola?  Adding dark chocolate to it is possibly the best thing a chocolate lover could imagine although you must use caution in eating this because it is definitely a snack.  Granola always has fat and of course chocolate does too, but it is a good alternative to a candy bar.  It has more nutritional value since it does contain whole grain and several vitamins and minerals.  The flavor is as satisfying as a candy bar and granola is pleasing as a snack because it is easy to munch on.  Overall A+!The pros:~The flavor is amazing!  I loved it!  It reminded me of a candy bar but more satisfying.~It is easy to munch on making it great for a snack.  It is packaged in a reselable plastic bag.~It is more nutritious than many snack foods on the market.  It has quite a bit of fiber in addition to other beneficial vitamins and minerals making it more nutritious than many "junk" foods.The cons:-The chocolate melted a little during shipping. Although it wasn't completely melted, some of the chocolate melted before I opened it.-Granola still contains fat no matter how you cut it.  Although more nutritious than many things, this granola contains 6g of fat per serving.-The bags are hard to open.  The tear here strip resulted in me searching for a pair of scissors to actually open the position.If you are looking for a great choclately snack, you will love Chocolate Delight Granala from Back to Nature.

column9: Delicious with a capital "D"...but Expensive wtih a capital "E"
column10: The good folks at "Back to NATURE" have put together an absolutely scrumptious granola offering.  It's so good that you can sit there with the open bag and snack on it handful after handful.  The granola is heavily punctuated with chunks of real dark chocolate.I wanted to try more of this before it was gone, but before I knew it my family had discovered and devoured the entire bag...and that's a good sign!I could also see adding nuts, perhaps almonds or cashews, maybe some M&Ms, and before you know it you'll have a super-fantastic trail mix...good for hiking or camping.  It's the sort of thing you could send out the door with your teenagers and be happy knowing that they are getting something that is good, and good for them.At the same time, this treat may deserve to be stashed away in your secret place for those times when you need something great for yourself.  Perhaps this granola is too good for kids to wolf down before they realize what they had.  You'll have to make the call on this one :-)Now why doesn't this product get 5-stars, with all that glowing praise?It's like this...this granola is pricey, pricey, and expensive!!!  That's the only reason this product misses out on the 5-star mark (at least for me).  Again, only you can judge whether your budget can handle an item like this."Back to NATURE", thanks for a great tasty treat!

This is gourmet granola with a great chocolate taste.  The chunks of chocolate are actually that: real chunks of quality dark chocolate.  The granola itself is also really good---crunchy and with a great bite.It's not exactly health food, but a small handful makes a great snack between meals.

I love granola...in both bar and crumbled form.  So I jumped at the chance to try this Chocolate Delight Granola.  Long story short, it tastes great.  If you like chocolate and granola, you'll like this (that isn't really saying much is it).However, my major problem with granola of any kind is that it isn't particularly healthy.  Don't get me wrong...it isn't like going out and eating some lard enriched southern breakfast.  But it isn't very low on the calories either.  A single serving of this stuff is about 200 calories...and there are 8 servings per bag.  I don't know about any of you, but 1.5 ounces of tasty granola isn't going to be enough for me :)...especially since it comes in large pouch form.  Suffice it to say that this bag lasted me two morning drives to work...and 800 calories a morning is just a bit too much for me :/

column9: Crunchy, chocolatey, not bad at all
column10: I had doubts about this cereal.  I don't like super-sweet cereals, and I haven't cared for chocolate breakfast food since I got over the Cocoa Krispies craze of my youth.  Therefore, I was pleasantly surprised to find that the chocolate flavor, while definitely present, is not overwhelming, and the sweetness level is tolerable.  Best of all, it reminded me why I used to like Cocoa Krispies - it left the same chocolate milk in my bowl at the end!I compared Chocolate Delight to Post Bran Flakes, a cereal that was recently named a "Best Bite" by Nutrition Action Newsletter.  Both are made primarily of whole grains (oats in the case of the granola, wheat in the bran flakes).  Both contain sweeteners, and as one would expect, the chocolate granola contains more sweetener because it includes chocolate chips.  The flakes have 5 g of fiber in a half-cup serving; the granola, 4.  The bran flakes have much more sodium - 220 mg compared to 5 mg in the granola.  The granola has more carbs (again, the chocolate), but also more protein, 5 g to the flakes' 3 g.  The bran flakes have significantly more vitamin A and iron, but the granola has more calcium (although only 2% of the RDA, not counting any milk added).There is a whopping difference in calories:  for half-cup servings, 100 calories for the bran flakes, 220 calories for the granola.  But hey, no one thinks they can eat chocolate for free, do they?The granola is also more expensive, 30 cents per ounce (assuming Amazon's price and super-saver shipping), 24 cents for the bran flakes (purchased at a non-sale price at a grocery store).  I'm not sure that's a significant difference, though, as most sweetened cereals cost more than unsweetened (it's also debatable whether the bran flakes can be considered "unsweetened," since they contain both sugar and corn syrup).Both cereals are crisp in milk, the granola more so because of its crunchy granola clusters, and the granola maintains its crunch, a plus if you like to dawdle over your breakfast bowl.  I don't tend to eat dry cereal as a snack, but if I did, the granola would certainly be the hands-down winner there.  All in all, I was much more satisfied with Chocolate Delight than I expected to be, and if your taste runs to chocolate for breakfast or granola for snacks, it's worth trying.  (If you like it a lot, note the discount for automatic shipping.)

Ingredients:  Whole grain rolled oats, semi-sweet chocolate chunks, a few natural binders to hold the oat clusters together, and vitamin E as a natural antioxidant/preservative.  Voila.  With 6g of fat (2g saturated) per 1/2 cup, 4g dietary fiber, and a fair amount of various vitamins and minerals, this snack tastes delicious and has some real nutritional value.  Not for low-carbers, of course (37g), but other snackers seeking some positives in their dessert/snack moments will not be disappointed.

column9: Delicious and I always disliked granola
column10: This Chocolate Delight Granola is absolutely scrumptious and the main ingredients are whole grain rolled oats and semi-sweet chocolate chunks.To me this is a five-star product. The only reason I gave it four stars is because it is a calorie dense product since you really need a one-cup serving to be satisfied and that's 440 calories. There are seven half cup servings per package at 220 calories each (50 fat calories).  However, for me this is not enough breakfast or snack per serving so I was only able to get three servings out of the package.

If you like granola and chocolate, this is pretty much a no-brainer. Tastes good and comes in a re-sealable pouchMy only problem with is was that, ordering online, you get the package after its been sitting in the heat and most of the chocolate is melted to the sides of the bag and not in the mix where it should beSo in the future i might just buy this in a store somewhere and take it home in my air conditioned car. If you live somewhere cold, this probably won't even be an issue for you

column9: rated very highly by 4 year olds
column10: Our preschool kids really liked this. They called it "chocolicious" "scrumptioos" and "yummilicious".Many granola products can be hard and hurt the mouth, but this one is just right. And has a very good balance of chocolate.Can be used as a snack or cereal.The bag is nice (reclosable and stands up on its own), but quite hard to open (the tear strip doesn't go evenly and we had to resort to scissors)

This is a good granola.  Some other granolas seem very dry and hard to eat, but this stuff has a nice consistency and the bits of chocolate are just enough to give it a little pop of flavor.  The ingredients are pretty good and simple, with whole grain rolled oats and chocolate chunks as the main ingredients and then a few sweeteners and other stuff to hold it all together.  It also has 5 grams of protein and 4 grams of fiber per serving, so it's pretty filling.  If your looking to try a new granola and like chocolate but don't want a bunch of extra stuff in your food, this is a good choice.

We eat our oats every day, usually as plain boring oatmeal.  What a treat to have chocolate granola for breakfast!  Thinking about it, the combination seems so natural; why didn't I think of it before? Well, even if I had thought of it, I would not have done as good a job as Back To Nature did with the combination.  Not too sweet, not greasy, not overwhelmingly chocolate ... just the right blend of flavor and texture to make this a fair breakfast food or a decent snack.
I'm not a big granola fan, but this stuff is VERY good.  It's not too sweet and not too chocolaty..... a handful is just right for a quick pick-me-up between meals.

If you liked Cookie Crisp cereal as a kid, you'll probably love Back to Nature Chocolate Delight granola as an adult. Yes, the thought of eating chocolate for breakfast might make some people's stomachs turn, but this product is anything but unappetizing. Tasty, not-too-sweet chocolate chunks accent but don't dominate this granola, which - quite fortunately - isn't heavily sweetened otherwise. It's fairly filling and doesn't leave that oily feeling in your mouth that some granolas do. Folks who prefer really toasty oats in their granola might be a little disappointed; this isn't the crunchiest cereal in the breakfast aisle. But for a yummy, healthy breakfast - or, maybe even better, a snack - this granola is worth a try.

column9: Tastes wonderful, makes a great snack.
column10: I really like this cereal. It stays crisp in milk and is sweet, but not to sweet.  It also makes a great snack. I put some in one of those small snack size zip bags and carry it for in between the meal hungries. It meets my sweet tooth need but still has nutritional value, I would recommend this cereal to anyone who wants it as a breakfast or is looking for a more nutritional snack.  The chocolate is real, meaning it tastes wonderful, but also, like all chocolate melts at 98 degrees. If you are having this shipped to a warm climate keep that in mind. Otherwise, I highly recommed this product.

I saw another review that warned against buying this product from Amazon if you live in a hot climate.  I would concur!  My weather is pretty close to what you'd find in Las Vegas and the chocolate had melted all over the place.  I think that was actually nice for what got stuck on the food but a lot of it stuck to the bag and was uneaten chocolate.  In some cultures, uneaten chocolate is one of the seven deadly sins.  So beware!Otherwise, this tasted pretty good.  If you love Granola, you can't go wrong by adding some chocolate to it.  It was a little hard for trail mix but it makes a good breakfast.  I'd say the only ones who shouldn't have this are those who do not like dark chocolate.  If you prefer milk chocolate than this product isn't for you.

Back To Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is a great product, but it could be better.  Specifically, the granola did not have uniform clusters of chocolate.  Some clusters were large and had adequate chocolate coating while others were small and had little or no coating of chocolate.  Because of this I gave the product one less star than I would have had the product been more uniform.  That said the product was otherwise great!  For granola lovers (or even those who don't regularly consume granola) the addition of chocolate is quite clever and actually changes the expected taste and texture of granola.  I decided to try sprinkling the product over top some vanilla ice cream and couldn't believe the wonderful experience.  Adding some walnuts and a little extra Hershey's dark chocolate syrup was incredible.  You can of coarse consume the product straight from the bag, but if you want to stretch the product out over a number of weeks I would recommend using the chocolate granola as a topping of sorts on your favorite desert.  I would highly recommend this product.

These are a great on the go snack.  A great source of fiber (4g per serving) and 5 grams of protein.  Whole grain oats and dark chocolate, what a nice combination.  Best of all, it has no lousy high fructose corn syrup.  I normally try to stay away from dairy, but if I get it by way of chocolate, I'm ok with it.  Plus, it's dark chocolate, oh so nice.To me, these are perfectly sweet, not too sweet and just perfect.  It's a great tasting and healthy addition to anybody's diet.

I must say, this is a very tasty granola.  The pieces are bite size, the chocolate flavor just right and the fact that there are no artificial ingredients, makes it quite a delight to eat.  As a matter of fact, it is so addictive that I ate the whole bag within a day.  A great treat for granola lovers!
The granola is delicious!  It has a good crunch, great chocolate mix and only lightly sweetened.

column9: The word "Chocolate" is first for a reason!
column10: I'm a fan of some Back to Nature products and regularly buy these:Back To Nature Peanut Butter Sandwich Cr¿me Cookies, 9.6-Ounce Boxeses (Pack of 6)Back To Nature Crispy Wheats Cracker, 8-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)Back To Nature Stoneground Wheats, 6-Ounce (Pack of 6)I've tried of their granola in the past and didn't buy it again, so I had an idea what this would be like.  The granola is the same as other varieties, but I was surprised to find the dark chocolate's overpowering taste overwhelming the granola.  It may make a better snack or dessert than breakfast cereal.To some this may be a great positive.  To me, I would prefer the chocolate taste to be more subtle.Despite that, I will be finishing the bag...

column9: Only one star taken off for not putting the word "snack" on the packaging and the clusters being too small.
column10: CLUSTERS: If you're going to call them clusters they should be only a bit smaller than popped corn kernels.  These clusters are so small that you couldn't even call them that if this was cereal.  What we've really got here is a granola cereal with bits of chocolate in it to be eaten a pinch at a time.CHOCOLATE CHUNKS: Looking at the granola through the window in the packaging you would think you could hardly taste the chocolate, like when you're eating Chips A'Hoy and somehow get a cookie that only has a couple of chips in it, but you actually taste plenty of chocolate in every bite.  It's very good, not too sweet, and very chocolatey without murdering the taste of the granola--which is also delicious.WHOLE GRAIN: There are two main reasons why whole grain is good.  First, it's more filling; one sandwich made with whole grain bread is as filling as two sandwiches on white bread for example.  You simply wont feel the need to keep stuffing yourself and that will reduce your total calorie intake by hundreds of calories per day if you have whole grain snacks like this one in addition to whole grains in your meals. The other is that whole grains range from tougher to impossible to metabolize, so your body works harder, burning more calories trying to do that (calcium does this too by the way, so it's a good idea to take a swig of milk with your whole grain snack).One added feature of whole grain is that it adds volume to your stool, so make sure to have that plunger at the ready if you're suddenly adding whole grain foods to your diet.PACKAGING: If I saw this on the shelf in the supermarket I would assume it's a cereal to put milk into or to top yogurt with.  Whomever designed the packaging and omitted the word 'snack' should be flogged.WITH MILK, EATEN WITH A SPOON: Hey, guess what, it is good as a cereal.  A half cup serving, with milk, would be about 350 to 400 calories I guess, which isn't bad for breakfast.THE F-WORD: Yes, it's got fat in it, like all granola, but since it's not in bar form, molded together with marshmallows or corn syrup you really shouldn't worry about it.  'Fat is the flavor' as the saying goes, and that warning only purtains to people who somehow think one bag of cookies should be eaten in one sitting.  Even the suggested serving size here is quite large for a snack.  Personally I found myself eating two pinches of this granola whenever I went into the kitchen to feed an urge to eat something, and that was enough to do the trick.  So don't worry about the slightly over the line fat percentage.If you're really worried about gorging yourself not only on granola, but ice cream or crackers and cheese and other delicious little goodies, don't bring the whole container with you to the living room for your several hours of nightly television.  Instead, put any snack you're going to eat in a 6oz custard cup and don't fill it more than three quarters of the way--which is about half a cup since it gets wider towards the rim.BOTTOM LINE: There really isn't any supplement that can substitute for getting your nutrients and whole grains from actual food such as granola.This is really delicious, healthy, proper snack food to get you through those periods between meals when you just want to stay satiated, keep your energy level up, and reduce any cravings you might have for something bulkier and with more calories.

I received this product as part of the Amazon Vine program.I like granola, but I don't really get to eat it a lot, due the high carb nature of all granola.  I also like chocolate, ok I love chocolate.I thought this might be a match made in heaven.I first tried it in cold milk as cereal.  The granola is typical granola.  Lots of chewing, so so taste.  On top of that was the chocolate.  Something about the chocolate and the milk made the chocolate taste practically overwhelm the granola.  Not bad, just not what I was expecting.I next tried it as a dry snack.  Except for the mess of eating granola without a spoon and some milk to hold it in place, this was better.  The chocolate taste was a little more subtle, basically coming in the bites that had chocolate.  Plus with it being dark chocolate, it's not overwhelming.Back to Nature products are expensive.  That's what you get when you go with a small company who is actually producing less processed products.  This isnt' that important to me, but it could be important to you.As some others here have suggested, the idea is a good one.  Maybe having a bag of chocolate chips that you love mixed with a bag of granola that you love, and coming up with a good ratio would make for a wonderful snack (or even a wonderful breakfast) but to me this isn't it.

This granola is not near as good as many others I have tasted.  The chocolate leans toward bitter or there isn't enough sweetness or richness to the mix.  Something isn't quite right.  Oh, it's edible, of course, but with spendy granola, it needs to be really delicious before you fork over that kind of dough for the product.  It's just not worth the price.

I love this product! It's crispy and delicious. It's not very nicely clustered, so might be challenging to use it as a finger food/snack. I tried it with milk and soymilk and I personally like it with soy milk better. :)

I am by no means a granola connoisseur, but this stuff is pretty darn tasty.  This product is made with all natural ingredients. There honestly isn't a lot of chocolate in it -- just the right amount. It's dark chocolate but isn't too bitter or too sweet. Overall it's just a very nice blend and tastes delicious. Maybe a little pricey, but not a dealbreaker when considering it's made with real ingredients. I'd say 5/5 for taste, 3/5 for value. Recommended.

column9: What will they think of next?
column10: I suppose the problem with a product like this is that it's too easy to create for yourself once you get the idea.  I mean, who would even think of buying their favorite granola, in bulk perhaps, and then their favorite chocoloate chips, or chunks, and throwing them together one's self.Now, this particular product for me is defintely OK.  In fact, if you're hungry and you're just sitting in front of the computer typing stuff you could much through a whole back of it before you can say "one thousand calories".  So, as a snack food it's almost as dangerous as cashews as far as I'm concerened.However, I found the granola taste to be uninspiring.  It just didn't seem very fresh, if that makes any sense, and the chocolate chunks couldn't save the day.  This product just makes me want to do it myself because I know with my hand picked ingredients I could likely do better and not have to pay as much.

column9: Great Granola, from a non granola guy
column10: The is an Amazon Vine review, and my first one.  When I saw this product, I decided to give it a try, wow am I glad I did.  Several simple points of interest.1) The packaging is nice, the colors and textures of the bag make you feel like it is "environmentally friendly."  I am not in any way suggesting it is, but the coloring and make up of the bag make you think it's a natural type of product.2) Upon opening the bag, one is treated to an olfactory delight.  The smell is fresh and good, and you will be tempted to dig right in, and not share with others.3) Texture and taste.  The granol is fresh and not at all dry or stale.  It could be mashed together and would "hold" large pieces together it is so moist, it is not wet, but certainly not dry.  The taste is a nice blend of flavors and the addition of the chocolate chunks is very welcome.  When you get a mouthful that has a piece of chocolate in it, it is a real treat.In the interest of full disclosure, I am not a granola eater; however, this is an excellent product.  My somewhat choosy eater 6 and 7 year old children love it as well.Highly recommend.

This granola is a mix of rolled oats and semi-sweet chocolate chunks.  I couldn't find a description on the bag as to whether it's a snack or a cereal.  As a snack, it's a bit dry for my taste and isn't as sweet as the delicious Quaker 100% Natural, but I quite enjoyed it with milk.  Its crunchy texture is just right and the chocolate is a treat.  If you like granola, this is a good one.  A good source of fiber.

..is what i said when i popped a mouthful of these. they are really good. the granola is mixed in with tiny chocolate bits and the packs are bigger than i expected them to be. a 1/2 cup serving has 220 calories 50 cal from fat and the ingredients are pretty straight forward(whole grain rolled oats, semi-sweet chocolate chunks, vanilla extract, molasses, etc..) as far as taste goes this is great. my husband plans on taking the bag with him when he goes hiking. its perfect for him.

I requested this item from the Amazon Vine program and decided to have my family help me get more info for my review. I love eating healthy and was looking forward to a better alternative to the already semi-healthy granola I was enjoying. So, I sat my family down at the table. My dad, mom, two brothers, one sister and one grandmother and asked them to taste test it.My mom and sister were the first to protest. Now, I hadn't tried it at this point but everyone else had. My sister and mom told me it was too bland and the chocolate was too grainy. It didn't taste natural.My two brothers were next. My older brother (who is 28 years old) told me that the only time he would eat this would be if he was walking through the woods and hadn't eaten anything and had stumbled over it. My younger brother (22) said that while the taste wasn't awful, it "just wasn't good either".My grandmother was indifferent. She was the first person to like it a little bit even though she claimed it tasted like dry oatmeal and tiny flakes of chocolate.My dad said the same thing. That it tasted as if there was no chocolate in it at all and the granola had an oatmeal taste that didn't sit right with him.I figured that maybe they were making a fuss out of nothing so I decided to try it. In my hand it looked harmless but upon eating it, I found that I could not produce enough saliva to even slightly moisten the granola chunks and the chocolate used was horrible and crumbled in my mouth instead of melted.This is my very first bad review and I have to say... it deserves it. I will never purchase this item and if anyone wants the half of bag I got, it's being fed to my hampster. He happens to think it's wonderful!

"Back to Nature" Chocolate Delight Granola was certainly a pleasant surprise.  I have always been a fan of granola bars, oatmeal, and, of course, chocolate, but I never expected to enjoy this food quite as much as I did.  The taste is not merely the blandness of oats or the sugary sweetness of the chocolate but a wonderful combination of the two, neither of which comes across as overpowering but as a subtle, healthy snack for one to eat.  If you are interested in this product, you might also be most interested to note the excessive fiber content, which is another of granola's additional benefits.Any complaint I have regarding the product is purely logistical.  Let's be honest: eating loose, bulk granola isn't easy.  I dropped as much on my floor as I put in my mouth.  I suppose the most effective method of eating the granola would be to put it in a bowl and spoon it like cereal, but that eliminates the ability for the product to be carried around for a snack, taken camping, etc.  While one cannot as easily control the portion size of granola bars, they remain a much easier and more effective method of consumption than loose granola.

Delicious with dark chocolate chunks (plenty of them).  It's granola and I ate the bag in 2 days; couldn't stop munching.  I won't buy it again because eating this stuff is no way to stay a size 6 (can't I brag?).  1/2 cup has 220 calories, 6 grams total fat, 4 grams of dietary fiber, 5 mg of salt and 13 grams of sugar. NOT BAD AT ALL, especially the fairly high fiber and very very low sodium.  The ingredients do not offend.  It's crunchy and delicious.

column9: May be natural, but apparently not organic
column10: It tastes like granola with chocolate chunks thrown in, and it tastes good. That aside, the main thing this product is trying to be is natural, which it appears to be. An important distinction, though, is that it doesn't claim to be organic. It seems to me that if I was going "Back to Nature," it would be organic. I don't think I'd pay a premium for this, but it tastes as good as expected.

This chocolate delight granola comes with rich dark chocolate chunks that create a tasty breakfast. I recommend adding some sugar with milk for a richer taste. Dark chocolate has lowering of high blood pressure and it is a potent antioxidant. Although I liked the taste of this mix, but I thought it is a little pricey. If you are health conscious and like chocolate this could be your choice. You may also be pleased to know that it doesn't have artificial flavors or fructose corn syrup.1. Galaxy Granola Not Sweet Vanilla Munch - 6 Pack2. Hi-Country Cereal Mix3. Kingslake & Crane Hale & Hearty Granola

very tasty, but watch the calories!!! A 1/2 cup has over 200 calories! And the fat content is high, also. I tend to eat more than a half cup of cereal at a time. Having said that, the flavor and texture are very nice. Yummy chocolate pieces. Not too soft, and not too crunchy. So, if you don't mind the calorie/fat content, it's a very good cereal. Probably better as a small snack or treat.

The texture is good, the chocolate bits are good, but oh my goodness, this is so sweet.  It's way too sweet for me as luck would have it.  I expected sweet with the chocolate but wow!  Blech!And at 220 calories for a half cup, there's not much nutritional value.  It is filling, I'll give it that, and it has a significant amount of fiber.You might like this if you pour sugar in your cereal.  And it's OK for a snack, but I wouldn't eat this on a regular basis.  There are far too many tasty, healthy products around for me to eat this <gag>.

column9: High calories disguised as a health food.
column10: The first encounter I had with "Back to Nature" was one of their breakfast cereals.  I found it to be very good, yet nothing that Special K red berries couldn't tackle.  Nevertheless I stumbled upon this granola and figured I give it a taste.I must say that this granola has a good taste.  It could be easily used as breakfast cereal, put into yogurt, used in baking or just eaten out of the bag.  However, I was really surprised at the serving size versus the calorie count.  A half of cup of this "all natural" granola is 220 calories.  That seems like a lot.  Then if one reads the ingredients, it is quite plausible why the calorie count is so high.Overall, this granola is good, but nothing to get excited about or shell out a great deal of money for.  Besides once you read what is in it and how "unhealthy" it is, you be wondering how you are getting back to nature.

column9: A Failure for Granola - Maybe a Win for Cereal?
column10: I wanted to like this product, but I didn't on so many levels.Since this was marketed as a snack, I expected to be able to reach into the bag and grab a cluster or two of delicious chocolately granola.  No.The top-most layer of the bag did indeed have clusters, but they didn't last long.  The bottom 80% of the bag was tiny pieces of granola and flakes of choclate... better suited for cereal than snacking.The clusters, when they were together, don't contain chocolate.  So even if you managed to get a few clustery snacks, it was just granola stuck together.  Tasteless granola.  The chocolate is there in little flakes, which were good, but unless you were scooping the stuff into your mouth you're not going to get any.I should probably have tried the product again as a cereal with milk, alas I was out of milk and rarely enjoy cereal anyway.Oh, and anyone tagging this as "healthy" has another thing coming.  Half a cup of the stuff is 220 calories.The only thing this product has going for it is the resealable packaging which was quite good.

column9: Never cared for granola still don't
column10: I wasn't sure what I was getting. I have never really cared much for granola so I thought I'd see what they would do with chocolate. It's just square bits of chocolate mixed with granola. The chocolate is nothing special and it's just plain old granola. You might as well buy bulk granola and a bag of chocolate. That way you can have granola however you want it: with milk, alone or with chocolate. And you can have the chocolate by itself as well.

column9: Yum! Very tasty snack!  And lives up to its promise of "natural"!
column10: Basically, with this snack, the granola (comprised of rolled oats) is a delivery mechanism for the CHOCOLATE.  Big, rectangular pieces of chocolate, that dominate the taste of this snack.  If you love chocolate like I do, you'll like this snack.Now, my next question would be, how healthy is this?  I was for some reason expecting this to be another "faux healthy" snack like so many of the granola bars you find these days, which are loaded with hydrogenated oils and artificial flavorings.  The ingredients list of this granola is 100% comprised of things YOU could buy at the grocery store!  Sugar, skim milk, molasses, etc.. even the preservative is plain old vitamin E.Next I was curious about the calorie/sugar/fat content as compared to my usual granola, Kashi Apple Orchard.  This product (same serving size) has 1 gram less of total fat (though saturated fat is 1 g more than the Kashi), 1 gram less of carbohydrates, and one less grab of protein.  Total calories are the same per serving.  Contrasting with the Kashi, I would never eat this for breakfast since my days of chocolate (Count Chocula) early in the morning are long since past.  But I do think this granola is a good snack and worth checking out.  I bet it would be easy to make GREAT cookies out of this, as well.Hope this helps you decide whether or not you want to try it.

BACK TO NATURE'S CHOCOLATE DELIGHT GRANOLA tastes really good and has the perfect blend of crunchy and sweet that makes this a tasty snack, either as a cereal or right out of the bag.It's made from natural ingredients and doesn't contain artificial flavors, preservatives, hydrogenated oils or high fructose corn syrup.But here's the rub... the BACK TO NATURE CHOCOLATE GRANOLA, like all granola, is high in fat. Some of it is the good fat, Polyunsaturated and Monounsaturated, but it does contain 6g of total fat--2g of that Saturated Fat. It also packs 220 calories per 1/2 cup serving, which is about 2 1/2 handfuls, and it's very easy to keep eating it.Since opening the bag, I've probably eaten three servings already, because it's that good, but that can't be good for my waist!OK, I shouldn't be that harsh and deduct 1-star from BACK TO NATURE... for my own lack of will power, but many customers will see the words "nature" and "whole grain" and think "healthy treat." The small serving size of the granola is also deceptive because many will think "this is such a tiny amount that I'll just eat a little more" because it really does seem like you're eating a small amount, but then next thing you know you can't zip up your jeans.On the plus side, that means that the product is delicious but just be aware of serving size and portions. Otherwise, it's a good alternative to say a 180-calorie cookie that's full of high fructose corn syrup and sugar and no fiber.

column9: Like Chocolate & Granola??? To me, 'tis a Match Made in Heaven!!
column10: Heaven... I'm in heaven... OOOPS!! If you love "All Things Chocolate" and/or "All Things Granola", you simply have to try this dee-lish-us cereal.As with all Back To Nature products that I've sampled, "Chocoate Delight" has the perfect harmony. of ingredients and flavors. Pure culinary symmetry - even Adrian Monk would approve.As much as I like the BearNaked brand, I like 'BTN' even better. You will like it as well, Mikey. ;)Ok, let the "0 of 30 reviewers found this review helpful" onslaught begin!

this stuff is like eating a bowl of cement. i took a handful and tried it and it was lousy, very dry and just a really bad taste and texture. then i sid maybe it will improve with milk, no luck. it was still really, really, really awefull. this is the first item i have reviewed after purchasing hundreds or things off of amazon. i felt i had to WARN people. DO not buy this if you have never tried it Before!!! only purchase it if you have tried it and like eating a bowl of cement. horrible stuff.. i CANNOT understand all the great reviews, they have to be made up.

column9: Granola for people who don't love granola.
column10: While you read this review, please keep in mind that I'm not a huge granola/trail mix/nut type fan at all. Nuts only appeal to me if they are super salty. I'll only snack on trail-mix if it's got a lot of M&Ms. I'll eat a granola bar, but only if it's got enough junk food in it to render it a mislabeled candy bar. It's just never appealed to me even though I'm an extremely healthy eater.However, "Chocolate Delight" is satisfying to me. It's basically like a crumbly, crunchy lightly-sweet oatmeal cookie with small chunks of chocolate laced throughout. I didn't find it sweet OR salty, to be honest- it's just lightly sweet which makes it snackable. The chocolate isn't bitter, nor is it overly sweet- it's just the right compliment for the granola. I also like that the chocolate doesn't leave a weird aftertaste in my mouth like a lot of other dark chocolates do. There's not a whole lot of chocolate, just enough to provide a nice "kick" to the granola.It's definitely a satisfying snack because it's got some bulk to it- if you eat it by the handful, you won't feel like you've just crunched on baked air, like a lot of other healthy snacks. It feels like you've actually eaten something satisfying.My husband, who IS a fan of granola, said he would have preferred it without the chocolate. I probably wouldn't *eat* it if it didn't have the chocolate, so your milage may vary on that one.By the way- this *isn't* a cereal, as another reviewer noted - it's meant to be eaten as a snack. I'm actually anxious to try it out with my daughter when she gets home from school. She's three and an EXTREMELY picky eater. I'm hoping this might be something she can snack on instead of cereal and chips. I think the chocolate will be a huge draw for her and I can feed it to her without worrying about all the salt and sugar she's getting.

I needed a little afternoon pick-me-up today, so I tested out the Chocolate Delight Granola.  Chocolate Delight is right.  Those little semi-sweet chocolate bits are pretty potent.I tried this both without and with milk (eating it as cereal).  I liked it better without the milk.  It is nice and crunchy and simple.  I don't think that I would eat this in the morning for breakfast--I love chocolate, but that much early in the morning is too much for even me.This is a good, simple, whole grain, fiber-rich (4g) snack.  Don't go overboard with it, though, because it does have plenty of calories (220 per 1/2 cup).  A 1/2 cup is just enough for a pick-me-up in the afternoon.  I'm keeping a bag at my desk at work for the afternoon slump.If you like semi-sweet chocolate and you like granola, you can't go wrong with this snack.

column9: Yummy - my tastebuds are on overload!
column10: I've got to admit, I wasn't expecting much from another granola product but "Back to Nature" has certainly caught my attention. Having just arrived home (and I was hungry) when this product arrived, it couldn't have been better timing - I'm sitting here munching on this delightul blend of fiber mixed with just the perfect amount of semi-sweet dark chocolate is putting me into a state of granola-bliss. In fact, I really can't remember a time when I've had granola that tastes this good! Just as wonderful is that all-natural ingrediants are used and contains a lot of fiber. This would be a great product to take with you on outings or to the movie as an alternatative for popcorn. Regardless, "Back to Nature" simply tastes good!

I place an order for the back to nature granola almost 3 to 5 cases a month and I love it... Unfortunately my love for it is turning to hatred... This is mostly due to the time delay in shipping has gotten completely insane. I am almost waiting 1 month for this and that is just not acceptable. Then when it finally comes and it is left on the delivery truck for who knows how long all the chocolate in the granola is melted!!! I don't know how much more of this I can take because it sure is not fair if I'm paying full price and not getting 100 percent satisfaction for my product.....

I love this amazing product.  I eat it daily in coffee yogurt or in natural vanilla yogurt.  I love the crunch with a bit of chocolate.  I am fortunate that I do no have to order this item online here.  I can find it MUCH cheaper at my local grocery and then sometimes even cheaper when on a B1G1 sale.  Anyway, I love the product!

This granola is delicious.  Crunchy, with satisfying chunks of chocolate mixed in clumps of granola as well as chips of loose chocolate.  I use it in yogurt and it is awesome.  I like the packaging, too ... The resealable bag is convenient and practical.

I have been a fan of this granola for about a year - I add it to a cup of vanilla soy yogurt for breakfast. It is a tasty, hearty granola. I don't think there is puffed rice filler, just oat clusters and chocolate pieces. This granola flavor is regularly out of stock at my local grocery store and find Amazon's subscription service extremely convenient.

I eat this as a cereal with rice milk and it is GREAT!  I have not experienced the issues other customers have had with opening the bag.  Just be sure to tear across and downward.  I have received a bag or two that was melted, but the chocolate did not stick to the sides of the bag, it just formed clumps in the middle.  My shipments originate from Allentown, PA.

I tried this at my daughter's house recently.  Her husband couldn't find it in the grocery store so is now purchasing through Amazon.  I put some in my yogurt and a smile came across my face:)  I didn't read the nutrition label before ordering some for myself but not sure if that would have changed my mind.  It's high in calories - fat and carbs, especially for only a 1/2 cup serving.  However, protein and fiber is a positive for me.  I love the flavor and crunch.

column9: best granola ever-  kids hooked on it too!
column10: buy this and you won't regret it.  good quality dark chocolate adds a delicious flavor!!  good healthy snack too for kids!

It's hard to compare food items since everyone has a different taste for what they like. For me this is the best chocolate granola. It has a significant amount of chocolate, which I find particularly good since pretty much every other I have tried just has a bit of chocolate chunks. This one is generous with the chocolate, which is also of very good quality, I think about 60% cocoa contents. So if you like chocolate this is one granola worth trying.

column9: Excellent granola, resealable bag, natural ingredients.
column10: It passes the taste test of multiple people. I like granola and chocolate, and desire organic and/or natural products over all else.Now that we as consumers have many choices for most products, it will come down to taste, packaging, and the environmental awareness of the company itself.Will definitely buy again.
The chocolate squares are a perfect size. The granola is tasty, too. Great combination of cereal.

Very good stuff. Maybe a little hard, but I guess that's what REAL granola is all about. Very nice in vanilla yogurt or mixed with other granola cereal. Resealable packaging makes sure it doesn't turn into a big pile of amalgamated mush.

What is there to say about granola and chocolate mixed together? Plenty if it is done as well as this Back to Nature treat is. The combo is a nice break from boring granola but without the guilt of pure chocolate or candy. It is a very dry snack so have a liquid handy. The chocolate is a little biter which detracts from the overall flavor resulting in a 4.

I loved this granola. The chocolate pieces were a great addition! Wonderful flavor and great in milk. My own personal preference is a little chunkier granola, and this is definitely not chunky. The kids wanted some and I let them try (they loved it too), but the package is pretty small, so not economical for our big family. I can't imagine anyone not liking this if you like granola and chocolate!

This granola has bits of chocolate in it, which I thought would be way too sweet for my taste. But it works. The chocolate is in small slivers and it doesn't overwhelm the cereal, and it's really not sweeter than most cereals. So far, this cereal hasn't even made it into a bowl because I keep snacking on it straight from the bag, but I think it will do quite well in milk. If you like granola and chocolate, it's definitely worth a try.

column9: not overly sweet, relatively healthy granola
column10: I'm not one of those people who consider granola as breakfast because it's often too sweet and sticky. This one could almost qualify because it's not overly sweet, and there aren't that many chocolate pieces. So it's like an oaty breakfast with chocolate chips.However,if you're wanting that super-sweet granola flavor often eaten as snacks or for energy on hikes, this probably will not give you the burst of energy and flavor you might want.I was debating between 3 or 4 stars, but I decided to go lower because I felt like the product was a compromise to be both healthy and sweet, but not exactly succeeding in either. I guess I'd rather go all healthy or all indulgent.

It's rare to find a cereal that is reasonably sweet and healthy. Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola contains chocolate chips made from natural ingredients. It DOES NOT contain vanillin or other artifical colors and flavors commonly found in cheap chocolate products and often found in cereals. I have two children allergic to artificial colors and flavors. This is a great find, allowing the whole family to have a special treat for breakast. My children also snacked on the granola. This is easy to do because it comes in a portable 12 ounce plastic package.

This granola is everything you can ask for more.  It is a snack filled with grains and fiber and had added dark chocolate chunks.  It is healthy and natural.  It is delicious and tasty.  One can indulge in this granola without feeling guilty for such an enjoyable treat. It is good.

This is some of the best granola I have ever had.  Crunchy, great flavor, and just the right amount of chocolate make it extremely satisfying.  Great as a cereal with milk, or just straight out of the bag.  My daughter loved it and ate most of it!

The idea of chocolate granola was a new one, and I wasn't sure, despite loving chocolate, that this was going to be a hit, but its perfect.  Small chunks of dark chocolate mixed in the granola at just the right proportion means intense chocolate flavor mixed with the flavor of the toasted oats.  With ice cold milk, it was almost like a milk shake!This is going to be one of those items that frequently appear on our table-its a great treat!

The granola itself is fairly unsweet but the abundant semi-sweet chocolate chunks provide an overall appropriate sweetness and a chocolate flavor that is not overpowering.  I'm not into chocolate cereal, so I didn't try it with milk, but it quickly disappeared as a snack when left on the counter (I didn't even get to finish it).

I must say this is some very tasty stuff!!!  I love chocolate anyway and combining it with the "grains" sounds good to me...and it is!!  The only problem I have with the product is that it's too "crummy".  It's like a bag of crumbs.  No "bite size" here...  but it is delicious.  I even sprinkled some on my morning cereal..mmmm!

column9: More a snack food than a cereal
column10: Chocolate indeed! Lots of decent quality chocolate bits mixed with a basic granola. So much chocolate in fact that it's more a trail mix or snack food than a cereal.No 'bad' stuff like hydrogenated oils here either. This is a quality food and the price reflects that. It's a bit too pricey for my wallet, but you get what you pay for. If you can afford it, buy it, you shouldn't be dissappointed.

Sure you could put it in milk and eat it like cereal, sprinkle it as a topping on ice cream or fro-yo, but it is perfect enough to snack right out of the bag.  I love how sweet it is.  I am not a fan of dry-barely-sweet granola but the gooey sugary stuff marketed toward children isn't great either (I'd rather eat a cookie or cake).  This hits that midpoint that is perfect when craving a sweet snack (without going for a full-fledged dessert).  The chocolate is perfect and sweet without being bitter like found in many healthier snacks.Nice perk... the zipper closure at the top.  I can never seem to find a "Chip Clip" in my house when I need one though I have bought dozens.

I'm not a granola eater -- it tends to be too high calorie and processed to be a healthy breakfast for me as I watch my weightSo I ordered "Chocolate Delight Granola" to check it out as a snack. The pieces are too little to make an easy snacking food, but the flavor is nicely balanced -- it's not overwhelmingly chocolate-y.I finally found a good use for this granola as a yoghurt topping. My recipe:Stir together these ingredients:1/2 cup plain yoghurt1 tablespoon honey2 tablespoons roasted wheat germTop with:1/4 cup Chocolate Delight GranolaThe granola adds textural interest to the yoghurt while not being overwhelmingly sweet.

While I don't generally go for chocolate "cereals", I really enjoyed this as a snack. The flavor is reminiscent of an oatmeal-chocolate chip cookie, of course, and a handful is as satisfying as a cookie without quite as much fat or sugar. It's also great sprinkled over ice cream or frozen yogurt.

Very good taste, and pleasing to the eye.  Seems to be fresh and packed well.  Everyone who tried it enjoyed it.  Bag color scheme seem drab, of course I know your not buying it for the bag colors.  You should be pleased with the contents.

column9: Should be on the DEA's Controlled Substance List!
column10: This stuff is tremendous!  I'm not a big chocolaholic, but I rapidly consumed the entire package in the course of a week.  I never did try it as a cereal with milk, but that would b just as good also.Unfortunately, I cannot find Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola in the local stores, but an upcoming trip to New York ought to provide the opportunity to smuggle a case of this back to West Virginia.If you even slightly like chocolate, you will find this stuff addicting!

Back to Nature's Chocolate Delight Granola is pretty straightforward stuff -- basically just oat clusters and chocolate chunks, with some sweeteners and oils thrown in. So, if you like oats and chocolate (I do!), then it's a tasty, if not wildly original, granola.However, it IS very messy to eat. The oat clusters fell into tiny bits and the chocolate smeared all over me when I tried to eat it by hand, so I ended up dumping it directly into my mouth from the bag to try to minimize the extent of the damage. (Not the greatest strategy for portion control!) This would be best eaten as a breakfast cereal, I daresay, than an on-the-go snack (especially for kids).

I was a little skeptical about eating chocolate for breakfast - but this is a very good granola with just the right amount of chocolate.  The granola part is not overly sweet which helps to balance the chocolate chips.  It is great in a bowl with milk or as a convenient snack out of the bag.

column9: good quality granola with quality dark chocolote
column10: I love granola and have tested lots of brands. I love back-to-nature and udi's. This one has good quality dark chocolate chunks. The granola is not too chewy, not too sweet. Here is a simple recipe for this granola - 1/2 cup plain yogurt, 1/4 cup granola, 1 tsp good quality berry preserves. yummy!

I was very surprised by the quality and flavor of the dark chocolate. It is better than most of the chocolate bars I've picked up at a specialty chocolate shop.The granola is not overly sweetened and tastes very clean, but not bland.I even like it it straight out of the pouch.edited to add- after closer review of the ingredients, I realized the chocolate bits are not 100% vegan. :(

column9: Plain taste, but lots of chocolate
column10: This is a basic granola mix - granola and chocolate chips. It tastes alright, but is not too exciting. I did like that it was all natural.It can also be used as cereal.

This granola really surprised me as to how good it is!  I love chocolate, but only darker, less sweet types, and I thought this cereal would be way oversweet but it was not.  I loved it as did everyone else in my family, young and old.It tasted equally as good dry as a snack.  I probably would prefer it this way most of the time.It is very crunchy and does not lose its crunch in milk very quickly.  The taste was fresh and chocolaty, but not overly so, a good balance.

column9: Chocolate granola? Now that's my idea of health food! LOL
column10: I'll admit right up front that I am not the biggest fan of or authority on granola (most of it is too sweet for my taste and I am not a sweet-for-breakfast kind of person).  I used to eat granola on yogurt--back when I was trying to train myself to like yogurt--but I rarely eat it anymore, so I don't buy granola anymore either.But THIS granola--Back to Nature's Chocolate Delight--intrigued me because I am a chocoholic.  I couldn't imagine eating it as a breakfast food, but I did find quite a yummy use for it--I sprinkled it on ice cream.  I LOVE the flavors of coffee and chocolate together, so I thought sprinkling it on my coffee ice cream (or frozen yogurt) was worth a try.  It was quite a tasty combination and gave my dessert a great crunch factor, which I love.This granola, unlike most, is NOT oversweet.  When I ordered it, I thought the oaty part would be choclate too, but it isn't (or, if it's intended to be, it's so mild that I can't tell).  When I tried the oaty part of the granola with the chocolate chunks that come in it, it had just the right level of sweetness for me.  When I tried the oaty part by itself, it was surprisingly low in sweetness.  The chocolate chunks are dark chocolate (my favorite) and are surprisingly rich tasting--no cheap chocolate taste here.I don't have any other granola here at home to compare the numbers, but my guess would be that this is a bit healthier than many granolas.  According to the package it is "made with whole grain rolled oats perfectly sweetened with natural ingredients."  Reading the ingredient list, those natural ingredients would appear to be evaporated cane juice and brown rice syrup.  It is high in calories (220 for a 1/2 cup serving), but I think that is true of any granola.  It has 6g of fat, 2 of which are sat fat, and it has no trans fat.  It has 13g of sugar (which I think is probably lower than most granolas), 4g of fiber and 5g of protein.In terms of eating this granola as a snack by itself, the downside to me is that it is not very chunky.  The majority of my 12-oz. bag was loose oaty bits and chocolate chips...chunks of more than a few oats stuck together were in the minority.  Now, as an ice cream topping, that was a positive thing, but it wouldn't be for snack eating.Will I buy this again when this bag is gone?  Probably not.  But not because it wasn't good and not because it didn't make a great ice cream topping.  As stated, I'm just not that much of a granola person and I really don't need one more snack food laying around the house to tempt me.

column9: A great granola and chocolate treat!
column10: This granola is the best granola I have ever had!  The salty andcrunchy oats balanced with the dark chocolate was amazing.  It is nota super healthy granola but I did find the chocolate to be highquality.  I enjoyed this granola by itself rather than adding toyogurt or eating with cereal.  Therefore eating it with my hands wasa little awkward because there were many small pieces of granola thatwere not clustered together with the chocolate.  Overall I wouldrecommend this granola to all of the chocolate lovers.

What a great way to start the day, delicious crunch and chocolate! Yum! I don't know what else to say about this granola, except that it is the perfect breakfast for me. It is not too sweet, and, if it's healthy, too, than that is just a bonus. My oldest grandchild loves it also (age 12), although the other two, who are under 5 years old, have some trouble with the texture, and prefer softer cereals. I don't take that as a negative, as they have the same problem with any granola. If you enjoy granola and enjoy chocolate, then I would definitely recommend that you try this product!
This is an excellent granola. The chunks of granola are large. The semi-sweet chocolate is wonderful with the granola, and the granola is not very sweet. A great combination of flavors.

What's not to like? Rich chocolate and crunchy granola, yummy!If I had any complaint, it would be the seemingly melty chocolate chips. I am unsure if the clumps of chocolate covered in granola were intentional or if the chips were supposed to be freefloating, but either way it worked.I put it in a bowl and it was gone in a matter of 30 minutes. My 87 year old grandmother loved it as much as my 2 year old, who requested it many times over.I think it would be delightful even with milk as a cereal. I will buy this again!

column9: Melts in your bag, not in your mouth...
column10: WARNING:  Do not buy this product from Amazon in the summer if if you live in a warm climate.  The chocolate chips will melt, while the box sits on the delivery truck.Other than that, I thought this was a pretty tasty product, and the price isn't too bad either.  My kids liked it, but mostly they gobbled up the chocolate bits and left a lot of granola crumbs.  Give it a try.

This is a rather ordinary granola. The chocolate added a nice touch and helped boost this granola to a higher rating than I would have otherwise have given it.It was not overly chocolate, nor was there so little chocolate that you couldn't taste it. There seemed to be a just right amount of chocolate. My children and husband agreed.The granola is very crunchy. The pieces were very very small. I tend to like a granola that is a little bit more chunky; more bite to it. The taste was fine though.This is  a fairly healthy snack with a fine taste. It is not an outstanding item but certainly worth a try if you are looking for a fast snack.

column9: Very good but a tad too chocolatey for me!
column10: This was a very good tasting cereal. Nice crunch and did not get soggy in the milk. The only thing I would say is that it had just a bit too much chocolate for me (I know I sound crazy saying that). I took some of the chocolate pieces out on the second bowl and it was perfect. The chocolate seems to throw the sweetness over the top for me and I don't like cereal to be too too sweet in the morning. However, if a sweet cereal suits you, then this is quite nice and the granola nuggets even flavor the milk a little. I enjoyed it and would recommend it. Very very good.

I really liked this it was very good. I liked the fact that it wasn 't overly sweet like some other brands I have had in the past. I really,really enjoyed the chocolate bits. It's excellent with milk or mixed in with yogurt as well,or on its own plain. I would most definitly buy this again its tasty and one of those things thats too good but good for me so I don't mind having it as a treat now and then.

column9: A Good Out of The Bag Snack
column10: I was interested to try Back To Nature's Chocolate Delight Granola because I'm always looking for new healthy snacks or yogurt mix ins.  I was unsure what to expect though, because I've had hit and miss experiences with Back to Nature products before--I've enjoyed some of their cookies, but found most of their breakfast cereals to be too sweet.Like the earlier products, I found this granola to be a mixed bag.  I thought it was good out of the bag--just enough crunch, not too much chocolate--a good healthy-ish snack for kids who get turned off by regular granola that is often full of seeds and nuts.  But then when I added this granola to milk or yogurt I felt like the taste wasn't as good. I don't know if it was the dairy-chocolate reaction or the granola getting a bit soggy pretty fast, but I just didn't like the cereal as much when it wasn't dry.So my verdict is mixed--this is a good snacking granola, but not such a good cereal granola in my book.

column9: Great with milk; by itself: not so much
column10: I've found Back to Nature products to be somewhat "hit or miss."  I LOVE their Classic Granola -- it's probably my favorite "plain" granola, perfect mixed with peach yogurt or eaten with milk.  Their Summer Berry Blend cereal was, to me, wayyy too sweet and the flakes were thick and hard.  I'm sure someone somewhere will absolutely love it, but it wasn't for me.This Chocolate Delight Granola is somewhere in the middle.  It works great as a cereal, eaten with milk.  The flavor is reminiscent of oatmeal chocolate chip cookies.  The sweetness level was just about right, and the amount of chocolate was nice.  I'm not sure I'd want to eat it for breakfast, but for a snack, this works great.  I also tried it mixed with vanilla yogurt.  I used a 6-oz carton of vanilla yogurt, and added about 1/3 C of granola.  This worked well, too.Straight out of the box -- this doesn't work for me.  The chocolate chips have a sort of off-putting texture that seems to disappear with milk.  The cereal is kind of crumbly, so you don't have a huge amount of large clusters to grab onto.So, if you're looking for a "snacking" granola that you can nibble right out of the box, this might not be what you're looking for.  But if you're looking for a tasty chocolate, relatively healthy, granola to eat with milk or yogurt, this stuff is pretty darned good.

column9: Whole Grain Snack is a Delight
column10: As the name says, this Back to Nature whole grain snack is delightful -  Tasty, crunchy, with just enough dark chocolate to add a moderate sweetness.  It's difficult to stop once you start munching!The one problem with Chocolate Delight Granola is the consistency.  After a few nice, crunchy clusters at the top of the bag, the rest amounted to tiny clusters or loose grain with a cereal like consistency.  It makes for a messy snack and almost makes you want to run for a cereal bowl, milk and spoon.Still the taste is very good and the crunch remains even when the remaining clusters are tiny.  Plus the added benefit of whole grain makes this a worthwhile snack.

Back to Nature Chocolate Delight Granola is about as tasty as granola gets.  It makes excellent snack food and tastes very good - especially the chocolate chunks with are high quality and very good.  Made with all natural ingredients, it is healthy - as healthy as natural granola can be, given the high calorie and fat contents of the natural ingredients.
