The cups come in sealed bags of 10 cups at a time to preserve freshness, so buying 80 is no problem.  This purchase was cheaper than my local Costco, too.  I also bought the decaf, and it is great as well.  Definitely a recommend!

This product is exactly what I have been looking for - a reasonably-priced per-serving K-cup!  San Francisco Bay has successfully found a solution to the royalty/licensing issue that has kept K-cup prices in the $0.60-0.80 per-serving range.My requirements for coffee are best described by Louis L'Amour - "hot as hell and black as sin."  Surprisingly, the quality of this coffee tops any Starbuck's I have ever tasted.  In fact, having tasted nearly every coffee offered by Gevalia (of which I am a subscriber, and have been for years), I can say San Francisco Bay Coffee rivals even some of the seasonal/limited edition coffees from Gevalia.For anyone snobbish enough to bad-mouth the quality of this coffee, if one is really such a connoisseur of coffee, one should also know enough to keep the bag tightly closed and preferably in the freezer.I wish this family-owned company the best of luck, kudos on meeting a market need in such a delicious way, and PLEASE offer subscriptions in 2- or 3-week intervals!  36ct. will not last me a full month!Protip: Store in an emtpy resealable plastic coffee container in the freezer.EDIT: Looks to me as though someone was dissatisfied with the coffee (for some reason...maybe poor taste) and reinforced their lack of taste by systematically voting every 5-star rating as Unhelpful.  Classy.

I have found this to be an excellennt value for the money.Purchasing this excellent full bodied coffee in bulk is a great way to save money over the full retail costs in the grocery store. I like the fact that the mesh K-cups are easy to refill and reuse when if you order the k-cup disposable lids.
I was going to go back to a traditional coffee maker until I found these pods.  They are the strong and I enjoy the flavor of the coffee.

I just received my order for the San Francisco Bay K-cups "Fog Chaser" I am drinking it as I am writing , it is the BEST....If you like a nice robust coffee with yet a smooth flavor, then this is it. I have tried the actual K-Cup variety and NONE of any of their flavors came even close to this strong, yet , smooth great taste. I will def. be re-ordering this in my future. For the price and the amount you get , $17.49 FOR 36 COUNT whatttttaaaaa deal !!! They are also a lil different then the original K-cups, the have a filter type bottom but fit and brew just fine. I have not tried the Lavazza Gran Crema Expresso or the Dark Hot Chocolate, which was also part of my order, yet... San Francisco Bay Coffee One Cup for Keurig K-Cup Brewers, Fog Chaser, 36-Count
This is a good strong coffee. The modified k-cup pack works well in my Keurig brewer and I suppose is less wasteful. You can't beat the price especially with subscribe and save!

column9: Great cuppa Joe with less plastic at a lower price
column10: Really love this newly designed cup for my Keurig. Coffee is delicious and aromatic. Less plastic waste is produced and the price is much lower than the traditional k-cups.

I really didn't know what to expect when I ordered this, but the reviews were mostly good so I tried it. I occasionally like a cup of Tully's Kona (outrageously priced right now) or Folgers Black Silk, but I have made the San Francisco Fog Chaser my regular morning cup. The 36-pod order comes in three air-tight bags of 12 each.  I open them as I use them, putting the pods in a jar to maintain freshness.  Going to order more soon!

column9: One of the best coffee variety for Keurig!
column10: Having tried 20 or more different k-cup varieties from Amazon over the past 2 years, I must say that this is probably one of the best (if not THE best) k-cup variety I have purchased.  I was skeptical at first because the pictures showed a lack of complete shell for the coffee, and I wasn't sure how the pressure brewing would work.  But I must say that this coffee has more aroma, strength and flavor than most Keurig brewed coffees.  It comes in small bags, containing 12 each.  I usually transfer them to a freezer bag right away once I open each bag.  This helps keep the flavor a little more.  I like it so much that I started my first coffee subscription from Amazon for this product!  If you love coffee, you MUST give this a try, at least once.

I used to like to try different coffees but after wasting (a lot) of money buying kinds that were a disappointment, I've finally found one to stick with. San Francisco Bay Fog Chaser is my favorite Great coffee - deep, rich, full bodied but not bitter. I especially appreciate the minimal plastic used in the cup. Cups don't fit 100% in my Keurig storage turntable but they do fit. They just fall out a bit more easily.

I was skeptical about this coffee packaging but read the reviews and took the plunge. I was SOOOOO amazed at this coffee. First of all, it is a wonderful, decent strength coffee with no bitterness. Secondly, the packaging is much better for the environment. Thirdly, the value is outstanding!! Just be prepared for a small amount of residue at the end of the cup, a minor thing for such a great coffee!!!

I read the other reviews and decided to give this brand and style of Keurig cup a try. I, like many, am now a believer. The coffee is excellent and I agree with others who say the taste is enhanced by eliminating the plastic cups other brands use. My wife who is not a "coffee drinker" (per se) even prefers these. Also, the price is relatively reasonable.

We took a chance after reading the good reviews for this coffee.  We love it.  I find the way they package it to be great for the environment as there is almost no waste.  We keep it sealed in zip lock bags to retain freshness.  We will order it again.

I consider myself a bit of a coffee snob. Living alone I love K-cups ability to brew a single cup instead of wasting a whole pot. I have tried dozens of different K-cups and all of them made a decent cup of coffee but when I really wanted something good I had to use the french press. These K-cups are by far the best. I love opening up a bag of them and smelling that sweet smell of coffee, something you just don't get with the plastic ones. The taste of these is bolder and stronger than even the most potent plastic version. Lastly these will biodegrade a lot quicker than the plastic ones making them better for the environment.One last quick tip: Put them in a ziplock to retain that fresh ground coffee smell and taste.

Found this coffee at Costco, 80 count for $25.95, purchased 1 box, should have bought more!!! Went back today to buy more and they have discontinued it ! My whole Italian Family loves this Fog Chaser Coffee, we have been using other flavors, mostly Paul Newman's, but we like this much better, It is Rich, but not strong, it has a wonderful taste that appeals to us. I will be ordering the 80 count from Amazon, I am so happy to find it available.

I read some reviews stating this coffee was stale and didn't taste good, so I was skeptical, but the price was low enough for me to try at least once.  I'm glad I did!  I would pay $25 for the same amount of K-cups at the store, and this gets delivered to my door for $14!  Not only does this product waste less plastic because of the design, but it also tastes good.  Now, I use a lot of flavored creamer in my coffee, so I may not be the best judge, but my husband, who likes his coffee strong and black, also drinks this coffee daily.  He agrees that it is good, and a bargain too!  This product comes in three individual, sealed bags, each with 12 cups, so I think this helps keep it fresh.  It is definitely worth a try, and they do sell these in stores if you want to buy a smaller package.
This coffee is so much better than the K-cups you get in the grocery store. And I love the K-cup design. I'mon auto-ship so I don't run out.

column9: Fits in my Keurig and tastes great!
column10: I really enjoy this coffee! I was skeptical about the packaging, thinking it wouldn't fit correctly in my Keurig, but it did! And for the price, AWESOME! I have used the refillable Kcups, the ones where you can get lids and "refill" other cups, but hate it! (I guess I am too lazy to keep refilling and cleaning my kcup) This coffee tastes good too, not the best I have had, but good! I still get most of my Kcups from Kohls when I get a 30% off, I stock up-I love the variety packs there! But I will definitely keep getting these!

this is a very enjoyable 'cup'. the packaging is not a normal plastic,but a mesh of a sort.it did not pose any problem for my machine. the only thing i worry about,perhaps needlessly, will the 'mesh cause a decrease in shelf life.it comes in a airti ght clear plastic package but i break the package and add the kcups to my other kcups on 50 unit display unit. anyway the coffee is nice. im not a expert but i would say its a medium,so it required 2 mugs for my normal bowl movement.im retired so it does not pose a problem.but you younger whipper-snappers may want to keep that in mind. i always kept a small bucket in my car for that reason when i was young,just saying. and no,thats not gross,whats gross is not to have a bucket,cant make it to a rest room,or when u get to one,its in use. be perpared,anyway happyness and peace to u,ur family,and friends,bye-bye.

I had not heard of this brand before, and happened upon it in my local grocery store.  The lower price for a box of 12 cups made me take notice, so I thought I'd try it.  Instant coffee gratification :-)  This is a strong cup of coffee, but it's not overwhelming - at least to my taste.  I prefer some kick and this has got it.  I love the environmentally friendly pod as well.  Definitely will be subscribing and saving!

they are not contained in the keurig plastic cup so once you open the package, you'll want to put them in an airtight storage but i was really impressed with the smooth flavor and good taste. these were a little cheaper than most of the keurig kcups i've found so i was not sure what to expect but these are deff up there on my favorites list.
My daughter introduced me to the San Francisco Bay coffees.  I love them.  This is my favorite of the ones that I have tried.  Fog Chaser!!  The best coffee ever!

I really like this coffee, this was my second order so far. I haven't had a bitter after taste like I have experienced with some other higher priced K-cup brands. I will order again , the price is great & I like the pods better than the original K-cups because the lid is the only plastic in the pod.

Great strong coffee perfect for the morning.  Like the minimal plastic use on the k-cup itself - instead of a plastic bottom it has a paper filter that works fine.  Comes in three bags of 12 cups each, once a bag is opened I just store them in a tupperware until I use them.
I am very pleased with the quality of these coffee k-cups, it makes a great cup of coffee and leaves less of a container going into the landfills.

column9: Great coffee at a great price!
column10: I was disappointed that Timothy's Midnight Magic was no longer available as a Subscribe and Save item. I looked around for a replacement that has a bold flavor and was economical. After reading several reviews I ordered a case of Fog Chaser. This coffee is great. Really great. I also picked up a case of Starbucks Cafe Verona and I prefer the Fog Chaser. It has a wonderful aroma and a bold but not harsh flavor that I really enjoy. The slight inconvenience of having to keep it in a air tight bag to keep it fresh is mitigated by the excellent flavor and price. It's a good trade-off. I have a case coming every month and I may run out sooner.
Great bold taste and aroma.  I would recommend to coffee drinkers who enjoy a strong cup of coffee  Tha pods are "greener"  in packaging.  Good job San Francisco  bay Co.Fairly priced.
SanFrancisco Bay coffee is GREAT love this stuff.  Flavor is very good flavor dark but not bitter will buy again

The price of this coffee and the fact that it could be a little "earth friendly" convinced me to at least try it. The coffee came packaged as described, so "hat's off" to the seller. But that first cup just didn't do it for me. It's lacking that rich dark coffee taste and the pods leave a residue at the bottom of the cup, so that last gulp just doen't happen. I'd rather fill the little coffee baskets, use a mini-coffee liner and fill it with my favorite coffees than buy this product again. But again, this is a $reasonable$ price for Keurig compatible cofee.

I was hoping this would be as good as many people said, but it falls way short!  The price was great, but the taste wasn't.  It tastes like cheap regular coffeepot coffee!  And it was too weak as compared to many stronger Keurig coffees.  I will stick with my trusted Dark Magic.  I can make a 12oz. cup and have it taste like coffee.  This brand I had to reduce it to 6oz. to get something I could drink. That's not cheaper nor more convenient when I have to make two cups in the morning.
Very good coffee, but must keep bag sealed at all times.  It will pick up other flavors.  Other than that it is great!  AND takes up less room than a kcup.

column9: review of unique cup design-not the coffee inside it
column10: This is a first impressions review of the unique cup SF Bay uses in place of the traditional sealed K-cup design after using 12 cups.The cups work fine. They may take a few more seconds to brew (I haven't timed it) because the filter bag inflates with the hot water before the coffee comes out. This makes me think that the mesh bag is actually sealed somehow and that seal is broken with the pressure of the hot water as it's injected into the cup. A strong smell test indicates that there is some sort of seal there because there is not a strong coffee smell coming from the dry cups.If there is some sort of seal these cups should stay fresh longer than they would if the coffee was completely exposed to air. I am still storing these cups in the sealed 12 pack bags they came in and would recommend storing them in a sealed container if you don't go through them quickly. The need to store them sealed takes some convenience out of the K-cup system but the lower price of these cups should offset that.As for the coffee itself, it was good, strong, and tasted more like a fresh cup of coffee than any other k-cups I've tried. It could be the coffee or could be the cup itself. I plan to order a few different flavors in this cup style to find out.

I was looking for affordable k-cups online, and came across the San Francisco Bay Fog Chaser - YUM! is all I can say.  It's rich bold coffee with strong flavor, and an environmental friendly packaging at an excellent price.  Highly recommend it if you're thinking about it.
Brews a very good cup of wake up coffee, but wish they had packaged it in a zipper pouch to keep it fresh.

I opened my Fog Chaser coffee and immediately thought I had ordered the wrong thing because it looked different from my k cups. I read the reviews and found out I was just confused by the different packaging. I brewed a cup and it was a very good cup of coffee. It worked perfectly in my Keurig maker. My story has a happy ending.
Fog Chaser lives up to it's name!!  One cup and I'm good to go.  I love the style of the cup as well... less plastic!

Good and bad for without a bottom k-cup plastic.  Good is that like one user say, no hot water going through another plastic.  Bad, is that you need to keep the coffee in a sealed bag once you opened the factory sealed bag.  I wish it comes with a resealable bag for this.  They already save money by not using the plastic bottom half of the k-cup.The coffee do taste good though.

column9: This is my absolute favorite coffee!
column10: Fog Chaser is the tastiest full bodied coffee I have had from my Kerig maker. I love this coffee! My husband calls it my "Foggy day" coffee. It truly chases the fog away!

This coffee is very rich and fresh .  The only downside of this product is that when you brew it you should have a wide brimmed cup under it, because it comes out of the pot, in an uneven stream and goes all over.  Other wise its delicious.

column9: Better tasting than any of the K-Cups to date!
column10: This is really a great cup of coffee. It has a deep complex taste and is not at all bitter. It is a good balanced strong tasting brew if made at the 8oz recommended level. While not a K-cup per se, it is just as well thought out with it's open mesh design. It is basically the inside of the K-Cup without the plastic bottom.  The person that gave it 2 stars because he/she says the 1st cup may be good but the rest will go stale, is just plain stupid. I guess he/she has never heard of a plastic bag or container. Once you open the package just stick them in an airtight container or plastic bag...oooh that's difficult! I wonder when he wrote that review if he had something more than just coffee in his cup??

We wanted to try something different and this coffee didn't disappoint!  We prefer bold flavored coffee which this is.  I was concerned that the pods might not fit my basic model Keurig but they fit perfect.  Less waste with these K-Cups because they have a filter type bottom instead of the plastic cup.  We will definatately order these again!
The coffee tastes good and the packaging is less wasteful. The price is very nice also. Thanks for providing an alternative to the standard K cup.

Before I purchased this coffee, I read the other reviews. All rated this coffee extremely well, with a few concerns stating it did fit their coffee maker. Not knowing if that would be the case with me, I took a chance and was not dissapointed. It fit my machine with no problem, the smell of the coffee is exquisite and it lives up to the excellent reviews.  Everyone in my family that tried it, loves it.. Keep up the good work!

column9: Flavor ok but they do not fit right
column10: I ordered these because the price seemed good. I didn't care so much that they weren't the same as regular K-Cups as people said they fit. They do not. On our brewer, you have to hold the handle down because the cup doesn't fit all the way down into the holder. I like to do other things while I'm brewing the coffee knowing it will be ready when I'm ready to grab it. Not so with this one. You have to babysit the machine.  We have a B-40.I will not buy again. THEY DO NOT FIT!

No, these do not look like traditional K-cups, but worked perfectly in my machine. You need a small container as you only open 12 at a time-the rest stay vacuum sealed. I can't understand the fuss about the packaging-it is a simple thing to put them in a Tupperware type container. The bottom line for me is that the subscription price for this coffer is about $.41 per serving as opposed to $.70 per serving-and the coffee is GREAT! I love the coffee and I now drink it daily. column9: Great price for a strong, delicious k-cup coffee!

column9: Chasing the Fog and Forgetting the Bug!
column10: I have been drinking coffee for over 40 plus years now.  Folks, I have tried so many varieties from Instant to Drip to K cups, and the list goes on.  Hopefully, the reader gets the picture...I love my coffee.  Yet, I am not sure what this "stuff" is.  Here is my experience...First, I get the shipment.  Open it up, and I must admit, I do like the nice box the coffee arrives in.  I do appreciate the added note on the box from the Robinson Family along with their mission statement."Taste the Difference - Make a Difference - Community Aid Program" and there is more information on the side of the box which really sort of made me "feel good" about my purchase.  The Robinson Family goes on to state "Offering the best value to you, our customer.  Treating our employees, suppliers, and customers as if they were part of our family."  I mean all this really made me feel good and I was glad I had purchased a product where a "family" supported others...Yet, that is where it ended.  I opened the box, cut open the plastic sealed containers this "cups" come in, and grabbed my first little strange looking but new looking "k cup".  Please note, as others have said, these are completely different than an actual "k cup", but I thought unique and liked the design....UNTIL...yes, UNTIL...I hate to write this, but the very first thing I noted on the side of this "bag cup" was something that looked like a bug!!  It politely dropped in the palm of my hand, and since it was not "wiggling", I figured I could examine it very closely.  I did....YUCK!  It was some sort of freaking small, slim BUG!!  I thought maybe it was my ole' eyes, but had my son examine it and he confirmed my verdict....Did I go ahead and try the coffee???  Well, again, I hate to admit this, but I figured the bug could not "kill" me, so yes...I went ahead and tried the other "cup" things (honestly, I don't know what to call these little cups").  My first reaction was just "disgust"...The flavor was weak and the cream and sugar simply diluted to the bottom of the cup.  Nothing like the Rev K Cups or other K cups I had used...So, I went to the computer to write a review...no, not today I thought...I wanted to be fair, because, again, I felt a part of the "Family" the manufacturer had written about on the box...and maybe the "bug" was still in my mind!Thus, here I sit today several days later, and just finished another of these cups....and after using a few of the things...I just honestly cannot understand why all the high positives written by other reviewers?  Honestly?  I am trying to like these things due to the price and the "Family" caring thing...but, this coffee is simply too weak and does not taste like "coffee" to me.  In comparison, it sort of reminds me of an off the wall instant coffee on the weak scale...Folks, all of you who have written such positive reviews...trust me, I want to be open minded...I want to like this coffee.  I tried smaller cups on my K cup machine, and it simply gets worse...So, in conclusion, maybe I got a "bad box"?  I mean should there have been a "bug" in it to begin with??  Even with that...get past the bug issue...where is the flavor?  Why does the cream and sugar simply dissolve to the bottom of the cup leaving a bad looking residue as you get to the last sip?  It dissolves "into the coffee" with other brands...I love the price, and wish I could like this...is there another type other than the "Fog Chaser"???  Would like to stay with the Robinson Family, but not left in the "Fog" as this is sort of how I feel trying to drink this coffee ....."Fog Chaser"????  Well, I am definitely "chasing the Fog"...trying to understand how this is called "coffee"????I will continue through this box the best I can, and "if" I find one of the cups different, then in all fairness, I will update this review to treat the "Robinson Family" fair...And yes, I guess maybe I am crazy to drink through all these things since the bug was on the first one, but I figure the hot water should kill any harmful bacteria...hope I am right??  But, again, I want to emphasize, it is not the "bug" that is causing my dislike of this "wattery, weak...very odd coffee".....

While I am happy with the coffee itself, I find the description of this item as "for Keurig K-Cup Brewers" to be slightly misleading.As a recent reviewer points out that these OneCup pods are mesh pouches with a foil top. Twelve of these pods are contained in a sealed plastic bag. Once the bag is opened, the coffee does seem to be more "exposed" to air which raises the possibility that they then go stale faster than a sealed K-Cup.Comments on the previous review said that the coffee has noticeable degradation in quality after 14 days of opening the sealed plastic bag. column4: Dave "Brevity is the soul of wit"
column10: What some think is residue is actually crema, though not as heavy as in an espresso shot. Crema is a flavorful, aromatic, reddish-brown froth made when air bubbles combine with fine-ground coffee's soluble oils. The strong presence of crema indicates a quality, well-ground coffee Crema helps give espresso a fuller flavor, longer aftertaste than drip coffee. This is excellent coffee and the crema makes it better.

column9: Not the best, not the worst.
column10: I recently ordered this because I was excited about the reduced plastic in the packaging. Interestingly, the day I ordered it my husband came home with the same brand from the grocery store, so I've now tried 2 different flavors. I would give both the same review. The coffee is okay. It's not horrendous, as some people seem to imply, and its not amazing either. The smell is good and smells like nice fresh coffee when you open the box. The flavor is nice enough too. I also love super strong coffee. I drink Revv, Jet Fuel, Wake Up Call, etc. I would not say that this coffee rivals them, but it is stronger than some other medium roast coffees.Big reasons why I wouldn't give this 5 stars:1) The coffee gets very watered down when brewed on a larger cup size. I usually do the 10 oz size and this coffee just doesn't cut it for that. I feel it becomes more like coffee flavored water at that point. 8 oz is better, but its ideal at 6 oz. So, now I just save it for when I want a small cup.2) There is a strange film that brews with the coffee. You can see it floating on top and it sticks to the sides of the mug when you tilt it, so there is like a ring of residue that gets left around the edge where the coffee moved away. You can also see it as darker specks floating on top after you add creamer. I don't know what this is. I have no other coffee that does this. It doesn't really change the taste or texture or anything, but I just don't like it.I think the packaging is a big plus though. I am not sure why the cups being open is such an issue for people. I just put all mine in a zip lock bag (that I can just keep reusing) to keep it air tight. It's really not that difficult. Plus I think it's important to cut down on plastic waste.So all in all, I do plan to buy this coffee again. I like that I can reduce waste and I like it enough that its good for a midday refresher since it has to be a small cup. We are also on a tight budget so that helps as well. However, I don't see myself replacing all my coffee with it, because I want a much larger and stronger cup of coffee in the morning and brewing two of these eliminates both the value and the positive aspects of less waste.

column9: Not your average K-cup, but worth a taste
column10: I have my concerns about this coffee's packaging, but the important part first: It tastes good. Fog Chaser is a little more robust than I like for a morning blend (I tend toward a Dunkin Donuts style coffee first thing in the AM), but is perfect for afternoon or evening. The nonstandard pods fit into my B70 and while there has been occasional sediment, it's not been a problem with the majority of my 36-pod pack; at least, not as bad as (say) Grove Square. Yes, I'd buy these again.Now the negatives. As has been stated, the pods aren't plastic cups with embedded filters, sealed by a foil cover, but rather filter pouches with a plastic ring and foil cover. There's no need to punch a drain hole in the plastic cup, since there isn't one. I've heard concerns about the Keurig success causing more spent K-cups to be dumped in trash tips and landfills; I'd also guess that the construction makes it a non-trivial recycling task. So a redesign with less plastic would seem like a good thing.However, one of the charms of Keurig is that the cup is packed in a relatively inert gas: I've heard nitrogen, which would make sense. Oxygen is the enemy of coffee. Old coffee goes stale because it oxidizes. Keeping air away from coffee keeps it fresh... but the coffee in the San Francisco Bay Coffee company's packaging hasn't this feature. The bags (containing twelve pods each) are heavy-duty plastic with a metal button of unknown purpose, and perhaps those bags are filled with something other than oxygen... but as soon as you take them out, the coffee begins to deteriorate.Not that this happens in a matter of seconds, or even days. After all, keeping the lid on a pound can of coffee (I can actually remember when a pound was sixteen ounces, not 13.5) kept the coffee fresh enough, assuming you were a regular drinker. If you use a ziploc bag to store the unused pods from an opened bag, I'm sure that they'll stay fresh enough in the week or two that the bag lasts.My concern, though, is for occasional coffee drinkers, for whom the Keurig system is a godsend. For example, I dated a woman who hated coffee, but wanted me to have some when I visited. Having fresh coffee in an inert storage container would have been great. These, though, might go bad in between my visits to her house.So in conclusion, go ahead and buy these if you're a frequent coffee drinker who will finish a whole 12-pod bag in less than a month. Keep a couple of ziploc bags (sandwich bags hold 6) for storage. Companies that go through a whole lot of K-cups ought really to like these, especially since they're about 10% under the cost of most K-cups.

I was a little worried about this k-cup since it is shaped differently from the regular k-cups. Instead of being in a fully plastic container, only the top is plastic. The bottom part is enclosed in a coffee filter type holding. While this means that when I opened the sealed wrapper I was hit with the delicious aroma of coffee, something I miss when I open a regular pack of k-cups, it also means I have to store the remaining cups in a tupperware or storage ziploc type bag to keep the remaining cups from going stale. This isn't a big deal, just something to mention. These also wouldn't fit in the normal k-cup carousel.I have a b60 and the cup fit perfectly, brewed up great, disposal was easy and the filter didn't tear or leak as I was throwing it way.Fog chaser is a bold deep brew (I brew on the middle button of my keurig) The coffee is very smooth and mellow with a terrific aroma. There is no bitter or burned taste. This is quickly becoming my favorite keurig coffee and I can't wait to try the other offerings from this company.

column9: Doesn't fit in all Keurig makers
column10: This is decent coffee at a good price, but the K-cup is made different and doesn't fit in all Keurig brewers.  The instructions on the package actually tell you that but the description when you buy it does not. I have two brewers and it only fits in one of them

column9: WARNING - open mesh coffee pods, NOT K-Cups
column10: I've urged Amazon to change this product's listing so as not to trick anyone else into buying it, but until they do, I want to add my voice to the revelations hidden in a few reviews that are already here. Please be warned that while the first cup of this coffee is tasty, the second is unlikely to be as good, and the twelfth is almost guaranteed to be disappointing unless you're the twelve-cup-a-day sort of household.Why? Simply put, these are not K-Cups. They are not individually sealed portions, but instead are open mesh coffee pods, not dissimilar to Senseo pods, topped with a K-Cup-like plastic ring and foil cover. That cover does make them work in Keurig brewers, but you lose the important freshness-preserving feature of K-Cups. The company could lessen this problem by putting its pods in a resealable plastic bag, but they chose to instead use a plastic bag reminiscent of those in cereal boxes -- just much, much harder to open. That's especially ironic given Amazon's recent move toward frustration-free packaging.I strongly encourage you to move on to another product until the San Francisco Bay Coffee folks can temper their (laudable) green-focused pod design with some reasonable solution for keeping the coffee fresh for more than a day or so once you open the box.

I have not picked this item up on Amazon but in a retail store in my area in North Carolina.  I had seen it on Amazon but when I saw it local I gave it a try and I am glad I did.  This is a rich and robust flavor, with a note of nuts, one that wipes the cobwebs away in the morning.  Yes it is nice that the product uses less plastic but that is only a side note the quality of the coffee is top notch.  The only negative side comment I can make is that sometimes the top gets stuck on the upper needle of the Keurig but no problem just pull it off from the top rather than picking it up out of the brewing basket, and if you close the machine and open again it is always off the needle anyway.

This is my second favorite flavor from SFBC.  Breakfast blend is still the best.  All flavors have plenty of flavor for a 16oz travel mug. (If you don't have the larger cup size on your machine, brew at the small cup setting and lift the handle and brew again) Can't beat the value especially if you get them via Amazon subscription.  Hey Amazon when are you going to sell these in the 80 pack?

column9: Very good coffee, nice alternative to k-cup
column10: Having a cup, soon to be two cups, of Fog Chaser from San Francisco Bay Coffee this morning. Very good. They call these "OneCup" but they work in Keurig brewers. Guessing this is a result of the k-cup patent or copyright, whatever it is, running out but wow, this is some good good coffee.

column9: Good Coffee at Good Price (good=not GREAT)
column10: We've ordered the Fog Chaser OneCup twice now. The first time we ordered it, I LOVED it. We are avid coffee drinkers in my house, and both love a nice bold coffee. Since the price was right and we liked the coffee, we ordered again. The 2nd shipment we received was still "good" coffee, but it wasn't as great as the first. My husband says he couldn't tell much difference, but the 2nd shipment did not have the same smooth finish and mouth-watering aroma as the original. That being said, it did not stop us from drinking it all, but I do have to wonder which is the abnormality! I rated this at a 4 since we were so impressed by the first shipment, and I really like the way the OneCup brews. As other reviewers mentioned, there is a "crema" produced by the OneCup that you rarely see with a K-Cup, which is NICE! I like the less packaging, and don't mind the occasional sediment in my cup (when we brew coffee, we generally do French Press, so we can handle that!). If I had the option of rating 3.5 I would have, since the quality of the 2nd shipment would definitely rank a 3 most likely. I do think we will try this again and see if "the third time is the charm". I will try to remember to update on what we think so that we can provide some feedback as far as consistency goes.Thanks for reading!

Bold and rich. LOVE this coffee for a fast wake-me-up in the morning, and pick-me-up mid day. The name is perfectly suited to the delightful temperament of this brew. MUST store in airtight container after opening the plastic bags though, or coffee will lose it's potency.

column9: finally coffee for my picky palate!
column10: Recently I have become more and more choosy with my coffee. I own a Keurig one-cup brewer as well as a traditional coffee maker.For years, I have been using the same coffee brand ( med or dark, middle-of-the road priced) and it was affordable and it tasted just fine. Lately, I was lacking depth and body when brewing in the keurig( I have the cup you can put your own coffee in, which saves resources and $). It seemed like I couldnt' pack enough flavor into the little chamber to really have the right strength. The pre-packed, ready to use K cups were much better, but at 3 cups/day for me not feasible in the long run.I read the reviews of the San Francisco Bay coffee ( fog chaser) and the price appealed to me and also what customers had described, so I tried it. Besides the much more affordable price and far more "green" packaging, I find the flavor fantastic!Bold, yet sophisticated, not just strong- really pleasant flavor ! A very good choice at an attractive price!. These cups look different, but I like them much better with their filter-like body and 12-count bagging. Now I don't feel guilty when I indulge with more than 1 K cup. For loose coffee to put into the reusable cup I choose a def. dark roast like italian or french, which is very comparable to the Fog chaser's aroma.

There are so many k cups and flavors out there...for a baseline, my go to cup was donut shop by the coffee people, until now.  I really enjoy this coffee and will purchase again.  Smells very fresh, like the packaging (not just 50 thrown in a box), lower price than competitors, and the flavor is perfect for me.  Great job San Francisco Bay!

SFBC's Fog Chaser is on the bold side... dark, rich, but not too much aftertaste.  A great daily coffee. Be aware that the entire cup is not plastic, but the bottom portion is almost filter material. This might affect how long you keep the cups before using. The cups are vacuum sealed into a larger plastic bag, so that should help with freshness...The cost is on the low end for k-cups and makes this coffee even more inviting!!!  I definitely recommend as a staple daily coffee.All the best,Jay

The Keurig cups always had something missing. They reminded me of coffee but always tasted a little funny. I really do think it's all the plastic surrounding the coffee. I didn't get much use out of my Keurig until I found this coffee. I am reordering today!
Can't beat this price and tastes decent! Impressed with the k cup design, no mess. Will be buying more for sure

Fantastic Coffee, at a a fraction of the price of the freeze dried Keurig K-cup's, all of which are made by the same company, with the same tasteless coffee bean, no matter what the name of the coffee.  I can't imagine paying a dollar a cup for a "donut house" k-cup that is made of Folgers.  What a joke.

This is a great pod to reduce some of the wear and tear on the keurig, the coffee tastes good, no grounds in contrast with other reviews, less packaging, and it's a nice size package to keep "in reserve".  Better than Folgers, better than Donut House, not as good as Newman's Own.  That's about the limit of my K-cup experience so far.
I love this coffee. I started buying it in the grocery store, but this is a lot cheaper at Amazon. Rich, flavorful, and smells just like I ground the beans myself. Going to re-order right now.

I just received my 80 count box of San Francisco Fog Chaser K-Cups.  I ripped open one of the dated/sealed packets, pulled out one of the 10 coffee pods.I made a cup of coffee, perfecto.  Best coffee I've had from this machine hands down, and I've probably put 50 different brands and made over 1000 cups from this guy.Highly recommended.

The coffee comes in the K-cup filters without a bottom.  I assume this is to save money and reduce plastic.  It works fine in all K-cup brewers that I've tried.The coffee itself is really good.  It has a very bold taste but not too bitter.  Tastes much better with some cream and sugar.I ended up subscribing to these because I like them so much.  Definitely worth a try for coffee drinkers.  I only give items 5 stars if they far exceed expectations, so this gets 4 stars.

I was looking for a good quality coffee in a K-cup to use with my Kuerig. I have the reusable cup and love it but was looking for the convenience of the pre-filled K-cups for workday mornings.These K-cups were exactly what I was looking for, convenience and delicious coffee! I prefer a bolder coffee and this Fog Chaser fit the bill. I also felt this was an excellent deal considering most K-cups retail for $10.00-$16.99 for a package of 12 K-cups (and sometimes 10) and this was 80 cups for just over $30.00. The other thing I love about this is being able to have it on the subscription program.  You can set up your delivery to be delivered whenever you like beginning with 1 month intervals and you get a small discount on the price when you order through a subscription. With a quantity of 80, I've set my deliveries to come every 4 months but it may turn out that I will have to shorten it to every three months.If you have a Kuerig and love the convenience of the pre-filled K-cups, you can't go wrong with this product. It is a bold coffee but this company makes several types that are available in several blends. I highly recommend this product and the added  value of the subscription option.

column9: Replaced Starbucks as my all time favorite!
column10: When I got my Keurig, I couldn't wait to get my favorite Starbucks coffee in K Cups. When I saw this, I liked the design of the cup and the price is much better too. I'm so glad I decided to give it a try. Doing a side by side comparison, Fog Chaser wins hands down! If you like a bold cup that lingers on your tongue and hold up under creamer too (I use unsweetened coconut milk), you will be happy you tried this coffee. Oh! A huge added bonus of the new environmentally friendly K Cup design is that you get that heavenly coffee aroma from the minute you open the vacuum sealed bag! You don't have to wait until its brewing to "wake up and smell the coffee!" :)

This is the best coffee I've had since my Mom's percolator brand.  The best part though is the cup can be re-used. I have a K-cap My-Kap Green Reusable 3 Piece Cap Set for K-Cups and I just clean out the cup and refill with whatever coffee I choose.  It's really the perfect design for re-use as the grounds dry out completely overnight and dump out very easily. I'm buying the whole bean San Francisco coffee to grind and refill the cup. The possibilities are endless!

Personally, I received this product by going down the list of K-Cups trying to find that perfect cup to put on scheduled delivery.  This is a nice bold coffee, and oddly fiscal.  I personally like the first brew, and the house mate likes the second and third, now THAT is a good deal.

Cheaper than typical k-cups, more environmentally friendly, and better, fresher, stronger coffee. This stuff is dynamite.  They're priced where the traditional k-cups used to be priced, but they're better coffee.

column9: SIMPLY THE BEST COFFEE OUT THERE & THE BEST PRICE!!
column10: I adore this coffee!!! I also tried the french roast style (which i usually drink in other brands) BUT I LOVE this FOG LIFTER roast so much better! It's simply the best K-Cup I've had! And the cost is amazing, especially if you sign up for auto delivery, which is cool because you can choose your delivery time and not just a default one!!! LOVE IT! WILL KEEP PURCHASING FOR SURE!

column9: Decent product but not a good way to keep fresh
column10: Bought this product however it doesnt seem like a great way to keep the coffee airtight. I tried the other K-cup similar cups and they seem to keep it fresher.
This is a robust roast. Definitely a morning coffee.  We love the flavor and the value! Be sure to store in an airtight container to maintain the flavor.

column9: Don't let the smell fool ya. It's pretty awesome.
column10: I don't usually write a review unless I think a item deserves it but this coffee deserves it. It came in 3 separate vacuum sealed bags. Make sure you store them in a proper container after you open them or they will go bad. When I opened one, the smell was super strong. I thought the coffee was going to be bitter but after brewing it in my Keurig B130 a few times I was hooked. Not bitter at all but the smell is a little strong. But it grew on me. I brew it with 8oz. of water and the strength is good enough for me. Just a bit of creamer or milk and no sugar. I drink only a cup a day. Also, its cheaper than normal K cups and less waste. I'm not going to say that this will be my favorite forever, but it is good and if you are looking at trying something new with your K cup maker then these are worth a shot. I will keep these stocked along with other the flavors of K cups I have enjoyed.

I recently purchased these K-Cups, I have to admit, because of the price per cup. And now I can honestly say I will never go back to the regular K-Cups again! I usually run a K-Cup through the largest setting and then through the smallest (my coffee cup is rather large :). This Fog Chaser coffee holds up rather well. I've gotten a great, bold cup of joe every morning since receiving these. There have been no problems with grounds in the cup as sometimes happens with regular K-Cups or the refillable K-Cups.The 80 count box came with a reusable storage container that holds a week of pods. It's just a flimsy, clear plastic container but it does keep the coffee fresh.

column9: Great cup of coffee and the price is right!
column10: This is the second month we've ordered this coffee and love it!  If you like a strong cup of coffee, this is it.  And, the price can't be beat!
The fog chaser has a great bold body taste,unlike some brands which leave a harsh after taste.Great product which I recommend.
I have tried 5 or 6 different brands and found this brand to be the better one. I am sticking with this for now.

First time trying SF coffee and found it to be a good coffee with a reasonable taste. Yes, the coffee smells burned prior to use but I believe thatunless you are a  connoisseur of coffee I believe most might smelled "burnt".  Good coffee for the price and the "K-Cup" new packaging works just as well as the original stle K-Cup packaging. I believe I will try another brand for taste but would stay with SFbay if the price were 5 cents less per cup.  I drink alot of coffee.!!

column9: Beware even if you don't open you can't return
column10: Not the coffee for us. Very strong. Did the subscribe and save, for got to cancel the next shipment, went to and complete the return forms- No such luck. Great idea, just tastes awful. First item that I could not return, back to buy coffee at QVC, they will take it back if we do not like it.

Ahhh...nothing like a good cup of coffee! I'm a bargain hunter and have considered going back to my drip coffee due to the rising prices of K cups.I read all the reviews,and feeling there was nothing to lose I debated between French Roast and Fog Chaser. San Francisco Bay Fog Chaser did not disappoint (haven't tried the French Roast yet). Fog Chaser is a moderatly bold coffee, smooth, with no hint of bitterness. As for the skeptics concerned with the "netted" base of the cup affecting taste and freshness...the product is packaged in mini packs ( sealed thick plastic) of 8 cups to protect freshness. In addition, I feel the netting (not flimsy by any means) offers a better fitration system that the typical K cup. I only write reviews about products that excite me, or repulse me. Obviously, I am a San Francisco Bay Coffee fan. If you choose to try this product, I'm pretty sure you will be pleasantly surprised.

column9: Excellent Taste and More Robust Brewing with These Type of Pods
column10: I decided to give these a try based on the price, the favorable reviews here on Amazon, and its sales rank in the K-cup store.  I was not disappointed as this is a strong, but not too strong, good-tasting coffee that not only tastes great but has a nice aroma.The pods are a little different than your traditional plastic K-cup portion as, instead of any plastic around the sides or bottom you have basically a mesh coffee filter holding the coffee grounds.  This appears to make a more complete brew, and allows more of the flavor to come into the actual coffee.  You will see a dirty residue at the bottom of your cup due to this filtration system vs. a "clean" look from a normal K-cup pod.  This seems to make sense as the normal K-cup pod has all of the brewed coffee escaping through the pinprick hole vs. the full brewing experience of these pods.As the pods are in this filtration medium the coffee is not air-tight sealed after you open the package of pods.  I have put the unused ones in a sealed Ziploc bag to keep them fresh.I also shared this with some folks in the office, who liked it so much they ordered their own so it's not just me who likes this stuff.  Who knows, I may have found a new favorite coffee!

column9: Good Alternative to More Pricey "Bold" K-Cups
column10: SF Bay Coffee's Fog Chaser was a nice "bold" surprise.  I am a big fan of Amazon's Subscribe & Save program and have been getting my K-cups this way for over a year.  Of course, once you find one you absolutely love (Timothy's World Midnight Magic), poof!  The Magic's gone!  Midnight Magic is still available on Amazon, though no longer offered through Subscribe & Save, and I refuse to pay $35 for 48 K-cups of any brand.  S & S now offers SF Bay Coffee's Fog Chaser and based on the quantity of favorable reviews, I decided to give it a shot.  The pods are far different than what we've all been used to, but they work like a charm, have less waste, and deliver a pretty bold, smooth cup of coffee.  My morning coffee always consists of two pods at the 6 oz. setting each for one eye-opening 12 oz. mug of coffee.  On that setting, Fog Chaser lives up to its name.  I have noticed some residue occasionally, but it certainly is minimal.  The pods come packed in plastic bags (12 pods/bag).  Once cut open, I just fold over the edge, clip it and store the bag in the fridge.  Strength is a personal decision, and to me, more than 6 oz. of water with ANY pod is too weak.  If you are a fan of Rev of Jet Fuel, this coffee is comparable.
This coffee was really good Fogchaser will get you going. It's a strong bold cup of coffee.  This cofee is valued price with a great taste!

column9: Great Price, but change in concept....
column10: Decided to give these a try based on price.  The coffee tastes great but since the 'cups' don't have the plastic bottoms (a filter element), we had to store in a sealed jar to keep them fresh and not have the coffee bean smell thru-out the house.  (or you could use a plastic ziploc - original bag was not re-sealable).  They did one thing finally right - you don't have to pay MORE for going green when buying LESS packaging.  Kudos.
My new favorite!  A few Gr. Mtn. are great: Br. Blend, Half/Caff especially.  Most other brands are more like Folgers than real flavor brews.  How do I get free shipping?

column9: Love the packaging! Could be a smoother coffee
column10: These k cups are great for being green!  I love less plastic and don't get grounds in my cup. That being said the coffee is pretty good.  It's hard to find a really strong K cup coffee that's not burnt or harsh tasting.  This one is pretty close to being smooth.  I wish Amazon would offer B***sta kcups on auto delivery!

i dont no what the big fuss is about a lot of bad reviews but if u read the description you shoulld no it comes revealed and not in plastic like regualr kcups anyhow i ordered the fogchaser and they were great i amade iced coffee with mine and the flavor was perfect i just keep it in some tupperware to keep fresh is all i plan on buying all 3 flavors and encourage they should come out with even more flavors the price is awsome beats paying 15 bucks for 18 kucps when i just paid 14 for 36 kcups i will def keep on buying these

The price was the initial reason for my purchase but I would have to say now that my reorder is based on the taste. Coffee is very rich and fresh tasting even without the sealed k-cup design. I will continue to reorder if the price stays down under the other k-cups.

column9: Very Good K-Cup Coffee at a nice price
column10: Fog Chaser has a very good flavor, and it is reasonably strong especially for a K-Cup.  I like it better than their French Roast version, which seems stronger but more harsh to me; and I like very strong coffee.  Their Rainforest version has a more mellow taste that is also very good, but it is weaker strength than Fog Chaser.  The price for any of the versions, especially for the "subscribe and save", is very good.  The packaging, which is a box of 3 sealed bags of 12 is fine to deal with; once you open a sealed bag (you can't reseal the bag), just use a ziplock to seal the remainder for the week.

I have been a picky Keurig fan for about ten years, have always bought my coffee from either onegreatcup or amazon (because stores just don't have the selection), and until now had settled on Jet Fuel as my favorite -- just so you know what I like. FogChaser is in that league: rich, deep, dark, zesty, overall INTERESTING and best of all (unlike the plastic-bottomed K-cups) brewing it makes my kitchen smell good again. I'm putting it on subscription.  A good find; a keeper -- glad I tried it.

25 lbs. of hard licorice pieces were dumped into kitchen trash bags, unsealed, then put into a cardboard box.  The most disgusting, unsanitary packaging I've ever seen.  I tossed the entire thing in the trash.To top it off, the first ingredient in the whole thing was corn syrup.  Yuk.Avoid like the plague.

column9: A nice step up from plain rice cereal
column10: Our nine-month-old daughter is ready for a more substantial breakfast than plain cereals.  We want her to get the nutrients and vitamins she needs (especially iron), so plain fruit or vegetables aren't enough.  This blend of fruit and grains (and, in some cases, yogurt) provides everything she needs for a good breakfast and keeps her full for several hours.  Plus, the flavors are not overly sweet.  One note:  at least two of these flavors include yogurt.  Some babies younger than 1-year may have a reaction to yogurt and other dairy foods, so just watch out for that.

column9: Buyer Beware - Jars break in transit!
column10: My daughter loves Earth's Best food items but after two broken shipments from Amazon, I decided to buy from the grocery store.  I sent an email to Amazon but my issue was never resolved.
My son loves all the food by earths best but would like to mention that it's way cheaper buying in store than amazon. Amazon charges 2 - 3$ more than stores.

We feed our baby this Wholesome Breakfast at any time of the day, not just for breakfast.  We're happy she's getting a good balance of vitamins and minerals.  Most jarred baby food is pretty light on the calories and nutrition, but the plain cereals that are fortified with essential vitamins/minerals are so boring and don't train a baby to enjoy different flavors.  We've been mixing cereal into our baby's food to enhance the nutrition, but that's inconvenient and messy.  This Wholesome Breakfast provides the best of both worlds:  the vitamins/minerals of a fortified cereal but with the stronger flavors of a real food.  We particularly like that this food contains yogurt.  When she was young (~6 months old), our baby loved yogurt but couldn't eat it plain because it would cause a rash around her mouth.  She was never bothered by the yogurt in this food, though, perhaps because it was mixed with other things.  Now that she's older (10 months), our baby can eat all the yogurt she wants without a skin reaction, but for awhile, this variety of Wholesome Breakfast was the only source of her favorite food.

We're not sure why, but this this flavor of Earth's Best Wholesome Breakfast (Peach, Pear, and Barley) is our baby's favorite flavor.  She'll eat this any time of the day, and we're happy she's getting a good balance of vitamins and minerals.  Most jarred baby food is pretty light on the calories and nutrition, but the plain cereals that are fortified with essential vitamins/minerals are so boring and don't train a baby to enjoy different flavors.  We've been mixing cereal into our baby's food to enhance the nutrition, but that's inconvenient and messy.  This Wholesome Breakfast provides the best of both worlds:  the vitamins/minerals of a fortified cereal but with the stronger flavors of a real food.  Also, our baby is a picky eater, so we're thrilled to find something she likes that's more substantial than Puffs!

My daughter loves the entire Earths Best line.  I taste everything before I feed it to her and each item tastes pure and fresh.  Very happy.  We've tasted other popular name brands, and Earths Best is really good in comparison.

My son is lactose intolerant but he's able to eat this for some reason!  Moreover, it's great to start off a day with a nutritious meal versus eating empty calaries with little to no nutritional benefit.  Regardless, I'm very pleased with the quality and taste.  Yes, I tasted this and it is delish!

column9: Fruit, dairy & grains...what more could you ask for!
column10: My little guy just loves this jar. I love the line of breakfast blends.  I am happy with Amazon's "grocery" business. It is great to have the convenience to order these on-line and have home delivery.  I can't imagine going the store and having to get a whole case and go through check out. I try to make him some meals, but I trust Earth's Best and love the flavor combo's and they are so convenient.

column9: Earth's best Organic Pears and apple oatmeal
column10: I tried all kinds of oatmeal to give my LO but this is her favorite one. I also love the fact that it comes on time.

If I had only figured out to order baby food online before.  The price is right on the money and the convenience of the shipping to the house is great.  No need to go to the store and have baby jars flying all over the cart.  This flavor is my baby's favorite.  It's a go to when she is not in the mood for anything else.

I love Earth's Best products and only use them to feed my baby, besides home made foods. I rate this one one star because the seller didn't specify that this product contains milk, which my baby cannot tolerate since he is lactose-intolerant. So for us, it was a waste of money, and I bought two packs...

This baby food, labeled for 6+ months, contains heavy cream. My baby could not digest it; we had a very bad day. Maybe I missed that in the description, but in any case, everywhere I've read and according to my pediatrician, you're supposed to avoid cow's milk products before age 1 (why they make formula using cow's milk and not a much more digestible milk like goat baffles me and is a rant for another time--my son drinks the lactose free kind, in any case). I ordered another variety of "Wholesome breakfast" too: Pear, Apple, Oatmeal. Same thing there. I'm guessing they all have heavy cream in them.
My daughter likes it now, but when she was younger she did not want to have it! Go figure! Now she is almost 14 months she digs the flavor.
My son hated it. I tasted some and saw why. It's tart and the barley gives it a weird smell and flavor. Yuck!

I wish Amazon would include a list of ingredients on baby food in bulk. This has cream in it and my baby has a cow's milk intolerance. I had already opened the jar when I read the ingredients and now I'm stuck with 15 jars of food I can't use. So disappointing.
I bought quite a lot of these in the past. My son loved them. I like the fact that they are organic and the combination of fruits and vegetables in them is just right.

column9: Good breakfast, especially on the go.
column10: We do fruit and cereal for breakfast daily.  This comes in handy when we are on the go, since i dont have to bring cereal long.  I also like that it is 4.5 ounces, since some of the earth's best fruit and cereal combos are only 4 ounces.
My son eats these for breakfast every morning and he seems to really enjoy them. It is a nice alternative to fruit and rice cereal and it has all the nourishment my son needs to start his day.
Price was great, variety, flavor was good, baby likes it! She takes a while to eat, but it's safe and clean to leave in the refrigerator.
Great baby foods!  I like the variety pack.  Much cheaper than buying it from the local grocers or co-op!  I Just wish they came in the squeezie pouches!

column9: Great and easy food for the baby
column10: Right combination. We originally thought our baby had some allergies. However, as we fed these food baby got used to them and she liked them all.
Little one loves these and glass is recyclable forever which plastic (Gerber) is not. About the same price, food is healthier and she's more likely to eat this stuff.
We love the organic baby food. It costs just a small amount more, but it is totally worth it.  Our son loves the different choices.
I love how it's thicker than other Stage 2 baby food. My son gobbles it down! Way better than the lunch or dinner varities!
This was by far my daughters favorite Earth's Best breakfast.  It's nice that it contains organic fruit and whole grains.  Plus the prices on amazon can't be beat, especially with subscribe and save!

column9: My son loves it! Very nutritional!
column10: This is one of my sons favorites. Even though it's called "wholesome breakfast" he usually has this for lunch. It is packed with nutrients, including 35% of his daily iron. This is a staple in our baby's diet!

We initially tried few sample from Ralph's and our Baby started liking it .. We don't give formula to our Baby and we give only Mom's milk.i think when we combine that with this wholesome breakfast you will have a satisfaction that you are really taking a good care of the Baby..What's more it had got more calories than the regular baby foods and it had got 35% iron which i consider important.. It has dates in it. Very few baby foods for breakfast have dates in them.. on the whole it's really a wholesome breakfast.. Add organic on top of that what else can you ask for.. I had only one thing to complain about.. it's availability is rare.. i had to wait for a month to get it.. I don't find it in the store shelves either..

We feed our baby this Wholesome Breakfast at any time of the day, not just for breakfast.  We're happy she's getting a good balance of vitamins and minerals.  Most jarred baby food is pretty light on the calories and nutrition, but the plain cereals that are fortified with essential vitamins/minerals are so boring and don't train a baby to enjoy different flavors.  We've been mixing cereal into our baby's food to enhance the nutrition, but that's inconvenient and messy.  This Wholesome Breakfast provides the best of both worlds:  the vitamins/minerals of a fortified cereal but with the stronger flavors of a real food.  Also, our baby is a picky eater, so we're thrilled to find something she likes that's more substantial than Puffs!
I enjoy most of the Yogi teas but this particular one tastes almost sinful. I don't know that it necessarily tastes a lot like vanilla or hazelnut but it has a very delicious spicy taste.

The title above refers not only to a semi-obscure Damon Runyan-based movie with Bob Hope (we ALL knew that), but to these classic lemon drops with a truly international pedigree:Made in Spain; owned by the French(Cadbury France, located at 143 Boulevard Romain Rolland, Paris; imported by New Jersey's own "Euro-American Brands," Paramus, NJ  07652.All the way from Paris to your local candy seller or movie theater (which is where I experieced my first taste of La Vie en Lemon).  They were everything a lemon drop should be: A sugary entrance, developing into a deeply satisfying, soul-stirring essence of pure lemon. The mouth-watering joy of the lemon drop is seductive and addictive, and I am nearly certain that sucking on these golden gems made Kurosawa's "Savage Dogs" even more enjoyable.They're hard candies. but not so hard that you couldn't cheat and bite into one, breaking it up into ten or so smaller candies, zig-zagging around your mouth like offshoots from a single magnificent fireworks explosion.One 2-ounce tin lasted longer than the 2 hours or so of Kurosawa's brilliant detective drama, one of his first with Toshiro Mifune, who once again delivers a compelling performance.  Although the packaging is a bit precious, there's nothing pretentious about the taste of Les Citrons, and as for value, these drops are the working man or woman's workhorse.  They're far less expensive than other candy (to say nothing of popcorn), and their staying power is extraordinary.Still, this vendor charges more than some others, and with the added shipping fee one may wish to purchase these  at a local outlet (or occupying it until your lemon drop demands are met). If you're serious about your lemon drops, tt's Paris 1968 all over again.Nutritional Information per Package (30 pieces; you could try to eat the suggested serving size of 3 drops, but I find this highly unlikely). 240 calories, no fat or sodium, 60 grams carbohydrates, 60 grams of sugar, no protein, and no trace of food allerges. Sugar, corn syrup, citric acid, natural flavor, and tumoric for color. THh lemon-decorated little tin adds a touch of Europe to any room, and is ideal for holding cuff links, tickets, keys, small, delicate make-up products, or quarters for the laundry.  To paraphrase the great Margaret Dumont:"Les Citrons, Toujours...Les Citrons!"

Some years ago my husband and I were lucky enough to visit Ireland several times. While there we discovered Bewley's Tea Shop in Dublin, and also their Irish Afternoon Tea. It was better than any other tea I have ever had -- and I am a committed tea drinker. The 'finish' is incredibly smooth, with just the right 'body' for an afternoon pick me up.We bought several boxes to take home in our suitcases;then when we ran out, we had coworkers who were going to Ireland bring more of it back to us. When our Irish trips ended and our sources dried up, we were truly disheartened, since we had only found it in one location in the States [a little tea shop in Alexandria, Virginia.]When I found out that it is now available through Amazon/Sullivan's I was elated and placed my order that day. Unfortunately I didn't see that the large box of it [80] teabags would soon be available until after I had placed my order for smaller boxes. The large boxes are a MUCH better value [80 teabags for $8.99 as oppossed to 25 teabags for $5.99]. That is certainly the way I will order in the future. But I'm delighted to find a source for Bewley's teas, especially Irish Afternoon. And I am anxious to try the Dublin Morning tea, which I also ordered.  Happy Nonnie!

About 10 years ago while visiting disneyworld in orlando florida my wife and I met a nice english couple. Being a tea drinker I inquired about good english teas and they gave me a napkin with the names of bewleys tea on it and about 6 teabags for me to try. I put the napkin in my back pocket and the teabags got wrapped up in an old sandwich bag and put in my wife's purse. We parted with the nice english couple and as we traveled around disneyworld it began to rain that afternoon and we got soaking wet. I found what was left of the napkin that evening at the hotel and it was unreadable. About 6 months later at home the bag fell out of my tea closet as i was fixing to make a cup and I decided to finally try the tea those nice folks from england raved about. I loved the tea and I believe I have finally found it in bewleys. Some of the best tea I have had. The english surely know their tea.

So far, my all time favorite teas come from Bewley's. Not quite as strong as PG Tips (i like that too, but a bit of a kick). This tea is more rounded out than Lipton and stronger. A wonderful flavor. -- Those Irish have got it going on!

I have been drinking Taylors of Harrogate, Yorkshire Gold Tea until I tried Bewley's.  I have always like my tea very strong using double the amount of most people.  I drink it with cream and sugar and this tea is perfect for me.  I do not have to put in extra because it is full bodied and stands up to cream and sugar wonderfully.  I have been drinking it in the morning and have been using the Yorkshire Gold for the afternoon. Bewley's is my favorite now, not that Yorkshire Gold sucks or anything but I like it strong.  I will still search for another tea perhaps as good. Life is an adventure and you never know when you're going to bingo.If you like a strong, not bitter brew try Bewley's!  After you've had Irish it is hard to go back, teawise that is.

column9: WARNING! Made all four of my dogs sick
column10: Recently purchased these treats for my 4 dogs from local grocery store. After giving my dogs these chews, my 3 month old puppy threw up the treat. By the next day at lunch time, he was exhibiting neurotoxic symptoms. We immediately took him to the vet for blood work, which all came back below normal limits. He was given IV therapy and monitored over night. Over the next two days, my older dogs (ages 4, 7 and 9)began vomiting and acting lethargic, but with no neurological symptoms. We traced the cause back to these chews, as it is the only coomon thing among all the dogs (puppy eats different food than adult dogs, puppy is walked on a leash not allowed to run around in yard yet, puppy is not out of his crate unless he is beig observed, etc.). After speaking with someone at a pet store, we learned some rawhide chews are pressed with water, while others are pressed with formaldehyde. While it is not listed which method these use, we are concerned it is the formaldehyde. In the case of the older dogs, their GIs are rejecting them due to the toxins. With the puppy, his immature renal and hepatic system exhibited neurotoxicity.

column9: Yes, it is like chewing on a sponge!
column10: I confirm another review here that perfectly describes the texture and taste of this product as like chewing on a cellulose sponge! OMG! I love tofu, by the way. This is the first tofu I've eaten in decades that I did not like.I bought this after reading that review and thinking the person was maybe not familiar with the taste of tofu, or perhaps tried to eat this without re-hydrating this first. No, it is like chewing on a sponge (Have we all by accident done this, or is it an early childhood memory of times when we tested everything with our mouths?) At any rate, you will instantly think "sponge" if you ignore these warnings and buy this tofu. I do not mean just the texture, it really tastes like a cellulose sponge!I am also a fan of Eden Foods and enjoy many of their products, they make great tamari, for instance. I was looking for that texture and taste I find in freeze dried tofu pieces that come in soup mixes as in instant miso tofu soup packets or soup cups. This isn't that tofu! It will not be wasted, it has good protein and I can chop it in very small pieces and mix it with Creamy Tomato Soup by Pacific Naturals, that makes it innocuous enough. But I'll never buy this again!I am looking into buying a food dehydrator to make my own. The cost of tofu is much lower that this item reflects. I will update this if I have success drying my own tofu. Believe the reviews here, this isn't good.

column9: This is really bad - sponge like when rehydrated.

column9: You Need to Learn How to Cook Dried Tofu
column10: Koya Dofu, or freeze-dried tofu, requires a specific approach to cooking. It not only has to be rehydrated in a particular way, but also will not taste good without proper cooking to flavor and soften it. Even at that point, it will have a chewy, slightly spongey texture, but if cut and cooked appropriately, it is not a strange texture and is very delicious as a side dish.Google recipes for Koyadofu and try one that involves simmering it (after rehydration) in a broth made of katsuobushi (if you are not vegetarian -- if you are, then use mushroom or vegie stock), shouyu or tamari, mirin, and a little sweetner. My child loves this, and I pack it in her school lunch box along with rice, and some vegies that have been simmered in the same broth.

I will now add this to the list of groceries I now order through Amazon.Highly recommend you to try this coffee and see if you agree too!
This coffee is nice and strong, but not bitter. Buttery smooth and just the right touch of vanilla.

We'd been buying the four-pack of Melitta French Vanilla coffee once a month for the past 2 years. We won't be any more. In the last month they changed their packaging, which is fine, but also changed the grind. All of a sudden, these four packs come in "extra fine grind," which simply doesn't work well at all in our drip coffee maker. The whole pot tastes weak until you get to the last couple of cups, which taste more like mud because all of the coffee has settled. Here's hoping they switch back at some point, because this is just bad.

When it comes down to so many Americans, they are right now skipping going to Starbucks to get their favorite flavor of coffee and lattes, and having them right at home. Fortunately, Melitta knows that feeling with their coffees, and make them well from the heart. Their French Vanilla is a delightful tast that just melts your heart away. It is delicious after the first cup, and just everlasting. My one and only gripe with Melitta though is that with their ground coffees is that they are very hard to open the cans, considering you'd have to use a regular can opener to get them open, rather than peel the top off from Folgers or Maxwell House. That definitely is the only thing that is not only frustrarting, but can easily cause the consumer to break the can. Still, the taste is great and if you want a nice soulfully delightful cup of joe, Melitta can take you there.Price: B-Taste: A-Convience: B-Overall: B

If you love good medium-roasted and well balanced coffee then you will love Melitta.PROS:1. Melitta only uses the top 2% of the world's supply of 100% Arabica coffee and it tastes it. (and NO, I don't work for the company!) Arabica is the finest grade of coffee available on the market.  The other grade, "Robusto" is generally less expensive, lower quality and used by most other major coffee processors such as Chock Full O' Nuts, Folgers, Maxwell House and almost all generic and store brands to name a few).2. The 11.5 oz. cans are nitrogen-flushed and well-sealed to retain its integrity and fresh roasted flavor upon opening. I have found consistently that coffee packaged in plastic or paper bags or pouches DOES NOT, in my opinion, retain its flavor and freshness well.3. If you have a drip coffee maker (Like Bunn, Mr. Coffee or others), Melitta's fine grind works exceptionally well. Remember...the finer the grind, the more flavor you will extract from the coffee. In addition, the finer the grind, the more efficiently your coffee maker will use coffee. Since you can generally use less coffee per cup, Melitta is a winner for price per ounce.4. Melitta seems to be a very transparent and consumer responsible company. They place clear "Best By" dates on the bottom of each of their products.CONS:1. Some of Melitta's flavors, like French Vanilla and a seasonally-offered coffee called "Morning Decadence", are very hard to find but well worth investigating and sampling if you have a chance.BOTTOM LINE:The best commercially available coffee for drip coffee makers. Outstanding grind, well-balanced flavors and consistent freshness can after can.

this was delicious coffee for a great price which i could not find at any store in my area or areas nearby

I just had to let you know what a miracle this food has been for me and my dogs!  I have four Chihuahuas of my own and a fifth as a foster, and I spent a long time researching foods to make a switch after P&G took over Natura (we were on Innova).  My female can be picky and does horribly with food pieces that are too big, so I was thrilled when I saw the thin triangles in the bag.  She happily crunches right through them, which is great, since she and one of my boys have horrible teeth and having to chew the food helps.My alpha male has been on Hills C/D almost all his life because he was diagnosed with struvite crystals as a young dog (he is almost 11 now).  He was the only one of my pack who looked old.  Dull coat, dandruff, and a gaunt look to his face and body. It may cost more than the lower quality foods, but if you added all the supplements it would take to get this level of nutrition, you'd be spending more anyway.  Love it, love it, LOVE IT!

If you've never tried Kona coffee, Aloha Island is definitely the one to start with.  Kona coffee is grown in the Kona district of the Big Island and regarded by some to be the best coffee in the world.  I'm not a coffee aficionado by any means, but you can taste the difference with Kona coffee - it's full and rich and almost mocha-ish.  I always reserve Kona for lazy weekend brunches or to serve with dessert after a lovely dinner.  Aloha Island operates the only quality management program in Kona, so their coffees are certified as 100% Kona.  Which just means that you're guaranteed to get quality Kona coffee if you order from them. Keep in mind that Aloha Island has three grades of Kona coffee that they sell - gold, platinum, and diamond (which is supposed to be their private reserve).  Obviously, it gets more expensive as you go up the ladder.  The gold is very good and a great place to start sampling their fare.
Hands down this is absolutely the best kona coffee I have ever had in my life..This is the smoothest and richest coffee you will ever have...Go ahead and spoil yourself, you'll be glad you did!!

column9: Smooth and Sublime--This is Kona for the Hawaiian Demigods
column10: The aroma from a pot of this coffee is earthy and heavenly at the same time. Everything about this product--packaging, texture, and taste--tells you that it was lovlngly produced under rigid standards. Moreover,if you've tried a lot of "kona" coffees like I have, you know how widely the taste and quality can vary. This is the coffee you serve to the treasured few in your life who really appreciate the finest.

I can see why plenty of people will think this is the best coffee ever. It's some of the smoothest, least bitter coffee I've ever tasted. The aroma is also delicious. Opening the bag and taking a whiff right away is a must if you want to try this.But I'm the type of coffee drinker who loves it black, so I need a coffee with a rich flavour on its own. I don't wanter bitterness, but I love coffee with kick to it.I'd call it too mild but that's kind of oversimplifying it. It's worth a try to make up your own mind though.

Aloha Island Coffee Company Bonzai Pipeline Dark Roast is a very mediocre, insipid coffee, rather acidic for a dark roast. The beans are of unknown origin, but if there are any Kona beans in this anonymous mix, they must be the ones other roasters threw out as it doesn't even vaguely taste like Kona. Actually, Aloha Island Coffee Co. isn't even in Hawaii, it's located in Santa Ana, CA, an area not exactly known for great coffee. The coffee is extremely overpriced for the poor quality you get, which is why I gave it one star, and you would be better off buying some of the better brands commonly sold in supermarkets at about one-third the price. I ordered the 2-8 oz bags, but I couldn't even make it through the first one and have thrown the second in the garbage. I would never buy anything from Aloha Island Coffee company again.
