I teased him at first that giving up soda for another kind of soda was pointless, but after trying these myself I am sold.  IZZE contains all natural ingredients and no artificial sweeteners--its only fruit juice and sparkling water!  It gives you the satisfaction of a bubbly drink without all of the bad things.  Low calorie and great flavor.  Our local stores only have a few of the flavors available, so we have not tried all of the different kinds, but so far pomegranate is our favorite.  We prefer the glass bottle drinks to the cans, but again they are hard to find locally.  I purchased this 24 pack on Amazon when I couldn't find any at Walmart.  I will buy more cases from Amazon in the future.

column9: good but you can find cheaper
column10: Love the drink.  Been drinking diet soda ever since, well, since diet soda came out.  Have not had a soda or artificial sweeteners for a week now.  Thought this would be a good alternative since I'm mostly addicted to the carbonation.  The flavor is mild but I think you can basically make your own by buying your favorite fruit juice and sparkling water.  I was also shocked by Amazon's price.  I bought the 24 pack at Costco for $13. I gave it 5 stars because it is really good if you want to spend the money on it.

I not only enjoyed every can of this flavored sparkling water, I also enjoyed every zip of it! I recommend it. It is a reasonable price, perhaps not the cheapest but it is definitely worth it! There's no doubt that I will recommend it....

This is easily my favorite fruit flavored soda. There is a perfect blend of citrus and sweetness in every single can. The only thing I would change is to increase the amount of soda in each can. Or make it cheaper... This is so refreshing to drink after a long day at work.

Absolutely love the Izze sparkling pomegranate drink.  It is much healthier for you than regular sodas.  Taste is great.  This is the only drink compatible to soda but none of the unhealthy issues.  This goes great in the pomegranite margaritas....LOVE IT...Was only available from Target and used to buy it by the case.  They no longer sell it.  Price is much better on Amazon plus no tax and free shipping.  Has a sharp fruity taste...If you get the chance to try one you will be hooked.  By the way I grew up not drinking sodas...

These cans are a notch below the flavor of the Izze in the bottles, but buying the cans by the case is much more economical.  And drinking 8oz rather than 12oz is the lower calorie choice. Glad to find these cases at amazon.com

I first bought this beverage a couple of years ago on a whim, since I was getting bored of drinking just water and Dr Pepper all the time. Needless to say, it certainly did the trick: it's much healthier for you than pop, yet still tasty enough to not miss Dr Pepper.
I bought the whole pack because I liked the IZZE grapefruit sparkling juice. Great disappointment after the first taste. It doesn't taste like natural pomegranate.
well i am just about finished with all 24 cans.  has a nice fizz to them. not overly sweet. refreshing with a tart aftertaste

I buy IZZE when it's on sale on Amazon. This Pomegranate flavor is pretty good. If you're looking for pure Pomegranate juice this is not it - go buy that Pom Wonderful stuff. This is a pomegranate flavored sparkling juice - with different juices mixed together. It's not too sweet, kinda tart, and very refreshing. To me the taste is a cross between pomegranate and cranberry. It's 70% fruit juice and 30% water - that's it. No added ingredients that you can't pronounce, none of that corn syrup stuff that everyone is scared about and no added sugar. I really like it.

IZZE has seemed to find the balance between healthy fruit taste and the sensation of carbonated soft drinks with their sparkling juice line.  I haven't had a soft drink in over a year since discovering these wonderfully refreshing, healthy alternatives to carbonated soft drinks.  Since it's pure fruit juice, it's also naturally weet (but not too sweet) so it also satisfies that "sweet tooth" as well.  Although not a substitute for plain ol' H2O, this beverage definitely satisfies and quenches my thirst.  Can't get enough of these beverages.......
This is the best alternative to soda ever.  It is light and fresh.  It is smaller so you consume less and it perks you up when you drink it because it is so refreshing.

Upon first trying this drink, I was somewhat put off. I've never had pomegranate anything, but based on other reviews I decided to give it a try. It tasted different, for sure, but after the first one, I realized I was having to limit myself to 2 cans a day. I guess it's an acquired taste, but once acquired, you'll never have enough! I love these things, and can't wait to try the other flavors.
My son loves this drink and it is much better than soda. It's a little pricey but very good.
My son and I each start our mornings off with a can of this delicious, low-cal fizzy drink.  It has a great fruity flavor and is better than a glass of juice or soda!

Izzes are relatively low in calories, no added sugar, and are natural.  They are basically sparkling natural fruit juice.  Pomegranate is a great flavor, harder to find than some of the others.  I also really like grapefruit, blackberry and clementine orange Izzes.  Pear is great but I haven't been able to find it for quite some time.

column9: A bit of a let down.
column10: I'm a fan of (most) Izze sodas and a big fan of pomegranate, so I thought this flavor would be a sure bet.  I was, however, disappointed.First up, the good.  The 8.4 ounce can size is perfect for a quick thirst-quencher.  While the calorie count is comparable to other regular sodas, it's a bit lower and consists of natural sugars from juices... not high fructose corn syrup. (What is that stuff anyway?) And, it's fizzy.  I like the fizz.Now for the bad: it barely tastes like pomegranate.  I realize that most folks would be turned off by an overly-tart, full force pom flavor; but the can promises pomegranate.  Yet reading the ingredients, pomegranate is listed fifth in the juice list. Fifth.  Behind apple, grape, pineapple, and lemon.  Oddly enough, the sixth juice: cranberry, seems to steal the show as that's the flavor I was able to notice other than the over-powering grape.And that makes me sad.  Izze's other flavors (like grapefruit and clementine) really showcase the fruit on the label.  Just not here.If you'd rather have a sweet drink than a real pom experience, give this a shot. But if you're looking for some honest pomegranate flavor, look elsewhere.

column9: Pomegranate: Oddly tastes more like grapefruit, with no grapefruit.
column10: I have tried four flavors of the Izze drinks.  Pomegranate, Blackberry, Apple and Grapefruit.My main interest in the four was the Pomegranate, and it's surprising my least favorite.  First of all, it's bitter, tastes like grapefruit, contains no grapefruit, and their Grapefruit drink is sweeter and more enjoyable.  -- which I would have expected to be my least favorite.I never drink sugar, so Izze is a welcomed beverage alternative to aspartame sodas.All of their drinks have a white grape and apple juice base. And all from concentrate with a slightly sparkling water mix.  Not carbonated, just a little fizz.Slightly on the pricey side, but for pomegranate product, it's acceptable.  But the pomegranate comes after the grape juice, apple, pineapple, lemon and cranberry in the ingredient list.

I tried two flavors of these Izze cans - Clementine and Pomegranate.What I like: Real juice - no artificial sweeteners or high fructose corn syrup. Better for you than a soda. The smaller serving size is just right and the can is a comfortable shape to hold. I liked both of these flavors, with the Pomegranate coming out slightly ahead. Both were a nice mix of tart and sweet. They also make great vodka mixers.What could be better: These really need to be cold to be at their best in flavor and fizz. I often prefer drinks to be room-temp because my teeth can be cold-sensitive. If you're looking for a fizz fix, then there are flavored, unsweetened sparkling waters out there that would satisfy without any calories at all.Miscellaneous notes: As others have said before, be aware that the flavor juice is not necessarily the main juice (pomegranate), or even present at all (clementine). They're not a complete source of the fortified vitamins, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing.It all comes down to what you're looking for. Looking for a sparkling juice that's relatively good for you? This is an excellent and recommended answer.

My husband and I tried the pomegranate, which is tart and refreshing, but as I don't drink soda at all, I tasted a bit too much sugar for my taste. But something in the flavor put us in a creative frame of mind, and we decided to have a little fun. So we tried Izze pomegranate and vodka, Izze pomegranate and gin, and then both of these with some OJ. The OJ adds a definite sweet/citrus taste and is quite refreshing with or without the alcohol. This is how we named and rated them:1. Pomegranate/OJ/gin--a Bloody Orange2. Pomegranate/gin--a Gin Izze3. Pomegranate/OJ/vodka--an Izze Navel4. Pomegranate/vodka--a Dizzy IzzeTry them this summer!

Soft drinks and sparkling water drinks rarely meet over due to their nature. Increasingly, like San Pellegrino, companies have decided to use a simple sparkling water and fruit juice blend to keep sugar contents down and your palatte refreshed.I've been a fan of Izze drinks for a while, but I really really like this Pomegranated Flavored Sparkling Juice. I have always been a fan of mixing almost anything with club soda or mineral water (tonic water has too much sugar... have you read the calories?)  to cut down the bite of some of the stronger juices and alcohols. Izze has done a nice job here. The pomegranate juice still retains it's acidic bite while the bubbly mineral water smoothens it out at the end. At 8.4 ounces, it's a nice little glass of juice and a perfect mid afternoon refresher with cheese or fruits. I'll be buying a few more packs of these!

column9: A tad too sweet for my taste
column10: Izze makes some very good juices, and advertises that their juice contains nothing other than fruit juice and sparkling water.  These are undoubtedly far, far better for you than, say, a Coke or a Pepsi.  They taste better and are more refreshing, and they certainly have a more natural feel to them.My only complaint is that, like many juices that claim to be all fruit juice, the vast majority of the juice in this particular blend appears to be apple and grape, which are much sweeter fruits in comparison with the tarter flavors.  Everyone knows pomegranate is good for you, but my guess is that the percent of this juice that is actual pomegranate is quite small--perhaps as low as 2 or 3 percent--and so contrary to what other reviewers have said, any health advantages are quite minimal.All that being said, these are certainly a superior option to other soft drinks.  Just don't think these are as good as water.

column9: Pretty good, Could be a little sweeter.
column10: I think the warnings about drug interactions should have no bearing on the product review. Obviously, if you're on a certain medication with known food interactions, you need to be cautious of certain foods. That shouldn't effect how we rate those products for the rest of the world. Medication concerns aside, the drink is very fruity, and refreshing. It is a very nice alternative to plain fruit juice or soda, and far healthier since soda contains no nutrition whatsoever.  This does taste very much like a fresh fruit juice spritzer with authentic flavor, not artificial in any way.  It doesn't have a "canned" taste as some fruit drinks in cans do.  I would have liked it to be a tad sweeter, but accomplished that by adding a splash of fresh fruit juice or a flavored syrup such as Torani. The flavor of the product itself is akin to an Italian soda.  I withheld one star because I thought the product straight from the can was a little overly "fuzzy" but fares well when poured over ice.  For those trying the pomegranate flavor, be forewarned that this is a "blend" including other fruit juices, not straight pom.  The flavor of pomegranate is still plentiful, but not like drinking it straight.  Overall, I think this would make a wonderful addition to the summer picnic cooler or to serve guests at a dinner party. Served in glasses, rather than a can, it would make an impressive dinner beverage to accompany an elegant meal for guests. I would recommend it.

column9: Serve cold for a refreshing taste!
column10: Although a little bitter, I do like the IZZE sparkling pomegranate carbonated fruit drink.  With a case of 24, I was able to share and get the opinions of friends and co-workers as well.  They noted the bitter taste but one friend mentioned how that could lend itself to be excellent in a mixed drink...come up with your own cool creation.Carbonated fruit drinks are always my favorite. I always mix ginger ale or club soda with my fruit juices.  It's especially great cold.  For me, the 8.4 oz size is perfect.  I tend to waste when I have 10 oz or more.This is something I would definitely buy and I would love to try the other flavors.  In addition, I love that IZZE has partnered w/Global Education Fund to help children around the world. A good drink, great cause...wonderful combination.

In a nutshell this is a refreshing drink. It is sparkling and has pomegranate juice in it. It is a bit tart in a good, thirst quenching kind of way.Not only do I like it, but my seven year old child loves it too.I prefer to chill it and to pour it into a glass before serving.

column9: I didn't like the Pomegranate as much-It didn't taste as good as I had hoped
column10: i want to preface this by saying I do not drink carbonated beverages, but was hoping the IZZE drinks were closer to fruit drinks.  I think I would have liked this more if if weren't so tart, but I think others who enjoy carbonated drinks will like it.  this review is for the pomegranate flavor drink.

I wish this product wasn't made from concentrate, but this type of drink is so new, eventually someone will do it.  Having said that, this IS refreshing and delicious drink.  The small size is perfect.  Mine even arrived cold!

column9: Too sour and bitter for my taste
column10: The Izze all natural Pomegranate drink is a great idea.  A Natural drink with no artificial sweeteners or even refined sugar. Best of all, no corn syrup.  It sounds like a nice healthy drink, right?  Well, the reality is that it just didn't taste very good to me. And, although it claims to have 70 percent juice... most of the juice isn't Pomegranate juice.Here's the rundown:Pros:-All Natural-No refined sugar or corn syrup added-70 percent juice content-Fortified with vitaminsCons:-Doesn't taste good. Sour, bitter, and tastes more like wine than juice.-Most of the juice isn't pomegranate... it's a mix of apple, pear...etc-Isn't sweet enough... they could have used raw sugar, I wouldn't mind.Conclusion:I just didn't like the taste of it. It may be more healthy for you than most other drinks... but if it doesn't taste good, what's the point? I expected it to taste like pomegranate, and it totally didn't. There's not even much pomegranate juice in it. Though, if you are into wine, you may like it. It tastes more like wine than juice.

In the Beginning there was Fruit Juice, and there was Soda Pop, and never the twain should meet... unless you mixed them yourself.  But then somebody got the Great Idea -- when reconstituting fruit juice after Pasteurization, why not reconstitute it with carbonated water?  Thus was born...Soda Juice!And I tasted it, and it was Good!  Apple and Blackberry were both rather mild tasting; Clementine and Grapefruit a little stronger and more tart; and Pomegranate had the strongest taste.  I'd say Pomegranate and Grapefruit were my favorites, but I enjoyed all of them.In the cans you have 5 flavor choices: Izze All Natural Sparkling Juice, Apple, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), Izze All Natural Sparkling Juice, Blackberry, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), Izze All Natural Sparkling Juice, Clementine, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), Izze All Natural Sparkling Juice, Grapefruit, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), and Izze All Natural Sparkling Juice, Pomegranate, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24).  The only difference between Izze in the cans and Izze in the bottles, other than the obvious of size and container, is that only Izze in the cans is fortified with vitamins: C, B6, and Niacin, plus the fact that currently Izze Sparkling Blueberry Soda (12 ounce) and Izze Sparkling Peach Soda (12 ounce) are only available in bottles.Since virtually nothing is added, the slight nutritional differences must be due to the characteristics of the different juices being used.  Apple, Blackberry, and Grapefruit have the highest calories, 90, Clementine and Pomegranate the lowest, 80.  Apple, Blackberry, and Clementine have the highest sodium, 15mg; Grapefruit and Pomegranate the lowest, 10mg.  Apple and Blackberry have the highest total carbohydrates, 21; Clementine, Grapefruit, and Pomegranate the lowest, 20.  Finally Apple has the highest sugars, 21g; Blackberry and Grapefruit are next, 20g; and Clementine and Pomegranate the lowest, 19g.Note: as other reviewers have already mentioned, all of these are fruit juice blends so those with fruit juice health concerns need to be aware of more than just the title juice.  All contain white grape, apple, and lemon juice.  In addition to their title juices Blackberry contains raspberry; Grapefruit contains orange; and Pomegranate contains clarified pineapple and cranberry juice.Compare and Contrast: a similar product is worth considering: essn Sparkling Blood Orange & Cranberry Juice, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), essn Sparkling Fuji Apple Juice, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), essn Sparkling Mango & Passion Fruit, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), essn Sparkling Meyer Lemon Juice, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), essn Sparkling Minneola Tangerine Juice, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24), and essn Sparkling Pomegranate & Montmorency Cherry Juice, 8.4-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24).  The difference?  The essn products lack the vitamin fortification, have a higher carbonated water to juice ratio, and have roughly twice the calories, total carbohydrates, and sugars of the Izze products, probably because they contain the fruit pulp, which the Izze products do not.

column9: Pleasantly sophisticated tasting, in a reasonable portion
column10: I've been a fan of IZZE drinks for some time.  The taste is sophisticated, the ingredients are natural, and the stuff is pretty to look at in a clear glass.  It's casual enough to drink with your lunchtime sandwich but it wouldn't be out of place served with H'ors deurves or in a nicer setting in place of sparkling water or wine.For this flavor, pomegranate juice is several entries into the ingredient list.  That means the pomegranate flavor is not very pronounced (though it's there), which may be a good thing since the juice normally packs a major flavor punch.I'd describe the carbonation as light-to-medium, pleasant like sparkling water rather than burn-y like Coke.This drink is now labeled "Fortified" but tastes the same to me as the previous non-fortified version; some additional vitamins have been added according to the label.Other thoughts: It's nice to see a reasonably sized portion (both in quantity and calories, only 80) in this era of supersized food, and supersized people.  The lightweight aluminum can is an enviro-friendly way to package drinks.  Recycle it!

column9: Satisfying with just enough of a tang to make your mouth water
column10: If you're like me, you try to steer clear of colas and especially anything with high fructose corn syrup, yet you're a bit nervous of the calorie count from, say, orange juice, and you like a bit of sparkle to your drinks, as well. When I saw IZZE, it looked like the ideal solution. It's got a bit of fizz, real fruit juices, and a few vitamins. At 80 calories per 8.4 oz can, it won't break your diet, and it doesn't have any high fructose corn syrup.So, how does it taste?Actually, it's pretty good. The pomegranate flavor gives it a nice tang without being overwhelming. The carbonation is light, just enough to give the drink a bit of extra zip without being threatening to overwhelm your stomach. And IZZE is sweet enough that I can enjoy it as a sort of reward for a workout, without being sticky or overly-sweet the way some traditional soft drinks can be.As a test, I tried one can at room temperature--it's a test I won't repeat. But served nicely chilled and straight out of the refrigerator or over ice, IZZE is an enjoyable treat--without completely busting the calorie count.

We first started buying Izze drinks when my wife was pregnant and she was looking for alternatives to soda and coffee. The Izze products were among her favorites -- especially the Black Cherry flavor. The Pomegranate variety is tasty as well, consisting of 70% fruit juice and 30% sparkling water. They make for a refreshing drink, although not a very large one (just over 8 ounces). One thing to note is that these drinks have 80 calories each, so that is something to be aware of. They're better than soda, but are far from calorie-free.

Wow!  Izze is a bright taste indeed.  Major Plus Factors: It is neither too sweet, too heavy, or loaded with any kind of additives. It is a healthful drink and this factor alone makes it ideal for people who search for alternatives to those ghastly flavored, carbonated sugar water soft drinks like coke or pepsi, etc, or other type of fruit drinks loaded with high fructose corn syrup which create false hunger and are so toxic to the liver.  AND, Izze is FREE of the dangerous caffeine junk that fries your nervous system like some of those such as red bull, etc. guzzled by silly "celebrities".  Izze is carbonated which works for my husband, albeit it is not my personal preference.  That said, Izze is great in fruit smoothies adding a lift with the fizz. I experimented by adding it to regular, unsweetened Dole orange/pineapple fruit juice and it really punched up that concoction. My taste buds were twangin'! I also see this used to add zip to homemade fresh fruit sauces,(think all kinds of berries, peaches, apricots, etc) for use over ice cream or frozen yoghurt sundaes, or in fruit shakes, custards, and yummy syrups over pancakes and waffles. The fact that is has zero sugar is a major plus for diabetics as well as those who seek alternatives to sugar overload. For those who do want a sweeter taste, I suggest adding a mere eighth teaspoon of Xylitol which I use in place of sugar because it is healthful and tastes just like sugar. AND, Xylitol doesn't adds a single calorie. Nor will it skew blood sugar values or promote sugar high and low crashes. This small addition of Xylitol really punches up the overall taste.  Bottom Line: This family really likes Izze for it's clean, sparkling and light taste plus the health benefits of the pomegranate fruit in this specific drink.

column9: Far superior to your local vending machine
column10: Izze Beverages offers a variety of aromatic and refreshing line of drinks that are healthier and better-tasting alternative to soft drinks. Consisting of all natural ingredients (70% juice and sparkling water) and with no added sugars or caffeine, Izze's drinks are simply a better choice for you and your body. With a creative blend of juice concentrates -- for example, the pomegranate drink consists of apple, white grape, pineapple, lemon, cranberry and pomegranate juice -- the taste experience is far, far superior to almost any drink you'll be likely to find in your local vending machine.Interestingly, Izze is packaged in 8.4 fluid ounce cans. A trade-off in using natural fruit juices is higher calorie content, so perhaps the tall, slim design of the can and its smaller volume is intended to help offset, both psychologically and materially, the reality of consuming an 80 calorie drink.However, Izze does not fare as well with competitive products from R.W. Knudsen whose drinks are made with 100% juice and are offered in 12 fluid ounce cans for about the same price as Izze. But perhaps more tellingly, Knudsen does not feel compelled to fortify their drinks with needless vitamins nor do they wear their corporate philanthropy on their sleeves to the extent that Izze feels compelled to do. One wonders if all this might be due to Pepsi's acquisition of Izze in 2006; the benefit of Pepsi's sales and distribution network might have come at the cost of marketing hyperbole and the production of a slightly less desirable product.Still, Izze shows that the soft drink industry is on the right track. If you normally consume artifically-sweetened soft drinks, choosing to enjoy the unique taste experience of Izze's all-natural product line (with delicious specialty flavors such as grapefruit and pomegranate) should be an easy decision for you to make. But if you are a little more finicky and prefer an 100% juice drink, you might also look into some of the other alternatives that are available to you.

I'm not big on sodas, but I do like pomegranate juice, so thought I'd give this tasty beverage a try. It is indeed tasty, a mix of several juices and sparkling water. The more expensive pomegranate comes in fifth out of five juices in terms of content, but the pomegranate taste predominates. There are 80 calories in the 8.4 oz. can, so it's not like diet soda, but it's a refreshing alternative when you feel that you can stand a few calories.

My family loves this product.My wife likes the small compactness, it's easy not only easy to carry but satisfying in flavor and the handy 8 oz amount.  Even our teenage son finds it refreshing and just sweet enough.The mix of pure fruit juice and sparkling water is nicely balanced and the fact that it is "vitamin fortified" is a plus factor. At the very least it helps rationalize drinking this tasty canned juice.  And who know, it might even be good for you!Personally, I am especially fond of the sparkling pomegranate and like to dilute it with an equal amount of club soda or just cool water.  It also makes a great mixer for all kinds of drinks, alcoholic or not.I hope this drink catches on and that other exotic flavors are added to the product line.Definitely recommended for those who like fruit flavored drinks in nice packaging and handy sized containers.

My husband and I both tried Izze All Natural Sparkling Pomegranate Juice and here's what we think:First Impressions...We are not sure we can taste the Pomegranate in it, but my husband definitely tastes apple juice which is really not surprising because that's at the top of the ingredient list, followed by grape juice and others. I like that it is not super-sweet and only sparkles moderately, quite pleasant and refreshing actually.Second Sips...We both come to the conclusion that it almost has a wine-y taste, as if one were drinking an alcoholic beverage - maybe due to the grape juice? My husband also remarks that it would probably be great as a mix with alcohol, but let's not go there for the purpose of this review :-)Conclusions...We like it better than we thought we would, especially my husband who at first was very skeptical of the idea of having to drink sparkling pomegranate juice. It is quite refreshing and a great thirst quencher on hot days although I am not sure that it is something other than a regular, not-so-sweet soda. I don't have much to say about the added vitamins - I, for one, don't need them but they likely won't hurt either.We will probably buy this again from time to time, just for a change from the same-old sodas in our fridge...

I'm a single guy in my mid-50's. I like to work-out and stay in shape.  During the week, I drink bottled water and non-sugar fruit juices. I like the Izze Natural Juice. It's tangy, and full of Vitamin C and Vitamin b6(a helpful ingredient for good disposition). There's no sugar, no caffine, and no preservatives. This flavor has apple, grape, and pineapple. cool. My only gripe is it comes in a can. I like Diet Snapple because it's in a bottle. Something about metal cans. I drink Red Bull, but not for the taste.

I often take some juice and add a bit of seltzer to make my own more natural soda.  Now with Izze, I have a company that has taken that idea and created a line of sparkling beverages.  I just drank my first can of Sparkling Pomegranate.  I found the taste to be enjoyable, with just the right amount of fizz.  These are rather small cans, being tall and skinny and holding 8.4 oz.  There is very little sodium and no refined sugars, though natural sugar does amount to 19g for a can.  I liked the fact that it was all natural fruit juice.  The only thing to note is that this is not 100% Pomegranate, it is a mix of apple, white grape, pineapple and cranberry with pomegranate.  Very nice smooth taste and something I would purchase.

I love pomemgranates and found that I really, really liked this flavour of the Izze sparkling juice. It's not too sweet or too fizzy, but just a good mix of that juice and sparkling water. I don't usually drink carbonated drinks, but this was a nice treat. Everyone else in my family really liked them, too.

column9: Very tasty and with vitamins added
column10: Izze All Natural Sparkling Juice is a refreshing drink with a tangy Pomegranate flavor that is not overly sweet. With fortification of vitamins, 70% fruit juice and only 80 calories per can, I will use this as a non-caffeine alternative to energy drinks for a quick, but healthier energy jolt. It was my first time tasting Izze, but now I intend to try other flavors too.

Izze All Natural Sparkling Pomegranate Juice is a nice alternative to the normal breeds of soda such as Coca-Cola, Pepsi, and Dr. Pepper.  It doesn't compare, however, to sodas that it will probably have more direct competition from such as Sunkist, the numerous Fanta flavors and others.  Why?  Because when most folks want a soda, they want a sugar-laden treat that'll give them a little spark.  This is soda for folks who care a bit more about their health than the average joe.  It's also a good choice for people who may not be able to drink sugar-shockers like Cherry Coke.I'm not saying that Izze Sparkling Juice is bad.  In fact, it tastes pretty good.  It contains seventy percent fruit juice (and most of that is white grape and apple) and thirty percent sparkling water.  The sugars that are contained in this drink are all natural.  It's also got a few vitamins in there, which are a plus.The pomegranate juice has a bit of a tart bite to it, and in my opinion the lemon juice that's also contained in this drink stands out a bit.  The can is 8.4 ounces, so you won't be getting the usual twelve ounces from the average can of soda.  Be sure to drink it very cold, because much like Miller Lite, it's pretty rank when it's warm or just a tad cool.In closing, Izze's got a good thing going with their sparkling juices.  This item will probably fit best in the health niche market, and I don't see it hurting the sales of Sunkist any time soon.  Give it a shot if you are looking for a Coca-cola subsitute.

I like that the soda is made from fruit juice but it is misleading in that it is not all pomegranate, it also has apple, white grape, pineapple, lemon, cranberry and the last on the list is pomegranate. If you like a sweet soda you probably won't like this since it is very tart, I was surprised at how tart this was. It has a good fizz to it and is 80 calories per can, the cans are only 8.4 oz so it is smaller than other types but is refreshing. I would recommend this soda since it is a healthy alternative to other types of soda.

Izze's All-Natural Sparkling Pomegranate Juice is a good, tart juice.  It tastes great on its own, and would probably also work well as a mixer (with a small scoop of natural vanilla ice cream?) -- the possibilities are limitless.I just got this juice today, and decided to give it the most extreme test I have -- drinking some right after finishing a little bit of exercise.  I was very pleasantly surprised; after drinking this juice, I felt more refreshed and even a bit more filled than other juices of this type.  (And for a dieter, this is a big-time plus.)Note that this isn't a sweet juice; if you're seeking that, look elsewhere.However, as a natural juice (unsweetened by anything save the fructose of the fruit itself), it has a fine, full-bodied taste that is worth savoring over a tall glass of crushed ice.  It's a bit similar to natural cranberry juices; if you like those, you will like this.Four stars, recommended.Barb Caffrey

column9: Soda you can feel good about drinking
column10: It's hard to go wrong with Izze. It's just like soda, except it's made with actual fruit juice. No sugar or artificial sweeteners.This particular blend is described as pomegranate, but it's a mix of apple, grape, pineapple, lemon, cranberry and pomegranate. Overall it's tart and refreshing, not too sweet. However, the taste of grape and cranberry rather overpowers the pomegranate. Also, with the recent focus on pomegranate as a particularly healthy juice, it would be nice if the pomegranate-to-everything-else ratio was higher, so I'm only going to give it 4 out of 5.As to the fortification, as with most fortified foods it's more of a selling point than something of real value. You're better off getting your vitamins from a healthy diet, or (if you must) a multivitamin tablet.However, I'll keep drinking Izze when I feel an urge to drink soda. It may not be the healthiest drink, but it's a lot healthier than the high fructose corn syrup and chemical flavorings sold by the two big name soda makers.

So, I havent even seen this product in a store near where I live, but do like to try new foodstuffs- so I was happy to order it as part of the vine program.  I was a little trepidatious about drinking it at first, but decided to pop the top of seven or eight cans (not all at once!) and drink quite a few before I reviewed it.  Now that I have that out of the way I can write a quick review.This soda is different.  Different good. Its got a taste that reminds me of Red Bull without the caffeine buzz.  On first sip, its got a funky aftertaste like beer, but then delves into a more tart, bitter taste before the natural sugars of the fruit juice come into play.  It tastes more like cranberry than pomegranate to me, and the others that I have shared this soda with with agree with me on that point.True, its not full of artifical sugars and so this soda isnt a sweet taste like we are all used to with carbonated beverages.  Its more "dry" in flavor and tastes like fruit juice mixed with seltzer water.  Not a bad taste, mind you, but one that takes two or three cans before it grows on you.  I like this soda, and if the stores in my area ever decide to stock it, I will happily pick up a case and even adventure out into other flavors to try.  Heck, I might have to shop on Amazon so I can pick some up every now a then  :)I dont give this soda to my kids, because to me, it has a more "grown-up" flavor to it.  Its not sugary and sweet and syrupy like modern soda, but it does have a refreshing, fresh, tart flavor that is surprisingly good.  At 8.4 ounces per can, it is a bit smaller than the 12oz. sodas we usually see, but this wasnt even a issue to me.  I like this stuff and cant wait to try the other flavors.  Trust me on this, do not jude this stuff by the first can alone.  Drink a couple and then form your opinion.  Good stuff, a refreshing change from Coke and Pepsi products.

This is by far the best of the Izze flavors.  It's light and delicious, and compared to the others I've tried (all but Apple) it easily tops the list.  The beverage is surprisingly thirst-quenching for such a slim, tiny bottle, and the best thing is that it's also quite versatile.  Too tired after work to break out multiple bottles and shake up a cocktail?  Just add two shots of your favorite brand of Vodka or Gin to one of these babies, cold out of the fridge, and drink up.  It's a light, fantastic way to relax.  The beauty of Izze drinks is that they aren't heavily carbonated like soda, so they don't really go flat, and they aren't heavily sugared like most juices, so they don't overwhelm your palette.  I couldn't recommend this product more highly.  Enjoy!

The Izze Pomegranate sparkling juice is a bit tart, but very tasty.  Along with pomegranate, there are the definite flavors of apple and cranberry juices, which make for a refreshing cocktail.  The can is small, but 8.4 ounces is just enough juice, and at only 80 calories per can, this is a better choice for dieters than many of the other sparkling juices on the market.I'm really looking forward to enjoying a cold, refreshing Izze on a hot Texas summer day, and I plan to check out all the juices in the Izze line.  Clementine is next!

Izze Sparkling Pomegranate is not too sweet, but it is just as refreshing and fun as sugary soft drinks. The cans are small and stylish, perfect for carrying in your purse or backpack. Kids like it, and the smaller size makes it a more sensible serving.The company is ecologically and socially responsible, too.What's more, this flavor is very nice with a touch of Cointreau for a sophisticated and festive cocktail.An excellent alternative to sodas.

column9: Not very sparkling.  Tasted like Cranberry Juice.
column10: This drink was pretty flat.  Pretty much tasted like cranberry juice with a tiny bit of bubbles.  I've had the bottled versions before (not of this flavor) and thought they were much better.
I absolutely love this elixir! It is refreshing and delicious as well as good for you.

column9: Great drink, healthy, tasty and refreshing!
column10: I read about the benefits of pomegranate and I wanted something that was a little tart but refreshing, so I decided to try this drink. Boy, this beverage is great and with Subscribe & Save, I save money as well and free shipping also. I like it so much I decided to buy it twice a month. By the way I'm just a regular consumer and not affiliated in anyway with IZZE or Amazon.
These are my favorite of the fortified sparkling juice brands. The serving size is perfect. I saved both time and money having my IZZE delivered.

If you are used to Hawaiian Punch, Snapple, sugary Kool-aid, or other "fruity" drinks, you won't find the same high fructose corn syrup kick in this product.  It actually tastes like real fruit juice...imagine that.I'll admit I like sweet fake-fruit drinks as much as the next person, so my first few sips of Izze's pomegranate sparkling water made me question my selection.  I had expected something more akin to lightly flavored water, but the taste was an overwhelming tartness.I have learned to enjoy though and wish my parents had given me this as a kid so that my tastebuds would consider this "sweet".  It is still a little strong and tart for me, so I mix it 1-to-1 with water.  Diluted by half is still enough flavor for me, so each 12 once can actually doubles in size when I drink it.Lastly, everything about the company suggests they will appeal to progressive-minded individuals, from their use of all natural products, their green endeavors (factories powered by wind) and their philanthropic operations.

I've been enjoying my Izze Pomegranate juice, and I'll tell you why:1. It's crisp and refreshing. Since it is mostly fruit juice and carbonated water, the only sugar is naturally occuring in the juice.2. It has 70% real fruit juice. The benefits of that are spelled out on the nutritional facts label. 10% of your daily vitamin C, B6 and niacin is in every can.3. The absensce of high fructose corn syrup. That heavy, ubiquitous sugar substitute we find in nearly every processed food in America these days, especially in the soft drinks. Izze has none of that.One gripe - The cans are small at 8.4 ounces. That usually leaves me wanting more. It's an encouraging sign that people are willing to eat food in small quantities like this, but making these closer to the size of a typical soda can and adding another 20-30 calories would be great.

column9: Real, True Earl Grey Tea, Delicious and Hard to Find
column10: *****If you love bergamot (as I do) then this is your tea. Numi Tea is all high quality, and this aged Earl Grey is no exception. It is a strong, fine tea, and the bergamot is the star. I noticed that it has been mentioned here that the bergamot flavor is too mild; to me, the bergamot flavor is quite prominent, but I don't drink artificially flavored tea, so if you do, this might be a change for you. I love it and would not go back to fake bergamot for anything--real bergamot is a treat and hard to find. Over time, you really don't want anything else and the fake stuff tastes chemically. So if you want to try the real thing, I think you'll love this tea.This tea is certified organic and contains just Organic Assam Black Tea TGFOP Grade 1 (Oxidized Camellia Sinensis) scented with organic Italian Bergamot Fruit (Citrus Bergamia). It is also kosher. On the box, the manufacturer writes: "Numi's special Earl Grey is oil-free, using a unique method of aging premium Italian bergamot fruit with malty Assam black tea. When brewed, it imparts an exquisite red-orange hue that calls to mind dawn's finest moments. Balanced and stunning, we've recreated this timeless classic."The price is perfect, a nice savings over single boxes. If you like Earl Grey tea, get it---you won't be sorry.Highly recommended.*****

This tea has a smooth, well rounded flavor and goes very well with steamed milk. I drink tea all day, and Earl Grey is my go to black tea. Earl Grey is great black, and a bit of extra dark chocolate on the side is better. Nothing breaks a hot day, or tension like a good tea. This tea has an aroma that pulls. Of the many brands out there this is definitely in my top 5(like #4 or maybe 3), because of the consistency in flavor, good selection, and the company mantra doesn't hurt either. I generally let this tea steep much longer than other brands, because it just doesn't get bitter. My wife got me hook on Earl Grey lattes, and everyone I've offered it to. If you're looking to try something new or a different brand, Numi is well worth a try. And if you've never had the latte it's: a splash of hot water, tea, vanilla syrup (I like just a shot for 16 to 20 oz, but the amount's up to you), and fill with hot milk.

column9: not very strong on the bergamot scent
column10: One of the reasons why I love Early Grey tea is the scent of bergamot oil and the strong black tea flavor. This tea, was no Earl Grey. It was more like Assam, with a hint of bergamot oil. If you like Earl Grey, I suggest you try Mariage Frères French Blue Earl Grey or Adagio's Earl Grey. If you like organic, try Mighty Leaf.
This is the best earl grey blend we have tasted so far.  Good enough we are on auto ship for it.

The tea is weak, without the slightest hint of bergamot scent or taste.  Even if it were plain black tea, it is of inferior quality. They make a big deal of their organic, wholesome, green image. It's all fancy marketing and packaging. I paid 8.99 for a box of 18 bags at a drugstore. I truly feel gypped.
I am sorry to say I found this tea very weak in flavor.  I was very dissapointed in this tea, in fact I felt theyput more work in the packaging than they did the tea.

column9: They ruined their perfect product (the only legit, non-oil-sprayed EG widely available)
column10: As you can see, I ordered a set of three boxes of these, happy for free shipping and a good price, which Amazon usually lacks on groceries... and how disappointed I was, not in Amazon but in Numi...I guess too many complained that the SMELL wasn't like other EGs, and they're right... it wasn't. Others spray alcohol-containing, leaf-wrecking oils on the leaves, leaving behind a horrible taste to me and also making the leaves oxidize rapidly, making the tea quality suck! Numi HAD it absolutely perfect. I was ready to tell you how to get, out of their tea, the perfect GENUINE Earl Grey tea, one where the tea wasn't killed by modern techniques of spraying chemicals (essential oils are almost all alcohol, after all; bergamot oil is almost always mixed with cheaper and easier to process citrus that grows far more places than a tiny town in Italy)... and now, I'm just here to say "move along, nothing here to see" because in changing their fruit supplier or aging/malting process or -something- (the tea leaves wouldn't likely vary so much, the brews side by side making the same color and the leaves being cut the same way and clearly the same region and process--yes, I'm one of THOSE tea drinkers, Steepster reviews and all), from the bags smelling like another brand, a rather costly one that starts with R and nearly rhymes with fishy, which has rather funky EG (that brand sprays the leaves, which Numi proclaims my shared disdain for)... well, what was--back when they had the boxes with the old man and his walking stick slumped in front of a cottage or whatnot--the first and only EG I would drink happily, a tea I went to specific 24/7 restaurants at 2am when needing food just because I could at least count on the tea... well, it's a passing memory, one I have about half a dozen more memories to treasure before parting ways with Numi, probably with an email expressing sadness.I DO overall recommend their teas: The lemon myrtle chamomile, now deceptively called lemon chamomile when it's the FLOWER not the fruit added to lovely organic chamomile, is hopefully still as wonderful, their Moroccan Mint is unsurpassed and the smoothest, sweetest mint imaginable, impossible to oversteep for that matter, able to handle a trio of steepings for that matter [whereas Stash uses PNW mint that is medicinal, which is honestly only good to make yogurt sauce or ... medicine!], and even for the ones like Golden Chai that aren't to MY liking, they're still well made, just not a blend I care for ingredient-wise...I simply can't recommend THIS Numi product anymore (and I hope as I use the last of my others this proves the ONLY one that got "revamped" somehow, the "how" seemingly the fruit, whether they are doing it faster or using different fruit or outsourcing the bergamot processing or... whatever they changed to make it a stinky-bagged, fruitless flavored, bitter chemical-aftertaste tea). I tasted the new just one night after a week of delighting in their original blend night after night, using my reliable method with precise timing and all, went away from it a full month, and in finding the last half box of the old, decided to compare them to be sure it wasn't simply me being thrown off. It's not. I don't deem it so unworthy that it can't be a pleasant change for the people who benefit from our brunch outreaches geared at homeless populations, and it'll probably be a welcome addition, but I will NOT be drinking the other 51 bags from this purchase myself, not when I have teas I genuinely love (as I did this, which was barely drinkable with a LOT of sugar that rendered it barely-even-tea anymore--before, it was best with a tiny bit of sugar and milk, but it was absolutely palatable with no additions).
Although I love Numi teas, the flavor from the tea bags is very weak for aged earl gray. I will keep this first shipment though will look for a brand with more flavor.

column9: Good quality tea at a discount
column10: This is one of the best Earl Grey teas on sale in the U.S., but all too often supermarkets don't even carry it, and when they do they tend to price it rather high. I placed a recurring order for 3 boxes per month and get it cheaper than I ever would in a store owing to the discount applied for multiple purchases (and no postage costs). The parcel arrives promptly each month and the process is trouble free. I'd recommend it to any tea connoisseur.
Love this tea. We tried other Earl grey teas. So far this is the very best. Love the fact that it is Organic, Fair Trade and more. You got to try it!

This tea is advertised as full leaf tea. If you're expecting full leaf tea, like you get at Starbucks these days, you will be disappointed (like me). It's not cut to a fine powder, like your average Lipton tea bag, but the tea does come in a regular tea bag, not a "satchel" with full leaf tea. If I had bought this tea as a regular bag Earl Grey, like a Twinings Earl Grey, I'd give it 4 stars. But, since it advertises full leaf, I'm giving it only 2. In my opinion, it is similar in quality and taste to Twinings.I up'd my rating to 3 stars. It is one of the better bag Earl Grey teas that I have had. I'm still disappointed that it's not a fuller-leaf tea, like you get from Revolution.

These are the small boxes of Juicy Juice. I love the small boxes. Kids can actually finish the box and I don't have to worry about spilled half juice boxes. The kids on my son's t-ball team seem to prefer the orange tangerine flavor. These go much quicker than grape and strawberry kiwi.
These are perfect for my little guy. They are the perfect size for him and I love that they are 100% juice.

column9: Great flavor, perfect size for little people
column10: These are great juice boxes. First: the Orange Tangerine is delicious and generally hard to find in grocery stores. Second: this size is PERFECT for little people. These juice boxes are as small as you are going to find - but that is the point right? The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends no more than 4-6oz of juice per day for children, so at 4.23 oz per box - you aren't loading them up with juice. We have these on subscribe and save, so always have them on hand when we are on the run. My kids love them for the flavor, and I love them for their size and 100% juice (no added sugar, additives) - a win for everyone!

Juicy Juice is always a hit in our family and with my students. Being 100% juice makes it a winner for school snacks and general meal accompaniment. This pack contained the 4 oz size, which is perfect for a quick refresher. Purchased through the Amazon Grocery Subscribe & Save feature, this product was perfectly affordable. When partnered with our Amazon Prime membership for free shipping, it cost less than our local grocer. Simply can't beat having a favorite treat delivered straight to your door for less! And what a fun afternoon...juice by mail! Thank you UPS and Amazon! Very pleased. Looking forward to our next shipment!

Somebody help me with my math -- either I'm off or Amazon is. I hope Amazon is because it means this juice is an even better bargain for our meetings. Anyway, here's what I get:8 count boxes of 4.23-Ounce ea.  = 33.84 oz.5 Packs of 8 boxes or 5 X 33.84 = 169.2 oz.5 boxes for $11.64 divided by 169.2 oz. = $0.0688 per oz.Amazon shows $0.55 per oz.My calculations showing these little boxes at 29 cents each is a bargain for some really good juice.

This juice is my favorite (so delicious) but the juice boxes are smaller than I remember. My little kindergarten sister who is very petite needed at least 2 of these boxes in her lunch. I use these boxes to swallow pills and one pill takes 1 juice box b/c these are gone in 3-4 sips.
This is our favorite Matzo.  The Everything tastes like an everything bagel.  We like it year around with butter & salt.  The price on Amazon was far better than our grocery store too.
I was very pleased with my latest order of Biscotti.  I will definitely by this product again.  Everything arrived in perfect order.

I love these biscottis. They are 15 calories each and taste wonderful. Because there are so few calories these falls under a diet product which means they aren't cheap. However I got them here for about 30% less than the other vendor I used online.

According to the FDA, the reason for the recall was:"The firm decided to recall the wheat flour products they repack that do not declare "wheat" on the finished product labels." ([...])So there is really nothing wrong with the product itself and it should be rather obvious that Gluten Flour should contain wheat unless indicated otherwise....

Stored in the fridge, this product lasts for years, and remains insect free and ready to add to anything to which you wish to add extra body during the baking process.......this high quality gluten does a great job of trapping the bubbles of carbon dioxide produced by the yeast and your baked goods will rise much higher and be lighter to the taste.
The product seems satisfactory. My husband uses gluten in  the making of his whole wheat honey bread.
I like the resealable pouch.  It works well crumbled in soup.  I also add crumbles to miso.
great when you want something light; can take with you anywhere; lots of fiber; low calorie; perfect part of my diet; taste as good as the strawberry flavor

These are convenient for when I need to have something to eat and don't have time.  All I need are in the nutrients.  And my son thinks they are good.  He has been getting into them and drinking as fast as I do.

column9: A great alternative for quick breakfast and a cheaper way to get your smoothie fix.
column10: These smoothies are perfect for just grabbing out of the fridge and going. When I absolutely have to miss a meal or have to cut one short, having one of these keeps me going better than anything else I've tried. It keeps me full while at school or work and the amount of protein makes me feel good about having it as a post-workout shake.
Tastes great cold! Just shake it up and pound it after your workout and start recovery. I just ordered 8 cases! Not grainy or clumpy like other products.

column9: I love these smoothies.  I bought mine at Costco and they have discontinued for some reason.
column10: I love these smoothies and feel that they are satisfying and healthy.  I am looking for other sources since I was buying mine at Costco and now they have discontinued them.  I think they had them in the wrong section.  They are a few dollars less at costco.

These shakes are delicious and filling. There are times I need something to hold me over until dinner and these shakes do the trick plus they help me keep my liquid intake up.  I usually drink half first thing in the morning and then another half later in the day.

column9: Keeps me full and it tastes great!
column10: This is the best protein shake out there, not only is it affordable but it tastes great. This is a great for work when i dont have time to eat lunch this will keep me full for hours. I would recommend this shake to anyone, and i love drinking this after a workout. You will not be disappointed.

column9: Good Product but Not All Natural
column10: I like the product and it does give you energy but the product is not all natural.IngredientsPurified water, whey protein isolate, blackberry juice, buleberry juice, rasberry juice, strawberry juice, papaya juicek, aleo vera leaf juice, fruit and vegetable juice, concentrate, sugar, soluble fiber, pectin, citric acid, natural and artifical flavors, guar gum, sucralose, ascorbic acid.The artifical ingredients in the product are the sucralose, asorbic acid (manufactured in a laboratory Vitamin C) and the artificial flavors.  I see no reason to have these in the product because it does contain a lot of fruit and sugar (8g)which is why I gave the product 4 stars.
Love this smoothie drink;Body Choice Orange Smoothie, 16-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 12) it keeps me feeling full for hours.  I have now signed-up to have it delivered on a regular basis.
Love this product!  Perfect for school lunches for my little guy!  He loves it and the ingredients are wholesome.

I just tried this for lunch. It was pretty good for a gluten free item. If you are used to gluten free (or similar) food you will probably like this. If you not used to gluten free food then I don't know. The flavor was good. I like the size for myself, but if my husband were to eat it he may need 2+ packages for a filling meal. I really like that this product offers a portable, shelf stable food that I can have as a meal if I am on the road and do not have access to safe gluten free food. We have some trips planned for the summer and I plan to take these (and the other flavors) on all of my trips.

nice product, nice product worth every penny and i most definitely needed it for my diet. a purchase that you couldnt get a better price for. excellent product and a recommended buy for those fish eaters

column9: Not Like Mom Used To Make But Still Pretty Good
column10: I initially purchased a few varieties of the Bumble Bee Salad snack kits to take out deer hunting with me.  I was looking for something easy to carry, didn't take up much room, was tasty, and would last for awhile without spoilage.The kit comes with a 3 ounce can of tuna salad, 6 crackers, and a small plastic paddle to spoon the salad on the crackers.  The tuna is in a metal can with a foil lid and the crackers are in a small cellophane (foil looking) pouch.  The little plastic piece is just floating around in there.After being carried and tossed around for a few weeks, I tore open a pack.  The crackers did not hold up too well to the abuse and were mostly a stack of pieces and crumbs.  The cardboard was splitting open allowing dirt to get inside, but at least the little plastic thing was still in there.The taste of the salad was actually quite good.  I did not think it had an overwhelming fishy smell which could be beneficial if you are eating it in close quarters to others who might not like fish.  There is more than enough salad for the crackers which is a nice surprise as most snacks seem to make you ration the spread.If you are on a diet, this meager snack is definitely not worth the 300 calories.  If you are looking for something portable to take on the road, hiking, fishing, hunting, or a snack to send to a soldier in the field, this is a handy, self contained snack.  If the packaging was a bit more durable to protect the crackers, I would say this would be pretty close to the perfect field snack.J. E. Nelson
Quick filler-up if your on the go when your in a hurry to be some where, just open, slap and eat... BAM!!

Samsclub sell this like $10, much better price, this is great for office use, when you want something quick without need of microwave.  Wish it has napkins, it does has folk, couple piece of craker, the tuna salad itself is delicious, try to eat like 2 of them same time, it has has some fat on it.

Millet flour is great for my gluten free recipes (just remember the xanthan gum). This company takes a little while for shipping and the shipping is a little high, but, the products they sell are cheaper than anywhere else with a greater variety offered.

column9: Good but not quite like the real thing
column10: I was happy to find Avena smoothies available in the US, as it is a delicious, smooth and nutritious drink that blends oats and milk. The Tetra pack with straw makes it perfect at home, for school lunches or on the go. It can be drunk by the glass, in cereal, or as a snack. The long expiration date (about 6 months without refrigeration) is a big plus. It is made in the USA and distributed directly by the manufacturer, Alpina Foods, out of Miami FL.That said, I was surprised at the ingredients: water, sugar, powdrered milk, oat flour, mono & diglycerides, carragenan, guar gum, xhantan gum, salt, sodium tripolyphosphate. In terms of nutrition: 180 calories, 4 grams of fat (3 are saturated), 10 mg cholesterol, 115 mg sodium, 22 gr sugar, 1 gr fiber, 5 gr protein, Calcium 16 DV%. While it tastes similar to real avena, the overly processed ingredients give me pause. I will be looking for a recipe for real avena which is probably not that hard to make and a lot healthier.As a sidenote, you can buy this at your local supermarket (in the section of south american foods) in 8 oz containers for half the price.

column9: Fun codd-neck bottles with a marble lock.
column10: This is so far my favorite flavor of all of the Ramune flavor I have tried.It has a fun look to it and is great for those who love sweet drinks and don't like or drink caffeine.I being one who avoids caffeine when possible was excited to find a drink I could add to me fridge to give me a change from the few caffeine free drinks I can tolerate.I would recommend these to anyone. If nothing else you have to try at least one in your life time.

I bought the melon flavor for myself and this strawberry for my father.  I was surprised that I really liked the melon, and my father had a great time opening the bottle of his strawberry.  He's the type who HAS to know how things work, so after finishing the drink he went about taking apart the top of the bottle!  Plus, he said that it "was a pretty good drink", which is a good compliment from him.We enjoyed the drinks quite a bit, and the bottle made an interesting conversation topic.  I'm sure that kids would love this.
When I got these, I was so excited. They were great, except one thing. Make it cold before drinking. It does not taste good warm.
Before buying this, I was unsure of what it would be. When I tasted it it was very sweet a little too much for my liking. Others may find it appealing, but only $1.99. Go ahead and try it

Not sweet and syrupy like US sodas. Very refreshing with only 90 calories per 6.76 oz.  Bottle (7% carbs). Zero sodium, fats and cholesterol. The weird glass bottle is a hoot. No plastic bottle aftertaste.

Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin food was a big hit with my dog.  It has a variety of pieces, meat and vegetables, soft and crunchy. It has big chunks that are meant to emulate real pieces of beef. My dog seemed to especially like those. He took each piece out of the bowl and chewed it up in the same manner he would eat a big piece of meat. When I first put some of this food in his bowl, he ate it up in no time and came sniffing around the bag for more. He's a big dog and eats a couple of good sized scoops of dry food each day, so this 4.5 pound bag lasted less than a week. It would last longer for a smaller dog and I'll buy a bigger bag next time I get some.The only thing I don't like about this dog food is the bag.  It has to be cut open, which is slightly less convenient than just ripping it or pulling on a string, but not a big deal. I also wish the bag were resealable with a Ziploc-type closure. I have to either transfer this food to another container once opened, or fold it up just so and push the open end against the wall to keep it shut. The bag, however, is not a deciding factor when I'm looking for a food my dog enjoys. I'll certainly consider this dog food in the future.

My dog was and I repeat a WAS a Beneful eater.  However, I decided to try this brand and he loves it.  I have also purchased the chicken dry dog food.  The food is light and he can easily chew it.  There is a difference in price, the Chef Michael's brand is about $4 more than the Beneful bag at my local Shoppers.  But the higher cost is worth it for his enjoyment.

My foster doxies gobbled this food right up. It arrived at the perfect time for one of them; he had been picking at his regular food and generally not feeling well, we found out he was having problems with a tooth and this softer dog food was perfect for him. Now that he's better, he still prefers it. I was happy that the first ingredient was beef, not beef by-product. My only concern is that it has food dyes, Red 40 and more, I know that there are organic vegetable dyes like beet juice that might be better for them. They've eaten half a bag in the last 2 weeks and no adverse effects. Good job Chef Michael.

column9: Sure to please the most finicky......
column10: My thirteen year old mixed breed Lady loved this food from the moment we first put it in her bowl.  Typically she does not eat all of her food at one time but grazes through out the day.  She ate this each time it was put out in one single feeding.  For her it was a meal that was a treat.  Will be looking at purchasing other Chef Michael.

I wanted to try this Chef Michael's for a while so when it came I put Chef Michael's in one bowl and Beneful in the other.  Well, pretty much all three would sniff the Beneful then walk over to Chef Michael's and start eating.  The food itself didn't look too much different than regular dog food but the dogs (all three) seem to enjoy it.  They have been pretty quiet as too how much....but they finished the whole bag.  ha ha ha

Our dog Snowball just ~loves~ Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin, and he will make a point of nosing around in the bowl to eat the "meaty bits" first, and then finish off the rest.  He's a fairly picky eater, but this has certainly been one of his favorites.  Our local grocery store isn't carrying this (yet) so this is one purchase for which Amazon Prime shipping will come in quite handy.

Our dog rarely eats her entire bowl of food at one time.  She usually eats a little and returns to it throughout the day.  That all changed as soon as I tried this food.  She quickly consumed the entire bowl when I poured it in.  In addition, she is more eager than ever for her food when I reach for this bag.  This has been surprising to me since I was sure dog food is dog food is dog food.  However, it is clear that this dog food is much preferred by our dog at least.

column9: Chef Michaell's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food
column10: This dog food is palatable according to my dogs.Taking a closer look.Pros :Beef is the first ingredient23 vitamins and minerals100% complete nutrition for adult dogsprotein 28%fat 16%fiber 3%water 12%No added artificial preservatives.Cons :Ground Wheat (Wheat Gluten)Added Color _ Red Dye 40I mention these as some of my cats are allergic to Red Dye 40 and some dogs can become allergic as well as to corn and soya.Tender pieces (The Beef Part)with crunchy kibbles (The Died Vegetable Part)Moderately more expensive than the average dry dog food but worth it for a finicky eater. The primary protein is chicken.

column9: Great - Just Possibly Not a Daily Food
column10: I'm really torn on this dog food because I know my dogs really like it but i also know it really isn't filled with the best stuff for the animal. When i put it down my dogs went through the process of devouring it, treating it like a snack and not like food, and that was a good sign. They really liked it. I do try to give them treats now and again and give them at least decent food, but this was well beyond what they were accustomed to. That got me thinking whether this was the best thing for them or not and, reading the bag, I decided it wasn't. The ingredients read like a laundry list of items my vet says to avoid, and I don't think that's the greatest thing to feed them all the time.I guess the best thing to say on this is that it would be a superb addition to the diet of the animal, given that you did not use it as a main item. As a supplement, my dogs would love it and anything they love loves me back. since it did not clump or show any signs of being cheaper food that makes it great too, and the price really isn't bad. This was a trial bag, but i am going out to pick some up and use it when I think the dogs really deserve something they will savor.Thanks.
My pug is kind of picky but she really took to the Chef Michael's sirloin dry kibble' I gave it to her mixed with her usual kibble and we had no problem with digestive upset.

I don't really know how to review dog food other than to say my Cocker Spaniel Bonnie is a finicky eater and she just gobbles this up. Sometimes I wish she could talk. However, if she could, I have a feeling she'd be telling me she loved, loved, loved this dog food. Or maybe in the words of a dog food commercial from yesteryear, she'd say it was, "Doggone good!"
Judging by the way the dogs eat this food, they love it.  We also put some in a small container and are using the nice size bites as treats.

There are surely some tasty morsels in Chef Michaels Grilled Sirloin Dog Food and there are a few things which my dog wants nothing to do with. My 11 year old dog is pretty set in what she likes and does not like. She is about as discerning as a dog can be. She might have some cat in her as far as her taste buds go because she can be very picky. My dog, LueLue seems to pick some bits out and chow them down pretty fast and leaves alot lying all around her bowl. Then she also does that dog thing where she leave a little trail. I though this would be a good change for her but I can see that we are headed back to Beneful.

Okay, I have a black lab that will eat almost anything...she rejects green peas, banana peels, most fruit and most trash.  I feel that it is important to tell you that, as she aids significantly in this review.  With that said, she does seem to really like this food.  We are pleased and will definitely consider it in the future.  I have no clue what a finicky dog's verdict would be.  This bag is a good size for a trial run though and there isn't a shelter out there that couldn't use the unused portion if you Fido decided it wasn't up to his standards.  Daisy liked it!

My dog just plain loves Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food. But, I'm not sure that's a good thing. Though better than some other dog foods from the larger dog food companies, it still is full of unhealthy ingredients. The good news is that corn-based products are less in this than many other similar products.

column9: It will certainly do for most
column10: I concur with the majority of the reviews here: my dog seems to quite like this food. It feels a bit moist, looks somewhat colorful, and even smells a bit of beef. In other words, it certainly comes across as good-quality dog food. However, it's worth noting that the ingredients seem to be somewhat of a mixed bag.Beef is the most prevalent ingredient, which indicates a slightly higher quality of product. Look at the labels of many other bags of dog food, and you'll see that the first ingredient is usually some filler -- unfortunately, fillers seem to take up several of the succeeding slots on the ingredients list of this Chef Michael's product. So it's certainly not the highest quality you'll find, but it's definitely not the worst either.Bottom line, my guess is that it seems to be a bit higher quality than your average bag of dog food, and that makes it a bargain for the price. You could do better if you're willing to pay for it, but I think this food will do well for most dog owners.

column9: Dog loves it, but it isn't very healthy
column10: This is like a junk food for doggies. My dog loved this, he scarfed it up and didn't leave behind a single crumb. I'd rather use this as treats than his actual daily food. Which is what I am doing with the remainder of the bag.Even though I am sure this dry food smells and tastes great to my dog, that is where my satisfaction ends. The ingredients aren't of high quality. It has artificial coloring, isn't a natural dog food and I think I am going to go back to Natural Balance.I wouldn't recommend this if you're looking for a lean, high quality dog food!

Our dogs have been eating chicken and rice for quite some time now, but they have no problem when I put some Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin in their bowls. They eat it right up. They seem to look eager when I'm crinkling the bag for the next serving as well.

My dog is really picky about what dry food she'll eat. It was only because I trusted the brand so much that I was willing to give it a try and I am happy I did.Daisy has liked the food since her very first bowl - I didn't have to mix it with her old food and try to sneak it to her - really unusual for her.I like the different sized pieces that are in the bag because the shapes seemed to make her eat more slowly, they probably cleaned her teeth good, and she seemed to get full on less food than what I was giving her before.So far we have only tried 1 bag and part of a second but there have been no health issues and my trust in the Purina brand has paid off.

column9: Pups like it, though I don't like the colors and animal by products
column10: This was a great hit with the dogs (two Boston terriers). I mixed it into their blue buffalo and they gobbled it right up. However, the ingredients are kind of yucky - added colors and animal by products, as well as a fair amount of corn. I didn't see any extra itching or allergies to the food. I just prefer avoiding colors and by products.  I'll keep mixing it in as an occasional treat, though.

Since I feed my dogs Science Diet (recommended by my vet), I've been giving this to them as 1/4 of their regular meal.Honestly, they really do enjoy the taste and often times will finish this food before their regular food. Using it as a snack or 1/4 of their meal, they have not had any stomach upset.There are dry kibble bits along with a more moist kibble.The more moist parts are flakes which seem elastic and rubbery.It has a savory scent which just calls them to the dinner bowl. You can separate the moister bits and keep them as reward or treats, another tip given by my vet.

My dogs loved this food. I wasn't surprised that the younger liked it. Her name should be Kirby.  Our older dog is a bit more picky, but seemed to really enjoy the food.As a pet owner, I'm not very fond of it. I think it's a bit pricy, especially for the amount. Also, I don't think it's good for them, too much soy, corn and added colors. I read somewhere that dogs really can't see colors so why was it necessary to add colors, especially since some dogs don't react well to color dyes.Even though my dogs enjoyed it, I won't be switching from our regular brand.

I have to admit, the dogs do like it!  I think this is similar to the kids liking fast food vs a home cooked meal. The ingredients are all the healthiest for your pet, but they do eat it! I know that we try to stick to Iams, but decided to give this a try. The dogs couldn't eat it any faster than they did! They loved it!  I would make it the occassional purchase to perhaps mix in with my dogs normal food.

column9: My dog looks like me with my favorite ice cream while eathing this.
column10: I loved watching my dog eat this food because he did love it and each time he would have eaten far more had I let him do so.  He looked a lot like me when I am sitting in front of a big bowl of my favorite ice cream.  You know the ice cream with all the stuff in it -chocolate, marshmellow and nuts that I should never eat very much of if I want to stay healthy.But back to the dog food! The food looks more moist and appealing than most and the photo on the bag looks great so if the ingredients were not so clearly poor, I think this would be a big seller.  But  because of some really awful sounding ingredients, I doubt I will purchase more.  I will likely go back to the healthier one recommended by the vet, the one that keeps his coat beautiful and keeps him lean and fit.

I try to feed Maggie quality food because she is a valuable member of my family.  This food was great, I loved the mea tand vegeatble chunks and so did she.  She was getting to the point that she wouoldn't eat Iams or Science Diet and now I can mix this in with it and she eats it.  The only complaint I have is that noe of the local stores carry it.

column9: Dog's Liked It, But Basically Junkfood
column10: My dogs seemed to like Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin dog food, but after reading the ingredients, I realize there wasn't much nutrition. Yes, beef is the first ingredient listed, so that's a plus, but it pretty much went downhill from there.I'm not so keen on products such as soybean meal, soy flour, brewers rice, soy protein concentrate, corn gluten meal and ground yellow corn.These are cheap additives that do nothing but make BIG POOP because the dogs really don't digest much of these things. With 2 one hundred pound dogs, I'm not crazy about big poop in my yard. Also, corn does really nasty things to some dogs, dry skin, itchy hot spots and outer ear infections. We're sticking to Costco brand dog food, which is much more nutritionally sound.

I am not going to get into the nutritional side of this product because Brenda has done an outstanding job of covering that. The woman knows her dog food! I am simply going to tell you our dogs opinion of the taste quality:Beckham is a two year old whippet who is more pup than dog. He typically eats Purina One for meals, meaty bones and pigs ears for snacks and a denta-bites for his teeth. His breeder (who I am sure was glad to see the backside of Beckham) recommended the above, well, okay not the pigs ears but that is just so deliciously disgusting to impose on the kids. Beckham has also been known to eat grass, slugs, deer poo and other revolting items. What Beckham will not eat is Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin. Said Sirloin has been hand fed to Beckham, hidden in with his standard kibble and offered as a treat for not pulling on walks. Nope, nope, nope, Beckham is not having it. Chef Michael please report back  to the kitchen.Not recommended by Beckham. (Or Brenda)

column9: Especially good if your dog is a Vegetarian
column10: On the back of the package there's the question "What makes a well rounded meal for adult dogs"?  Well, according to the Chef Michael recipe it's MEAL.  Though beef is listed as the first ingredient (and is about 28%) the rest of the meal is meal.  Soybean meal, corn gluten meal, poultry by-product meal, plus soy flour, brewers rice, soy protein concentrate, ground yellow corn (corn flour), ground wheat (isn't this flour?), pearled barley and glycerin.  Additives include animal fat preserved with mixed-tocopherols and animal digest (duh!).  Other fun stuff like salt, grilled sirloin steak flavor (so it tastes like steak not meal) dried green beans and dried potatoes and a lot of chemicals.  If you're wondering why so many meal and other flours, it's so that they can say that Beef is the number one ingredient.The bag says all the stuff up above makes it "Grilled sirloin steak flavor and potato & green bean garnishes".  A "garnish" is an item or substance used as a decoration or embellishment accompanying a prepared food dish or drink, per Mr. Collegiate Webster.  In other words, it's there to make things look better, but better for who (or is it whom?).  Now my dog doesn't have that sophisticated a palate, he's a rescue from a West Virginia and he likes a garnish of dog poop with his road kill, vegetables are for 'sissy' metro-dogs.This is a 'well rounded meal for adult dogs' containing 23 essential vitamins and minerals. (Since so many of these Vs and Ms are supplied by those unpronounceable chemicals, I feel like I'm poisoning my dog while I'm making him healthier.)  Per the bag they (Nestles Purina PetFood Company) prepare it with care (no added artificial preservatives, just lots of natural chemicals) and you then serve it with love (love is not included, you have to supply your own)."Animal feeding tests using Association of American Feed Control Officials (AAFCO) procedures sustantiate that Chef Michael.... provides complete and balanced nutrition for maintenance of adult dogs.  (Just remember to change their oil every six months, rotate their paws and vacuum their coats periodically. 'I confess, I made that up.')
