All in all my satisfaction factor is very high ... and Liam loves it too!INGREDIENTS:Beef, soybean meal, soy flour, animal fat preserved with mixed-tocopherols (form of Vitamin E), brewers rice, soy protein concentrate, corn gluten meal, ground yellow corn, glycerin, poultry by-product meal, ground wheat, animal digest, pearled barley, calcium carbonate, calcium phosphate, salt, grilled sirloin steak flavor, dried green beans, dried potatoes, sulfur, Vitamin E supplement, choline chloride, zinc sulfate, ferrous sulfate, added color (Red 40, Blue 2, Yellow 5, Yellow 6), niacin, wheat flour, potassium chloride, L-Lysine monohydrochloride, manganese sulfate, Vitamin A supplement, calcium pantothenate, thiamine mononitrate, copper sulfate, riboflavin supplement, Vitamin B-12 supplement, pyridoxine hydrochloride, garlic oil, Vitamin D-3 supplement, folic acid, calcium iodate, menadione sodium bisulfite complex (source of Vitamin K activity), biotin, sodium selenite. C-5900NUTRITIONAL INFORMATION (from Purina):Crude Protein (Min)  28%Crude Fat (Min)  16%Crude Fiber (Max)  3.0%Moisture (Max)  12%"Animal feeding tests using Association of American Feed Control Officials (AAFCO) procedures substantiate that Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Steak Flavor and potato & green bean garnishes provides complete and balanced nutrition for maintenance of adult dogs."CALORIE CONTENT:Metabolizable Energy (ME)3801 kcal/kg1728 kcal/lg270 kcal/cupRECOMMENDED DAILY FEEDING:*  One cup for each 10 pounds of body weight*  "If you wish to mix with Chef Michael's canned dog food, you may substitute one can (3 oz.)  for each 1/2 cup of dry product."

column9: Good for a picky eater - not good for a healthy eater
column10: "Grilled Sirloin" sounds great for a dog food, and my dog was sniffing the package and followed me from the door to the kitchen with intense interest. He was more interested in this food than many types of treats he has had. So, if your dog is a picky eater who would lose weight rather than eat a food that doesn't interest it (I have had a dog like this), then this might be a viable choice for you in order for you to get your dog to eat.On the flip side, if your dog has no problems at mealtimes and you want to provide him/her a healthy meal at a fair price, you may want to keep looking. My dog eats 4 cups of his regular food, maintains his weight and energy and has good stools. With this food, he needs about seven cups and a couple more trips outside each day. More food and more waste, because less food/volume is being absorbed by the dog. Less nutrition and more fillers. Pet food manufacturers often split up a filler food into separate types (soy meal/soy flour) so that a meat type will move to first in line of ingredients. First up is "Beef" although not specified as grilled sirloin or not, it is still generally better than foods that start with four types of corn product or a meat byproduct. This also has poultry byproduct meal, plus 3 soy ingredients, 2 wheats, brewers rice, corn, barley,  and 4+ artificial colorings. While it is not the worst dog food on the market, it is certainly not the best, and certainly not at this price point. Your dog will probably love this stuff -kind of like how people love junk food.

Lexie is a picky eater and does not like most dog food or most treats.  But she loves Chef Michael's.  We discovered this brand about a year ago, and were astounded at how much better she ate than with other brands.  The Grilled Sirloin flavor is new to us, and she likes it just as much as the chicken flavor she'd been eating.

****When my six-year-old, seventy-pound dog, PheyeG'hdeaux, hears me opening his usual bag of Eukanuba he does wander over after a while and watch me till I've dumped several pounds into his giant feeding tub, and then he does typically aimlessly meander over to it and sniff it and eat some.  I think he's just checking to make sure I haven't added a live squirrel or a robin, both of which he's 100% sure he can catch out in the wild if he tries just a little bit harder, which he always does but which never quite works.But shortly after I opened the bag of this product, Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food 4.5 Pound Bag, PheyeG'hdeaux not only RAN to the kitchen, he actively sniffed up a veritable storm as I walked a few steps here and a few steps there preparing to present him with the food that so tickled his extraordinarily sensitive olfactory palate.  He snarfed, if I'm using that term correctly, down several bites more than he would snarf up of Eukanuba, which tells me there's something special about this dog food.  I think -- and I admit I'm just guessing here -- that the Purina people have somehow managed to synthesize a special molecule or compound whose only purpose is to appeal to a dog's taste buds and smell neurons, and they've added it to the product under review.  If your dog is a picky eater, this might be a good choice.In any case it's important to consider not only taste and texture but healthfulness.  In order to test the nutritional value of Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food 4.5 Pound Bag I myself went ahead and ate it exclusively for three days, and now that I'm conscious again I can report the results.First, second and third, it tastes awful.  I realize it might taste really good to a dog, especially if that dog usually eats Eukauba (but see my review of June 7, 2012, of PURINA Beneful Original Dog Food, 15.5-Pound) for years at a time with only the rarest of desserts of bunny carcass or cat poop, but as a human I can tell you here and now, without any doubt, that this product tastes awful not just after a few days, not just after a few bites, but after a few chews of the first bite.  There are different shaped bits and they are different colors, but no matter which bit you choose it will turn out to be dreadful shortly after you bite into it.  You try the first bit and it's nasty from the first chew to the last swallow.  Hopefully you try a second shape of bit, but it turns out to be even worse.  Still hopefully, you try a third shape or a different color, and it proves to be yet even more dreadfully awful-tasting.As I say, I ate nothing but Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food 4.5 Pound Bag for three days, and at this time I also wish to report that my bone marrow has turned green, which the many doctors who've attended to me since this morning when I had to take myself to the emergency room because of several unusual and quite alarming alarming symptoms say is not just uncommom but downright unprecedented.  Also, they say my blood tests indicate I'm pregnant, which is a whole new problem since, as you know from previous Amazon reviews, I'm still a virgin.  I'll keep you updated, because I think we might have something here.****I subtract one star because the bag is not nearly as handy as the Beneful one.  It's not as tough, and it has no opener or closer.In case you didn't click to read my review at http://www.amazon.com/review/R1BESE8R6UU51I/ref=cm_cr_pr_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B001VJ0B0I&nodeID=&tag=&linkCode=of the Beneful product, you probably should if you're ever going to get another dog or cat.  Go to the section titled AD LIB FEEDING.  Also, note that I have updated the list from seven pets to eight.

Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin dog food is like McDonald's for dogs.  The stuff looks tasty, smells great (apparently), and must taste really good because my papillon practically swallows the stuff whole without chewing.  But, is it healthy?  Not really.  If you read the ingredient list (and read a few of the user reviews), you'll see that this dog food is really not that healthy (or that great of a deal, considering how much more the dog needs to eat in comparison to a high quality brand to get full.If I were judging this dog food just based on favor and reaction from my dog, this would be a winner!  He loves it and sucks the stuff down.  However, if I were judging from the more parental side, I probably wouldn't give this to him to eat all too often just based on the nutritional value.

column9: My friend's 2 dogs and 5 shelter dogs ate this dog food eagerly
column10: Since my friend is into rescue work, I figured this dog food would be great to test on her two dogs and the five shelter dogs she is working with.  All the dogs ate this food eagerly and they were not starving dogs; so I'd say it gets five stars for taste.According to the packaging, Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food is 100% Complete and Balanced for adult dogs with 23 essential vitamins. Since dogs are carnivores, meat should be high on the ingredient list and the first four ingredients in order are beef, soybean meal, soy flour, animal fat preserved with mixed-tocopherols (from of Vitamin E).Each serving contains:Crude Protein 28%Crude Fat 16%Crude Fiber 3%Moisture 12 %Overall, the dogs loved it and since the food states it is 100% complete and balanced and the first ingredient is beef, I give this five stars.  From the dogs point of view, it appears to be delicious.

Chef Micheals Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food Rocks !! It s catnip for dogs . I have two shitzus they won't stop eating it. I usually feed them Imes but they seem to like this much better.It does'nt seem like the pieces are too large because they are chowin' down.It must be the sirloin flavor .Anyway if you have finicky dogs they will probably like it. I would give it a try.

column9: Dog enjoyed it but ingredients no better than any other Purina brand - Lotsa CORN, WHEAT & GLUTEN
column10: The images on the bag make this Premium Purina dog food look well worth the price but a quick look at the Ingredients list should warn you that if you are gonna spend extra money on your dog's food, you might as well go for the brands that DON'T fake you out with photos of sirloin steak and fake green beans formed from corn & dehydrated green beans.  I'll be truthful - my dog loved this and ate it happily.  I mixed it it with his regular dog food and he just gobbled it right up.  However, my dog doesn't do well on foods loaded with grains so I won't likely be buying this despite how much he loved it.  Here are the ingredients in order by weight:Beef  - good to see it's the Number 1 ingredient but from her, it gets sketchySoybean mealSoy FlourAnimal fatBrewers Rice (an empty calorie filler leftover from Beer making process)Soy Protein ConcentrateCorn Gluten Meal (another filler)Ground Yellow Corn (filler)GlycerinPoultry By Product - (ground up bones and feathers)Ground WheatAnimal Digest (??? I think I know what this is and it makes me sick)Pearled Barley (Grains again)Calcium Carbonate (ground up rocks)Calcium Phosphate (ground up rocks)SaltGrilled Siloin Steak FLAVOR (no meat)Dried Grean BeansDried PotatoesSulfur, Vitamin E, Choline Chloride, Zinc Sulfate,  Ferrous Sulfate (both colorants)Added colors - about 5NiacinWheat Flour (grains again) and so on and so forth.. the same as basically what's in Beneful.My advice - if you have to go with a Grocery Store brand, don't be folled by a fancy photo on the bag of Sirloin Steak.  Compare the ingredients and buy what you can get the most of for your money IF YOUR DOG CAN EAT THAT STUFF.  Mine can but I still go the extra mile and try and by a more meat based diet.  While I was pleased that Beef was the first ingredient, I prefer to see the first few ingreidents be meat and never to see fillers like Corn and Brewers Rice.So  2 stars for taste, 1 star for being the same as every grocery store brand from Purina who makes this and  two stars OFF for deceptive packaging and advertising.  READ THE LABELS!

column9: Read Ingredients First.... Nutrition is Misleading....
column10: So its been a week since I let my dogs "try" this food. We have 4 dogs so this bag went quick! 3 Small dogs, Shih Tzu and Maltese's and One Yellow Lab, all adults.The product states how tender the pieces are and how your dog will love it... and that they do... It also says theres no artificial perservatives and that the #1 ingredient is the beef that your dog wants.. but... is this what your dog needs???Just because the product looks good and colorful and says your dog wants it doesn't mean its good for him. This was more like a treat for my dogs then "food" and even then a very unhealthy treat. There is a ton of soy and corn in this food and by products. I think the colored bites are more to please the humans then the dogs! That means there are aritifial preservatives or flavors or colors of some sort to get the colors. Does a dog really need this? but mainly is it healthy.... For a 4.5lb bag of unhealthy food it is pricy too.You are what you eat... and if you give your dog a healthy food with NO byproducts and no corn etc.. your dog will be alot more healthy (and less gassy if gas is a factor) I'd recommend trying good healthy food for a week or two if your not already, you will see a difference and there are a bunch out there on the market. Yes they are more costly.. but think of the benifits as well. Why give your dog stuff thats unhealthy? Can lead to problems... and more bills.I don't recommend this food, and my dogs enjoyed their short treat while it lasted. We didn't fully finish the bag either as after a few days I didn't want to keep giving them "junk food"

column9: Struggled with this rating because my dog loves it.
column10: I picked this up on a whim. My thought was to uses a very small amount as a sort of snack for my dog before bed.I do this with my cats, too. I give them each a very small amount of a dry cat food that is low on the nutrition scale,but high on the cat  junk food scale. I had been giving my dog an oatmeal biscuit or two each night. When I saw thisI thought I would try it and give him the same sort of treat as I do the cats.First of all, he loves it. He practically kisses my feet when I give it to him. It has an odd texture, in my opinion. Sortof similar to a handful of raisins, not quite dry but? And Duncan gobbles it up and clearly wishes for more. I have afairly spoiled dog. Due to health issues, I cook for him every week. He eats cooked fish, beef or chicken with rice or pastapeas, and some supplements. So if I ever do give him dog food in any quantity at all, it is a very high quality, not so yummyas this ( apparently) dog food. So I am very concerned with what is in the food he is given. I see no problem with a tablespoonor two a night for my 70lb dog, but I would not feed this as his sole diet. The nutrition value is very low, which is usually theway it is with the food dogs like best.So, I really wanted to give this a higher rating since he likes it so much, but since I am writing this for dog people who aresurely interested in keeping their dogs healthy as well as happy, I had to go with two stars. Now, as a treat, or an occasionalmeal, I see no problem with this. Dogs enjoy junk food, too.

The rating is one star because the dog liked it a lot and one star in thanks for the Vine program which allows us to try products without spending good money on them.My dog is 130 Mastiff and he did not like or eat the Beneful dog food that we reviewed a few months ago. Not so with this bag. He was interested in the smell as soon as I opened the bag and ate the whole bowl when it was placed in front of him. He is not a dog who is normally interested in food. He doesn't beg at the table, shows no interest in scraps and usually has to have wet food mixed in with the dry before he will eat. His preferred diet is couches, dog beds, remotes, eyeglasses, and a 9" ratchet wrench. Yet he likes this food. I wonder what the attraction is , since he usually shuns table scrap meats.In spite of the fancy name, the colorful textured kibble, the grilled sirloin label, this bag is full of stuff that is not good for dogs as a daily diet. Too much soy, soy products, artificial colors, etc.We will be using this bag as a training treat, because he seems to like the taste, but we are still on a hunt for real, unadulterated, healthy food.

I'm not normally a dog owner who buys her furbabies food made with either corn or food coloring.  My five big dogs eat a variety of high-quality brands like Taste of the Wild Lamb, Blue Buffalo Chicken n' Rice, Dogswell Chicken or Wellness 5.  I rotate these brands to add variety for them.  They graze out of a large bucket as they please.I poured the contents of this bag into the bucket, separating it from the Taste of the Wild kibble already in the bowl.  I wanted to see if my spoiled dogs would care for this stuff.  The contents did look like little pieces of ground steak and peas, only dried.Well, the two youngest dogs went right for this product with gusto.  Perhaps my mutt Zeke really did think he was eating Grilled Sirloin Steak and peas?!  HA!  The first ingredient listed on the bag is indeed "Beef," but for the pet food industry that basically means anything from the cow not suitable for human consumption.  "Grilled sirloin steak flavor" is in this stuff, but further down the list, after soybean meal, soy flour, animal fat, brewer's rice, soy protein concentrate, corn gluten meal, ground yellow corn, glycerin, poultry by-product meal, ground wheat, animal digest, pearled barley,  calcium carbonate, calcium phosphate and salt.  There are also four added colorings to this.(For a more detailed list of ingredients and their true effect, please read the one-star review by Brenda Franks below.)Crude protein is between 16-28%, crude fiber between 3-12%.The fact that my active dogs ate this stuff must mean there's something in it they like, so this is not a total waste.  I would buy this food if I were on a strict budget since there are better nutrients in this food than in most other popular Purina dry foods for dogs and cats.  In fact, for those whose pets love this stuff, a better deal would be the larger bags of this stuff.If you do not like serving your pets corn or food coloring, though, stay away.  This food won't harm your pets if served only occassionally--the "beef" chunks could serve as treats during training sessions--but for those who want to feed their dogs the very best, look for foods that do not contain food coloring, corn or other cheap fillers.I posted two photos of two of my dogs eating this stuff.UPDATE 22 July 2012:  After gobbling up the entire 4.5-pound bag in 24 hours, the dogs are obviously telling me they really, REALLY like this stuff.  Unfortunately, it gave the dogs some serious runny, yellow poop, and lots of it.  I scooped up more poop in a 24-hour period than I normally do feeding my dogs the high-quality dry kibble.  Poop isn't normally yellow, nor is it runny soft.  The yellow is from the undigestible food coloring.  Just remember that healthy food creates healthy, dark, solid poop!

column9: He ate it once and then never again
column10: We have three dogs.  One will eat anything, one will eat almost anything, and one is a picky eater.  Fortunately, the picky eater is the chihuahua.  Part of the picky eating comes from his sensitive stomach, and we avoid chicken and turkey because that consistently upsets his stomach.The first time he was offered Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin dog food, he devoured it with pleasure, and I was ecstatic to have a dry food that got some enthusiasm.  Unfortunately, that enthusiasm was gone by the next day, and he absolutely refused to eat it for two days.  We gave up.  If he'd rather eat the big dogs' food than eat his premium food, there is no  point in spending extra for a more expensive food.From my point of view, the "premium" seemed to be mostly the "Chef Michael" name, as it didn't seem to have any better ingredients than the other Purina foods.  Beef was the first ingredient, but it was followed by soy meal and soy flour. (Can we say GMO?) It also contained chicken by products (a long ways under the soy products, by the way.)  Even salt appears before green beans and potatoes.  It is cuter than regular kibble, but I don't think the dogs care.  It also has varying textures, but once again, even when I let the big dogs try it, they weren't overly impressed.My opinion is that either spend more and get real premium food or save your money (unless you want attractive kibble) and just buy a standard dog food.

column9: Great taste, but not something I'd feed my dog regularly
column10: It took about ten seconds to realize that this product tastes great to my dogs.  We have a lab and a pug, and both of them attacked their bowls like I'd given them steak.  I'm sure they weren't happy when I went back to "boring" Hill's the following day, but this isn't a product I'd recommend for keeping any dog healthy.The reason I've only given this product four stars is that many of the ingredients aren't something I want my dogs eating regularly.  They don't have many problems with soy, but I know a lot of other dogs do.  They (and I) do have problems with the heavy use of corn, the always-worrisome chicken by-product, and artificial colors.  That last one seems like an obvious admission from the makers of this product that they're really targeting dog owners more than they are dogs.  My lab certainly wasn't awestruck by the various colors on the package.My feeling is that this is a nice treat or occasional meal-topper for my dogs, but it won't be something I purchase for daily consumption.  Both dogs certainly love the taste, and I commend Chef Michael for that, but for long-term health I'd recommend other options.

column9: Two out three dogs liked it but there are better foods out there
column10: Length:: 4:43 MinsAfter experimenting with grocery store-type dog foods I settled on one sold by my vet. However, I thought that this brand might be worth trying.  You will see from my video review that not all dogs are fond of it.  I thought that it was just okay and the ingredient list is not very impressive.  I hope that you enjoy my video.

The picture on the bag of the food looks really healthy. One can only assume by the name they are trying to push a better food product for our beloved pets.I mean Chef Michael's? How can someone not buy it? It has to be great!My dog ate it quickly, but then again, my dog isn't a picky eater.I had a bag of Blue Buffalo. I try to feed my dog better food. Here are the list of the first few ingredients: deboned chicken, chicken meal, whole ground brown rice, whole ground barley, oatmeal.... etc. etc.This is what is in the Chef Michael's: beef, soybean meal, soy flour, animal fat preserved with mixed tochpherols(eh whats that?) brewers rice, soy protein concentrate etc. etc.As you can see there is a big difference. While the food looks decent. Its softer. The brown stuff looks like meat. And it has bits of yellow/brown and green hard nuggets.While your dog will probably eat it, I'd say spend the extra 4 bucks and get a bag of something better. Its $13.87 in the store for a for a 4.5 pound bag.  I think I paid $17.00 for a 6 pound bag of BB. Or something a little healthier.Bottom line is that each pet owner must choose what they think is best for their four legged buddy.

Beef might be listed as the first ingredient but that hardly makes it the main ingredient.  After reading the ingredients list this "food" seems to be mostly made up of various forms of soy.  I am not a fan of soy & with all the GMO crap being pushed on us, I like it even less.Upon presenting this artificially flavored & dyed product to my fur babies, they started to eat up.  But then one by one they stopped & looked at me as if to say, "What is this crap?  We don't want this.  Where's the stuff you normally give us?"  I left the food for them.  Several hours later, the food was still in the bowl & a disgusting explosion of black runny vomit was all over everything.  Jerk that I am, I continued to try to get them to eat it.  After all, I have a review to do - that's how I ended up with the food in the first place.  After several days I gave up.  One of my babies simply stopped eating.  That was the final straw.  I am not torturing my pets any longer.  They are back on their usual grub. No more black vomit.  Everyone is once again eating until the bowls are empty & my furbabies are back to their joyful behavior.

This dog food is amazing it even smells good. Since the pieces are good size I decided to use these as rewards when our dog Sadie successfully completes a trick. Its a very effective reward and she really seems to enjoy the taste,using the product in this way is also cost effective since its not exactly cheep. I would recommend this product to dog owners, especially for training purposes!
Not sure what other criteria exists to judge dry dog food -- the shapes look like pieces of meat?Seriously, my two dogs ate this willingly and even returned for seconds.

Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food, doesn't that sound tasty? The packaging is slick and pretty. And, really, who wouldn't want a chef preparing their dog's food?We have three dogs, a Boston Terrier and 2 Doxles, (beagle/mini dachshund). They are normally very picky eaters, and yet they loved this! It even LOOKS appetizing! Chunks of stuff that looks like meat and more chunks that look like healthy veg!So, the dogs loved it, why am I giving it a 3 star rating? The ingredient list. There is so much grain in this food, you may as well buy the cheap stuff! I choose to feed my dogs something that is better for them! Go back to the kitchen, Chef Michael and try again!

column4: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
column9: Doggie Desert - updated review a week later
column10: I may want to live on caramel and ice cream, butterfingers and apple pie - but after a few months of this diet, I'd be an overweight diabetic. This dog food, even though the name sounds (lets use the thesaurus here) resplendent, delightful, and even pulchritudinous (!) - is canine candy. I mean, come on - "Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin"? Sounds like something I'd want to eat. But read further, and it's "sirloin flavored" and is full of corn and other fillers.  Sure, the way my dog devoured this looked like I had not fed him in days - he was ready to lick the chrome off the bowl. "Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin" is a name dreamed up by the marketing department.Unfortunately, the food is flavor and filler, low quality protein, and high in carbs/calories.  If your dog is a lay-about, couch potato, indoor pooch - this stuff is better as a mix-in for finicky eaters, or as an occasional treat. A dog will have to be pretty active to burn off the calories if this was his/her staple.A week later? The dog won't touch it. Just nuzzles the stuff and gives it a tentative lick. Guess he wizened up!

column4: Jeri Zerr "formerly a Road Rarrior of the Nth...
column9: it's okay... but there's so much better available for the buck!
column10: The Chef Michael's dog food by Nestle Purina is an OK dog food, but there's soo much better available for similar bucks with wholesome ingredients such as bison, salmon, blueberries and tomatoes. Examples include Taste of the Wild Dry Dog Food, Hi Prairie Canine Formula with Roasted Bison & Venison, 15-Pound BagMy German Shepherd Dogs took to Chef Michael's much better than to PURINA Beneful Original Dog Food, 15.5-Pound but not nearly as well as Taste of the Wild Dry Dog Food, Hi Prairie Canine Formula with Roasted Bison & Venison, 30-Pound Bag which they absolutely love and thrive very well.To my stunned disbelief the bag of Chef Michael's recommends feeding 1 cup per 10 pounds of dog's body weight. 9.5 cups of dog food, per day.. wow... imagine the "landmine waste" they would be producing! I have 95 pound dogs... they only eat at most 3 - 4 cups of Taste of the Wild.. usually much less. The reason being is rather evident in the list of ingredients:  beef, soybean meal, soy flour, animal fat preserved with mixed tocopherols (form of Vitamin E), brewers rice, soy protein concentrate, corn gluten meal, ground wheat, animal digest, pearled barley, calcium carbonate, calcium phosphate, salt, grilled salmon steak FLAVOR, dried green beans, dried potatoes, sulfur, Vitamin E Supplement, choline chloride, zinc sulfate, ferrous sulfate, added color (red 40, blue 2, yellow 5, yellow 6), niacin, wheat flour, potassium chloride, l-lysine monohydrochloride, manganese sulfate, Vitamin A supplement, calcium panthothenate, thiamine mononitrate, copper sulfate, riboflavin supplement, Vitamin B-12 supplement, pyrodoxine hydrochloride, garlic oil, vitamin D-3 supplement, folic acid, calcium iodate, menodione sodium bisulfite complex (source of vitamin K activity), biotin, sodium selenite. According to the package the Metabolizable Energy (ME) is 3801 kcal/kg, 1728 kcal/lb or 270 kcal/cup.The Chef Michael's customer service is 1-866-738-3663 Mon - Fri 7am - 7pm CST.

column9: I let the dog eat it....
column10: Unfortunately he can't write the review!Whenever you switch dog food on a dog they will be all excited the first time. Discovering something new in their bowl , scarfing up how ever much you give them; and then the newness goes away. A few servings and they seem tired of the taste.Not so with this Chef Michael's product. Until the bag was empty , our dog looked forward to his morning feeding with great anticipation.Usually the dog is in our bedroom waiting for us to get up...three of the last four days he has been sitting by his bowl.Think he likes it

column9: My dog loved it, but the ingredients aren't healthy.
column10: My dog loved this food. He scarfed it down and wanted more. However, when I looked at the ingredients, I was disappointed. Lots of soybean meal and soy flour, and corn meal. Is it really so hard to make dog food that's not full of this stuff? When I buy Purina, I'm expecting something that is actually good for my dog as well as delicious. A definite let-down.

column9: My dog likes it a lot but the quality is not 5 star
column10: Opening the bag I noticed there's no zip to reseal.  It would be helpful if there was even a zip closure. I had to put the bag up high because I was worried about my dog food loving cat getting in it - she was all over it. It smells like people food to me, it's got a smell that is a lot like steak.My dog eagerly ate it, even though he really shouldn't have been all that hungry.  His first taste of this was after he'd already ate his regular food.  He seemed to really enjoy it and he ate it all.  He can be picky about food and is one to turn his nose up at a lot of the healthier dog foods.  He's also the type that will leave kibble in the bowl of a certain type in a combo if he doesn't like just that type - but he ate all of this.  There wasn't a chunk left in his bowl.The ingredient list is subpar though so I can't give it 5 starts- it has corn and soy both, and it is probably filled with GMOs.  The rest looks like it is mostly animal byproducts and flavor enhancers.  For the price I'd expect it to be a bit better.  My dog has not had any gas issues or allergic reactions though - he is allergic to a fleas and who knows what else but this has not bothered him.

If you feed your dog Supermarket grade kibble, then this might be a step up for your dog in taste if not nutrition.  Two of my dogs loved it, the third, who has a sensitive stomach, didn't really care for it.  It has nuggets that look like vegetables and others that look like bits of meat although the distinction is purely cosmetic.  The meaty bits are supposed to be tender but they felt as hard and crunchy as the rest of the nuggets.Also, the protein content is pretty high at a minimum of 28%.  I know, we have been told by dog food companies of late, that our dogs crave meat and lots of it.  The truth of the matter is that too much protein can damage your dog's kidneys.  Sadly, we found this out the hard way with our beloved Shiloh.  The pain and expense of having a dog suffer through kidney failure is significant and not something I would want to go through again.  Our vet told us that we should switch to a kibble with a protein content in the range of 18-20% and to get out of the habit of feeding our dogs high protein treats like jerky and pig's ears.  I don't know, but you might want to talk to your vet about it before switching.Now on the other hand, if you feed your dog premium dog food or organic premium dog food, then I would definately not advise switching.  Our vet also recommends organic natural dog food based on a suspected link between preservatives and fillers used in cheaper dog food and certain types of cancer in dogs.  Some articles I've read in various dog magazines have also reported the link between preservatives in dog food and cancer in dogs.  Again, you might want to discuss this with your vet.  Also, FYI I'm suspicious of any vet who tends to only recommend the brand of dog food that they sell at their office.  So, if this happens to you you might want to do your own research on line just make sure your truely getting an unbiased opinion.So anyway, I had been feeding our dogs the "good stuff" for several years but my husband would frequently comment (which in guy speak is like complaining) on the doggy food bill.  He ultimately suggested that we give this stuff a try because, after all, Chef Michael feeds it to his dog.  So I tried it and well, I'm sorry to have to tell you this dear but we're switching back to the premium stuff.

column9: She LOVED the taste, but not so healthy
column10: I will echo the concerns about the healthiness of this product but without question, my dog ate this food like nothing else I've given her. The odor isnot overly strong and it does appear to be a nice mix of meat and vegetables. I will be using this as a supplement to her normal dog food, which is much healthier but for a little treat, I'll mix this in with her food. The pellets are small enough that you could use these bits as a snack and not for the principal meal.

I was surprised watching out two Huskies eating Chef Michael's creation and then asking for more because they would not normally eat bagged, dry dog food unless hungry. This may be a first because, as it's probably the case with most dogs, they would rather eat human food then dog food and if human food wasn't available they'd first go for some fresh 'rabbit' or 'field mouse' if they could catch any.I haven't tasted the food myself but our dogs seem to find it delicious. As for its nutritious qualities, the number one listed ingredient is 'beef' so it appears to be so. There is some text on the bag claiming that there are vitamins and minerals that would give the dog a shiny coat but that's probably speculation. I don't know of anything that I could eat and make my hair turn shiny so I can't see how such a miracle food ingredient could exist for dogs. If you want your dogs to have a shiny coat, there's shampoo.The food appears to smell good too and it comes in a variety of bits, some soft, some crunchy. The bits come in different colors but that's probably something that we humans are more likely to notice or appreciate because dogs' vision is believed to be either black and white or something close to an old 50's color TV.Since this is the first 'from the bag' food other than Milk Bone that our dogs actually love, it gets a well-deserved five star rating.

This dog food has beef as the #1 product ingredient as well as 23 essential vitamins and minerals.  Yet that isn't good enough for a lot of people out there.  Yes it has soy and corn in it.  Oh well.  Dogs will eat it up.  Who cares from what part this by-product comes from?  Dogs are scavengers folks, just check Wikipedia.  Some use this product as a dog treat -- great idea.  I suppose if you have a show dog this dog food will not be good enough for you, but what did you expect for this price?  The only think that really bothers me about this product is the food coloring added.  Is that for the dog owner or the dog?  I just can't see the dog really caring about the color of the food.  The dog bag is a thicker plastic sealed extremely well so this food is going to be air tight.  I'm not a big fan that I have to use scissors to open it however.

column9: Picky Shih-Tzu kind of likes this mixed with canned food....
column10: Our picky Shih-Tzu won't even eat doggy snacks. I topped his canned food with a few Chef Michael's kibbles. He ate around the kibbles first, then finally gobbled them up with the rest of his canned food. He won't eat any dry dog food unless it's mixed into his canned food.Our mutt loved this food, but she'll eat anything.Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin contains mostly semi-moist kibble bits and some crunchy bits too. It was given a low rating by  the Dog Food Advisor web site.  I'm not  sure I agree, but thought I'd share it with you.

My dog loves this stuff.  That's a bad sign.  We normally feed her very healthy dog food, and she always looks at us with disdain when we put it out for her.  We've tried plenty of different foods and it's clear to me that her appetite is just like our kids': The worse it is for her, the more she likes it.The price for this small bag is also higher than I like to pay for dog food.I'm not a health nut by any means, but the ingredients look more like Cap'n Crunch than a  healthy meal for my dog.I will keep this bag (and maybe even buy more in the future) for when we camp.  Our dog is always off her feed when we take her camping.  She loves to camp, but there are so many distractions that she tends to ignore her food.  This isn't good when we're out for more than a short weekend.  So on those longer weekends, it's puppy Cap'n Crunch for her.

This Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food loved by the retriever puppy we tested it on, but I do have concerns with the content. This puppy will eat just about anything put in front of her, intended or not, but she absolutely devoured this stuff.The issue is that it has a lot of soy, corn, and rice, and unidentified animal fat high on the ingredient list. It does have beef listed as the first ingredient, which is probably why Sissy loves it so much. I am not sure that it isn't "good enough", but this will not be our dog food of choice and it will be given as a treat on occasion.Recommended, with the caveats above.CFH

column9: Five big sniffs from my Wheaten
column10: I'm going to have to defer to my 6-year old Wheaten Terrier regarding this Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin kibble and he gives it five big sniffs.My dog, like many others, is highly allergic so I'm careful to make certain that the first ingredient listed is not wheat and/or corn.  And, most importantly, with all the dog food scares from food made in China and distributed by US companies, I make certain that it is both manufactured AND distributed in the USA.  This product met my requirements and my dog's appetite and my reward was a slobbering kiss.

column9: Take good care of your doggies
column10: Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food 4.5 Pound Bag is listed in Grocery and Gourmet as well as the Pet section of Amazon but I would not at all label this as a gourmet item.  I would not rely on this food as a nutritional foundation for dogs and would only either mix it with another more healthy food or would present it as a tasty artificially enhanced treat for training or rewarding purposes in limited amounts, sort of like liver treats.  Our dog likes it and it's a good size kibble for her, but I just can't get behind the ingredient list on the package.  Is Purina preparing for a doggie food channel by creating an imaginary Chef Michael?  If so, I wish Purina would use better ingredients.  If you don't really care about ingredients, then I'd still recommend another option because I think this one is more expensive than others in the same class of dog food product.

column9: My dogs love it, but the ingredient list gives me paws...ahem, pause
column10: Chef Michael might be a fictional character in the same vein as Aunt Jemima and the Keebler Elves, but that doesn't excuse him from putting some truly nasty ingredients into his Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food. So many other reviewers have pointed out the list of dubious ingredients that it doesn't pay to duplicate them again, but I urge you to take a long, hard look at that list before you commit to purchasing this item.Nutrition aside, this is a very tasty food item based on my dogs' response to finding it in their bowl. Frankly, they went bonkers over Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food. I'm probably not going to make this part of their regular diet, but I will continue using it as a treat.

column9: 2 Paws up from my picky Beagle!
column10: I have a beagle who is a pretty picky eater (weird for a Beagle, but she's kind of a diva).  So I thought she might turn her nose up at this food, but I was totally wrong! She LOVES it-we did mix it with her normal Pedigree food so that she didn't get a sick stomach from an immediate switch, and I would recommend doing that if you're switching b/c this food is much more rich and fresh than normal dry dog foods.  The ingredient list includes A LOT of added vitamins (D-3, B-12, E, K) which is better than the Pedigree I normally feed her. It is dry, which is great b/c it keeps for a long time and requires no prep other than just tossing it in the bowl! It is considered a premium dog food, so that does make it more expensive, but it's a great treat that is good for my dog and she loves it too!

I've never seen my dogs go as crazy over a dog food as when I gave this to them.  They absolutely love it.  The food looks just like it does on the bag, with pieces that are supposed to be beef that look like shredded beef and then little round balls that are supposed to be potatoes and green beans.  The potatoes and green beans are a little under 1/2 inch, but the beef pieces are closer to 3/4 to 1 inch, so this food might be best for a bigger dog.  The smell of the food is not as strong as some other dog foods we've purchased, but it definitely must have a good flavor.  It's made by Purina, which has been around forever, so I think it's a product we can feel safe using.

column9: Yet Again, the Yorkie Politely Declines
column10: While other dogs may perceive this dog food as delish, my Yorkie says no. Why?  I cannot know with certainty, but I suspect that she resists any dog food with corn as an ingredient.  Perhaps she smelled something she does not like, but she walked away, letting me know that this was not a treat.  It remains in her bowl, hours after offering it to her.It's back to the super expensive stuff. . . and the cooked chicken.  Spoiled dog?  Sure, but she's a healthy dog!

column9: My dog like the smell but not texture.
column10: If this is a snack it looks like it. The pieces remind me of cheese puffs. Their texture is puffy and it was hard for my dog to chew and swallow. The smell was appetizing even to us humans but my dog was actually scared of it after several attempts to swallow it. It has no weight and only puffed up space so it obviously has no nutritional value.
I'll keep this short as others have given long descriptions of the product.  Chef Michael's is pricey but I have a very pickey eater & she likes it.

column9: Bichon went crazy for this food
column10: It's true.  I've never seen him want food that wasn't in my kids happy meals more than this.  He even whined for more after his bowl was empty.  This stuff is great for at least one dog!

column9: Animal Fat Preserved with Mixed-Tocopherols & Animal Digest
column10: Animal digest? She does that on her own already, LOL!natural filet mignon flavor?added color:Red 40, Blue 2, Yellow 5, Yellow 6 and other color, does our Bea really need added color?Note the name is Grilled Sirloin Steak `FLAVOR' and not grilled sirloin steak.The texture is less crunchy so nice for older dogs who may not have the heartiest teeth and the sizes vary.We have blended it in with her TD & LD, also in a dish to give as treats.Kibble Crack for our 13 year old ten pound Miniature Fox Terrier.

I have two small dogs who are very picky eaters and they like this dry dog food. They don't like many dry dog foods, but they will eat this one, especially when it's mixed with some canned dog food. They like the beef flavors of the Chef Michael's canned food, so I'm assuming this dry food must have some of the same flavors. I noticed the larger pieces of food, which appear to be those that are the beef-flavored bites, get eaten first. They do eventually finish all of the food, which with my picky eaters is something to celebrate.

column9: Seems to be a Healthy dry food.
column10: I just recently moved back in with my parents. My little one is still a puppy and on puppy food, I tested it out on my parents dogs which are both adults. Since it seemed like a nice healthy choice, since my parents usually give their two chihuahuas dry food topped with a package of moist food on top. They grazed at this and didn't really finish it till their favorite part of the meal (the package of moist food) was added to the top. It is a healthy food, and just because my parents dog was not totally find it their favorite, doesn't mean all dogs will not like it. It is just not something that I will be buying on a regular basis.

column9: Finally! The spoiled dog eats her food!
column10: My dog is spoiled. She was a rescue, but I think she forgets this. When I buy her food with crunchy dog food and soft pieces mixed up, she typically only eats the the soft pieces. And when there are both red and yellow soft dog pieces, she picks out the yellow pieces first. So, due to my dog's finicky eating habits, I did not have much hope that this dog food would impress her. Still, I try to expose her to different dog foods in hopes she will like one. We've tried quite a few varieties and I always end up giving unfinished bags to my neighbors to give to their pets.  This bag, however, will finally be finished.  My dogs loves the little steak pieces.  As a senior dog, the ability for her to easily eat the food is important and it was my perception that she was able to eat this food easily -- she ate both the moist pieces and the kibble.

I am not sure if the hype about this "gourmet" dog food is for the dogs or the owners (and I expect its the latter), but Purina has come up with a great product that the dogs really enjoy, without sacrificing any of the nutrition necessary for maintaining good canine health. Both my beloved pets and myself can recommend this food.

The 4-legged critics on my taste panel are 3 hardened street dogs who usually eat anything. Yet, they will turn up their noses at something if they don't like it. They liked this. These are rescue dogs and need fattening up. Fillers in a gourmet dog food will do nicely.
My dog approved this in no time and he is super picky about his food.it is very good quality and he loves it.

column9: Strong Steak Smell Gets My Dog's Attention
column10: I currently use an upscale dog food, dry kibble with no grain, all meat and sweet potatoes. My dog likes it but gets sick of it unless I embellish it. So I was intrigued by Amazon's offer for me to try Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin. I decided not to replace my dog food with Chef Michael's but to use it as an enhancer and as a snack food.Bottom-line: My dog Gretchen loves Chef Michael's, both its strong steak smell and its taste. I decided not to do a total replacement in part because Chef Michael's has soy and corn ingredients and while I'm no expert I've read that these aren't prized ingredients in a top dog food. Let me say, though, that I don't know this as fact. This is just what people in the "dog community" tell me.However, if push came to shove and my picky dog would only eat Chef Michael's, I'd use it. For me what the dog eats is a huge factor. So if your dog doesn't have soy and/or corn allergies, you might give Chef Michael's a try.

I've got to say this is the ONLY dog food my dog has ever tried and wanted more AND I don't have to doctor it up with shredded cheddar cheese or leftovers or anything else.  She just devours it!  I don't know how to recommend this any higher than that.I know it's a tad bit more expensive than some other Purina foods, but it's well worth the money.  I will be purchasing Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Dry Dog Food again, and again, and again!Thank you Purina!!!

This is what I can tell you - my dog loves almost all of the food she eats, sneaks or straight out steals (she is a rescue dog with food issues). I cannot honestly tell you anything about this food (not having tried it myself) except that my dog loves it and snarfs it down.After looking at it on the package and than in the bowl my wife did make the comment that this dog food looks better than a lot of the stews and casseroles we have eaten.

This part of the review is being provided by a cairn terrier -- her owner is just transcribing the notes. The terrier says: I have never been that crazy about dry dog food, especially when it's compared to that great mushy stuff that comes out of a can. But this smelled and tasted so good that I pounced on it immediately and scarfed it right up. And begged for more. It tastes like meat, so I guess it is.From Divascribe: I was surprised at how quickly my dog took to this food -- she's never been particularly enthusiastic about dry food before. But the bag says "Real beef is the #1 ingredient." I looked at the ingredient list, and beef is listed first. There's a long, long list of other ingredients, some of which don't sound that appetizing (poultry byproduct meal), but unfortunately that's the case with most dog food. It has a nice, beefy scent that got my dog to stick her head in the bowl. My only concern is that, because I have an older dog, this might be a bit rich for her. So I plan to mix it in with her regular dry dog food for a while. No problems so far, though, and one very happy dog.

column9: A pet favorite in our home
column10: Our 4 year old mutt is loving this hearty dry dog food!  We had always been fans of the Chef Michael's wet canned food, giving it to our healthy dog since she was a year old.  But this new dry food is a great addition with thick, tasty chunks and nutritious ingredients.  The combination of veggies and meat make for a well balanced meal.  We don't add water to make it juicy since our dog loves sinking her teeth into the crunchy pieces, but for an occasional variation the added water mixes a nice soupy texture.  One thing I particularly like is that the food doesn't stink really badly like other commercially prepared pet foods.  An affordable, healthy choice for your pup.

column9: Great flavour and the dog seems to love it!
column10: We feed our black lab in the IQ treat ball (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003ARUKTG/). There are always a few final bits he would leave in it, but when we tried this Grilled Sirloin dry food, he would bring the ball to me to try and get even the final bits out! So it must taste pretty good. The beef pieces are a bit -odd shaped and might get stuck in those treat ball holes, but otherwise, it's fine.The daily feeding recommendations are 1 cup per 10lb body weight which seems a bit high for beef-containing dog food. For a 50 lb dog, the 4.5 lb bag might last for ~ a week (One cup of this food is ~70-75g).

column4: Shana "That's my opinion- I could be wrong!"
column9: Real beef is first ingredient, puppy loves it
column10: I'm slowly weaning my puppy off Puppy Chow, so I've been adding Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin dry food to his dry food. Pooper, my puppy, is a picky eater and he loves to steal cat food and he will hardly eat dry food unless I mix wet food into it. Though, he will eat this dog food without any wet food added to it. This dry food actually smells good even to me. My cats even tried to steal a piece of this dry food.I have 4 dogs, 3 outside my husband's coonhounds and my one inside dog,Pooper, who is a lovable mutt who is 1/2 German Shepard, 1/4 Boxer and 1/4 Cocker Spaniel. I will continue to buy this dog food for my inside dog. Though, it's too pricy on my budget to feed all of my dogs.I'd highly recommend this for any picky dog. My picky Pooper loves it.

column9: Woof! Woof! Woof, woof, woof! (... or, apparently tastes great, but...)
column10: Normally my daughter's Pomeranian is fed a diet of Taste of the Wild Dry Dog Food, Hi Prairie Canine Formula with Roasted Bison & Venison, 15-Pound Bag, or another of their variety's of dry dog food.  Thanks to some previous recommendations (a nice chart/web site that compared the various dog food products and rated them based on meat content, grain and other by-product inclusion, etc.), we'd settled on that as one of the better quality products to feed to our furry little friend.  Unfortunately there were issues with a recall related to possible salmonella in the dog food that required taking back one bag of the T.o.t.W. food, but even that was quickly enough resolved by the local store we tend to get her food from (that bag was accepted back for store credit, with me already having obtained a bag of another flavor T.o.t.W. product that wasn't on the recall list), and at this point the recall issues are long resolved for us.To get back on topic, our furry friend crunches through the small handfuls of the T.o.t.W. product about as quickly as we give it to her.  Like most dogs, she has no concept of "full" and will eat whatever is put in front of her and then come back for more.  Normally it is probably more correct to say she inhales her food, though I do hear her crunching on each piece so I know she's at least chewing it up before swallowing it.  Trying out a different brand is something we do cautiously as making too drastic a change to the diet seems to wind up providing us a dog that is capable of some pretty nasty biological output of the very odoriferous type (how a smell that potent can be emitted by such a small dog, I don't have a clue, but whew!).  On the other hand though, we do like to offer the dog a variety of food so she can enjoy something different and not just be stuck eating the same old dry food again and again.This Chef Michael's food, a product from Purina, a pet food manufacturer I remember from many, many years ago (back in my youth), sold itself to me in the "Grilled Sirloin" name.  Meat in general seems to be a favorite of the family dog, but especially beef flavors, so it seemed an easy assumption that she'd like this product.  In that area, I wasn't wrong.  As I gave her a good sized handful of food in her bowl she pulled out a chunk and went off to the side where she went to work on chewing it up and savoring the taste a bit before she decided it was something she needed to go back to get more of.  Sure enough, that chunk was quickly enough swallowed up and the rest of the bowl was soon emptied.When I put the handful of food in the bowl I noticed that the food itself did seem to resemble pieces of meat.  Definitely not a dry kibble type food, but more along the lines of a moist meat product, perhaps along the side of say a stick of pepperoni or perhaps a Slim Jim (Slim Jim Giant Slim Pepperoni, .97-Ounce (Pack of 24)).  Or, perhaps more along the lines of something I'd expect to see in a beef stew.  In that area, well, lets just say that if there was a category for "visual" appeal on the part of the human, this product would get a decent score.  But, well, there's the question of just what is in the product and that is where I'd have to say I'm not as inclined to consider purchasing this product too often.This would seem to be a product that falls more on the lower (half) end of the quality scale when it comes to not being comprised of too many fillers and products that aren't as necessary in a dog's diet.  From past experience in researching what to feed the dog, I'd long ago learned that many of what I'd call lower quality foods are filled with, well, lots of fillers.  While dogs will eat it and not really care, they don't need those fillers and given that it isn't that much more expensive to buy higher quality products, I've tried to keep our pet on a diet that would hopefully be better for her in the longer term.As an occasional change of pace in our dog's diet, I think this would be an ok product.  Perhaps just as a "treat" every now and then, but I just don't see myself rushing out to get more bags of this product instead of the Taste of the Wild products, or other products that I tend to have a bit more respect for.

It's dog food, so I really have to take Maggie's word for it.  She eats it, she doesn't seem to get tired of it, she even does a sort of doggie buffet where she grabs a mouthful, takes it a couple feet away from the bowl and puts down a line of the dog food then eats it.  I won't guarantee that your dog will do the buffet thing - she's a bit peculiar. Anyway, Maggie gives it 5 stars.

column9: Nice looking but did not excite the dog
column10: It's a visually appealing dog food (to the human eye), but I'm afraid the dog wasn't all that excited; she ate it about as much interest as her usual middle-of-the-road kibble.

I always read the ingredient labels on my food to avoid product preservatives like sodium benzoate.  Any food for my dog needs to meet the same standards.  Costco's Kirkland branded dog foods have met my budget needs as well as provided quality nourishment.  Was Chef Michael's quality enough for me to shell out twice the price?  No.  But then again, I'm cheap and I know it.I personally dont have a problem with grains and soy.  I grew up on the same ingredients in mom's cooking.  And if it's good enough foe me, it's good enough for my dog.  As long as my dogs likes the taste and receives the essential nutrients he needs, mission accomplished.

I have a dog that can be rather picky about his dog food as he much prefers to eat the human food with our dinner.  Because of his tendency to develop weight problems, we really try to discourage that and keep him on dog food.He loved this food and I had no problem getting him to accept a bowl of this happily instead of incessantly begging to share our dinner.  I was quite satisfied and will definitely be purchasing this product for future use.

I generally don't give my dog food with corn or other grains because dogs are not supposed to eat them! I actually didn't realize that this food had corn until it arrived, I didn't read the list of ingredients carefully and since it wasn't the first ingredient, I was excited and quickly made the order.My dog usually eats high quality food - either all natural foods or home made meals consisting of raw meats and vegetables. She loved this food, and ate it right away. She doesn't do that with typical dog foods unless she's really hungry so I think she enjoyed the taste. 4 stars was because it has grains in it - AND SOY!!

Our dog loved this food.  He does like most food, but he really seemed to get excited about this stuff.  It was his first adult dog food after puppy food.  He actually seemed to get a bit thin on it at times, maybe because it doesn't pack down and I was feeding him a bit less than I thought I was.  His stool seemed very healthy while on this food.  It's a good product.

column9: It looks and smells good, but my pets just didn't care for it
column10: When I first opened the bag it had a meaty smell and I thought my pets would dig in and love it.But they just sort of smelled it and left it in the bowl.I was surprised.  I read some of the other reviews before posting mine and other dog owners had some that liked it and some that didn't.It seemed like with its soft texture it would be a sure hit with any dog but such is not the case.Sorry I couldn't give a more glowing endorsement but you have to call 'em like they are.

Sometimes I feel sorry for our dogs having to eat the same kibble every day. We can tell that they also hate having the same stuff every day. One of the worst problems for a dog owner is getting them to eat once they become disenchanted with their fare. The problem s that once we lose them, they stay lost. But with this dry food they take an interest and dinnertime becomes competitive once agin as everyone tries to glom the kibble so as to deny the other a good meal. And we'd rather see that than watch them ignore their food altogether.

column9: Tasty, soft and crunchy, DOGGIE Approved
column10: My dogs, a jack russell and chihuahua, like this dry food,  the jack russell loves eating most of the soft meaty bits first then eats the crunchy veggie bits.  The chihuahua prefers the soft meaty bits and will nibble on the crunchy veggie bits last.  I can also use both the soft and crunchy bits as training treats for the dogs.  Chef Michael's dog food also has a nice aroma, quite organic and does not smell arificial and funky like some dog food, just smells natural.  There is also a lot of natural and healthy ingredients with the food.  I would definitely buy this for my dogs again.

column4: Julie A. Dawson "Bards and Sages Publishing"
column9: Average dog food above average price
column10: Despite the fancy gourmet name, it's generic dog food. Lots of fillers and average nutritional value. Chewy ate it, but for the premium price I would expect higher quality ingredients. As my vet likes to say, "How much corn do you think wolves eat in the wild?" All these grain fillers added to dog food have zero nutritional value for your pet and can lead to pet obesity and digestive problems. Better option is something like Blue Buffalo Healthy Weight Large Breed Dry Dog Food, Chicken and Rice Recipe, 30-Pound Bag (But get it at your local pet shop for half the price Amazon is selling it for!)

I know this dog food is supposedly healthy and packed full of nutrients, but I just can't shake the pet-owner's gut feeling that it's not necessarily the healthiest. It is though, a GREAT little "appetizer" that I add to the top of my dogs' regular food that gets them to start eating (they're both a little picky). They love the abundant chunks of meat and I think it adds a little variety to their meals. I will probably keep a bag on hand to add a little to their regular food as a way to encourage them to eat, since they obviously really, really like it (I caught one of my dogs with his head in the bag in the laundry room).

I'm not entirely sure if I can give an objective review for this product. Why? Well, unlike me, my dog is not a picky eater. He'll eat anything we give to him, including carrots and the occasional licking of a yogurt spoon. I think his voracious appetite was passed on to him by his predecessor, who once ate a pound of cheddar cheese my mother and I naively placed on our kitchen counter before going out to run a few errands.So for that reason, I don't think my review is going to be all that helpful for those considering buying this product. My dog was on another brand of dog chow, but we slowly began the transition from his food to this product. When James is usually fed breakfast, lunch, or dinner, he eats it pretty fast. But once he was fully on Chef Michael's dog chow, James inhaled his meals. I have never seen my dog eat his food so fast.So I guess it was a hit, after all!

. . .but when you get to the middle of the bag, all the larger pieces are gone and all you're left with are small pieces of dog food, even pebbles.  The food at the top of the bag contains larger, "fluffier" pieces of dog food that look very appetizing, and when these pieces fill our dogs dish, she eats the food rather quickly.  But as the bag is emptied and you get to the middle and bottom of the bag, all those larger pieces are gone and all that's left are small round pebble-like pieces of dog food, that my dog usually lets sit in her dish for a while.  Shaking up the bag, or mixing it up could help, but it would be nice to see an even consistency to the food, rather than having all the "good stuff" at the top, with crumbs and pebbles at the bottom.  I also don't think the food is very nutritious or filling, as our dog is always looking for more food or appears hungry after eating this. We seemed to go through the bag rather quickly, even though it was a large bag.  Perhaps this is meant to be mixed with regular dog food or only as an occasional "treat" and not part of a dogs regular diet.  In my opinion, it's not worth the extra cost if my dog doesnt appears satisfied after eating, which she rarely did with this food.

column9: My dogs favor the sirloin over the chicken
column10: My dogs liked the previous flavors (chicken, etc.) so I was enthused to try this new flavor.  My dogs seemed to liked this even better than the chicken.  Not sure what more to say about it since I am only able to see a visual response.  Appears to be a good, premium, slightly expensive dry dog food.

This didn't last long. The amount of food was fairly generous,but my dogs really loved it! My only complaint is my 3 three dogs liked it too much and I would be purchasing more very soon. In the future We'll mix it in with their regular food as a treat rather than a meal just so it would last. As a footnote, one of our dogs was off her feed for awhile,but this snapped her out of it.

I must confess to having two of the pickiest eaters on the planet.  Granted, there are plenty of websites toting that Chef Michael's is not the best food for the pooches.  I scanned the ingredients and saw that, yeah, that may be true.  However, we live a very active lifestyle (to stay trim and slim) and this is a food that they devour nearly before the bowl hits the floor.  Amazing.  Pedigree?  Not so much.  Purina?  Nada.  Blue?  Yeah, right.With Chef Michael's, I actually garnish their bowls with fresh steamed brocoli and they adore it.  Highly recommended as a food solution.

column9: Better than many other dog snacks,but still too many chemicals & filler
column10: My dog loved it, and so did my cats! (They got into the bag when it first arrived)But then again, my dog eats bugs and sometimes his own poo... despite being a purebred, he's not exactly what I'd call a connoisseur.At first I was quite impressed with this latest development in processed foods - Chef Michael's sirloin bits really look like real steak, and it doesn't need to be refrigerated. However, the "realistic" shape & texture of the food isn't important to my dog, but the ingredients ARE important to me!This is better than most dry dog foods, with beef as the first ingredient. But it's also has too much corn & grain fillers, preservatives, & chemicals.So if you have a super finicky pet who won't eat the healthy stuff, this is super tasty and not as bad as most. However, I won't be buying it, as there are too many healthy & natural alternatives which my dog loves just as well (and for about the same price) ... Nutro, Newman's Own, and Nature's Variety, just to name a few.Hope this helps!

My two senior dogs are very picky eaters, they even turn down some treats! When dog food was tainted and recalled a few years ago I switched my male cockapoo and female cairn terrier to a fresh cooked diet from a pet "deli."  It is expensive and an hour from my home but they have remained on this diet because every time I tried to change back they went on hunger strikes.  I have been incoorporating Michael's dog food into their diets slowly over the past few weeks and they both have been eating every morsel.  These dogs hae been offered no less than six other brands of dog food in the past and usually they just walk away from their dishes. I finally told my family to remind me next time I complain about their food price that they will not switch and just bite the time and money bullet to keep them on the deli diet. I ordered a sample bag from the Vine review program and I am so happy to report the dog reviewers really like it. Just remember to introduce a new food gradually to ease the stress on any dog's digestive track.

column9: Soft chewy and great treat for a smaller dog as well as biggie
column10: Our Jack Russell is used to her controlled diet, but we sometime like to give her a handful of treats here and there. This 5 lb bag is loaded with chewy, and mixed food that she goes crazy for, and we use as a supplement for being good (watching a dog nose away the old food for this is something funny to see).Terrific, balanced dietary food that has the feel and texture of premium food and is a superb product. Saw it on shelf at Target; got it here, really pleased with it.  Chef Michael's is very, very good!

column9: My dog thinks he's died and gone to heaven (or something like that)
column10: This dog food has made my dog very happy.  I have been using a quality dog food before trying the Chef Michael's, and he liked it just fine, but would eat the chewy pieces first and sometimes the dry pieces would sit for a while before he would finally eat them.  With Chef Michael's dog food, he not only eats the chewy pieces, but also the crunchy potato and green bean kibble.  It even smells better than other dog foods and I feel pretty good about feeding him something he enjoys so much.Beef is the first ingredient listed, which is great, and unlike some dog foods where corn is the first ingredient, corn is the 7th ingredient listed.  Also listed as ingredients are 23 minerals and vitamins, including Vitamins E, B-12, and D, folic acid, niacin, calcium, manganese, potassium and lysine.  However, it also contains a few strange ingredients such as "animal digest", and it has a lot of "meals" and "flours" in it. I do not know if they are optimum for dogs or are just used as fillers.Pricewise, it compares nicely to Purina One and Beneful, which I have also fed my dog.

OK - So I haven't tasted this myself, and my dog can't type, so I can only go by my impressions of my dog's behavior.Ingredient-wise, it's nice to see that beef is number one, though one assumes that is only the red pieces. The others have ingredients some folks want to avoid in pet foods, but that's personal choice of course. I'd suggest closely reading the ingredient list to see if it suits your needs.As another reviewer said, there are a lot of calories in a serving, and that serving is only 28% protein: surprising if the first ingredient is meat, though understandable when you factor in the vegetable kibble. Again, these are all choices pet owners need to make for themselves.What it really comes down to in the end, assuming the issues above are acceptable, is how a dog likes it. In my case, our dog likes it quite a bit up to a point: she picks out the meaty bits and leaves the veggies behind. I suppose if we just left those bits there she'd eventually eat them, but that doesn't seem like a balanced way to feed her.So for us, obviously, this food simply won't work. What our dog eats she loves, but she avoids more than she enjoys.

column9: A Month Later and They're Still Eating It
column10: My two little yorkies are finicky pups.  They'll eat something when it's new, but a week later turn their noses up at it.  It's been a month now and they're still eating it.When I first opened the package, they didn't exactly jump for joy.  In fact, they backed away from it.  I held one of the pieces out to them and they seemed very disinterested.  I was thinking for a minute there they weren't going to eat it at all.  And, this is a very big bag of dog food for two little dogs.  However, when I put it in their dish they started eating right away.  Because the pieces are rather large for small dogs, they can only eat one piece at a time.  The food seems to be a bit chewy, so it takes a while to eat one piece.  There's no real oder that I can smell, but because it doesn't smell like Pupa-roni they aren't fighting over it.

column9: Good dog food, but a bit pricey
column10: If they're picky eaters dogs may care about the size, shape, texture, smell, and/or taste of a food; or, if they're like my dog, they care that it stays still long enough that they can gobble it down.  Owners should care about calorie content, that the food is intended for the proper age group (puppy, adult, or senior), and that the food is certified to meet the nutritional requirements set by the Association of American Feed Control Officials (AAFCO). And, unless you are independently wealthy, price.Because my dog is not a picky eater, I can't comment on the taste of Chef Michael's. However, it is much higher in calories than a basic dog food such as Pedigree Adult Complete Nutrition Small Crunchy Bites Original Beef Dry Dog Food, 30-Pound, which means that a much smaller amount should be fed, something that she definitely objects to.There is one notable point about Chef Michael's-All pet foods produced in the United States must meet certain minimal nutritional requirements, which are set by AAFCO. Somewhere on its bag or can each food will have a short statement saying that is has either been *formulated* to meet AAFCO standards, or has undergone *feeding trials* and been shown to meet AAFCO standards. AAFCO has set standards for 2 life stages; growth (i.e. puppies) and reproduction, and adult. (Senior is not recognized as a separate stage.) Because feeding trials are so expensive, such foods are usually formulated to meet the needs of *all life stages*. Growth and gestation/lactation have much higher nutritional requirements than a normal adult dog has. Therefore, such a food may not be ideal, particularly if you pet has a weight problem.  Foods that are *formulated* (i.e. do not undergo feeding tests), are more often designed to meet the needs of a specific life stage. Chef Michael's is the only pet food (dog or cat), that I have ever found that has undergone feeding trials AND is designed for a specific life stage.The importance of feeding trials, formulations, and life stages is debatable, and in the end is an individual decision.Finally, despite what some people claim, it is not possible to assess the quality of a food from the ingredient list. Ingredient descriptions, for example any listing of a meat product or by-product, are vague and there can be huge variation in the quality of a product with the same name from one food to another. In the same vein, claims that certain ingredients shouldn't be in dog food should be taken with a grain (or large jar) of salt. When chosing a food for your pet, talk to your vet, don't believe a stranger on the internet with unknown qualifications.As for me, although my dog enjoyed Chef Michael's, both the calorie content and price are too high to make it her normal dog food.

I have two dogs, both Pomeranians. One is 16 and has no teeth, and the other is eight and an extremely picky eater. My older dog will eat just about anything, so it was no surprise to me that the minute I poured this into a bowl he beelined straight for it and tried to chow down. Only -- poor dog -- these pieces were too hard and too large for him.The picky eater, on the other hand, gave these a whiff and timidly tried a few bites. In my household, this is a success! It's a rare story for him to even try anything new we buy for him. We leave these out all day for the dogs to eat whenever they get hungry and I will spy the picky dog going for a nibble throughout the day.

Mickey, my toy poodle..who is overweight by the way, has been eating Beneful (healthy weight) not sure why, since he is as I stated overweight. I was trying to save this bag for when I ran out of the big bag I already have. I noticed that Mickey eats all of the soft pieces from his bowl, and leaves the others there until he is starving,so I thought why not try it out.Well he was excited by the bag itself..and it does look good enough for human consumption if you just look at the bag, so he probably thought it was real food, I don't think he caught the "Chef Michael" but maybe he did since he sometimes acts as if he can read. Anyway, he was jumping up and down and ready to eat.I only give him half a cup, but he munched it right up. Afterwards, I caught him going in the bag..which he never does, so I had to lock it up! This am, he was so ready to eat that he came straight in from his morning business..I didn't have to call him or hunt him down!I don't know if it's actually good for him..I don't read labels..sorry but from some of the other reviews..it ain't good for him! If Mickey were writing the review I think he would give it 10 stars..maybe his old food is boring. If you are concerned about the ingredients, you may want to pick another kind. Mickey is 8yrs old..so I treat him like a senior citizen and let him eat almost whatever he wants. :)

column9: The Chef is in, but is he cooking my dog "fast food?"
column10: Tested on RUGER, 11 year old male neutered beagle type dog, 17 inches high and 25 pounds. Moderate activity level.Slightly crazy, very lovable, goofy disposition, quite the momma's boy.Over a week I offered this food to my dog along side a bowl of his regular diet. His regular diet is Purina D/H mixed Loyall Lamb and Rice kibble.He is a pretty predictable dog, and every day he chose to eat his D/H chunks out first, then a few kibbles of the Loyall, than he would eat a few bites of the Chef Michaels.So, he did like it, and he did eat it.There were a few things that drew my attention.1. No where on the bag does it say where the ingredients are sourced. Is he eating American beef? Mexico?Now, it doesn't say where his food is sourced on his D/H (Purina Dental Health) BUT, he loves that food SO MUCH and it keeps his teeth so nice I do continue to feed it to him. After all, I can't source where all the ingredients I EAT come from, so why should my dog eat better than I do? So, it isn't a major issue, but for those who really want to know, well, you will have to contact Purina.2. The food felt FLUFFY and a bit greasy, and the red dyed beefy bits drifted with handling to the top. So, you have to shake before serving to get the kibbles to mix in a more uniform way before feeding. Otherwise, your dog gets a bowl of soft beefy bits and no kibble.3. The kibble pieces did not seem crunchy enough to prevent tartar build up. Hummm. Perhaps after a long feeding diet of this your pet will NEED Purina D/H. I may be on to something here. I doubt this diet will do anything for dental health for your dog.4. Why add artificial colors? Really? He doesn't even look at the food. At 11 years old, His sight may be questionable anyway and as a BEAGLE he doesn't look in the bowl before eating. He sniffs everything. To my dog, smell is everything. And for most dogs, I've never seen them eye each piece of kibble before chowing down. I seriously doubt dogs care if the potato bits are brown, the green bean kibbles are green, or the meat is red. Actually, after cooking, it should be brown as well. The colors can be left out, they are unnecessary. BUT, then again, as a kid who grew up on Kool-Aid, Mom enjoyed mixing up all those great colorful drinks for us, and we grew up fine (twitch twitch) but I state again, no sense in my dog eating better than me. (Now I want some red fruity punch just writing this)5. Serving size is WAY too much. Each cup of this food has 270 calories. THAT IS A LOT! 28% protein and 16% fat. That is a bit more protein and fat than my guy is used to, so, it may be a bit "rich" for some dogs. ALSO, take notice, not all that protein is from those dried beefy looking chewy chunks. There are other sources of proteins in here, from Chicken by product meal, corn gluten, and soy. These are all sources of protein, but it may seem misleading if you think the protein is all from beef (which is, by the way, the number one ingredient)6. The fat is "animal fat" so your guess is as good as mine. Emu? Llama? Pig? Sheep? Deer? Bison? Snake?
